While the packaging is being opened at the tray
After the container has been sealed for collection
preguntas.explicacion: Injuries from sharps commonly occur between the use of a needle or similar device and its disposal, which is the window that recapping, disassembly and a distant sharps container all lengthen. Discarding into a puncture-resistant container straight away markedly reduces these injuries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), Normal Results
preguntas.subtema: Timed drug levels · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 medication levels · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A lithium level is ordered for a patient with bipolar disorder. How long after the dose should the blood be drawn, and what is the target range?
opciones: 12 hours after the dose, for a target of 0.5 to 1.2 mEq/L
12 hours after the dose, for a target of 5 to 10 mEq/L
2 hours after the dose, for a target of 0.5 to 1.2 mEq/L
24 hours after the dose, for a target of 1.2 to 2.0 mEq/L
preguntas.explicacion: Lithium is reported with the sample taken 12 hours after the dose, and the target range is 0.5 to 1.2 mEq/L (0.5 to 1.2 mmol/L). The same 12-hour rule applies to cyclosporine, tacrolimus and sirolimus. Ranges of 5 to 10 belong to aminoglycoside levels in mcg/mL, and 0.8 to 2.0 ng/mL is digoxin: mixing the units is what makes these figures easy to confuse.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Clinical Resource Management Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care: Capitated payment
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Under capitation, how is the clinician paid?
opciones: A fixed amount per patient, no matter what services that patient uses
A fixed amount per service, set in advance by a published fee schedule
A single payment covering every service tied to one condition or treatment
A share of the savings earned when quality benchmarks are also reached
preguntas.explicacion: Capitation pays the clinician a fixed sum for each patient, whatever services that patient goes on to receive. It pushes clinicians to hold costs down and to put preventive care first, though it also raises worries about patient selection and about services being underused. Fee schedules, bundled episode payment and shared savings are the other arrangements described.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient receives ABO-incompatible blood. What happens to the transfused red cells, and which organ is at risk of failing?
opciones: Antibodies clump them; hemolysis then overloads the kidneys with hemoglobin
They sickle and lodge in narrow capillaries, starving the brain of oxygen
They are phagocytized by macrophages in the spleen, which fails under the load
Platelets coat them and form thrombi that occlude the coronary arteries
preguntas.explicacion: In a transfusion reaction, antibodies bind the foreign antigens on the donated erythrocytes and clump them together, a process called agglutination; the clumps block small vessels, and as they are degraded (hemolysis) their hemoglobin floods the blood. The kidneys cannot clear that load and the patient can rapidly develop kidney failure. Sickling and thrombi are other disorders entirely.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A hospice patient being cared for at home asks what she may be charged for a medicine given to control her pain.
opciones: A copayment of up to $5 for each drug prescribed for pain or symptom control
A copayment of up to $35, the ceiling that applies to a month of covered insulin
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most services covered by Part B
Five percent of the approved amount, which is the share for inpatient respite care
preguntas.explicacion: Covered hospice services cost the patient nothing under Part A. What she may still owe is up to $5 in copayment on each prescription drug, and on similar products used at home to relieve pain and control symptoms, plus five percent of the amount approved for respite care given as an inpatient. The $35 ceiling belongs to covered insulin under Part B.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Electrical injury", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found slumped against a floor lamp with a frayed cord and is not moving. What is the first action?
opciones: Turn off the current at the breaker before touching the patient at all
Pull the patient away by an arm and start checking for breathing
Unplug the lamp and then move the patient with a metal walker frame
Start compressions at once and have someone unplug the lamp meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: The current goes off first: unplug the cord, pull the fuse or trip the breaker, since switching an appliance off may not stop the flow. The patient is not touched with bare hands while still in contact with the source; a non-metallic object is used to separate them. Only then are airway, breathing and pulse checked and first aid begun.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Collection; Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Short draw in citrate tube · PBT IV.A.3 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(5) INR (2027: b.(8)) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A light-blue-top tube for a PT/INR arrives filled to about half its volume. How does this affect the result?
opciones: Excess citrate relative to plasma prolongs the clotting time, so the result is falsely high
Excess citrate relative to plasma shortens the clotting time, so the result is falsely low
The 9 to 1 ratio corrects itself during centrifugation, so the PT is not affected by the volume
Only the aPTT is affected by underfilling; the PT can be reported exactly as it was measured
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate tubes are pre-filled with 3.2 % sodium citrate for a blood-to-anticoagulant ratio of 9 to 1, and the tube must be filled to at least 90 % of its stated volume, marked by a line. A short draw leaves too much anticoagulant for the plasma present and prolongs clotting times, giving a falsely long PT and high INR. Nothing in centrifugation restores the ratio, and the effect applies to clot-based tests generally.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Active features
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A safety needle requires the user to activate its shield after the draw. How does the FDA say an active feature should be designed to work?
opciones: It can be activated with one hand, with the hands staying behind the exposed sharp
It can be activated with two hands, so that the shield locks firmly over the needle tip
It activates on its own as the needle leaves the vein, with no user action
It is activated after the needle has been placed in the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: For active features, those the user must trigger, FDA Table 1 recommends that activation be possible with a single-handed technique that lets the user's hands remain behind the exposed sharp. A two-handed action brings a hand toward the point. Automatic activation describes a passive feature, and the feature is meant to protect during handling before and through disposal, not after.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Plasma Proteins and Blood Plasma; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Common Pathway
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is essential for clotting and is therefore no longer present in serum?
opciones: Fibrinogen
Albumin
Transferrin
Immunoglobulin
preguntas.explicacion: Fibrinogen is the third major plasma protein group, made by the liver and required for coagulation; in the common pathway thrombin turns it into insoluble fibrin. Because serum is plasma with the clotting factors removed, fibrinogen (factor I) is gone from serum. Albumin and the immunoglobulins are not clotting factors, and transferrin is the plasma carrier of iron.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.c · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: What separates HCPCS Level I from HCPCS Level II?
opciones: Level I is CPT, kept by the AMA; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by CMS
Level I is CPT, kept by CMS; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by the AMA
Level I codes diagnoses and Level II codes the procedures done to treat them
Level I is used by hospitals for inpatient care and Level II by offices for visits
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS has two subsystems. Level I is Current Procedural Terminology, a numeric system of five digits that the American Medical Association maintains and republishes each year. Level II is a standardized alphanumeric system, a letter followed by four digits, for products, supplies and services outside Level I such as ambulance and durable medical equipment, and CMS maintains it. Diagnoses are coded in ICD-10-CM.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: What makes an interpreter 'qualified' under the ADA effective-communication rules?
opciones: Interprets accurately, impartially and effectively, receptively and expressively
Holds a state license and is directly employed by the covered entity
Is a family member fluent in sign language and already known to the patient
Is certified only for the specialized vocabulary of the medical setting
preguntas.explicacion: A qualified interpreter is someone who can interpret accurately, impartially and to effect, both receptively, understanding the person, and expressively, carrying the information back, using whatever specialized vocabulary is needed. Family members often lack the impartiality and the vocabulary, and the definition turns on skill rather than on employment or licensing.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Acute and Chronic Diseases
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which contrast between a latent disease and a chronic infection is correct?
opciones: In a latent disease the pathogen goes dormant with no active replication
In a latent disease the pathogen replicates faster than in a chronic one
In a latent disease the pathogen is cleared and cannot ever come back
In a latent disease the pathogen is always a bacterium rather than a virus
preguntas.explicacion: In a latent disease the causal pathogen goes dormant for long stretches with no active replication, unlike a chronic infection. Herpes simplex, varicella-zoster and Epstein-Barr all do this and can wake up later, which is why chickenpox in childhood can return decades on as shingles.

preguntas.subtema: Contingency operations · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A burst pipe closes the suite, and the technicians need to get inside the damaged office to bring the data back. Which specification should have planned for that?
opciones: Contingency operations, which arrange facility access in support of the recovery plans
Emergency access procedure, which gets a clinician to the record during an emergency
Applications and data criticality analysis, which ranks what has to come back first
Testing and revision procedures, which put the contingency plan through a rehearsal
preguntas.explicacion: Contingency operations is the physical safeguard: procedures allowing access to the facility so that lost data can be restored under the disaster recovery and emergency mode plans. The emergency access procedure is the technical twin, and it is about reaching the information itself, not the building.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A cuff that is too small for the patient's arm is used. Which way does the reading err?
opciones: Falsely high, while a cuff that is too large produces a falsely low reading
Falsely low, while a cuff that is too large produces a falsely high reading
Falsely high, and a cuff that is too large errs in the same direction
Neither, so long as the bladder still encircles the arm without a gap
preguntas.explicacion: An undersized cuff pushes the value up and an oversized one pulls it down. That asymmetry is why guidance says to take the larger cuff when the choice is not obvious: an artificially low reading is less likely to trigger treatment nobody needs. Cuff size is checked before the arm is even wrapped.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Fire Hazards, 29 CFR 1910.38(b) and 1910.39(b)
preguntas.subtema: Emergency action plan · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan must be in writing. What does OSHA's rule provide?
opciones: With 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
It must be in writing regardless of size and posted at each exit
With fewer than 25 employees it may be oral; above that it must be written
It may be oral only if the clinic also has no fire prevention plan
preguntas.explicacion: Under 29 CFR 1910.38(b), as the eTool summarizes it, an emergency action plan is normally written, kept at the workplace and available to employees; where there are 10 employees or fewer, the employer may simply brief them orally. Section 1910.39(b) sets the same threshold for the fire prevention plan. The two plans stand apart, so having or lacking one changes nothing for the other. With 8 employees this clinic may brief its staff by word of mouth, though the minimum elements of 1910.38(c) still have to be covered.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Conduction System of the Heart; Atrioventricular Bundle, Bundle Branches, and Purkinje Fibers
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A student is asked to put the conduction system in order, from where the impulse starts to where it reaches the ventricular muscle. Which sequence is right?
opciones: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, bundle of His, AV node, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV node, Purkinje fibers, bundle of His, bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting components run in order: the sinoatrial node starts the impulse, internodal pathways carry it across the atria to the atrioventricular node, where it pauses about 100 ms; it then runs down the bundle of His in the interventricular septum, splits into the two bundle branches, and reaches the Purkinje fibers, which spread it through the ventricular muscle from the apex up.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.1 The Language of Epidemiologists, Patterns of Incidence
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k42 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Malaria is constantly present at a low level in some regions of Brazil but not in the United States. Which pattern of incidence is that?
opciones: Endemic, a disease constantly present within a geographic region
Sporadic, a disease seen only occasionally and without concentration
Epidemic, a disease with more cases than expected in a short time
Pandemic, a disease whose case count has grown on a worldwide scale
preguntas.explicacion: The four patterns run by scale and expectation. Sporadic diseases turn up only now and then and scattered, such as tetanus, rabies and plague. Endemic ones are always there in a region, as malaria is in parts of Brazil. Epidemic means more cases than expected in a short time, and a pandemic is an epidemic gone worldwide.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Clotting Factors Involved in Coagulation and Table 18.1; and MedlinePlus, Coagulation Factor Tests, Why do I need a coagulation factor test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with severe liver disease and a vitamin K deficiency bleeds longer than usual after a draw. Why is coagulation impaired?
opciones: The liver makes most clotting factors and needs vitamin K for many
Vitamin K is factor IV, the calcium needed for the entire cascade
The liver stores the platelets that release ADP and serotonin
Vitamin K activates plasmin, so clots dissolve as fast as they form
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting factors come mostly from the liver and the platelets, and the liver cannot build several of them without vitamin K, which is fat-soluble: factors II, VII, IX and X carry that mark in the table. Serious liver disease and a shortage of vitamin K are both listed causes of bleeding. Calcium is factor IV, and it is the spleen, not the liver, that stores platelets.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Downtime job aid · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which job aid does the contingency guidance suggest an organization hand its staff for use during an outage?
opciones: A small self-contained card or checklist of the resources and actions available
A printed copy of the whole electronic record of every patient booked that day
A telephone list of the software developer's support engineers and their hours
A binder holding the last six months of temperature and equipment inspection logs
preguntas.explicacion: Next to training and drills the guidance names a concrete tool: a job aid, which it describes as a reference card or checklist, small and self-contained, that helps staff locate the resources and the actions open to them while the record system is down. It is meant to work when nothing on the screen can be consulted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(5) (2027 I.C.6.g(5)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which exposure accounts for most cases of COPD in high-income countries, and what does that leave for the rest?
opciones: Cigarette smoking, with up to a quarter or more of patients who never smoked
Cigarette smoking, with essentially no patients who have never smoked at all
Biomass fuel smoke, with cigarette smoking a distant second in those countries
Occupational dust, with cigarette smoking a distant second in those countries
preguntas.explicacion: Cigarette smoking is behind roughly 70 to 80 percent of COPD in high-income countries, but between a quarter and nearly half of patients have never smoked, so smoke from burning biomass fuel, exposures at work and the patient's own genetics matter too. The disease itself is persistent, progressive airflow limitation from small airway disease and emphysema.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(c), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k92 · PBT VI.F (CLIA) · CCMA 3E14 k146 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory cannot perform a test and wants to send the specimen out. To which kind of laboratory may it refer the specimen under CLIA?
opciones: Only to a CLIA-certified laboratory or one CMS deems to meet equivalent requirements
To any laboratory that agrees in writing to return results within the clinic's turnaround time
To any hospital laboratory, since hospitals are exempt from the CLIA certificate requirement
To any laboratory accredited by a private body, whether or not it holds a CLIA certificate
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(c) restricts referral to laboratories that hold a CLIA certificate or that CMS has determined meet equivalent requirements. A turnaround agreement, hospital status or private accreditation on its own does not satisfy the rule. When a laboratory accepts referrals, it must in turn give its clients written instructions on preparation, collection, labeling, storage, transport, processing and acceptability.

preguntas.subtema: Automatic logoff · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The record system ends a session by itself after fifteen idle minutes. Which technical specification is that, and what is its status?
opciones: Automatic logoff, an addressable specification of the access control standard
Unique user identification, a required specification of that same standard
Emergency access procedure, a required specification of that same standard
Person or entity authentication, a standard with no specification of its own
preguntas.explicacion: Access control carries four specifications: unique user identification and emergency access are required, while automatic logoff and encryption are addressable. Ending a session after a predetermined period of inactivity is automatic logoff, so it may be replaced by an equivalent measure if the practice documents why.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: How does the red-gray tiger top or gold serum separator tube separate the serum, according to the WHO table?
opciones: A gel at the bottom of the tube separates blood from serum when it is centrifuged
A clot activator on the tube wall makes the blood clot so the serum can be poured off
Lithium heparin keeps the blood liquid and a gel separates the plasma on spinning
Sodium citrate binds calcium and the serum rises above the cells within an hour
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists no additive for the serum separator tube and describes its action as a gel at the bottom that separates blood from serum on centrifugation, for chemistries, immunology and serology. The clot activator belongs to the plain red tube; lithium heparin with a gel is the light green PST, which yields plasma; and sodium citrate is the coagulation tube, which never yields serum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Undetected hemolysis in POCT · CPT D5 k90 · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 k111 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why is hemolysis a particular concern for fingerstick whole blood point-of-care tests such as potassium?
opciones: Hemolysis cannot be seen in whole blood, so an affected result may be reported without anyone noticing it
Hemolysis is detected automatically by every whole blood device, which then refuses to display any result
Hemolysis only develops after 24 hours of storage, so it never affects a sample tested at the bedside
Hemolysis affects urine reagent strips but not blood analytes, so potassium results are unaffected by it
preguntas.explicacion: Detecting hemolysis in whole blood samples, including fingerstick specimens, is challenging. Central laboratories measure hemolysis, icterus and lipemia indices spectrophotometrically, but in POCT these can be recognized only by looking at a centrifuged aliquot, a step whole blood devices skip. Hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can give inaccurate or incalculable results, and potassium measurements are especially susceptible, so a hemolyzed fingerstick potassium can pass unnoticed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples); and MedlinePlus, Medical Tests, Flu (Influenza) Test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen for bacterial culture cannot be plated for two hours, and a technician places it in the refrigerator to preserve it. What is wrong with that?
opciones: CSF for microbiology is never refrigerated: cold cuts the survival of Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis
CSF for microbiology must be frozen at −20 °C or lower, because refrigeration alone does not stop cellular degeneration
CSF for microbiology must travel on wet ice, since room temperature lets the glucose fall before the culture is set up
CSF for microbiology belongs in a carbon dioxide incubator only; room temperature is not an accepted alternative for it
preguntas.explicacion: Hold cerebrospinal fluid for microbiology at room temperature, or in a carbon-dioxide-enriched incubator, until it is worked up. Chilling costs the survival of fastidious organisms, Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis among them, and the culture can come back falsely negative. Freezing belongs to delayed serology, wet ice to bronchoalveolar lavage, refrigeration to serum awaiting prompt serology.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Body Cavities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.d (2027 I.C.6.c) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures are housed in the dorsal body cavity, and how is that cavity subdivided?
opciones: The brain and the spinal cord, in a cranial and a spinal portion
The heart and the lungs, in a pleural and a pericardial portion
The stomach and the liver, in an upper and a lower portion
The bladder and the rectum, in a pelvic and a perineal portion
preguntas.explicacion: The body has two great cavities. The dorsal one is the smaller and holds nervous tissue: the cranial portion houses the brain and the spinal or vertebral portion the spinal cord, and the two run into each other without a break. Heart, lungs and digestive organs all sit in the ventral cavity instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which body measurements carry the widest variation from one measurer to the next?
opciones: Head circumference, waist circumference and the ratios built from them
Weight, standing height and the body mass index built from those two
Recumbent length, bare weight and the head circumference of an infant
Waist circumference, standing height and the length of the upper arm
preguntas.explicacion: The classical measures, weight and height and the body mass index they produce, are the least prone to measurement error. Head circumference, waist circumference and head-to-waist ratios vary far more. Error is also more frequent in patients with obesity, where the bony landmarks are harder to find, and training improves the figures only slightly.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(2), (3), (4) and (5), Inspection, maintenance and testing
preguntas.subtema: Extinguisher inspection · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.5.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: How often must portable fire extinguishers be visually inspected, and how often given a maintenance check?
opciones: Visually inspected monthly; maintenance check annually, with the date recorded
Visually inspected annually; maintenance check every 6 years
Visually inspected weekly; maintenance check every 12 years, the hydrostatic interval
Visually inspected monthly; maintenance check every 3 years, kept with training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e) of 29 CFR 1910.157 puts inspection, maintenance and testing on the employer: a visual inspection every month, and once a year a maintenance check whose date is written down and kept for a year past the last entry, or for as long as the shell lasts, whichever comes first. Stored-pressure dry chemical units due for a 12-year hydrostatic test are also emptied and serviced every 6 years. While a unit is away for maintenance or recharging, equivalent protection has to be provided.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1252(e); CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Preparing for Testing; Appendix A
preguntas.subtema: Do not mix kit lots · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.f
preguntas.pregunta: A kit of rapid test cassettes is running low on extraction reagent, and an opened kit with a different lot number has plenty left. May the reagents be combined?
opciones: No; components of kits with different lot numbers are not interchanged unless the manufacturer allows it
Yes, provided both lots are within their expiration dates and stored at the same temperature
Yes, if an external control is run once with the mixed reagent and gives the expected result
No, unless the two lots were received in the same shipment from the same distributor
preguntas.explicacion: Components from kits of different lot numbers are not to be swapped around unless the manufacturer says otherwise, and the waived-testing guidance says the same: every component reagent of a kit comes from one kit lot, and reagents are never mixed across lot numbers. Lot numbers are recorded as well, so any result can be traced back. A passing control does not make a combination the manufacturer forbids acceptable.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Layers; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart, Layers of the Heart Wall
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Name the three layers of the heart wall from outside in, and identify the thickest.
opciones: Epicardium, myocardium, endocardium; the myocardium is thickest
Endocardium, myocardium, epicardium; the myocardium is thickest
Epicardium, myocardium, endocardium; the epicardium is thickest
Pericardium, myocardium, endothelium; the endocardium is thickest
preguntas.explicacion: From superficial to deep the wall is epicardium, myocardium and endocardium. The epicardium is also the visceral layer of the pericardium; the myocardium, made of cardiac muscle in a swirling pattern, is the middle and thickest layer and does the pumping; the endocardium lines the chambers. Reversing the order puts the endocardium outside, which is wrong.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act, Title III
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, ADA · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.1.c laws and acts · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance
preguntas.pregunta: Under which title of the ADA does a private physician's office or an independent laboratory fall?
opciones: Title III, which covers nonprofits and businesses that serve the public
Title I, which covers employers with fifteen or more employees
Title II, which covers the programs of state and local governments
Title IV, which covers telecommunication companies and relay service
preguntas.explicacion: The law splits into five titles by the kind of organization. A doctor's office or a hospital is named among the nonprofits and businesses that serve the public, which is Title III. A public hospital, or a clinic run by a state or local government, falls under Title II instead; Title I is the employment title, and Title IV covers telephone companies.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k148 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1
preguntas.pregunta: The ten leads are attached and the strip is about to run. What is the patient told?
opciones: To relax, breathe normally and lie still without talking
To relax, breathe deeply and hold each breath in turn
To relax, breathe normally and cross the ankles loosely
To relax, breathe normally and keep the arms folded up
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is to relax, breathe normally and stay still without speaking while the strip runs, together with the reassurance that nothing will hurt. Talking and moving are what put tremor and drift on the tracing, and the arms stay at the sides with the legs uncrossed.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital maps where its rejected specimens are collected, so it can aim its training at the worst areas. What did the published audit find?
opciones: Rejections came mainly from the adult emergency department, not the pediatric one
Rejections came mainly from the pediatric emergency department, well above the adult one
Rejections came mainly from surgical intensive care, well above the non-surgical units
Rejections came mainly from inpatient services, ahead of every emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency departments produced 41 % of the rejected samples, intensive care 31 % and inpatient services 28 %. Broken down by service, the adult emergency department alone accounted for 31 % and the pediatric one for 10 %, a threefold difference the authors themselves called surprising. Neurology intensive care followed at 14 % and internal medicine inpatients at 10 %.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Classifications of Disease
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which group of pathogens is acellular rather than cellular?
opciones: Viruses, viroids and prions
Bacteria, parasites and fungi
Bacteria, viruses and parasites
Fungi, protozoa and helminths
preguntas.explicacion: An infectious disease is one a pathogen causes directly, and pathogens fall into two camps. The cellular ones are bacteria, parasites and fungi; the acellular ones are viruses, viroids and prions. Helminths are parasitic worms, most of them large enough to see without a microscope.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), sections 1 and 4
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.A.3 · CCMA 3D5 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to hold specimens longer than the kit insert allows so that it can batch its runs. What does it owe before changing the acceptability criteria?
opciones: An in-house study showing the specimen still holds up under its own conditions
Written approval from the manufacturer covering the modified storage condition
A comment on every report stating that the insert conditions were not followed
Registration of the modified condition with the organization that accredits it
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories do modify manufacturer instructions to suit their workflow or to stretch a reagent, and the responsibility for validating specimen stability, and so for defining what it will accept, falls on the laboratory itself under accreditation requirements. Most supplement the kit recommendations with their own stability studies, and where resources will not stretch to that, the advice is to take the more conservative published criteria rather than the longer one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asystole", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: A monitor shows a flat line while the patient sits up and talks. What is the likely explanation?
opciones: An electrode has come off, so that lead has no signal
The patient has gone into asystole and needs CPR at once
The paper speed was set too low for the rhythm to show
The standardization was halved, flattening every complex
preguntas.explicacion: Telling a dysrhythmia from an artifact starts with the patient. A person who is awake and speaking has a circulation, so a flat trace in one lead points to an electrode that has fallen off, a known problem on hairy or loose skin. Real asystole is confirmed on at least two leads in an unresponsive, pulseless patient.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with dark nail polish and acrylic nails. How does that affect the oximeter?
opciones: Both can block the light the device sends through the finger and distort the reading
Both cool the fingertip, and the drop in temperature is what distorts the reading
Only the acrylic nails matter, because polish is transparent to the wavelengths used
Neither matters, because the sensor reads the pulse wave and not the light absorbed
preguntas.explicacion: The device works by shining light through the tissue, so anything that blocks the path interferes: dark polish and artificial nails are the classic examples. Poor circulation, cold skin and tobacco use are also listed. When a polished finger gives nothing, turning the sensor sideways across the nail bed has sometimes worked.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.b · RMA III.B.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: What can a powered goniometer record that a nonpowered one cannot?
opciones: Acceleration and the forces a joint exerts, on top of the range of motion
The angle of the joint, which the mechanical instrument cannot show at all
The length of the two limb segments on either side of the joint measured
The exact moment the joint stops, which a manual one cannot catch
preguntas.explicacion: The nonpowered instrument is mechanical, and all it measures is the range of motion of a joint. The powered version assesses how the joint works by recording that range along with acceleration or the forces the joint puts out. The extra readings are the acceleration and the force, not the angle itself.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Capillary sample, Why the Test is Performed and Risks
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k71 capillary considerations · PBT I.B.1 types of blood, II.I · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii advantages and disadvantages · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: Which laboratory values may a capillary sample falsely elevate?
opciones: Sugar, electrolytes and blood counts
Bilirubin, cholesterol and clotting times
Blood gases, lactate and ammonia
Hormones, drug levels and iron studies
preguntas.explicacion: The drawbacks listed for a capillary sample are results that can read wrong, with sugar, electrolytes and cell counts coming out too high, the small amount of blood available, and cells damaged in the collection that force a repeat from a vein. Its advantages are that it is easy to get, especially in infants, that sites can be rotated, and that it works at home.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth troubleshooting · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls minutes before her video visit to say the picture keeps freezing. Which step is on the troubleshooting list the office hands out beforehand?
opciones: Closing every other application, and if that fails trying a different device
Removing the platform and installing it again so the settings are rebuilt
Carrying the router into the same room and starting the appointment again
Waiting for the clinician to drop the call so the visit can be rebooked
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are easier in their minds when they already know what to do if something goes wrong, so the office gives them the common fixes in advance: restart the computer or the device; check it is charged or plugged in; check the connection is strong enough for the platform; shut every other application; bring the browser up to date; try a different device; and ring the number given for help.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 2.4.2.4 Storage of Electrodes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k149 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: A card of electrodes was left open to the air for weeks. Which problem do they cause?
opciones: A drifting baseline, from unstable electrode contact
Interference from the alternating current in the room
Muscle tremor coming from the arms and the legs
A standardization mark that comes out too short
preguntas.explicacion: The conductive hydrogel loses its performance when a card of electrodes is left open to the air, and a dried electrode is one of the six listed causes of unstable contact and therefore of drift. That is why unused cards are kept in their pouch or in a sealed plastic bag in a cool dry place.

preguntas.subtema: Defective authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A release form comes back to the desk with the line describing the purpose of the disclosure left blank. What is the status of that authorization?
opciones: Defective, because an element required of the form has not been filled in
Defective, unless the patient initials the blank line in front of a witness
Valid, because the purpose may be supplied by the party asking for the records
Valid, because a patient who starts the request need not state a purpose at all
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization is not valid where any required element has been left incomplete, where its expiration has passed, where the entity knows it was revoked, or where material information in it is known to be false. A description of each purpose is one of the core elements; only where the patient initiates the request does asking at her own request suffice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Equipment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 3.1
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k55 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A cannula hub is marked 24G and another 18G. What does the difference in number mean?
opciones: The 24G is the narrower of the two, since higher numbers are finer
The 24G is the wider of the two, since higher numbers are coarser
The numbers give the length in millimeters, not the internal bore
The numbers give the flow rate in milliliters per minute of fluid
preguntas.explicacion: Gauge describes the internal diameter, and a higher gauge number means a narrower device; the sizes commonly stocked run from fourteen through to twenty-four, with the hub color-coded to the gauge. The same convention explains why sixteen to eighteen gauge is reserved for blood donation.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Critical Items
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A tray of instruments will be opened into a wound and will enter sterile tissue. Under the Spaulding scheme, what does that require?
opciones: Sterilization, because any microbe on an item entering sterile tissue can transmit disease
High-level disinfection, the minimum set for items touching mucous membranes or broken skin
Intermediate-level disinfection, the level used for surfaces that briefly touch broken skin
Low-level disinfection, the level listed in the tables for items that touch only intact skin
preguntas.explicacion: Spaulding sorts items by the risk their intended use carries. Anything entering sterile tissue or the vascular system is critical and must be sterile, because any contamination at all could transmit disease. High-level disinfection is the floor for semicritical items; intermediate and low levels belong to items that meet intact or briefly broken skin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Contamination
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and contamination · CPT D3 k57 3B · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: While setting up, a phlebotomist's ungloved finger brushes the top of a blood culture bottle. Why does this matter?
opciones: The sterility of the culture bottle cap must be preserved, or the results are unreliable
The cap is where the bottle's vacuum is stored; touching it lets the vacuum escape early
Skin oils degrade the SPS anticoagulant inside the culture bottle within minutes
It does not matter, because the bottle is mixed 8 to 10 times after filling
preguntas.explicacion: Among the issues of concern in tube collection is contamination before, during or after the collection, with the specific example that the sterility of the cap of blood culture bottles must be ensured and kept from any potential source of contamination, or the results become incorrect and unreliable. Mixing 8 to 10 times combines blood and medium; it does not undo contamination of the cap.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Cells, Tissues and Membranes: Body Tissues
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What fills the spaces between the cells of a tissue and gives that tissue much of its character?
opciones: The intercellular matrix, a nonliving material with salts and fibers
The interstitial fluid, a living material with salts and fibers
The cytoplasm, a nonliving material rich in salts and fibers
The nucleoplasm, a living material rich in salts and fibers
preguntas.explicacion: A tissue is a group of cells of similar structure working as a unit, and between them lies the intercellular matrix, a nonliving material that can be abundant in one tissue and scarce in another. Special substances in it, such as salts and fibers, are what make bone hard and other tissues soft. Cytoplasm and nucleoplasm are inside the cell.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Physical Properties and Shapes; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A school screening letter uses the word scoliosis. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
A part meaning humped plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning an inflammation
A part meaning shape plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
preguntas.explicacion: Scoli- and scolio- mean twisted, and -osis is a condition, usually an abnormal one, so the term names something twisted. Its neighbors in the group of shapes are kypho-, humped, and morph- or morpho-, shape itself. Had the ending been -itis the word would have named an inflammation instead.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 no squeezing · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood flows slowly from a heel puncture and the phlebotomist begins squeezing the heel firmly. What does this do to the specimen?
opciones: It dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid and increases the probability of hemolysis
It concentrates the specimen with red cells and raises the measured hematocrit
It speeds the flow safely, as long as the first drop has already been wiped away
It draws in skin flora, which is why the WHO limits capillary blood to a few tests
preguntas.explicacion: Hard squeezing pushes tissue fluid into the sample and raises the chance of hemolysis; heavy massaging of a finger does the same and slows the flow besides. When blood is slow, the answers are warmth and asking the parent to tighten and release the child's wrist in a rhythm.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · RMA I.D.1.a age-group specific responses · CMA II.F.1.c(7)(a) geriatric
preguntas.pregunta: An 82-year-old woman arrives for a fasting draw. How should the phlebotomist address her?
opciones: By a formal title such as Ms. at first, then ask how she prefers to be addressed
By a friendly word such as dear, which settles an anxious older patient more quickly
By her first name from the start, since informality shortens the social distance
By asking the daughter beside her how her mother prefers to be addressed today
preguntas.explicacion: Older patients are often used to more formal terms of address, so the default is a title and a surname, and the simplest way to get it right is to ask the patient herself. Familiar words like dear read as disrespectful. The wider rule behind it is to speak to an older patient as a fellow adult: an impairment does not reduce an adult's maturity.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Detect Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Verifying a new patient · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient is being registered at the desk. Which identity check does the Red Flags guidance describe for someone opening an account in person?
opciones: Take a name, an address and an identification number, and look at a current government card
Take a name, an address and an identification number, and telephone the number she gave
Take a name, a date of birth and her mother's maiden name, and look at a current card
Take a name, an address and an identification number, and copy the card into the record
preguntas.explicacion: Reasonable procedures for verifying someone opening a new account may include getting a name, an address and an identification number, and, in person, checking a current identification card issued by a government, such as a driving license or a passport. That may then be compared against other sources. Data easily found in a wallet does not authenticate anyone.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities
preguntas.subtema: Reporting to authorities · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: A county health department, acting under state law, asks the office to report a case of a communicable disease. What is required?
opciones: Nothing further, since a public health authority may receive the report without authorization
A signed authorization from the patient, because the diagnosis is sensitive information
A subpoena, because a government agency reaches records only through legal process
A business associate agreement with the department before the report can be transmitted
preguntas.explicacion: Public health activities are one of the twelve national priority purposes. A covered entity may disclose PHI to a public health authority that the law authorizes to receive it in order to prevent or control disease, injury or disability, and to authorities that take reports of child abuse and neglect. The same paragraph also covers warning a person who may have been exposed to a disease that is communicable, where law authorizes it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: How is a temperature of 38.6 °C (101.5 °F) graded on the published grading of fever?
opciones: Moderate-grade fever, the band from 38.1 to 39.0 °C (100.6 to 102.2 °F)
Low-grade fever, which is the band from 37.3 to 38.0 °C (99.1 to 100.4 °F)
High-grade fever, the band from 39.1 to 41.0 °C (102.4 to 105.8 °F)
Hyperthermia, which is any recorded value above 41.0 °C (105.8 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: Fever is graded in bands: low from 37.3 to 38.0 °C, moderate from 38.1 to 39.0 °C, high from 39.1 to 41.0 °C, and above 41.0 °C the term used is hyperthermia. A value of 38.6 °C falls in the middle band. Grading the reading matters because the reporting thresholds a clinic sets are written in those terms.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: On one strip the baseline sits at a different height from one complex to the next; on another, small extra signals ride along the baseline of a shivering patient. What is each?
opciones: The first is baseline drift and the second is muscle tremor
The first is muscle tremor and the second is baseline drift
Both are drift, one from cold skin and one from movement
Both are tremor, one from the arms and one from the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Drift is a baseline that will not hold its level, which is why the quality check measures the vertical distance between neighboring complexes. Tremor is a separate signal thrown off by the arm and leg muscles of a patient who is tense, cold or has a nerve disorder.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation
preguntas.pregunta: How does a pulse oximeter arrive at the saturation it displays?
opciones: It compares how two wavelengths of light are absorbed by the pulsating tissue bed
It measures the electrical resistance of the fingertip as the blood volume changes
It samples a drop of capillary blood held against the sensor inside the clip
It reads the color of the nail bed and matches it against a calibrated chart
preguntas.explicacion: Oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin absorb light differently, at 940 and 660 nanometers, and the device works out saturation from the difference across a pulsating bed. Nothing is sampled from the patient, which is why the test is painless and carries no known risk, and why perfusion at the site matters so much.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why the tube feels warm right after the draw. Compared with a core temperature of 37 °C, what is the normal temperature of blood?
opciones: About 38 °C (100.4 °F), a little above the core
About 37 °C (98.6 °F), the same as the core
About 37.5 °C, half a degree above the core
About 36.5 °C, half a degree below the core
preguntas.explicacion: The normal temperature of blood is about 38 °C (100.4 °F), slightly higher than the 37 °C (98.6 °F) of an internal body reading, and daily swings of 0.5 °C are normal. The extra heat comes from friction as blood flows against vessel walls, especially as vessels age and lose elasticity. Half a degree above or below 37 °C describes the daily variation, not the difference between blood and core temperature.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(1); OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Label Elements
preguntas.subtema: Label elements · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which elements must appear on the label of a shipped container of a hazardous chemical under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: Product identifier, signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, pictograms and supplier contact
Product identifier, CAS number, concentration, flash point, PEL and the date of preparation
Signal word, pictograms, the 16-section SDS summary, lot number, expiration date and PPE symbol
Chemical name, NFPA hazard rating, storage temperature, disposal method, supplier name and phone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 and OSHA's labeling brief list six elements for a container that leaves the workplace: the product identifier, a signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, pictograms, and the supplier's name, address and telephone, be that the manufacturer, the importer or another responsible party. The product identifier has to match section 1 of the SDS. CAS numbers, concentrations, flash points and exposure limits live in the SDS sections on composition, physical properties and exposure controls, not on the label; an HMIS-style PPE symbol may be added only as supplementary information.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Performing the Test
preguntas.subtema: Timing of strip reading · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.1 / IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.3.a · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: While dipping three urine specimens at once, a medical assistant reads all the strips four minutes after the last dip, well past the times printed on the bottle. Which error is this most likely to produce?
opciones: False positives from colors that kept developing after the specified reading time
False negatives on every pad, because all reagent pads fade within the first minute
No error, because reagent strip reactions stop on their own once the pad has dried out
Invalid results only on the pH pad, which is the single time-critical reaction on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Each pad must be read at the interval the manufacturer specifies, using a timer if indicated. Reading after the stated time can produce false positives from over-development of color, false negatives when a reaction fades, or invalid results when the reaction moves beyond the visible area; reading too soon gives invalid or false-negative results because sample and reagent have not finished reacting. Running several tests at once is exactly when timing slips.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: When the order of draw is summarized in four groups (sterile tubes, coagulation tubes, plain or gel tubes, additive tubes), where do the plain and gel tubes fall?
opciones: After the coagulation tubes and before the other additive tubes
Before the coagulation tubes and immediately after the sterile tubes
After all the additive tubes, at the very end of the sequence
Before the blood culture bottles, as the first tubes drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Compressed into four steps, the order runs: blood culture or sterile tubes first, coagulation tubes second, plain tubes and gel tubes third, and tubes with additives last. This matches the WHO table, where red clot activator and serum separator tubes occupy positions 4 and 5, after the light blue tube and ahead of heparin, EDTA, ACD and fluoride.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rhythm
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which leads are inspected when the rhythm is being read?
opciones: Leads I, II, aVF and V1, looking at five separate points
Leads V4, V5 and V6, looking at five separate points
Leads III, aVR and aVL, looking at five separate points
Leads I and aVF alone, looking at five separate points
preguntas.explicacion: Those four leads are the ones read for rhythm, and five things are checked in them: whether regular P waves are there, whether the QRS is narrow or wide, whether the P waves and the complexes go together, whether the spacing is regular, and what shape the P waves have.

preguntas.subtema: Dipstick waived, sediment is PPM · PBT IV.A.1 / VI.F · CMA I.C.10.a.(2)-(3) · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: A physician's office holds only a Certificate of Waiver. Which urinalysis component may NOT be performed there?
opciones: Microscopic examination of the urine sediment
Dipstick determination of protein and glucose
Dipstick determination of nitrite and leukocytes
Reading the specific gravity pad on the reagent strip
preguntas.explicacion: Non-automated dipstick or tablet urinalysis for bilirubin, glucose, hemoglobin, ketone, leukocytes, nitrite, pH, protein, specific gravity and urobilinogen is on the list of tests a Certificate of Waiver covers. Urine sediment examination is a provider-performed microscopy procedure, which is moderate complexity and requires a PPM certificate or higher and a qualifying practitioner.

preguntas.subtema: Expiration of an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: An authorization names the records, the sender and the recipient, but nothing about when it stops. Which core element has been left out?
opciones: An expiration date, or an event that ends the authorization
A statement of the fee the recipient of the records will pay
An estimate of how long the copies will take to be prepared
A list of the staff members allowed to assemble the records
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements are the information described specifically, who may disclose it, who may receive it, the purpose, an expiration date or expiration event tied to the individual or the purpose, and the individual's dated signature. For research, wording such as the end of the study, or none at all, is accepted as the expiration.

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must the warning sign at the entrance to an HIV research laboratory carry?
opciones: The infectious agent, any special entry requirement, and the director's phone
The date of the last decontamination and the brand of disinfectant that was used
The single legend BIOHAZARD, in a color that contrasts with the background
The list of employees trained to enter and the date of their last training
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(ii)(A) sets out three lines for that sign: the name of the infectious agent, any special requirement for entering the area, and a name with a telephone number for whoever is responsible, usually the laboratory director. Subparagraph (B) puts the sign in fluorescent orange-red, or mostly that color, and the lettering and symbols on it in a color that contrasts. The single-word legend belongs to the warning labels of (g)(1)(i), which go on containers, refrigerators and contaminated equipment.

preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 3R k22 · PBT II.I III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Which three problems are named as the major consequences of errors made while a blood sample is being collected?
opciones: Inaccurate labeling, contamination and hemolysis
Hemolysis, clotting and delayed transport to the bench
Contamination, clotting and an expired collection tube
Inaccurate labeling, clotting and an underfilled tube
preguntas.explicacion: A poorly collected sample can give inaccurate and misleading results and cost the patient a repeat test, and the three major issues singled out are inaccurate labeling, contamination and hemolysis. Each of the three is decided at the bedside, before the specimen reaches the analyser.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 6.3 Precautions to Prevent Transmissions of Infections
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: What is done to the examination table between one patient and the next?
opciones: It is covered with clean examination paper for the next patient
It is covered with a clean sheet and a blanket for the next patient
It is wiped down with alcohol and then left open to dry for a while
It is wiped down with a detergent solution after every two patients
preguntas.explicacion: Keeping infection out of the room rests on two habits: the equipment gets a regular clean and disinfection, and the table is covered with fresh examination paper once each patient is done. The wipe with a mild detergent belongs to the start of each session, not to every patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pelvic Inflammatory Disease", History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(8) (2027 I.C.6.g(8)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of risk factors is listed for pelvic inflammatory disease?
opciones: Being under 25, multiple partners, prior sexually transmitted infection
Being over 50, obesity, smoking and a diet of fatty and spicy foods
Being over 65, immobility, low calcium intake and declining estrogen
Being under 2, attending day care and a recent upper respiratory infection
preguntas.explicacion: The risk factors are the ones shared with other sexually transmitted infections: age under 25, several partners, a partner with an infection or symptoms, early first sexual activity, a prior infection, inconsistent barrier use and bacterial vaginosis. Risk also rises in the first three weeks after an intrauterine device is placed, but not after that.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists DVT after a long hospital stay. Which problem does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A clot that has formed in a deep vein
A defect in the vessels of the circulation
A disturbance of the rhythm of the heart
A disease of the arteries outside the heart
preguntas.explicacion: DVT stands for deep-vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot. The abbreviations that sit near it name other circulatory problems: AVM is an arteriovenous malformation, a defect in how the vessels are built; AFIB is atrial fibrillation, a disturbance of the heart's rhythm; and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, of arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 2; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E1 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: During the interview before a draw, a patient mentions having fainted during a previous blood test. What should be done?
opciones: Have the patient lie down for the draw
Draw quickly while the patient stands
Postpone the draw until after a meal
Seat the patient with the head between the knees
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 asks about allergies, phobias and any history of fainting during injections or blood draws, and settles the patient comfortably, lying down where that can be done; patients who faint with blood draws are told to warn the provider and be lying down when the test is done. Head between the knees is a measure for someone who has already fainted and cannot lie flat.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gynecologic Pelvic Examination", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k63 · CMA I.C.5.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which vaginal speculum is the wider of the two in common use and holds itself open once inserted?
opciones: The Graves speculum, generally kept for women who have already given birth
The Pedersen speculum, which is narrower and has to be held during the exam
The pediatric speculum, much shorter and narrower than the adult instruments
The anoscope, which is introduced with an obturator that is then taken out
preguntas.explicacion: Two styles cover most adult examinations. Graves is the wider one and it is self-retaining once in place, which frees a hand; it is generally reserved for parous women. Pedersen is narrower, usually more comfortable, and must be held throughout because it does not stay open on its own. Pediatric specula are a separate, much smaller size.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP), What is it used for?; Why do I need a BMP?
preguntas.subtema: What the BMP reports · CMA I.C.10.c.(2)-(3), (6) · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A basic metabolic panel is drawn on a patient seen for vomiting that has gone on for weeks. Which areas of the body does that panel report on?
opciones: Kidney function, the balance of fluid and electrolytes, the blood glucose, and metabolism
Kidney function, the balance of fluid and electrolytes, the liver enzymes, and blood proteins
Liver function, the clotting factors, the blood glucose, and the body's stores of iron
Kidney function, the thyroid hormones, the blood glucose, and the balance of acid and base
preguntas.explicacion: The eight substances are read together, and between them they answer four questions: how the kidneys are working, whether fluid and the electrolytes are in balance, what the blood sugar is doing, and how the body is making energy out of food. That is why the panel turns up at ordinary checkups, where it can find trouble before there are symptoms, and also in the emergency room and in patients with fatigue, confusion, breathing difficulty or long-running vomiting. Proteins and liver enzymes are what the comprehensive version adds on top; thyroid, clotting and iron are ordered separately.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62
preguntas.pregunta: What separates a manual stethoscope from an electronic one?
opciones: The electronic one amplifies the sound electrically; the other is mechanical
The electronic one is meant for lung sounds and the other for heart sounds
The manual one carries only a bell and the electronic one only a diaphragm
The manual one is used over arteries and veins and the other over the chest
preguntas.explicacion: A manual stethoscope is a mechanical device that carries the sounds of the heart, the arteries, the veins and other internal organs. The electronic one does the same work with electrical amplification. Both are described for the same sounds, so what separates them is the amplification, not the part of the body they are used on.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Enteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k21 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(vi) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a tablet swallowed by mouth often need a larger dose than the same drug given by vein?
opciones: Much of the swallowed dose is broken down in the liver before it reaches circulation
Much of the swallowed dose is broken down by the kidney before it arrives at the liver
Oral drugs are absorbed in the stomach, whose surface is smaller than the intestine's
The stomach destroys the whole dose, so only a coated tablet is ever absorbed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Oral is the most convenient and most used route, and the small intestine is usually where absorption happens; how much crosses the intestinal epithelium sets the bioavailability. The portal system then carries the drug to the liver, where the first-pass effect turns part of the dose into inactive metabolites. Less active drug arrives, so the oral dose has to be bigger than the intravenous one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Mechanism of Action and Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.j
preguntas.pregunta: Which antiseptic has the fastest onset but almost no residual activity, and is a fire risk with electrocautery?
opciones: Isopropyl alcohol swab
Chlorhexidine gluconate
Povidone-iodine scrub
Chloroxylenol solution
preguntas.explicacion: Isopropyl alcohol damages membranes and denatures the proteins microbes need, working best at 60 to 90 percent in water. It is one of the weaker cleansing agents and leaves little residual activity, but it has the fastest onset of the antiseptics, and it is flammable in the setting of electrocautery, which is why it must be dry before any current is used.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(v); OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Biological Hazards, Wear gloves; CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings
preguntas.subtema: Gloves and hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: The CDC warns that putting on gloves does not replace cleaning the hands. Which rule in the OSHA standard says the same thing?
opciones: Hands are washed immediately or as soon as feasible after gloves are removed
Gloves are worn whenever hand contact with blood can reasonably be anticipated
Disposable gloves are replaced as soon as feasible when torn or punctured
Utility gloves may be decontaminated and reused while they remain intact
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's paragraph (d)(2)(v) has hands washed the moment gloves or other PPE come off, or as soon after as is feasible, which is the regulatory form of the CDC's warning. The Hospitals eTool supplies the reasons: gloves can carry small defects, can tear while in use, and hands can pick up contamination as the gloves come off, so gloving never stands in for washing and gloves change between patients. The other three options are OSHA glove rules too, in (d)(3)(ix)(A) and (C), but they govern when gloves go on or get replaced, not hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Body Fluid Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A pleural fluid aspirate is split for cell count, chemistry and culture. How is the portion for microbiological culture transported?
opciones: Promptly, at room temperature, to keep the organisms viable
Promptly, on wet ice, to slow down cellular degeneration
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C until the culture can be set up
Frozen at −20 °C if the culture cannot be set up the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Serous and joint fluids, pericardial, peritoneal, pleural and synovial, are aspirated with aseptic technique into sterile containers. Color, turbidity, viscosity and any clot are noted, and aliquots go out to cell count and differential, to protein and glucose, to culture and to cytology. The culture aliquot travels promptly at room temperature so the organisms stay alive; like CSF for culture it is never chilled, and ice, refrigeration and freezing are instructions written for other specimens.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Chemical Examination: pH; Proteins)
preguntas.subtema: Stale specimen and pH · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen tested six hours after collection, unrefrigerated, reads pH 8.5 with trace protein, although the patient's previous urinalyses were normal. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: Bacteria in the standing urine broke down urea into ammonia, and the alkaline pH can falsely raise the protein pad
The patient has early renal tubular acidosis, which raises the urine pH and lets albumin leak through the glomerulus
The specimen became too concentrated while standing, and concentrated urine lowers the pH while raising the protein
The patient ate a high-protein meal before voiding, which alkalinizes the urine and produces transient proteinuria
preguntas.explicacion: The most common cause of an alkaline urine is a stale specimen: bacteria multiply and break down urea, releasing ammonia and pushing the pH up. An alkaline pH, in turn, is a listed cause of false-positive protein on the strip. Renal tubular acidosis can produce alkaline urine but is not the likely reading for a six-hour-old specimen, and a high-protein diet is associated with acid, not alkaline, urine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Intramuscular Injection", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · RMA III.G.2.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which complication is specific to the site chosen for an intramuscular injection?
opciones: Nerve injury: the sciatic in a gluteal site, the radial in the deltoid
Nerve injury: the sciatic in the deltoid, the radial in a gluteal site
Abscess formation, which happens only when the deltoid is the site used
Glass particles injected, which happens only when a vial is used for the dose
preguntas.explicacion: The nerve at risk depends on where the needle goes: the sciatic nerve with a gluteal injection, the superior gluteal nerve with a dorsogluteal one, the femoral nerve at the vastus lateralis and the radial nerve at the deltoid. The other complications listed are not site specific: persistent pain, muscle fibrosis and contracture, abscess, gangrene, skin slough, periostitis, vascular injury, and glass particles from ampules and vials.

preguntas.subtema: SDS access · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: When must safety data sheets be accessible to laboratory employees under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: During each work shift, while employees are in their work areas
Within 10 working days of a request, through the safety officer
During business hours only, in the administrator's office
At the annual training, when the chemical inventory is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 has the employer keep the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments of hazardous chemicals and keep them readily accessible on every shift to laboratory employees while they are in the areas where they work; the same wording governs sealed-container operations in (b)(4)(ii). Labels on incoming containers stay intact, and the training of paragraph (h) is given. A sheet obtainable only days later, or only in an office during business hours, fails the test.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many vertebrae are in the cervical, thoracic and lumbar regions of the spine?
opciones: Seven cervical, twelve thoracic and five lumbar
Five cervical, twelve thoracic and seven lumbar
Twelve cervical, seven thoracic and five lumbar
Seven cervical, five thoracic and twelve lumbar
preguntas.explicacion: The vertebral column runs seven cervical vertebrae in the neck, twelve thoracic ones that carry the ribs, and five lumbar ones in the small of the back, ending in the sacrum and the coccyx. The count matters when a report places a finding at a numbered level.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes; and StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: The patient's medicine list shows a blood thinner. Which team member does the phlebotomy guidance say to consult?
opciones: The pharmacist, about medicines that might cause complications
The pathologist, who supervises the laboratory that will test it
The phlebotomist, who chooses which tube additive will be used
The ward clerk, who records the medicines on the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Providers have to know the patient's medical history and any pre-existing condition, and where the patient takes blood thinners, or other medicines liable to bring on unwanted complications, the pharmacist is the one consulted. When a case is complex and the veins are hard to find, it is a certified phlebotomist who gets called; the pathologist supervises the laboratory itself.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4
