preguntas.subtema: Signature log · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Records submitted for review carry initials nobody can identify. Which document is meant to resolve that?
opciones: A signature log matching the printed name of the author to the initials used
An amendment adding the missing names to each of the disputed chart entries
A business associate agreement with the company that scanned the paper charts
An accounting of disclosures listing everyone who has opened the record so far
preguntas.explicacion: A signature log lists the typed or printed name of an author alongside the initials or the illegible signature used in the documentation. It may sit on the page itself or stand as a separate document. Reviewers are told to consider every log submitted regardless of when it was created, and may not deny a claim just because the log leaves out credentials, although listing them is encouraged.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports a critical glucose value three hours after it was measured because the result sat unreviewed. In which phase of the total testing process did this error occur?
opciones: Post-analytical, which includes failure or delay in reporting critical values
Analytical, which includes undetected failure of the quality control system
Pre-analytical, which includes sorting, routing and labeling of specimens
Post-post-analytical, which includes the clinician's delayed reaction to the report
preguntas.explicacion: The post-analytical phase, 13 to 20 % of errors, covers wrong validation of data, failure in reporting or addressing the report, excessive turnaround time, transcription mistakes and failure or delay in reporting critical values, which is exactly a result left unreviewed for three hours. The clinician's own delayed reaction to a report that did arrive would be post-post-analytical.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a Schiøtz tonometer arrive at the pressure inside the eye?
opciones: It puts a known force on the globe and measures the indentation
It flattens the cornea with a small disc and reads the force used
It sends a thin beam through a diaphragm and reads the chamber
It changes lenses of several powers until the retina comes clear
preguntas.explicacion: The Schiøtz type indents: a known force is put on the globe and the amount of indentation gives the reading. Flattening the cornea with a small flat disc is applanation, the other method named in the same device definition. The narrow beam belongs to the slit lamp and the set of lenses to the manual refractor.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient moves to a skilled nursing facility and stays thirty days. What does Part A leave her to pay in 2026?
opciones: Nothing for the first twenty days, then $217 for each of the ten that follow
No charge for the first sixty days, then $434 for each of the ten that follow
A charge of $217 for every one of the thirty days, counting from admission
The whole cost herself, because a skilled nursing stay sits outside Part A
preguntas.explicacion: A skilled nursing facility stay costs the patient nothing for days one to twenty, then $217 a day from day twenty-one to day one hundred, and the whole cost from day one hundred and one onwards. Part A helps pay for inpatient care in hospitals and in critical access hospitals, for skilled nursing facilities, and it also covers hospice and some home health care.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Competency Assessment · RMA III.C.1.a.vi level of competency
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the procedures CLIA lists for evaluating the competency of testing personnel?
opciones: Watching instrument maintenance and the function checks being carried out
Verification of the test procedures and of the system's performance characteristics
Selection of a test methodology appropriate for the clinical use of the results
Setting out which levels of analytic performance count as acceptable
preguntas.explicacion: The competency list has six items: watching routine patient testing, monitoring how results are recorded and reported, reviewing worksheets and quality control and maintenance records, watching maintenance and function checks, retesting known or blind samples, and probing problem-solving skills. The other three choices are duties of the technical consultant, not ways of measuring an employee.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k127 k138 · NCMA 2C.5 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Insufficient volume was the second most common reason for rejection in the emergency laboratory. Which measure did the laboratory adopt for pediatric, geriatric, oncology and neonatal ICU patients?
opciones: Preferring microtainers and microtubes, together with analyzers that need minimal specimen and dead volume
Drawing a second full set of tubes from every such patient so that one set can serve as a backup
Accepting any fill level from these units and adding a comment on the ratio to the report
Pooling the blood from two partially filled tubes of the same patient before centrifugation
preguntas.explicacion: Because collecting enough blood from newborns, children, oncology and intensive care patients is difficult, and because frequent draws put children at risk of anemia, the laboratory prefers microtainers and microtubes for those groups and uses automated instruments with minimized specimen and dead volume. Short fills still fail the ratio criterion, extra sets increase the blood taken, and pooling tubes is not an option offered.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 technique · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: During a heel-prick the phlebotomist presses the lancet device hard against the skin to be sure it fires. What is the problem with this?
opciones: Too much compression can produce a deeper puncture than is needed for good flow
Too much compression makes the puncture shallower, so a second stick is usually needed
Pressing hard is required, because a lancet held loosely will not reach 2.4 mm
Pressing hard is acceptable on the heel but not on the finger, where bone is closer
preguntas.explicacion: Leaning hard on the device is avoided: it drives the tip in further than the flow requires. Skin flattens under pressure, so the wound ends up a little deeper than the lancet is long, and that is exactly why the length chosen is a little under the depth wanted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Interfering Factors; Clinical Significance; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Hematocrit (003646), What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Physiologic hematocrit changes · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D3 k141 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these patient situations is associated with a higher hematocrit rather than a lower one?
opciones: Living permanently at high altitude
Being in the later months of pregnancy
Retaining too much water in the body
Having chronic kidney disease for years
preguntas.explicacion: Lasting hypoxia at altitude drives the red cell count up, so people who live high have a higher hematocrit; smokers and patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease run high for the same reason. Pregnancy lowers it by dilution, and too much water in the body and chronic kidney disease are both listed causes of a low hematocrit. Newborns start high, and adult men sit above women.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Nonmaleficence
preguntas.subtema: Nonmaleficence and competence · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7C · CMA II.E.7 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declines to attempt an arterial puncture she has not been trained to perform. Which ethical principle does this reflect?
opciones: Nonmaleficence: avoiding a risky procedure outside one's competence
Beneficence: bringing goodness by attempting any procedure the patient needs
Justice: giving each patient the same procedures regardless of skill
Autonomy: the phlebotomist's right to choose which tasks to do
preguntas.explicacion: Nonmaleficence means not bringing harm, and the Hippocratic tradition lists attempting a risky procedure outside the practitioner's competence among the things to avoid, together with violating privacy. Staying within one's training is therefore an ethical duty as well as a scope-of-practice rule. Beneficence would be misread if it meant attempting anything a patient needs regardless of skill; justice concerns fair distribution of resources; and autonomy in medical ethics refers to the patient's self-determination, not the worker's preferences.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Periods of Disease
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is exposed to a pathogen but feels nothing for several days. Which period of disease is that, and what is happening?
opciones: The incubation period, while the pathogen multiplies below the level that causes signs
The prodromal period, while the pathogen multiplies below the level that causes signs
The period of decline, while the pathogen multiplies below the level that causes signs
The convalescent period, while the pathogen multiplies above the level that causes signs
preguntas.explicacion: Disease runs through five periods, from incubation and the prodromal stage into the illness itself, then the decline and finally convalescence. During incubation the pathogen is already multiplying but has not reached the numbers needed to produce signs and symptoms, so the patient has no idea anything has begun. General complaints such as fever and aching mark the prodromal period that follows.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(iv) and (d)(2)(v), Methods of Compliance
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene · CPT D1 k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, when must an employee wash their hands after removing gloves?
opciones: Immediately, or as soon as feasible, after the gloves come off
Only when blood or OPIM reached the skin beneath the gloves
At the end of the work shift, as with contaminated work surfaces
Not at all, if an antiseptic hand cleanser was used instead of soap
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(v) puts the duty on the employer: employees wash their hands right away, or as soon as it is feasible, once gloves or any other protective equipment come off. The rule does not wait for blood to reach the skin; that is a separate trigger in (d)(2)(vi). End of shift is the timing the standard gives for possibly contaminated surfaces, not for hands. And paragraph (d)(2)(iv) allows antiseptic cleansers or towelettes only where handwashing facilities are not feasible, adding that hands must still reach soap and running water as soon as that becomes feasible afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7; and Annex E, Disassembly of needle from syringe
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: The last tube has been filled from the syringe. What does the guidance forbid at that point?
opciones: Recapping the needle and taking it off the syringe by hand
Placing the syringe and needle together into the sharps bin
Inverting the additive tubes before they leave the bedside
Checking the labels against the request form a second time
preguntas.explicacion: The step that covers filling tubes ends with an instruction not to recap and remove the needle. If a used needle really has to come off a syringe it is re-sheathed with a one-hand scoop and taken off with a removal device, never with bare hands, and discarded at once.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conjunctivitis", History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a red eye with thick discharge that keeps coming back after it is wiped away and sticks to the lashes. Which cause does that discharge suggest?
opciones: Bacterial conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Viral conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Allergic conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Toxin-induced conjunctivitis, which gives purulent discharge and no redness
preguntas.explicacion: The type of discharge is the most useful clue. Bacterial conjunctivitis produces purulent discharge that reforms after it is removed, or thicker mucopurulent discharge that clings to the lashes. Watery discharge is what the viral and the allergic kinds give, and a swollen node in front of the ear points to the viral one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the arm is the preferred site for a limb electrode, and why?
opciones: The inside of the lower arm, where the skin is thinner
The outside of the upper arm, where the skin is thinner
The inside of the upper arm, where the muscle is thicker
The back of the forearm, where there is the least hair
preguntas.explicacion: The inner surface of the lower arm is chosen because the skin there is thinner, which gives a better signal. The tab of the electrode points up toward the arm, and the clip connector is attached to the tab once the electrode is pressed down.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cardiac Cycle", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What makes the first heart sound?
opciones: The mitral and tricuspid valves closing as systole begins
The aortic and pulmonic valves closing as systole begins
The mitral and tricuspid valves opening as diastole begins
The aortic and pulmonic valves opening as diastole begins
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure in the ventricle passes that of the atrium, the mitral valve shuts together with the tricuspid, and that closure both marks the start of systole and produces the first sound. The second comes at the other end, when the aortic and pulmonic valves close.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Interfering Factors (Preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: Boric acid and strips · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 preservatives · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory receives a urine in a boric acid tube and is asked to run both a culture and a reagent strip on it. What is the concern with the strip?
opciones: Boric acid can produce false-negative strip results for protein, leukocytes and ketones, and it alters the pH
Boric acid can produce false-positive strip results for leukocyte esterase, glucose and urobilinogen
Boric acid dissolves pus cells, so the leukocyte pad reads falsely high while the culture stays valid
Boric acid raises the pH above 7, which produces a false-positive protein reaction on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the usual preservative for culture: it keeps the pH below 7 and prevents pus cells from dissolving, but it interferes with several strip pads and is linked to false-negative protein, leukocyte and ketone readings, which limits combining strip testing and culture in one tube. False-positive leukocyte esterase, glucose and urobilinogen are the effects of formaldehyde, and an alkaline pH is what boric acid prevents.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are described as more likely to have a vasovagal faint during a venous procedure?
opciones: Those seated rather than lying, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those lying rather than seated, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those seated rather than lying, when more than three tubes are drawn
Those lying rather than seated, when the needle is larger than 21 gauge
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting of this kind is reported more often in people who are sitting up than in those lying down, and in people who have fainted before or who are markedly anxious about blood or needles. Those are exactly the patients who are asked about earlier faints and offered a lying position.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Excluded Services
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A treatment appears on the plan's list of excluded services. What does the patient need to be told?
opciones: The plan does not pay for it or cover it at all
The plan pays for it once the deductible is met
The plan pays for it outside its own network only
The plan pays for it if it is preauthorized first
preguntas.explicacion: Excluded services are the health care services a plan does not pay for or cover, so no amount of cost sharing or paperwork turns them into a covered benefit. Meeting a deductible, going out of network or obtaining a preauthorization all belong to services the plan does cover, which is what makes those answers tempting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.D.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant's forearm brushes the edge of the sink partway through the scrub. What is required?
opciones: Wash that area for an extra minute before going on with the rest of the scrub
Start the whole scrub again from the nail cleaner, since the count has been broken
Carry on, because the sink is scrubbed between cases and counts as a clean surface
Rinse that arm at once and then resume, since rinsing removes what the sink deposited
preguntas.explicacion: Touching an already-scrubbed area, or bumping the sink, means washing that area for an extra minute and continuing. The rule hardens once the scrub is finished: from then on touching any nonsterile surface means scrubbing again from the start. Rinsing is not begun until both hands and arms are done.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Cane Basics
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who had surgery on the right knee is being taught to use a cane. In which hand does it go?
opciones: The left hand, opposite the leg that is weaker or was operated on
The right hand, on the same side as the leg that was operated on
Either hand, as long as the tip lands ahead of the stronger leg
The right hand, changing to the left once the knee bears weight
preguntas.explicacion: The cane is held on the side away from the weak leg. Cane and weak leg then swing forward together and land level with each other, some of the load shifts onto the cane, and the strong leg steps past. Turning is done by pivoting on the strong leg. The tip, or all four prongs, must be flat on the floor before any weight goes onto the cane.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heat emergencies", Symptoms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Which change tells you a patient with heat illness has reached heat stroke?
opciones: A temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) with confusion, and sweating may stop
A temperature above 100 °F (38 °C) with heavy sweating and severe thirst
A temperature below 95 °F (35 °C) with shivering and cool moist skin
A temperature above 102 °F (38.9 °C) with cramps in both of the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Heat stroke is the point where the body can no longer control its temperature and the temperature keeps climbing: fever above 104 °F (40 °C), confusion, irrational behavior, slurred speech, seizures or unconsciousness, and sweating may stop. Death, organ failure, damage to the brain and shock can follow, so the emergency number is called at once.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Developmental Stages of Social Emotional Development in Children", 6 to 12 Months of Age
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: At what age does stranger anxiety typically appear?
opciones: Between 6 and 12 months of age
Between 2 and 4 months of age
Between 18 and 30 months of age
Between 3 and 5 years of age
preguntas.explicacion: Between 6 and 12 months an effective attachment forms with a responsive caregiver, and stranger anxiety emerges as the infant starts telling the familiar from the unfamiliar; distress at separation belongs here too. Recognizing the primary caregiver by sight comes earlier, at around 5 months.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Classifications of Disease
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops an infection at a surgical site after an operation. Which two labels describe that disease?
opciones: Iatrogenic, caught because of a medical procedure, and nosocomial
Zoonotic, transferred from an animal to a human, and noncommunicable
Congenital, present at or before birth, and degenerative in its course
Idiopathic, of unknown cause, and inherited from parent to offspring
preguntas.explicacion: An iatrogenic disease is one the medical procedure itself brings on: a wound treatment, a catheterization, surgery whose site becomes contaminated. Diseases picked up in a hospital are called nosocomial, and the two labels often describe the same event. A zoonosis, by contrast, passes from an animal to a person.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Topical and Transdermal Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(4) · RMA III.G.4.d(iii)
preguntas.pregunta: A new transdermal patch is being applied. Which sequence is correct?
opciones: Remove the old patch, clean and dry the skin, then press the new one 10 seconds
Apply the new patch beside the old one, and remove the old one the following day
Clean the skin with alcohol, apply the patch, and rub the medication surface in
Warm the skin first, apply the patch, and cover it with an occlusive dressing
preguntas.explicacion: Gloves are worn and the rights are checked as for any medication. The previous patch comes off first, the skin around it is assessed for irritation, and the site is cleansed and dried. The clear plastic backing is removed without touching the medication surface, the patch goes on an area the manufacturer allows, such as the upper arms or chest, and it is pressed firmly for ten seconds. Broken or irritated skin is avoided.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 1. Comprehensive Care
preguntas.subtema: Team-based care roles · CCMA 4G k167 · CMA II.F.4.c / 2027 II.F.2.c · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which group of workers does the medical home model name as part of the care team?
opciones: Advanced practice nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists and social workers
Only the physician and the nurse, with other disciplines seen on referral
Hospital case managers and payer staff, who direct the practice's decisions
The hospice nurse, the chaplain and the medical director of the agency
preguntas.explicacion: Comprehensive care takes a team, and the model names its members: physicians and nurses, nutritionists, physician assistants, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses, educators, care coordinators and social workers. Smaller practices may build virtual teams instead, linking themselves, and their patients, to the providers and services their own communities hold.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls asking for a refill on a Schedule II prescription. What does federal regulation allow?
opciones: No refill at all; the prescriber may write several prescriptions for a 90-day supply
Up to five refills within six months, counted from the date the prescription was issued
One refill only, if the pharmacist records the date and quantity on the back of it
Refills with no set limit, as long as the prescription is less than six months old
preguntas.explicacion: A Schedule II prescription cannot be refilled at all. What the practitioner may do instead is write several prescriptions on the same occasion that together let the patient receive up to a 90-day supply, each of them issued for a legitimate medical reason within the ordinary practice of medicine. Five refills inside six months is the Schedule III and IV rule, and it does not reach Schedule II.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 5.2 Review, Observations, and Replication
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: A strip was cut short and carries only two complete complexes in each lead group. Why does it fail the quality check?
opciones: Four standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Ten standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Six standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Two standard complexes have to appear in every lead
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptance list is short and mechanical: the complexes clearly drawn with the P wave in plain view, the P wave and the QRS upright in lead I, a baseline that does not wander past 5 mm, and four standard complexes on the tracing. A short strip fails on the last one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 18. Storage of Sterile Items
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.D.2.n
preguntas.pregunta: What information does the guideline require on the label of a sterilized item?
opciones: A load number naming the sterilizer, the cycle or load, the date, and any expiration date
The initials of the person who wrapped it, the cycle length, and the chamber temperature
The names of the instruments inside, the wrap material used, and the date of the last service
The department it belongs to, the number of previous cycles, and the shelf it is stored on
preguntas.explicacion: Labeling exists so a pack can be traced back to its run. The label carries a load number identifying which sterilizer was used, the cycle or load number, the date it was processed and, where it applies, an expiration date. That is what makes a recall possible when a spore test later comes back positive.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why one lab result is labeled hyperglycemia and another hypoglycemia. Which pair of prefixes explains the difference?
opciones: Hyper- means above or excessive; hypo- means under or deficient
Hyper- means quick or rapid; hypo- means slow or delayed
Hyper- means large or long; hypo- means small or short
Hyper- means outer or outside; hypo- means within or inner
preguntas.explicacion: These two prefixes sit in the group of numbers and amounts: hyper- is above, beyond or excessive, and hypo- is under or deficient. Attached to the root for sugar and the ending -emia, a blood condition, they name too much and too little glucose in the blood. Fast and slow are tachy- and brady-; large and small are macro- and micro-.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: The morning reading shows the sample refrigerator drifted above its acceptable range some time overnight. What is the required sequence?
opciones: Stop testing, ask the person who supervises testing, and document what was done
Move the samples to a second refrigerator and carry on with the day's testing
Repeat the reading in an hour and act only if it is still out of range
Discard every reagent in the unit and record the loss in the maintenance log
preguntas.explicacion: If the temperature strays outside the recommended range for any length of time, testing stops and whoever directs or supervises it is contacted for guidance on what comes next, including whether the affected reagents, kits, controls or samples have to be thrown out and when testing may start again. Every corrective action taken is documented.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP), What is a basic metabolic panel?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · PBT II.G · RMA III.C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition reads 'chem 7'. Which test goes by that name?
opciones: The basic metabolic panel
The comprehensive metabolic panel
The complete blood count
The hemoglobin A1C test
preguntas.explicacion: The basic metabolic panel also goes by BMP, chemistry panel, chemistry screen, electrolyte panel and chem 7; it measures eight substances, including glucose, four electrolytes, BUN and creatinine. The CMP is the fourteen-test version with liver enzymes, the CBC counts blood cells, and the A1C is also called glycated or glycosylated hemoglobin.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging, X-Rays
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a suspected wrist fracture is sent for the least expensive study that shows bone well. Which one is it, and why does it work?
opciones: A plain X-ray, because hard tissue blocks the beam and shows up light
A plain X-ray, because hard tissue absorbs no beam and shows up dark
An ultrasound, because sound waves pass easily through cortical bone
A PET scan, because the tracer collects in the mineral part of bone
preguntas.explicacion: X-rays are only slightly slowed by soft tissue, which comes out gray, while bone and teeth block most of the beam and leave a light shadow on the plate. That contrast is why the X-ray is still the workhorse for fractures and for dentistry. Ultrasound cannot get through bone or gas at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which Korotkoff phases mark the systolic and the diastolic pressures?
opciones: Phase I marks the systolic and phase V, when all sound goes, marks the diastolic
Phase I marks the systolic and phase IV, the abrupt muffling, marks the diastolic
Phase II marks the systolic and phase V, when all sound goes, marks the diastolic
Phase III marks the systolic and phase IV, the abrupt muffling, marks the diastolic
preguntas.explicacion: Phase I is the clear tapping heard for at least two beats in a row, and that is the systolic pressure. Phase IV is the sudden muffling into a soft blowing sound, and phase V is silence, which is the diastolic. Phases II and III, the swishing and the return of sharper sounds, have no known clinical meaning.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Acknowledgment of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient takes the notice of privacy practices and politely declines to sign the acknowledgment. What must the front desk do?
opciones: Record what was tried in order to get the acknowledgment, and why it failed
Record the refusal and hold the appointment until a signed acknowledgment is on file
Record the refusal and post a second copy of the notice by certified mail within 60 days
Record the refusal and count the notice as acknowledged once the visit is documented
preguntas.explicacion: A direct treatment provider hands the notice over no later than the date of first service and, emergencies aside, tries in good faith to get a written acknowledgment that it was received. Where no acknowledgment can be had, the file records what was attempted and why it came to nothing. The notice also goes to anybody who asks for it.

preguntas.subtema: Record confidentiality · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Besides limiting who may receive information from a chart, what else must a hospital's confidentiality procedure prevent?
opciones: Unauthorized people gaining access to the records or altering what is in them
Authorized staff consulting a record outside the hours the department is open
Clinicians correcting an entry that they themselves made earlier in the same day
Copies leaving the department without the medical record service's own stamp
preguntas.explicacion: The condition asks for a procedure that keeps the records confidential in two directions: information and copies go only to authorized individuals, and unauthorized individuals must not be able to reach the records or change what they contain. Originals leave the hospital only under federal or state law, a court order or a subpoena.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Termination and the critically ill · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient already served with a termination notice is admitted in a critical condition the week the notice period runs out. What does the practice owe her?
opciones: To hold the termination until she is medically stable again
To end care on the date in the letter and refer the hospital to it
To hold the termination until she signs a fresh consent to treat
To end care on the date in the letter unless she asks for more time
preguntas.explicacion: Staying clear of an abandonment claim means giving notice that is adequate and a fair chance to line up another clinician. Where there is an emergency, or the patient is critically ill, termination has to wait until she is medically stable again. Courts have held that the duty to go on treating someone at a critical stage of illness applies whatever her ability to pay.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these findings is an underlying cause of petechiae?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia
Hemoconcentration
Hypoglycemia
Venous fibrosis
preguntas.explicacion: Petechiae have four primary causes: too few platelets, platelets that work badly, coagulation disorders and a loss of vascular integrity. Hemoconcentration is the tourniquet artifact in the phlebotomy chapter, hypoglycemia is a mimic of syncope, and venous fibrosis is a local contraindication to puncture; none is listed as a cause of petechial bleeding.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.4 Postexamination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k150 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How are the wax pencil marks taken off the chest once the recording is over?
opciones: With gauze and baby oil, after the electrodes are removed
With gauze and alcohol, after the electrodes are removed
With soap and warm water, before the patient gets dressed
They are left in place for the next recording on that patient
preguntas.explicacion: After the tracings are taken from the machine and labeled and the electrodes are peeled off, the cosmetic pencil marks are wiped away with gauze and baby oil, and the patient puts the gown back on. Alcohol has a different job: cleaning the sites beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Hemoglobin (003645), Normal Results; What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Hemoglobin by age · CPT D5 5G · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D3 k141 · CMA I.C.10.b.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.i / 4.d
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's point-of-care hemoglobin reads 19 g/dL. A new assistant wants to flag it as dangerously high. How should the result be interpreted?
opciones: It is within the newborn reference range of about 14 to 24 g/dL and is not abnormal for this age
It exceeds the adult male upper limit of 17.2 g/dL and should be reported to the provider as critical
It is above the infant range of 9.5 to 14 g/dL, so the sample was probably too concentrated
It is high for any age and suggests chronic low oxygen, which is the usual cause of a raised hemoglobin
preguntas.explicacion: Reference values depend on age: adult men run about 13.8 to 17.2 g/dL and women 12.1 to 15.1, but newborns normally measure 14 to 24 g/dL, and infants 9.5 to 14. A value of 19 g/dL in a newborn is therefore expected, not critical. Chronic hypoxia is the most common cause of a truly high hemoglobin in other patients, and laboratories' ranges vary slightly, so the age-specific range is what should be checked.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone) Test, What is a TSH test?; What do the results mean?
preguntas.subtema: Interpreting TSH · CMA I.C.10.c.(7) · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's TSH result is well above the reference range. What does this most likely indicate about the thyroid?
opciones: The thyroid is probably underactive, so the pituitary is releasing more TSH to drive it
The thyroid is probably overactive, so the pituitary is releasing more TSH to match it
The pituitary has stopped responding to thyroid hormone, and thyroid output is unknown
Graves' disease is confirmed, since it is the most common cause of an abnormal TSH result
preguntas.explicacion: TSH is made by the pituitary gland to tell the thyroid how much hormone to produce. When thyroid hormone in the blood is too low, the pituitary makes more TSH to push the thyroid to work harder, so a high TSH points to hypothyroidism; when thyroid hormone is too high, the pituitary makes little or no TSH. The test cannot say what is causing the problem, so abnormal results lead to T4, T3 or thyroid antibody tests; Graves' disease is the usual cause of hyperthyroidism, not of a high TSH.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Foreign Body Removal", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k63
preguntas.pregunta: A child has a bead lodged in the ear canal. Which approach succeeds on the first attempt most often?
opciones: Taking hold of it with forceps, which works about four times in five
Flushing it out with saline irrigation, which works about two in three
Sticking it to a cotton-tipped applicator with tissue adhesive
Hooking it out with a Katz extractor passed beyond the object
preguntas.explicacion: Forceps of one kind or another, straight or mosquito or bayonet or alligator, are the instrument reached for most often and had the highest first-pass success at 78.3 %. Saline irrigation came next at 65.2 %. Tissue adhesive on a cotton-tipped applicator reached 19.1 % and the Katz extractor 16.5 %.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Treatment / Management: Epinephrine
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 k82 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: By which route and at which site is epinephrine given for anaphylaxis?
opciones: Intramuscularly, into the outer middle part of either thigh
Subcutaneously, into the fatty layer over the back of the arm
Intramuscularly, into the deltoid muscle of the dominant arm
Intravenously, at the concentration used for an intramuscular dose
preguntas.explicacion: Epinephrine goes into muscle, and the thigh is preferred over the deltoid. Intramuscular delivery works faster and gives better outcomes than the subcutaneous or the intravascular route. The intravenous route uses a different, more dilute concentration and carries a much higher risk of cardiovascular complications.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Valve Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which heart valve has two cusps, and where is it located?
opciones: The mitral valve, between the left atrium and left ventricle
The tricuspid valve, between the right atrium and right ventricle
The aortic semilunar valve, at the base of the ascending aorta
The pulmonary semilunar valve, at the base of the pulmonary trunk
preguntas.explicacion: The mitral valve, also called bicuspid or left atrioventricular, has two cusps that chordae tendineae tie to a pair of papillary muscles, and it guards the doorway from the left atrium into the left ventricle; in the clinic it is called mitral. The tricuspid carries three flaps, and the pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves have three flaps each and no chordae tendineae.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is preparing the skin. For which collection does the thirty-second alcohol swab instruction not apply?
opciones: A blood culture set
A coagulation panel
A fasting glucose
A cross-match sample
preguntas.explicacion: The alcohol swab for thirty seconds with thirty seconds of drying is written for routine draws, and the exception named is a blood culture, which is prepared differently. Alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine for the routine case, because iodine can raise potassium, phosphorus and urate.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Benefits of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Effect on demand · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Physicians at a practice fear that offering same-day appointments will bring a flood of extra visits. What does the reported experience suggest?
opciones: Demand tends to fall, mostly because patients more often get to see their own clinician
Demand tends to rise sharply, which is why a contingency plan is needed from the first day
Demand stays flat, but the visits shift out of the afternoon and into the morning session
Demand tends to fall, mostly because patients settle more of their problems by telephone
preguntas.explicacion: Against what many physicians anticipate, the demand for appointments goes down, and the reason given is that patients more often manage to see their own clinician. Seeing one's personal physician strengthens continuity of care, which goes with better care and higher satisfaction. Practices also report savings, because fewer no-shows free clinical and staff time.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), Sharps injury log; govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(5)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps injury log · CPT D1 k12 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, asks the log for three things at minimum: which device was involved, by type and brand; where it happened, meaning the department or the work area; and an explanation of how the incident came about, all of it written so that the injured employee's confidentiality holds. Names, source status and prophylaxis live in the confidential medical record; training details in the training record; and the route of exposure and the written opinion in the post-exposure evaluation file.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the median cubital vein the most common choice for a blood draw?
opciones: Its thick walls tolerate the negative pressure of the draw
It is the only vein in the fossa that lacks an accompanying nerve
It is the site of choice when an intravenous line has to be started
It is the most prominent vein without any tourniquet applied
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is superficial, sits over the bicipital aponeurosis and is the usual choice because its thick walls can withstand the negative pressures used when drawing blood. The dorsum of the hand, not this vein, is described as the preferred site for an IV; and the chapter does not claim the vein is nerve-free or always visible without a tourniquet.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Actions for Unexpected QC Results; Figure 1
preguntas.subtema: Control out of range · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 / IV.B.3 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.3.d · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: The glucometer's liquid control reads outside the range printed on the bottle. Three patients are waiting. What should the operator do?
opciones: Hold patient results, look for the cause, correct it, repeat the control, then retest the patients
Test the patients now and note on each result that the control was out of range that morning
Repeat the control once; if it is still out, average the two readings and proceed if within range
Switch to a new bottle of control solution and report the patients if the second control passes
preguntas.explicacion: An unexpected control result, internal or external, stops patient reporting until the problem is found and fixed. The checklist: were the instructions followed, are the reagents, kits or controls outdated, were they stored correctly, could caps have been switched and cross-contaminated the vials, and what do the insert's troubleshooting steps say. Only after acceptable repeat QC are patient samples retested and final results reported.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.3.e · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: The morning temperature log for the specimen refrigerator reads 10 °C (50 °F). Why does this reading call for action?
opciones: A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F), so 10 °C is above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 15 and 30 °C (59 to 86 °F), so 10 °C is below range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), so 10 °C is far above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 0 and 4 °C (32 to 39 °F), so 10 °C is above range
preguntas.explicacion: Patient samples are normally refrigerated between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F); the 15 to 30 °C band is room temperature for testing and storage, and −25 to −15 °C is the usual sample freezer. What fixes the acceptable range for any given unit is the manufacturer's instructions for the reagents, kits, controls and samples inside it, and the temperature is read and logged every day even where an alarm or a data logger is fitted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is wrapping up a long intake interview. Which technique both shows active listening and can close it?
opciones: Summarizing what was said, in the interviewer's own words
Reflecting the patient's words back, at times word for word
Offering social pleasantries that put the patient at ease
Providing the rationale for why the information is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Summarizing pulls together what the patient said in the interviewer's own words. It demonstrates active listening, builds a shared understanding, and occasionally serves to complete the interview. Social pleasantries belong at the start, and reflecting repeats a single statement rather than gathering several.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Proper Donning
preguntas.subtema: Donning sequence · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: In what order does the CDC-recommended sequence put on personal protective equipment?
opciones: Gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection, then gloves
Gloves, then gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection
Mask or respirator, then gloves, then gown, then eye protection
Eye protection, then mask or respirator, then gown, then gloves
preguntas.explicacion: The donning order is gown first, covering neck to knees and wrapping the back; then the mask or respirator, with the nose band fitted and a fit check for respirators; then goggles or a face shield; and gloves last, pulled over the cuffs of the gown. Donning takes place outside the patient room. Gloves go on last so that they are the cleanest item when patient contact begins and so that they cover the gown cuffs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on a strong opioid is breathing 9 times a minute. Which term and which mechanism fit?
opciones: Bradypnea, which sedatives and opioids cause by depressing the drive to breathe
Bradypnea, which opioids cause by stiffening the chest wall against expansion
Hypoventilation, which in this patient comes from weakness of the breathing muscles
Apnea, which is the term for any rate under 12 breaths per minute in an adult
preguntas.explicacion: Fewer than 12 breaths a minute in an adult is bradypnea, and the usual company it keeps is sedative or opioid use, alcohol intoxication, hypothyroidism and traumatic brain injury. Neuromuscular disease causes hypoventilation through muscle weakness, and apnea means breathing has stopped, not that it has slowed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth instructions · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: How does the telehealth guidance want the setup steps delivered to a patient who has never used the platform?
opciones: As written step-by-step instructions, or as direct personal support from staff
As a single reminder message sent on the morning the appointment is due to start
As a printed leaflet given to her at the next office visit she attends in person
As a spoken summary during the opening minutes of the video appointment itself
preguntas.explicacion: Skills and comfort vary from patient to patient, and so do their computers, their software versions and their bandwidth, so what needs reviewing is never the same twice. What the guidance asks for is a written set of instructions covering every step of the process from beginning to end, plus a tip: have a coordinator, a nurse, an administrative staff member or a community health worker take the patient through it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Related terms ("CLIA-exempt"); CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): exempt states
preguntas.subtema: CLIA-exempt is a laboratory · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does the term "CLIA-exempt" formally refer to?
opciones: A laboratory in a state whose licensure program CMS has found equal to or stricter than CLIA
A test system so simple that CLIA does not regulate the site that performs it
A test cleared by the FDA as substantially equivalent to one already on the market
A waived test that a Certificate of Waiver site may run without any inspection
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA-exempt describes a laboratory, never a test. It is a laboratory licensed or approved by a state whose laboratory laws CMS has judged equal to or more stringent than CLIA, with a CMS-approved licensure program; Washington and New York are the two states with approved programs. The substantially-equivalent wording is the definition of FDA-cleared, and simple low-risk tests are waived tests.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, 3.1 Diversity Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Culturally responsive care · CCMA 6A k193 · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What does holistic care take into account?
opciones: Needs of body and mind, and spiritual, cultural and social ones
Physical findings plus the current medication list
Insurance coverage plus the billing code for the visit
Provider orders plus the written policies of the office
preguntas.explicacion: Holism means treating the whole person: care is holistic when the patient's needs of body and mind, and the spiritual, cultural and social ones, are all folded in. Developing cultural competence with an attitude of cultural humility is described as the route to providing that kind of care.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Which minimum exposure is recognized for wrapped supplies in a gravity displacement steam sterilizer?
opciones: 30 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
45 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
15 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
60 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: Steam works at two temperatures, 121 °C, which is 250 °F, and 132 °C, which is 270 °F, and the recognized minimums for wrapped supplies are 30 minutes at the lower one in a gravity displacement machine and 4 minutes at the higher one in a prevacuum machine. Forty-five minutes at 121 °C is the figure for decontaminating microbiological waste, where trapped air slows the steam.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with heavy bleeding from a leg wound turns pale, cool and clammy and cannot answer questions clearly. How is the patient positioned?
opciones: Flat on the back with the legs raised about 12 inches (30 cm), head not raised
Sitting upright in a chair with the injured leg resting on a low stool
Flat on the back with the head raised about 12 inches (30 cm) on pillows
On the left side with the knees drawn up and the injured leg supported
preguntas.explicacion: The shock position is supine with the legs lifted roughly 12 inches, or 30 centimeters, and the head left down. It is used only when the patient is conscious and has no injury to the head, neck, spine or leg; if raising the legs causes pain or harm, the patient is left flat. The patient is kept warm and tight clothing is loosened.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I 5F · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician calls asking why no result was issued for a specimen sent that morning. The specimen had been rejected. What does the emergency laboratory do with rejected samples?
opciones: Stores them up to 24 hours at 4 °C and issues an immediate LIS report stating the sample was not processed
Discards them at once as biohazardous waste and telephones the ward within 30 minutes of rejection
Runs the tests anyway and reports the results with a comment noting the reason for rejection
Freezes them at –20 °C for one week in case the physician asks for the analysis to be repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Unsuitable samples are recognized at arrival by visual inspection and serum indices; those rejected are kept for up to 24 hours at 4 °C, and a report goes out immediately through the laboratory information system saying the sample was not processed. That report is how the ordering physician learns that a new specimen is needed; testing a rejected tube or discarding it unrecorded defeats the purpose.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3 · CPT Core k3 k5 (applied D4 4D)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood bank reports may call the surface antigens of red cells by another name. Which term is it?
opciones: Agglutinogens
Agglutinins
Isoantibodies
Immunoglobulins
preguntas.explicacion: With red cells the antigens may be called isoantigens or agglutinogens, and the antibodies isoantibodies or agglutinins, though the plainer words antigen and antibody are more common. Immunoglobulin is another name for antibody. The agglutinogen is the marker on the cell; the agglutinin is the Y-shaped antibody that clumps cells carrying it.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health: Complementary, Alternative, or Integrative Health — What's In a Name?
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starts acupuncture on her own, keeps taking the medication the physician prescribed, and has told neither side, so nobody is coordinating the two. How is that approach described?
opciones: Complementary, because it is used together with conventional care
Alternative, because it is used together with conventional care
Complementary, because it is used in place of conventional care
Integrative, because the two kinds of care are coordinated
preguntas.explicacion: The three words are not interchangeable. A non-mainstream approach used alongside conventional medicine is complementary; one used instead of conventional medicine is alternative; and integrative asks for more than sitting side by side, because there the conventional and the non-mainstream are deliberately brought together and coordinated, which is not what happens when the patient starts on her own and tells no one. Most people who take up non-mainstream approaches also stay in conventional care, so complementary is the commoner of the two.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Iron — Consumer
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(d) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(d) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A woman of 32 who eats no meat asks how to get her iron. What is the best guidance?
opciones: Pair plant iron with vitamin C foods, since nonheme iron absorbs poorly
Pair plant iron with calcium-rich foods, since calcium carries iron in
Plant iron absorbs the same as meat iron, so no pairing is needed
Take a vitamin C supplement daily, which is what corrects hemochromatosis
preguntas.explicacion: Food iron comes as heme iron, in meat, seafood and poultry, and nonheme iron, in plant foods and fortified products. The body takes up nonheme iron less readily, so vegetarians need close to twice the listed amount, which for women 19 to 50 is 18 mg a day. Vitamin C foods eaten alongside improve that absorption.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Sugar interference on meters · PBT IV.A.4 / IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 k111 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on peritoneal dialysis with an icodextrin solution has a fingerstick glucose done on the clinic's meter. What interference should the tester be aware of?
opciones: Some meter systems read falsely high glucose in patients exposed to icodextrin, maltose, galactose or xylose
Some meter systems read falsely low glucose in dialysis patients because the dialysate dilutes the capillary blood
There is no interference, because glucose meters measure glucose specifically and ignore all other sugars
The interference affects only urine glucose strips, so the blood meter result can be reported as usual
preguntas.explicacion: Reading the manufacturer's instructions or the package insert matters because particular substances interfere with particular devices: some point-of-care glucose systems report glucose falsely high where the patient has had icodextrin, maltose, xylose or galactose. Hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can also make a result inaccurate or impossible to calculate, and a patient with poor peripheral circulation may not give an adequate capillary sample.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A biological indicator from the same lot is left unexposed and then incubated alongside the tested one. What is that for?
opciones: To verify that the spores were alive to begin with and that the incubation itself was proper
To give a second reading of the load, so a single doubtful result never stands on its own
To measure how long the spores survive at room temperature before the next lot is opened
To compare two manufacturers, which is how a product defect in the lot is normally found
preguntas.explicacion: The unexposed control is what proves the test was valid: it confirms the spores were viable before sterilization and that the incubator ran correctly. Using a control with every run is the most conservative practice, though weekly may be enough. Pairing indicators from different manufacturers is a separate move, used when a product defect is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-scheduling limits · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses the portal at midnight to book a visit for chest pain that started an hour earlier. What is wrong with that use of the portal?
opciones: Portal self-scheduling is offered for non-urgent appointments, which this is not
Portal self-scheduling is offered only to patients seen within the past year
Portal self-scheduling is offered only during the hours the office is open
Portal self-scheduling is offered only for visits with her own primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: The portal is open at any hour from any internet connection, and beyond reading her own record some portals let a patient send a secure message to the clinician, ask for a refill, look up benefits and coverage, change her contact details, make a payment, download forms and book appointments that are not urgent. That last limit is built into the scheduling feature itself.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why might a tracing be ordered for a patient who already has a pacemaker?
opciones: To check the device is working and pacing as programmed
To decide whether the device should be switched off first
To measure the battery charge left inside the device
To confirm the device is safe before an MRI is done
preguntas.explicacion: One of the listed indications is detecting malfunction of a pacemaker or defibrillator, evaluating how the device is programmed and functioning, checking its reading of arrhythmias and confirming that the pacing is being delivered as it should.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Contact Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Contact Precautions PPE · CPT D1 1I k34 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is sent to draw blood from a patient on Contact Precautions for a multidrug-resistant organism. Which PPE does the CDC call for?
opciones: A gown and gloves, put on when entering the room and discarded before leaving
A surgical mask put on at the door, with gloves only for the venipuncture itself
A fit-tested N95 respirator, with gown and gloves added only if the patient has a draining wound
Gloves alone, since Standard Precautions already cover blood contact during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: For Contact Precautions the CDC recommends a gown and gloves for any interaction that may bring contact with the patient, or with the environment around them, put on as the room is entered and taken off before leaving so the pathogen stays inside. A mask on entry is the Droplet rule, and the fit-tested N95 belongs to Airborne. Standard Precautions still run underneath, so the gloves the phlebotomist would wear anyway are not enough on their own; the gown is added because this pathogen travels by contact with the patient and the surroundings.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Gustation and Olfaction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many tastes are recognized within the sense of gustation, and where do the receptors for smell sit?
opciones: Five tastes, and the smell receptors sit high in the nasal cavity
Four tastes, and the smell receptors sit high in the nasal cavity
Five tastes, and the smell receptors sit on the surface of the tongue
Four tastes, and the smell receptors sit within the pharynx and larynx
preguntas.explicacion: Taste long counted four submodalities, sweet, salty, sour and bitter, and umami was recognized as the fifth in the mid-1980s. Smell works on chemicals too, but its receptor neurons live in a small patch of olfactory epithelium high in the nasal cavity, where inhaled molecules dissolve in the mucus and reach the dendrites.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(b), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D k112 · NCMA 2C.1 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician phones the laboratory to order a test and says the written order will follow. Under CLIA, how long does the laboratory have to obtain the written or electronic authorization?
opciones: 30 days from the oral request
7 days from the oral request
24 hours from the oral request
90 days from the oral request
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1241(b) an oral request is acceptable provided the laboratory then solicits authorization in writing or electronically inside 30 days, and keeps either that authorization or a record of its attempts to obtain it. The default is a written or electronic request from an authorized person; the oral route is the exception, and its ceiling is 30 days, not a day, a week or three months.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance and Issues of Concern (damages)
preguntas.subtema: Burden of proof · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: A tort case is decided on a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, better than 50 percent. The criminal yardstick of beyond a reasonable doubt has no place here, and in a number of states the jury need not even be unanimous to hold a tortfeasor responsible. One is liable for a tort rather than guilty of it. Damages are a separate question: they have to be proved to a certainty instead of estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that goes to the amount awarded, not to the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Insect bites and stings", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.r · 2027 I.B.8.r · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: After the stinger is out of an insect sting, how is the site treated?
opciones: Washed with soap and water, then ice wrapped in cloth, 10 minutes on and off
Washed with soap and water, then ice put straight onto the skin for an hour
Left dry and covered, with a warm compress applied every 10 minutes
Rubbed with alcohol and left open, with the area kept above heart level
preguntas.explicacion: The stinger is scraped off with a straight edge such as a credit card, never squeezed with tweezers, and the site is washed thoroughly with soap and water. Ice wrapped in a washcloth goes on for 10 minutes and off for 10 minutes, repeated. An antihistamine or an anti-itch cream may be used, and the site is watched for days for signs of infection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fasting", section Cellular Level
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: How far into a fast are the liver's glycogen stores described as running out?
opciones: After about 24 hours
After about 8 hours
After about 12 hours
After about 72 hours
preguntas.explicacion: During a fast, blood glucose is first held up by glycogen in the liver and skeletal muscle, and the liver carries the greatest part of that work through the first 24 hours. After roughly 24 hours the stores are depleted and the body turns to fat and protein. Eight and twelve hours are fasting windows asked of patients, not the glycogen limit.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Electrical Safety, Recognized Controls and Work Practices
preguntas.subtema: GFCI protection · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.d III.C.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which protective device belongs on all 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles in a hospital, according to OSHA's recognized controls?
opciones: A ground-fault circuit interrupter, which shuts off power on a ground fault
A surge protector, which absorbs voltage spikes from the power line
A three-prong adapter, which grounds equipment lacking a ground prong
A step-down transformer, which lowers the voltage below 1,000 volts
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's Hospitals eTool recommends ground-fault circuit interrupters on all 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles. A GFCI is a fast-acting circuit breaker that cuts power the moment a ground fault occurs, so that current from a damaged cord or an energized metal enclosure does not flow through a worker's body and cause burns or electrocution. The standard also requires electrical service near water sources to be properly grounded under 29 CFR 1910.304(g)(6); adapters that bypass a missing ground prong are the kind of damaged connection the eTool warns against.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad; and StatPearls, "Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)" (NBK559281)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An imaging report describes hepatomegaly. Which ending carries the meaning of enlargement?
opciones: -megaly, which is added to the root for the organ
-sclerosis, which is added to the root for the organ
-ectasis, which is added to the root for the organ
-trophy, which is added to the root for the organ
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -megaly means enlargement, and hepat- names the liver, so hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver. The near neighbors mean other things: -sclerosis is a hardening, -ectasis an expansion or dilation of a hollow structure, and -trophy is growth in the sense of nourishment, as in atrophy and hypertrophy.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.4 Specimen contamination
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A molecular laboratory sees sporadic false-positive results in negative specimens. Which workflow controls does the review recommend against sample and amplicon contamination?
opciones: One-way workflow through separate pre- and post-amplification areas, frequent glove changes, aerosol-barrier tips
A single shared bench for extraction and amplification, so that every step is handled by the same pair of gloves
Reusing pipette tips within one patient's series of tubes, so that no foreign template can enter the reaction
Leaving opened sample tubes uncapped in the post-amplification area to let aerosols settle before analysis
preguntas.explicacion: Because amplification makes millions of copies from a few templates, a positive sample or its amplicons can contaminate a negative one at collection, processing or analysis. Guidelines therefore ask for separate pre- and post-amplification areas, ideally physically apart, a one-way workflow from pre to post, separate clean protective equipment for each area with frequent glove changes, dedicated equipment, aerosol-barrier tips and pipetting technique that limits aerosols, plus routine cleaning with 10 to 15 % bleach and wipe-tests of the environment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Goniometer", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · RMA III.B.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: A goniometer is used to record both active and passive range of motion at the same joint. What differs between the two readings?
opciones: For the passive reading the examiner moves the joint through its range
For the passive reading the patient repeats the movement without help
For the active reading the examiner holds the distal segment throughout
For the active reading the instrument stays in place the whole time
preguntas.explicacion: The instrument can evaluate active as well as passive range. For the active figure the goniometer is taken off, the patient moves the joint, and the instrument is replaced and realigned to read the result. For the passive figure the examiner moves the joint through its range and the same steps are repeated.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare drug plans work, Tiers
preguntas.subtema: Drug formulary · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her copayment for one drug is higher than for another in the same plan.
opciones: The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers cost more
The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers are generic
The plan charges more for drugs bought before the deductible has been met
The plan charges more for drugs a specialist prescribed than for others
preguntas.explicacion: Plans place covered drugs in tiers, and a drug in a lower tier generally costs the patient less. In the example given, tier 1 holds most generic drugs with the lowest copayment, tier 2 preferred brand-name drugs, tier 3 non-preferred brand names, and a specialty tier the very high-cost drugs. Generics sit at the bottom, not the top, and the tier does not depend on who wrote the prescription.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: What is a contracture?
opciones: The loss of full passive motion from a joint, muscle or soft tissue limit
The loss of muscle bulk that follows a long stretch of time spent in bed
A joint that moves further than it should because the tissues have slackened
A painful spasm that locks a muscle group for a few minutes at a time
preguntas.explicacion: A contracture means the joint can no longer be moved through its full passive range, because the joint itself, the muscle or the soft tissue limits it. It is what long-term range-of-motion programs are meant to prevent after a stroke or a spinal cord injury, in neuromuscular disease, and after a traumatic brain injury.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Where is the HIPAA Privacy Rule Applicable; 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Stricter state law · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.a(2) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. The notice of privacy practices must reflect the more stringent law when it limits a use or disclosure. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Complete Blood Count (CBC), What is a complete blood count?; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", Lavender
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count is ordered. Which tube is used, and what does the CBC measure?
opciones: A lavender EDTA tube; red cells, white cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and MCV
A light blue citrate tube; the seconds the sample takes to clot and the INR
A gray fluoride tube; plasma glucose and the average glucose of recent months
A gold serum separator tube; electrolytes, kidney waste products and the liver enzymes
preguntas.explicacion: Hematologic assays go in the lavender EDTA tube, and a CBC counts the blood cells: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and the mean corpuscular volume. Clotting seconds and the INR belong to the PT/INR in citrate, glucose to the gray tube, and electrolytes, BUN, creatinine and liver enzymes to the metabolic panels run on serum.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Diversion Control Division, Definition of Controlled Substance Schedules: Schedule V
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k15 · CMA 2027 I.D.1 · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: A cough preparation holds no more than 200 mg of codeine per 100 mL. Which schedule does it belong to?
opciones: Schedule V, whose preparations hold limited quantities of certain narcotics
Schedule IV, whose potential for abuse is lower than that of Schedule III
Schedule III, where a product holds up to 90 mg of codeine per dosage unit
