preguntas.pregunta: During a lumbar puncture, how much cerebrospinal fluid is collected and into how many containers?
opciones: 1 to 10 mL, collected into 4 or more vials once the pressure has been measured
1 to 10 mL, collected into a single vial once the pressure has been measured
20 to 30 mL, collected into 4 or more vials once the pressure has been measured
1 to 10 mL, collected into 4 or more vials before the pressure is measured at all
preguntas.explicacion: The patient lies on one side with the knees drawn toward the chest and the chin tucked down, the back is cleaned and the spinal needle goes in at L3-L4 or L4-L5. An opening pressure may be taken first, and then 1 to 10 mL is collected into 4 or more vials; normal pressure runs 90 to 180 mm H2O. The laboratory account of the same fluid counts three numbered tubes, for chemistry, culture and cytology.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Otitis Media", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which event most often opens the door to acute otitis media in a child?
opciones: A viral upper respiratory infection that disturbs Eustachian tube function
A viral upper respiratory infection that perforates the tympanic membrane
A build-up of cerumen that blocks the external auditory canal completely
A rise in middle ear pressure caused by hearing loss in the affected ear
preguntas.explicacion: Acute otitis media appears where pathogens, a susceptible host and the environment meet, and the usual trigger is a viral upper respiratory infection that upsets the working of the Eustachian tube. Once drainage fails, the middle ear inflames and microbes multiply. Immunocompromise and genetic predisposition raise the risk further.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conjunctivitis", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Among the infectious causes of conjunctivitis, which comes first and which pathogen leads it?
opciones: Viral conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Bacterial conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Allergic conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Viral conjunctivitis, led by Staphylococcus aureus
preguntas.explicacion: Infection is only one branch of the causes of red eye with discharge, and within it the viral form comes first and the bacterial one next; adenoviruses alone account for 65 to 90 percent of viral cases. The noninfectious branch is headed by allergens and toxins, and allergic conjunctivitis is reported to affect 15 to 40 percent of the population, which is why the question asks only about the infectious causes: across every cause, allergy would come out ahead. Staphylococcus aureus leads the bacterial causes in adults.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Where open access works · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A fee-for-service practice is told that open access only suits capitated managed care. Is that right?
opciones: No: it is reported to work in fee-for-service settings as well as in managed care
Yes: the model rests on capitation, since a same-day slot is not separately billable
Yes: the model was designed inside managed care and has not been tried outside it
No, but it holds up only where the practice also carries a large managed care panel
preguntas.explicacion: Experts in designing and implementing the model report that it works in fee-for-service settings as much as in managed care. Its logic has nothing to do with how a visit gets paid for: it brings queuing theory and industrial engineering to bear on matching the demand for visits against the supply of clinician time, on the supposition that the trouble is not a shortage of capacity but an imbalance between the two.

preguntas.pregunta: When should anti-HBs be tested to document a healthcare worker's response to the hepatitis B vaccine series?
opciones: 1 to 2 months after the final dose
6 months after the final dose
Within 10 working days of the final dose
Every year, at the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Postvaccination serologic testing for anti-HBs is done 1 to 2 months after the third dose, so that the worker's response status is on record for any future exposure; a level of 10 mIU/mL or more after a documented series is the correlate of protection. For workers who also received HBIG, testing may have to wait until the HBIG antibody has cleared, about 6 months after it was given. Ten working days is the OSHA deadline for offering the vaccine, and annual testing is not recommended for immunocompetent responders.

Only if the patient disagrees with the decision itself does she appeal, and the last page of the notice sets out step by step when and how to do that.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pregnancy Test, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; What do the results mean?; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: HCG in urine (003619)
preguntas.subtema: False-negative urine hCG · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.d.(4) · RMA III.C.4.b.iv · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose period is two days late drank several glasses of water before giving a random urine sample, and the office pregnancy test is negative. How should this result be handled?
opciones: It may be a false negative from dilute urine or early testing; a repeat on first morning urine in about a week is advised
It is reliable, because office cassettes detect hCG from 10 days after conception regardless of urine concentration
It should be repeated immediately with a second cassette from the same kit, since a single negative can never be reported
It confirms that the patient is not pregnant, because urine tests are 97 to 99 % accurate at any point after a missed period
preguntas.explicacion: Drinking large amounts of fluid before collecting the sample can dilute the hCG so that it does not show on the test, and testing too soon after conception may precede detectable hormone levels; both produce false negatives. First morning urine is the most concentrated. Because hCG rises daily in early pregnancy, a negative test is repeated about a week later, and a still-suspected pregnancy is referred to the provider. The 97 to 99 % accuracy figure applies to tests done a week or two after a missed period.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38
preguntas.pregunta: What does an automated external defibrillator do once its pads are on the chest?
opciones: It reads the heart rhythm and shocks only when the rhythm calls for a shock
It delivers a shock as soon as the pads are attached to an unresponsive patient
It paces the heart at 100 to 120 beats a minute while compressions go on
It confirms the pulse and holds compressions until a pulse can be felt
preguntas.explicacion: The device analyzes the rhythm on its own and delivers a shock if, and only if, a shock is what that rhythm needs; the rescuer follows its spoken instructions exactly. When a shock is advised, compressions pause and everyone stands clear; the moment the shock is delivered, or if none is advised, CPR resumes without delay.

preguntas.pregunta: A conventional 12-lead ECG is being set up. How many wires are attached to the patient?
opciones: Ten: four on the limbs and six across the chest
Twelve: four on the limbs and eight across the chest
Six: two on the limbs and four across the chest
Fourteen: six on the limbs and eight across the chest
preguntas.explicacion: Twelve leads are produced from ten wires. Four limb electrodes generate the six limb leads, and each of the six chest positions has its own wire. The limb leads look at the heart in the vertical plane and the chest leads record it in the horizontal plane, which is why both groups are needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Facial Laceration Repair", Special Considerations for Suture Choice
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A superficial laceration is closed with cyanoacrylate skin glue. What should the patient be told to expect?
opciones: It gives a water-tight seal and tends to come away on its own after about 7 to 10 days
It gives a water-tight seal and has to be dissolved off with acetone at the follow-up visit
It gives a water-tight seal and is removed with a staple extractor once the wound is closed
It gives a water-tight seal and stays on until the scar has finished maturing at 12 months
preguntas.explicacion: Skin glue seals the wound against water and lends it tensile strength while it lasts, and it generally falls off after roughly seven to ten days. It is quick and comparatively painless, which suits pediatric and percutaneous wounds, but it is only good for superficial lacerations: anything deeper needs a layered suture closure underneath.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Healing Phases", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: How much of its original strength does a healed incision regain, and when does maximal tensile strength arrive?
opciones: About 80 percent, reached at roughly 11 to 14 weeks after the injury
About 80 percent, reached at roughly 4 to 6 weeks after the injury
About 100 percent, reached at roughly 11 to 14 weeks after the injury
About 50 percent, reached at roughly 9 to 12 months after the injury
preguntas.explicacion: The remodeling phase starts around week three and can run up to twelve months; excess collagen degrades and contraction peaks around week three. Maximal tensile strength of an incision wound comes at roughly 11 to 14 weeks, and the scar never regains full strength, settling at about 80 percent of the original.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory counts every mislabeled specimen for a month, and then adds a two-person identity check before every draw. How are these two activities named?
opciones: Counting the mislabeled specimens is quality control; adding the identity check is quality assurance
Counting the mislabeled specimens is quality assurance, and adding the identity check is quality control
Both are quality control, because each one measures how well the collection system performs
Both are proficiency testing, because outside samples decide whether the laboratory passes
preguntas.explicacion: Quality control is the measuring arm: it sets the standard and gathers data to see whether work stays inside it. Quality assurance is the wider process that gives confidence the standard will be met, and it uses control data to do so. Counting wrong-side surgeries is the control task; the time-out before the incision is the assurance task. Both sit under quality management.

Patients with dementia, who need one idea presented at a time

preguntas.explicacion: The note under the table of techniques warns that eye contact, and sitting close to the patient, may destabilise some people, among them patients with paranoia or a psychotic disorder, and should be used with caution; where the provider's safety is uncertain, sit at a safe distance without leaving the patient feeling isolated. preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.g · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: What is done to the work surface itself before any sterile supply is placed on it?

It is disinfected and covered while still visibly wet
It is wiped with sterile water and dried with a towel
It is covered with a second drape without being wiped
preguntas.explicacion: The surface is disinfected and left to dry all the way through before anything sterile goes down on it. Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit

preguntas.explicacion: This is a synchronous model: the patient travels to a nearby site stocked with diagnostic equipment, usually a clinic, while the clinician joins from somewhere else. preguntas.pregunta: A patient in shock begins to vomit and a spinal injury is suspected. How is the patient turned?

Yes: a worsening condition after treatment is what negligence means
Yes: any deviation from the expected recovery is a compensable injury
preguntas.explicacion: A medical intervention can leave the patient better, worse or unchanged, and all three are possible with entirely appropriate care. Negligence cannot be read off an unexpected result, a failure to cure or a failure to recover. Even an error that fell below the standard may have caused no damages, in which case there is probably nothing to claim.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who never worked long enough to earn premium-free Part A asks what buying it will cost her in 2026.
opciones: Either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long she or her spouse paid the taxes
A flat $202.90 a month, which is what every enrollee pays for Part A in 2026
A flat $283 a year, payable once the first hospital benefit period has opened
A flat $1,736 a year, the same figure as the inpatient hospital deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Part A costs most people nothing, because Medicare taxes were paid long enough by them or by a spouse, generally ten years' worth. Someone who does not qualify may be able to buy it: in 2026 the amount is either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long those taxes were paid. Part B has to be taken as well in order to buy Part A.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 1, 7, 8 and 11
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 8 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which Safety Data Sheet section tells the reader which gloves and eye protection to use with a chemical and lists its exposure limits?
opciones: Section 8, on exposure controls and personal protection
Section 7, Handling and Storage, with incompatibilities
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with routes of exposure
Section 1, Identification, with the emergency phone number
preguntas.explicacion: Section 8 brings together the OSHA permissible exposure limits and ACGIH threshold limit values, the engineering controls such as local exhaust ventilation, and the personal protective measures, down to the glove material, for example nitrile or PVC, and its breakthrough time. Section 7 gives safe handling and storage conditions and incompatible chemicals; Section 11 describes toxic effects, symptoms and carcinogen listings; Section 1 identifies the product and supplier and gives the emergency telephone number.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k71 · RMA III.G.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: What has to be retrievable by prescription number each time a Schedule III or IV prescription is refilled?
opciones: Drug name and form, the date, the quantity, the pharmacist's initials and the total
Registration number of the prescriber, the diagnosis, and the plan that is billed
The date, the quantity, and the number of the order form the substance came on
Only how many refills are left, since the original prescription holds all the rest
preguntas.explicacion: Each refill goes on the back of the prescription or into another document or electronic record kept uniformly and readily retrievable. Retrievable by prescription number must be the controlled substance's name and dosage form, the date it was filled or refilled, how much was dispensed, which pharmacist dispensed each refill by their initials, and how many refills that prescription has had in total.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Religious Competence in Clinical Practice", sections Islam, Judaism, Eastern Orthodox and Baha'i
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which religious observance is a month-long fast from food and drink during daylight hours?
opciones: Ramadan, in the Islamic tradition
Yom Kippur, in Judaism
Great Lent, in Eastern Orthodoxy
The month of Ala, in the Baha'i faith
preguntas.explicacion: Ramadan is a month-long fast from food and drink during daylight, lasting 29 or 30 days, with children, pregnant women and the ill possibly exempt. Yom Kippur is a single day without eating or drinking; the Orthodox Great Lent is a 40-day fast from meat, dairy and oil; and the Baha'i fast runs March 2 to 20, sunrise to sunset.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling decisions · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a practice starts booking video visits it is told to settle several scheduling questions. Which one belongs on that list?
opciones: How the office will decide that a particular request suits a telehealth appointment
How the clinician will write the visit up in the record once the video call ends
How the practice will train its current health care team to use the new platform
How the practice will support a caregiver who is helping the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Under scheduling, the questions are when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether patients will book online or by telephone, how the office will judge whether a telehealth appointment is appropriate, and how and when reminders go out. Training the team is a staffing question, supporting a caregiver falls under meeting patient needs, and documentation comes afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction (Yellow, Pink, and Blue)
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 3N k57 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A blood culture bottle has just been filled. Which anticoagulant does it hold, and how is it mixed?
opciones: Sodium polyanethole sulfonate; the bottle is mixed eight to ten times
Sodium citrate at 3.2 percent; the bottle is inverted three to six times
Sodium fluoride with oxalate; the bottle is inverted three to six times
Lithium heparin with a gel; the bottle is mixed eight to ten times over
preguntas.explicacion: Culture bottles hold sodium polyanethole sulfonate, which works as an anticoagulant and blocks activation of complement, and the bottle is mixed eight to ten times once filled. Three to six inversions is the figure for the citrate tube, and fluoride with oxalate belongs to the glucose tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cardiac Cycle", Cellular Level
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A tracing is being read beside a pressure curve. When does ventricular contraction actually begin?
opciones: As the QRS complex reaches the peak of the R wave
As the P wave returns to the baseline of the tracing
As the T wave reaches its highest point on the tracing
As the ST segment begins to climb above the baseline
preguntas.explicacion: Electrical activity comes first and the muscle follows a moment later. The QRS complex is ventricular depolarization, and the ventricles start to squeeze as that complex peaks at the R wave, which is why the QRS sits just before the rise in ventricular pressure. The T wave is the recovery phase, not the contraction.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT VI.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee asks how often laboratory errors actually affect patients. What do the published data indicate?
opciones: About 24 to 30 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, and actual or potential harm occurs in 3 to 12 %
About 3 to 12 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, and actual or potential harm occurs in under 1 %
About 46 to 68 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, and actual harm occurs in 24 to 30 % of them
About 62 % of laboratory errors affect patient care, matching the share that arises in the pre-analytical phase
preguntas.explicacion: Published data put the share of laboratory errors that touch patient care at 24 to 30 %, and the share that causes actual or potential harm at 3 to 12 %, with some fields, molecular genetics among them, reaching far higher harm rates; a five-point scoring study found most errors scored lowest for actual impact and highest for potential impact. The 46 to 68 % figure belongs to the pre-pre-analytical phase and the 62 % to the pre-analytical share in the Italian stat laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Why may the timing of a therapeutic drug monitoring draw differ between two patients on the same drug?
opciones: The reason differs: dose adjustment, adverse effects, or suspected intoxication
The tube additive differs between morning and afternoon collections
The half-life of the drug is reset by each meal the patient eats
Peaks are always drawn at 4 p.m. and troughs at 8 a.m. regardless of dosing
preguntas.explicacion: For therapeutic drug monitoring the timing of the draw may differ according to the specific reason for the test, whether to justify a dose, to monitor adverse effects or to rule out intoxication, and that diurnal sampling may be requested for markers with a circadian pattern. Fixed clock times and tube additives have nothing to do with it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Evaluation: Clinical Criteria for Anaphylaxis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: After a likely exposure to an allergen, how many body systems must be involved before anaphylaxis is considered?
opciones: Two or more systems, such as skin plus breathing or skin plus gut
Three or more systems, one of which has to be the airway itself
One system only, and only when that system is the skin with hives
Four or more systems, including a fall in the systolic pressure
preguntas.explicacion: With a likely exposure, involvement of any two of skin or mucosa, breathing, blood pressure and gastrointestinal symptoms meets the criteria, even without airway swelling or hypotension. Known exposure plus hypotension alone also counts. The criteria are a guide for recognition: treatment is never held back to make them fit.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B15 k85 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does federal regulation require when a controlled substance is prescribed electronically?
opciones: It is created and signed inside an application that complies with part 1311
It is printed out and manually signed before it is transmitted on to the pharmacy
It is followed by a paper copy mailed to the pharmacy within seven days of issue
It is limited to Schedules III, IV and V, because Schedule II still needs paper
preguntas.explicacion: When a controlled substance is prescribed electronically, the prescription has to be produced and signed inside an application that complies with part 1311. A paper prescription is signed the way the practitioner would sign a check or a legal document, and a computer-generated one that gets printed or faxed must be signed by hand; the compliant application replaces that step rather than being added to it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How is the paper of a standard 12-lead recording laid out?
opciones: Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Three lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in three groups of four
Twelve lines of graph, with one lead printed on each of them
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing paper is set out in six channels. The twelve leads are written in four groups of three, so the first three channels carry lead I with aVR, V1 and V4, then lead II with aVL, V2 and V5, then lead III with aVF, V3 and V6.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4
preguntas.subtema: Signature requirements · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A provider wants to sign chart notes with a rubber stamp because handwriting is slow. What does CMS say?
opciones: A stamp is not usually acceptable, apart from a disability accommodation
Stamped signatures are acceptable whenever the provider keeps the stamp locked away
Stamped signatures are acceptable if a signature log lists the stamp and its owner
Stamped signatures are acceptable on orders but never on progress notes or reports
preguntas.explicacion: A handwritten signature is a mark made by a person to signify knowledge, approval, acceptance or an obligation. CMS says a stamp is not usually acceptable, and lets one be used only under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, by an author with a physical disability who can show a contractor that the disability prevents signing. A signature log is a different device altogether, for tying initials or an illegible signature to a name.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The record describes the same condition as both acute and chronic, and the Index has separate subentries at the same level. What does the coder do?
opciones: Code both of them, and sequence the acute or subacute code first
Code both of them, and sequence the chronic code first of the two
Code the chronic one alone, since it is the longer-standing problem
Code the acute one alone, since it is what brought her in this time
preguntas.explicacion: Where the same condition is written up as acute or subacute and also as chronic, and the Alphabetic Index carries separate subentries indented to the same level, both codes go on and the acute or subacute one is sequenced first. Signs and symptoms that routinely accompany a disease process are not coded in addition unless the classification says so.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the conduction system sets the rate and rhythm of a normal heartbeat?
opciones: The sinoatrial node, in the upper wall of the right atrium
The atrioventricular node, in the lower right atrium
The atrioventricular bundle, inside the interventricular septum
The Purkinje fibers, spread through the ventricular walls
preguntas.explicacion: The sinoatrial node depolarizes faster than any other part of the system, reaches threshold first, and imposes its pace on everything downstream. That is why it is called the pacemaker and why the pattern it produces is called sinus rhythm. The other structures can fire on their own, but only at slower inherent rates.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2; and Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 3M k54 k59 · D1 1G k30 · PBT II.F VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A tube is being filled by injecting through its rubber stopper. Which precaution applies?
opciones: The tube stands in a sturdy rack and is not held in the other hand
The tube is held in the other hand so the angle can be corrected
The tube is laid flat on the tray so the blood runs down its wall
The tube is held by an assistant while the worker steadies it
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratory sample tubes are placed in a sturdy rack before the needle goes through the stopper, and the paired prohibition is not to inject into a tube while holding it in the other hand. Where a rack is not available, one hand fills the tube or a needle shield protects the other.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.5 Wound Dressings
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.k
preguntas.pregunta: Why is plain gauze moistened before it is used as wound packing?
opciones: Because dry gauze sticks to the wound base and injures the granulation tissue
Because dry gauze absorbs too much exudate and dries the wound bed out entirely
Because dry gauze cannot be cut to shape unless it has been softened with saline
Because dry gauze loses its sterility once it is in contact with the periwound skin
preguntas.explicacion: Gauze is the least expensive dressing and has to be changed often, at least daily, but left unmoistened it adheres to the wound base and damages the granulation tissue when it comes off. Packing gauze is dampened with sterile normal saline and wrung out so it is damp rather than wet, because gauze that is too wet macerates tissue and absorbs less.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.11 Checklist for Staple Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m
preguntas.pregunta: What safety step is taken before and after removing a run of staples?
opciones: Count the staples first and compare the count with the number actually taken out
Photograph the incision first and compare the image with the line after removal
Measure the incision first and compare that length with the length after removal
Palpate the incision first and compare the firmness with the firmness after removal
preguntas.explicacion: The staples are counted before the procedure begins and the removed ones are counted against that number at the end, so none is left behind. The wound is also inspected first for uniform closure, drainage, redness and swelling, and it is irrigated with sterile normal saline to lift debris and crusted exudate before the extractor is used.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heat emergencies", Symptoms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which is the first stage of heat illness?
opciones: Muscle cramps, most often in the legs or the abdomen
Cool moist skin with dark urine and severe thirst
Confusion and slurred speech with a very high temperature
A rapid weak pulse with rapid shallow breathing at rest
preguntas.explicacion: Cramps in the legs or abdomen are the first stage; fatigue, thirst and very heavy sweating come with them. If exposure goes on untreated, heat exhaustion follows with cool moist skin, dark urine, dizziness, headache, nausea and a rapid weak pulse, and after that heat stroke.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A pathology department wants to attack ordering errors, which a review puts at roughly seven orders in ten. Which measures are described as effective?
opciones: Governance of ordering, decision support, reflex algorithms and feedback to prescribers
A ban on panel ordering, a paper countersignature and a monthly audit of each ward
Restriction of ordering rights to consultants and a fixed weekly quota per patient
Automatic cancellation of any test repeated within a week of a normal result
preguntas.explicacion: Ordering is an easily overlooked step, and about 70 % of orders carry some sort of error: a test ordered twice, a test forgotten, or simply the wrong test. Governance programs, clinical decision support, reflex testing with interpretation and algorithms, feedback to the ordering physician and diagnostic stewardship have all been shown to cut inappropriate ordering and improve turnaround.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, section What do the results mean
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D II.K · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: What is the 'therapeutic range' of a monitored medicine?
opciones: The range of blood levels that is medically helpful without being dangerous
The range of doses a pharmacist may dispense without a new prescription
The time window before the next dose during which a trough is drawn
The reference range printed for healthy people who do not take the drug
preguntas.explicacion: TDM results show whether the level sits where the medicine helps without turning dangerous, which is what the therapeutic range means; it varies with the drug and with the patient, and where the level falls outside it the provider adjusts the dose and repeats the test. The pre-dose window is the trough timing, a separate concept.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare; and What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks which part pays for the doctor visit and the walker ordered today.
opciones: Part B, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part A, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part D, which covers provider services and the equipment ordered during them
Medigap, which covers provider services once Part A benefits are exhausted
preguntas.explicacion: Part B is the medical insurance half: services from doctors and other providers, outpatient care, home health, durable medical equipment such as walkers and wheelchairs, and many preventive services. Part A is hospital insurance, Part D pays for prescription drugs, and Medigap is private supplemental insurance that helps with the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than covering new categories.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Practitioner's Manual (2023 Edition), Recordkeeping Requirements
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k71 · CMA I.D.1.e · RMA III.G.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: How long does a practitioner have to keep the records of controlled substances?
opciones: At least two years, available for inspection and copying by DEA officials
At least six months, the span for which a Schedule IV prescription is valid
At least seven years, the span used for retaining the patient's own record
At least thirty days, after which the next inventory replaces those records
preguntas.explicacion: Complete, accurate records are kept up to date for every controlled substance the practice buys, receives, stores, sells, distributes, dispenses or otherwise disposes of, and they stay available to authorized DEA officials for inspection and copying for no less than two years. Records and inventories for Schedule II are kept apart from all the rest; those for Schedules III to V may be separate or simply readily retrievable.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k152 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the chest marks drawn again right after the sites are scrubbed?
opciones: The rubbing takes the marks off and the spots are lost
The alcohol makes the wax pencil marks hard to read
The marks have to be moved a space down after cleaning
The marks are copied onto the log sheet for the record
preguntas.explicacion: Each chest site is briskly rubbed with alcohol and gauze, and the cosmetic pencil marks come off with the oil and dead skin. The recommended habit is to keep an eye on the spot while cleaning it and re-mark it immediately, so the landmark work does not have to be repeated.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: slander; Wex: libel
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(2)-(3) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A staff member repeats a false and damaging claim about a patient out loud in the break room. Which tort is that, and what does it require?
opciones: Slander, and unlike libel the damages have to be proven by the person suing
Slander, and like libel the damages are presumed from the fact of publication
Libel, and the damages have to be proven by the person bringing the lawsuit
Libel, and the damages are presumed once the statement has been repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Defamation is a statement that harms someone's reputation, and it splits in two: libel is generally written or otherwise recorded, slander is generally spoken. With slander, damages are not presumed and the party suing has to prove them. Traditional libel rules go the other way and take the injury as given once the statement was published.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's skin is oily at the electrode sites. How is each site prepared?
opciones: Rub it with alcohol and gauze about ten times
Rub it with alcohol and gauze about three times
Wipe it with dry gauze and then let it air dry
Part the hair and press the electrode down firmly
preguntas.explicacion: Each site is scrubbed vigorously with alcohol and gauze roughly ten times to take off oil, sweat and scaly skin. Applying an electrode to a surface that was not cleaned that way is one of the causes of a drifting baseline. Parting the hair is a separate trick, and it helps the electrode stick.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Overview
preguntas.subtema: Which title applies · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under which part of the disability law is a privately owned medical office covered?
opciones: Title III, which reaches businesses and non-profits that serve the public
Title I, which reaches employers with fifteen or more people on the payroll
Title II, which reaches the services and programs of state and local government
Title IV, which reaches the companies that provide telephone and relay services
preguntas.explicacion: A private hospital or medical office is a place of public accommodation, and doctors' offices and hospitals are named among the businesses that serve the public. A clinic run by a state or a city falls under Title II instead, and Title I is the employment side, which applies to the same office as an employer.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube was drawn to only 67 % of its nominal volume. According to the fill-level study cited in the rejection paper, which coagulation result remains relatively reliable at that fill?
opciones: Prothrombin time
Activated PTT
Fibrinogen level
Factor VIII level
preguntas.explicacion: Lippi and colleagues found a clinically significant bias once tubes fall below 89 % of total fill for aPTT, below 78 % for fibrinogen and below 67 % for factor VIII, whereas prothrombin time and activated protein C resistance stayed relatively reliable even at 67 % of nominal volume. The laboratory still sets its acceptance line at 80 %, so the practical answer is a redraw, but PT is the test least disturbed by the short fill.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Lateral Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b · RMA III.F.2.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the lateral position often chosen for a pregnant patient who must lie down for a while?
opciones: It keeps the inferior vena cava from being compressed, so blood flow to the fetus holds up
It raises the pubic symphysis above the trunk, which increases the return of venous blood
It presses the abdominal contents upward, so that the diaphragm can move more freely
It lets the uterus rest against the table, so that fundal height can be measured better
preguntas.explicacion: Lying on one side with the top leg flexed over the bottom one takes pressure off the coccyx and, in pregnancy, keeps the weight of the uterus off the inferior vena cava so that blood keeps flowing to the fetus. Tilting the pubic symphysis to the highest point of the trunk is Trendelenburg, which presses the abdominal organs up against the diaphragm, the opposite of what a pregnant patient needs.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: What to expect on connecting · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has been told to connect early asks what she will see while she waits. What does the guidance say to describe for her?
opciones: A virtual waiting room, or hold music, until the clinician joins the appointment
A message telling her to ring the front desk so that she can be let in
A form she has to finish on screen before the video will start at all
A recorded message that reads out the practice's policy on canceling appointments
preguntas.explicacion: Appointment setup guidance tells the office to describe what the patient will meet when she connects early, and names the virtual waiting room and hold music. Connecting fifteen minutes ahead for a video appointment is what leaves room for last-minute troubleshooting, so she needs to know that the wait is expected and not a sign that something has gone wrong.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.2 Basic Concepts Related to Wounds
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the phases of wound healing occur?
opciones: Hemostasis, inflammatory, proliferative, maturation
Inflammatory, hemostasis, maturation, proliferative
Proliferative, hemostasis, inflammatory, maturation
Hemostasis, proliferative, inflammatory, maturation
preguntas.explicacion: Vessels constrict and clotting factors act first, which is hemostasis and lasts up to an hour depending on the injury. Vasodilation then lets white cells in to clean the bed, showing as swelling, redness and exudate. The proliferative phase brings epithelialization, angiogenesis, collagen and contraction, and maturation lays down more collagen for strength.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug coverage (Part D); and HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicare Part D
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does a person with Original Medicare get prescription drug coverage?
opciones: By joining a separate Medicare drug plan run by a private company
By joining a separate Medigap policy run by a private company
By asking the pharmacy to bill Part B for the drugs bought there
By enrolling in Part A, which adds drug coverage after the first year
preguntas.explicacion: Part D coverage arrives in two ways: a standalone Medicare drug plan bolted onto Original Medicare, or a Medicare Advantage plan that already has drug coverage built in. Either way, private companies Medicare has approved run the plans. Medigap helps with the patient's share of costs, not with pharmacy drugs; Part B covers only limited outpatient drugs; and Part A adds no drug benefit.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: What fasting window is recommended before routine morning blood sampling?
opciones: Not less than 12 hours after the last solid meal
Not less than 8 hours after the last alcoholic drink
Not less than 24 hours after alcohol, with no limit on food
Not less than 2 hours after any food or drink
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation is morning sampling in a fasting state of not less than 12 hours since the last solid meal, with water allowed, coffee and energy drinks not allowed that morning, alcohol avoided for 24 hours, non-emergent medicines avoided, and no heavy exertion for 24 hours. The two-hour question comes from the WHO Annex C interview, and 8 hours is the glucose minimum.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.1; and StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2N · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i · RMA I.D.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Drawing blood on an open ward, what do the WHO best practices and the therapeutic communication techniques both direct about privacy?
opciones: Close the bed curtain or the door to respect the patient's privacy
Ask the visitors to stay at the bedside so that the patient feels supported
Keep the curtain open so that a colleague can observe the draw
Explain that privacy is not required for such a short procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO says that at an inpatient bedside the curtain is closed to give privacy, and that the sampling itself happens in privacy and in clean conditions; the StatPearls table lists respecting privacy and minimizing interruptions, closing the door or the curtain according to the setting. Neither source treats a short procedure as an exception.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: Several staff members would normally each gather part of an older patient's history. What does the guidance advise?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating tires them
Have each staff member ask again, so that errors are caught
Have the caregiver give the history so the patient can rest
Have the history taken from scratch again at every follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is needed with older patients, and where possible the patient should tell their story only once, because giving it to one staff member and then again to another is tiring. The history is built up and updated visit by visit rather than started over, and it is the patient, not the companion, who tells it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Light-sensitive analytes · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen was left uncapped on a sunny windowsill for two hours before dipping. Which two strip results are most likely to be falsely decreased?
opciones: Bilirubin and urobilinogen, which break down when exposed to light
Glucose and ketones, which evaporate from an uncovered container
Protein and specific gravity, which fall as the urine warms up
Nitrite and leukocyte esterase, which are consumed by bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: Bilirubin and urobilinogen are unstable when a specimen sits in light and warmth for any length of time: they break down and their pads read falsely low. Room temperature also feeds bacterial growth, which can fake a positive on the blood pad and move the pH. Microorganisms may metabolise the glucose in the specimen and lower the pH with it, but the light-sensitive pair is bilirubin and urobilinogen.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium; and Glossary: Deductible
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes the amount a person pays every month for their health insurance, whether or not they use any care?
opciones: Premium
Deductible
Copay
Network
preguntas.explicacion: The premium is the monthly price of the coverage itself, owed whether or not any service is used. HealthCare.gov adds that, on top of it, the patient usually pays other costs when care is actually received: a deductible, copayments and coinsurance. Its glossary describes a copay as a fixed amount per covered service, such as $30. The network is the set of contracted providers, not a payment at all.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient bought a Medicare SELECT policy and has changed her mind about it. What right does she have?
opciones: Twelve months in which to switch across to a standard Medigap policy instead
Six months in which to switch, matching the Medigap open enrollment period
Thirty days in which to switch, after which the policy holds for the whole year
No right to switch, since every policy with the same letter is the same anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Some states also sell a kind of Medigap policy called Medicare SELECT, and a buyer of one has the right to change her mind within twelve months and move to a standard Medigap policy. That is separate from the six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period, which governs when a policy can be bought without health questions in the first place.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fiber — Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(f) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How much fiber a day is recommended for older children, adolescents and adults?
opciones: 21 to 38 grams, against an actual average of about 16 grams
21 to 38 grams, against an actual average of about 30 grams
10 to 20 grams, against an actual average of about 16 grams
40 to 60 grams, against an actual average of about 30 grams
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation runs from 21 to 38 grams a day, while people in the United States average around 16 grams, so most patients are short. Younger children cannot eat enough calories to reach that range, but whole grains and fresh fruit still belong in their diet.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth-appropriate visits · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks whether her diabetes education can be done by video instead of in the office. What does Medicare list?
opciones: Diabetes self-management training is among the services it covers by telehealth
An annual wellness visit with a physical examination is covered by telehealth
A screening mammogram read at the imaging center is covered by telehealth
A vaccine given at the patient's own home by a nurse is covered by telehealth
preguntas.explicacion: Plenty of services that normally happen face to face can be delivered by telehealth. Medicare names advance care planning, rehabilitation for the heart and the lungs, caregiver training, assessments of cognition, screening for depression, training in diabetes self-management, medical nutrition therapy, outpatient psychotherapy and speech therapy, and warns that the list is not everything it covers.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Recertification Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: How long is an NHA certification valid, and what keeps it current?
opciones: Two years, with ten continuing education credits inside each cycle
Two years, with twenty continuing education credits inside each cycle
Five years, with ten continuing education credits inside each cycle
Three years, with fifteen continuing education credits in each cycle
preguntas.explicacion: A certification runs for two years from its issue date and expires on the date printed on the certificate. Inside each two-year cycle the holder submits documentation of at least ten continuing education credits relevant to their field. Certified pharmacy technicians are the exception: twenty hours, including one of pharmacy law and one of patient safety.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which way do the tabs of the chest electrodes point when they are applied?
opciones: Toward the yoke of the patient cable
Toward the midline of the sternum
Toward the patient's left shoulder
Toward the top of the patient's head
preguntas.explicacion: Once the six chest sites have been scrubbed and re-marked, the electrodes go on with their tabs turned toward the cable yoke, and the clip connectors are then attached to those tabs. On the legs the tab is pointed the other way, up toward the upper leg.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO say the alcohol swab should be moved over the venipuncture site?
opciones: From the center outward and downward, covering at least 2 cm
From the outside toward the center, covering at least 2 cm
Back and forth over the vein until the skin looks clean
In one pass along the vein, from the tourniquet toward the hand
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 describes firm but gentle pressure, starting at the center of the site and working downward and outward to cover an area of 2 cm or more, then letting the skin dry. The other patterns are not described. The step also forbids touching the cleaned area afterwards, and if it is touched the disinfection is repeated.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient is having blood pressure measured for the first time. What is recommended?
opciones: It is measured in both arms at that first evaluation
It is measured in the dominant arm and only that arm from then on
It is measured in one arm sitting and the other arm lying down
It is measured in the arm and again at the ankle for comparison
preguntas.explicacion: At the first evaluation the pressure is taken in both arms, because a difference between the two sides is itself a finding. After that the arm used is recorded so later readings can be compared with the same conditions, since the position and the limb both influence the number obtained.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Goniometer", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62
preguntas.pregunta: Active range of motion at the elbow is being measured with a goniometer. How many readings are taken and what is recorded?
opciones: Three readings, and the average of the three is what gets recorded
Three readings, and the largest of the three is what gets recorded
Two readings, and the larger of the two is what gets recorded
One reading, taken after the joint has gone through its full range
preguntas.explicacion: For active range of motion the measurement is repeated three times and the average of the three is the figure. Each pass starts from the neutral position, with the bony landmarks palpated and the instrument realigned, because the goniometer is taken off while the patient moves the joint and put back afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Exercise stress test
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient told before an exercise stress test?
opciones: Not to eat, smoke, or take caffeine or alcohol for 3 hours
Not to eat, smoke, or take caffeine or alcohol for 30 minutes
Not to drink water for 3 hours and not to eat for 12 hours
Not to take any regular medicine on the day of the test
preguntas.explicacion: Food, smoking, caffeine and alcohol are left off for three hours or more, and in most cases caffeine-like substances for 24 hours. Comfortable shoes and loose clothing are asked for, and no medicine is stopped without asking the provider first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Adjustments for blood flow · CPT D3 3F k61 k67 · PBT II.E II.F · CCMA 3E4 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: Besides the veins themselves, which working conditions are said to improve the chance of a successful puncture?
opciones: The worker's posture and position, and enough light in the room
The temperature of the tubes and the height of the sharps bin
The number of tubes on the tray and the color of the stoppers
The width of the tourniquet and the brand printed on the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Among the strategies put forward for difficult access are tapping the skin over the vein, a warm compress or a brief soak of the limb, and optimizing the operator's ergonomics, which covers the positioning of the patient and adequate ambient lighting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the bladder is very full and asks whether that matters. What is the effect?
opciones: A full bladder adds roughly 10 mm Hg, so the patient empties it before the reading
A full bladder lowers the reading by roughly 10 mm Hg through a vagal reflex
A full bladder has no measurable effect, so the reading proceeds as scheduled
A full bladder matters only in men, in whom the effect can reach 20 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: A distended bladder raises the reading by around 10 mm Hg, and figures of 10 to 15 mm Hg on both the systolic and the diastolic have been reported. Emptying the bladder is therefore part of the preparation, alongside no food or drink for 30 minutes and five minutes seated with the back supported.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications: cold packs · CPT D3 k69 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls the next day about a painful bruise at the puncture site. What first-aid advice applies to a bruise?
opciones: Ice wrapped in a towel for up to 15 minutes each hour, never directly on the skin, with the area raised above the heart
Ice placed directly on the skin for 30 minutes at a time, with the arm kept below the level of the heart
A warm compress for 15 minutes each hour and vigorous massage to disperse the pooled blood under the skin
A tight adhesive strip over the bruise for 24 hours, kept on until the color turns greenish-yellow
preguntas.explicacion: Place ice on the bruise to speed healing and reduce swelling, wrapped in a clean towel and never directly on the skin, for up to 15 minutes each hour; to hold the bruised part above heart level where that can be managed; and to rest it. It also describes the color change from pinkish red to bluish to greenish-yellow as the bruise heals. Warm compresses are a measure to raise veins before a puncture.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: A tracing looks like electrical interference, yet the wires lie straight and no equipment is running nearby. What is checked next?
opciones: The hook-up, because reversed leads can imitate that effect
The paper, because a low supply can imitate that effect
The gel, because a dried electrode can imitate that effect
The grid, because a slow paper speed can imitate that effect
preguntas.explicacion: Swapped lead wires sometimes write something that looks like alternating-current interference, so once contact and surroundings are ruled out the wiring is verified. The same reversal of the arm wires turns every complex in lead I upside down.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors (Feb. 13, 2025), Who to contact in an emergency; CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP
preguntas.subtema: PEPline · CPT D1 k24 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k96 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which resource do NIOSH and the CDC give clinicians for urgent advice on managing an occupational exposure?
opciones: The Clinicians' PEPline at 1-888-448-4911
The OSHA hotline, 1-800-321-6742
FDA MedWatch, for the device involved
The Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System
preguntas.explicacion: A worker with questions about medical treatment after an exposure is told to ring 1-888-448-4911, the Clinicians' Post Exposure Prophylaxis Line, which the National Clinician Consultation Center runs; the CDC's PEP guidance gives that same number with its hours. The OSHA hotline is for reporting severe injuries, fatalities and hospitalizations; MedWatch takes voluntary reports about device problems; and VAERS collects adverse events after vaccination, hepatitis B vaccine included.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Normal and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What range is normal for oxygen saturation on a pulse oximeter in a healthy adult?
opciones: 95% to 100%, with hypoxemia defined below 90%
90% to 100%, with hypoxemia defined below 85%
85% to 95%, with hypoxemia defined below 80%
92% to 98%, with hypoxemia defined below 88%
preguntas.explicacion: A healthy adult reads 95% to 100%, and a saturation under 90% is hypoxemia. People with a lung disease such as COPD or pneumonia, and people who live at high elevation, may sit somewhat lower and still be acceptable, which is why the reading is judged against the patient rather than against the number alone.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Providers
preguntas.subtema: Medicare eligibility verification · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is enrolling so that it can check Medicare eligibility electronically. Which of its own identifiers does the enrollment ask for?
opciones: Its PTAN and the NPI it uses to bill Medicare electronically
Its PTAN and the tax identification number of the practice
Its NPI and the Medicare number of each beneficiary checked
Its NPI and the enrollment date of every patient on its list
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment asks for the name of the person authorized to sign for the organization, an email address, the Provider Transaction Access Number, and the individual or group National Provider Identifier used to bill Medicare claims electronically, along with the dates the relationship with the vendor or clearinghouse begins and ends. A group number used for claims has to be the one used here too.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis; Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Before the scrub · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: What has to happen before a clinician begins a surgical hand antisepsis procedure?
opciones: Rings, watches and bracelets come off and the skin is inspected
The sterile gloves are opened and laid out on the sterile field
The antiseptic is poured into a basin and warmed to body heat
The nails are trimmed with the kit's clipper at the scrub sink
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation comes before the water: all jewelry, rings, watches and bracelets, is removed, and the hands and forearms are checked for cuts, abrasions or broken skin. The cap, mask, eye protection and shoe covers go on first as well, since they cannot be handled afterwards with scrubbed hands. Debris under the nails is removed with a nail cleaner under running water once the rinsing has started, and the sterile gloves go on only after the hands are dry.

preguntas.subtema: Cost of employee copies · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: An employee asks for a copy of her exposure record for the first time. What may the employer charge her?
opciones: Nothing for that first copy; a later request for another copy may be charged
A reasonable search and copying fee, since the record is the employer's own
No charge at any time, since copies of these records are free to employees
A flat administrative fee set by the employer and applied to every request
preguntas.explicacion: The employer has to hand over the copy at no cost, or lend the record so a copy can be made, or make copying facilities available free of charge. Once a record has gone out at no cost, administrative costs that are reasonable and applied without discrimination may be charged for further copies, except on a first request covering information newly added.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Carbohydrates — Side Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(a) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says a friend told him to cut carbohydrates out almost completely. What does the body do when carbohydrate is restricted that severely?
opciones: It shifts to burning fat for energy, a state called ketosis
It shifts to burning muscle protein first, a state called ketosis
It stores the fat that is eaten instead, a state called ketosis
It turns dietary fiber into glucose to keep blood levels steady
preguntas.explicacion: Cutting carbohydrate that far pushes the body into ketosis, where fat is used for energy because food is not supplying enough carbohydrate. The opposite excess matters too: too much processed, starchy or sugary carbohydrate raises total calories and can crowd out fat and protein. Fiber is never broken down for glucose.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: An insurer's letter uses the word precertification. Which term means the same thing?
opciones: Prior authorization, another name the federal glossary gives the same decision
Predetermination, the plan's estimate of the dollars it expects to pay later
Coordination of benefits, the way payers settle which of them pays first
Assignment of benefits, the patient's permission to pay the office directly
preguntas.explicacion: The federal glossary lists prior authorization, prior approval and precertification as other names for preauthorization, the plan's decision that a service is medically necessary before it is delivered. Coordination of benefits sorts out the order in which two payers pay a claim, and assignment of benefits is a form the patient signs so the plan pays the office rather than the patient.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Adult BMI Calculator: BMI Category Ranges
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: An adult patient has a body mass index of 27.4. Which category is that?
opciones: Overweight, the band from 25.0 to 29.9
Healthy weight, the band from 18.5 to 29.9
Obesity class 1, the band from 25.0 to 34.9
Underweight, which covers everything below 30.0
preguntas.explicacion: For adults of 20 and over the bands are: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 healthy weight, 25.0 to 29.9 overweight, and 30.0 or more obesity. Obesity is then split further into class 1 at 30.0 to 34.9, class 2 at 35.0 to 39.9 and class 3, also called severe obesity, at 40.0 or more.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Membrane Potentials in Cardiac Contractile Cells
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Why can heart muscle not be stimulated again right after a beat?
opciones: An absolute refractory period of about 200 ms stands in the way
An absolute refractory period of about 50 ms stands in the way
An absolute refractory period of about 500 ms stands in the way
An absolute refractory period of about 25 ms stands in the way
preguntas.explicacion: The absolute period runs about 200 ms and the relative one about 50 ms more, some 250 ms in all. That length is the point: the muscle has to finish contracting to move blood, and without it premature contractions would follow one another and life could not go on.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which vein of the antecubital fossa does the WHO describe as usually the easiest to puncture, and why is the basilic vein riskier?
opciones: The median cubital vein, which lies between muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein
The basilic vein, between the muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the median cubital vein
The cephalic vein, since it is visible with no tourniquet; the basilic is where veins are diverting
Whichever vein already has a peripheral venous access in place; the basilic is too deep to reach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 of the guideline singles out the median cubital vein: it sits between muscles and is usually the easiest to puncture. The basilic vein has an artery and a nerve running beneath it, so a puncture there risks damaging one of them and tends to hurt more; swapping the two veins reverses the guideline. The same step warns against putting the needle in where veins branch, because that raises the chance of a hematoma, but it does not say that of the basilic vein, and it does not single out the cephalic vein at all. And in hospitalized patients it says NOT to draw from an existing peripheral venous access, because the result may be false.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Claim
preguntas.subtema: Claims and revenue cycle · CCMA 5L k181 · CMA III.G.3.b · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 6C k89 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: After a visit, the office sends the insurer a request for payment for the services provided. What is that request called?
opciones: A claim
A copay
A referral
A denial
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a claim as the request for payment that the patient or the provider sends to the insurer for items or services believed to be covered. It comes AFTER the care. A copay is the fixed amount the patient pays for a covered service, a referral is the primary care doctor's written order to see a specialist, and a denial is an answer the plan gives, not a request the office sends.

preguntas.subtema: Calibration per the manufacturer · CPT D1 k27 · PBT IV.B.2 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: At what frequency does CLIA require a laboratory to calibrate a test system?
opciones: Following the manufacturer's instructions, at least as often as the manufacturer recommends
Once every 6 months, using the same three-level materials that calibration verification uses
Every day that patient specimens are assayed, before the first control material is run
Whenever a newly trained operator begins to run patient testing on the instrument
preguntas.explicacion: Calibration follows whatever instructions the manufacturer gives for the test system, with the calibration materials it provides or specifies and at least as often as it recommends, against criteria the laboratory has verified. It is repeated too whenever calibration verification falls outside the laboratory's acceptable limits. The 6-month cycle is for verification, and daily runs and new operators are quality control triggers.

preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(1) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must appear on a written consent to disclose substance use disorder records?
opciones: A description of each purpose for which the disclosure is being made
A notarized signature witnessed by two members of the program staff
A statement that the consent cannot be revoked before it expires
A copy of the recipient's own privacy notice attached to the form
preguntas.explicacion: The written consent, on paper or electronic, must carry the patient's name, who is authorized to disclose, a specific description of the information, the recipient, a description of each purpose, how the patient may revoke it, an expiration date or event, the signature and the date. Revocation is a required element, not something the form can waive.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Managed Care: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which managed care plan lets the member choose between the HMO and the PPO arrangement each time care is needed?
opciones: A point-of-service plan, which keeps the choice open at each visit
A preferred provider organization, which pays more inside the network
A health maintenance organization, which pays for network care only
An accountable care organization, which shares the savings it earns
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of managed care plan are named. A health maintenance organization usually pays only for network care and asks the member to pick a primary care doctor. A preferred provider organization usually pays more inside the network and still covers part of the cost outside it. A point-of-service plan lets the member choose between an HMO and a PPO each time care is needed.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: tort (Distinguishing Torts)
preguntas.subtema: Civil and criminal acts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4 · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does a tort differ from a crime?
opciones: A tort is a private wrong and aims to compensate; a crime wrongs society
A tort is heard by a jury and a crime is decided by a judge alone
A tort applies to institutions and a crime applies only to individuals
A tort is defined by state statute and a crime only by federal statute
preguntas.explicacion: A crime is a wrong against the state, or against society at large, and criminal liability exists to enforce public justice. Tort law deals with private wrongs, and its central purpose is to compensate the victim rather than to punish the wrongdoer. The same act can be both: gross negligence endangering other people's lives can be a tort and a crime at once.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Head circumference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A baby's head circumference is growing much faster than expected. Why does the provider follow it up?
opciones: Faster than normal head growth can be a sign of problems such as fluid on the brain
Faster than normal head growth is the earliest sign that the child is overweight
Faster than normal head growth is expected only in children born after 40 weeks
Faster than normal head growth is measured only to fix the size of a helmet later
preguntas.explicacion: A head larger than normal or growing faster than normal can point to several problems, hydrocephalus among them, while a very small head or very slow growth may mean the brain is not developing as it should. That is why the measurement belongs to routine well-baby care rather than being taken only when something looks wrong.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.5
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · CPT D3 k55 · D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.C · CCMA 3E4 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which categories of blood sampling are singled out as requiring specialist training?
opciones: Arterial gases on ventilated patients, neonatal sampling and capillary sampling
Routine adult venous draws, cross-match sampling and coagulation sampling
Arterial gases on ventilated patients, adult venous draws and donor collection
Neonatal sampling, adult venous draws and blood collection for transfusion
preguntas.explicacion: Most sampling is done for ordinary laboratory testing, but three categories are listed as needing specialist training: arterial blood gases in patients on mechanical ventilation, neonatal and pediatric sampling by heel-prick or scalp vein, and capillary sampling at any age.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks how a filled additive tube should be moved to mix it. Which pattern is described?
opciones: Inverting the tube in a figure-of-8 pattern
Inverting it until the blood froths in the tube
Shaking the tube eight to ten times in a row
Inverting it once and standing it in the rack
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant need enough mixing, and the movement described is inversion following a figure-of-8. Overmixing can produce hemolysis and inefficient mixing leaves small clots, so neither brisk shaking nor a single inversion serves. Eight to ten mixes is the figure given for culture bottles.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): how long are they effective?; What kind of fees?; CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005): Renew the CW every 2 years
preguntas.subtema: Two-year certificate and fee · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: How long is a CLIA Certificate of Waiver effective, and what must the site do to keep it?
opciones: Two years; pay the waiver fee and renew every two years
One year; pay the waiver fee and renew every year
Five years; renew after a routine survey by the state agency
Indefinitely, as long as ownership does not change
preguntas.explicacion: All CLIA certificate types are generally effective for two years. A site with a Certificate of Waiver or a PPM certificate pays only a waiver or PPM fee on that two-year cycle, with no registration or compliance survey fees. Renewal does not depend on an inspection, because waived sites are not subject to routine surveys, but the certificate must be kept current.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Snellen Chart", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(10)(b)(ii) · RMA III.F.5.c · NCMA 2B.8
preguntas.pregunta: A result is recorded as 20/40. What does the lower number mean?
opciones: The distance at which normal eyes read that same smallest line
The distance in feet at which the patient was standing from the chart
The number of letters the patient managed to read on that line
The percentage of normal vision the patient retains in that eye
preguntas.explicacion: The top number is how far the patient stood, in feet, and the bottom number is how far away someone with normal sight could still read the smallest line the patient could read. So 20/40 means at 20 feet the patient sees what a normal eye sees at 40. Letters at the 20/40 size are twice as large as those on the 20/20 line.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: QT Interval
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A strip is measured and the QT comes to 420 ms. How is the normal QT interval stated?
opciones: As a ceiling: under 400 to 440 ms, women slightly longer than men
As a ceiling: under 200 to 240 ms, women slightly longer than men
As a closed band: 400 to 440 ms, women slightly longer than men
As a closed band: 120 to 200 ms, women slightly longer than men
