preguntas.explicacion: The QT interval runs from the start of ventricular depolarization to the end of repolarization, and normal is stated as a ceiling rather than a band: under 400 to 440 ms. A shorter value is not abnormal for that reason alone, and the corrected interval is called prolonged above 440 ms in men and above 460 ms in women. It shortens as the rate rises, and a long QT raises the risk of dangerous ventricular rhythms; 120 to 200 ms is the PR range and 80 to 120 ms the ST segment.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 6: Inject Vaccines Rapidly Without Aspiration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(1) · RMA III.G.2.i · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC say that aspiration is not needed before a vaccine is injected?
opciones: The vessels near the recommended sites are too small to take a push of vaccine
The vaccine does no harm if it enters a vein, so the check adds no safety here
Aspiration is skipped only when the site chosen for the vaccine is the deltoid
Aspiration is replaced by injecting slowly, which does the same job more gently
preguntas.explicacion: Aspiration was recommended for theoretical reasons at the start and has never been evaluated scientifically. At the sites used for vaccination the veins and arteries a needle can reach are so small that an intravenous push would blow the vessel out. Aspirating also adds pain, through longer needle dwell time and the shearing of tissue; injecting rapidly without it hurt infants less in one study.

preguntas.subtema: Copy of the authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signs an authorization at the desk so her records can go to her attorney. What does the practice owe her before she leaves?
opciones: A copy of the authorization she has just signed
A log of every disclosure the form will produce
A written estimate of the copying fee she will owe
A receipt showing the date the records were sent
preguntas.explicacion: When it is the covered entity that asks the individual for an authorization, the individual has to be handed a copy of the form she signed. The entity documents and keeps the signed authorization as well. The form is written in plain language and warns that information released under it may be passed on again and lose the rule's protection.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 k6 (applied D3 3I) · PBT I.B.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the blood filling the tube is dark red rather than bright red. What does that color indicate?
opciones: Venous blood carrying deoxyhemoglobin, which is a darker red
Arterial blood carrying oxyhemoglobin, which is bright red
Hemolyzed blood in which hemoglobin has left the red cells
Blood with a high hematocrit from living at high altitude
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin is a pigment whose color depends on oxygen: freshly oxygenated blood is bright red, and blood that has given up oxygen in the tissues is a duskier, darker red. Oxyhemoglobin is the bright red form and deoxyhemoglobin the darker form. Dark red is therefore the expected color of venous blood, not a sign of hemolysis or of a high hematocrit.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Proficiency Testing · RMA III.C.1.a.iii proficiency testing
preguntas.pregunta: A proficiency testing shipment arrives and the supervisor asks the most experienced technologist to stay late and run the samples twice. What is wrong with that plan?
opciones: PT samples go through the routine workload, with the staff who normally test, the usual number of times
PT samples go to the laboratory director in person, who then attests that each reported value is right
PT samples are run twice as often as patient samples so the value reported is the mean of both runs
PT samples are run before any patient specimen that day so the analyzer matches the program's timing
preguntas.explicacion: PT samples get examined exactly as patient specimens are: worked into the regular patient workload, run by the staff who do that testing day in day out, with the laboratory's routine methods, and tested as many times as a patient sample would be. Both the analyst and the laboratory director attest to that routine integration; the director does not take over the bench.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Retractable Sharp
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A retractable safety needle is activated after the draw. What has to be true of the sharp afterwards?
opciones: It ends up drawn completely back inside the body of the device
It is fully covered by a cap held on with adhesive tape
It is bent back on itself so it cannot be straightened
It is left partly visible so the worker can confirm it fired
preguntas.explicacion: For a retractable design the recommendation is that the sharp ends up fully retracted inside the housing. That sits alongside two rules for every design: the user should be able to tell easily that the feature has fired, and once fired it cannot be undone and stays protective through disposal.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, "Communicating With and About People with Disabilities", People-first language
preguntas.subtema: Person-first language · CCMA 6B k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is charting about a patient who gets around in a wheelchair. Which phrasing follows people-first language?
opciones: A person who uses a wheelchair
A wheelchair-bound patient
A person confined to a wheelchair
A handicapped person in a wheelchair
preguntas.explicacion: People-first language puts the person ahead of the disability, using constructions such as a person who or a person with, and it promotes understanding, dignity and respect. Wheelchair bound and confined to a wheelchair stress the limitation, and handicapped sits in the do-not-use column.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture (003751), How to Prepare for the Test; and Clean catch urine sample (007487), How the Test is Performed; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia — Urine culture - catheterized specimen (artículo 003752) (003752)
preguntas.subtema: Bladder dwell time · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: Ideally, how long should urine have been held in the bladder before a clean-catch sample for culture is collected?
opciones: About 2 to 3 hours
At least 1 hour
At least 8 hours
About 15 to 20 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Both the clean-catch instructions and the urine culture instructions ask, when possible, for urine that has been in the bladder for 2 to 3 hours. One hour is the minimum wait before a catheterized specimen or a urethral swab, and 15 to 20 minutes is how long before a catheterization a patient may be told to drink a glass of water if there is no urge to void. An eight-hour hold appears in neither set of instructions.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Auto-disable syringes
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Two further drawbacks are listed for auto-disable syringes in a blood-drawing context. Which are they?
opciones: The mechanism can trip while probing, and air in the syringe alters results
The mechanism cannot be reset, and the needle is too short for adult veins
The mechanism can trip while probing, and the barrel cannot hold two tubes
The mechanism jams when cold, and air in the syringe dilutes the additive
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond the fact that this device is designed against reuse rather than against needle-sticks, the table warns that the safety mechanism can be activated while the worker is probing, forcing a fresh venepuncture, and that air in the syringe can affect test results. It also needs extra training.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Procedure
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.c.i · CCMA 3B3 k64 · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given a guaiac card kit for occult blood at home. How are the samples taken?
opciones: From several areas of the stool, repeated on three separate days
From one area of a single stool, repeated only if the result is positive
From several areas of the stool, all taken from one bowel movement
From the toilet water below the stool, on three consecutive mornings
preguntas.explicacion: Bleeding into the gut is intermittent and blood is not spread evenly through stool, so the sample is taken from more than one spot and the collection repeated over three separate days. The stool must not touch toilet water first, because hemoglobin leaches out of it and bowl sanitizers interfere. Dried cards keep at room temperature for up to 14 days.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Competency Assessment · RMA III.C.1.a.i training
preguntas.pregunta: What does CLIA require a laboratory to have in place for competency assessment itself?
opciones: Written policies and procedures, established and followed, to assess employee and consultant competency
A signed job description for every employee, kept in the personnel file for the length of employment
An annual written examination for every employee, scored by the laboratory director in person
A training log listing each in-service session, made available to any client that asks for it
preguntas.explicacion: The competency standard is short and blunt: the laboratory establishes written policies and procedures to assess the competency of employees and, where applicable, consultants, and then follows them. The personnel subpart supplies the detail of who is assessed and how often; the quality systems subpart supplies the obligation to have it in writing.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Somatosensation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a general sense rather than a special sense?
opciones: Somatosensation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Gustation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Olfaction, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Equilibrium, whose receptors are spread through many organs
preguntas.explicacion: The special senses each have their own organ: taste, smell, hearing, balance and vision. Somatosensation is a general sense instead, a group of modalities including pressure, vibration, light touch, temperature, pain and proprioception, and its receptors sit in skin, muscles, tendons, joints and the walls of the viscera.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Sims Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(6) · RMA III.F.2.a.i · NCMA 2B.9
preguntas.pregunta: An enema is about to be given. Which description matches the position asked for?
opciones: Halfway between supine and prone, legs flexed and a pillow under the top leg
Flat on the back with a small pillow supporting the head and both of the knees
Sitting up with the head of the bed raised and the hips slightly flexed
On one side with the top leg crossed over the bottom one and arms forward
preguntas.explicacion: Sims is the side-lying position placed between supine and prone: the legs are flexed, a pillow goes under the upper leg, and the arms rest beside the patient rather than trapped underneath. It is the position used for an enema and it also serves for anal procedures. Plain lateral, by contrast, keeps the top leg simply flexed over the bottom one.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection and tourniquet · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO procedure, at what point is the tourniquet applied in relation to finding the vein?
opciones: After a vein is located that is visible without it; it is then applied and the vein re-examined
Before looking for any vein, so that all the veins stay engorged during the whole of the inspection
Only if no vein is visible after the site has been disinfected and allowed to dry
Immediately after the needle enters, to keep the vein distended while the tubes fill
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says the vein should be visible before the tourniquet goes on, that finding it helps decide the needle size, and that the tourniquet is then applied four to five finger widths above the site and the vein examined again. Disinfection is Step 5 and comes after the site is chosen; and the tourniquet is in place before the needle enters, not applied afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: After the Visit, Vaccine and Supply Disposal; Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.j · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A vaccine has just been administered. Where do the used syringe and the empty vial go?
opciones: The syringe into a sharps container; the vial into medical waste per state rules
Both into the sharps container, since the vial held a parenteral product as well
The syringe into a sharps container; the vial into the ordinary office wastebasket
Both into medical waste, once the needle has been recapped and taken off the barrel
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe and needle go straight into a sharps container with the safety shield applied and without recapping, because recapping is how needlestick injuries happen. Empty or expired vaccine vials count as medical waste, and each state's own regulations govern how they are discarded, with the state or local immunization program or environmental agency giving any further guidance.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Fees for Copies
preguntas.subtema: Access fees · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which cost may a practice include in the fee it charges a patient for a copy of her record?
opciones: The labor of copying the information, plus postage when she asks to have it mailed
The time staff spend searching for and retrieving the chart from the storage room
The share of the electronic system's annual license attributable to storing her data
The cost of verifying her identity and documenting the request in the practice log
preguntas.explicacion: The fee has to be reasonable and cost based, and only four components may go into it: labor for copying, whether on paper or electronically; supplies such as a CD or USB drive if portable media are requested; postage where the copy is mailed; and preparing an explanation or summary if the patient agreed to one. Verification, documentation, search and retrieval, and system maintenance may not be charged, even where state law allows it.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(a)(1)-(4), Standard: Access to protected health information
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to access · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which information is excluded from the HIPAA right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a legal proceeding
Laboratory results, which belong to the ordering physician until released
Billing records, which are financial rather than clinical
Records older than 6 years, which need not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access in 164.524(a)(1) covers PHI in a designated record set for as long as it is kept, with two exceptions: psychotherapy notes, and anything assembled in reasonable anticipation of a legal action, civil, criminal or administrative, or for use in one. Access may also be denied without review in limited cases such as certain correctional and research situations, and with a right to review where a licensed professional judges that access is likely to endanger someone. Laboratory and billing records are part of the designated record set and stay accessible.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Health Information Privacy and Control
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is listed as an exception to a patient's confidentiality rights?
opciones: Sharing what is needed to head off imminent danger to someone
Sharing a diagnosis with a coworker who asks out of concern
Sharing a chart with a relative who is not involved in the care
Sharing a record with a magazine once the name is left out
preguntas.explicacion: The exceptions are named and narrow: sharing inside the organization, or with its business partners, for reasons of medical care, revenue, quality or risk management; heading off imminent physical danger to the patient or to somebody else; helping a criminal investigation when a law official demands it; protecting public health, which is why certain infections are reportable; and dealing with a surrogate when the patient has no legal capacity to decide. A colleague asking out of concern is not on that list.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: During the Visit, Needle Length
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(1) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Where does an intramuscular vaccine go in a 4-month-old infant, and with which needle?
opciones: Vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh, with a 1-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle
Vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh, with a 5/8-inch 23 to 25 gauge needle
Deltoid muscle of the arm, with a 5/8-inch to 1-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle
Ventrogluteal site, with a 1 to 1.25-inch 22 to 25 gauge needle, thigh in reserve
preguntas.explicacion: For infants from 1 to 12 months the intramuscular site is the vastus lateralis of the anterolateral thigh and the needle is 1 inch, 22 to 25 gauge. A neonate of 28 days or younger takes five eighths of an inch at the same site. The deltoid becomes the preferred site from 3 years onward, and 5/8 of an inch with 23 to 25 gauge is the subcutaneous needle at every age.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, ABO Transfusion Protocols
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In an acute hemorrhage with no time to cross match, type O negative blood is transfused. Why is O negative called the universal donor?
opciones: Its cells lack A, B and Rh D antigens, so recipient antibodies do not react
Its plasma lacks anti-A and anti-B, so it cannot agglutinate any cells
Its cells carry both A antigen and B antigen, matching every recipient
It is the most common type, so it is the one always kept in stock
preguntas.explicacion: Type O erythrocytes display neither A nor B antigen, so the anti-A or anti-B antibodies in the recipient's plasma find nothing on the donated cells to attack, and Rh negative cells also lack the D antigen. One caution: type O plasma does carry anti-A and anti-B, but the transfused volume is small compared with the recipient's own blood, so the effect is usually limited.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(i), Housekeeping: General
preguntas.subtema: Written cleaning schedule · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.4 III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: What must the employer's written cleaning and decontamination schedule take into account?
opciones: The location, the kind of surface, the soil present, and the tasks done there
The brand of disinfectant and the date its container was first opened
The number of employees on each shift and the dates of their training
The volume of regulated waste the area produced during the past year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(i) makes the employer keep the worksite clean and sanitary, and then requires a written schedule for cleaning and a method of decontamination decided from four things: where in the facility the area is, what kind of surface has to be cleaned, what kind of soil is on it, and which tasks or procedures are performed there. A draw room and a storage corridor therefore do not get the same schedule. Disinfectant brands, staffing and waste volume are not the criteria the paragraph names.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.3, Order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw, capillary vs venous · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.H.2 · CCMA 3E6 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO describe the order of draw for skin-puncture (capillary) specimens compared with venipuncture?
opciones: It is the reverse: hematology first, then chemistry and blood bank
It is the same: culture first, then coagulation, then the additive tubes
It is the reverse: chemistry and blood bank first, then hematology
It has no fixed order, because microtubes hold too little for carry-over
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.3 says that in a skin puncture the hematology specimen goes first, followed by chemistry and blood bank, and that this is the reverse of the venipuncture order. The reason given is to limit the effect of platelet clumping. The same section adds that when more than two specimens are needed, venipuncture may give more accurate results.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Safe blood-sampling equipment, Tourniquet
preguntas.subtema: Cleaning the tourniquet · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k104 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reuses the same elastic tourniquet all morning without cleaning it. Why is that a problem?
opciones: Tourniquets have been found carrying hospital-acquired bacteria
Tourniquets lose their elasticity after several patients in a row
Tourniquets absorb the alcohol used to prepare the puncture site
Tourniquets have to be discarded after each patient is finished
preguntas.explicacion: Best practice for the tourniquet is a clean elastic band reprocessed between patients, and the reason is blunt: tourniquets have been documented carrying nosocomial bacteria, so one that travels from arm to arm carries them along. The related warning in the same table is that a latex glove must never stand in as a tourniquet for a patient who reports a history of latex allergy.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee reviews a one-year audit of an emergency laboratory that received 453,171 specimens. Which test group carried the highest rejection ratio?
opciones: Coagulation testing, rejected at about 13 % of what arrived
Blood gas analyses, rejected at about 10 % of everything arriving
Urine analyses, rejected at about 9 % of what arrived
Biochemistry testing, rejected at about 3 % of what arrived
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation led that audit at 13.3 %, with therapeutic drug monitoring close behind at 12.8 % and hormone testing around 12 %. Blood gases reached 9.8 % and urine 9.2 %, while biochemistry at 2.5 % and the complete blood count at 3.2 % were the least affected. Coagulation suffers most because red cell clots and a wrong blood-to-anticoagulant ratio are exactly what ruin a citrate tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Piaget", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A nine-month-old lifts a cloth to find the toy hidden under it. Which achievement is that?
opciones: Object permanence, which closes the sensorimotor period
Conservation, an achievement of the concrete operations
Semiotic function, the mark of the preoperational period
Hypothetical thought, which belongs to formal operations
preguntas.explicacion: The sensorimotor period runs from birth through the first 18 to 24 months and culminates in object permanence: knowing that objects exist apart from the child's own contact with them. Recovering a hidden toy, or knowing a parent still exists after leaving the room, are the classic examples.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 2.4 Staining Microscopic Specimens, Preparing Specimens for Light Microscopy
preguntas.subtema: Wet mount versus fixation · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.e-f (8.e desde 2027) · RMA III.B.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: How is a wet mount prepared, and how does it differ from a fixed preparation?
opciones: The specimen goes into a drop of liquid under a coverslip and stays alive, while fixing kills it
The specimen goes into a drop of liquid under a coverslip and is killed, while fixing keeps it alive
The specimen is smeared and heated, then a coverslip is added over a drop of immersion oil
The specimen is placed dry on the slide and a coverslip holds it down without any liquid
preguntas.explicacion: A wet mount is the simplest preparation: the specimen sits in a drop of liquid, water or a stain, with a coverslip on top. Something like a drop of urine is liquid already; a solid such as a skin scraping goes down first and the liquid after. Fixing, by heat or by a chemical such as formalin, sticks the cells to the slide and kills the organisms while their structures are preserved.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which reading is usually described as hypotension in an adult?
opciones: Under 90 systolic or under 60 diastolic, read together with the symptoms
Under 100 systolic or under 70 diastolic, read together with the symptoms
Under 120 systolic or under 80 diastolic, which is the lower limit of normal
Under 80 systolic alone, since the diastolic value carries no weight here
preguntas.explicacion: There is no universal cut-off, but clinicians commonly speak of hypotension below 90 systolic or below 60 diastolic. The diagnosis leans on the context and on the symptoms: feeling weak, feeling sick, seeing blurred, feeling dizzy or light-headed. Dehydration, acute illness and medicines are the usual causes.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Compared with the rest of health care, how well does the analytical phase of a clinical laboratory perform?
opciones: It performs close to 5 sigma, an error rate of about 0.002 %, among the best sectors in health care
It performs at 1 to 2 sigma, roughly the same level as health care as a whole
It produces four to five times more errors than the pre-analytical and post-analytical phases combined
It accounts for 46 to 68 % of all laboratory errors because of instrument malfunction
preguntas.explicacion: The analytical work of the laboratory reaches nearly 5 sigma, about 0.002 %, more than 3,000 times lower than infection and medication error rates, which is why it is called the best-performing sector in health care; health care overall sits at 1 to 2 sigma. It is the extra-analytical phases that carry four to five times more errors, and the 46 to 68 % share belongs to the pre-pre-analytical phase.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.10 Checklist for Intermittent Suture Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through a suture removal the wound edges begin to gape. What is done?
opciones: Stop removing, apply Steri-Strips to pull the edges together, and notify the provider
Remove the rest quickly, since a partly sutured line pulls unevenly on the wound edges
Stop removing, cover the line with a dry sterile dressing, and reassess in seven days
Remove the rest and close the gap with a skin adhesive, then dress the line as usual
preguntas.explicacion: Open edges mean the removal stops there. Steri-Strips are cut and applied with tension so they draw the edges back together, and the provider is notified. The wound line is watched for separation the whole time the sutures are coming out, and the procedure is halted at any concern, because dehiscence is what removing them too early causes.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Right Patient
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which identifiers are acceptable for confirming the right patient before a medication is administered?
opciones: The full name, the date of birth, or the identification number the facility assigns
The room number and the bed letter, both of which the chart lists on admission
The full name on its own, since two patients never share a name on one unit
The barcode scan on its own, which was brought in to replace two identifiers
preguntas.explicacion: Acceptable identifiers are the full name, the date of birth, and the number the facility assigns to the patient, checked against the wristband, an identification card, what the patient says when they can say it, or another method the policy allows. A room number is never used, because patients move. Barcode scanning adds a layer of safety but does not replace the requirement for two identifiers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature a
preguntas.pregunta: A digital thermometer has just been used on one patient and is picked up for the next. What has to happen before that second reading?
opciones: The device is reset to a value below 35 °C (95 °F) before the new measurement
The device is left to cool for five minutes so the sensor returns to room level
The device is calibrated against a glass thermometer at least once every shift
The device is switched to the rectal setting, which resets the display to zero
preguntas.explicacion: A digital thermometer holds the last value it read. Before each new measurement it is reset below 35 °C (95 °F), otherwise the retained figure can be mistaken for the new patient's temperature. Waiting for the sensor to cool is not the instruction, and these devices are not calibrated against a glass probe at the bedside.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Goniometer", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.c · RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62
preguntas.pregunta: Which part of a universal goniometer is laid over the joint together with the body and can be tightened to hold the moving arm still?
opciones: The fulcrum, the screw at the center of the body of the instrument
The stationary arm, which lines up with the fixed part of the joint
The moving arm, which lines up with the part of the joint that moves
The scale of the body, which is read once both arms are lined up
preguntas.explicacion: A universal goniometer comes in three parts: a body shaped like a protractor and carrying the scale, a fulcrum, and the two arms. The fulcrum is a screw in the middle of the body; tightening it fixes the moving arm in one position and loosening it lets the arm swing. It is the fulcrum and the body that go over the joint.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Storage
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How far from the floor, the ceiling and the outside walls should sterile supplies be stored?
opciones: 8 to 10 inches from the floor, 5 from the ceiling and 2 from the outside walls
2 to 4 inches from the floor, 8 from the ceiling and 5 from the outside walls
12 to 18 inches from the floor, 2 from the ceiling and 8 from the outside walls
5 to 8 inches from the floor, 18 from the ceiling and 10 from the outside walls
preguntas.explicacion: The clearances exist for air circulation, ease of cleaning and local fire codes: 8 to 10 inches up from the floor, 5 inches down from the ceiling and 2 inches away from outside walls, with supplies kept at least 18 inches below any sprinkler head. Twelve to eighteen inches is the separation used for furniture from the walls when a sterile field is being set up.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician cannot find a pulse on the top of a patient's foot but finds every other pulse. What is one explanation?
opciones: That pulse is missing in roughly 10% of people because of anatomical variation
That pulse is missing in roughly 10% of people because of arterial stiffening with age
That pulse is felt only while the patient holds the first toe fully extended
That pulse disappears whenever systolic pressure falls below 100 mm Hg in the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The dorsalis pedis lies on the front of the foot, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus, and it is absent in about 10% of people for anatomical reasons. Asking the patient to extend the big toe lifts the tendon and helps find it when it is there. When pedal pulses are felt on both sides, peripheral arterial disease is unlikely.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k150 k151 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: A woman has pendulous breast tissue sitting over the V4 landmark. What is done?
opciones: The electrode goes on its landmark, even on top of the breast
The electrode goes below the breast, off its usual landmark
The breast is taped upward so the electrode sits on the wall
The electrode is left off and the tracing runs on five leads
preguntas.explicacion: The breasts are allowed to fall naturally, and the chest electrodes are placed on their landmarks even when that means placing one over breast tissue: correct position counts for more than closeness to the chest wall. The patient must stay very still so the tissue does not shift the electrode.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (tourniquet application)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: About how far above the intended puncture site is the tourniquet applied, measured in inches?
opciones: About 3 inches above the site
About 1 inch above the site
About 6 inches above the puncture site
About 2 cm above the site
preguntas.explicacion: A preferably disposable tourniquet goes almost 3 inches above the targeted venipuncture site, tight enough to stop venous flow while arterial flow continues. The WHO expresses the same distance as four to five finger widths. Two centimeters is the minimum area the alcohol swab must cover in the WHO's Step 5, not a tourniquet distance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Exercise stress test
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: When does an exercise stress test come to an end?
opciones: At the target rate, or on symptoms or worrying tracing changes
At the target rate alone, no matter what the patient reports
After a fixed 20 minutes on the treadmill in every case
When the systolic pressure has climbed by 10 mm Hg or more
preguntas.explicacion: The test runs until the target heart rate is reached, or until chest pain or a worrying blood pressure change appears, or the tracing suggests the heart muscle is short of oxygen, or the patient is too tired or has leg pain. A rising pressure with each stage is the expected response, not a reason to stop.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Alcohol: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: At what concentration in water are ethyl and isopropyl alcohol most bactericidal?
opciones: 60 to 90 percent
30 to 50 percent
95 to 100 percent
40 to 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohols work by denaturing protein, and protein denatures faster with water present, so absolute alcohol is weaker than a mixture. The optimum band runs from 60 to 90 percent in water, and cidal activity drops sharply once the solution is diluted below 50 percent. They kill bacteria fast, and fungi, viruses and the tubercle bacillus too, but never spores.

preguntas.fuente: 21 CFR 884.4530(a)(12); and StatPearls, "Intrauterine Device Placement and Removal", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · CCMA 3B4 k63
preguntas.pregunta: An IUD is about to be placed. The tray holds a speculum, a tenaculum, a sterile uterine sound and long-handled scissors. What is the sound there for?
opciones: To find how deep the uterine cavity runs before the device goes in
To hold the cervix still while the device is pushed through the os
To open the cervical canal step by step until the device will pass
To scrape a sample of the lining out and send it to the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The sound is passed into the uterine cavity to determine its depth. Steadying the cervix is the job of the tenaculum lying on the same tray, opening the canal belongs to a set of dilators, and scraping the lining out is what a curette does.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Commonly Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: Assistance at the visit · CCMA 4 k157 · CMA II.F.1.c(4) / 2027 II.F.1.d(1) · RMA I.D.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Booking a patient who uses a wheelchair, a receptionist tells her to bring somebody along who can help her onto the table. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, she may come alone and the practice provides the assistance she needs
No, unless the office has no lift and no member of staff trained to transfer
Yes, so long as the same is asked of every patient who uses a wheelchair
Yes, because helping a patient undress falls outside a receptionist's duties
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may bring a friend or relative if she wishes, but she may equally come by herself, and the provider then gives the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help with dressing, with getting on and off the table, with positioning, and with staying balanced once there. The staff member asks the patient what help she wants and how.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k9
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair correctly matches an everyday word with the root used for the same structure?
opciones: Windpipe with trache-, and voice box with laryng-
Windpipe with laryng-, and voice box with trache-
Windpipe with pharyng-, and voice box with bronch-
Windpipe with bronch-, and voice box with pharyng-
preguntas.explicacion: The trachea is the windpipe and the larynx is the voice box, so trache- and laryng- go with those plain words. The other two roots name neighbors along the same route: pharyng- is the throat, and bronch- the large airway that leads from the trachea into a lung.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Prefilled Syringes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.h(iv)
preguntas.pregunta: What advantage does a prefilled syringe give over drawing the dose from a vial?
opciones: A premeasured dose, less waste, and less chance of an inadvertent needlestick
A premeasured dose that staff can adjust at the bedside to any ordered amount
A filter inside the hub that holds back glass particles from the drawn dose
A gauge and a length that suit every route, so no needle is ever exchanged
preguntas.explicacion: Prefilled syringes cut the risk of an inadvertent needlestick and of exposure to toxic products, both of which come with withdrawing medication from vials. Because the dose is already measured, they also reduce dosing errors and waste, and they are particularly useful in urgent situations that call for rapid administration. The filter belongs to the blunt fill needle used with an ampule.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Reasons for Termination
preguntas.subtema: Why patients are dismissed · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: In the review of 536 formal terminations, which cause came second after repeated no-shows, and how large was it?
opciones: Disrespectful or disruptive behavior, at 22 % of the cases reviewed
Self-termination by the patient, at 22 % of the cases reviewed
Nonadherence with the treatment plan, at 15 % of the cases reviewed
Violation of an opioid agreement, at 15 % of the cases reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Repeated appointment no-shows headed the list at 38 %. Disrespectful or disruptive behavior came next at 22 %, then so-called self-termination at 15 %, violating an opioid contract at 4 %, non-adherence with treatment plans at 3 %, and illegal behavior such as altering a written prescription at 2 %.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Two terms sit side by side in one report: arteriosclerosis and stenosis. Which contrast between those endings is correct?
opciones: The first names a hardening and the second a narrowing or blockage
The first names a narrowing and the second a hardening or stiffening
The first names a hardening and the second an expansion or dilation
The first names a blockage and the second a softening or weakening
preguntas.explicacion: Sclera- and sclero- mean hardness, and -sclerosis is a hardening; on the artery root that gives hardened arteries. Sten- and steno- mean narrowed or blocked. Two more parts fall into that space and mean the opposite or something else: -ectasis is an expansion or dilation, and -malacia is a softening.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starts breathing again during CPR while the office waits for the ambulance. What is done next?
opciones: Roll the patient onto one side and keep watching the breathing
Sit the patient upright in a chair and offer small sips of water
Keep the patient flat on the back and raise the legs about 12 inches (30 cm)
Resume compressions at once, since breathing after a code is agonal
preguntas.explicacion: Once breathing returns, the patient is rolled onto one side with the lower arm supporting the head and the upper knee bent to a right angle, and breathing is rechecked until help arrives. Raising the legs about 12 inches belongs to shock and fainting, and compressions on someone who is breathing, coughing or moving can stop the heart.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.10
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for a scar left by a burn two years ago. How is that coded?
opciones: With two codes, the residual condition first and the sequela code second
With two codes, the sequela code first and the residual condition second
With one code only, since a sequela is a combination code by definition
With no sequela code, because more than a year has passed since the burn
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is what remains once the acute phase of an illness or an injury is over, and the examples given include a scar from a burn, a deviated septum following a nasal fracture, and infertility after old tuberculosis. Coding one usually takes two codes: the condition or nature of the residual goes first, the sequela code second. No time limit applies.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans and patient cost · CMAA 5C k76, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Under Original Medicare in 2026, what does a patient generally pay for a covered Part B service after the yearly deductible?
opciones: 20% of the Medicare-approved amount, when the provider accepts assignment
20% of the provider's own charge, which may sit above the approved amount
A fixed copayment of $20 for each service, set by the Medicare fee schedule
A share of 20% for equipment only, since visits are paid in full by Part B
preguntas.explicacion: Part B coinsurance is usually 20% of the Medicare-approved amount for each covered service or item once the yearly deductible, $283 in 2026, has been paid, and it applies when the provider accepts the approved amount as full payment. The share is figured on that approved amount, not on the provider's own charge; it is not limited to equipment, since doctor visits carry the same 20%; and Part B has no single fixed copayment per service.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Incision and Drainage", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.B.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument is used for blunt dissection after the abscess is opened during an incision and drainage?
opciones: A curved hemostat, worked inside the cavity to break up the loculations
A staple extractor, worked inside the cavity to lift the cavity wall apart
A periosteal elevator, worked inside the cavity to strip the lining free
A needle holder, worked inside the cavity to spread the deeper pockets open
preguntas.explicacion: The incision is made with the scalpel straight over the center of the abscess and parallel to skin tension lines, until pus comes out; then a curved hemostat is used for blunt dissection to break up the loculations inside. Copious irrigation with sterile normal saline follows, and the wound is left to close by secondary intention.

preguntas.subtema: Header of the notice · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is laying out its notice of privacy practices. What has to sit at the top of the page as a header, or otherwise be displayed prominently?
opciones: A statement that the notice covers how the patient's information is used, shared and reached
A statement that the practice is a covered entity subject to federal privacy enforcement
A statement that the patient consents to treatment, to payment and to operations
A statement of the date the notice takes effect and the officer who approved its wording
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation prescribes a header telling the reader that the document describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking that it be reviewed carefully. The effective date is required too, but it is not the header; the whole notice has to be in plain language.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1; and Annex C, Table C.1
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3D k9 k55 · PBT II.J II.I · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor reviews hemolyzed samples from a children's clinic. Which two examples of too great a vacuum are given?
opciones: An oversized tube on a child, or a syringe of ten to twenty milliliters
An oversized tube on an adult, or a syringe of one to two milliliters
A reduced-vacuum pediatric tube, or a syringe of two to five milliliters
A butterfly set on an adult, or a syringe of ten to twenty milliliters
preguntas.explicacion: Excessive vacuum is listed as a cause of hemolysis, and the two examples given are a tube too large for a pediatric patient and a syringe of ten to twenty milliliters. The matching remedy in the device table is a smaller tube of one to five milliliters with a lower vacuum for children.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Administrative Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Privacy administration · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Besides written policies, which administrative duties does the Privacy Rule place on a covered entity?
opciones: Naming a privacy official and a contact for complaints, and training the whole workforce
Naming a privacy official whose approval is needed before any record leaves the office
Training only the staff who handle claims, since billing carries the greatest privacy risk
Filing the practice's privacy policies with the Office for Civil Rights before they take effect
preguntas.explicacion: The rule obliges a covered entity to name a privacy official who answers for its policies and its procedures, plus a contact person or office to take complaints and answer questions. It has to train every member of the workforce as their functions require, sanction those who break the policies, mitigate any harm it comes to know about, and never retaliate against someone who exercises a right or files a complaint.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Contamination
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 k9 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the purple EDTA tube before the serum separator tube that will be used for a chemistry panel. What problem does this kind of error create?
opciones: Anticoagulant on the needle can be carried into the following tube and contaminate it
The serum tube will fail to clot within the 10 to 15 minutes expected before it is spun
The vacuum of the second tube is lost, so it fills only partially or not at all
The EDTA tube will show platelet clumping and a falsely low platelet count
preguntas.explicacion: Under Issues of Concern, the tube review describes contamination in which anticoagulant from one tube sticks to the vacutainer needle and passes into the next tube; that is why the sequence matters. Clotting time, loss of vacuum and EDTA-related platelet clumping are all real issues in the same material, but none of them is caused by drawing the tubes out of order.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD reads 93% and is upset at not being in the usual range. What is the explanation?
opciones: Somewhat lower values can be acceptable in chronic lung disease and at high elevation
Any value under 95% is abnormal for everyone, and oxygen is started at that point
Chronic lung disease raises the acceptable floor, so 93% is lower than it should be
The reading has to be repeated on the earlobe, which is the site used in lung disease
preguntas.explicacion: The normal band of 95% to 100% describes healthy adults at sea level. In someone with COPD or pneumonia, or someone living where the air holds less oxygen, a value below that can be acceptable, and what matters is the patient's own usual level and the trend. The reporting thresholds of 92% and 88% still stand.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern: privileging
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · RMA I.C.6 · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: Does holding a professional license mean a person may provide any service in that field?
opciones: No: each state's law and the licensing body set what the license permits
Yes, as long as the employer's job description includes that service
Yes, once the institution has finished credentialing that professional
No: only the institution's privileges list decides, and state law does not
preguntas.explicacion: Every state has its own laws on medical practice, and simply holding a license does not mean the holder may deliver whatever service they want: an advanced practice nurse cannot start prescribing on that basis alone, and a family physician cannot start inserting central lines. Credentialing checks the qualifications; privileging then authorizes a specific set of services after evaluating credentials and performance.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: How does an under-filled citrate tube distort coagulation results?
opciones: PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out longer and fibrinogen comes out lower
PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out shorter and fibrinogen comes out higher
PT and aPTT are unchanged, but the platelet count comes out falsely low
PT comes out longer while aPTT and fibrinogen are unaffected by the fill level
preguntas.explicacion: When too little blood meets a fixed volume of citrate the sample-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong, and the clotting times PT, aPTT and thrombin time become significantly longer while fibrinogen levels come out significantly lower. The direction matters for the exam: the error mimics a bleeding tendency, not a hypercoagulable one, and it touches the citrate tube, not the platelet count from the EDTA tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient who has fainted kept lying flat rather than allowed to sit up right away?
opciones: Standing up too soon can bring the episode back before the postural hypotension has resolved
Sitting up compresses the abdomen and forces blood down into the legs, raising the heart rate
The horizontal position lets the tourniquet be reapplied safely for the remaining tubes
Sitting up too soon converts the faint into a seizure with tonic-clonic activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should sit or lie down quickly with the legs raised to recover from reflex postural hypotension, and they should be kept horizontal after the event while being prevented from standing up too soon. The chapter does not describe abdominal compression, does not say a faint turns into a seizure, and nothing in it involves resuming the draw.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.c (2027 I.A.2.c) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A surgeon repairs a torn tendon and the operative report names the procedure with the ending -rrhaphy. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: Suturing the structure named by the root
Crushing the structure named by the root
Binding the structure named by the root
Puncturing the structure named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -rrhaphy is a suture, so a tendon repair with stitches carries it. Its neighbors on the same list name other acts: -desis is a surgical binding, -tripsy a crushing, and -centesis a surgical puncture that draws off fluid. Two more, -pexy and -plasty, anchor a part in place and rebuild it.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Denial of Access
preguntas.subtema: Denial of access · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice decides to deny part of an access request. What must the written denial contain?
opciones: The basis for the denial in plain language and how to complain to the practice or to OCR
The name of the workforce member who located the records and the date they were pulled
A copy of the practice policy on retention and disposal of protected health information
The fee schedule for copies, so the patient can decide whether to renew the request later
preguntas.explicacion: A denial, whole or partial, has to reach the individual in writing inside 30 calendar days of the request, or 60 where an extension was announced. It has to be in plain language, has to set out the ground on which access was refused, has to explain the right to a review of that decision and how to ask for one where it applies, and how to complain to the covered entity or to the HHS Office for Civil Rights. Whatever the ground does not cover still has to be released.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Patient portal · CCMA 5U · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 4E k56 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what she can see through the practice's patient portal at two in the morning.
opciones: Allergies, medications, immunizations, recent visits, discharge summaries and lab results
Only the balance she owes the practice and the date of her next scheduled appointment
Only the documents a staff member has chosen to release to her during office hours
The complete record of every patient the practice treats, filtered by her search terms
preguntas.explicacion: A patient portal is a secure web site that opens personal health information round the clock, from anywhere there is an Internet connection, entered with a username and a password of one's own. What can be looked at there includes allergies, medications, immunizations, recent visits to the doctor, discharge summaries and laboratory results.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Protein in diet — Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(c) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(c) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What share of a healthy adult's total calorie needs should come from protein?
opciones: 10 percent to 35 percent of total calories
10 percent to 20 percent of total calories
20 percent to 45 percent of total calories
35 percent to 50 percent of total calories
preguntas.explicacion: Protein intake is written as a band of total calories, 10 to 35 percent, so it moves with how many calories the person needs. Protein supplies 4 calories per gram, which means 100 grams on a 2,000-calorie day is 400 calories, about 20 percent of the day. Teens and children may need different amounts.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: In which of these situations should 911 be called for a person who has fainted?
opciones: The person does not become alert within a couple of minutes
The person is pale and weak for a few minutes after waking
The person fainted while seated and woke up within a minute
The person reports having fainted once before during a blood draw
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency help is called when someone who has fainted fell from a height, above all if hurt or bleeding, when they do not come round within a couple of minutes, or when the patient is pregnant. Pallor and weakness for a few minutes after waking are the normal aftermath of a faint, and a past faint is a reason to draw the patient lying down, not an emergency.

preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.c · 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: How often are the portable fire extinguishers in a workplace checked?
opciones: Looked over every month, plus a maintenance check once a year
Looked over every week, plus a maintenance check every two years
Looked over every three months, plus a maintenance check yearly
Looked over once a year, plus a maintenance check every five years
preguntas.explicacion: The employer is responsible for inspection, maintenance and testing: portable extinguishers are visually inspected monthly and get an annual maintenance check. The date of that annual check goes on record, and the record is kept either until a year has passed since the last entry or until the shell reaches the end of its life, whichever comes first, and is shown to OSHA on request.

preguntas.subtema: Uses requiring authorization · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which use of protected health information always requires a HIPAA authorization, even when it relates to treatment, payment or operations?
opciones: Sale of protected health information
Referral of the patient to a specialist
Consultation between two treating providers
Submission of a claim to the health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Three things need an authorization whatever else the rule allows: psychotherapy notes in most of their uses and disclosures; marketing that goes beyond a face-to-face communication or a gift of nominal value; and any disclosure amounting to a sale of PHI, where the authorization has to say that the covered entity will be paid. Section 164.502(a)(5)(ii) separately forbids selling PHI except under such an authorization. Referrals, consultations between treating providers and claims are treatment and payment activities that 164.506 permits.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 3: Composition/Information on Ingredients; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(i)(1)
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 3 and trade secrets · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A safety data sheet says the exact percentage of one ingredient has been withheld as a trade secret. Where does that statement belong?
opciones: In section 3, with the chemical names and the identification numbers
In section 15, with the other regulatory information on the product
In section 10, with the stability and the incompatible materials
In section 16, with the revision date and any other information
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3 lists what is in the product: chemical name, common names, the Chemical Abstracts Service number and other identifiers, and the impurities and stabilizing additives that count toward the classification. Exact percentages are required, with ranges allowed only for a trade secret claim, batch-to-batch variation, or a group of very similar mixtures. When an identity or a percentage is withheld as a trade secret, the sheet must say so, and it says so in this section.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 5. Cleaning and Disinfecting Environmental Surfaces in Healthcare Facilities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Staff propose wiping down exam room counters with the glutaraldehyde solution left over from the scope bath. What does the guideline say?
opciones: Do not use high-level disinfectants or liquid chemical sterilants on noncritical surfaces
Do it, but only on surfaces that a patient with broken skin has actually been resting on
Do it, since a stronger agent than the counter needs can never leave the surface underprocessed
Do it, provided the counters are rinsed with water and dried before the next patient enters
preguntas.explicacion: Countertops are noncritical environmental surfaces, and the recommendation on them is flat: high-level disinfectants and liquid chemical sterilants are not to be used for them. What they call for is an EPA-registered hospital disinfectant used according to its own label. Rinsing and drying is the rule for infant bassinets terminally cleaned with phenolics, not a license here.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.3 Order of draw
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3P k72 capillary order of draw · PBT II.H.2 · CCMA k130 order of draw with microtubes · NCMA 2C.7 · RMA III.C.4 order of draw · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A skin puncture must supply a hematology specimen, a chemistry specimen and a blood bank specimen. In what order are they collected?
opciones: Hematology, then chemistry, then blood bank
Blood bank, then chemistry, then hematology
Chemistry, then hematology, then blood bank
Blood bank, then hematology, then chemistry
preguntas.explicacion: On a dermal puncture the hematology tube comes first, then chemistry, then blood bank; that sequence matters because platelets start clumping as soon as the skin is broken. It runs backwards to the venous order of draw. Beyond two specimens, a vein is likely to give the laboratory better numbers.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), What is a comprehensive metabolic panel?; and Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP)
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · PBT II.G · RMA III.C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which measurement is included in a comprehensive metabolic panel but not in a basic metabolic panel?
opciones: ALT, one of the liver enzymes
Potassium, one of the electrolytes
Creatinine, a waste product
Glucose, an energy source
preguntas.explicacion: The BMP measures eight substances (glucose, the electrolytes sodium, potassium, chloride and carbon dioxide, and the kidney waste products BUN and creatinine among them) and the CMP adds six more: albumin, total protein, the liver enzymes ALP, ALT and AST, and bilirubin. So the liver enzyme ALT is the one found only in the CMP; the other three are in both panels.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist in a hurry inserts the needle while the alcohol is still visibly wet. What does the WHO say is the consequence of not allowing enough contact time?
opciones: The risk of contamination increases
The wet alcohol haemolyses the sample
Potassium is falsely increased
The tourniquet limit is exceeded
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 states that too little contact time raises the risk of contamination; the swab is applied for 30 seconds and the skin is then left to dry completely, about 30 seconds more. The potassium artifact is the WHO's warning about povidone iodine, not about wet alcohol, and the tourniquet limit is unrelated to drying time.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.1
preguntas.subtema: Patient positioning · CPT D3 3A · D2 2N · D1 1C k13 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3E5 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Blood is being drawn at the bedside on a ward. What does the guidance ask for first?
opciones: Close the bed curtain, so the draw is private and clean
Move the patient to the outpatient cubicle down the corridor
Ask visitors to hold the tray while the tubes are filled
Open the curtain fully, so the light falls on the arm
preguntas.explicacion: For inpatients the instruction is to close the bed curtain at the bedside to give privacy, and to see that the sampling is done privately and cleanly. The dedicated cubicle with two chairs and a hand-wash basin is what is described for outpatient departments and clinics.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Tube positions and filling · CPT D3 k59 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: To fill an evacuated tube from a syringe more easily, a trainee removes the rubber stopper first. Why does the WHO forbid this?
opciones: Removing the stopper releases the vacuum
Removing the stopper lets the additive evaporate
Removing the stopper activates the safety mechanism
Removing the stopper breaks the order of draw
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says to inject downward through the appropriately colored stopper with the tube in a rack, and not to remove the stopper because doing so releases the vacuum; the same loss of vacuum happens whenever a tube is uncapped. The safety mechanism belongs to the needle device, and the order of draw is about which tube comes next, not about the stopper.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet removal · CPT D3 3E k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The last of three tubes has just started to fill. What should the phlebotomist do at this moment?
opciones: Release the tourniquet from the arm
Ask the patient to bend the arm
Withdraw the needle and apply gauze
Invert the collected tubes 8 to 10 times
preguntas.explicacion: When the last tube is filling with blood, the tourniquet is removed, and it should in any case come off within one minute of placement. This matches the WHO instruction to release it before the needle is withdrawn. The needle comes out only after the tube is full, the WHO asks the patient not to bend the arm, and 8 to 10 inversions is the culture bottle figure.

preguntas.subtema: Device and media controls · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does the device and media controls standard cover, taken as a whole?
opciones: Hardware and media coming into the office, leaving it, and moving around inside
Hardware bought from an approved supplier and kept on the practice's asset list
Media held by the software vendor on the practice's behalf under its contract
Hardware that stores records, but not the media used only to back them up
preguntas.explicacion: The standard asks for policies on hardware and electronic media that hold the information: how they come into a facility, how they leave it, and how they move around inside. The four specifications then fill that in: disposal and media re-use are required; accountability and a data backup before equipment moves are addressable.

preguntas.subtema: Revoking an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient telephones to cancel the authorization he signed last week. What does the rule require of a revocation, and what does it not undo?
opciones: It must be in writing, and it does not undo what was already done in reliance on it
It must be in writing, and it does not undo disclosures made in the previous six years
It may be spoken, and it does not undo what was already done in reliance on it
It must be in writing, and it undoes every disclosure the form had authorized
preguntas.explicacion: An individual may revoke an authorization at any time, provided the revocation is in writing. Two things survive it: action the covered entity has already taken in reliance on the authorization, and, where the form was signed to obtain insurance coverage, the insurer's right under other law to contest a claim or the policy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Adjustments for blood flow · CPT D3 k67 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: Only a tiny drop of blood appears after the needle enters and the flow stops. What is the likely cause and the adjustment?
opciones: The bevel may still be partly outside the vein; flatten the angle and advance 1 to 2 mm
The vein has been passed through completely; withdraw the needle fully and re-puncture above
The tube has lost its vacuum; pull the needle back out of the skin and change the tube
The tourniquet is too tight; remove it entirely and wait for the flow to return
preguntas.explicacion: If only a small drop appears, part of the needle bevel may still be outside the vein, and the device is laid flatter and pushed on 1 to 2 mm at a time until the flow is adequate. A lost vacuum is a separate cause described in the tube collection review and calls for a new tube, not for withdrawing the needle. Deep insertion beyond the lumen produces a hematoma, according to the phlebotomy chapter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Fainting", When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.l · 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which detail turns a fainting episode into a call for the emergency number?
opciones: The patient does not become alert again within a couple of minutes
The patient felt dizzy and nauseated for a moment before going down
The patient was standing in a warm room and had not eaten breakfast
The patient looks pale and sweaty for a minute after coming round
preguntas.explicacion: Help is called when the patient does not become alert within a couple of minutes, or fell from a height, is pregnant, is over 50, has diabetes, reports chest pain or an irregular heartbeat, cannot speak, see or move a limb, or had convulsions or loss of bladder control. Dizziness, nausea and sweating before the faint are typical warnings.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C III.D.3 · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A plasma sample will be tested for viral load now and possibly retested several times over the coming months. Why is it aliquoted before freezing?
opciones: So each retest thaws a fresh portion, avoiding the loss seen after repeated freeze-thaw cycles
So the erythrocytes settle in one portion and the plasma stays free of heme when it thaws
So the laboratory can send one portion to a reference laboratory without a referral record
So the heparin concentration falls below the level that inhibits amplification in each portion
preguntas.explicacion: Serum and plasma tolerate freezing, but the number of freeze-thaw cycles a target survives varies: one study saw a 16 % fall in HCV RNA titres after five cycles and recommended aliquoting the sample to limit the loss, while others found no loss after eight or ten. Splitting the sample lets each retest use a portion thawed only once. Erythrocytes are removed before freezing, not by aliquoting, and heparin is a reason to reject the tube, not to split it.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Staff at a practice about to start booking video visits ask how to get ready for the first one. Which step does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Do a practice run of a telehealth visit with a co-worker
Run the first week of visits with audio only, then add video
Ask a patient to test the platform and report back on it
Book the first video visits at the end of the working day
preguntas.explicacion: Among the things a practice settles before it offers telehealth are staffing, technology, scheduling and how it will meet patient needs, and the guidance closes that list with a tip: try the visit out with a co-worker first. Audio-only is offered as a fallback when the video fails, not as a way of phasing the service in.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Rights of Medication Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5
preguntas.pregunta: How many times are the rights of medication administration verified before a dose is given to a patient?
opciones: At least three times, checking the six rights on each of those occasions
Once, at the bedside, at the moment the medication is handed to the patient
Twice, once against the written order and once against the pharmacy label
Five times, one for each of the five traditional rights of administration
preguntas.explicacion: The six rights are patient, drug, dose, time, route and documentation, and they are verified at least three times before the dose is given. They are the last safety check in a chain that runs from the prescribing provider through the pharmacist and the nurse to the patient. Recent literature stretches the list to as many as ten, adding history and assessment, drug interactions, the right to refuse, and education.

preguntas.subtema: Standing orders and order sets · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital wants to use pre-printed order sets for a common admission. What does the medical record condition require before they may be used?
opciones: Review and approval by the medical staff and by nursing and pharmacy leadership
Review and approval by the medical staff and by the governing body of the hospital
Review and approval by the medical staff and by the accrediting organization used
Review and approval by the ordering practitioner at the time each set is applied
preguntas.explicacion: Standing orders, order sets and protocols, whether pre-printed or electronic, may be used only where the hospital has had them reviewed and approved by the medical staff together with its nursing and pharmacy leadership, has shown they follow guidelines that are nationally recognized and evidence-based, and has arranged for them to be reviewed regularly. Each use is still dated, timed and authenticated promptly.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, The ABO Blood Group; and Rh Blood Groups
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How do anti-Rh antibodies differ from the anti-A and anti-B antibodies of the ABO system?
opciones: They form only in Rh− people after exposure to Rh+ cells (sensitization)
They are preformed from early exposure to antigens in foods and microbes
They form in Rh+ people after a first transfusion of Rh− blood
They are present in all type O plasma along with anti-A and anti-B
preguntas.explicacion: The two systems differ: ABO antibodies are preformed because A and B antigens are met early in life in food and microbes, whereas antibodies to the Rh antigen are made only by Rh negative individuals after exposure to Rh positive cells, a process called sensitization, which follows an Rh-incompatible transfusion or, more often, the birth of an Rh positive baby to an Rh negative parent.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth privacy setup · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient plans to join her video visit from a coffee shop network. What should the office check with her beforehand?
opciones: Whether she understands how the platform handles security on public Wi-Fi
Whether the coffee shop has agreed in writing to act as an originating site
Whether her device is enrolled in the practice's own equipment inventory list
Whether she is willing to sign a waiver releasing the practice from the rules
