preguntas.explicacion: The checklist for finding out what technology a patient has asks whether she owns a device with a camera and a microphone, whether her internet connection carries enough bandwidth, and whether she has somewhere with secure internet from which to take the appointment; it adds that a patient on public Wi-Fi needs to understand how the telehealth platform handles security. Providers are told to deliver telehealth from private locations and to apply reasonable safeguards.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports its three leading preanalytical problems for the year as 4.34 %, 0.81 % and 0.36 % of specimens. Which three are these, in that order?
opciones: Hemolysis of serum, identification errors, and clots in anticoagulated blood
Identification errors, hemolysis of the serum, and clots in anticoagulated blood
Hemolysis of serum, clots in anticoagulated blood, and transcription errors
Clots in anticoagulated blood, hemolysis of serum, and identification errors
preguntas.explicacion: Out of 868,441 samples received in one year, hemolysis headed the list: 4.34 % of the serum samples were hemolysed. Identification errors came second at 0.81 %, most of them labels carrying fewer than two identifiers, and fibrin clots in anticoagulated tubes third at 0.36 %. Transcription errors on the request were far rarer, 0.257 %, and a wrong fill level rarer still, 0.066 %.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Redundant internet path · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A small clinic cannot run two cable connections in separate trenches. What backup route to the internet does the guidance suggest for a practice that size?
opciones: A wireless access point over the mobile network, able to carry a cloud-hosted system
A wireless access point over the mobile network, used only to send claims overnight
A dial-up line kept on standby, which carries the read-only copy of the records
A second cable from the same provider, brought into the building by another route
preguntas.explicacion: Larger organizations are expected to hold a redundant path to the internet, two different cables in different trenches, with a microwave or other wireless link acceptable when two different providers supply it. Smaller ambulatory clinics are told to have at least a cellphone-based wireless access point capable of running a cloud-hosted record system.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Desirable Characteristics of Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Choosing a safer device · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic is choosing between two safety winged-steel needles. Which feature matches what is recommended for a device with a safety mechanism?
opciones: The shield is part of the device and stays protective all the way to disposal
The shield is added by the user after the needle leaves the patient's vein
The shield can be switched off when the phlebotomist needs to reuse the holder
The shield is activated with two hands, one on each side of the exposed tip
preguntas.explicacion: The list of desirable characteristics is short and demanding: no needle at all where that is possible; a safety feature built into the device rather than added on; passive operation if it can be had; a feature the user can see is engaged; one that cannot be switched off and keeps protecting through disposal; and a device that is reliable, practical and safe for the patient. A shield that is added afterwards or can be undone fails those tests, and two-handed activation puts a hand in front of the tip.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", Home Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Once the jerking of a seizure stops, why is the patient rolled onto one side?
opciones: So that vomit is not breathed into the lungs while awareness returns
So that the tongue can be held forward with a gloved finger
So that blood pressure can be taken on the upper arm at once
So that the jerking is less likely to start over on the other side
preguntas.explicacion: Turning the patient onto one side keeps vomit from being inhaled into the lungs, which is why the recovery position lowers the risk of asphyxiation and aspiration after a tonic-clonic seizure. Nothing is given by mouth until the convulsions have ended and the patient is fully awake and alert, and someone stays with them meanwhile.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Mobile health · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's telephone application records her walking and reminds her when a dose is due. Which telehealth category covers that?
opciones: Mobile health, one of the other asynchronous forms available to patients
Remote patient monitoring, which sends clinical data on to her provider
Synchronous telehealth, because the reminder reaches her in real time
A virtual check-in, because each exchange runs for ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: Mobile health is the use of a digital device, a smartphone for instance, or of something the patient wears, in support of her own health; the examples given are a fitness tracker, applications that record exercise, automatic reminders about when a medicine is due, and storage of things like discharge instructions. Remote monitoring, by contrast, sends patient data on to the provider.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, 2026 Ambulatory Health Care National Patient Safety Goals
preguntas.subtema: Two identifiers · CCMA 3A2 · CMA I.A.1 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 3A k42 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is checking in for an injection. Which practice does the 2026 ambulatory patient safety goal require?
opciones: Using at least two ways to identify the patient, such as name and date of birth
Using the room number as the second identifier once the patient has been seated
Using the patient's insurance member number as the only identifier at check-in
Using one identifier at registration and a second one only before a procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The first ambulatory goal is to identify patients correctly, and the wording is to use at least two ways to identify a patient, the example given being name and date of birth. The purpose stated is making sure each patient receives the correct medicine and treatment. The same goal appears, worded for residents and for individuals served, across the other program settings.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter and 26
preguntas.subtema: Chain of custody form · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f) drug screen
preguntas.pregunta: A donor starts listing the prescriptions they take while the collector fills in the custody form. How should that be handled?
opciones: The collector records no medical information; the donor may list drugs on their own copy
The collector writes the medicines on the remarks line so the laboratory can see them
The collector records them in the donor section, which exists for that purpose
The collector stops the collection until a medical review officer can take the list
preguntas.explicacion: Collectors must not solicit medical information, and none may be recorded on the chain of custody form or on any other record the collector keeps or hands on. What the donor may do is list prescription and over-the-counter medicines on a separate sheet or on the back of their own copy of the form, which helps them remember if the medical review officer calls. That list stays off every other copy.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.5 Homeostasis, Negative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(1) (2027 I.C.6.f(1)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient becomes overheated. Which set of responses does the heat-loss center of the brain set off?
opciones: Skin vessels widen, sweat glands step up output, and breathing deepens
Skin vessels narrow, sweat glands shut down, and breathing grows shallow
Skin vessels widen, the thyroid speeds metabolism, and shivering begins
Skin vessels narrow, blood shifts to deep veins, and shivering begins
preguntas.explicacion: When the temperature center reads a value above the normal range it stimulates the heat-loss center, and three things follow: vessels in the skin dilate so core blood can radiate heat at the surface, sweat glands increase output so evaporation carries heat away, and respiration deepens. The narrowing, deep-vein shift and shivering belong to the heat-gain response to cold.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Cortisol Test, section Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient ran 10 km at dawn before his morning cortisol draw. Which preparation point was missed?
opciones: Stress and exercise raise cortisol; rest before the test was needed
Cortisol requires a 12-hour fast, which the run interrupted
The draw should have been at 4 p.m., when cortisol normally peaks
Running is acceptable as long as he drank only plain water
preguntas.explicacion: Stress and exercise can raise cortisol levels, so the patient may need to rest before the test, and a blood cortisol needs two appointments in one day. General preparation also bans on excessive physical activity in the 24 hours before outpatient sampling. No fast is imposed for cortisol, and 4 p.m. is the low point, not the peak.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Periods of Disease
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why do patients in the period of decline become vulnerable to a second infection?
opciones: The primary infection has weakened the immune system while symptoms fade
The primary infection has strengthened the immune system while symptoms fade
The pathogen count rises again in that period and overwhelms the defenses
The convalescent period always begins with a relapse of the first infection
preguntas.explicacion: In the period of decline the number of pathogen particles falls and the signs and symptoms ease off, but the immune system has been worn down by the primary infection, so a secondary infection can take hold just as the patient seems to be improving. Recovery proper comes in the convalescent period.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.3 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: An erythrocyte sedimentation rate rack stands on a bench beside a centrifuge, leaning a few degrees off the vertical. What does that do to the result?
opciones: The rate rises, and a tilt of only 3° can add as much as 30 % to it
The rate falls, because tilted red cells settle against the tube wall
The rate is unchanged, since the reading is corrected for the angle
The rate rises, but only when the tube was also underfilled at collection
preguntas.explicacion: Technical conditions move this test more than most. A tube tilted 3° from the vertical can raise the value by as much as 30 %, and vibration from nearby equipment raises it too. A warm room lowers blood viscosity and pushes the rate up, and direct sunlight also raises it. Underfilling adds air bubbles, which lift the reading as well, so the rack belongs upright, still and out of the sun.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 5.2 Review, Observations, and Replication
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: A finished tracing is checked for quality before the patient leaves. How much baseline shift between neighboring complexes is still acceptable?
opciones: A vertical distance of no more than 5 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 1 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 10 mm between them
A vertical distance of no more than 25 mm between them
preguntas.explicacion: A recording is accepted only against a short list of minimums, and one of them puts a ceiling on drift: measured from one complex to the next, the baseline may not climb or fall by more than 5 mm. Anything beyond that is sent back to be run again.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccinated clinicians with anti-HBs documentation and Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Documented vaccine responders · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A vaccinated phlebotomist with a documented anti-HBs level of 10 mIU/mL or more is exposed to an HBsAg-positive patient. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: No post-exposure treatment and no source testing; the documented response is protective
One dose of HBIG plus a vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months afterward
Two doses of HBIG one month apart, since vaccinated workers cannot be revaccinated
A repeat anti-HBs test now, with HBIG only if the level has fallen below 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: For a clinician with written documentation of a complete series and a recorded anti-HBs of 10 mIU/mL or more, the CDC says testing the source for HBsAg is unnecessary and no post-exposure prophylaxis is needed regardless of the source's status; the table lists a documented responder as needing no action. Immunocompetent responders have long-term protection and do not need periodic retesting, even though antibody levels wane. HBIG with revaccination is for those found below 10 mIU/mL without prior documentation, and two HBIG doses are for non-responders after two series.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 13.2 The Central Nervous System (CC BY 4.0)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the brain is the largest, and what connects its two halves?
opciones: The cerebrum, whose hemispheres are joined by the corpus callosum
The cerebellum, whose hemispheres are joined by the corpus callosum
The brain stem, whose halves are joined by the corpus callosum
The diencephalon, whose halves are joined by the corpus callosum
preguntas.explicacion: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, and a deep longitudinal fissure splits it into two hemispheres; what joins them is the corpus callosum, an arching band of white fibers. The cerebellum, below the occipital lobes, is the second largest part, and the brain stem lies between the diencephalon and the cord.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium tax credit
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is the premium tax credit?
opciones: Help that lowers the monthly cost of a Marketplace plan, based on income
Help that lowers the deductible of a Marketplace plan, based on family size
A refund of premiums paid for job-based coverage during the previous year
A discount an insurer applies for staying with the same plan several years
preguntas.explicacion: The premium tax credit is financial help that lowers the monthly payment for a plan bought through the Marketplace, figured from household information and estimated income; incomes between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level qualify in every state. Discounts on what is paid at the point of care are cost-sharing reductions, a different item, and the credit is available only through the Marketplace.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A marathon runner has a resting pulse of 48 beats per minute and no symptoms. How is this read?
opciones: It fits the 40 to 60 band reported for well-trained athletes at rest
It is bradycardia in any adult and is reported to the provider before the visit ends
It is a counting error, since a rate under 60 cannot be palpated at the wrist
It fits the range for adults over 65, in whom the resting rate falls with age
preguntas.explicacion: Well-trained athletes rest at 40 to 60 beats per minute, so 48 with no symptoms fits that group rather than signaling disease. The general adult floor is 60, and resting heart rate does not fall simply because a person is older: what declines with age is the maximum rate reached on exertion.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Fecal Samples and Urine Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT V.B · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(4)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given a pot and told to bring a stool specimen for culture from home. Besides using a clean, dry, tightly lidded pot, which sampling instruction belongs in the written procedure?
opciones: Include the first, middle and last portions passed, and any part carrying pus, mucus or blood
Include only the first portion passed, before the later stool is diluted by intestinal fluid
Include only the firm outer surface, keeping away from any part that carries mucus or blood
Include a midstream portion caught once the first part has been discarded, as with urine
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen drops straight into a clean, dry pot with a lid that seals, and travels on inside a labeled transport container. What makes it diagnostic is that it stands for the whole stool, the first portion, the middle and the last, together with anything abnormal the eye can pick out in it: blood, mucus, pus. Midstream is a urine instruction, not a fecal one.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · CCMA 3E1 k127 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient's daughter stays for the whole visit. When does the guidance suggest asking her to step out?
opciones: For part of the visit, so sensitive topics can be raised in private
Only once the patient signs a release form naming her as a contact
As a rule never, since a companion may stay through the whole visit
Only when the patient is being asked about paying for the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Companions can help the patient express concerns and reinforce what is said, but the patient is first asked how they see the companion's role. Asking the companion to step out for part of the visit gives the patient private time for sensitive matters, and it stops the companion answering for the patient or covering cognitive lapses during a test of thinking.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A5 k56 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a home reading of 99.5 °F. Which Celsius value is charted, and what does it mean by mouth in a child?
opciones: 37.5 °C, which is exactly the oral threshold for fever in a child
37.2 °C, which is the axillary rather than the oral threshold in a child
38.0 °C, which is the rectal rather than the oral threshold in a child
36.5 °C, which is the lower edge of the normal adult reference range
preguntas.explicacion: Clinical sources publish the two scales as pairs: 99 °F is 37.2 °C, 99.5 °F is 37.5 °C and 100.4 °F is 38 °C. The middle pair is the point at which an oral reading counts as fever in a child, and in an adult the mouth is said to show fever above roughly 99 to 99.5 °F, depending on the hour of the day.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Chemical Examination: Blood Cells; Glucose)
preguntas.subtema: Vitamin C interference · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.v · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports taking high-dose vitamin C supplements. On which of these pairs of dipstick pads is vitamin C listed among the causes of a false-negative result?
opciones: Occult blood and glucose
Protein and bilirubin
pH and specific gravity
Ketones and urobilinogen
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C appears in the false-negative list of the blood pad and of the glucose pad, in each case beside an elevated specific gravity; it is listed for the nitrite and leukocyte esterase pads too, so it is not an interferent limited to a single pair. The blood pad reads the peroxidase activity of erythrocytes, hemoglobin and myoglobin. Protein, bilirubin, ketones and pH carry other interferents: alkaline urine for protein, and a stale specimen for bilirubin and for ketones.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Specimen preparation, serum vs plasma · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on serum. Which tubes from the WHO table will provide it?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the red-gray or gold serum separator tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube and the light green plasma separator tube
The purple EDTA tube and the light blue sodium citrate tube
The light gray oxalate/fluoride tube and the pale yellow ACD tube
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3 the clot activator tube lets the blood clot so the serum can be separated by centrifugation, and the serum separator tube holds a gel that separates blood from serum when spun. Every other tube listed carries an anticoagulant, so the liquid it yields is plasma: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA and citrate in the purple and light blue, oxalate in the gray and ACD in the yellow.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Collecting the Sample (Labeling Samples); Test!: Resolving Problems
preguntas.subtema: Labeling test devices · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D4 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.a · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic tests three walk-in patients for influenza at the same time on cassettes. When and how should each cassette be identified?
opciones: Label each cassette with a patient identifier before the sample is collected, and label samples with two identifiers
Label each cassette after the result has developed, so that the ink does not interfere with the reading window
Write the patient's initials in the log next to the result instead of on the cassette, which stays unmarked
One identifier, the patient's last name, is enough on site because the cassettes never leave the testing area
preguntas.explicacion: A sample is labeled the moment it is collected, with two or more identifiers unique to that patient, name and date of birth for example, so that nothing gets mixed up; the label may also carry the date, the time and the collector. Where a test needs the sample applied straight onto the device, a strip or a cassette, that device is labeled with a patient identifier before collection. Improperly labeled samples are among the problems that have to be documented and reported.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.D.2.f
preguntas.pregunta: Sterile gloves are on for a dressing change. What does non-touch technique still require?
opciones: Handling key parts only when needed, and applying the dressing by its edges
Handling key parts freely, since sterile gloves make the whole surface sterile
Handling key parts with forceps only, since gloved fingers may never touch them
Handling key parts after a second pair of gloves is pulled over the first pair
preguntas.explicacion: Non-touch remains the goal even when sterile gloves are worn. Contact with key parts and key sites is limited, deliberate and only when needed: syringes are held away from the hub, key parts are handled at the moment they are assembled or used, and bandages are applied by the edges away from the part that will meet the wound.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccine documentation; Vaccine protection and anti-HBs testing
preguntas.subtema: Undocumented vaccination · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist says she was vaccinated against hepatitis B as a child but has no records. How does the CDC treat her?
opciones: As unvaccinated: only written, dated records count, so she should complete the series
As vaccinated: a single anti-HBs test of 10 mIU/mL or more proves immunity
As vaccinated: childhood vaccination is routine and needs no post-vaccination testing
As a non-responder: she should receive HBIG at hire and be tested every year
preguntas.explicacion: Only written, dated records count as proof of hepatitis B vaccination, so a clinician who cannot document three doses is treated as unvaccinated and should complete the series, with anti-HBs measured 1 to 2 months after the third dose. A result of 10 mIU/mL or above is a reliable marker of protection only where the test came after a documented series of three doses, so a lone result in someone with no records should not be read as immunity. Facilities are encouraged to hunt for old records and to enter doses in the state immunization system.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A digital sublingual thermometer is chosen over a glass one for a busy intake. Which advantage does it offer?
opciones: It reports in about 10 to 20 seconds, against the 3 to 5 minutes a glass probe needs
It reports in about 3 to 5 seconds, against the 20 seconds a glass probe needs
It reaches core temperature values that a glass probe under the tongue cannot reach
It removes any need to ask about hot or cold drinks taken shortly before the reading is done
preguntas.explicacion: Digital sublingual thermometers take a disposable probe cover and give a result in roughly 10 to 20 seconds; a glass probe needs 3 to 5 minutes in place. Neither device corrects for a recent hot or cold drink or a cigarette, so that question is asked before either one is used.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 1 and 9
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.J · CCMA 3E6 k129 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A fungal culture of the blood is requested. Which container is used, and where does it fall in the sequence?
opciones: The culture bottle with broth, drawn first of all the containers
The culture bottle with broth, drawn after the coagulation tube
The pale yellow ACD tube, drawn first of all the containers used
The purple EDTA tube, drawn before any of the serum tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: The yellow and black striped culture bottle holds a broth that keeps micro-organisms viable, and its listed uses are aerobes, anaerobes and fungi. It is number 1 in the sequence, ahead of every other container. The ACD tube preserves nothing microbiological: it is used for tissue typing and DNA.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Collecting the Sample (Using Collection Devices)
preguntas.subtema: Kit swabs only · PBT IV.A.5 / IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 k113 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.3.a · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: The swabs packaged with a rapid strep kit have run out, and sterile swabs from the culture supply are available. May they be used to collect the throat sample?
opciones: No; only the swabs supplied with the collection or test kit are used, because different swab materials can interfere with the result
Yes, if they are sterile and individually wrapped, since sterility is the only property the manufacturer's instructions require
Yes, if they are the same length and tip size, since only the physical dimensions of the swab affect the antigen extraction
Yes, but only from another kit made by the same manufacturer, since the swab material is standardized across all of its products
preguntas.explicacion: Collection devices are used as the manufacturer's current instructions say, which means the swab out of the sample collection kit or the test kit and no other. Swab materials differ, and a substitute can interfere with the result. Fingerstick and venipuncture devices are single-use and never reused, and some collection devices deliver a set volume or carry additives the test depends on.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a lancet described among the sharps used in health care?
opciones: An instrument with a short two-edged blade that draws drops of blood
A hollow needle with a bevel that draws blood into an attached tube
A tubing system with a needle used to deliver drugs into the body
A needle that connects to tubing for transferring fluids in and out
preguntas.explicacion: A lancet, also called a fingerstick device, is an instrument with a short two-edged blade used to obtain drops of blood for testing, and it is commonly used in diabetes care. Infusion sets and connection needles are separate categories of sharp, used to deliver or transfer fluids.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An accredited laboratory is asked to show how it monitors the journey its specimens make from the collecting clinics. Which four aspects does the quality standard name?
opciones: Temperature, time frame, safety and the preservatives used
Time frame, distance, courier training and safety
Temperature, humidity, light exposure and safety
Temperature, container type, preservatives and cost
preguntas.explicacion: The medical laboratory quality standard wants the transport of samples into the laboratory monitored on four counts: how long it takes, at what temperature, with which preservatives, and how safely. It is less prescriptive than the accreditation checklists on most extra-analytical matters, but on transport it names those four outright.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which leads are written on the lower three channels of the paper as the rhythm tracings?
opciones: V1, II and V5, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
I, II and III, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
V1, V2 and V3, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
II, aVF and V6, on the fourth, fifth and sixth channels
preguntas.explicacion: Three leads run without a break along the bottom of the sheet: V1, lead II and V5, on channels four, five and six. Those are the continuous strips the rhythm is read from, and the same three appear on the display of the unit before the run starts.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", How do you ensure password protection; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Passwords and Unique User Identification
preguntas.subtema: Password safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which password practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance?
opciones: Unique passwords for each user, never shared, written down or emailed
A single department password changed each year at annual training
Passwords posted near the workstation so that coverage staff can log in quickly
Passwords of consecutive digits, which are easier to audit
preguntas.explicacion: Every worker who accesses patient records needs a unique, strong password that mixes letters, numbers and symbols, is changed periodically, is never shared, verbalized, written down near the computer or emailed, and is not built from consecutive digits or easily guessed information; the IT department checks password quality before granting access. Uniqueness matters because HITECH requires systems to track each user's activity. Passwords alone are considered weak protection, which is why some institutions add biometric authentication.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Breathing difficulties - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.p · 2027 I.B.8.p · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with asthma is wheezing and struggling to breathe in the waiting room. What is done?
opciones: Call for help, loosen tight clothing and help with the prescribed inhaler
Give a cup of warm water to sip and walk the patient to an exam room
Place a pillow behind the head and let the patient lie down to rest
Wait to see whether the wheezing settles before the call is made
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency help is called right away for breathing difficulty; then airway, breathing and pulse are checked, tight clothing is loosened, and the patient is helped to take whatever medicine has been prescribed for them, an asthma inhaler or oxygen kept at home. Nothing is given to eat or drink, and a pillow under the head can close the airway.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.f · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: A sterile drape hangs four inches below the edge of the tray table. What is the status of the part that hangs down?
opciones: Contaminated, since anything extending below the planar surface no longer counts as sterile
Sterile, since it came out of the same package and has touched no unsterile surface yet
Sterile, but only until someone walks past it, at which point it must be lifted back up
Contaminated, but it can be folded back onto the tray as long as sterile gloves are worn
preguntas.explicacion: Any part of a field that drops below the plane of the tabletop is contaminated, and it cannot be brought back: lifting it would carry the contamination onto the field. The same list rules out whatever sits under the waist or over the shoulders, whatever lies within an inch of the edge, and whatever the person has stopped watching.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.c (2027 I.A.2.c) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Fluid is drawn off from around a lung in a procedure called a thoracentesis. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: A surgical puncture made in order to remove fluid
A surgical opening made from an organ to the outside
A surgical binding that fixes two structures together
A crushing of something hard that has formed inside
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid, and thorac- names the chest, so the two together say where and what. The endings around it name other acts: -ostomy and -stomy make an opening, -desis is a surgical binding and -tripsy is a crushing, as in the treatment of a stone.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(d), (f), (g) and (h), Administrative requirements
preguntas.subtema: No retaliation · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a privacy complaint against a clinic. What does HIPAA say about how the clinic may respond?
opciones: It may not intimidate or retaliate against the patient for filing the complaint
It may decline further treatment, since the relationship of trust has been broken
It may require the patient to waive the complaint as a condition of care
It may share the complaint with other providers so they are warned
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(g) forbids a covered entity from intimidating, threatening, coercing, discriminating against or retaliating against any individual for exercising a right under the rule or taking part in any of its processes, including filing a complaint, and 164.530(h) forbids requiring individuals to waive their rights as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits. The entity must have its own complaint process, document complaints and their disposition, and mitigate any harm from a violation. Sharing the complaint with other providers would itself be an unpermitted disclosure.

preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, High Blood Pressure: Diagnosis, Blood Pressure Levels
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An automated reading shows 186/122 mm Hg and the patient feels well. What does the value call for?
opciones: The provider is contacted immediately: above 180 or above 120 is a hypertensive crisis
A recheck at the next visit, since a single high value cannot diagnose hypertension
A repeat reading in five minutes and no report unless the second one is also high
Documentation only, because a patient free of symptoms is not held to be in danger
preguntas.explicacion: Readings above 180 systolic or above 120 diastolic are dangerously high and call for immediate medical attention, whatever the patient reports: high blood pressure usually carries no warning signs at all. That threshold is separate from the rule that diagnosing hypertension needs three or more measurements at separate visits.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k136 k139 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: A phenytoin level is ordered and the phlebotomist draws it into a serum separator tube with gel. Why will the laboratory not accept that tube for therapeutic drug monitoring?
opciones: The barrier gel can absorb drugs such as carbamazepine, lidocaine, phenobarbital and phenytoin
The clot activator in the gel tube breaks down phenytoin before the serum can be separated
The gel prevents the sample from being carried on ice and in the dark as drug levels require
The gel tube cannot be centrifuged, and drug assays are run only on centrifuged specimens
preguntas.explicacion: For therapeutic drug monitoring the laboratory turns away tubes with serum separator gel, because the barrier can soak up some drugs, carbamazepine, lidocaine, phenobarbital and phenytoin among them; they were recovered from the gel after extraction with methanol, and plain tubes without gel are suggested instead. Ice and darkness are the methotrexate rule, not a property of the tube.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2)(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(3)(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A hard-of-hearing patient cannot make out her date of birth when it is read back to her for identification. What does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Give the sounds context: name a word for each confusable letter, and say the digits one by one
Give the sounds volume: repeat the whole date louder and at a higher pitch until she agrees
Give the sounds time: repeat the whole date slowly, one syllable at a time, until she agrees
Give up on speech: hand her the requisition and have her point to her own date of birth on it
preguntas.explicacion: Some letters and numbers sound so alike that no amount of repeating separates them for a patient who is hard of hearing. The advice is to build context around them instead: pin a letter to a word that starts with it, and split a two-digit number into its digits rather than saying the number whole. Care is asked for especially with the letters that sound alike. Volume is the wrong lever — shouting distorts the sounds of speech and a raised pitch is harder to hear, not easier.

preguntas.subtema: Backup before a move · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The server holding the record system is about to be carried to a new suite. Which physical safeguard specification speaks to that move?
opciones: Data backup and storage: a copy that can be retrieved exactly is made before the move
Contingency operations: facility access is arranged so that lost data can be restored
Disaster recovery plan: the written procedures that restore data once it has been lost
Emergency mode operation: the critical processes keep running while systems are down
preguntas.explicacion: Three of these belong to the contingency family and answer what happens after an emergency. The one written for a planned movement of equipment is data backup and storage, an addressable specification of device and media controls: copy the information first, so that a mishap in transit does not take the only version with it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", Home Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 k83 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: When is CPR started on a patient who has just had a seizure?
opciones: Only once the seizure has clearly ended and breathing or pulse is absent
As soon as breathing pauses during the stiff phase of the seizure
As soon as the lips turn blue, even while the jerking continues
Only after the patient has been fully awake for several minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are not begun while the convulsion is running: CPR waits until the seizure has clearly stopped and the patient is found not breathing or without a pulse. A temporary stop in breathing and clenched teeth are part of the seizure itself. Every seizure is reported to the patient's provider afterward.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a walker — Going from Sitting to Standing
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.iii · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being taught to stand up from a chair using a walker. What is the instruction?
opciones: Push up from the chair arms first, then take hold of the walker handles
Pull up on the walker handles, tilting it back for leverage while rising
Push up from the chair arms while a helper holds the walker steady in place
Pull up on one walker handle and one chair arm, rising toward the strong side
preguntas.explicacion: The walker is set in front with the open side facing the patient and all four tips on the floor. The patient leans slightly forward and pushes up with the arms from the chair arms or handrails, and only then grasps the handles. Pulling on the frame or tilting it to rise is what tips it over. Standing still until steady comes before the first step.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Problems with the collection tube
preguntas.subtema: Adjustments for blood flow · CPT D3 k67 k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: During a draw, an evacuated tube that was briefly uncapped earlier is pushed onto the needle and no blood enters it. What is the likely cause?
opciones: The vacuum inside the tube was lost when it was uncapped
The anticoagulant was missing from the tube during packaging
The needle bevel is lying against the wall of the vein
The tube was drawn out of sequence and its additive was spent
preguntas.explicacion: Among the issues of concern, the review notes that tubes can be damaged and that the vacuum can be lost when a tube is uncapped; without vacuum the tube cannot pull blood. A missing anticoagulant is listed as a separate packaging defect that turns plasma into serum, not a cause of no flow, and tube order affects additive carry-over rather than filling.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Provide written materials and videos in patients' languages
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: How are an interpreter and a translator distinguished in the health-literacy guidance?
opciones: Interpreters listen or watch then speak or sign; translators work in writing
Interpreters work in writing; translators listen and then speak or sign
Interpreters must be certified by the state; translators need no training
Interpreters handle spoken tongues; translators handle sign language only
preguntas.explicacion: They are described as two different professions with different skills. An interpreter listens or watches in one language and then speaks or signs in another; a translator reads text in one language and writes what it meant in another. Where materials are not available in the patient's language, an interpreter trained in sight translation reads the document aloud.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter and 24a
preguntas.subtema: Chain of custody form · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 chain of custody · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A donor refuses to put their initials on the tamper-evident seals of the two bottles. What is the consequence?
opciones: It is noted on the remarks line and the collection is completed as usual
It is recorded as a refusal to test and the urine is discarded at once
The collector initials the seals instead and the specimen goes out normally
A second collection is done under direct observation with new bottles
preguntas.explicacion: The donor is asked to initial each label or seal, but failing or refusing to do so is noted on the remarks line of the chain of custody form and the collection is completed; it is not a refusal to test. Refusing to sign the certification statement, or to give the donor information, is handled the same way. What does count as a refusal is walking out before the process ends, or refusing a second attempt.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Specific Gravity; pH)
preguntas.subtema: USG and pH ranges · PBT V.A physiology · CCMA 3D k116 · CMA I.C.10.a.(1)-(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair gives the usual reference ranges for urine specific gravity and urine pH?
opciones: Specific gravity 1.002 to 1.035; pH 4.5 to 8
Specific gravity 1.002 to 1.035; pH 7.2 to 8.0
Specific gravity 1.010 to 1.050; pH 4.5 to 8
Specific gravity 1.002 to 1.035; pH 5.5 to 9
preguntas.explicacion: Specific gravity normally falls between 1.002 and 1.035 (most often 1.016 to 1.022) and pH between 4.5 and 8 (most often 5.5 to 6.5); both are laboratory dependent, and a value of 1.010 corresponds to roughly 300 mOsm/kg. Urine is slightly acidic in health, and the commonest cause of an alkaline reading is a stale specimen in which bacteria have split urea into ammonia. Contrast media and proteinuria falsely raise the specific gravity; alkaline urine falsely lowers it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Menstrual Cycle", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k54 · RMA III.E.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports cycles of 25, 28 and 34 days. What decides whether that counts as regular?
opciones: The patient's age: a 9-day spread is regular at 43 but irregular at 26
The average length: any set of cycles averaging under 30 days is regular
The longest cycle: a cycle of 34 days is itself outside the normal frequency
The shortest cycle: a cycle of 25 days already counts as frequent menstruation
preguntas.explicacion: Regularity is judged by the spread between the shortest and the longest cycle, and the allowance changes with age: 7 days or less between ages 26 and 41, and 9 days or less from 18 to 25 and from 42 to 45. The same 9-day spread is therefore regular at 43 and irregular at 26. Infrequent menstruation means cycles longer than 38 days.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A hemolyzed specimen arrives for an erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Why is that a particular problem for this test?
opciones: Free hemoglobin reddens the plasma and hides the boundary that is read
Free hemoglobin clots the specimen and stops the red cells from settling
Free hemoglobin binds the citrate and leaves the specimen unanticoagulated
Free hemoglobin raises the viscosity so the red cells settle far too quickly
preguntas.explicacion: The reading is taken where the settled red cells end and clear plasma begins. Hemolysis releases hemoglobin into the plasma and turns it red, so that boundary can no longer be picked out; an icteric sample causes the same trouble with dark yellow plasma.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: An irregular strip carries 14 QRS complexes across the ten-second recording. What rate goes on the report?
opciones: 84 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by six
70 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by five
140 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by ten
56 per minute, from the beats in ten seconds multiplied by four
preguntas.explicacion: The square methods assume evenly spaced beats, so an irregular rhythm is counted across the whole ten-second strip and the count is multiplied by six. Fourteen complexes give 84 per minute, which falls inside the band of 60 to 100.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2; and Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which two practices are forbidden once a sharps container is in service?
opciones: Overfilling it, and emptying its contents out to use it again
Sealing it with a lid, and moving it closer to the drawing chair
Labeling it, and keeping it within arm's reach of the worker
Overfilling it, and sealing it before it has been fully filled
preguntas.explicacion: The container is sealed with a tamper-proof lid, and the two things not to do are overfilling it and decanting it. Keeping it within arm's reach and clearly visible is the correct practice, since the used device is meant to go in immediately rather than travel across the room.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: Why are range-of-motion exercises started as early as possible in a patient who cannot walk?
opciones: Changes in the joints can set in after three days of immobility
Changes in the joints can set in after three weeks of immobility
Muscle strength falls away within the first eight hours in bed
The joints stiffen only once the patient has been in bed a month
preguntas.explicacion: Range-of-motion exercises are prescribed when a patient cannot walk or has an injured limb, and they should begin as soon as possible: three days without movement is enough for the joints to start changing. Long-term programs exist to prevent contractures in conditions such as spinal cord injury and stroke.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cranial Nerve Testing", Technique or Treatment: Cranial Nerve II
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(10)(d) · RMA III.F.5.c
preguntas.pregunta: How are visual fields checked by confrontation at the bedside?
opciones: One eye at a time, examiner three feet away, object brought in from four quadrants
Both eyes open, examiner three feet away, object brought in from four quadrants
One eye at a time, examiner arm's length away, object held still in the center
One eye at a time, examiner three feet away, object moved out from the center
preguntas.explicacion: Each eye is tested on its own with the other covered, the patient fixing on the examiner's eyes or nose from about three feet, while a finger or pen is brought toward the center from each of the four quadrants and the patient says when it appears. Fields are described from the patient's point of view, and any deficit goes to an ophthalmologist.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Conducting telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth troubleshooting plan · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a patient's first video visit, what does the workflow guidance have the office tell her about technical trouble?
opciones: How to deal with problems, and what happens if they carry on, such as moving to audio only
How to deal with problems, and that the visit is canceled if they carry on past the start time
To ring the vendor's help line, which handles the problems the practice cannot resolve
How to deal with problems, and that a failed connection is logged as a missed appointment
preguntas.explicacion: On the list of things done before the visit, the office makes sure the patient knows what to do about technical problems and what happens should they persist, dropping to audio only for instance. The same list carries the reminder, guidance on the technology, the forms, a staff walk-through of audio, camera and lighting, consent, and finding somewhere quiet and private.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Patient Safety and Early Detection of Clinical Deterioration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the respiratory rate charted in an office often inaccurate?
opciones: It is estimated by eye rather than counted by a standardized method
It is counted while the patient talks, which raises the rate artificially
It is counted over 15 seconds, which is too short to be multiplied up
It is recorded from the oximeter, which reports a rate that is always low
preguntas.explicacion: Outside intensive care the respiratory rate is the least reliably measured of the vital signs: it is frequently estimated visually instead of counted by a set method, so accuracy and reproducibility both suffer. Documentation rates in one review ranged from under 1% to about 82%, and substituting an oximeter reading was one of the problems named.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cardiac Cycle", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What is going on between the closing of the mitral valve and the opening of the aortic valve?
opciones: Pressure is building while no blood leaves the ventricle
Blood is being driven quickly out of the ventricle
The ventricle is filling from the atrium above it
Pressure is falling as the ventricle starts to relax
preguntas.explicacion: That short stretch is isovolumic contraction: the muscle squeezes and pressure climbs, yet nothing leaves the chamber until the ventricle has beaten arterial pressure and the aortic valve gives way to ejection. The mirror stretch, after that valve shuts, is relaxation.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant is about to take a carotid pulse. Which precaution applies?
opciones: Only one side is palpated at a time, and the patient sits or lies down first
Both sides are palpated together so that the two can be compared for symmetry
The patient stands, so that the vessel fills better against gravity in the neck
Firm pressure is applied over the thyroid cartilage until the beat is felt clearly
preguntas.explicacion: The neck vessels are pressure sensitive in some people, and pressing them can bring on fainting or slow the heart, so the patient sits or lies down before the pulse is taken. Both sides are never pressed at once: doing so cuts blood flow to the head. The fingers go beside the Adam's apple, in the soft hollow, not on the cartilage.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Formulary
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether their new prescription is covered. Which document of the plan answers that?
opciones: The formulary, the plan's list of covered drugs
The plan's network directory of contracted providers
The preauthorization letter from the insurer
The claim the office files after the prescription is written
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the formulary as the list of prescription drugs a drug plan, or any plan with prescription benefits, will cover; the glossary also calls it a drug list. The network directory says which providers are contracted, not which drugs are paid for; a preauthorization is the plan's decision on one specific service or drug, not the list; and a claim is a request for payment sent after items or services are received.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(2) and (A)(3), Contaminated Sharps Discarding and Containment
preguntas.subtema: Moving a full sharps container · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finds the sharps container at her station filled to the marked line. What does the standard require before it is carried away?
opciones: Close it immediately before removal, and use a second closable container if leakage is possible
Press the contents down so the lid will close, then carry it to the soiled utility room
Open the lid and tip the sharps into a red bag that is closed before it is removed
Leave it in place until the end of the shift, the deadline set for contaminated surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(3) covers the moment a sharps container leaves the area where it was used: the lid goes on first, so nothing can spill or poke out while it is handled, and if the container could leak it travels inside a second one that closes, holds everything and carries the label or the color code. Paragraph (A)(2) already required the container to be replaced routinely and never allowed to overfill, so pressing the contents down is the opposite of the rule, and (A)(4) forbids opening or emptying a reusable container by hand. The end-of-shift deadline belongs to work surfaces in (d)(4)(ii)(A).

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What is gained by teaching a patient to recognize the warning signs of a faint?
opciones: The faint is often prevented and the risk of a traumatic fall drops
The faint is shortened, although the risk of a traumatic fall is unchanged
The blood pressure stays high enough for the draw to be completed
The pulse rate rises enough that the tourniquet may be left in place
preguntas.explicacion: Knowing the symptoms often prevents the episode outright and reduces the risk of a traumatic fall, because the patient lies down before consciousness goes. That is the practical reason for asking, before a draw, whether the person has ever fainted during an injection or a blood test.

preguntas.subtema: Calibration verification every 6 months · CPT D1 1F / k27 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: How often must a nonwaived laboratory perform calibration verification, and what materials does it use?
opciones: At least every 6 months, with a low or zero, a mid-point and a high value near the top of the range
At least every 12 months, with two control materials at different concentrations run in duplicate
Only when a control fails, with a calibrator from the same lot that was used to calibrate the system
Each day of testing, with a single calibrator traceable to a certified reference material
preguntas.explicacion: Calibration verification confirms the system still reads accurately across its reportable range. It runs at least once every 6 months, and again after a complete change of reagents, after major maintenance or after a critical part is replaced, when controls drift oddly or fall outside limits that other corrective steps will not fix, and whenever the laboratory's own schedule says so. Materials cover a minimal, a mid-point and a maximum value.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which sites are used for a pulse oximeter probe when the fingertip is not available?
opciones: The toenail bed, the earlobe, the forehead, the nasal alar or the lips
The toenail bed, the wrist over the radial artery or the inner elbow
The earlobe, the neck over the carotid artery or the top of the foot
The forehead, the upper arm under the blood pressure cuff or the ankle
preguntas.explicacion: Fingernail and toenail beds are the usual sites, and the lips, the nasal alar, the forehead and the earlobe have all been used successfully. In infants the palm, foot, arm, cheek, tongue and nasal septum are also options. Probes are calibrated for particular sites, so the site-specific sensor is used whenever one exists.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(B), (C) and (E), Labels
preguntas.subtema: Biohazard label · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What color and legend does OSHA require on a biohazard warning label?
opciones: Fluorescent orange or orange-red, with the biohazard symbol and legend in a contrasting color
Bright yellow with a black skull and crossbones, the GHS pictogram for acute toxicity
Red with white lettering, matching the red bags that may replace the label
Fluorescent orange-red with a black frame set on a point, as on chemical labels
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraphs (g)(1)(i)(B) and (C) fix both the color and the wording. The background is fluorescent orange, or orange-red, or a color that is predominantly one of the two; against it the BIOHAZARD legend and symbol are printed in a contrasting color; and the label is affixed so that it cannot be lost or removed by accident. Red bags or containers may stand in for the label under (g)(1)(i)(E), but the label itself is nowhere described as red with white text. A skull and crossbones, and a red square standing on one point, belong to Hazard Communication chemical labels rather than to this standard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Grading the exposure · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: In the three-step assessment of an occupational HIV exposure, what does the first step establish?
opciones: Whether an infectious fluid was involved, and by which route and how severe
Whether the source patient is on treatment and what the viral load is
Whether prophylaxis is indicated or observation alone is enough
Whether the worker completed the hepatitis B vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The three steps run in a fixed order, and the first describes the exposure itself: blood, another body fluid able to carry infection, or a device with blood on it, together with the route and the severity. Intact skin carries no meaningful risk. On a mucous membrane the volume and the contact time count. For a percutaneous injury what matters is whether the needle was solid or hollow-bore and whether it had been sitting in a vein or artery. Step two is the source patient's status, and step three is the decision on prophylaxis.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Unsolicited advice
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k40 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.g / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient mentions she is thinking of stopping a medicine, and the phlebotomist tells her what to do. Which pitfall is that?
opciones: Unsolicited advice, which can feel intrusive and unempathetic
Providing false reassurance, which can rupture the relationship
Changing the subject abruptly, which can come across as dismissive
Responding defensively, which closes off the patient's own view
preguntas.explicacion: Advice the patient never asked for lands as intrusive and lacking in empathy, unless they have expressly asked to be advised. False reassurance risks a severe rupture in the relationship, above all when the desired outcome is not achieved; an abrupt change of subject can be perceived as dismissive; and a defensive answer leaves the patient no room to express frustration.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is standing height measured with a stadiometer?
opciones: Buttocks, shoulder blades and heels touch the board, and footwear is removed first
Only the heels touch the board, and the patient looks upward at the headpiece
The patient leans back against the board with the knees slightly bent for balance
Buttocks and heels touch the board while the shoulders are rolled forward and relaxed
preguntas.explicacion: Shoes and hair ornaments come off, and the buttocks, shoulder blades and back of the head rest against the board while the headpiece is brought down onto the crown. The head is held in the Frankfort horizontal plane and the patient takes a deep breath, which straightens the spine and steadies the reading.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Interprofessional Team Members (Social Workers)
preguntas.subtema: Team member roles · CCMA 4G k167 · CMA II.F.4.c / 2027 II.F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which team member helps set up community resources according to a patient's financial needs?
opciones: The social worker, who also gives psychological support and counseling
The dietitian, who also teaches about regular and therapeutic diets
The pharmacist, who also guides safe and effective use of medicines
The prosthetist, who also fits and adjusts an artificial body part
preguntas.explicacion: Social workers counsel patients and support them psychologically, arrange community resources to suit the patient's financial situation, and belong to the team keeping care continuous after discharge. Dietitians handle regular and therapeutic diets and dietary education, pharmacists safe prescribing and dispensing, and prosthetists the fitting of an artificial limb.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(c) and (d), Standards: Privacy and safety; Confidentiality of patient records
preguntas.subtema: Access to hospital records · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Under 42 CFR 482.13(d), how may a hospital patient request access to their own medical records?
opciones: By oral or written request, in the format requested if readily producible
Only by written request notarized and signed by the attending physician
Only through an attorney, since records are hospital property
Only after discharge, once the record has been completed and coded
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard gives the patient access to their medical records, the current ones included. The request may be spoken or written; the record arrives in whichever form and format was asked for when that is readily producible, electronic included, and otherwise as readable hard copy or in some agreed format, within a reasonable time. The hospital may not frustrate legitimate efforts to obtain records, and it has to answer as fast as its record system allows. The same standard protects the confidentiality of clinical records and, separately, the right to personal privacy and to care in a safe setting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", section Definitions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k18 · CCMA 6 k194 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: What does 'gender identity' mean?
opciones: One's own sense of gender, matching or differing from the sex assigned at birth
The appearance, dress, mannerisms and speech associated with femininity or masculinity
The sex recorded for an infant on the basis of the external genitalia
The gender that an observer assigns to a person on first meeting them
preguntas.explicacion: The glossary defines gender identity as the sense a person has of their own gender, which may line up with the sex assigned at birth or may differ from it. The neighbouring entries are the distractors: gender expression covers appearance, dress and mannerisms; sex assigned at birth rests on an infant's external genitalia; and gender attribution is the gender an observer takes someone to be.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: In published studies of laboratory errors, which phase of the total testing process consistently accounts for more than half of all errors?
opciones: The pre-analytical phase
The analytical phase
The post-analytical phase
The post-post-analytical phase
preguntas.explicacion: Taken together the two extra-analytical phases carry four to five times the errors of the analytical phase, and the pre-analytical phase on its own accounts for over half of all errors in the published series; an Italian stat laboratory found the same split in 1996 and again in 2006, 62 % of errors before the analysis, 15 % inside it and 23 % after it. The analytical phase itself runs close to 5 sigma.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Amendment
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.1.c right to amend records · RMA I.C.1.b disclosure laws
preguntas.pregunta: A patient believes her recorded date of birth is wrong and asks the laboratory to correct it. If the laboratory denies the request, what must it do?
opciones: Give her a written denial and let her file a statement of disagreement in the record
Give her a written denial and refer her to the provider who first entered the data
Amend the record anyway, because a patient's own identifying data cannot be refused
Give her a written denial and forward the request to HHS for a compliance review
preguntas.explicacion: The right to amend covers information in the designated record set that is inaccurate or incomplete. A covered entity that accepts the amendment must make reasonable efforts to pass it to the people the individual names and to those who might rely on the old data to her detriment. A denial has to be written, and she can then submit a statement of disagreement to sit in the record alongside it.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?, Special Enrollment Period
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signs up for Part B during the eight-month window that opened when she retired. When does that coverage begin?
opciones: The month after her completed forms reach Social Security
The same month her completed forms reach Social Security
The first day of the calendar quarter that follows them
Three months after the forms are signed and posted off
preguntas.explicacion: The special enrollment period for Part B runs for eight months from the day the patient or the spouse stops working, or from the end of the job-based coverage, whichever of the two lands first. Coverage starts in the month that follows the arrival of her completed forms at Social Security or at the Railroad Retirement Board, and an extra form proving the job-based coverage goes in with them.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 6. Disinfectant Fogging
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What position does the guideline take on disinfectant fogging of a patient-care area?
opciones: Do not do it for routine purposes
Do it weekly in procedure rooms
Do it after every spill of blood
Do it in place of terminal cleaning
preguntas.explicacion: Fogging a room with disinfectant is not to be done for routine purposes in patient-care areas. Environmental surfaces are handled by cleaning housekeeping surfaces regularly and when they are visibly soiled, by wet-dusting horizontal surfaces with a cloth moistened in an EPA-registered product, and by decontaminating spills promptly.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: P-wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A strip in sinus rhythm is checked wave by wave. Which P wave description is normal?
opciones: Three small squares wide, positive in leads I and II
Five small squares wide, positive in leads I and aVR
Three small squares wide, negative in leads I and II
Two small squares wide, biphasic in leads I and II
preguntas.explicacion: A normal P wave is about three small squares wide and two and a half tall. In sinus rhythm it is always upright in leads I and II because atrial activation spreads downward from the sinoatrial node, it is consistently negative in aVR, and it is often biphasic in V1.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: negligence (Legal Duty of Care)
preguntas.subtema: Negligence · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(1) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the duty of care in a clinic come from?
opciones: From the relationship itself, as between a doctor and a patient
From the written service agreement the patient signs at check-in
From the facility's accreditation by an outside review organization
From the professional license the state issues to the practitioner
preguntas.explicacion: Duty is the first element of negligence, and some relationships create it by themselves. The list runs from a shop and its customer, or an inn and its guest, to a landowner and a lessee and, of course, a doctor and a patient. It can also arise from creating the risk, from knowing that one's conduct will harm the person, or from voluntarily undertaking to protect them.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2D k15 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: How should a phlebotomist decide how to address an older patient?
opciones: Default to formal terms such as Mr. or Ms., and ask how they prefer to be addressed
Use first names, which feel warmer to most older adults than formal titles
Use affectionate terms such as 'dear' to put the patient at ease quickly
Use the name the companion uses for the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Speak to the patient as a fellow adult and establish respect by using formal language as the default, such as Mr. or Ms., and avoid familiar terms like 'dear', which can be perceived as disrespectful; staff can also check with patients about the form of address they prefer. Older people may be used to more formal terms of address.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.2
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · CPT D3 k62 · D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.F.2 · CCMA 3E4 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which collections fall outside the scope of the best-practice guidance on drawing blood?
opciones: Indwelling central lines, arterial lines, cord blood and stem cells
Pediatric venous draws, capillary sampling and donor collection
Arterial blood gases, capillary sampling and adult venous draws
Blood for transfusion, cord blood and adult capillary sampling
preguntas.explicacion: The document covers venous and arterial sampling and collection for transfusion in adults and children, but it says it does not deal with collection from indwelling central lines, from arterial lines or of cord blood, and it does not cover stem cell collection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Indications; and Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is least likely to manage crutches?
opciones: A very elderly patient, who may lack the torso strength and coordination
A patient with a sprained ankle who has been told to keep weight off it
A patient with full upper body strength recovering from knee surgery
A patient who needs support for a few weeks while a fracture knits
preguntas.explicacion: Crutches call for enough upper body strength and coordination to carry and move one's own weight. Age is the contraindication named most often: the very old and the very young may not have the torso strength or the coordination for them. The other three are the ordinary indications for crutch use.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Storage
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.D.2.f
preguntas.pregunta: A sealed instrument pouch is found lying on a shelf beneath a sink with a damp corner. What is its status?
opciones: Contaminated, because moisture carries microbes in from the air and the surfaces around it
Still sterile, because the heat seal is unbroken and moisture only affects woven wraps
Still sterile, because event-related shelf life counts only tears and punctures as events
Contaminated, but only if the pouch also passed the expiration date printed on its label
preguntas.explicacion: Sterile items that get wet are considered contaminated, since moisture brings microorganisms with it from the air and from surfaces. That is exactly why supplies are not to be stored under sinks or anywhere else they can become wet. Wetness is one of the named events that ends event-related shelf life, alongside a tear, a puncture or a broken seal.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Coping with Chronic Illness, Summary
preguntas.subtema: Psychology of chronic illness · CCMA 1E k32 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient newly diagnosed with a chronic illness says he is angry and feels out of control. What is suggested?
opciones: A trained counselor and support groups, to regain control
A change of provider, so the diagnosis gets reconsidered
A pause in all teaching until the anger settles on its own
A referral for laboratory testing to rule out depression
preguntas.explicacion: A long-term illness can bring fatigue, pain, changes in appearance, lost independence and money trouble, and those changes can produce stress, anxiety and anger. Seeking help matters: a trained counselor can build strategies for regaining a feeling of control, and support groups show the person they are not alone.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Treatment for the Exposure: HCV; CDC, Guidelines for Health Care Personnel Exposed to Hepatitis C Virus, HCV postexposure prophylaxis
