preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis C after exposure · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck with a needle used on a patient known to have hepatitis C. What does the CDC say about prophylaxis?
opciones: No vaccine and no recommended PEP exist; follow-up testing finds infection early so it can be treated
Immune globulin is given within 24 hours, followed by baseline and 6-month antibody tests
A 28-day antiviral course is started within 72 hours, as for HIV
A single dose of vaccine plus HBIG is given if the worker's antibody level is under 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: Hepatitis C has no vaccine and no post-exposure treatment that prevents infection: no immune globulin and no antiviral therapy are recommended once the exposure has happened. The 2020 guidance declines to recommend routine PEP with direct-acting antivirals, noting a percutaneous transmission risk near 0.2 percent, and sets a testing schedule instead so that infection is caught and treated early. Immune globulin, and HBIG with vaccine, are hepatitis B measures; the 28-day course begun within 72 hours is HIV PEP.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · CMA I.A.1.g · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with chronic pain goes from 7 out of 10 to 5 out of 10 and can now shop and sleep. Which tool captures that gain?
opciones: The pain, enjoyment and general activity tool, which scores function alongside intensity
The numeric rating scale, whose two-point change already carries the whole story
The 4-item Patient Health Questionnaire, which screens for depression and anxiety
The Geriatric Pain Measure, a 24-item questionnaire covering the preceding week
preguntas.explicacion: A drop of two points looks small on its own. The tool that scores pain, enjoyment of life and general activity from 0 to 10 each, where higher means worse, shows the improvement in daily function that the intensity number misses. It is quick, repeatable and usable in any setting.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Health Care Settings (Primary Care)
preguntas.subtema: Levels of care · CCMA 1A k7 · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Immunizations, health screening and wellness teaching in a clinic belong to which level of health care?
opciones: Primary care, the level that promotes wellness and works to prevent disease
Secondary care, the level reached once a person has an illness or an injury
Tertiary care, the level that treats the long-term effects of a chronic condition
Palliative care, the level that treats the discomfort of a serious illness
preguntas.explicacion: Health care runs on several levels. At the primary level the work is promoting wellness and preventing disease: protection such as immunizations, education, screening done early, and attention to the environment; physician offices, public health clinics and school nursing are typical settings. Secondary care starts once someone has contracted an illness or injury, and tertiary care aims at restoring function after chronic disease.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asystole", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: What does asystole look like on the monitor, and how is it handled?
opciones: A flat line with no P, QRS or T, and it is not shockable
A flat line with no P, QRS or T, and it is shocked at once
A wavy line with no clear complexes, and it is not shockable
A flat line between wide complexes, and it is shocked at once
preguntas.explicacion: Asystole is the complete stop of electrical and mechanical activity, so the monitor shows a flat line without P waves, QRS complexes or T waves. It is not a shockable rhythm: once it is confirmed on at least two leads, defibrillation is not attempted and high-quality compressions continue.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) Test, Is there anything else I need to know about an A1C test?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a blood disorder is told her A1C may not be the right test for diagnosing diabetes. Which conditions are named alongside hers as making the figure unreliable?
opciones: Anemia and other blood disorders, kidney failure and liver disease
Anemia and other blood disorders, high cholesterol and heart disease
Prediabetes, polycystic ovarian syndrome and a family history of diabetes
Being overweight, a stroke in the past and gestational diabetes
preguntas.explicacion: Where a condition affects the red cells, as anemia and other blood disorders do, the coated fraction stops mirroring the average glucose; kidney failure and liver disease can shift the figure as well, and another test is used instead. The test is also not used to diagnose gestational diabetes. Weight, a stroke and a family history are reasons to be tested, not reasons to distrust the number.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Interfering Factors (Foods and Drugs) and Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Color)
preguntas.subtema: Urine color interferences · PBT V.A physiology · CCMA 3D k116 · CMA I.C.10.a.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's urine is pink-red, yet the reagent strip is negative for blood. Which is a recognized cause of red urine of this kind?
opciones: Eating beets or blackberries, or taking rifampin
Eating asparagus, or taking methylene blue
Eating carrots, or taking phenazopyridine
Eating fava beans, or taking metronidazole
preguntas.explicacion: Foods and drugs can change the color, odor or pH of urine without any blood being present. Pink or red urine is associated with beets, blackberries, rhubarb, food dyes, rifampin, phenolphthalein and senna, among others. Asparagus and methylene blue turn urine green or blue, carrots and phenazopyridine orange, and fava beans and metronidazole brown to black. A sample that reddens on standing suggests porphobilinogen.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(b), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D5 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A courier delivers a batch of specimens from a clinic. Which piece of information does CLIA require the receiving laboratory to document at that moment?
opciones: The date and time the specimen was received
The name of the courier and the vehicle used
The temperature inside the transport container
The number of tubes drawn from each patient
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1242(b) the laboratory must record the date and time at which it receives each specimen; the same data point reappears in 493.1283 as a required element of the test record system. Transport temperature and packaging belong to the laboratory's own written procedures for transport conditions, and courier or tube counts are not federal requirements.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: Caregivers · CCMA 6C k195 · CMAA 2A k13 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives at the visit with an adult daughter. What is settled first?
opciones: How the patient sees the companion's role in the visit
How the daughter would summarize the medical history
Whether the daughter can sign the visit paperwork
Whether the patient will step out for a private word
preguntas.explicacion: To protect and honor privacy, ask the patient how they see the companion's role before going on. Sit so both can be addressed face to face and do not aim the remarks only at the companion. Asking the companion to step out comes later, for sensitive topics or a check of the patient's cognition.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Treadmill Stress Testing", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: How is the Bruce protocol organized?
opciones: In 3-minute stages, each one faster and at a steeper grade
In 5-minute stages, each one faster and at a steeper grade
In 3-minute stages, each one slower and at a flatter grade
In one long stage held at a fixed speed and a fixed grade
preguntas.explicacion: It is the protocol used most often on the treadmill, built from successive three-minute stages in which the patient walks faster and up a steeper slope, aiming for a total of six to twelve minutes. The modified version adds two easier stages ahead of stage one for patients who cannot exert themselves.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin, Considerations; and StatPearls, "StatPearls (NBK482331) — Petechiae" (NBK482331)
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: petechiae, purpura, ecchymosis · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: How is bleeding into the skin distinguished from simple redness (erythema)?
opciones: Bleeding into the skin does not blanch when pressed; erythema does
Bleeding into the skin blanches when pressed; erythema does not
Bleeding into the skin is always larger than 2 mm; erythema is smaller
Bleeding into the skin is warm to the touch; erythema is cool
preguntas.explicacion: Redness of the skin should not be taken for bleeding: an area of bleeding into the skin does not go paler under pressure, whereas the redness of erythema does. The same test defines a non-blanching spot: one that does not disappear after brief pressure. Size separates petechiae (under 2 mm) from purpura (over 2 mm), not bleeding from erythema.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE; Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Putting on the mask · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What must be done as a mask or respirator is put on, before the eye protection?
opciones: Shape the band to the bridge of the nose and check the fit
Loop the straps under the chin so it can be pulled down later
Tuck the lower edge under the collar of the gown that is on
Wet the inner layer so it seals against the skin of the face
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the mask or respirator comes second, after the gown. Its ties or straps are placed around the head and neck, the flexible band is adjusted to the bridge of the nose so that it fits, and a respirator gets a fit check. Anyone required to use a respirator such as an N95 must also have been fit tested beforehand, and where fit testing cannot be done a powered air purifying respirator may be considered.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, What is informed consent?; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Withdrawing consent · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who signed a consent form for a procedure says she has changed her mind. What does patient-rights guidance say?
opciones: She may change her mind about consent at any time
She is bound by the signed form until the procedure is done
She may withdraw only if a second physician agrees
She may withdraw only in writing, with 24 hours' notice
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is a process in which the provider gives the information needed to decide, including the risks and benefits of the care and details of the condition, and the patient must understand it before consenting; a signature on a form is written consent, but the patient has the right to change her mind at any time. The CMS condition frames the same idea as the right to make informed decisions and to request or refuse treatment. No second opinion, notice period or written withdrawal is required to revoke consent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality checks · CPT D3 3B k57 k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A tube left the factory without the anticoagulant it should contain. What happens when it is used?
opciones: The blood clots and yields serum where plasma was required
The tube keeps its vacuum but draws only half its volume
The plasma settles above a gel barrier as in a PST tube
The red cells haemolyse because no additive protects them
preguntas.explicacion: Among the problems listed for collection tubes is an anticoagulant missing at packaging, which means serum is used for testing where plasma was meant to be. That is a different fault from a damaged tube whose vacuum was lost when it was uncapped, and no gel appears in a tube that never held one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pregnancy Dating", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.d · RMA III.F.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which method dates a pregnancy most accurately?
opciones: Ultrasound before 13 6/7 weeks, measuring the crown-rump length
Ultrasound between 18 and 20 weeks, with the full anatomic survey
Fundal height in centimeters, taken with a non-elastic tape measure
The last menstrual period, when the patient is sure of the first day
preguntas.explicacion: First-trimester ultrasound is the most accurate, within about five to seven days, and it uses the average of three crown-rump measurements. Past a crown-rump length of 84 mm, around 14 weeks, accuracy drops and full fetal biometry takes over. Fundal height is mostly used to follow growth, and menstrual dating is used until an ultrasound overrules it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a walker — How to Walk with Your Walker
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.iii · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a new walker sets it two feet ahead and steps toward it. What should be corrected?
opciones: The walker goes only a short distance ahead, and the weaker leg steps in first
The walker goes a short distance ahead, and the stronger leg has to step in first
The distance is right, but both feet must move at once with the weight on the arms
The distance is right, but the walker has to be lifted rather than rolled forward
preguntas.explicacion: The walker is pushed or lifted a few inches, at most an arm's length, ahead. All four tips or wheels have to touch the floor before any weight goes on it, and then the weaker leg steps in first, followed by the other leg placed in front of it. Space is kept between the patient and the frame, with the toes inside it, or balance is lost.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What is it used for?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which set names medicines listed as commonly monitored by blood level?
opciones: Vancomycin, digoxin, phenytoin and lithium
Vancomycin, ibuprofen, phenytoin and insulin
Amoxicillin, digoxin, warfarin and lithium
Amoxicillin, ibuprofen, warfarin and insulin
preguntas.explicacion: The table of commonly monitored medicines groups antibiotics such as amikacin, gentamycin and vancomycin; heart medicines such as amiodarone, digoxin, lidocaine and procainamide; anti-seizure medicines such as phenobarbital and phenytoin; cyclosporine and tacrolimus for autoimmune disease; and lithium and valproic acid for mental health conditions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge for coagulation · CPT D3 k56 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Coagulation factor testing is ordered. Which needle gauge range is suggested for coagulation specimens, and which end of the range is preferred for factor assays?
opciones: 19 to 22 G, with 19 G preferred to limit hemolysis
19 to 22 G, with 22 G preferred to limit hemolysis
16 to 18 G, with 16 G preferred for a faster fill
23 to 25 G, with 23 G preferred to protect the vein
preguntas.explicacion: For most coagulation tests the suggested needle range is 19 G to 22 G, and a wider needle, 19 G for instance, may be preferred for coagulation factor and platelet function testing to minimize hemolysis and keep the sample intact. Preferring 22 G gets the reasoning backward, 16 to 18 G is the blood donation range, and 25 G is not given in any of the sources.

preguntas.subtema: Evaluation standard · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice has just merged with another and doubled its staff. Which Security Rule standard is triggered by a change of that kind?
opciones: Evaluation, a periodic technical and non-technical check of the safeguards in place
Assigned security responsibility, which names the official who runs the policies
Isolating clearinghouse functions, which walls off part of a larger organization
Response and reporting, which identifies and documents any security incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Evaluation calls for a periodic review, technical and non-technical, showing how far the policies and procedures still meet the rule's requirements. The baseline is the standards as first implemented, and the review is repeated whenever changes in the environment or in operations bear on the security of the information, which is exactly what a merger is.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN: NPI - What You Need to Know
preguntas.subtema: National Provider Identifier · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: What is the National Provider Identifier assigned to a clinician?
opciones: A ten-digit number carrying no information about the provider
A nine-digit number that encodes the State where the provider practices
A ten-digit number that changes whenever the provider moves or is renamed
A number issued by each health plan for use in its own claims only
preguntas.explicacion: The NPI is a ten-digit numeric identifier that carries no information about the provider, not the State of practice, not the provider type, not the specialization, and it stays the same when name, address or taxonomy change. The registry that assigns it is NPPES. In HIPAA standard transactions it takes the place of older provider identifiers.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.1 and 2.2.3, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: Why is drawing a specimen through an intravenous or central line a hemolysis risk as well as a contamination one?
opciones: It sits on the published list of factors that increase hemolysis
It sits on the published list of factors that increase clot formation
It sits on the published list of factors that increase nerve damage
It sits on the published list of factors that reduce tube vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Taking a specimen through an intravenous or a central line is itself one of the listed factors that raise hemolysis, quite apart from the contamination and the dilution by fluid and medication that make an existing peripheral access a poor source of specimens.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Storing Your Medicines: Store Medicines Safely
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k23 · CMA I.D.1.e · RMA III.G.3.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient keeps her medicines in the bathroom cabinet. What do you advise?
opciones: Move them to a cool, dry place, because heat and moisture damage medicines
Move them to the refrigerator, which is the correct place for any medicine
Leave them there, but transfer each one into a labeled weekly pill box
Leave them there, but add the cotton ball back into each bottle for dryness
preguntas.explicacion: Heat, air, light and moisture damage medicines, and the heat and moisture from a shower, a bath or a sink make the bathroom cabinet a poor place: pills can lose potency or spoil before the expiration date. A dresser drawer, a kitchen cabinet away from the stove and sink, a shelf or a closet is better. Medicines stay in their original container, and the cotton ball is taken out because it pulls moisture in.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Otoscopy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62 · NCMA 2B.10
preguntas.pregunta: An otoscope is about to be used on a 6-month-old. Which way is the pinna pulled?
opciones: Posteriorly and inferiorly, which is the direction used under 12 months
Posteriorly and superiorly, which is the direction used in adult patients
Anteriorly and inferiorly, which shortens the canal in a small infant
Straight outward without any traction, since the canal is already straight
preguntas.explicacion: Pulling the pinna straightens the external auditory canal so the tympanic membrane comes into view. Under 12 months the pull is back and down; in adults it is back and up. The hand not holding the otoscope does the pulling, and the speculum then goes in gently while the canal is inspected for inflammation, discharge, cerumen or infection.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Droplet precautions
preguntas.subtema: Airborne Precautions without an AIIR · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k98 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic has no airborne infection isolation room and a patient with suspected measles arrives. What does the CDC advise?
opciones: Mask the patient and place them in a private room with the door closed until transfer or discharge
Place the patient in the waiting area at least 3 feet from others, as for Droplet Precautions
Seat the patient in an exam room with the door open so air can circulate freely
Turn the patient away, since without an AIIR there is no way to isolate airborne spread
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC anticipates settings that lack the engineering resources for an AIIR: put a mask on the patient, place them in a private room with the door shut, and the chance of airborne spread falls while they wait to be transferred to a facility with an AIIR or sent home. The 3-foot separation is the fallback StatPearls describes for Droplet Precautions when no room is available, not for airborne pathogens; an open door defeats the purpose; and turning the patient away is not among the CDC's options.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Finding a telehealth vendor
preguntas.subtema: Platform capacity · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to bring a specialist into some of her video visits. Which question about the platform settles whether that is possible?
opciones: Whether it allows more than two participants in one telehealth session
Whether it supports visits taken on demand rather than booked in advance
Whether it limits the number of individuals who may use the technology
Whether it integrates with the electronic health record the practice keeps
preguntas.explicacion: Among the questions put to a prospective vendor are whether the product supports on-demand visits, what it costs and whether the charge is per visit or a single one, whether there is a cap on the number of individuals who may use it, and whether it allows more than two participants in a session, for instance when a specialty consult is to be brought in.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Manually retractable evacuated tube systems
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3A 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a manually retractable evacuated tube system described as safer than a needle and syringe?
opciones: It needs no transfer of blood, and it allows many tubes per puncture
It needs no training, and it costs less than a needle and syringe does
It needs no tourniquet, and its vacuum is lower than in ordinary tubes
It needs no holder, so there is no disassembly step after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: This system is called safer because the blood never has to be transferred and several samples can be taken through one venepuncture, while its safety mechanism prevents reuse. It still requires skill and extra training, costs more, and reusing its holder brings back the disassembly risk.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A 9-month-old's length and weight are plotted on the WHO charts. Which band is treated as the normal range on those charts?
opciones: The 2nd to the 98th percentile, two standard deviations either side of the mean
The 5th to the 95th percentile, the band that those particular charts mark out
The 10th to the 90th percentile, one standard deviation either side of the mean
The 3rd to the 97th percentile, three standard deviations either side of the mean
preguntas.explicacion: The two chart families draw the normal band differently. On the CDC charts it runs from the 5th to the 95th percentile, with the 85th to 95th marked as overweight or at risk. On the WHO charts normal is two standard deviations either side of the mean, z-scores of −2.0 to +2.0, which works out as the 2nd to the 98th percentile.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note records only appendicitis, with nothing about acute or chronic. Which code does the coder assign?
opciones: The default code, the one listed beside that main term in the Alphabetic Index
The other specified code, the one the Index marks with the abbreviation NEC
The acute code, because acute is the nonessential modifier under that term
No code at all, until the provider has been queried about the missing detail
preguntas.explicacion: The code sitting next to a main term in the Alphabetic Index is the default code. It stands either for the condition most commonly associated with that term or for its unspecified code, and the guidelines take appendicitis as the example: document the condition without anything further, acute or chronic for instance, and the default code is what gets assigned.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Quality assurance · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1E k28 · PBT VI.A.1 · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which elements make up the quality assurance framework set out for phlebotomy?
opciones: Training, written procedures, patient identification, sample condition, transport, incident reports
Training, written procedures, patient billing, sample volume, storage, satisfaction surveys
Equipment purchase, staff rotas, patient identification, tube color, transport, audit visits
Training, tube color coding, patient billing, sample condition, storage, incident reports
preguntas.explicacion: Quality assurance here is built from education and training, standard operating procedures, correct identification of the patient, the condition of the sample, safe transportation and a system for reporting incidents. Each element is there to keep one kind of mishap out of the process.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guides
preguntas.subtema: SAFER guide structure · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: How is the 2025 set of guides on the safe use of record systems arranged, and where should an organization begin?
opciones: Eight guides in three groups, starting with the two foundational ones
Eight guides in two groups, starting with the one on contingency planning
Three guides in eight sections, starting with the section on patient safety
Eight guides in three groups, starting with the group on clinical processes
preguntas.explicacion: The set holds eight guides sorted into foundational, infrastructure and clinical process groups, and most organizations are told to start with the foundational pair and then go where their own concerns are. The high priority guide gathers sixteen recommendations pulled from the other seven.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(7), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 k112 k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition for a Pap smear arrives with the patient's name, date of birth, sex and the ordering provider, but nothing else. Which item specific to this test must the requisition solicit under CLIA?
opciones: Her last menstrual period, and any earlier abnormal report, treatment or biopsy
Her parity and the date of her last cervical examination by the ordering provider
The name and address of the laboratory that examined her previous cervical smear
The patient's fasting status and the time elapsed since her last sexual intercourse
preguntas.explicacion: On top of the general requisition elements, 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(7) makes the Pap smear requisition ask for the date of the patient's last menstrual period and whether she has had an abnormal report, treatment or biopsy before; paragraph (c)(8) then sweeps in whatever else a particular test relevantly and necessarily requires. Parity, contraception and the address of a previous laboratory are not named there, and fasting has nothing to do with this specimen.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · RMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of abbreviations is confused with the other and appears on The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list?
opciones: MS or MSO4 for morphine sulfate, and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate
HCT for hydrocortisone, and HCTZ for hydrochlorothiazide on an order
MTX for methotrexate, and HCT for hydrocortisone written on an order
IU for the international unit, and IV for the intravenous route used
preguntas.explicacion: MS and MSO4 stand for morphine sulfate and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate, and each is read as the other; both carry the double asterisk that marks The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list, and the fix is to write the complete drug name. HCT and HCTZ are confused the same way and MTX is read as mitoXANTRONE, but those rows do not carry that mark. IV is not an abbreviation on the list at all.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.2 Basic Concepts Related to Wounds
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: New capillaries begin to grow into a wound at about what point, and what is that process called?
opciones: About 24 hours after the injury, and it is called angiogenesis
About 24 hours after the injury, and it is called epithelialization
About three weeks after the injury, and it is called angiogenesis
About five to seven days after the injury, and it is called contraction
preguntas.explicacion: Capillaries start developing inside the wound roughly a day after the injury, during angiogenesis, and they bring oxygen and nutrients in. That is why dressing changes are done so as to protect the granulation tissue and its fragile new vessels. Epithelialization is the growth of new epidermis, and contraction closes the wound down at the end of the proliferative phase.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture (not a blood culture), how does the WHO say the site should be disinfected?
opciones: A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then let it dry completely, about 30 seconds
A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then insert the needle at once while the skin is still wet
Povidone iodine for 30 seconds, since it disinfects better than alcohol before a routine draw
A 70% alcohol swab kept wet for 10 minutes, the contact time given for bleach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 gives the numbers: a 70% alcohol swab applied for 30 seconds, then complete drying, which takes about 30 seconds more. Blood cultures are the one exception the step names. The guideline says that too little contact time raises the risk of contamination, so the drying is part of the disinfection rather than a delay, and inserting while wet skips it. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, because iodine can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results. Ten minutes wet is the contact time the guideline gives for a bleach solution on a blood spill, not for skin.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · RMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: An order arrives written as "amoxicillin 500 mg PO QD". Why should the frequency be clarified before the dose is given?
opciones: QD is read as QID, so a once-daily dose can be given four times in a day
QD is read as QOD, so a once-daily dose can be given every other day only
QD is read as PO, so an oral dose can be given by an entirely wrong route
QD is read as PR, so an oral dose can be given as a rectal suppository
preguntas.explicacion: QD stands for once a day and gets read as QID, four times daily, above all when a handwritten q trails off or the period that follows it looks like the letter i. That is a four-fold overdose of an antibiotic. The abbreviation carries the double asterisk of The Joint Commission's Do Not Use list, and the recommended practice is to spell daily out rather than abbreviate the frequency at all.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: How is a double-ended needle joined to the barrel of a vacuum system?
opciones: The end covered by a rubber cuff screws in, past a central thread
The end that enters the vein screws in, past a central thread
Both ends are pushed in, and a locking collar holds them together
The cuffed end is held by a luer-lock connector, as a winged set is
preguntas.explicacion: The needle has a point at each end. The end sheathed in rubber screws into the barrel, which is also called the tube holder, and a thread between the two ends is where that connection is made. The barrel then holds the tube and keeps the worker away from direct contact with blood.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Bleeding", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: A patient cuts a forearm on a broken specimen tube and the wound is bleeding freely. What is the first step?
opciones: Press directly on the wound with a sterile dressing or a clean cloth
Press on the artery above the wound at the nearest pressure point
Wrap a tourniquet above the elbow and write down the time it went on
Rinse the wound under running water until the bleeding slows down
preguntas.explicacion: Direct pressure is the first and most important step, and it stops most external bleeding; gloves go on first. Pressure points are no longer recommended, because collateral circulation defeats them. A tourniquet is a later step, for bleeding that continuous pressure has failed to control and that threatens life.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Organizational Options
preguntas.subtema: Joint notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Several practices in an organized health care arrangement produce one joint notice. What happens when a patient is given that notice by one of them?
opciones: The distribution duty is met for every covered entity the joint notice applies to
The distribution duty is met only for the entity whose staff handed the notice over
The distribution duty is met for the visit in hand, and starts again at the next site
The distribution duty is met once the patient signs an acknowledgment at each site
preguntas.explicacion: Where entities take part in an organized health care arrangement they may issue one joint notice, provided certain conditions are met, among them that the notice say which entities and which service delivery sites it applies to. Once any one participant gives that notice to an individual, the distribution requirement is satisfied for all of them as regards that individual.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient walks in from the car park, sits down, and the phlebotomist reaches for the tourniquet at once. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Have him sit for at least 15 minutes first; posture changes alter results
He should lie down for 2 minutes first, the time it takes the veins to fill
He should stand for a few minutes first so the arm veins distend
Draw right away; posture matters only for coagulation samples
preguntas.explicacion: Changing a patient's position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is kept for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the draw, and office patients are advised to sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand. Any unavoidable change of posture is recorded so that the results can be interpreted.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists CVA in the problem list. Which event does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A cerebrovascular accident, that is, a stroke
A cardiovascular arrest, that is, a heart attack
A central venous access, that is, a line placement
A chronic valvular anomaly, that is, a valve defect
preguntas.explicacion: CVA stands for cerebrovascular accident, the event patients call a stroke or a brain attack. A smaller, temporary version is a TIA, a transient ischemic attack. A heart attack is written MI or AMI, for myocardial infarction, and the two are worth keeping apart because the treatments differ.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Anatomical Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A procedure note says the patient was placed prone. How was the patient lying?
opciones: Face down, the opposite of the supine face-up orientation
Face up, the opposite of the supine face-down orientation
On the left side, with the right shoulder turned upward
Sitting upright, with the trunk raised above the hips
preguntas.explicacion: When a patient is horizontal, the note says prone or supine: prone means face down, supine means face up. Both words turn up in physical examination notes and in surgical procedure notes. Confusing them puts the patient the wrong way round for whatever follows.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: A PNAS study looked at medical trainees who held false ideas about how Black and White bodies differ biologically. What did holding those ideas lead to?
opciones: Lower ratings of Black patients' pain and less accurate treatment recommendations
Higher rates of hypertension among the trainees who held the beliefs
More referrals of Black patients for kidney transplantation
Overtreatment of pain in Black patients compared with White patients
preguntas.explicacion: Medical students and residents who endorsed ideas such as thicker skin or duller nerve endings rated the pain of Black patients lower, and their treatment recommendations came out less accurate, a legacy still visible in the undertreatment of pain. The kidney example runs the other way: a race-corrected eGFR delays diagnosis and narrows access to transplantation.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant pulls up a chair to talk with a patient who has just been given a new diagnosis. What does the SOLER mnemonic call for?
opciones: Sit with an open posture, lean in, hold eye contact and stay relaxed
Stand at eye level with the arms folded and keep the pace brisk
Stay four to ten feet away, on your feet, with the chart in hand
Sit within the patient's view and raise the voice to hold attention
preguntas.explicacion: SOLER is the mnemonic used for nonverbal communication: sitting with open posture, leaning in, good eye contact, done in a relaxed manner. Bringing a chair to the bedside helps, because initial or sensitive exchanges land better when both people are at eye level. Folded arms are listed among negative body language.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Delivery discrepancies · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: The contents of a vaccine delivery do not match the packing list and a temperature excursion is suspected. What happens to those doses?
opciones: They are labeled not for use, kept apart in the storage unit, and the maker is called
They are put into stock and used first, so that no dose is wasted before it expires
They are returned to the carrier at once, since the office never took delivery of them
They are discarded on the spot and the loss is recorded in the inventory account
preguntas.explicacion: A discrepancy or a suspected excursion is reported to the manufacturer immediately. Meanwhile the doses are marked so nobody uses them, and they stay in the proper storage unit but separated from the rest until somebody decides whether they are still viable. Publicly funded stock also means a call to the state or local immunization program.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), Non-verbal communication; and section Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k197 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which non-verbal behaviors signal active listening during the patient interview?
opciones: Eye contact, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient
Standing at a right angle to the patient, near the exit
Sitting at a safe distance and avoiding eye contact
Typing notes while nodding so the patient keeps talking
preguntas.explicacion: The table pairs expression, stance and gestures: eye contact and facial expressions that show interest, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient. Its footnote reserves distance and caution with eye contact for patients with psychosis or paranoia, and standing at a right angle near an exit is a de-escalation technique for agitation. NIA separately warns against talking while typing.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the light gray top tube (sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate) the usual choice for a glucose specimen?
opciones: Its antiglycolytic additive keeps the glucose level stable for days
Its gel separator keeps the plasma away from the cells after spinning
Its clot activator produces serum faster than a plain red top tube
Its broth mixture keeps microorganisms alive until they can be cultured
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table describes the additive of the gray tube as an antiglycolytic agent, that is, one that blocks the breakdown of glucose, and says it keeps the glucose value stable for up to five days. Glucose is the use the table gives for it, with a note that it needs a full draw because a short draw may cause hemolysis. Gel separators belong to the serum separator and PST tubes, the clot activator to the red top, and the broth to the blood culture bottle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Safety cannulae come with active and with passive mechanisms. How do the two differ?
opciones: Active ones need the user to act; passive ones deploy on withdrawal
Active ones deploy on withdrawal; passive ones need the user to act
Active ones retract the needle; passive ones bend the tip over safely
Active ones work only in adults; passive ones work only in children
preguntas.explicacion: Both kinds shield the needle once it leaves the cannula hub. An active system waits for the user, typically a button that pulls the needle into a plastic sheath, while a passive system puts a small guard out by itself as the needle is withdrawn. The same split is used for phlebotomy devices.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order for a pain medication is marked PRN. What does that tell the person giving it?
opciones: It is given as needed rather than on a fixed schedule
It is given four times a day on a fixed schedule
It is given once at bedtime on a fixed schedule
It is given only by the intravenous route as ordered
preguntas.explicacion: PRN on a prescription means as needed, so the dose is tied to the patient's symptoms instead of the clock. The scheduled frequencies have their own abbreviations, such as BID, TID and QID. A route is written separately, and IV stands for intravenous while IM stands for intramuscular.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Preparing the Patient; Safety Issues
preguntas.subtema: Limitations section of the insert · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Before running a waived test, where does the guidance say to look for medications or other substances that could interfere with the result?
opciones: Under Limitations in the instructions the manufacturer supplies with that test
In the Safety Data Sheet supplied by the manufacturer for the test reagents
On the CLIA Certificate of Waiver that is posted in the testing area
In the quality control log kept for the current lot of test kits
preguntas.explicacion: Preparing the patient includes going over pretest information: the medical indications, any medication, anything else that might interfere and shift the result. Where that is set out is usually the Limitations section of whatever instructions the manufacturer supplies. The site also checks that pretest instructions were kept to, fasting for a glucose test for instance. The Safety Data Sheet is there for exposures, not for test interferences.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Mechanism of Action: Absorption; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia — Therapeutic drug levels (artículo 003430) (003430)
preguntas.subtema: Peak timing · CPT D2 k45 high and low levels · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: At what moment does an intravenous drug such as vancomycin reach its serum peak concentration?
opciones: Immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed
Immediately before the intravenous infusion is started
About 12 hours after the intravenous infusion is completed
About 30 minutes before the following dose is administered
preguntas.explicacion: Vancomycin has a rapid onset, with the serum peak concentration reached immediately once the intravenous infusion finishes; that is the moment a peak sample represents. The 30-minutes-before-the-dose window is the trough, and 12 hours after the dose is the collection time for lithium, tacrolimus, cyclosporine and sirolimus, none of which are given as short intravenous infusions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Health Information Privacy and Control
preguntas.subtema: Minors and confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A sixteen-year-old is seen alone for treatment of a sexually transmitted infection. Who usually controls that information?
opciones: The minor, since state law commonly grants confidentiality here
The parent, who is the personal representative in every case
The school nurse, who must be told of a reportable infection
The insurer, which receives the record with the claim it pays
preguntas.explicacion: When a patient lacks the legal capacity to decide, information goes to a surrogate, and for a child that is normally the parent. State law carves out exceptions: a minor who has been emancipated keeps control, and so does one who is sexually active and comes in alone for contraception or for care of a sexually transmitted infection. Reportable infections still reach public health authorities under a separate exception, which is not the same as sending word to a school.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): How do I apply?; When can I begin testing?
preguntas.subtema: CMS-116 to the state agency · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.v · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: A new urgent care wants to run only waived tests. What is the correct sequence to obtain its CLIA Certificate of Waiver?
opciones: Complete Form CMS-116, send it to the state agency, pay the fee, then test once the certificate arrives
Register with the FDA CLIA database, pay the fee to CMS, then begin testing the same day
Request an on-site survey from the state agency, pass it, then submit Form CMS-116 to CMS
Enroll in a proficiency testing program, submit the first results, then apply on Form CMS-116
preguntas.explicacion: The application for every certificate type is Form CMS-116. It goes to the state agency for the state where the site is located, which processes it and sends a fee coupon; after payment the certificate is mailed. Testing generally begins once the certificate is received, and the state may add its own requirements. No survey or proficiency testing is a precondition for a Certificate of Waiver.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.15(e)(1); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), CLIA Requirements for Waived Testing
preguntas.subtema: Follow the manufacturer's instructions · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Once a site holds a Certificate of Waiver, what is the ONLY CLIA requirement for how each waived test is performed?
opciones: Work to the test's current instructions from the manufacturer
Run external controls each day patient samples are tested
Enroll every analyte in an approved proficiency testing program
Have testing personnel who meet the CLIA education requirements
preguntas.explicacion: A waived site is not routinely inspected and has no personnel requirements to meet: it obtains the certificate, pays the biennial fee, runs only waived tests, and works to the manufacturer's current instructions. Quality control is required only where the insert requires it, and proficiency testing is voluntary. That single requirement is also the one CMS surveys of waived sites find broken most often.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: How is a HCPCS Level II code built, and who decides on additions and deletions to it?
opciones: One letter followed by four numeric digits, with CMS maintaining the set
Five numeric digits, with the American Medical Association maintaining the set
One letter followed by six numeric digits, with the NUCC maintaining the set
Three to seven characters, with the National Center for Health Statistics in charge
preguntas.explicacion: Level II codes are alphanumeric: a single alphabetical letter followed by four numeric digits, and CMS maintains them, including additions, revisions and deletions. Level I is CPT, a numeric system of five digits kept by the American Medical Association. The three-to-seven-character structure belongs to ICD-10-CM instead.

preguntas.subtema: Integrity standard · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the integrity standard of the Security Rule address?
opciones: Information being altered or destroyed when nobody was authorized to do so
Information being unavailable to a clinician who has the right to consult it
Information being seen by a member of staff whose role does not need it
Information being sent to the wrong recipient by a mistake at the keyboard
preguntas.explicacion: Integrity is defined as the property of data not having been altered or destroyed by anyone without authorization, and the standard calls for policies protecting against exactly that. Its addressable specification is an electronic mechanism corroborating that the information is still as it was. Availability and confidentiality are the other two objectives, not this one.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Media Mail
preguntas.subtema: Media Mail eligibility · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office wants to post a set of training videos on memory sticks at the cheapest media rate. What does the Postal Service say about that?
opciones: Digital drives do not qualify, and disallowed contents mean a higher rate is charged
Digital drives do not qualify, and the parcel is returned to the sender unopened
Digital drives qualify where the content is educational and the parcel is under 70 lb
Digital drives qualify, and only computer games are excluded from the media rate
preguntas.explicacion: The media rate is a cheap route for books, media and educational material that qualify, but only certain kinds of media are allowed: video games are named as not qualifying, and so are computer drives and digital drives. Enclosing something that is not allowed means the sender or the recipient pays the higher postage, and these parcels may be opened and inspected.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which preanalytical problem tops the list of reasons clinical laboratories reject a sample, and how big is it?
opciones: In vitro hemolysis, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
Clotted samples, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
In vivo hemolysis, present in about 2 % of routine samples and most rejected specimens
Insufficient volume, up to 22 % of routine samples and the majority of unsuitable specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis is the preanalytical error seen most often, and hemolysis occurring in vitro is the single largest reason samples are rejected: it reaches 3.3 % of all routine samples and covers 40 to 70 % of unsuitable specimens, close to five times more than other causes such as clotted or incorrect samples. Fewer than 2 % of samples with detectable hemolysis broke down in vivo, so the damage is done during collection and transport.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5: Administering Subcutaneous Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(2) · RMA III.G.2.a(ii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A very thin patient with little fat at the chosen site needs a subcutaneous injection. Which angle is used?
opciones: 45 degrees, because 90 degrees is used for normal-sized and obese patients
90 degrees, because 45 degrees is used for normal-sized and obese patients
5 to 15 degrees, which is the angle chosen whenever the tissue layer is thin
15 to 45 degrees, adjusted within that range to the fold that can be pinched
preguntas.explicacion: A subcutaneous injection enters at 45 or 90 degrees depending on the size of the patient and how much adipose tissue lies at the site: 90 degrees for a normal-sized or an obese patient, 45 degrees for someone thin or with little fat there. The skin is pinched first and released once the needle is in. The 5 to 15 degree range is the intradermal angle, not a thin-patient version of this one.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the Do Not Use list ban IU for international unit?
opciones: It is misread as IV or as the number 10, so unit is written out
It is misread as mL or as the number 15, so unit is written out
It is misread as IM or as the number 11, so unit is written out
It is misread as ID or as the number 12, so unit is written out
preguntas.explicacion: IU sits on the list because it gets taken either for IV, an intravenous order, or for the number 10, and either misreading changes the order completely. Write unit or units instead: an international unit can simply be called a unit. The same reasoning bans the plain U.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What is it used for? and Why do I need TDM?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A prescriber orders a drug level with the note 'is he actually taking it?'. Which listed use is that?
opciones: Making sure the medicine is being taken as it was prescribed
Finding the best dose when the medicine is first started
Watching for the symptoms of a serious side effect of the drug
Checking that an immune response has not rejected the drug
preguntas.explicacion: Therapeutic drug monitoring may also be used to make sure a patient is taking the medicine as prescribed. Its other listed uses are settling the right dose when a medicine is first started, testing regularly so it stays effective without becoming harmful, and testing where symptoms of a serious side effect appear. Rejection by the immune system is watched for with biologics.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order is handwritten as 4U of insulin. Why is that on the Do Not Use list, and what should be written?
opciones: The U can read as a zero or a four, so the word unit is spelled out
The U can read as an IV order, so the word unit is spelled out
The U can read as a liter, so the abbreviation mL is used instead
The U can read as a nanogram, so the word microgram is spelled out
preguntas.explicacion: Written by hand, the U for units is mistaken for a zero or for the number four, so 4U can be read as 40 and 4u as 44, a tenfold overdose or worse. The fix is to spell out the word unit. Reading it as an intravenous order is the hazard of IU, and the liter confusion belongs to the lowercase letter l.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Interoperability: TEFCA
preguntas.subtema: Interoperability · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 7 k97 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does TEFCA establish, according to ONC?
opciones: A nationwide floor of governance, policy and technical rules for interoperability
A federal registry listing every patient treated in the United States by name
A certification that every medical office must earn before buying an EHR system
A payment program that reimburses practices for each record they send elsewhere
preguntas.explicacion: TEFCA lays a nationwide floor of governance, policy and technical rules for interoperability, cuts down the connections an organization needs in order to exchange information securely, and gives individuals a way of gathering their own health information. ONC also runs a voluntary certification program for health IT and obliges certified products to adopt the USCDI data set.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: Parents and Unemancipated Minors
preguntas.subtema: Minors and representatives · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a parent whether he may speak with her sixteen-year-old confidentially, and the parent agrees. What follows under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: The parent stops being the personal representative for that care
The parent keeps full access, since minors have no separate privacy rights
The minor becomes emancipated for every purpose the rule recognizes
The physician must document the conversation on the accounting of disclosures
preguntas.explicacion: A parent is normally a minor child's personal representative, since it is normally the parent who holds the authority to decide about health care. The rule sets out three exceptions: where State law does not require parental consent for the service and the minor gives it; where somebody else is authorized by law to consent and does so; and where the parent assents to a confidential arrangement between the provider and the minor, which is exactly the conversation described.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Quality assurance · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1D 1E k26 k28 · PBT VI.A.1 · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: What should training for everyone who draws blood include, according to the quality assurance table?
opciones: Anatomy, the risks of blood exposure, and what poor infection control causes
Anatomy, the cost of consumables, and how to file an insurance claim
Pharmacology, the risks of blood exposure, and the layout of the laboratory
Anatomy, the history of bloodletting, and the maintenance of centrifuges
preguntas.explicacion: Education and training is required for all staff who draw blood, and it should cover the anatomy, an awareness of what exposure to blood can bring, and what follows when infection prevention and control are poor. Written procedures sit beside it as a second element.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient slumps forward in the exam room but is coughing and moving an arm. What should the assistant do?
opciones: Hold off on compressions, call for help, and keep watching the breathing
Start 30 compressions and 2 breaths, since the patient is not fully alert
Give two rescue breaths first and then decide about compressions
Place the defibrillator pads and let the machine decide about compressions
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are not started on someone who has normal breathing, coughing or movement: pressing on that chest can stop a heart that is still beating. Help is summoned and the patient is monitored closely until the ambulance arrives. Compressions begin only when the patient is unresponsive with absent or gasping breathing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What do the two numbers of a blood pressure reading represent?
opciones: The peak pressure during ventricular systole and the lowest during diastole
The pressure in the arteries and the pressure returning through the veins
The pressure at the heart and the pressure measured out at the brachial artery
The average pressure over the cycle and the pressure added by each contraction
preguntas.explicacion: The upper figure is the peak arterial pressure while the ventricle contracts and the lower one is the trough during relaxation. A third value, mean arterial pressure, is derived from the two and approximates the average pressure across the cardiac cycle. The pair is written with a slash between them and the units after.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: Minimum Necessary
preguntas.subtema: Role-based access · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Scheduling staff can open any chart in the system, including those of patients they never book. Why is that a minimum necessary problem?
opciones: Access has to be limited by role to the information each person needs to do the job
Access has to be logged in an accounting of disclosures given to the patient every six years
Access has to be reviewed case by case before any employee opens a record for any purpose
Access has to be approved in advance by each patient through a signed authorization form
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities must adopt policies identifying who in the workforce needs PHI, which categories they need and under what conditions. Routine access does not require case-by-case review, but unimpeded access by someone whose job does not call for it means the standard is not being applied, and any incidental disclosure that follows, such as a conversation overheard, becomes an unlawful one.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(ii), Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Contents of the medical record · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs in the confidential medical record an employer keeps for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: The hepatitis B vaccination dates and the written opinion of the professional
The type and brand of the device involved and the work area where it happened
The names and job titles of everyone who attended the annual training session
A copy of the exposure control plan, signed by the employee once every year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(ii) fills the record with the employee's name; the hepatitis B vaccination status, with the date of every dose and any record bearing on whether the person could be vaccinated; the results of examinations and of follow-up after an exposure incident; the copy the employer holds of the written opinion from the healthcare professional; and a copy of everything sent to that professional. Device brand and work area are sharps injury log entries under (h)(5)(i); names and job titles of those who attended belong to the training record under (h)(2)(i).

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Procedures: Immunochemical methods
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.c.i · CCMA 3B3 k64
preguntas.pregunta: What advantage does the fecal immunochemical test have over the guaiac card?
opciones: It needs no dietary restriction and is more sensitive for colon lesions
It needs no dietary restriction because it reads peroxidase far better
It detects bleeding in the upper gut, which the guaiac card cannot find
It can be read at home without a laboratory, which the guaiac cannot be
preguntas.explicacion: The immunochemical test uses an antibody against hemoglobin instead of a peroxidase reaction, so food does not interfere and no diet is required, and it is more sensitive than guaiac for lesions in the colon. It is also more specific for lower gut bleeding, because globin from the upper tract is broken down by digestive enzymes before it arrives.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2, Selecting the length of lancet
preguntas.subtema: Lancets · CPT D3 k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: A finger-prick is planned for a 5-year-old. What puncture depth does the WHO recommend for this age?
opciones: 1.5 mm
2.4 mm
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.2 gives 1.5 mm as the recommended finger-prick depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years, and 2.4 mm for a child over 8 years, which is also the limit an adult finger-prick should never exceed. The 0.85 mm lancet is the one available for premature neonates, and 3.32 mm is the distance from skin to bone at the medial and lateral heel of a 3 kg baby.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Shock", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Into which four broad categories is shock divided?
opciones: Obstructive, cardiogenic, hypovolemic and distributive
Septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic and endocrine in origin
Compensated, uncompensated, refractory and irreversible
Hemorrhagic, non-hemorrhagic, traumatic and infectious
preguntas.explicacion: The four categories are obstructive, cardiogenic, hypovolemic and distributive. Septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic and endocrine shock are subtypes of the distributive group, which is defined by peripheral vasodilation. Pre-shock, shock and end-organ dysfunction are the stages a patient passes through, not the categories.

preguntas.subtema: Timing of advance directive information · CCMA 5D · CMA I.A.5 · RMA I.C.1.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: At what moment must a rural emergency hospital hand a patient the written information on advance directives?
opciones: When the patient is registered as a patient of the hospital
When the patient is admitted to the hospital as an inpatient
When the patient is first seen by the treating practitioner
When the patient is discharged, along with the follow-up plan
preguntas.explicacion: Each kind of provider has its own moment. A hospital gives the information at admission as an inpatient and a skilled nursing facility at admission as a resident; a home health agency does it before the patient comes under its care, at the latest on the first home visit and before care; a hospice at the first receipt of care; a rural emergency hospital at registration.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccination offer · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A newly hired phlebotomist begins drawing blood on Monday. By when must the employer make the hepatitis B vaccine available to her?
opciones: Within 10 working days of the initial assignment, after the required training
Within 15 days of the initial assignment, the deadline for the written opinion
Within 30 days of the initial assignment, before the first annual training
Only after a prescreening antibody test shows the employee is not immune
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(i) sets the clock: the vaccine and the series are offered within 10 working days of the initial assignment to a job with occupational exposure, and only after the employee has had the training on the vaccine described in (g)(2)(vii)(I). The offer is not owed if the employee already completed the series, has antibody testing showing immunity, or has a medical contraindication. Fifteen days is the deadline for the written opinion in (f)(5), and (f)(2)(ii) forbids making a prescreening program a condition of getting the vaccine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a video visit says she will be staying with family in another state that day. Which question does that raise for the practice?
opciones: Whether the clinician is licensed in the state she will be in
Whether her plan pays the same rate outside her home state
Whether the platform can reach a device on another network
Whether the visit still counts as a real-time appointment
preguntas.explicacion: As a rule the clinician needs a current license issued by whichever state the patient is sitting in while the encounter takes place, which is why her location on the day matters to the booking. Compacts between states, and waivers granted for a time, have opened practice across state lines in some settings, but they do not settle the question by themselves.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, nails and rings; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Personnel
preguntas.subtema: Fingernails and rings · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC recommend for a phlebotomist's fingernails?
opciones: Natural nails no longer than the fingertip; no artificial nails with high-risk patients
Artificial nails are acceptable if hand hygiene is performed with soap rather than sanitizer
Nail polish is recommended to seal the nail surface against transient organisms
Nails may be any length as long as gloves are worn for every patient contact
preguntas.explicacion: A natural nail is kept level with the fingertip and no longer, and artificial nails or extensions are not worn by anyone in direct contact with high-risk patients; the CDC also notes that the skin under a ring carries more germs. StatPearls adds that long or artificial nails have been tied to outbreaks in intensive care and surgical settings, that current guidance holds nails under 0.5 cm, and that they should be free of polish and of artificial coverings. Gloves cancel none of this, since they do not stand in for hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2 and section 4.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.3 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E10 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An add-on for a viral RNA test is requested on an EDTA whole blood tube that has been in the refrigerator for two days. Under the general stability guidelines for whole blood, can it be used?
opciones: No: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for only about 4 hours, though DNA holds 72 hours
Yes: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for 72 hours, the same period given for DNA
Yes: EDTA whole blood is stable for RNA targets at 2 to 8 °C for 5 days, the figure the guideline gives for plasma
No: whole blood is never acceptable for RNA targets; only serum stored for 2 to 7 days at 2 to 8 °C can be used
preguntas.explicacion: The general guideline for whole blood gives room temperature for 24 hours and 2 to 8 °C for 72 hours when DNA is the target, but only 4 hours at 2 to 8 °C for RNA, with EDTA or ACD as the additives; plasma is the specimen listed at 2 to 8 °C for 5 days and serum for 2 to 7 days. When RNA is the target the recommendation is a tube with an RNA-stabilising reagent, so a two-day-old EDTA tube fails the add-on.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Surgical wound care - closed: When to Call the Doctor; and Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e (Chippewa Valley Technical College, CC BY 4.0, NCBI Bookshelf), Chapter 20 Wound Care: valoración de heridas, tipos de cierre, retiro de suturas y grapas, curaciones, vendajes, irrigación (NBK593201)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: Which change around a healing incision should the patient be told to report to the surgeon?
opciones: The wound growing larger or deeper, or looking dried out and dark
The scar softening and flattening over the months after the operation
A thin line of new pink tissue closing across the length of the incision
A small amount of clear watery fluid on the dressing in the first days
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to call about more redness or pain, swelling or bleeding, a wound that is getting larger or deeper, and a wound that looks dried out or dark. Scars normally soften, flatten and pale over months, and a small amount of clear watery plasma early on is normal drainage during the inflammatory stage.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing well into the tubes. When does the WHO say the tourniquet should be released?
opciones: Before the needle is withdrawn, once enough blood has been collected
After the needle is withdrawn, while gentle pressure is applied with clean gauze
After it has been in place for two minutes, even if more tubes remain to be filled
As soon as the needle enters the vein, before any blood flow is established
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 is explicit: once sufficient blood has been collected, the tourniquet comes off BEFORE the needle is withdrawn; the gauze and gentle pressure come after the needle is out. The guideline adds that some other guidelines go further and recommend removing it as soon as blood flow is established, and in any case before two minutes have passed with it in place. Two minutes is therefore a ceiling, not the moment to release, and before flow is established is earlier than any guideline the WHO cites.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) Test, What is a hemoglobin A1C test?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · PBT II.G · RMA III.C.4
preguntas.pregunta: What does a hemoglobin A1C result represent?
opciones: The average blood glucose over the previous two to three months
The blood glucose level at the moment the sample was drawn
The average blood glucose over the previous two to three weeks
The share of red cells destroyed by high glucose in the past year
preguntas.explicacion: Glucose sticks to hemoglobin for the life of the red cell, red cells live about three months, and the A1C therefore reports the percentage of red cells with glucose-coated hemoglobin as an average of the past two to three months. A home glucose reading shows the level at that moment; weeks and a full year are the wrong time frames.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalist telephones the office and asks for the whole chart to treat a patient admitted overnight. How does the minimum necessary standard apply?
opciones: It does not apply, because the request comes from a provider and the purpose is treatment
It applies, so the office must send only the last progress note and withhold the rest
It applies, so the office must review the request individually against non-routine criteria
It does not apply, because a telephone request is an oral disclosure rather than a written one
