opciones: Outer upper arm, front of the thighs, upper back, upper gluteal area, abdomen
Ventrogluteal area, vastus lateralis and deltoid, chosen by age and body mass
Upper third of the forearm, outer upper arms, and the area between the scapulae
Deltoid alone, located three finger widths below the acromion process of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Subcutaneous doses go into the outer side of the upper arm, the front of the thighs, the upper back, the upper ventral gluteal area, and the abdomen between the costal margin and the iliac crest, staying more than two inches from the umbilicus. Each area is wide enough to rotate within it. Skin that is bruised, broken, scarred, over bone or poorly perfused is passed over.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Health Savings Account (HSA)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a health savings account can be used for. Which answer is correct?
opciones: Untaxed dollars for qualified medical expenses, but generally not for premiums
Untaxed dollars for premiums, but generally not for deductibles or copayments
Employer dollars that are lost in full if they are not spent by the plan year end
Plan dollars that pay the provider directly once the out-of-pocket limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: A health savings account lets a person set money aside before taxes and spend it on qualified medical costs such as deductibles, copayments and coinsurance; the funds generally may not go toward premiums, and only someone with an HSA-eligible plan may contribute. The use-it-or-lose-it design with an employer-set limit describes a flexible spending arrangement instead, and no savings account pays providers on the plan's behalf.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Pulse Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's radial pulse is full on the right and barely detectable on the left. Why does the difference between sides matter by itself?
opciones: An uneven pulse can mark major vascular disease such as an aortic dissection
An uneven pulse is a normal variant found in roughly a tenth of all people
An uneven pulse only reflects which arm the patient uses for daily work
An uneven pulse appears whenever the rhythm is irregularly irregular
preguntas.explicacion: A full pulse assessment goes beyond the rate to the rhythm, the volume and the amplitude, how fast the wave rises, and whether the two sides match. Symmetry earns its place because an uneven pulse may point to a coarctation of the aorta, to occlusive disease of a large vessel, or to a dissection of the aorta. That is why both sides are compared rather than one side measured and charted.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Where can I get help; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Who Monitors; 45 CFR 164.530(d) and (g)
preguntas.subtema: Privacy complaints · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Where can a patient file a complaint about a violation of their health information privacy rights?
opciones: With the HHS Office for Civil Rights
With the state insurance oversight agency
With the hospital's patient advocate only
With the long-term care ombudsman office
preguntas.explicacion: The Office for Civil Rights, at the federal Department of Health and Human Services, takes complaints from people who believe their health information privacy rights were violated, or who were discriminated against in their medical care; it investigates, audits, and may pass criminal matters to the Department of Justice. Patient advocates, state health departments, insurance oversight agencies and long-term care ombudsman offices handle other kinds of problem. A covered entity must also run its own complaint process and may not retaliate against anyone who files.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, comorbidity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.A.2.b · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: One patient's chart lists hypertension, chronic kidney disease and diabetes at once. Which term names that situation?
opciones: Comorbidity, when two or more diseases run at once
Etiology, the set of causes behind two or more diseases
Prevalence, the count of people who have several diseases
Remission, the fading of the signs of several diseases
preguntas.explicacion: Comorbidity means carrying more than one disease at the same time, and it changes both the risk and the plan of care. A risk factor is something else again: anything that raises the chance of developing a disease, such as age, family history, tobacco use or exposure to radiation or certain chemicals.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medicare: Summary; and Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A 62-year-old patient with permanent kidney failure asks whether she can have Medicare. Who is the program for?
opciones: People age 65 or older, and some under 65 with a disability or kidney failure
People with low income, under the rules that each state writes for itself
Children in families that earn too much to qualify for the state plan
Workers whose employer purchases the coverage as a benefit of the job
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is the health insurance program the government runs for people aged 65 or over. Some people under 65 qualify too: those with disabilities, with permanent kidney failure or with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. It helps with the cost of care without covering every medical expense, and it has four parts: A for hospital insurance, B for medical services, C for Advantage plans and D for prescription drugs.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.4 Electrodes Falling Off
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k152 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: An electrode will not stay on a patient with a very hairy chest. What is the recommended fix?
opciones: Part the hair before applying it, and tape it down if needed
Shave the whole chest and apply a second electrode on top
Move the electrode one space lower where there is less hair
Use extra gel so that the electrode floats above the hair
preguntas.explicacion: Parting the hair first gives the adhesive a surface to grip, and on extremely hairy chests the electrodes may have to be taped down. Moving an electrode off its landmark is never the answer: even a small displacement of a chest electrode can change the pattern considerably.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, sections First Aid and DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the swollen bruise on the arm can be drained with a needle at home. What is the advice?
opciones: Do not drain it, and rest the bruised part rather than using it
Drain it only with a sterile lancet after cleaning the skin first
Drain it once the color has turned bluish, but not before that
Do not drain it, but keep exercising the arm to disperse the blood
preguntas.explicacion: The instructions are explicit: a bruise is not drained with a needle, the painful part is rested rather than worked, and pain and swelling are not ignored. What does help is ice wrapped in a clean towel and keeping the bruised area raised above heart level where that is possible.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.4
preguntas.subtema: Backup practice · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What backup arrangement does the contingency guidance describe for patient data?
opciones: A daily, complete, encrypted copy held off site and restored as a test regularly
A weekly complete copy kept on a second drive inside the same server cabinet
A monthly copy of the day's new entries stored with the software developer
A copy made each time the system is upgraded and kept until the next upgrade
preguntas.explicacion: What is recommended is a complete backup, encrypted and taken off site, every day, with the most critical data copied as near to real time as can be managed. Restoring the whole system and the patient data is tested regularly, monthly at best, and the media are kept physically apart from the working data, air-gapped ideally, so ransomware cannot reach them.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment, Tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with cognitive impairment hears you but does not understand the instruction. What should you do?
opciones: Rephrase the statement, without speaking any faster or louder
Repeat it word for word until it finally registers with him
Speak much louder, since hearing is usually the underlying problem
Ask the caregiver to answer so the visit stays on schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient can hear but does not understand, the clinician rephrases rather than repeats, and does not speak faster or louder. Tell the patient plainly that no one is judging their answers, and keep addressing the patient directly rather than only the caregiver.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations for Workers
preguntas.subtema: Planning disposal first · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which habit is recommended to workers so that a used needle never becomes a hazard in the room?
opciones: Plan how the needle will be handled and discarded before the procedure starts
Recap the needle with one hand until a container can be brought to the room
Set the used needle on the tray until the tubes have been labeled correctly
Carry the needle to the container at the end of the round of draws
preguntas.explicacion: The advice to workers is a short list: avoid needles wherever a safe alternative exists; help evaluate the safety devices and then use them; do not recap; before a procedure with needles starts, plan how they will be handled and disposed of; get them into the proper container promptly; report every injury without delay; point out hazards; and take part in training and in hepatitis B vaccination. Leaving a used sharp on a tray, or carrying it around, is exactly the delay this list exists to remove.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizure", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: How long does a convulsion have to last before it meets the definition of status epilepticus?
opciones: More than 5 minutes, or repeated seizures without waking in between
More than 15 minutes, the longest a seizure is expected to run
More than 2 minutes, the point at which the airway must be opened
More than 20 minutes, when second-line medicine is started
preguntas.explicacion: A seizure of more than 5 minutes, or seizures that repeat without the patient returning to baseline awareness, is status epilepticus. Symptoms of an ordinary seizure stop after seconds to minutes, and rarely run past 15 minutes. The 20-minute mark is when second-line medicine is added, not when the definition is met.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Burns", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which burn counts as major rather than minor?
opciones: A second-degree burn wider than 2 to 3 inches (5.08 to 7.62 cm)
A second-degree burn narrower than 2 to 3 inches (5.08 to 7.62 cm)
A first-degree burn of the forearm that covers most of the skin there
A first-degree burn on the hand that stings for more than a day
preguntas.explicacion: A first-degree burn anywhere on the body counts as minor, and so does a second-degree burn under 2 to 3 inches across. Major burns are all third-degree burns, second-degree burns wider than that, and second-degree burns on the face, the hands or feet, the groin or buttocks, or over any major joint. When the type is not clear, it is treated as a major burn.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Combined Nasal and Throat Swab; and CDC, Information on Collection of Respiratory Specimens for Influenza Virus Testing, Outpatients
preguntas.subtema: Avoid the tongue · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A combined nasal and throat swab is being collected for influenza. Which area does the throat swab deliberately miss?
opciones: The tongue, while the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas are swabbed
The tonsillar areas, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are both swabbed
The posterior pharynx, while the tonsillar areas and the tongue are swabbed
The soft palate, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are swabbed
preguntas.explicacion: For the throat half of a combined specimen, a second dry polyester swab goes into the mouth and collects from the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas, and the instruction is to avoid the tongue. Its tip then goes into the same transport tube as the nasal swab and the applicator is cut off. Combining nasal and throat in one specimen detects influenza better than either alone.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Stroke", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.k · 2027 I.B.8.k · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the time of onset of stroke symptoms recorded so carefully?
opciones: Clot-busting medicine has to start within 4½ hours of the first symptom
Clot-busting medicine has to start within 24 hours of the first symptom
Blood thinners cannot be started until 4½ hours have gone by safely
The imaging study cannot be read until 24 hours after the symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: When a clot is the cause, thrombolytic therapy dissolves it, but to work it has to be started within four and a half hours of when the symptoms began, and the sooner it starts the better the outcome. Many patients reach the hospital too late for it. A catheter procedure to pull the clot out may be needed instead.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Low blood sugar", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.f · 2027 I.B.8.f · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes becomes shaky, sweaty and confused while waiting, but can swallow and follow directions. What is offered?
opciones: Juice, a sugary drink or glucose tablets, and then the provider is told
An injection of glucagon into the muscle of the outer part of the thigh
A glass of water and a rest in a cool room until the shaking settles
No food or drink, because the glucose must be measured in the lab first
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who is awake and able to swallow is given fast sugar: juice or another sugary drink, food, or glucose tablets. Glucagon, a medicine that raises blood sugar, is the route when the patient cannot take sugar by mouth. If the signs do not improve after a snack with sugar, the patient goes to the emergency room and does not drive.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth access route · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5U k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is deciding how patients will reach the video visits it books. Which route does the workflow guidance name?
opciones: Through the patient portal, with an e-mail or text reminder sent before the appointment
Through a link the clinician reads out over the telephone as the appointment begins
Through whichever public video service the patient already has on her own telephone
Through an address on the practice web site that any visitor is able to join
preguntas.explicacion: Among the technology questions to settle in advance is how patients will reach a telehealth appointment, and the example given is through a patient portal, with an e-mail or text reminder. The same guidance asks whether the platform is easy to use and whether it merges with the electronic health record, and the platform itself has to meet the HIPAA Rules.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Personal Health Records
preguntas.subtema: Personal health record · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a personal health record is. Which description fits?
opciones: A record the patient keeps herself, pulling together what several offices hold about her
The legal chart the practice maintains, printed and handed to the patient once a year
The set of records a health plan keeps to adjudicate the claims it has received
The archive a hospital keeps of records for patients who have moved out of the area
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may have charts at several doctors' offices and another at a hospital, on paper or electronically, and those charts are the medical records. Keeping track of all of it is the reason for a personal health record, which starts with items such as name, birth date, blood type, emergency contact and a list of medicines and supplements with doses and how long they have been taken.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Sputum Specimens; and StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Sputum for tuberculosis · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.3 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · RMA III.C.4.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: Tuberculosis is suspected. How does the sputum collection differ from a routine sputum culture?
opciones: A series of 3 early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL is collected on separate days
A single early morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL is collected and sent the same day
A series of 3 specimens is collected 2 hours apart on the same morning and pooled
A series of 3 specimens is collected on separate days and kept at room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each is collected on consecutive days, refrigerated and returned to the laboratory daily; the refrigerator is where each one waits, not the bench. A routine culture takes a single specimen sent in the same day. In an uncooperative patient the organism can also be recovered from gastric contents by stomach aspiration.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Hospice Care: Hospice Interprofessional Team
preguntas.subtema: Team-based care in hospice · CCMA 4G k167 · CMA II.F.4.c / 2027 II.F.2.c · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which staff make up the core hospice team that Medicare requires the agency itself to employ?
opciones: The hospice nurse, the social worker and the chaplain, plus the medical director
The home health aide, the physical therapist and the dietitian who visit the home
The attending clinician, the consultant subspecialist and the pharmacist on call
The case manager, the patient navigator and the volunteer coordinator on staff
preguntas.explicacion: The core hospice team is the nurse, the social worker and the chaplain, and those members must be employed by the hospice agency. The hospice medical director also belongs to the interdisciplinary team. Together they build an individual plan of care for each patient and family, covering physical needs and psychological, social and spiritual ones, with the nurse coordinating.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Head injury - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.s · 2027 I.B.8.s · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fell and hit their head is unconscious, but breathing and heart rate are normal. What is done?
opciones: Steady the head and neck with both hands and keep them in line with the spine
Turn the head to one side and place a rolled towel under the neck for support
Sit the patient up against a wall and watch the pupils for any change
Shake the patient gently by the shoulder until some response is obtained
preguntas.explicacion: An unconscious patient after a head injury is handled as though the spine were injured: the head is held between both hands, kept in line with the spine, and movement is prevented until help arrives. The spine is always assumed injured in a head injury, the patient is not moved unless there is no choice, and a dazed patient is not shaken.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A triage note reads: patient reports SOB on climbing stairs. What is the patient describing?
opciones: Shortness of breath during exertion
Soreness of the back during exertion
Swelling of both legs during exertion
Stiffness of both knees during exertion
preguntas.explicacion: SOB is the charted shorthand for shortness of breath, a symptom the patient reports rather than a sign anyone can observe. Written out it belongs with the respiratory complaints, and it is one of the entries that should be spelled out in anything the patient will read at home.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advance Directives", Issues of Concern: Types of Advance Directives
preguntas.subtema: Advance directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a / 2027 E.7 · RMA I.C.1.f · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which two documents dominate among health care advance directives?
opciones: A living will, plus the durable power of attorney over health care
The living will and the hospital's own general consent-to-treat form
The DNR order and the hospital's notice of privacy practices
The DNI order and the surrogate list written into state law
preguntas.explicacion: Several kinds of advance directive overlap, but two dominate: the living will, in which the person writes down which treatments they want and which they refuse, and the durable power of attorney covering health care, which names someone to speak for them. A DNR is a clinician's order, not a directive the patient writes, and the state surrogate list only operates when nobody was named.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood
preguntas.subtema: Venipuncture technique · CPT D3 k65 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: At what angle does the WHO guideline say the needle should enter the vein?
opciones: Swiftly, at 30 degrees or less, then along the vein at the easiest angle
At 30 degrees or more, steepening the angle as the needle advances along the vein
At 90 degrees, straight down, as when piercing a tube stopper directly from above
At 30 degrees or less, with the thumb anchoring the vein just ABOVE the puncture site
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to enter the vein swiftly at an angle of 30 degrees or less and then keep advancing the needle along the vein at whatever angle gives the easiest entry: the angle does not steepen. The step pairs this with anchoring the vein first, holding the patient's arm with a thumb placed BELOW the puncture site, not above it, and asking the patient to make a fist so the veins stand out. Piercing straight down from above is how Step 7 fills a tube through its stopper, not how the needle enters a vein.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 heel site · PBT II.E site selection · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A 5-month-old infant who weighs 6 kg needs a capillary blood sample. Where is the lancet placed?
opciones: On the medial or lateral plantar surface of the infant's heel
On the side of the middle or ring finger, across the print
On the posterior curve of the heel, where the tissue is deepest
On the great toe, which has more tissue over bone than the heel
preguntas.explicacion: The capillary site is chosen by age and weight: heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, finger-prick over 6 months and above 10 kg. On the heel the lancet goes on the medial or lateral plantar surface. In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance is 3.32 mm there, only 2.33 mm at the posterior heel, which is to be avoided, and 2.19 mm at the toe.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Adjustments for blood flow · CPT D3 k67 3F · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E4 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's veins are small and hard to see. Which measures can improve the chance of success before the puncture?
opciones: Tapping the skin over the vein and applying a warm compress or briefly soaking the limb in warm water
Applying an ice pack for up to 15 minutes each hour so the vein wall becomes firmer
Keeping the tourniquet in place for two to three minutes so the veins fill completely
Asking the patient to fast for 12 hours and avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Measures that help include ballotting or tapping the skin over the vein, then the antiseptic preparation, and a warm compress or a brief soak of the limb in warm water, along with good positioning and lighting. Ice is first aid for a bruise, a two-to-three-minute tourniquet exceeds both the WHO and StatPearls limits, and the fasting rules concern the tests, not vein visibility.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 10: Consider Culture, Customs, and Beliefs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMA F.2.a · 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d cultural differences
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given a diet plan built entirely around foods her household never cooks. What does the toolkit say about that?
opciones: Dietary advice that ignores a patient's foods and cooking will be hard to follow
Dietary advice is followed regardless of custom once its purpose is explained
Dietary customs are a private matter and stay outside the treatment plan
Dietary advice should be replaced by a written plan the family signs
preguntas.explicacion: Culture takes in customs, beliefs and values, and it shapes how people understand health, care for themselves and weigh medical advice. Dietary customs are named among the ways it shows up: advice about disease-related eating is hard to follow when it does not fit the foods or the cooking methods the patient actually uses.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine 24-hour volume (003425), How the Test is Performed; and StatPearls, "24-Hour Urine Collection", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: 24-hour storage at home · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient brings in a 24-hour urine container that he kept on the kitchen counter for the whole collection day. What was wrong?
opciones: The container should have been kept refrigerated or in a cool place throughout the collection period
The container should have been kept frozen, since freezing preserves urine better than refrigeration
The urine should have been carried to the laboratory after each void instead of being pooled at home
The container should have been kept at body temperature and delivered within 30 minutes of the last void
preguntas.explicacion: During a 24-hour collection the capped container stays in the refrigerator or a cool place, and the sample is kept refrigerated throughout the period; a preservative may be added by the laboratory to stabilize it. Freezing is not an accepted replacement for refrigeration in urine preservation, the urine is pooled at home rather than delivered void by void, and body-temperature delivery within 30 minutes is the semen instruction.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Burden of Proof
preguntas.subtema: Breach documentation · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: After deciding an impermissible disclosure was not a breach, what does the practice have to be able to show?
opciones: Documentation of the risk assessment or of the exception it relied on
A signed statement from the patient agreeing that no harm was done
A letter from the Office for Civil Rights closing the matter without action
A note in the chart of every patient the practice treated on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Proving that every required notification went out, or that a use or disclosure was not a breach at all, falls on the covered entity or the business associate. It should hold on to either the risk assessment showing a low probability that PHI was compromised, or evidence that one of the exceptions applied. Entities also have to keep written breach policies, train staff on them, and sanction workforce members who do not comply.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse d · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Pulse intensity is graded from 0 to 4+. What does a grade of 3+ mean?
opciones: A normal pulse, easily palpable, neither diminished nor stronger than expected
A barely detectable pulse, felt only after the fingers press for several beats
A bounding pulse, clearly stronger than expected for that site and patient
A slightly diminished pulse, present but weaker than the other side of the body
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs 0 for nothing palpable, 1+ barely detectable, 2+ slightly diminished, 3+ normal and easily felt, and 4+ bounding. Writing 3+ therefore records a normal finding, not a strong one, which is where the grading is most often misread. The value is charted with the plus sign after the number.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Treadmill Stress Testing", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: What has to be at hand before an exercise stress test begins?
opciones: Resuscitation equipment and drugs, with staff trained to use them
A spare treadmill and monitor, with a technician trained on them
A signed refusal of consent, with a relative waiting in the room
An imaging scanner in the room, with a radiologist to work it
preguntas.explicacion: The test is generally safe: serious cardiac events run around one in ten thousand patients. Even so, everyone conducting it must be able to recognize and treat complications, emergency equipment and medicines stay within reach, and consent is taken.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: deposition; and Cornell Law School LII, Wex: subpoena duces tecum
preguntas.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(2) · RMA I.C.3
preguntas.pregunta: What happens at a deposition?
opciones: The witness gives recorded testimony under oath, outside the courtroom
The witness files a written opinion with the clerk before the trial opens
The witness answers the judge's questions in open court before the jury
The witness turns over the medical records the attorneys have requested
preguntas.explicacion: A deposition is sworn testimony given out of court, and the witness giving it is the deponent. It belongs to the discovery stage, and only in limited circumstances does it reach the trial itself. In the room are normally the deponent, the lawyers for every party with an interest, and someone qualified to swear the witness in, with a stenographer or an electronic recording. Demanding the records themselves is what a subpoena duces tecum does.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN006903 Medicare Secondary Payer
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does a Medigap policy do?
opciones: It helps pay the patient's share of costs left by Original Medicare
It helps pay the patient's share of costs left by a Medicare drug plan
It replaces Part A and Part B with benefits from a private insurer
It pays the Part B premium for beneficiaries with limited resources
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Supplement Insurance, or Medigap, is bought from a private company to help with copayments, coinsurance and deductibles in Original Medicare, and a person must have Part A and Part B to buy it. Coverage that stands in for Part A and Part B is Medicare Advantage. Paying the Part B premium for people with limited income and resources is what Medicaid does for dually eligible patients.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Active Listening and Attending Behaviors
preguntas.subtema: Active listening · CCMA 6C k202 · CMAA 2A k21 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: During a report a coworker keeps steering the exchange back to his own view of the case. Which type of listening is that?
opciones: Competitive listening
Reflective listening
Attending behavior
Passive listening
preguntas.explicacion: Three types of listening are described. Competitive listening is being focused on putting your own point of view across instead of hearing the other person. Passive listening is a lack of interest plus the assumption that you understood without checking. Active listening shows interest and verifies understanding with the speaker, and reflecting is one of its techniques.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies - for Hospital Patients, Are you at Risk for a Latex Allergy; and StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", sections Etiology and Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient denies any latex allergy but says bananas and avocados make her mouth itch. How should that be handled?
opciones: Treat her as at risk for a latex reaction and ask further before using latex items
Fruit allergies are unrelated to latex; proceed with the standard latex gloves
Only a chestnut allergy is linked with latex, so no precaution is needed here
She must have a skin prick test for latex before any draw can take place
preguntas.explicacion: Some people with latex allergy also react to foods whose proteins resemble those in latex, the latex-fruit syndrome; bananas, avocado and chestnuts are the most strongly linked, with kiwi, peaches, nectarines, celery and melons less so, and the association runs in both directions. Skin prick testing for latex is not available in the United States for lack of an approved reagent.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2, Practical guidance on capillary sampling (paediatric and neonatal)
preguntas.subtema: Antiseptic agents · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn needs a heel-prick. Which antiseptic does the WHO say must NOT be used for a skin puncture in a newborn or a small child?
opciones: Povidone iodine
70% isopropyl alcohol
Chlorhexidine
Soap and water
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 7 states plainly that povidone iodine is not for a capillary skin puncture in a pediatric or a neonatal patient and that alcohol is used instead, as in the adult instructions. For adults, Step 5 already prefers 70% alcohol over iodine because of its effect on potassium, phosphorus and uric acid results. Soap and water is the WHO's hand hygiene method, not a skin antiseptic for the puncture site.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix A: Maintain Equipment (portable equipment note)
preguntas.subtema: Controls after moving equipment · CPT D1 1E / k27 · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: A portable hemoglobin analyzer is carried from the clinic to a community screening event. Before the first patient there, what does the pretesting checklist recommend?
opciones: Perform control testing or a calibration check after moving it, even if the manufacturer does not require it
No extra step; a waived analyzer needs controls only with each new lot or shipment, wherever it is used
Recalibrate it at the event using a patient sample of known value brought along from the clinic
Run it for 30 minutes without samples at the event so its internal temperature stabilizes
preguntas.explicacion: Portable equipment that has been moved may give inaccurate results, so the checklist advises verifying proper function with control testing or a calibration check after the move, even when the current manufacturer's instructions do not demand it. Calibration checks in general follow the insert, and equipment and electrical connections are inspected before use. Patient samples are not calibration materials.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: How long may chest compressions be interrupted so that the two rescue breaths can be given?
opciones: Less than 10 seconds, keeping the pause for the breaths short
Less than 30 seconds, the time needed to reposition the head
Up to 2 minutes, the interval at which compressors are rotated
Up to 1 minute, while the mouth is checked for a foreign object
preguntas.explicacion: Pauses in compressions are held under 10 seconds, because interruptions cost circulation and continuous CPR improves survival. Two minutes is the interval for switching the person compressing, and 10 seconds is also the ceiling a trained provider has for checking breathing and pulse before starting.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(i)(3), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E14 3E15 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory forwards a specialized assay to a distant laboratory and passes the result on to the ordering physician. What else must the referring laboratory tell that physician?
opciones: The name and address of the laboratory that actually performed the test
The reason the assay could not be performed on its own premises
The date on which the specimen was dispatched to the other laboratory
The name of the courier service that carried the specimen there
preguntas.explicacion: When specimens are referred, three rules apply at once: the referring laboratory may not revise the results or their interpretation, it may let the testing laboratory report straight to the ordering person provided it can produce an exact duplicate of that report, and it must tell whoever ordered the test the name and address of every laboratory location where the testing was done.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k9 k51 k59 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR tube is filled only two thirds of the way. What effect does the short fill have on the reading?
opciones: Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out higher
Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out lower
The citrate is diluted and the red cells stop stacking altogether
The plasma layer disappears and no reading at all can be taken
preguntas.explicacion: Filling the tube inadequately lets air bubbles into the column, and that raises the value measured. It sits alongside the other physical faults that push the reading up: a tilted tube and vibration. Delay in testing works the other way and lowers the result.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What if I make a mistake and have something to eat or drink besides water during my fast?; and MedlinePlus, How to Understand Your Lab Results, What can affect my results?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits she ate a biscuit two hours ago before a fasting panel. What does the guidance say happens next?
opciones: She tells the provider, and the test may be rescheduled for another time
She waits in the department for two more hours and is then drawn
She is drawn now, and the result is reported with a comment on diet
She is drawn now, since one biscuit adds no sugar to the bloodstream
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to say so if they ate or drank before the test, and that it may need to be rescheduled for a time when they can fast, so the results come out accurate. Eating and drinking are listed among the common factors that affect accuracy, since the bloodstream takes up sugar, fat and protein from whatever is consumed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", section Patient Versus Provider Use of Slang Terms
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k18 · CCMA 6 k194 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes himself as 'queer'. May staff use that word to describe him?
opciones: Follow the patient's lead, but staff should not use such terms to describe him
Use the same word in the chart, since the patient chose it himself
Correct the patient and suggest the clinical term 'homosexual' instead
Avoid noting any description of the patient's orientation in the record
preguntas.explicacion: Members of the LGBTQ community may use words like queer or gay for themselves, but the same words are considered derogatory when a provider uses them to describe a patient; staff listen, follow the patient's lead, and ask how the patient and partner should be described, then record the agreed terms. 'Homosexual' is listed as a term that has been replaced.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abandonment", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Contracts in practice · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(1) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which situation creates a clinician-patient relationship without the patient agreeing to it?
opciones: Emergency care given, or care given at the request of the patient's own clinician
A talk about some symptoms given to a neighbor at a weekend social gathering
A health fair booth where general advice is offered together with a written disclaimer
A phone call in which the office schedules a first appointment for next month
preguntas.explicacion: Usually the relationship starts by mutual consent, but an implied and limited one arises when a clinician provides acute care in an emergency, treats at the request of the patient's regular clinician, cares for a prisoner under court order, or performs an independent medical examination. A written disclaimer at a health fair or informal setting is used precisely to keep that from forming.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Medical Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Emergency treatment · CPT D1 1D k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 1A k2 · CMA II.E.3 · RMA I.C.2 · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no insurance arrives at an emergency department in crisis. Which federal law applies?
opciones: The one requiring an attempt to stabilize, whatever the ability to pay
The one requiring a written estimate before any care is given
The one requiring transfer to a public hospital within the hour
The one requiring the plan to be billed before treatment begins
preguntas.explicacion: The Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act, passed inside a budget reconciliation law, obliges an organization that devotes at least a third of its services to emergency care to attempt to stabilize an emergency condition whether or not the person is able to pay for it. It exists because patients known or suspected to be unable to pay were being turned away. What counts as an emergency, and when a patient is stable enough to stop, is left to each organization to interpret.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation specimen is about to leave the ward. Which details are required on the tube and on the request slip?
opciones: The name, a medical record number or birth date, the date drawn and the specimen source
Name, insurance policy number, ordering clinic and the room where blood was drawn
Name and medical record number only, since the laboratory time-stamps arrival itself
Name, date of birth and the phlebotomist's initials, with no need for the collection date
preguntas.explicacion: Results depend on specimen quality, and the labeling asked for on both the tube and the slip is the patient's name, the medical record number or date of birth, the date of collection and, where it applies, the source of the specimen. Arrival time in the laboratory does not replace those fields.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.3 Cardiac Cycle, Ventricular Systole
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In a resting adult, what are the end diastolic volume of a ventricle and the stroke volume?
opciones: EDV about 130 mL; stroke volume 70 to 80 mL
EDV about 70 to 80 mL; stroke volume 130 mL
EDV about 130 mL; stroke volume 50 to 60 mL
EDV about 5 liters; stroke volume 130 mL
preguntas.explicacion: Just before ventricular contraction a resting adult's ventricle holds about 130 mL, the end diastolic volume or preload; each ventricle then ejects 70 to 80 mL, the stroke volume, leaving 50 to 60 mL behind as the end systolic volume. Both ventricles pump the same amount. Five liters is roughly what the heart moves in a minute, not what one ventricle holds.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section Can I continue taking medicine during a fast; MedlinePlus, How to Prepare for a Lab Test, section How do I prepare for a lab test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 k128 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting blood work asks the phlebotomist whether to skip the morning blood-pressure pill. What is the right guidance?
opciones: Take usual medicines unless the provider said to stop, and tell the provider of every medicine, vitamin and supplement
Skip all medicines on the morning of a fasting test, since swallowing any pill counts as breaking the fast
Take prescription medicines but stop vitamins and supplements, which are the only products that alter results
Take the pill only if it can be swallowed without water, because liquids are not allowed during the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to ask their provider whether the prescription and over-the-counter medicines they take may be continued, and never to stop one unless the provider says so; for certain tests the provider will have them hold a drug, and that call is not the phlebotomist's. Vitamins and supplements get reported too, since a medicine can push blood glucose up or down and change a result drawn too soon after a dose. Plain water is allowed all through the fast.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Healthcare-Associated (Nosocomial) Infections
preguntas.subtema: Nosocomial infections · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k98 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: For an infection to be classified as healthcare-associated (nosocomial), which condition must be met?
opciones: The patient was admitted for a reason other than that infection
The infection was acquired from a healthcare worker rather than from equipment
The infection appeared within 24 hours of admission to the facility
The infection is caused by a multidrug-resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: A healthcare-associated infection is one picked up inside a health-care facility, and what defines it is that the patient was admitted for some other reason. They are often tied to surgery or to invasive procedures that open a portal of entry, and to contaminated equipment such as catheters and ventilators; in 2011 more than 720,000 occurred in U.S. hospitals, surgical sites and pneumonia accounting for about 22 percent each. The source may be equipment, staff or the environment, the organism need not be resistant, and the definition sets no 24-hour cutoff.

preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which disadvantage of the evacuated tube system arises after the draw rather than during it?
opciones: Reusing the tube holder risks a needle-stick while it is taken apart
Reusing the tube holder risks a hemolyzed specimen in the next tube
Filling several tubes risks losing the vacuum in the last of them
Filling several tubes risks carrying additive back into the syringe
preguntas.explicacion: Among the drawbacks listed for vacuum systems is that reuse of the needle holder creates a needle-stick risk during disassembly, which happens once the blood is already drawn. Skill in use, mixing components from different makers and higher cost are the other entries on that list.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Bleeding", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through the gauze being held on a bleeding wound. What should be done?
opciones: Lay another cloth over the first one and keep up the pressure
Lift the gauze to look at the wound and then press again harder
Replace the soaked gauze with dry gauze and press on the artery
Loosen the pressure for a moment so that a clot can start to form
preguntas.explicacion: A soaked dressing is not taken off: another one is placed on top and pressure continues until bleeding stops, and then the dressing is wrapped firmly in place. Peeking disturbs the wound and makes control harder. Bleeding that keeps seeping through calls for medical attention right away.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adult Diabetic Ketoacidosis", History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.e · 2027 I.B.8.e · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes is breathing deeply and rapidly and the breath smells fruity. What does this suggest?
opciones: Ketoacidosis, with acetone on the breath and Kussmaul breathing
Insulin shock, with the low sugar showing on the patient's breath
Hyperventilation from anxiety, which lowers the carbon dioxide level
An asthma attack, in which wheezing may be heard only on breathing out
preguntas.explicacion: Labored, deep and rapid respirations are called Kussmaul breathing, and a fruity smell on the breath comes from acetone; both point to ketoacidosis. The patient may also be passing a lot of urine, be very thirsty, and have nausea, vomiting or abdominal pain, with tachycardia and signs of dehydration on examination.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Designated Record Set
preguntas.subtema: Designated record set · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which category of information is expressly excluded from the individual's right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes kept separate from the rest of the patient's medical record
Laboratory results, which the patient obtains from the testing laboratory instead
Billing and payment records, which belong to the revenue cycle rather than the chart
Medical images such as X-rays, because they are not readily producible on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Two categories are excluded outright: psychotherapy notes, meaning a mental health provider's own notes on a counseling session kept apart from the record, and information gathered because a legal proceeding is expected or under way. Otherwise the right of access is broad; it expressly reaches insurance information, billing and payment records, laboratory results, and medical images like X-rays.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification; Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 k146 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A barcode scanner at the accessioning desk misreads a patient identification label. What did the emergency laboratory identify as the cause of such misreads?
opciones: A mismatch between the scanner settings and the print area size or symbology of the barcode on the wristband
Barcodes printed more than 30 minutes before collection, which fade beyond the reading threshold of the scanner
Labels printed with more than two identifiers, which overload the nine-digit internal code the scanner expects
Heat from the centrifuge, which distorts the code 39 bars so that the digits no longer match the record
preguntas.explicacion: Barcoding carries an evidence-based recommendation behind it, since it cuts identification errors in specimens and in testing, yet this laboratory still saw scanners misread patient barcodes when the symbology or the print area on a wristband or specimen label did not match the scanner's settings. Its own nine-digit code 39 barcode carries name, sex, age, tube and sample type, print and collection times, collection site, the tests, the ordering doctor and the phlebotomist.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Business Associate Defined
preguntas.subtema: Business associates · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice hires an outside company to process its claims. Under the Privacy Rule, what is that company?
opciones: A business associate, because it performs a function for the practice that uses patient information
A member of the practice workforce, because it handles the same records the front desk handles
A health care clearinghouse, because any outside company that touches claims fits that definition
An ordinary supplier outside the rule, since only entities that treat patients are regulated
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate is a person or an organization outside the workforce that performs functions or supplies services for a covered entity where the work involves using or disclosing health information that identifies an individual. Processing claims, analyzing data, reviewing utilization and doing the billing are the functions named. Someone whose work never touches PHI is not one.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A used needle really has to come off its syringe. How is the one-hand scoop performed?
opciones: Leave the cap on a surface, guide the tip in with one hand, then secure it
Hold the cap in one hand and push the needle into it with the other hand
Pinch the cap between two fingers and twist the syringe until it is covered
Hold the cap with forceps and press the needle down onto a firm surface
preguntas.explicacion: The cap is left resting on a surface, or propped against something firm and upright with the opening towards the worker, and the used tip is guided into it with one hand only. The needle and syringe are then lifted vertically and the other hand fixes the cap once the tip is covered.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: COBRA
preguntas.subtema: Coverage continuation · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's job ended last month and he kept his employer coverage under COBRA. What changed for him?
opciones: He now pays the full premium, including the employer's old share, plus a small fee
He now pays the same share of the premium he paid while he was still employed
He now pays no premium, and the plan bills the former employer for the coverage
He now pays a premium set by the Marketplace, based on his household income
preguntas.explicacion: COBRA is the federal law that lets a person keep employer coverage for a time after the job ends, after losing dependent status, or after another qualifying event. Whoever elects it pays 100% of the premium, the portion the employer used to cover included, plus a small administrative charge. Nothing shifts the cost back to the employer, and income-based premiums belong to Marketplace coverage instead.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System; and StatPearls, "Prescription of Controlled Substances: Benefits and Risks" (NBK537318)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient pulls a hand away from a hot surface before feeling the pain. Which part of the nervous system handled that?
opciones: The spinal cord, acting as a reflex center without the higher brain
The cerebral cortex, acting as a reflex center without the spinal cord
The cerebellum, acting as a reflex center without the spinal cord
The medulla oblongata, acting as a reflex center without the cord
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond carrying impulses up and down its ascending and descending tracts, the spinal cord works as a center for reflexes. A reflex arc is the unit that does the job: a response to a stimulus that needs no conscious thought, so the hand is withdrawn before the person is aware of the pain. Many reflexes never reach the higher centers at all.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Rapid shallow breathing
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An adult arrives with fast, shallow breathing and no history of anxiety. How is this handled?
opciones: It is treated as an emergency rather than something to be managed at home
It is observed at home for 24 hours, since the pattern often settles on its own
It is managed with an inhaler alone, which settles the breathing once the dose is taken
It is recorded as hyperventilation, which is the term for fast and shallow breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Unless anxiety is the whole story, fast shallow breathing is handled as an emergency: asthma, a clot in the lung, pneumonia, heart failure and chronic lung disease all present this way. Hyperventilation is the term for breathing that is rapid and deep, which is why the depth is charted along with the rate.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Dietary Fats — Summary
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(b) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(b) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient trying to lose weight asks why fat is watched so closely when some fat is necessary. What is true of dietary fat?
opciones: Gram for gram it carries twice the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries half the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries the same calories as protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries twice the calories that alcohol carries
preguntas.explicacion: Some fat belongs in the diet: it supplies energy, it helps the body absorb certain vitamins, and it shapes cholesterol levels. What makes it easy to overdo is density, since fat holds twice the calories that protein or carbohydrate holds for the same weight, so extra fat puts on weight quickly.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: After cleaning the site, a phlebotomist palpates the vein once more with a gloved finger to confirm its position. What does the WHO require now?
opciones: Repeat the disinfection, because the cleaned site was touched
Proceed at once, since the glove was clean and the alcohol has dried
Wipe the fingerprint with dry gauze and proceed without delay
Apply povidone iodine over the alcohol before inserting the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 says not to touch the cleaned site and, in particular, not to place a finger over the vein to guide the exposed needle; if the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. A clean glove does not change the rule. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, which can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adult Diabetic Ketoacidosis", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.e · 2027 I.B.8.e · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which three findings define diabetic ketoacidosis?
opciones: Hyperglycemia, acidosis and ketones in the blood
Hypoglycemia, alkalosis and ketones in the urine
Hyperglycemia, dehydration and a low potassium level
Hypoglycemia, tachycardia and a rise in the temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a metabolic emergency defined by high blood glucose, acidosis and ketonemia. It is most often seen in type 1 diabetes but can occur in type 2, and it is set off by new-onset diabetes, infection, poor adherence to therapy, or acute illness, trauma and certain medicines.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: A and B Recommendations — Breast Cancer: Screening
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C screening timelines · CMA I.A.5.a · 2027 I.A.5.a · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A 42-year-old woman asks when mammography screening should start and how often. What is currently recommended?
opciones: Screening mammography every two years from age 40 through 74
Screening mammography every year from age 40 through 74
Screening mammography every two years from age 50 through 74
Screening mammography every two years from age 45 through 65
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation, updated in April 2024, is biennial screening mammography for women from 40 through 74 years of age, and it carries a B grade. The age of 50 was the older starting point. No current breast recommendation runs from 45 to 65: 65 is where a different screening ends, the one for cervical cancer, which runs from 21.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Pictograms; and OSHA, 29 CFR 1910.1030 (texto oficial en osha.gov)
preguntas.subtema: Pictogram design · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How is a GHS hazard pictogram drawn on a shipped chemical label?
opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: A pictogram on a shipped container is a red square frame standing on one point, with a black symbol for the hazard set on white inside it, drawn wide enough to be seen clearly. A red frame left empty, with no symbol in it, is not a pictogram and has no place on the label. The fluorescent orange label carrying the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are what the Department of Transportation requires for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling; and "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist shakes a filled citrate tube hard to be sure the blood mixes. What is the consequence?
opciones: Frothing or hemolysis that makes the coagulation results inaccurate
Small clots in the tube, the result the review links to under-mixing
A rise in the citrate-to-blood ratio, as happens with a short draw
Loss of the vacuum, so the next tube in the sequence will not fill
preguntas.explicacion: Both the coagulopathies review and the prothrombin time chapter say the citrate tube is inverted gently and never shaken, because vigorous agitation causes frothing or hemolysis and the coagulation results become unreliable. Small clots are the opposite problem, inefficient mixing, in the tube collection review; the citrate ratio changes with underfilling, not with shaking.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Foreign Body Airway Obstruction", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A choking child has an object in the airway that the rescuer cannot see. Should a finger sweep be attempted?
opciones: No: only an object in plain view is removed; a blind sweep pushes it deeper
Yes: a sweep of the back of the throat comes before any back blows or thrusts
Yes, but only once five back blows and five chest thrusts have both failed
No, unless the child has lost consciousness and compressions have started
preguntas.explicacion: A foreign body that can be seen is removed carefully, but blind finger sweeps are avoided at every age because they can drive the object downward toward the larynx. If the child becomes unresponsive, compressions start, and the airway is looked at after each set of 30, again removing only what is visible.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iv)(A) and (d)(3)(iv), Laundry and PPE
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated laundry · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A lab coat is soaked with blood after a difficult draw. How do the standard's laundry rules apply?
opciones: Bag it where it was used, without sorting or rinsing, in a container that prevents soak-through
Rinse it in the nearest sink first, then bag it, so the laundry service is not exposed
Take it home to wash separately, since the employer is not responsible for laundering
Sort it with other soiled coats at the laundry, where staff wear gloves and gowns
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iv)(A) requires contaminated laundry to be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation, bagged or containerized at the location of use, and never sorted or rinsed there; when it is wet enough to soak through, the bag or container must prevent leakage to the outside. The employer, not the employee, cleans and launders required PPE at no cost under (d)(3)(iv), so taking the coat home is not an option, and the gloves worn by laundry staff under (d)(4)(iv)(B) do not permit sorting at the point of use.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Patient-initiated ending · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes that she is leaving the practice for a clinician nearer her home. Does the office owe her a termination notice?
opciones: No, though a letter confirming her decision is wise and cuts the risk of a later claim
Yes, and the same thirty days of care and medication refills still have to be offered
Yes, and it has to travel by certified mail with a return receipt like any other notice
No, and no letter should go out either, since the record closes with her last visit
preguntas.explicacion: When it is the patient who has ended the relationship, no termination notice is owed by the physician. Putting her decision on paper in a short letter is still the prudent move: it removes the ambiguity and lowers the exposure to a legal claim. The thirty days that are usually deemed reasonable, and the certified mail, attach to a termination the practice itself starts.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which two arteries are normally used to palpate a pulse?
opciones: The radial artery at the wrist and the common carotid in the neck
The brachial artery in the upper arm and the femoral in the thigh
The median cubital vein at the elbow and the cephalic along the arm
The dorsalis pedis on the foot and the popliteal behind the knee
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse is the expansion and recoil of an artery, and it is normally taken at the wrist over the radial artery or in the neck over the common carotid, though any artery near the surface will serve: the temporal, facial, brachial, femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis are the other listed spots. The median cubital and the cephalic are veins, and only arteries pulse.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: living will
preguntas.subtema: Advance directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.b / 2027 E.7.a · RMA I.C.7 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: Life-sustaining treatment is given to a patient whose living will refused it. What claim may follow, and what defeats it?
opciones: Medical battery; the claim fails if the provider did not know of the living will
Medical battery; the claim fails only if a relative asked for the treatment
Negligence; the claim fails if the treatment turned out to help the patient
Breach of contract; the claim fails if the document was signed years earlier
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is an advance directive listing what the person wants if they can no longer give informed consent or refusal, commonly which life-sustaining measures may be used when there is no reasonable expectation of recovery. Administering life-sustaining treatment against it can expose the provider to a medical battery suit, but a provider unaware of the living will will not lose such a claim.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Diagnostic Tests
preguntas.subtema: Sputum stains · PBT V.B.3 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.f / 2027 I.C.8.e · RMA III.C.4.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which stain does the laboratory add to a sputum smear when tuberculosis is suspected?
opciones: An acid-fast stain, which the mycobacteria keep through an acid wash
A Gram stain, which sorts organisms by the thickness of the cell wall
A methenamine silver stain, which is the standard one for fungal forms
A hematoxylin and eosin stain, which is the standard one in cytology
preguntas.explicacion: Gram staining is the first step on any sputum smear and separates organisms into gram-positive, which hold the crystal violet in their thick peptidoglycan wall, and gram-negative, which take the pink counterstain. When tuberculosis is suspected an acid-fast stain is added, because the rod-shaped mycobacteria retain the color after an acid wash. Silver stain looks for fungi, and hematoxylin and eosin is the cytology workhorse.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.1 The Language of Epidemiologists, Analyzing Disease in a Population
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A health department reports 43,165 new diagnoses of an infection in one year and 1.2 million people living with it. Which figure is the incidence?
opciones: The 43,165 new diagnoses, because incidence counts new cases in a period
The 1.2 million living with it, because incidence counts everyone affected
Neither figure, because incidence is always given as a percentage of deaths
Both figures added together, because incidence covers new and existing cases
preguntas.explicacion: Incidence counts the new cases that appear over a stretch of time, as a number or a proportion; prevalence counts how many people have the illness at one moment. For a long-lasting disease prevalence runs higher, because it piles up years of new cases minus those no longer active.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1 and Section 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet placement · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: How should the lancet be oriented on the fingertip in a capillary puncture?
opciones: On the side of the finger pad, crossing the fingerprint lines at a right angle
On the center of the fingertip pad, running along the fingerprint lines
On the side of the finger pad, running along the fingerprint lines instead
Over the very tip of the finger next to the nail, at a right angle to the nail bed
preguntas.explicacion: A finger puncture is made on the side of the pad, with the lancet crossing the print lines instead of following them; on the heel the spot is the medial or lateral plantar surface. One quick, firm stroke carried through gives a flow good enough that the patient need not be stuck again.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable modifications · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a change in how the office usually does things so that she can be seen. What is the limit on that duty?
opciones: The change is made unless it would alter the essential nature of the service
The change is made unless another patient objects to the way it affects his visit
The change is made unless it costs the practice more than a routine visit is paid
The change is made unless the practice has already made one for her this year
preguntas.explicacion: Providers owe full and equal access, and along with it modifications to policies, to practices and to procedures that are reasonable, whenever such a change is what makes the service fully available to a person with a disability. The single boundary written into the duty is a change that would alter the essential nature of what the practice does.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fasting", section Issues of Concern; and MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, How long do I have to fast before the test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasting since midnight reports a dull headache. Which mechanisms are proposed for it?
opciones: Low blood sugar, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal
Low blood sugar, high potassium and a raised cortisol
Dehydration, low iron stores and a raised cortisol
Caffeine withdrawal, high potassium and low iron stores
preguntas.explicacion: A tension-type headache is described as a notable effect at the beginning of a fast. Its precise cause has not been identified, and the mechanisms proposed for it are hypoglycaemia, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal. That is one more reason a fasting draw is scheduled early in the morning, so most of the fasting time passes during sleep.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Direct Laryngoscopy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: The laryngoscope blade has been advanced to the epiglottis. Where does it go next, and does that depend on the blade?
opciones: A Macintosh goes into the vallecula; a Miller goes over the epiglottis
A Miller goes into the vallecula; a Macintosh goes over the epiglottis
Either blade goes into the vallecula, and the tip is then lifted forward
Either blade goes over the epiglottis, and the tip is then lifted forward
preguntas.explicacion: The instrument enters on the right side of the mouth and the blade sweeps the tongue to the left, then rides forward to the epiglottis. From there the two blades part company: the curved one stops in the vallecula, the straight one passes over the epiglottis toward the entrance of the trachea, above the vocal cords.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Location of the Heart; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the heart sit in the body?
opciones: In the mediastinum between the lungs, with the apex pointing to the left
In the mediastinum, with two thirds of its mass to the right of the midline
In the left pleural cavity behind the sternum, with the apex pointing right
In the pericardial cavity below the diaphragm, at the level of the third rib
preguntas.explicacion: The heart lies in the chest between the two lungs, in the space called the mediastinum, wrapped in its own pericardial sac; the base reaches the level of the third costal cartilage and the apex points a little to the left of the sternum, between the fourth and fifth ribs, with roughly two thirds of the mass left of the midline. That position decides where the stethoscope goes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins on the back of the hand arise from which structure, and where do they drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the dorsal venous arch, into the radial and ulnar deep veins
From the deep palmar arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the median cubital vein, into the dorsal venous arch below it
preguntas.explicacion: On the dorsum of the hand the superficial veins spring from the dorsal venous arch, which drains into the cephalic and the basilic, the two main superficial channels of the limb. The palmar arches belong to the deep system and drain into the ulnar and radial veins instead.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, What Is Health Literacy? Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: How is personal health literacy defined since the 2020 update?
opciones: How far a person can locate health information and services, grasp them and use them
How far a person can read and pronounce common medical words correctly
How far a person can obtain and process basic information about a diagnosis
How many years of formal schooling a person has completed before adulthood
preguntas.explicacion: The definition was rewritten in August 2020 with Healthy People 2030. Personal health literacy measures how far someone can locate information and services, grasp them, and put them to use in making health decisions for herself and for others. The wording deliberately moved from merely understanding information to being able to act on it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · D2 2E k41 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Beyond first and last name and date of birth, which further identifier is described as accepted for matching a patient to a specimen?
opciones: The social security number or the patient's address
The name of the insurance plan covering the visit
The color of the identification bracelet in use
The number of the room where the draw took place
