preguntas.pregunta: Why does the WHO recommend closed vacuum-tube systems over open needle-and-syringe collection?
opciones: They reduce direct exposure to blood and ease multiple samples from one puncture
They are the cheapest devices and need no special training to use
They give better precision on small or difficult veins than any other collection device
They can be heparinized and used for arterial as well as venous sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 3 says closed systems have proven safer than open systems, and that vacuum extraction systems reduce the risk of direct exposure to blood and make several samples from one venepuncture easier to take, though they require training and skill. The other three statements are advantages that Table C.1 gives to the hypodermic syringe (cheap, no special training, heparinized for arterial blood) and to the winged needle (precision on small veins).

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Defects
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.1 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn is cyanotic, a 'blue baby'. Which congenital defect is the most common cause of cyanosis after birth?
opciones: Tetralogy of Fallot
Patent foramen ovale
Aortic coarctation
Patent ductus arteriosus
preguntas.explicacion: Tetralogy of Fallot pairs an opening in the interventricular septum with a blocked pulmonary trunk, so blood low in oxygen crosses from the right ventricle and mixes on the left; of the heart defects it is the one that most often turns a newborn blue. A patent foramen ovale is an opening between the atria, coarctation a narrowed aorta, and a patent ductus arteriosus a fetal vessel left open.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa", section Structure and Function (venous types)
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Four patterns are described for the superficial veins at the elbow. Which of them is the most common?
opciones: Type II, in which the median cubital vein joins the cephalic and basilic veins (the M pattern)
Type I, in which a dominant median antebrachial vein joins both veins (the N pattern)
Type III, in which the brachial cephalic vein is poorly developed or missing
Type IV, in which there is no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic
preguntas.explicacion: Type II, with the cephalic and the basilic joined by the median cubital vein, also called type M, is the most common pattern, followed by type I, the N type with a dominant median antebrachial vein. It adds that because of this variation, bruising, hematoma and sensory changes from mispuncture have been reported across health systems.

preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.G · CCMA 3E6 k129 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7

The purple top EDTA tube
The gold serum separator tube

preguntas.pregunta: Which measure is recommended for defining malnutrition in a child, and what does it express?

The percentile rank, the share of children of that age below the child
The body mass index band, from underweight up through the obesity classes
The growth velocity, the change in weight between two consecutive visits
preguntas.explicacion: Z-scores use standard deviations to place a child against the average population, and they are what the American Academy of Pediatrics puts forward for defining malnutrition. They exist for weight-for-height, weight-for-age, body mass index for age and head circumference. For classifying obesity the levels are not well established, which is why they were left out.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Priority Mail
preguntas.subtema: Priority Mail · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A practice mails a heavy set of imaging discs to a specialist and wants tracking and cover for loss included in the price. Which service fits?
opciones: Priority Mail, delivered in two to three days with tracking and cover included
First-Class Mail, delivered in one to five days at the lowest price per piece
Media Mail, delivered in two to eight days for recorded and printed materials
Priority Mail Express, delivered in one to three days with a money-back promise
preguntas.explicacion: Priority Mail is the everyday parcel service: two to three days, tracking and up to $100 of insurance built into the price, free flat rate packaging and a 70 lb ceiling. Express is faster but is bought for speed, and First-Class carries no tracking of its own.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A child's phase V cannot be heard at all during a manual reading. What is used for the diastolic value?
opciones: Phase IV, the abrupt muffling, is used when the fifth sound cannot be detected
Phase III, the return of sharper sounds, is used as the nearest available marker
The reading is abandoned, since only the disappearance of sound can be recorded
Zero is recorded, because sound that continues to the end means no diastolic point
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation in children is the same as in adults, phase V; but where that point cannot be found, phase IV is used instead. preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does the guidance suggest an older patient bring so that their medicines can be checked?
opciones: A list with dose and frequency, or everything in a bag
Only the prescriptions written since the last appointment
The pharmacy receipts covering the past twelve months
A note from the pharmacist listing the interactions
preguntas.explicacion: Older people often take many medicines, prescribed by more than one doctor, and some of those combinations end in serious complications. The patient is asked to bring a list of it all, what is prescribed, what is bought over the counter, the vitamins and the dietary supplements, with the dose and frequency of each, or simply to bring the lot along in a bag.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors (HIL indices)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 k93 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D k111 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: What do the letters H, I and L stand for in the serum indices that conventional laboratory analyzers measure, and how are the same problems detected at the point of care?
opciones: Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care only by visual inspection of a centrifuged aliquot
Heparin, infusion and light; at the point of care by a built-in spectrophotometric check on every strip
Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care by an automatic index reported with each result
Hematocrit, ionic strength and lactate; at the point of care by running a control before each sample
preguntas.explicacion: Conventional laboratories add a step that measures the serum index for hemoglobin (H), icterus (I) and lipemia (L), usually spectrophotometrically, because all three can make results inaccurate or incalculable, potassium being especially vulnerable. Point-of-care devices have no such index, so hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can be recognized there only by looking at a centrifuged aliquot; dilution may fix excess bilirubin and ultracentrifugation excess lipids.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: What separates hyperpnea from hyperventilation?
opciones: In hyperpnea the breathing matches metabolic demand and the blood gases stay normal
In hyperpnea the breathing is slower than normal while each breath grows much deeper
In hyperpnea the rise happens only during sleep, while hyperventilation happens awake
In hyperpnea the depth falls while the rate rises, which is what lowers carbon dioxide
preguntas.explicacion: Hyperpnea is breathing that has grown deeper and faster in step with what the body needs, during exercise or with a fever, and the blood gases stay where they should be. Hyperventilation goes beyond the metabolic requirement, so carbon dioxide falls and respiratory alkalosis follows; anxiety, pain, fever and panic can trigger it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "P wave", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A strip shows a PR interval under 120 ms with a sharp upward slope running into the QRS complex. What does that describe?
opciones: A tract that bypasses the node, as in Wolff-Parkinson-White
A delay inside the node itself, as in a first-degree block
A block below the node, as in a Mobitz type II block
A failed impulse at the sinus node, as in a sinoatrial block
preguntas.explicacion: A PR shorter than 120 ms says the signal reached the ventricles too quickly, classically through an accessory tract that goes around the atrioventricular node. The sharp slope rising out of the PR baseline into the complex is the delta wave that goes with it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cranial Nerve Testing", Technique or Treatment: Cranial Nerves IX and X
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.1.a(2)
preguntas.pregunta: A tongue blade is touched to one side of the posterior pharynx. Which nerves does that maneuver assess?
opciones: The glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves, tested together for the gag reflex
The trigeminal and facial nerves, tested together for facial sensation
The hypoglossal nerve alone, which is what moves the tongue in the mouth
The vagus nerve alone, since the glossopharyngeal carries only taste fibers
preguntas.explicacion: Cranial nerves nine and ten are tested at once. The patient opens the mouth and says aah while the palate is watched for symmetrical elevation and the uvula for staying midline; then each side of the posterior pharynx is touched with the blade and the gag watched for. Absence of the gag on both sides is a common finding and not necessarily abnormal.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dilation and Curettage", Equipment: Curettes
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a)
preguntas.pregunta: A dilation and curettage is being set up for a pregnant patient. Which curette is the one more commonly used?
opciones: A plastic cannula, straight or curved and rigid or flexible
A sharp metal curette with an open teardrop shape at the tip
A metal curette with teeth, for a more aggressive scrape
A metal curette sized by the widest diameter across its tip
preguntas.explicacion: Plastic curettes and cannulas are the ones usually reached for when the patient is pregnant. The sharp metal curette with the teardrop tip is the tool of the diagnostic procedure, the toothed one is kept for aggressive sampling after menopause, and it is the metal curettes that are measured by the largest part of the tip.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Protein in diet — Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(c) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(c) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A vegetarian patient is afraid she cannot get all her amino acids without meat. What should she be told?
opciones: Plant sources such as soy, beans and quinoa can supply what she needs
Only animal sources such as meat, milk and eggs supply amino acids
Essential amino acids have to be eaten together at every single meal
The body makes the essential amino acids out of the nonessential ones
preguntas.explicacion: Amino acids come from animal foods and also from plant foods such as soy, beans, legumes, nut butters and grains like quinoa and wheat germ, so animal products are not required. Essential amino acids are the ones the body cannot build and food has to supply, but the balance across the whole day is what counts, not each meal.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology: Central Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Name the three layers of meninges from the outside in.
opciones: Dura mater, arachnoid, pia mater
Pia mater, arachnoid, dura mater
Arachnoid, dura mater, pia mater
Dura mater, pia mater, arachnoid
preguntas.explicacion: The dura mater is the outer layer, tough white fibrous connective tissue. The arachnoid lies in the middle and looks like a cobweb; the space beneath it holds cerebrospinal fluid and blood vessels. The pia mater is innermost, thin and delicate, and bound so tightly to the brain and cord that it cannot be lifted without damage.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Growth chart
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.d · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How are a child's height and weight recorded so that they can be interpreted?
opciones: As points plotted on the growth chart, which places them as percentiles
As raw figures alone, since the chart is drawn only when a problem appears
As a percentage of the average value for children of that age and sex
As a single combined score, which the chart converts into an age equivalent
preguntas.explicacion: An isolated anthropometric figure is of little use: the value has to be set against the reference for that age and sex, and the charts do that by percentile curves. Each measurement taken at a well-child visit goes onto the chart, and the same chart follows the child from year to year.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Human Insulin", Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(2) · RMA III.G.2.b · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: You are teaching a patient to inject insulin at home. Which statement about the route and the equipment is correct?
opciones: Under the skin, with a disposable syringe marked in units and a fine short needle
Into the muscle, using a longer needle whenever the ordered dose is a large one
Into a vein at home, since regular insulin can also be given by that same route
Under the skin, with a tuberculin syringe marked in milliliters and a long needle
preguntas.explicacion: Insulin is given subcutaneously in almost every case, with a plastic disposable syringe that holds 30, 50 or 100 units and carries a fine needle, as thin as 31 gauge, from about 3/16 of an inch for infants to half an inch or more for adults. Pens and pumps are the other options. Muscle and vein are used only under close supervision in a hospital or similar setting, never as home teaching.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003); WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Precautions during follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: During the HIV follow-up period after an exposure, what does the CDC advise the worker to avoid?
opciones: Donating blood, semen or organs and unprotected sex, mostly in the first 6 to 12 weeks
Patient care duties of any kind until the 6-month antibody test comes back negative
Close contact with household members until the 12-week antibody test is negative
Any other medication, since it would interfere with the antiretroviral regimen
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC brochure asks exposed workers, especially during the first 6 to 12 weeks when most infected persons show signs of infection, to follow HIV prevention recommendations: no donation of blood, semen or organs, no sexual intercourse or consistent condom use, and consideration of not breastfeeding. WHO's annex adds no blood or organ donation for up to 6 months. Neither source restricts patient care or household contact, and the CDC asks workers to tell the treating provider about other medications, not to stop them.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What are the advantages of electronic health records?
preguntas.subtema: EHR advantages · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which benefit does ONC attribute to electronic health records?
opciones: Less duplicate testing, and legible documentation that supports accurate coding and billing
An automatic release of records to any provider who asks, without further authorization
A guarantee that no unauthorized person will ever reach the information they contain
An exemption from the Security Rule, since certified systems already meet its standards
preguntas.explicacion: The advantages ONC lists include having information that is accurate, current and complete right at the point of care; quicker access, so care is better coordinated; secure sharing with patients and with other clinicians; fewer medical errors; safer prescribing; documentation that is legible and complete, with coding and billing streamlined; better privacy and security for patient data; and lower costs through less paperwork and less duplicated testing.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: Besides reading the number, what does the daily temperature routine ask staff to look at on the thermometer itself?
opciones: Whether the column is separated, or there are gas bubbles or cracks
Whether the probe still sits in the middle shelf of the compartment
Whether the calibration sticker is still inside its expiry period
Whether the minimum and maximum display has been reset since the last read
preguntas.explicacion: The recording instructions add a physical check to the daily reading: each time the thermometer is read, look for a separated column, for gas bubbles and for cracks, where those apply. Resetting the minimum and maximum display belongs to the optional data logger used over weekends and closures, and it is done after the reading rather than instead of the inspection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Tachycardia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who hurried in and is visibly anxious has a regular strip at 108 with upright P waves in I and II. Which reading fits?
opciones: A sinus rhythm sped up by stress, one of the physiologic triggers
A rhythm from the AV node, since any rate past 100 starts there
An artifact of movement, which doubles the complexes counted
A recording error, since the paper ran at 50 mm per second
preguntas.explicacion: Sinus tachycardia is the same tracing as normal sinus rhythm with a rate above 100, and its physiologic causes are catecholamine-driven: exercise, stress, pain and anxiety. Those cases usually need no cardiac treatment, but the strip still goes to the provider to read.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(5), Healthcare Professional's Written Opinion
preguntas.subtema: Post-exposure written opinion · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a post-exposure evaluation, how soon must the employer hand the employee a copy of the evaluating professional's written opinion?
opciones: Within 15 days of completing the evaluation
Within 10 working days of the exposure incident
Within 30 days of the exposure incident
Within 90 days, once the baseline sample is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5) makes the employer obtain the evaluating professional's written opinion and put a copy in the employee's hands no more than 15 days after the evaluation is finished. The other periods sit elsewhere in the standard: 10 working days is the window for offering the hepatitis B vaccine after initial assignment, and 90 days is how long a baseline blood sample is kept when the employee consents to the draw but not yet to HIV testing. Thirty days is no deadline in this standard.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, introduction and Sections 12-15
preguntas.subtema: SDS structure · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How many sections does a GHS-format Safety Data Sheet have, and which of them does OSHA not enforce?
opciones: 16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 12 through 15
16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 9 through 11 and 16
12 sections; OSHA does not enforce the last two, transport and regulatory
8 sections, one per required pictogram; all are enforced by OSHA
preguntas.explicacion: A safety data sheet under the Hazard Communication standard has 16 numbered sections in a fixed order. Sections 12 through 15, ecological information, disposal, transport and regulatory information, must be present to match the GHS, but OSHA does not enforce their content because other agencies handle those matters. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold technical data such as physical properties, reactivity, toxicology and the date of preparation, and they are enforced. Eight is the number of pictograms OSHA requires, not of SDS sections.

preguntas.subtema: Uses described in the notice · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is drafting the part of its notice that deals with use for treatment, for payment and for health care operations. What does the rule require of that description?
opciones: A description of each of the three purposes, with at least one example of its own
A description of each of the three purposes, with the patient's consent alongside
A description of the three purposes together, with a single example covering them
A description of each of the three purposes, with the legal citation for each one
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must describe, and give at least one example of, the kinds of use and disclosure the entity may make for treatment, for payment and for health care operations. It must also cover the other purposes for which information may go out without written authorization, in enough detail for the reader to know what is permitted.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Surgical wound care - closed: Bathing or Showering
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: When may a patient shower after a closed surgical incision, and is a bath fine?
opciones: Usually after 24 hours, and showers are preferred because soaking can reopen the wound
Usually after 24 hours, and baths are preferred because the warm water loosens the tape
Usually after 7 days, and showers are preferred because soaking can reopen the wound
Usually after 72 hours, and either is fine as long as the dressing is left on throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The surgeon says when, but showering is usually fine after about a day. Showers beat baths because the wound is not left soaking, and soaking could reopen it or let it become infected. The dressing comes off before bathing unless told otherwise, the wound is rinsed gently without rubbing, the area around it is patted dry, and no lotions or powders go on it.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: consent
preguntas.subtema: Consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a-b · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: What has to be true for consent to be valid?
opciones: Enough mental capacity, and no coercion, fraud or mistake behind it
A signature on the practice's own form, witnessed by a staff member
A relative present at the time the person agrees to the procedure
A note in the record showing the person was told the likely outcome
preguntas.explicacion: Consent means the person voluntarily and willingly agrees to what is proposed. The person consenting must have sufficient mental capacity, and the agreement must be free of coercion, fraud or error. It divides into express consent, given directly in speech or writing, and implied consent, inferred from actions, signs, facts or even silence.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Information on Collection of Respiratory Specimens for Influenza Virus Testing, Outpatients; and CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Timing after onset · CPT D2 k45 timing · PBT V.C.2 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with influenza symptoms asks whether it matters how soon the swab is taken. What is the answer?
opciones: Yes: shedding in the upper airway falls off about 3 to 4 days after onset, so earlier is better
No: the amount of virus in the upper airway stays steady for about two weeks after onset
Yes: the virus is undetectable in the first 3 to 4 days, so waiting improves the yield
No: a negative rapid test rules out influenza whenever the swab happens to be taken
preguntas.explicacion: Influenza shedding in the upper respiratory tract drops substantially around 3 to 4 days after illness begins, so specimens are collected as close to onset as possible, ideally within four days. Infants and immunosuppressed patients may shed longer. A negative rapid antigen test never rules the infection out and should not stop further testing by molecular assay or empiric treatment.

preguntas.fuente: DailyMed, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide tablets, Boxed Warning: Fetal Toxicity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.e · NCMA 1.4
preguntas.pregunta: The label of a lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide tablet carries a boxed warning. What does that warning cover?
opciones: Fetal toxicity: the drug is stopped as soon as a pregnancy is detected
Lactic acidosis: reported cases have ended in death, hypothermia, bradycardia
Severe cutaneous reactions: the drug is stopped if the rash keeps spreading
Head and neck angioedema: reported more often in Black patients on this class
preguntas.explicacion: The box on this label is short and single-minded: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system injure and can kill the developing fetus, so treatment stops as soon as pregnancy is known. Lactic acidosis is the boxed warning of metformin and severe cutaneous reactions belong to the amoxicillin label. The angioedema sentence is in this same label, but under Indications and Warnings, not inside the box.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Essential health benefits
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act protections · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What are essential health benefits?
opciones: Ten categories of service that plans must cover under the health care law
Ten categories of service that plans may add to lower the monthly premium
The list of covered prescription drugs that each plan updates every year
The preventive screenings that plans must provide without any cost sharing
preguntas.explicacion: Essential health benefits are the ten service categories the health care law obliges plans to cover, among them prescription drugs, doctors' services, hospital care both inpatient and outpatient, pregnancy and childbirth, and mental health care. Dental cover has to be offered for children; for adults it is optional. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, and free preventive care is one protection among several, not the whole set of categories.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k40 · CCMA 6 k199 · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A patient cannot say back what he has to do before a glucose tolerance test. What comes next?
opciones: Explain it another way and ask again, until he can describe the plan in his own words
Hand him the printed instruction sheet and ask him to read the relevant lines out loud
Document that the teaching was offered and refused, and tell the ordering provider later
Repeat the same explanation word for word but more slowly, and move on once he nods
preguntas.explicacion: When teach-back uncovers a misunderstanding, the cycle repeats: explain it using a different approach, ask for the teach-back again, and keep going until the patient describes the information correctly in his own words. Words repeated back verbatim are a warning sign rather than a pass, and a nod proves nothing at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient breathes in clusters of deep, even breaths separated by pauses, with no build-up or fading within each cluster. Which pattern is charted?
opciones: Biot respiration, clusters of deep breaths broken by spells of apnea
Cheyne-Stokes respiration, breaths that swell and fade before a pause
Kussmaul respiration, deep and rapid breathing that never pauses at all
Paradoxical ventilation, the chest wall drawing in during inspiration
preguntas.explicacion: The pause is shared by two patterns, and the shape of the breaths between pauses tells them apart: Cheyne-Stokes grows and fades in a crescendo, while Biot keeps the same depth from breath to breath. Biot respiration follows damage to the pons from stroke, trauma or herniation, and also appears with opioid toxicity.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the lobby coughs forcefully after swallowing a piece of food and can still speak. What is the correct response?
opciones: Stay with the patient and let the coughing go on, watching it weaken
Deliver five firm back blows between the shoulder blades without waiting
Begin cycles of five abdominal thrusts before the airway closes completely
Sweep a finger through the mouth to hook out the piece of food lodged there
preguntas.explicacion: First aid for choking is not started while the person is coughing forcefully and able to speak: a strong cough often expels the object by itself. The rescuer stays ready to act if the cough weakens or speech is lost. A blind finger sweep can push the object further down toward the larynx and is avoided in every age group.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reached her out-of-pocket limit in September. What does she pay for covered in-network care in October?
opciones: No more cost sharing, since the plan pays the allowed amount
Her copayment only, because copays sit outside of that limit
Her coinsurance only, because it is a share and not a fixed sum
Her premium and her coinsurance, as she did before September
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit is the most a member pays for her share of covered services in the coverage period; once she meets it the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount. The premium is never part of that limit, so she goes on paying it, and neither the copayment nor the coinsurance survives the limit as a separate charge.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", sections Introduction and Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about discrimination in health care is correct?
opciones: It can rest on perceived group membership, and no harm needs to have occurred
It requires proof that the patient was harmed by the action or omission
It requires that the patient actually belong to the group in question
It is limited to the overt acts that Title VII and the ADA prohibit
preguntas.explicacion: Discrimination in health care is negative actions or lack of consideration based on preconceived notions about identity, adding that it can occur on perceived membership, that a person need not belong to the group, and that harm does not have to occur. Title VII and the ADA reduced overt racism, after which awareness shifted to the subtler microaggressions.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly, Actions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: When explaining fasting instructions, which approach follows the health-literacy principles for communicating clearly?
opciones: Give one to three need-to-know points in plain words, and repeat them
Cover every instruction once, quickly, so that none of them is left out
Use the precise medical terms so the patient learns them for next time
Hand over the printed sheet and skip the spoken explanation entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Keep it to one, two or at most three things the patient needs to know or to do, press each of them more than once, slow down, and use plain non-medical language, since jargon shuts patients out. Kessels found that up to 80% of what patients are told is forgotten at once, and that nearly half of what stays is wrong, which rules out a fast, exhaustive or paper-only approach.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient keeps chatting while the cuff deflates. What does that do to the reading?
opciones: It raises both numbers by roughly 10 mm Hg, so the reading is repeated in silence
It raises both numbers by roughly 2 mm Hg, which is inside the tolerance of the gauge
It lowers both numbers, because talking relaxes the patient and the vessels widen
It has no effect on an automated device, which is deaf to what the patient says
preguntas.explicacion: Talking or actively listening during the measurement adds about 10 mm Hg to both values, which is why the instruction is that nobody speaks while the cuff is deflating. The effect is on the patient's circulation, not on the microphone, so an automated device is affected in the same way.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which item is listed for the case where a large quantity of blood has to be collected?
opciones: A sterile glass or collapsible bleeding pack
A set of four pediatric microtubes in a rack
A second tube holder with a wider barrel fitted
A pair of gray fluoride tubes drawn back to back
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside the ordinary sample tubes, the equipment list names a sterile glass or collapsible bleeding pack for occasions when large quantities of blood are taken. Donation is also the setting for the widest needles on the gauge table, sixteen to eighteen.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Trough Versus Free Levels
preguntas.subtema: Trough timing · CPT D2 k45 high and low levels · PBT II.G common tests · CCMA 3E k139 medication levels · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A trough level is ordered for a patient on an antiepileptic drug. When is the sample drawn?
opciones: At the lowest point of the dosing interval, just before the next dose
At the highest point of the dosing interval, just after the next dose
Halfway between two doses, when the concentration is most stable
At the same hour each morning, independently of the dose times
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration of the drug in blood at its lowest point, which falls just before the next dose is due; it matters most for drugs with short half-lives. The value shows the minimum concentration reached between doses, so it tells the prescriber whether the level stayed inside the therapeutic range all the way through the interval and, for seizure drugs, whether breakthrough seizures are likely.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability
preguntas.subtema: Security objectives · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Security Rule, what does the word integrity mean?
opciones: Data has not been altered or destroyed in a manner that was not authorized
Data is accessible and usable on demand by a person who is authorized
Data is withheld from persons or processes that lack authorization
Data is stored on equipment the practice owns rather than on a vendor's servers
preguntas.explicacion: The rule sets out three objectives and gives each a definition. Confidentiality is the property of not being handed over or disclosed to persons or processes lacking authorization, which is what backs the Privacy Rule's limits on use and disclosure. Integrity is the property of not having been altered or destroyed without authorization. Availability is being reachable and usable on demand by a person who is authorized.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.D.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: How is the forearm handled during a surgical scrub, and how far up does it go?
opciones: In four planes scrubbed one at a time, from the wrist to two inches above the elbow
In two planes scrubbed one at a time, from the wrist to two inches above the elbow
In four planes scrubbed one at a time, from the wrist to just below the elbow crease
As one surface scrubbed in a spiral, from the fingertips to two inches above the elbow
preguntas.explicacion: The forearm is divided into four planes running from the wrist to two inches past the elbow, and each plane is scrubbed separately in a circular motion, ten strokes each in the counted method or one minute for all four in the timed one. Throughout, the hands stay higher than the elbows and the arms are kept away from the body.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, HIPAA Compliance, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA titles · CCMA 1 k2 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: HIPAA is organized into how many titles, and which one contains administrative simplification?
opciones: Five titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title II
Five titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title I
Three titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title III
Seven titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title IV
preguntas.explicacion: The 1996 statute, also known as the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act, has five titles. Title I protects insurance coverage for workers changing or losing jobs. Title II is the one that addresses health care fraud and abuse and promotes administrative simplification through national standards for electronic transactions and national identifiers. Titles III, IV and V deal with medical spending accounts, group plans and company-owned life insurance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Stool guaiac test (003393), How to Prepare for the Test; and StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors; and StatPearls, "StatPearls — Urinalysis" (NBK557685)
preguntas.subtema: gFOBT dietary restrictions · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which foods are patients told to avoid before a guaiac-based fecal occult blood test?
opciones: Red meat, cantaloupe, raw broccoli, turnip, radish and horseradish
Beets, blackberries, rhubarb, carrots and other strongly colored foods
Onions, garlic and asparagus, which change the odor of the specimen
Cranberry juice and a high-protein diet, which acidify the specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Red meat carries heme with peroxidase activity, and raw produce such as turnip, broccoli, horseradish, radish and cantaloupe is rich in plant peroxidases; either can turn a guaiac card falsely positive, and about 3 days of avoidance is advised. The other lists are urine interferences: colored foods alter urine color, onions and asparagus its odor, and cranberry juice or a high-protein diet its pH. Immunochemical kits need no diet.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Head injury - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.s · 2027 I.B.8.s · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which finding after a head injury means help is needed right away?
opciones: Pupils of unequal size, or vomiting more than once after the blow
A headache that eases with rest and a small bruise over the brow
One episode of vomiting in a child who is alert and behaving normally
Tenderness at the site of the blow with slight swelling under the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Unequal pupils, repeated vomiting, becoming very sleepy, abnormal behavior or speech that makes no sense, a severe headache or stiff neck, a seizure, inability to move part of an arm or leg, or any loss of consciousness even a brief one all call for immediate help. In children a single episode of vomiting after a head injury is common and may not be a problem.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ambulatory Electrocardiogram Monitoring", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: How long can an implantable loop recorder keep recording?
opciones: Up to three years, under the skin of the chest wall
Up to three weeks, under the skin of the chest wall
Up to three months, under the skin of the chest wall
Up to thirty days, under the skin of the chest wall
preguntas.explicacion: When symptoms come less than once a month, the external devices rarely catch them. The implantable recorder is placed under the skin in a minimally invasive procedure without general anesthesia, records for as long as three years, is compatible with MRI and rarely causes infection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which routinely available bedside site comes closest to core body temperature?
opciones: The rectum, still the yardstick other readings are compared against
The axilla, which is shielded by the arm and follows the core value closely
The tympanic membrane, which is convenient but not advised as a primary site
The temporal artery, whose skin sensor is the least invasive of the options
preguntas.explicacion: Of the sites used at the bedside, the rectal reading tracks core temperature best and is still treated as the standard of comparison. Tympanic and axillary readings are quick but less accurate, so they are not recommended as the primary site, and temporal artery thermometry is accepted as a reasonably accurate, less invasive alternative.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet removal · CPT D3 3E k60 k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist withdraws the needle and only then reaches for the tourniquet. Which instruction was missed?
opciones: The band comes off before the needle is withdrawn, not after
The band comes off once pressure has been applied with gauze
The band comes off before the first tube is pushed on the needle
The band comes off as soon as the needle has entered the vein
preguntas.explicacion: Once enough blood has been collected, the band is released before the needle is withdrawn; some guidance puts it earlier still, as soon as flow is established, and in every version before two minutes have passed. Pressure with clean gauze belongs to the step that follows the withdrawal.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.2 Pre-examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is the patient positioned for a resting recording?
opciones: Lying down with a pillow, arms at the sides, legs uncrossed
Lying down with a pillow, arms folded, legs crossed at the ankle
Sitting upright with the feet flat and arms resting on a table
Lying on the left side with a pillow placed between the knees
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits on the table first, then lies down carefully with a pillow under the head. The arms rest at the sides of the body and the legs stay uncrossed, which keeps the limb electrodes still and gives the machine a clean signal to write.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Fecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT), Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Vitamin C false negative · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient takes 1,000 mg of vitamin C daily and is about to do a guaiac stool test. What effect should be expected if she continues?
opciones: A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid blocks the guaiac color reaction
A false-positive result, because ascorbic acid has peroxidase activity
An unchanged result, because only vitamin C above 2,000 mg a day interferes
A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid stops intestinal bleeding for 3 days
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is a reducing agent that interferes with the oxidation the guaiac reaction depends on, so it hides blood that is really there. Patients are told to avoid more than 250 mg a day from supplements, juice or fruit, and high amounts for the 3 days before the test can cause a false negative; 1 to 2 grams daily has produced false negatives in studies. It does not stop bleeding and has no peroxidase activity.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(c)(7), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A moderately hemolysed serum is tested anyway because the patient cannot be redrawn, and the physician wants the figure. What must the printed report carry?
opciones: A note on the condition and disposition of the unacceptable specimen
The name of the person who decided to accept the flawed specimen
A recommendation that the ordering provider repeat the collection
The measured hemolysis index alongside every affected analyte
preguntas.explicacion: The test report standard lists what has to appear on the report, and among those items is whatever is known about the state of specimens that fall short of the laboratory's acceptability criteria and about what was done with them. Naming the decision maker, advising a redraw or printing the index may all be local practice, but the federal requirement is that the report say what was wrong with the specimen.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Effective Date of Coverage
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found eligible for Medicaid in June and still owes the practice for visits in April. What may the program allow?
opciones: Coverage reaching back up to three months before the month of application
Coverage reaching back up to six months before the month of application
Coverage starting on the date of the determination and never any earlier
Coverage reaching back to the first day of the year the application was made
preguntas.explicacion: Once eligibility is established, coverage starts either on the date of the application or on the first day of the month it was made in. Benefits may also reach back as far as three months before that month, provided the person would have qualified during that stretch had she applied then. Coverage generally ends with the month in which she stops qualifying.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k59 k51 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these tubes does the WHO order-of-draw table NOT mark as one that requires a full draw?
opciones: The red top with clot activator
The light blue sodium citrate tube
The purple EDTA tube
The light gray oxalate/fluoride tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 writes 'requires full draw' in the uses column of three tubes: the coagulation tube with sodium citrate, the EDTA tube for hematology and cross-match, and the gray glucose tube, for which it adds that a short draw may cause hemolysis. The red clot activator tube, used for chemistries, immunology, serology and cross-match, carries no such note.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fiber — Food Sources
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(f) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with high cholesterol asks which kind of fiber helps that number. Which answer is correct?
opciones: Soluble fiber, found in oat bran, barley, beans and lentils
Insoluble fiber, found in oat bran, barley, beans and lentils
Soluble fiber, found in wheat bran, vegetables and whole grains
Insoluble fiber, found in wheat bran, vegetables and whole grains
preguntas.explicacion: Fiber comes in two forms. The soluble kind draws in water and turns to gel, slowing digestion, and research shows it lowers cholesterol; barley and oat bran carry it, and so do seeds, nuts, lentils, beans, peas and some produce. Insoluble fiber, from wheat bran, vegetables and whole grains, adds bulk and speeds transit instead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Revised notice from a plan · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A health plan makes a material revision to its notice of privacy practices. Within what period must the people it covers receive the revised notice?
opciones: Within 60 days of the revision, to the individuals then covered by the plan
Within 30 days of the revision, to the individuals then covered by the plan
Within 90 days of the revision, to every individual enrolled in the last year
Within 60 days of the revision, to new enrollees only, at the time of enrollment
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans carry delivery duties of their own. When a revision is material, the revised notice has to reach whoever the plan covers at that moment inside 60 days; someone who enrolls later gets the notice when the enrollment happens. And any covered entity, plan or not, has to revise its notice and put it out promptly whenever it changes a privacy practice materially.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Skeletal System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Where does hematopoiesis take place, and which mineral does bone store more of than any other organ?
opciones: In the red marrow, and the mineral is calcium
In the yellow marrow, and the mineral is calcium
In the red marrow, and the mineral is potassium
In the compact bone, and the mineral is sodium
preguntas.explicacion: Blood cell formation happens mostly in the red marrow, which fills the bone cavities in infants and in adults is limited to spongy bone: the pelvis and vertebrae, the clavicles and sternum, the ribs and the skull. Yellow marrow stores fat. Bone also holds more calcium than any other organ and releases it when blood levels drop.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Materials and Methods; Results and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's CRP is ordered to monitor for perinatal infection and the serum returns a hemolysis index of about 800 mmol/L. What does the laboratory do with the CRP?
opciones: Rejects it and asks for a repeat sample, since an index above 622 mmol/L can underestimate CRP
Reports it, since specific proteins such as CRP are immune to hemolysis interference at any index
Reports it with a note, since only indices above 2,000 mmol/L count as severe in newborns
Dilutes the serum to bring the index below 31 mmol/L and reports the CRP from that dilution
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins are less sensitive to hemolysis than many chemistry tests, but severe in vitro hemolysis can still interfere: over a hemolysis index of 622 mmol/L the CRP is underestimated, and in that series 199 newborn CRP requests were rejected for severe hemolysis, the highest being 1,997. Each rejected CRP became reliable after the blood sampling was repeated two to five hours later. The figure 31 mmol/L is merely the index equivalent of 0.5 g/L free hemoglobin, the threshold that defines a hemolysed sample.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 4: Limits; and NHLBI, DASH Eating Plan
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A man with new hypertension asks about sodium. What daily limit do the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines set for a healthy adult?
opciones: Under 2,300 mg a day, and less than that for children under 14
Under 1,500 mg a day, and less than that for children under 14
Under 3,400 mg a day, which is what most adults already eat
Under 2,300 mg a day, but only for adults who already have hypertension
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines cap sodium below 2,300 mg a day for the general population and set lower amounts for children under 14. The 1,500 mg figure is the optional lower target of the DASH plan, which drops blood pressure further; 3,400 mg is roughly what people in the United States actually eat, not a goal.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Anchoring the vein · CPT D3 3H k64 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee is about to insert the needle. Which hand makes the skin taut over the vein?
opciones: The hand that is not holding the needle
The hand that is holding the needle itself
Either hand, whichever reaches the site first
The patient's own free hand, guided by the worker
preguntas.explicacion: The hand not being used for the draw is the one that tightens the skin above the vein, with the thumb pulling the skin down and slightly away from the site. The other hand then inserts the needle slowly at fifteen to thirty degrees to the surface of the arm.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), Why the Test is Performed; MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What do the results mean?
preguntas.subtema: Timed draws · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 timed specimens · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a therapeutic drug level have to be drawn at the scheduled time rather than whenever the patient arrives?
opciones: The useful range is narrow: too high is harmful and too low does not work
The tube additive breaks down if the specimen is collected off schedule
The laboratory only runs drug levels in fixed batches during the day
A late sample would need a larger volume to reach the same sensitivity
preguntas.explicacion: For most medicines a certain level in the blood is needed for the proper effect: some are harmful if the level climbs too high and useless if it falls too low, so monitoring keeps the drug inside its therapeutic range. The published ranges assume a set moment in the dosing interval, such as 12 hours after the dose, which is why the clock, not the workload, sets the draw time.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section How long do I have to fast before the test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: How long does a patient usually need to fast before a blood test, and who sets the exact time?
opciones: Usually 8 to 12 hours; the provider sets it according to the test ordered
Usually 4 to 6 hours; the laboratory sets it according to the tube type
Usually 24 hours; the provider sets it according to the patient's body weight
Usually 12 to 16 hours; the phlebotomist sets it at check-in
preguntas.explicacion: The usual fast is 8 to 12 hours, and the provider states exactly how long, depending on the test, sometimes with extra instructions such as avoiding alcohol for longer. Scheduling the draw early in the morning lets most of the fast happen during sleep. The 24-hour figure in the sources is the alcohol-free window before sampling, not a fast.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which set matches the informed-consent elements The Joint Commission requires to be documented?
opciones: Nature, risks and benefits, alternatives, their risks and benefits, and the patient's understanding
Nature, risks and benefits, alternatives, and the patient's signature with a staff witness
Disclosure of the information, the patient's competency, and a voluntary decision
Nature, risks, benefits and alternatives, documented only on the printed consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Five elements are documented: what the procedure is, the risks it carries and the benefits it offers, the alternatives that are reasonable, what each of those would risk and offer in turn, and a check on how far the patient has understood; the record may be a form, a progress note or another part of the chart. The three-part list belongs to research consent, and Bottrell's four leave out the understanding check.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How high is the cuff inflated for a manual reading, and how fast is it let down?
opciones: To 30 mm Hg above where the radial pulse disappears, then down at 2 to 3 mm Hg a second
To 30 mm Hg above the last recorded systolic value, then down at 10 mm Hg a second
To 200 mm Hg in every adult, then down at 2 to 3 mm Hg a second while listening
To 20 mm Hg above where the radial pulse disappears, then down as fast as the valve allows
preguntas.explicacion: The radial pulse is palpated while the cuff fills, and inflation continues to about 30 mm Hg past the point where that pulse vanishes. Deflation then runs at 2 to 3 mm Hg per second. Letting the pressure down too fast, or not inflating high enough, are listed causes of a false reading.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Vaccine Inventory Management
preguntas.subtema: Inventory assessment · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7E k99 · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: How often should a practice take stock of what it holds, and what does it weigh when deciding how much to order?
opciones: Monthly and before each order, weighing expected demand, storage room and stock
Weekly and after each order, weighing the price offered and the delivery times
Yearly and before each order, weighing last year's use and the budget approved
Monthly and after each order, weighing the number of patients seen that month
preguntas.explicacion: An inventory assessment is done at least once a month, and again before an order goes out, so that the practice knows what is really on the shelf. The quantity ordered is set by projected demand, by how much storage capacity there is, and by the current supply on hand.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR)
preguntas.subtema: Common tests and collection · CPT D3 k55 k57 · D2 k47 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A PT/INR is ordered for a patient with almost no usable arm veins. Which sample does the test also accept?
opciones: A sample taken from a fingertip
A sample taken from an ear lobe
A sample taken from a saliva swab
A sample taken from a urine specimen
preguntas.explicacion: This test may be run on blood from a vein or on blood from a fingertip, which is why point-of-care devices for it exist at all. A venous draw still takes under five minutes and the usual risks are no more than slight pain or bruising where the needle went in.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies - for Hospital Patients, Hospital Items That Contain Latex
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D II.J · CCMA 3E1 k128 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a latex allergy. Which items in a phlebotomy tray may contain latex?
opciones: Exam gloves, tourniquets and elastic bandages
Alcohol swabs, gauze pads and paper towels
Needles, tube holders and vacuum tubes
Glucometers, lancets and test strips
preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up in hospital items such as surgical and exam gloves, in catheters and tubing, in tourniquets and medicine vials, and in elastic bandages and wraps; sticky tape and electrode pads are now often latex-free but should be checked. The patient should be given vinyl or silicone alternatives, and latex items removed from the room.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Actions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with limited English insists that her sister interpret for her. What is the correct course?
opciones: Respect the request, and also bring in a qualified interpreter to confirm accuracy
Refuse the sister and proceed only once a telephone interpreter is on the line
Accept the sister alone, because the patient has the right to choose her
Accept the sister, or her 12-year-old son if the sister has to step out
preguntas.explicacion: Where a patient insists that a relative interpret, the request is respected, and a qualified interpreter is brought in as well so that the information travels accurately, since a relative may voice her own views and privacy goes with it. The toolkit is flat about one thing: a child is never used as an interpreter.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Measurement of Blood Pressure; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53)
preguntas.pregunta: When taking a manual blood pressure, where is the stethoscope placed, and which artery is being heard?
opciones: In the antecubital fossa, listening over the brachial artery
At the wrist, listening over the radial artery
At the neck, listening over the common carotid artery
In the antecubital fossa, listening over the median cubital vein
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff goes around the arm at heart level, and the stethoscope is placed on the antecubital region while the cuff deflates, to hear the Korotkoff sounds as blood returns through the brachial artery; the first sound marks the systolic pressure and the last the diastolic. The radial and carotid arteries are pulse sites, not where the cuff is read.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.9 Checklist for Wound Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.n · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A wound culture is being taken. From where in the wound is the swab taken?
opciones: From a square centimeter of viable tissue at or near the center, never from pus or slough
From the thickest pocket of pus, where the organisms are present in the largest numbers
From the eschar at the edge, where the oldest tissue holds the longest-standing organisms
From the skin just outside the margin, where exudate collects and dries against the dressing
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen has to come from the cleanest tissue available, so a square centimeter of viable tissue at or near the center of the wound is chosen, and pus, slough, eschar and necrotic material are avoided; exudate is never collected from the skin. The swab is rotated over that area for five seconds with enough pressure to express fluid, and moistened with saline first if the bed is dry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abdominal Examination", Technique: Percussion
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a(5) · RMA III.F.3.a.iv · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: Percussion over the abdomen produces a high-pitched, drum-like note. What is that note called?
opciones: Tympany, the note produced over air-filled structures
Dullness, the muffled note produced over solid organs
Resonance, the hollow note that is heard over the lungs
Hyperresonance, produced by a hyperinflated chest wall
preguntas.explicacion: Three notes are distinguished during abdominal percussion: tympany, high and drum-like over air; dullness, quiet and muffled over solid organs or fluid; and resonance, low and hollow, the note of the lungs. The method estimates liver and spleen size and picks up masses, and in ascites the note shifts from tympanic to dull as the examiner moves toward the flanks.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: What is the standing of skinfold thickness measurements in the clinic?
opciones: They vary widely between measurers and have had limited clinical use
They are the reference standard against which body mass index is judged
They have replaced waist circumference as the measure of central fat
They are taken with a tape rather than calipers at eight standard sites
preguntas.explicacion: Skinfolds are read with calipers at sites that include the chest and the abdomen, the subscapular area, the calf and the thigh, the iliac crest, the triceps and the biceps, pinching the skin about 2 cm from the point being measured. Even with a standard technique the readings vary a great deal, and their use in the clinical setting has so far been limited.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Muscular System: Muscle Types
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which three types of muscle tissue does the body contain, and which of them is both striated and involuntary?
opciones: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; cardiac is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; smooth is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; skeletal is striated and involuntary
Striated, spindle and rectangular; spindle is striated and involuntary
preguntas.explicacion: Skeletal muscle attaches to bone, is striated and is under voluntary control. Smooth muscle lines the hollow organs, is not striated and works involuntarily under the autonomic nervous system. Cardiac muscle sits in the heart wall and takes one feature from each: striated like skeletal, involuntary like smooth.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Burns", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A burn on a patient's forearm is red and painful and has raised blisters. How is that depth classified?
opciones: Partial thickness, the depth once called a second-degree burn
Superficial, the depth once called a first-degree burn
Full thickness, the depth once called a third-degree burn
Superficial with inhalation injury, since blisters mean smoke
preguntas.explicacion: Blisters mark the partial-thickness level, which reaches the outer layer and the layer beneath it and is painful, red and swollen. A superficial burn touches only the outer layer and gives pain, redness and swelling with no blisters. A full-thickness burn reaches the deep layers, looks white or charred, and the skin there may be numb.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Functional Elements of a Lawsuit
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, malpractice and negligence · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a professional liability torts · RMA I.C.3 legal terminology · CMAA 3 k31
preguntas.pregunta: A patient sues after an injury during a draw. Which four elements must the plaintiff prove for a medical malpractice claim to succeed?
opciones: A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and damages
A duty to the patient, a written complaint, an apology refused, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, an intent to harm, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and a policy in force
preguntas.explicacion: A mistake on its own is not malpractice. The plaintiff has to establish that the clinician owed this patient a duty, that the duty was breached measured against the standard of care, that the poor outcome came from the act or the omission and not from the underlying disease, and that damages followed. Intent is not on the list, which is what separates negligence from a deliberate wrong.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: Where should sterile gloves be donned, and where are the hands held once both are on?
opciones: Away from the sterile field, with the gloved hands interlocked above waist level
Directly over the sterile field, with the gloved hands interlocked above waist level
Away from the sterile field, with the gloved hands resting at the sides until needed
Directly over the sterile field, with the gloved hands held below the level of the tray
preguntas.explicacion: Gloving happens away from the field, so that powder, packaging or a fumbled glove cannot fall onto it. Once both gloves are on, the fingers are interlocked and the hands kept above the waist, because anything below waist level counts as contaminated. Letting the hands drop to the sides would put them straight into that zone.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Situation Monitoring Process
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What is the team outcome in which everyone ends up on the same page?
opciones: Shared mental model
Situation awareness
Situation monitoring
Cross-monitoring
preguntas.explicacion: Situation monitoring is the individual skill of scanning and assessing what is going on; situation awareness is what that produces in the individual, the state of knowing how things stand; and the shared mental model is the team outcome arising when every member keeps that awareness and communicates it. Cross-monitoring is watching each other for slips.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Growth chart; and StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement" (NBK537315)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.c · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is height measured in a child under 3 years old at a well-child visit?
opciones: Lying down, as recumbent length, with the head and feet against the boards
Standing at a wall-mounted stadiometer, with the child's shoes taken off
Standing, but with a parent holding the child upright against the device
Lying down, with a tape run along the child from the crown to the knees
preguntas.explicacion: Under the age of 3 the measurement is taken lying down and is called recumbent length; from 3 years on it is taken standing. The head goes against the headboard with the body supine and the footboard brought against the soles, and a second person keeps the body and legs straight.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; and Fibrinolysis
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the three steps of hemostasis occur after a vessel is punctured?
opciones: Vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation
Platelet plug, vascular spasm, coagulation
Coagulation, fibrinolysis, platelet plug
Vascular spasm, coagulation, fibrinolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a ruptured vessel, in three steps: first the smooth muscle of the vessel wall contracts (vascular spasm), then platelets stick to the exposed collagen and to each other (platelet plug), and finally a fibrin clot forms (coagulation). Fibrinolysis is not one of the three; it is the later breakdown of the clot as the vessel heals. Failure of any step leads to hemorrhage.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the stethoscope placed for a manual reading?
opciones: Over the medial antecubital fossa, at the usual course of the brachial artery
Over the lateral antecubital fossa, where the radial artery begins its course
Over the middle of the cuff, so the sound reaches it through the inflated bladder
Over the wrist at the radial artery, where the pulse was palpated before inflating
preguntas.explicacion: The bell or the diaphragm goes on the inner side of the crease of the elbow, where the brachial artery runs, which is why the cuff leaves that space free. Positioning matters: shifting the stethoscope makes the sounds appear earlier or later and moves the recorded pressure with them.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Nosebleed", Home Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room starts a nosebleed. How is it managed?
opciones: Sitting up and leaning forward, pinching the soft part for 10 full minutes
Sitting up and tilting the head back, pinching the bridge for 5 minutes
Lying down flat with a cold pack on the neck and the nostrils packed
Sitting up and blowing the nose gently every minute to clear the clots
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits, leans forward so blood is not swallowed, breathes through the mouth, and squeezes the soft part of the nose shut between thumb and finger for a full 10 minutes without checking early. Cold across the bridge of the nose may help; lying down is not advised, the inside of the nose is not packed, and sniffing or blowing waits.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The dorsum of the hand is the preferred location for what?
opciones: Establishing an intravenous site
Routine venous blood sampling in adults
Arterial blood gas sampling
Capillary sampling in infants
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is the common site for drawing blood; the dorsum of the hand, by contrast, is the site of choice for starting an IV line. Arterial sampling is indicated for blood gases and is done on arteries, and the capillary site the chapter names for infants is the lateral plantar surface of the heel.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The only clearly visible vein in a patient's antecubital fossa forks into two branches right at the point that would be easiest to reach. What does the WHO's Step 3 say about that spot?
opciones: Do not insert the needle where veins diverge, because it raises the chance of a hematoma
Insert the needle at the fork, because two branches give the best blood flow
Insert the needle just below the fork only if the tourniquet has been on for less than a minute
Use the fork, since the biceps aponeurosis beneath it prevents hematoma formation
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 instructs the phlebotomist not to put the needle in where the veins divide, precisely because that raises the chance of a hematoma, and to look for a vein of decent calibre, plainly visible, straight and unobstructed. The protective role of the biceps aponeurosis applies to the median cubital vein in general, not as a license to puncture a branching point.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Respiratory Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration c · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: What is recorded when the respiratory assessment is charted?
opciones: The rate, the depth of the breaths and the pattern they follow
The rate alone, since depth and pattern are subjective judgments
The rate and the oxygen saturation, which stands in for the depth
The rate and the position the patient was in during the counting
preguntas.explicacion: A respiratory rate on its own leaves out what the breathing looked like. The assessment characterizes rate, depth and pattern, because the pattern carries the diagnosis: deep and regular, cycling with pauses, or paradoxical chest movement each point somewhere different. Substituting an oximeter reading for a count is a known documentation problem.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrial Fibrillation", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation?
opciones: Irregularly irregular narrow complexes with no clear P waves
Regularly irregular narrow complexes with no clear P waves
Irregularly irregular wide complexes with clear P waves
Regular narrow complexes with a P wave before each of them
preguntas.explicacion: Atrial activity is so fast that no real P waves survive on the tracing, and only some impulses get through to the ventricles, which is what makes the spacing irregularly irregular. The pulse is irregular too, and the ventricular rate usually falls somewhere between 80 and 180 per minute.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Diabetes Diet, Eating, & Physical Activity — Plate method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(b) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(b) · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A newly diagnosed patient with diabetes is taught the plate method. How is the 9-inch plate divided?
opciones: Half nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter carb foods, one quarter protein foods
Half carb foods, one quarter nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter protein foods
One third each of nonstarchy vegetables, carb foods and protein foods
Half protein foods, one quarter nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter carb foods
preguntas.explicacion: The plate method controls portions without weighing or counting. Half the plate goes to nonstarchy vegetables, leafy greens, carrots, peppers or green beans for instance; a quarter to carb foods high in fiber, brown rice, whole grains, beans or fruit; and the last quarter to lean meats, fish, dairy or soy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: How should V4, V5 and V6 look once all six chest electrodes are on?
opciones: Lined up horizontally along the fifth intercostal space
