preguntas.pregunta: Under the Hazard Communication standard, which of these is classified as a health hazard rather than a physical hazard?
opciones: Skin corrosion or irritation
A flammable liquid such as a solvent
A gas under pressure in a cylinder
An oxidizing liquid or solid
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool splits the classifications into two families. On the health side: acute toxicity; corrosion or irritation of the skin; serious eye damage or eye irritation; sensitization of the airways or of the skin; germ cell mutagenicity; carcinogenicity; toxicity to reproduction; target organ toxicity; and aspiration hazard. On the physical side: explosives; gases under pressure; flammables and oxidizers; substances that are self-reactive, pyrophoric or self-heating; organic peroxides; anything corrosive to metal; and substances that release flammable gas on contact with water.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods · CMA II.F.1.c(2) hearing impaired
preguntas.pregunta: Speaking clearly at eye level has still not got the post-draw instructions across to a patient with hearing loss. Which two further measures does the guidance name?
opciones: Write the points that matter on a notepad, and use an amplification device if the clinic has one
Write the points that matter on a notepad, and book the follow-up in a quieter room later on
Print the points in large type on the discharge sheet, and use an amplification device if there is one
Have the patient repeat the points back, and use an amplification device if the clinic has one
preguntas.explicacion: Two things sit in the guidance alongside the tone of voice and the face at eye level. Keep a notepad within reach and write down what has to survive the visit — the diagnosis, the treatment, the terms that matter — and reach for an amplification device where the clinic or the hospital has one. Enlarged print belongs to the measures for poor eyesight, not for poor hearing, and while the change of subject is meant to be signalled clearly, nothing there asks the patient to recite the instructions back.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Formation of the Platelet Plug
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Bleeding from a small puncture stops within minutes, before any fibrin has formed. Which step of hemostasis is doing the work, and which plasma glycoprotein stabilizes it?
opciones: The platelet plug, stabilized by von Willebrand factor
The fibrin mesh, which factor XIII cross-links and stabilizes
The vascular spasm, which serotonin from platelets maintains
Fibrinolysis, which plasmin made from plasminogen carries out
preguntas.explicacion: In the second step of hemostasis, platelets meet the exposed collagen, become spiked and sticky and clump together, helped by a plasma glycoprotein called von Willebrand factor that stabilizes the growing plug. The plug can temporarily seal a small opening and buys time for coagulation. Factor XIII stabilizes fibrin, serotonin keeps the vessel constricted, and plasmin dissolves the finished clot.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Cross-Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does cross-monitoring involve?
opciones: Watching the actions and the stress of teammates to catch slips
Scanning the whole situation to keep track of what is going on
Helping a colleague with tasks when the workload gets heavy
Checking that a message was received the way it was intended
preguntas.explicacion: Cross-monitoring is a harm reduction strategy: keeping an eye on what other team members are doing and on the stress they are carrying, providing a safety net, and catching mistakes or oversights early. It is described as watching each other's back. Scanning the situation is situation monitoring, covering someone's work is task assistance, and confirming a message is a check-back.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Measuring Your Blood Pressure: How to measure your blood pressure at home
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B14 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being taught to monitor blood pressure at home. Which instruction is given?
opciones: Take two or more readings a minute or two apart, at the same time each day
Take one reading a day, at the hour the patient happens to be free that day
Take at least two readings 10 minutes apart, at a different hour each day
Take a reading only on days the patient feels unwell, and log those values
preguntas.explicacion: Self-measured monitoring works best with a routine: the same hour every day, at least two readings a minute or two apart, and every value written in a log. One common plan is a reading before breakfast and before dinner for five days, which gives the provider at least ten values to work from.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient walks with the left crutch and the right leg going forward together, then the right crutch with the left leg. Which gait is that?
opciones: The two-point gait, which pairs each crutch with the opposite leg
The four-point gait, which moves each crutch and each leg on its own
The three-point gait, which moves both crutches with the injured leg
The swing-to gait, which sends both crutches out before both legs
preguntas.explicacion: Pairing one crutch with the leg on the other side is the two-point pattern. Moving each of the four points separately is the four-point, which gives more support. Advancing both crutches together with the injured leg while the sound leg holds the weight is the three-point, and moving both crutches then both legs is the swing-to.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A problem list records a TIA two years before the CVA the patient was admitted with. What separates those two entries?
opciones: A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is the stroke itself
A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is a clot in a deep vein
A TIA is a heart attack, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
A TIA is a brief seizure, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
preguntas.explicacion: TIA stands for transient ischemic attack, listed as a small stroke, while CVA is a cerebrovascular accident, the stroke or brain attack itself. The abbreviations that get swapped in belong to other organs: AMI and MI are the heart attack, and DVT is the clot in a deep vein.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", sections Issues of Concern and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 k9 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the light gray fluoride tube before the purple EDTA tube. What is the main risk?
opciones: Additive carried from one tube into the next, giving unreliable results
Loss of the vacuum in the purple tube as soon as it is pushed on
A short draw in the gray tube, which can haemolyse that specimen
Clotting in the purple tube, because its additive was left unmixed
preguntas.explicacion: A fixed sequence exists so that the additive of one tube is not carried into the tube filled next, and falsely raised or lowered values can follow in chemistry, hematology, serology and microbiology. A short draw and unmixed additive are real faults, but they come from filling and mixing, not order.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Systolic and Diastolic Pressures; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of Circulation, Pulse and Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's blood pressure is recorded as 120/80. What does each number represent?
opciones: 120 is systolic, during ventricular contraction; 80 is diastolic, during relaxation
120 is diastolic, during ventricular relaxation; 80 is systolic, during contraction
120 is the pulse pressure in the aorta; 80 is the mean arterial pressure in the arteries
120 is the pressure inside the aorta; 80 is the pressure inside the venae cavae
preguntas.explicacion: A blood pressure of 120/80 is a normal adult value written as systolic over diastolic: the higher number, around 120 mm Hg, is the arterial pressure produced by ventricular contraction, and the lower, about 80 mm Hg, is the pressure during ventricular relaxation. Pulse pressure is their difference (40 mm Hg here) and mean arterial pressure is a separate calculated value.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A5 k56 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A caregiver reports a child's temperature as 38 °C. Which Fahrenheit value is recorded, and what does it mean by the rectal route?
opciones: 100.4 °F, which is exactly the rectal threshold for fever in a child
101.4 °F, which is above the rectal threshold for fever in a child
99.5 °F, which is the oral rather than the rectal threshold in a child
98.6 °F, which is the average adult value and not a fever at any site
preguntas.explicacion: The two scales are recorded as a pair in clinical sources: 38 °C is 100.4 °F, and that is the exact point at which a rectal reading counts as fever in a child. The oral threshold is 99.5 °F (37.5 °C) and the average adult value is 98.6 °F (37 °C), which is why the route is always written beside the number.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Endocrine System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(9) (2027 I.C.6.f(9)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does the action of the endocrine system differ from that of the nervous system?
opciones: It is slower and more generalized, working through hormones in the blood
It is faster and more localized, working through hormones in the blood
It is slower and more localized, working through impulses along nerves
It is faster and more generalized, working through impulses along nerves
preguntas.explicacion: Both systems regulate the body, but on different clocks. The nervous system uses electrical impulses and neurotransmitters, and its effects are local and last seconds. The endocrine system uses hormones carried in the blood, and its effects are measured in minutes, hours or weeks and reach far more of the body at once.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which tube in the WHO order of draw is filled immediately before the purple EDTA tube when a full set is collected?
opciones: The light green PST with lithium heparin and gel
The dark green sodium heparin tube
The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The red-gray tiger top or gold serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA is position 8 in Table 2.3, and position 7 is the light green plasma separator tube with lithium heparin and a gel separator. The dark green sodium heparin tube is position 6, the serum separator tube position 5, and the pale yellow ACD tube comes after EDTA at position 9. Reading the table by neighbours is the surest way to reconstruct the whole sequence.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood from a syringe has to go into a sample tube that has no rubber stopper. How is it transferred?
opciones: Injected extremely slowly, keeping pressure and speed to a minimum
Injected as briskly as possible so the tube fills before it can clot
Poured down the inner wall of the tube after the needle is removed
Injected only after the needle has been recapped for the transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Where there is no rubber stopper to pierce, the blood is injected extremely slowly, because keeping the pressure and the velocity of the transfer low is what limits hemolysis. The instruction that closes that step is not to recap and remove the needle afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Yellow, Pink, and Blue
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: After a blood culture bottle is filled, how many times should it be mixed?
opciones: 8 to 10 times
3 to 6 times
1 or 2 times
15 to 20 times
preguntas.explicacion: A culture bottle is mixed 8 to 10 times after the blood is added so that the contents combine properly. The 3 to 6 inversions belong to the light blue citrate tube in the coagulopathies review, done immediately after the draw. One or two turns is the kind of under-mixing the review links to small clots, and 15 to 20 is not a figure given for any tube.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Interprofessional Team Members (Respiratory Therapists)
preguntas.subtema: Team member roles · CCMA 4G k167 · CMA II.F.4.c / 2027 II.F.2.c · NCMA 3.1 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which team member manages oxygen therapy, draws arterial blood gases and runs mechanical ventilators?
opciones: The respiratory therapist, who also gives inhalers and nebulizer medicines
The physical therapist, who also teaches patients to use walkers and canes safely
The occupational therapist, who also assesses the home for safety needs
The clinical laboratory technologist, who also performs blood bank testing
preguntas.explicacion: Respiratory therapists treat respiratory conditions: drawing arterial blood gases, managing oxygen therapy, running mechanical ventilators and CPAP or BiPAP machines, giving inhalers and nebulizer medicines, intubating, assisting with bronchoscopy, performing chest physiotherapy, and taking a central part during cardiac and respiratory arrests.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A referral is addressed to a nephrologist. Which organ does the root of that specialty name?
opciones: The kidney, which is also named by the root ren-
The liver, which is also named by the root hepat-
The bladder, which is also named by the root cyst-
The stomach, which is also named by the root gastr-
preguntas.explicacion: Nephr- and ren- both name the kidney, which is why the same organ gives us nephrology and renal failure. The other roots belong to their own organs: hepat- the liver, cyst- a bladder or sac, gastr- the stomach. Two roots for one organ is common in this vocabulary, one from Greek and one from Latin.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Communication styles · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches a passive communicator?
opciones: One who puts the rights of others first and sounds tentative or apologetic
One who defends their own rights even at the cost of the rights of others
One who respects the rights of others while standing up for their own ideas
One who assumes the message was understood without ever verifying it
preguntas.explicacion: Three styles are described. The passive communicator places everyone else's rights above their own, sounds apologetic or unsure, and stays quiet even when wronged. Defending your own rights at the expense of others is the aggressive style, and balancing both is the assertive one. Assuming understanding without checking describes passive listening, not the passive style.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D II.I · CCMA 3E1 k126 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a history of a vagal attack during earlier draws sought out before the needle comes out?
opciones: So the team is ready with the means to act should a faint happen
So the draw can be logged as high risk and handed to a nurse
So the tourniquet time can be cut to under thirty seconds
So the patient can be given a sugary drink to break the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Particular attention goes to spotting the patient who is frightened of blood testing, or who has a positive history of a vasovagal attack during an earlier procedure of the kind, so that every means of acting on a vagal syncope is ready beforehand. Simple steps such as counting down may cut anxiety a great deal, and a severe history of panic attacks may call for lying the patient down.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: The office accepts assignment for a Medicare patient. What does that oblige it to do about her bill?
opciones: Charge her only the deductible and coinsurance, and file the claim at no charge
Collect the whole charge at the visit and let her seek reimbursement afterwards
Charge up to fifteen percent above the approved amount for each service given
Decide service by service whether the approved amount will be accepted as payment
preguntas.explicacion: Accepting assignment means treating the amount Medicare approves as payment in full, and it holds for every Part A and Part B service the provider gives. Such a provider agrees to charge only the deductible and the coinsurance, usually waits for Medicare to pay its share first, and has to send the claim to Medicare without charging the patient for doing it.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(h), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5H · PBT VI.B VI.F · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: The chemistry analyzer goes down and a stat troponin ordered from the emergency department will not be reported within the laboratory's established time frame. What does CLIA require?
opciones: The laboratory decides, based on the urgency of the test, whether to notify the appropriate person of the delay
The laboratory must notify the ordering person of every delayed result, regardless of the urgency of the test
The laboratory must refer the specimen to another CLIA-certified laboratory within 30 minutes of the failure
The laboratory may wait until the analyzer is repaired, since delays are addressed only by its accreditor
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(h) says that where the laboratory cannot get patient results out inside the time frames it has set for itself, it has to weigh the urgency of the tests ordered and decide whether the appropriate individuals should be told about the delay; a stat cardiac marker is the sort of request where that decision leans toward notifying. The rule neither demands notice for every delay, nor sets a referral deadline, nor lets the laboratory say nothing.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Syringes and Needles
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which parts make up a syringe and its needle?
opciones: Plunger, barrel and needle hub; the needle has hub, shaft and bevel
Plunger, barrel and filter; the needle has hub, shaft and safety shield
Plunger, cylinder and stopper; the needle has hub, bevel and canister
Barrel, spacer and hub; the needle has shaft, bevel and rubber seal
preguntas.explicacion: A disposable syringe is built from a barrel, a plunger and a needle hub, and sizes run from 0.5 mL to 60 mL. The needle itself has the hub that fits the syringe tip, the shaft, and the bevel, the slanted tip that cuts into the skin; all three parts stay sterile. A Luer lock syringe carries threads in the hub so needles and tubing connect securely, and the barrel holds the readable scale.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Head injury - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.s · 2027 I.B.8.s · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A scalp wound is bleeding and a skull fracture is suspected. How is the bleeding handled?
opciones: Cover it with sterile gauze without pressing down on the site
Press firmly with a clean cloth until the bleeding has stopped
Wash the wound out first and then press with a sterile dressing
Pull the debris out of the wound and then bandage it tightly
preguntas.explicacion: With a suspected skull fracture, direct pressure is not applied to the bleeding site and debris is not taken out; the wound is covered with sterile gauze. Otherwise bleeding is stopped by pressing a clean cloth firmly, and a soaked cloth gets another on top. A deep or heavily bleeding head wound is not washed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Enteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(8) · RMA III.G.4.d(ii)
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a drug given by the rectal route is correct?
opciones: The mucosa is very vascular, and only about half the dose goes straight to the liver
The mucosa is poorly vascular, so it absorbs more slowly than any other enteral route
The whole dose enters the portal vein, so the first-pass effect is at its very greatest
The route counts as parenteral, since the drug never enters the digestive tract at all
preguntas.explicacion: Rectal administration is counted among the enteral routes. Its mucosa carries a rich blood supply, so absorption is rapid and effective, and the drug diffuses passively as it does under the tongue. Only about half of what the rectum absorbs travels directly to the liver, so first-pass metabolism is partly avoided. Parenteral means the injection routes, and an intravenous dose bypasses the liver's first pass entirely.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and palpation · CPT D3 k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: On palpation, a vein feels hard and cord-like from previous punctures. Which contraindication does this represent?
opciones: Venous fibrosis on palpation
A vascular graft in the arm
Cellulitis or abscess
Ipsilateral radical mastectomy
preguntas.explicacion: Venous fibrosis on palpation is one of the local contraindications, alongside a site attempted before that has been left with scar tissue. A vascular graft, cellulitis or abscess and a history of radical mastectomy on the same side are separate entries in the same list, each with its own history or appearance rather than a fibrotic feel of the vein itself.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 16. Monitoring of Sterilizers
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: How often does the guideline call for biological monitoring of a steam sterilizer?
opciones: At least weekly, and in every load that contains implantable objects
At least monthly, and in every load that contains implantable objects
At least weekly, and in every load, including loads of routine reusable instruments
At least daily, and in the first load after any repair to the machine
preguntas.explicacion: Steam and low-temperature sterilizers are monitored at least weekly with the right commercial spore preparation, and every load holding implantable items gets its own biological indicator, with the items quarantined until the result is negative where that is feasible. Daily testing is an option in busy departments, because it finds a malfunction sooner and shrinks any recall.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", sections Introduction, Pathophysiology and History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A 'true' latex allergy is which type of reaction?
opciones: Type I, IgE-mediated, with symptoms within minutes of exposure
Type IV, delayed, caused by the chemical antioxidants added in processing
Irritant contact dermatitis from friction or chemical contact
Type IV, delayed, caused by inhaling the cornstarch powder on gloves
preguntas.explicacion: A true latex allergy is a type I hypersensitivity mediated by IgE antibodies bound to the rubber proteins; within minutes the patient may develop hives, wheezing, a runny nose and conjunctivitis, and systemic reactions up to anaphylaxis are possible. The processing chemicals cause a delayed type IV reaction, and irritant dermatitis is a non-immune reaction, neither of them a true allergy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Other Issues, Trough Versus Free Levels; and section Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: For which antiepileptic drugs is the trough level said to matter most?
opciones: Those with short half-lives, since the trough marks the between-dose minimum
Those with long half-lives, since the level then reflects long-term usage
Those given intravenously, since the peak arrives with the infusion
Those newly substituted between a brand and a generic preparation
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration at its lowest, typically just before the next dose falls due, and it matters most for an antiepileptic whose half-life is short, since the trough marks the minimum reached between doses. Phenytoin's long half-life is why its level reflects long-term usage, and monitoring can guide dosing where a substitution cannot be avoided.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9: Clean contaminated surfaces and complete patient procedure
preguntas.subtema: Sharps and waste disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: After a routine draw, which used item does the WHO say may go into the general waste (unless local rules differ), and which must go into a puncture-resistant container?
opciones: Gloves that would not drip blood if they were squeezed may go to general waste; the needle to the sharps container
The gauze pressed on the puncture site may go to general waste; the gloves go to the sharps container
The needle may go to general waste once its safety feature is activated; the gloves go to the sharps container instead
Every item from a blood draw, gloves included, goes to the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 drops the used needle and syringe, or the sampling device, into a sharps container a needle cannot pierce, and places the other items in their waste category: items that would not drip blood if they were squeezed, gloves being the example, can go to the general waste unless local rules say otherwise. An activated safety feature does not turn a needle into general waste.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypoglycemia", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.f · 2027 I.B.8.f · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What are the three parts of the Whipple triad?
opciones: Symptoms of hypoglycemia, a low measured glucose, and relief when it is corrected
Symptoms of hyperglycemia, a high measured glucose, and ketones found in urine
Sweating, tremor and confusion appearing together in a patient with diabetes
A low glucose, a high insulin level and a tumor found inside the pancreas
preguntas.explicacion: Since 1938 this triad has been the way hypoglycemia is described: the clinician recognizes symptoms of hypoglycemia, obtains a low blood glucose measurement, and then sees those symptoms lift immediately once the low glucose is corrected. It is the reason a reading is taken and repeated rather than judging by symptoms alone.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature b(iii) · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A rectal temperature is being taken with a digital thermometer. What is the described technique?
opciones: A lubricated blunt tip is inserted about 4 to 5 cm at a 20-degree angle, patient prone
A lubricated blunt tip is inserted about 15 cm at a 45-degree angle, patient supine
A bare blunt tip is inserted about 2 to 3 cm at a right angle, patient on the left side
A lubricated blunt tip is inserted about 4 to 5 cm at a 60-degree angle, patient seated
preguntas.explicacion: The described method uses a lubricated blunt-tipped thermometer inserted roughly 4 to 5 cm into the anal canal at about 20 degrees from the horizontal, with the patient prone. The route is reserved for children and for patients who cannot cooperate, and it is the preferred route when hypothermia is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins" (2023), sections Structure and Function, and Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53 hand) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does each of the two main superficial veins of the arm end once it has climbed past the shoulder?
opciones: The cephalic pierces the deep fascia at the axilla into the subclavian; the basilic joins the brachial or axillary
The basilic pierces the deep fascia at the axilla into the subclavian; the cephalic joins the brachial or axillary
Both stay superficial the whole way and empty together into the subclavian vein above the collarbone
The cephalic joins the median cubital at the elbow; the basilic runs on alone as far as the superior vena cava
preguntas.explicacion: The two superficial veins part company at the top of the arm. The cephalic goes through the deep fascia around the axilla and ends in the subclavian vein. The basilic ends earlier and less predictably: it may empty into the brachial vein or into the axillary vein, and which of the two it picks varies from person to person. Nothing of this is fixed by rule — the venous pattern of the limb is one of the most variable in the body, the basilic is usually the wider of the pair though sometimes the cephalic is, and the only constant is that everything comes back to the superior vena cava by way of the subclavian.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Putting on the gown · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How far should an isolation gown reach when it is put on correctly?
opciones: From the neck to the knees and to the wrists, wrapped at the back
From the shoulders to the hips, left open behind for ventilation
From the neck to the ankles, with the ties left loose at the neck
From the chest to the knees, over the uniform but under the badge
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the gown goes on first, outside the patient room, and it has to cover the body from neck to knees and the arms to the wrists, and wrap around the back, with the neck and waist ties fastened if the gown has them. Gloves go on last and are pulled over the cuff of the gown, so that no skin or sleeve is left showing between the two. A gown left open at the back is not covering what it was chosen to cover.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: When placing a peripheral IV line, how far proximal to the intended site is the tourniquet applied, and how tight?
opciones: 5 to 10 cm proximal, tight enough to swell the veins while the arterial flow continues
2 cm proximal, tight enough to abolish the radial pulse for the duration of the draw
15 to 20 cm proximal, loose enough that the veins remain flat until the fist is made
5 to 10 cm distal, tight enough to swell the veins while the arterial flow continues
preguntas.explicacion: For a peripheral line the tourniquet sits roughly 5 to 10 cm above the intended site, tight enough to swell the veins but not so tight that arterial flow stops, since engorgement is what makes the vein easy to identify and cannulate. Distal placement is the wrong side, abolishing the pulse means arterial occlusion, and 2 cm is the WHO's swab area, not a tourniquet distance.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(D), Housekeeping; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex F
preguntas.subtema: Broken glass and spills · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.6.b / 2027 I.B.5.b · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: A tube of blood shatters on the floor of the draw room. How must the broken glass be picked up?
opciones: By mechanical means only: dust pan and brush, tongs or forceps, never by hand
With gloved hands, since gloves are the barrier the standard requires for contaminated items
With paper towels soaked in disinfectant, so the glass is decontaminated as it is lifted
With a reusable sharps container held open, so the pieces can be swept directly into it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(D) is explicit: glassware that has broken and may carry contamination is never picked up directly with the hands, gloved or not; it is lifted mechanically, with a dust pan and brush, or with tongs or forceps. The WHO spillage annex describes the same sequence, tongs or pan and brush for the glass, which then goes into a sharps container, followed by absorbing the fluid, cleaning with detergent and applying 0.5 percent hypochlorite. Reusable sharps containers are never opened or emptied by hand under (d)(4)(iii)(A)(4).

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Exposure to HIV is a medical emergency; CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003)
preguntas.subtema: Timing of HIV PEP · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC describe an HIV exposure as a medical emergency?
opciones: Infection often takes hold within 24 to 36 hours, so PEP works best when begun within hours
Antibodies appear within 24 to 36 hours, so a rapid test must be done before any PEP
PEP is only effective if started before the source patient's viral load is known
The exposed worker becomes infectious to others within 24 to 36 hours
preguntas.explicacion: HIV takes hold fast, usually 24 to 36 hours after the exposure, which is why the patient is evaluated at speed and the first dose given immediately where a rapid test result is not yet to hand and PEP is indicated. The older CDC brochure makes the same point: treatment should begin preferably within hours rather than days, since animal studies suggest the benefit falls off after 24 to 36 hours. Antibodies and infectiousness take far longer to appear, which is why follow-up testing runs on for months.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act: Title V
preguntas.subtema: Declining an accommodation · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with low vision declines the large-print forms the office offers her. What does the law say about that refusal?
opciones: She is free to decline an aid or accommodation she does not want to accept
She must accept it once it has been prepared, or sign a waiver of her rights
She may decline it only if she brings a companion who will read the forms
She may decline it, but the office must then record the refusal in her chart
preguntas.explicacion: The last title of the law collects the rules on how the rest of it operates, and one of them says outright that nobody with a disability has to accept an aid, a service or an accommodation that is offered. The same title bars retaliation against anyone who has asserted these rights.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Amputation - traumatic", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: What is done first for the patient in a traumatic amputation, before the severed part is dealt with?
opciones: Airway, breathing and circulation are checked and the bleeding is controlled
The stump is rinsed with sterile saline and wrapped in a bulky dressing
The patient is walked to a chair so the injured limb can be raised
The part is searched for, since reattachment depends on finding it early
preguntas.explicacion: The patient comes before the part: airway, breathing and circulation are checked, rescue breathing, CPR or bleeding control is started if needed, and help is called. Bleeding is controlled with direct pressure and elevation, and a tight bandage or tourniquet is easier than direct pressure when the bleeding threatens life.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who faints at every blood test asks what can be done between visits. Which conservative advice fits?
opciones: Lie down at the first warning sign, drink more fluid, change position slowly
Stand up quickly at the first warning sign, drink less fluid, keep the arm raised
Lie down after the test only, restrict salt intake, and avoid all morning draws
Sit upright through the warning signs, drink more fluid, and hold the breath in
preguntas.explicacion: Management of these episodes is conservative: avoid known triggers, take more fluid to improve filling, and change position slowly. Patients are taught the warning signs and told to get themselves supine when one starts, which often stops the faint and prevents a fall.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k62 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E7 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time drawn through an indwelling line comes back markedly prolonged although the patient takes no anticoagulant. What is the likely cause?
opciones: Contamination of the sample by the heparin or saline used to flush the line
Contamination of the sample by the alcohol used to disinfect the skin surface
Excess citrate from a tube that was filled well beyond its stated volume line
Loss of citrate from a tube that was inverted more than six times after filling
preguntas.explicacion: Samples taken from indwelling catheters can pick up the heparin or other solutions used to flush the line, and that artificially lengthens clotting times. Overfilling is not the recognized fault: the problem described for citrate tubes is a short draw, which leaves too much anticoagulant for the plasma.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(iii), (d)(2)(iv) and (b), Definitions: Handwashing Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Handwashing facilities · CPT D1 k33 k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of employers regarding handwashing facilities?
opciones: The employer must provide facilities that are readily accessible to employees
Employees may substitute alcohol hand rub at any time, even when sinks are available
A sink is required only where research or production work involves HIV and HBV
Facilities must be foot- or elbow-operated and located near the exit door of every draw room
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(iii) has the employer provide handwashing facilities that are readily accessible, and paragraph (b) says what one is: potable water that runs, soap, and either single-use towels or an air dryer. Only where such facilities are not feasible does (d)(2)(iv) allow antiseptic hand cleanser or towelettes, and even then the hands still have to reach soap and running water as soon as that becomes feasible. Foot- or elbow-operated sinks by the exit door are what (e)(4)(iii) requires of HIV and HBV production facilities, not of an ordinary draw room.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xii), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Prohibited work practices · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice does the standard prohibit outright in areas where blood is handled?
opciones: Drawing blood or OPIM up by mouth, whether by pipette or by suction
Using a mechanical device to remove a contaminated needle when a procedure requires it
Decontaminating utility gloves for reuse when the glove is still intact
Keeping a sharps container upright and replacing it before it overfills
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xii) bans mouth pipetting and mouth suctioning of blood or OPIM with no exception. The other three are things the standard permits or requires: (d)(2)(vii)(B) allows needle removal by mechanical device or one-handed technique when the (d)(2)(vii)(A) exception applies; (d)(3)(ix)(C) allows utility gloves to be decontaminated and reused while their integrity holds; and (d)(4)(iii)(A)(2) requires sharps containers to be kept upright and replaced routinely.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Effective Team Event Tools
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: The team meets before the clinic session opens to share the plan, hand out roles and set expectations. Which tool is that?
opciones: A brief, held before the work starts
A huddle, called during the session
A debrief, once the session is over
A handoff, as responsibility passes
preguntas.explicacion: Sharing the plan is the brief: a short session before the start that covers team formation, roles and responsibilities, expectations, climate and likely contingencies. The huddle is the ad hoc meeting that monitors and modifies the plan along the way, the debrief reviews performance afterwards, and a handoff transfers responsibility for a patient.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.5 Wound Dressings
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.k · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which dressing is occlusive, promotes autolytic debridement, and is avoided on an infected wound?
opciones: A hydrocolloid, usually changed every three to five days
An alginate, usually changed every twenty-four to forty-eight hours
A transparent film, usually left over wounds with no exudate at all
A dry sterile gauze, usually changed at least once every twenty-four hours
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrocolloids act as an occlusive barrier against contaminants, hold a moist environment and bring about autolytic debridement, and the thicker ones take up moderate drainage. They are avoided in infected wounds, are common over pressure injuries, may smell on removal because of what they are made from, and are changed every three to five days.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.8 Checklist for Applying and Removing Sterile Gloves
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant is putting on the first sterile glove. Where may the bare hand touch it?
opciones: Only the inside surface of the folded cuff, held with thumb and index finger
Only the outside surface of the folded cuff, held with thumb and index finger
Only the fingertips of the glove, which stay clear of the patient's skin anyway
Only the palm of the glove, which will be covered once the hand slides inside
preguntas.explicacion: The nondominant bare hand grasps the inside surface of the cuff, using thumb and index finger, and lifts the glove clear without touching any surface. It is held no more than 12 to 18 inches above the table while the hand is worked in. That bare hand never touches either the package's inside or any sterile part of either glove.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Nerve injury · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What symptoms result from accidental damage to the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve during a venipuncture?
opciones: Painful tingling, altered sensation and numbness
Pinpoint non-blanching spots smaller than 2 mm
Pooling of blood under the skin with swelling
Lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: The medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve is prone to injury during venipuncture, and accidental damage brings painful tingling, altered sensation and numbness; the phlebotomy chapter adds loss of sensation over the medial forearm. Pinpoint spots are petechiae, pooled blood under the skin is a hematoma, and lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness describe vasovagal syncope.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services
preguntas.subtema: Proof of delivery · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: The office needs proof that a letter of withdrawal from care reached the patient. What does First-Class Mail alone provide?
opciones: No delivery confirmation, unless a service such as Certified Mail is added
Delivery confirmation on every letter, included in the price of the stamp
A money-back guarantee if the letter arrives later than the date promised
Insurance up to one hundred dollars, included at no additional charge
preguntas.explicacion: First-Class Mail covers standard-sized single-piece envelopes up to 3.5 ounces and large envelopes up to 13 ounces. The comparison table shows no delivery confirmation for it, with the note that confirmation becomes available once a service such as Certified Mail is added. The money-back guarantee belongs to Priority Mail Express, and the hundred dollars of included insurance to Ground Advantage.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Introduction; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Engineering controls
preguntas.subtema: Double gloving · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What does wearing two pairs of gloves do for a worker who suffers a sharps injury?
opciones: It cuts the volume of blood transferred, without stopping the puncture
It stops the needle from reaching the skin when the gauge is small
It removes the need to wash hands once the outer pair comes off
It counts as an engineering control under the bloodborne standard
preguntas.explicacion: Double gloving may reduce the volume of blood that gets through during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin, so it is a way of lessening an exposure and not of preventing one. Hand hygiene after removing gloves is required either way, and controls that isolate or remove the hazard, such as safer needles and sharps containers, are what the standard calls engineering controls; gloves are personal protective equipment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of features defines a normal sinus rhythm?
opciones: Regular, with a P wave before every QRS and a rate of 60 to 100
Regular, with a P wave after every QRS and a rate of 60 to 100
Irregular, with a P wave before each QRS and a rate of 60 to 100
Regular, with no P waves at all and a rate of 60 to 100
preguntas.explicacion: The criteria are a regular rhythm with one P wave ahead of each QRS complex, a P wave that is upright in leads I and II and biphasic in V1, a P wave no taller than 2.5 mm in leads II and III, and a rate between 60 and 100 beats per minute.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lactose tolerance tests (003500), How to Prepare for the Test; StatPearls, "Lactose Intolerance", section Proper Performance of Hydrogen Breath Testing
preguntas.subtema: Lactose test preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for lactose tolerance testing asks how to get ready. What are the instructions?
opciones: No food and no heavy exercise for the 8 hours before the test
No food for 8 hours, but light meals are allowed up to the test
No food for 12 to 16 hours and no exercise for 24 hours before
No dairy for 3 days, then a normal breakfast on the morning of the test
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is not to eat and not to exercise heavily for eight hours before lactose tolerance testing. For the breath version the fast is at least eight hours for children and adults and at least four for infants, with no smoking for two hours before and during, and physical activity kept down for two hours to prevent hyperventilation. Dropping dairy for days beforehand is not part of the preparation.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, The ABO Blood Group; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D donation) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is blood type A. Which antigen is on the red cells and which antibody circulates in the plasma?
opciones: A antigen on the red cells; anti-B antibodies in the plasma
A antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
B antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
Neither antigen; both anti-A and anti-B in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: ABO typing looks at two glycoprotein antigens, A and B. Type A cells carry the A antigen, and because people are exposed to A and B antigens in food and microbes early in life, a type A person has naturally formed anti-B antibodies. Type B has the B antigen with anti-A, type AB has both antigens and neither antibody, and type O has no antigens but both antibodies.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument opens like a compass and reads a thickness, a diameter or the gap between two body surfaces?
opciones: A caliper for clinical use, which opens across the part measured
A nonpowered goniometer, which reads the range of motion of a joint
A uterine sound, which reads the depth of a cavity from the inside
A manual refractor, which reads the refractive error with its lenses
preguntas.explicacion: The clinical caliper is compass-like and reads a thickness, a diameter, or the distance between two surfaces of the body — the measurement taken, for example, to size a prosthesis. The goniometer reads joint motion, the sound reads the depth of a cavity, and the refractor reads the error of the eye.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 k49 · PBT II.D II.I · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient has a running peripheral IV in the left forearm. What does the WHO guidance say about drawing from it?
opciones: Do not draw from the existing access; IV fluid and hemolysis can alter results
Draw through the IV, because it spares the patient a second needle stick
Draw from the IV only if a nurse disconnects the fluids for the sample
Drawing from the IV is acceptable, though not ideal, at any time
preguntas.explicacion: In a hospitalized patient, an existing peripheral line is not used as the draw site: hemolysis, contamination, and the intravenous fluid and medication running through it can all falsify results. Nurses and physicians may sample central lines under protocol, with a contamination risk attached, and the case called acceptable but not ideal is drawing as the device is first inserted, before the fluids are connected.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Cost-sharing Reductions
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A Marketplace shopper with a low income asks how to get the extra discounts on what she will pay at the doctor. What does she need to choose?
opciones: A silver level plan, which is where those discounts sit
A premium tax credit, which lowers what she pays monthly
A grandfathered plan, bought before the law took effect
A high deductible plan paired with a savings account
preguntas.explicacion: Cost-sharing reductions are discounts on what the member pays for covered services in an individual Marketplace plan. They are available where income is below a certain level and the member picks a silver level plan, or where the member belongs to a federally recognized tribe. The premium tax credit is the separate help that lowers the monthly premium.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.7
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A code tells the coder to code any causal condition first, if one applies, and none is known here. What follows?
opciones: That code may itself be the first-listed diagnosis
That code may not be reported at all at this encounter
The symptom code takes the first-listed position instead
An unspecified code from the category is listed first
preguntas.explicacion: A note that asks for the causal condition first, if any applies, means the code it sits under may be assigned as the principal diagnosis, or listed first, where that cause is unknown or does not apply here. Where the cause is known, that condition is what goes first, in the same way as the etiology in a code first note.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fetal Heart Rate Tracing", Fetal Heart Rate Terminology
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.d · RMA III.F.4.b.i · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: How is the baseline fetal heart rate determined from a tracing?
opciones: The mean rate over 10 minutes, present at least 2 of them, rounded to 5 bpm
The mean rate over 2 minutes, present at least 10 seconds, rounded to 5 bpm
The lowest rate seen over 10 minutes, rounded down to the nearest 10 bpm
The highest rate seen over 10 minutes, rounded up to the nearest 10 bpm
preguntas.explicacion: The baseline is the average over a ten-minute window, and that average has to be present for at least two minutes of it, reported in steps of five beats per minute. Accelerations, decelerations, stretches of marked variability and segments differing by 25 beats or more are left out. A normal baseline runs from 110 to 160 beats per minute.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Limitations of Vital Sign Measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which two vital signs vary the most from one person measuring to the next in the same patient?
opciones: The respiratory rate and the blood pressure
The oral temperature and the oxygen saturation
The pulse rate and the oral temperature
The oxygen saturation and the pulse rate
preguntas.explicacion: Measurement depends on technique, equipment and the observer, and studies have found substantial variation between observers, above all for respiratory rate and blood pressure. That is the argument for standardized training and competency checks. Patient factors such as pain, anxiety, movement, tremor or poor perfusion add error on top of that.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling detail · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A telehealth appointment has been booked for a nine-year-old. What should the office confirm with the family in advance?
opciones: Who needs to be available, since the minor must be present and the parent may be too
That the child will hold the device alone, so the clinician can assess her unaided
That the parent will complete the visit while the child stays out of the room
That the school nurse will join the call to act as the telehealth facilitator
preguntas.explicacion: Among the topics to discuss with a patient before a first virtual visit, the guidance lists treating the appointment as one would an in-person visit, how the patient will connect, and who needs to be available: for a minor, it says to make clear that the minor needs to be present and whether the parent should or should not also be there. It also covers what to do if the appointment cannot be kept or the connection fails.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Cells, Tissues and Membranes: Membranes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which membrane lines the body cavities that open to the outside, such as the digestive and respiratory tracts?
opciones: Mucous membrane, an epithelium over loose connective tissue
Serous membrane, an epithelium over loose connective tissue
Synovial membrane, a connective tissue without an epithelium
Meningeal membrane, a connective tissue without an epithelium
preguntas.explicacion: Epithelial membranes come in two kinds. Mucous membranes, or mucosae, line the passages that open to the outside world: the whole digestive tract, and likewise the tracts of respiration, of excretion and of reproduction. Serous membranes line the cavities that do not open outward. Synovial membranes and meninges have no epithelium at all.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through a phlebotomist's gown to the scrubs underneath. When must the gown come off?
opciones: Immediately, or as soon as feasible
Once the procedure has been completed
At the end of the shift, with other coverings
After hands are washed and gloves changed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(vi) says that a garment penetrated by blood or OPIM is removed immediately or as soon as feasible. The standard defines appropriate PPE in (d)(3)(i) as equipment that does not let blood reach work clothes, street clothes, undergarments or skin under normal conditions of use, so a gown that has been soaked through has stopped being appropriate. End of shift is the timing given for surfaces and protective coverings in (d)(4)(ii), not for garments; handwashing follows removal, it does not precede it.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6)(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(6)(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks lost when asked, 'Have you eaten, taken your pills, or had any coffee since midnight?' How should the questioning be reworked?
opciones: Ask one thing at a time, in yes-or-no form, and re-explain who you are
Repeat the whole question more loudly and quickly to hold his attention
Switch to open-ended questions so that he can tell the story in his own words
Put every question to the caregiver, since he cannot answer reliably
preguntas.explicacion: With cognitive impairment: address the patient directly with simple wording, one idea at a time, using yes-or-no or multiple-choice questions; help orient the patient by explaining or re-explaining who you are and what you will do; and avoid speaking too quickly or loudly. Yes-or-no questions also help when the patient struggles with open ones.

Sharing the plan and handing out roles before the work starts
Re-establishing awareness partway through and adjusting the plan
Passing responsibility and accountability on to the next person
preguntas.explicacion: The debrief reviews the team's performance: a structured, intentional but informal and quick exchange meant to improve performance through lessons learned and by reinforcing what went well. Sharing the plan up front is the brief, re-establishing situational awareness in the middle is the huddle, and passing responsibility is a handoff.

preguntas.pregunta: An operative report is titled appendectomy. Which ending would have been used instead if the surgeon had only cut into the appendix?
opciones: -otomy, the ending that names an incision
-ostomy, the ending that names an opening
-plasty, the ending for a reconstruction
-pexy, the ending for a surgical fixation
preguntas.explicacion: The four surgical endings are close cousins and each names a different act: -ectomy cuts the part out, -otomy only cuts into it, -ostomy makes an opening, -plasty rebuilds and -pexy anchors a part in place. An appendectomy removes the appendix, so an incision alone would have carried -otomy.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern of freezing does cryosurgery aim for, and how is a benign lesion margin judged?
opciones: Rapid freezing then slow thawing, with the white halo reaching 1 to 2 mm past the border
Slow freezing then rapid thawing, with the white halo reaching 1 to 2 mm past the border
Rapid freezing then slow thawing, with the white halo reaching 10 mm past the border
Slow freezing then rapid thawing, with the white halo reaching exactly to the border
preguntas.explicacion: Ice crystals form between and then inside the cells, and thawing damages them again as water rushes back in, so the ideal is fast freezing followed by slow thawing. On a benign lesion the freeze runs until a white halo stands 1 to 2 mm past the border, usually five to ten seconds, and thawing is complete when the original color returns and no frost remains.

preguntas.pregunta: How should peel packs and trays be positioned when a steam sterilizer is loaded?
opciones: Peel packs on edge in mesh baskets and perforated trays laid parallel to the shelf
Peel packs stacked flat on the shelf and perforated trays stood upright against the wall
Peel packs on edge in solid-bottom pans and nonperforated basins laid flat and nested
Peel packs laid flat under the trays so the heavier metal holds them against the shelf
preguntas.explicacion: Everything is arranged so the sterilant circulates freely and reaches every surface. A perforated tray lies flat, in line with the shelf; a container without perforations, a basin for instance, is stood on edge; small items lie loosely in wire baskets; and peel packs are set on edge in perforated or mesh-bottom racks. Items packed tightly or nested shield one another from the steam.

preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which vessels are the main site of resistance and of blood pressure regulation, and how wide are they?
opciones: Arterioles, with lumens of about 30 μm or less
Capillaries, with lumens of only 5 to 10 μm
Venules, with lumens of from 8 to 100 μm
Elastic arteries, more than 10 mm in diameter
preguntas.explicacion: Arterioles, with lumens averaging 30 micrometers or less, are called resistance vessels because they slow blood flow and cause the sharpest drop in pressure; their constriction and dilation are the main way blood flow is distributed and pressure is regulated. Capillaries are narrower but far more numerous, and their total cross-sectional area is greater, so they are not the main site of resistance.

opciones: Hinged items opened, removable parts taken off, and concave surfaces set so water drains
Hinged items closed, removable parts left on, and concave surfaces set to hold the steam in
Hinged items opened, removable parts left on, and heavy items laid on top of the delicate ones
Hinged items closed, removable parts taken off, and the whole set held to a fixed weight limit
preguntas.explicacion: After cleaning, drying and inspection, items go into trays arranged so the sterilant reaches everything: hinges opened, removable parts disassembled unless the manufacturer says otherwise, concave surfaces positioned to let water drain, and heavy pieces placed where they will not crush delicate ones. There is no longer a set weight limit for surgical sets.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a non-preferred provider?
opciones: A provider with no contract with the plan, whom the patient pays more to see
A provider with a contract with the plan whose discount is smaller than usual
A provider the plan removed from its network after a quality review of the care
A provider the patient may see only when the primary care doctor refers her there
preguntas.explicacion: The non-preferred provider is simply one who has no contract with the insurer or plan, so the patient pays more for that care. A contracted provider whose discount is smaller is described in the glossary as a participating provider inside a tiered network. Removal after a quality review and referral requirements are separate matters; the definition turns on the contract alone.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult and child after onset of puberty, Considerations and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Compression depth and time · CPT D1 1L k38 · CMA I.B.9.c / 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: How deep are adult chest compressions, and how soon can permanent brain damage begin once blood flow stops?
opciones: About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin in as little as 4 minutes
About 1 inch (2.5 cm); damage can begin after 10 minutes
About 3 inches (7.5 cm); damage can begin after 2 minutes
About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin only after 15 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions press the adult chest down about 2 inches, 5 centimeters, hard and fast without pausing, and the chest is allowed to rise all the way between them. Time is why CPR cannot wait: four minutes without blood flow is enough for permanent brain damage, or for death, and death may follow 4 to 6 minutes after that, so compressions continue until heartbeat and breathing return or trained help takes over. Where the person is breathing normally, coughing or moving, compressions are not started.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k75 · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which needle is commonly used for sewing skin, and how is most skin closure curved?
opciones: A reverse cutting needle, with the curve usually three-eighths of a circle
A conventional cutting needle, with the curve usually one-half of a circle
A blunt taper needle, with the curve usually one-quarter of a circle
A sharp taper needle, with the curve usually one-third of a circle
preguntas.explicacion: Cutting needles carry three sharp edges. The conventional kind has the cutting surface on the inside of the curve, the reverse cutting kind on the outside, and it is the reverse cutting needle that is commonly used to sew skin. Most skin closure needles are curved, and the usual curve is three-eighths of a circle, which lets the surgeon keep track of where the tip is.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: How deep should each chest compression go on an adult?
opciones: About 2 inches (5 cm), without using excessive force, with full recoil
About 1½ inches (4 cm), the depth used on the chest of an infant
About 3 inches (7.5 cm), going deeper when the patient is obese
About 1 inch (2.5 cm), just enough to move the sternum downward
preguntas.explicacion: The adult target is roughly 2 inches, or 5 centimeters, pressing hard but avoiding excessive force, and letting the chest recoil completely each time. An inch and a half (4 cm) is the infant figure, not the adult one. Rib fractures occur in up to 70 % of resuscitations, which is a known cost of compressions and not a reason to press less.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, remission
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told the disease is in complete remission. What does that phrase mean?
opciones: Every sign and symptom has gone, though cancer may still be present
Every sign and symptom has gone, so the cancer is considered cured
Some of the signs and symptoms have gone and the others have not
The signs have gone but the tests still show the disease clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Remission means the signs and symptoms of a cancer have lessened or gone. Partial remission is when some of them have gone; complete remission is when all of them have, although cancer may still be in the body. That last clause is why complete remission and cure are not the same word.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Lithotomy Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(4) · RMA III.F.2.a.i · NCMA 2B.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being placed in lithotomy for a gynecologic procedure. How are the legs handled?
opciones: Abducted 30 to 45 degrees from the midline, knees flexed, raised and lowered together
Abducted 60 to 75 degrees from the midline, knees extended, raised one after the other
Abducted 30 to 45 degrees from the midline, knees extended, raised one at a time
Abducted 15 to 20 degrees from the midline, knees flexed, lowered before the drape
preguntas.explicacion: The legs go out about 30 to 45 degrees from midline with the knees bent and the foot of the bed lowered or removed. Both legs move at the same time, up and down together, because moving one alone twists the spine and strains muscle. Padding under the legs keeps the supports from compressing nerves where they rest.

preguntas.pregunta: The provider is about to examine the abdomen of a patient with cramping. In what order are the four methods used?
opciones: Look, then listen, then percuss, then palpate
Look, then palpate, then percuss, then listen
Listen first, then look, palpate and percuss
Look, then percuss, then palpate, then listen
preguntas.explicacion: The abdomen breaks the usual pattern. Listening comes second, before any hand presses on the wall, because pressing can stir up or quiet the bowel and change what is heard. Everywhere else the order memorized is look, feel, percuss, listen. Getting the two mixed up is the classic error.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: Whole blood for a PCR assay cannot be extracted until next week. Which storage plan follows the recommendations?
opciones: Separate the plasma or serum from the red cells and store it at −20 °C or colder
Freeze the whole blood tube at −20 °C or colder until the extraction can be done
Keep the whole blood tube at 2 to 8 °C, where it stays stable indefinitely for DNA
Keep the whole blood tube at room temperature, since cold storage lyses the white cells
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood is not stored below 0 °C: when a frozen sample thaws, heme is released, and heme inhibits the polymerase and quenches the fluorophores used to detect the product. If extraction cannot happen within an acceptable time the erythrocytes are removed and the plasma or serum is frozen at −20 °C or colder. There is no absolute limit for whole blood at room temperature or 2 to 8 °C, but prolonged storage there raises the risk of hemolysis and of nucleic acid degradation from white cell lysis.

preguntas.pregunta: A gray top tube for glucose is drawn short and the laboratory reports the sample as hemolyzed. What does the WHO table say about this tube?
opciones: It requires a full draw, because a short draw may cause hemolysis
It requires a half draw, because its additive is concentrated for small volumes
It needs no fill requirement, since fluoride keeps glucose stable for five days
It should be filled last only when a hemolyzed sample is expected
preguntas.explicacion: In the uses column for the oxalate/fluoride tube, Table 2.3 states that glucose specimens require a full draw and that a short draw may cause hemolysis. The five-day glucose stability is a separate property of the antiglycolytic agent and does not remove the fill requirement. The gray tube is drawn last (position 10) in every case, not only when hemolysis is suspected.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(6) (2027 I.C.6.g(6)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports heartburn and regurgitation after meals. Which structure normally prevents that, and what is the diagnosis?
opciones: The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is peptic ulcer disease
The pyloric sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The upper esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: The usual complaints in gastroesophageal reflux disease are heartburn, regurgitation, and chest pain that is not cardiac; with symptoms as typical as those the diagnosis can be made presumptively. What normally holds the contents down is the lower esophageal sphincter, a physiological sphincter three to five centimeters long whose high resting tone keeps stomach contents out of the esophagus.

preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on plasma. Which tubes will supply it?
opciones: The heparin tubes, the EDTA tube and the citrate tube
The clot activator tube and the serum separator tube alone
The clot activator tube, the citrate tube and the EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma comes from tubes whose additive stops the blood from clotting: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA in the purple tube and citrate in the light blue tube, which is why coagulation testing uses plasma. The red clot activator tube and the gold separator tube are the ones that yield serum.

preguntas.pregunta: A bilingual receptionist offers to interpret the pre-draw questions. Why are staff untrained as healthcare interpreters ruled out?
opciones: Research shows untrained people make more clinically significant mistakes
Their interpreting time cannot be reimbursed by any state Medicaid program
They cannot be listed in the practice directory of bilingual clinicians
They are barred from signing the practice's interpreter ethics statement
preguntas.explicacion: The unacceptable services include a clinician or a staff member whose command of both languages falls short, and anyone not trained or certified as a healthcare interpreter, because research shows that people untrained in interpreting make more clinically significant mistakes. preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 9.5 Types of Body Movements, Dorsiflexion and Plantar Flexion
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A therapist asks the patient to lift the top of the foot toward the leg. Which movement is that, and at which joint?
opciones: Dorsiflexion, at the ankle joint
Plantar flexion, at the ankle joint
Inversion, at the intertarsal joints
Eversion, at the intertarsal joints
preguntas.explicacion: Lifting the front of the foot so the top comes toward the leg is dorsiflexion; lifting the heel and pointing the toes is plantar flexion. Those two are the only movements the ankle joint allows. Turning the sole toward the midline is inversion and away from it is eversion, and both happen between the tarsal bones instead.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a written termination notice sent, and what does the practice keep afterwards?
opciones: By certified mail, return receipt requested, keeping the receipt and a copy in the chart
By First-Class Mail, keeping a note of the date the envelope went to the post office
By a portal message, which is now the preferred way of sending these notices
By telephone, with the caller writing the date care ends into the progress note
preguntas.explicacion: Termination notices always go out in writing, and many states demand certified mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the latest address the file holds; the receipt and a copy of the letter then live in the medical record. preguntas.pregunta: How much medication may be given in a single intramuscular injection?
opciones: 0.5 to 1 mL in infants and children, and 2 to 5 mL in adults
Up to 1 mL in adults, and up to 0.5 mL in infants and children
0.1 mL at any age, the same volume used for a tuberculin test
Up to 3 mL at any age, at any of the recommended muscle sites
preguntas.explicacion: The volume for an intramuscular injection is 0.5 to 1 mL in infants and children and 2 to 5 mL in adults. Within that range the site still matters: the maximum for one injection at the vastus lateralis in an adult is 3 mL, and the deltoid generally takes about 1 mL. preguntas.pregunta: How long is a CLIA certificate valid, and how many certificate types does the CLIA program have?

Two years, and the program has three certificate types in all
One year, and the program has five certificate types in all
Three years, and the program has four certificate types in all
preguntas.explicacion: Every certificate type runs for two years, and there are five of them: waiver, provider-performed microscopy, registration, compliance and accreditation. Signal word, pictograms, hazard statements and the classification
Permissible exposure limits, ventilation advice and glove material

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(7) (2027 I.C.6.g(7)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A woman reports urinary frequency, urgency, burning on urination and suprapubic discomfort. Which organism most often causes this?
opciones: Escherichia coli, responsible for the majority of these infections
Klebsiella species, responsible for the majority of these infections
Staphylococcus aureus, responsible for the majority of these infections
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, responsible for the majority of these infections
preguntas.explicacion: Dysuria, urgency, frequency and discomfort above the pubic bone are the typical symptoms of an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, and Escherichia coli causes most of them, with Klebsiella next and Proteus, Enterobacter and Enterococcus behind.
