preguntas.pregunta: Absent a degree or a military laboratory course, what is the least education CLIA accepts for someone performing moderate complexity testing?
opciones: A high school diploma or equivalent, plus documented laboratory training for the testing performed
A high school diploma or equivalent, plus one year of documented experience in blood gas analysis
An associate degree from an accredited school in a medical laboratory, chemical or biological science
A high school diploma or equivalent, plus the state license, in states where a license is required
preguntas.explicacion: The lowest rung of the moderate complexity ladder is a high school diploma, or its equivalent, plus documented training in the laboratory suited to the testing to be done, obtained before the person touches a patient specimen. A state license is required on top of the qualification wherever the state demands one, so it is never the whole answer; the associate degree is a different, higher rung of the same list.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, 2026 Ambulatory Health Care National Patient Safety Goals, NPSG.03.06.01
preguntas.subtema: Medicine information at check-out · CCMA 4 · CMA I.A.1 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5H · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is leaving at the end of her visit. What does the 2026 ambulatory safety goal on medicines expect her to be given and told?
opciones: Written information on what she is to take, and to bring an up-to-date list to every visit
Written information on what she is to take, and to bring the bottles themselves each visit
A printed note of the changes made today, and to ring the office before her next refill
Written information on what she is to take, and to leave the list on file at her pharmacy
preguntas.explicacion: The goal on using medicines safely asks that a patient's medicines be found out and compared with anything new she is given, that correct information about them be recorded and passed on, that she leave with something written about what she needs to take, and that she be told it matters to carry a current list to every appointment with a doctor.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification (EJIFCC 2003), Table 1 (Glucose); Table 3 (neonatal); StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Glucose critical limits · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.d
preguntas.pregunta: In a published table of critical limits for urgent clinician notification, which adult glucose values require the physician to be notified immediately?
opciones: Below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L) or above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L)
Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or above 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L)
Below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) or above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L)
Below 25 mg/dL (1.3 mmol/L) or above 600 mg/dL (33.3 mmol/L)
preguntas.explicacion: The table of adult and pediatric critical limits sets glucose at below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L), where neuroglycopenic symptoms up to loss of consciousness occur, and above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L), the range of diabetic coma with osmotic diuresis and ketoacidosis; the limits apply after confirmation by repeat measurement in the same sample. The other pairs mix thresholds from elsewhere: 70 and 54 mg/dL mark hypoglycemia levels, 25 mg/dL is the neonatal limit, and 600 mg/dL characterizes the hyperosmolar state.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia (patient instructions): Latex allergies - for hospital patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: The WHO pre-draw interview asks specifically about allergies to which three items?
opciones: Latex, povidone iodine and tape
Latex, alcohol and chlorhexidine
Bananas, avocado and kiwi
Vinyl, silicone and neoprene
preguntas.explicacion: The Annex C interview asks whether the patient is allergic to anything, and it names three items to raise explicitly: latex, povidone iodine and tape. Bananas, avocado and kiwi are the fruits of the latex-fruit syndrome, a reason to probe further rather than the question itself, and vinyl, silicone and neoprene are the latex alternatives used once an allergy is known.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, Symptoms and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Shock position · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a / 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who cut himself badly is pale and clammy. Besides controlling the bleeding, what position does first aid recommend?
opciones: Lay him flat, raise the feet about 12 inches, and cover him with a blanket
Sit him upright with the head between the knees to improve breathing
Lay him on his side in the recovery position with the legs straight
Stand him up and walk him slowly to keep blood circulating
preguntas.explicacion: Pallor, clammy skin, a fast pulse, dizziness and confusion are the signs of shock from blood loss. For severe bleeding the guidance is to call for help, keep the injured part still, get the person lying flat with the feet propped about 12 inches, 30 centimeters, off the ground, and cover them with a coat or a blanket, avoiding movement where an injury to head, neck, back or leg is possible. Lying down also makes fainting less likely, since blood reaches the brain more easily. The recovery position is for someone breathing after CPR, not for shock.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Care Transfer Techniques", Clinical Significance: Slide Board Transfers
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2A.5 · RMA III.H.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is a sliding transfer board intended for?
opciones: One with paraplegia, who has upper-body strength but poor balance in the legs
One with quadriplegia, who lacks postural support and upper extremity strength
One who already transfers by standing and pivoting from the bed to the chair
One who cannot follow commands and must be guided through each step verbally
preguntas.explicacion: The board bridges the gap between two surfaces for someone whose arms work but whose legs will not hold them: paraplegia, lower-limb amputation, poor balance or leg strength. It does not suit a patient with quadriplegia, who lacks the trunk control and arm strength to use it, nor someone who already stands and pivots, nor a patient who cannot follow commands.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cholesterol Screening", section Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: In which situation is a non-fasting lipid profile acceptable?
opciones: Initial risk estimation in an untreated primary-prevention patient
Establishing the diagnosis of hypertriglyceridemia in a patient
Following a patient whose family has a history of genetic hyperlipidemia
Assessing a patient who is at risk for pancreatitis or has it
preguntas.explicacion: Two situations sit on the non-fasting side: estimating risk for the first time in an untreated primary-prevention patient, and clarifying a diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. The other three options belong to the list where fasting is preferred or mandatory, along with judging residual risk in a treated patient. The clinical question decides whether the patient fasts.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)(A)-(B); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex E
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D1 1G k30 · D3 k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep the tube holder and pulls the used needle off it with a gloved hand. Which rule does this break?
opciones: Under OSHA, contaminated needles are removed only by a mechanical device or one-handed technique, when no alternative is feasible
Under OSHA, contaminated needles may be removed by hand as long as clean gloves are worn and the tube holder is disinfected afterwards
The WHO allows removal by hand provided the needle is dropped into a sharps container that is within arm's reach
Removal by hand is permitted when the holder is reused on the same patient within two minutes
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) forbids bending a contaminated needle, recapping it or taking it off unless the employer can show no alternative is feasible or a specific medical procedure requires it, and then only with a mechanical device, or one-handed; shearing a needle or breaking it is prohibited outright. WHO Annex E says an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and Chapter 3 prefers discarding barrel and needle together.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with heart failure breathes in cycles that build up, fade away and then pause before starting again. Which pattern is charted?
opciones: Cheyne-Stokes respiration, a crescendo and decrescendo cycle with apneic gaps
Kussmaul respiration, deep and rapid breaths that keep an even depth throughout
Hyperventilation, rapid deep breathing that carries the carbon dioxide too low
Obstructive sleep apnea, in which snoring and shallow breaths alternate in sleep
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing that swells, fades and then stops for a moment before the next cycle is Cheyne-Stokes respiration. It is seen in heart failure and with raised intracranial pressure, and it carries a poor prognosis. The pattern is described in the chart along with the rate, because the rate alone would miss it.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: After a needle has been re-sheathed with the scoop technique on a work surface, what is the next step?
opciones: Disinfect the surface, so no blood is left behind on it
Rinse the surface with water and dry it with a paper towel
Cover the surface with fresh paper until the session ends
Leave the surface as it is until the end of the working shift
preguntas.explicacion: The maneuver is done beside a sharps container, and the needle goes into it straight afterwards. Because the cap was resting on the surface, that surface is then cleaned with disinfectant so that no blood is left on it. An exposed used needle is never taken apart by hand.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.d · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the technique call for repeating height, length and head circumference twice?
opciones: So two readings agree within 0.2 cm, and the average of the closest two is recorded
So the second reading can replace the first, which is treated as a practice attempt
So the larger of the two readings is charted, since the smaller one loses posture
So each reading can be taken by a different person and compared for agreement
preguntas.explicacion: Each of these measurements is taken twice and the two have to fall within 0.2 cm or 0.25 inches of one another; the average of the two closest values is what goes in the record. Head and waist circumferences vary more than height and weight and are the ones most prone to measurement error.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: What does the light green PST contain, and what kind of sample does it provide?
opciones: Lithium heparin plus a gel separator; plasma for chemistries
Sodium heparin without gel; plasma for lithium and ammonia levels
A clot activator plus a gel separator; serum for chemistries
Potassium oxalate plus sodium fluoride; plasma for glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 describes the PST as a light green tube holding lithium heparin as anticoagulant plus a gel separator, whose gel separates the plasma at the bottom of the tube; its use is chemistries. The dark green tube holds sodium or lithium heparin without gel, the serum separator tube has gel but no anticoagulant and gives serum, and oxalate with fluoride is the gray glucose tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: How does a monofilament suture behave compared with a braided multifilament one?
opciones: It has more memory and needs more knots, but passes through tissue with less reaction
It has less memory and needs fewer knots, but passes through tissue with more reaction
It has more memory and needs more knots, and it fractures far more readily under tension
It has less memory and holds knots better, and it carries more surface area for bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: A monofilament is a single strand with less surface area. It carries more memory, meaning it springs back toward its packaged shape and its knots loosen more easily, so it usually needs extra throws; but it slides through tissue more easily, causes less inflammatory reaction and fractures less than a braid. Multifilaments handle better and hold knots, at the cost of friction, capillarity and infection risk.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Affordable Care Act (ACA)
preguntas.subtema: Insurance fundamentals · CCMA 5 k181, k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which goal belongs to the Affordable Care Act as its own text describes it?
opciones: Expanding Medicaid to adults with income below 138% of the poverty level
Expanding Medicare to adults with income below 138% of the poverty level
Replacing employer coverage with a single federal plan for every worker
Setting a national fee schedule that every private insurer has to follow
preguntas.explicacion: The law enacted in March 2010 has three stated goals: make coverage affordable for more people through subsidies for households between 100% and 400% of the poverty level, expand Medicaid to adults with income below 138% of that level, and support delivery methods that lower costs. Not every state took the expansion. Medicare eligibility rests on age and disability, and the law created no single federal plan or universal fee schedule.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Supine Position Variations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b · RMA III.F.2.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: During severe hypotension the head of the bed is tilted below the level of the feet. Which position is that?
opciones: Trendelenburg, which drives venous blood back toward heart and head
Reverse Trendelenburg, which leaves the head as the highest point of the trunk
High Fowler, with the head of the bed raised to between 60 and 90 degrees
Lateral decubitus, with the patient turned onto the side that is not operated
preguntas.explicacion: Trendelenburg is a supine variant with the bed tipped head down so that the pubic symphysis becomes the highest point of the trunk. It is used to increase venous return in emergencies and to improve exposure in abdominal and laparoscopic surgery. Its costs are real: raised intracranial and intraocular pressure, and facial and airway swelling if held too long.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Detect Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Verifying identity · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Staff verify a returning patient online by asking for her date of birth and her mother's maiden name. What does the FTC say about that choice?
opciones: Those details make poor authenticators, since they are so easily obtained
Those details are the two identifiers the safety goal asks for before a procedure
Those details satisfy the rule, because they were collected on the intake form
Those details may be used once the patient has signed the privacy acknowledgment
preguntas.explicacion: For accounts that already exist, the program may take in reasonable steps for confirming who it is dealing with, watching transactions and checking that a change of address is genuine; for authenticating online the guidance points to multi-factor techniques built on PINs, passwords, tokens, smart cards and biometrics. What it rules out as reliable authenticators is exactly the easy stuff: a mailing address, a date of birth, a mother's maiden name, a Social Security number.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Facial Laceration Repair", Special Considerations for Suture Choice
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m
preguntas.pregunta: Staples were placed in a patient's scalp laceration. About when are they removed, and why not later?
opciones: About one week, because leaving them longer marks the skin with punctate train-track scars
About three weeks, because scalp wounds carry more tension than any other site on the body
About three days, because the scalp is so vascular that it has already closed by then
About one week, because after that the staple metal begins to corrode against the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Staples suit linear lacerations of the scalp and extremities and go in fast, which helps with brisk bleeding or several wounds at once. On the scalp they come out at roughly a week, since leaving them longer produces the characteristic punctate train-track marks along the line. They approximate edges less precisely than sutures but evert them well.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Prior authorization · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.1.d · RMA II.B.2.c · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: Before booking an imaging study, staff contact the insurer for its decision on medical necessity. What limits does that decision carry?
opciones: It is not a promise that the plan will pay the cost of the service
It removes the need for a referral from the patient's primary care doctor
It fixes the amount the patient will owe once the study has been performed
It obliges the imaging center to accept the amount the plan decides to pay
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the insurer's decision that a service, a treatment plan, a prescription drug or a piece of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary. A plan may demand it before certain services, emergencies aside; other names for the same thing are precertification, prior approval and prior authorization. The glossary states plainly that having it is no promise that the plan will pay.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dialysis Fistula", sections Clinical Significance and Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 3F k62 · D2 k49 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's arm carries a fistula with a palpable vibration under the fingertips. What does that vibration mean, and what is avoided on that arm?
opciones: A thrill, meaning the fistula is patent; draws, venous access and cuff readings are avoided
A thrill, meaning the fistula has clotted; draws and cuff readings may go ahead as usual
A pulsation, meaning the fistula is patent; only intravenous fluids are avoided on that arm
A pulsation, meaning steal syndrome has begun; the arm is used only for capillary sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the fingertips lightly over a fistula picks up a thrill, a vibration that means the fistula is open, and a thrill is distinguished from a merely pulsating fistula. To protect veins for dialysis, peripheral access, blood draws and blood pressure readings are kept off that side.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Microhematocrit centrifugation · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: For a spun microhematocrit, at what speed and for how long is the sealed capillary tube centrifuged?
opciones: 11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes
Roughly 3,000 rpm for 25 to 30 minutes
11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 10 to 15 minutes
1,500 to 2,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The microhematocrit method fills a capillary tube some 75 mm long and 1 mm across, seals both ends with clay or heat, and spins it at 11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes before it is read against the holder scale or a card reader. The 3,000 rpm, 30-minute spin belongs to the older macrohematocrit method with a Wintrobe tube, which the capillary method has largely displaced.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does the viscosity of blood compare with that of water, and what does that viscosity affect?
opciones: Roughly five times that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly twice that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly five times that of water; it lowers resistance to flow
Roughly the same as water, since plasma is 92 percent water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is viscous and sticky, with a viscosity about five times that of water, owing to the plasma proteins and the formed elements. Viscosity is resistance to flow, and it has a dramatic effect on blood pressure and flow: honey resists flow more than water, and blood behaves the same way relative to water. Plasma being mostly water does not make whole blood flow like water.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR), Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · PBT II.G · RMA III.C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a PT/INR asks whether to take the morning warfarin dose first. What is the usual instruction for preparing for this test?
opciones: The daily warfarin dose may need to be delayed until after the blood is drawn
The patient must fast for eight hours, as for a basic metabolic panel
No preparation of any kind is needed, exactly as for a PTT test
Warfarin must be stopped for 24 hours, just as alcohol is before a fasting draw
preguntas.explicacion: They may need to hold the daily dose until after the PT/INR is collected, following the provider's instructions. The eight-hour fast belongs to the basic metabolic panel, 'no special preparation' is the rule for the PTT, and the 24 hours without alcohol is general fasting advice, not a warfarin rule.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture (003751), Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Antibiotics before sputum culture · CPT D2 k48 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to give a sputum culture mentions he is on an antibiotic. What is the correct response?
opciones: Record it and tell the provider, since antibiotics can affect bacterial growth in the culture
Tell him to skip today's dose, since antibiotics can affect the bacterial growth in the culture
Ignore it, since antibiotics reach the bloodstream and not the airway secretions
Postpone the collection for 4 weeks, the interval used before a urea breath test
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics can suppress the growth the culture depends on, so the medication is documented and reported; the patient is told not to stop anything unless the provider says so. That is the same rule as in urine culture, where recent antibiotics can produce a false negative. The four-week hold belongs to the urea breath test for Helicobacter pylori.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Atrioventricular (AV) Node
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the cardiac impulse pause for about 100 milliseconds at the AV node?
opciones: So the atria complete their contraction before the ventricles begin
So the ventricles finish contracting before the atria start to refill
So the SA node can reset itself before the next sinus rhythm begins
So the Purkinje fibers reach the apex ahead of the two bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The AV node's small cells and less efficient junctions slow the impulse, so it takes about 100 ms to cross the node, and this pause is critical: it lets the atrial muscle finish contracting and pumping blood into the ventricles before the ventricles themselves are stimulated. The cardiac skeleton blocks any other route from atria to ventricles, so the AV node is the only gateway.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: Before opening an instrument tray for a procedure, what is checked on the outside of the container?
opciones: The plastic lock and its indicator change, the Julian date and load number, and any moisture
The plastic lock and its indicator change, the expiration date, and the weight of the set
The name of the operator, the load number, and the temperature printout from the cycle
The filter color, the Julian date, and the biological indicator sealed inside the container
preguntas.explicacion: Three things get checked on the outside: that the plastic lock has changed color, that the label carries the load number with its Julian date, and that this is the right set. The container is then looked over for moisture or condensation, and if there is any, that set is put aside and another retrieved. The internal indicator is found later, after gowning and gloving.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k9 k51 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: How does underfilling a tube contribute to hemolysis?
opciones: The ratio of anticoagulant to blood ends up greater than one to nine
The ratio of anticoagulant to blood ends up smaller than one to nine
The vacuum left in the tube pulls the red cells against the stopper
The additive settles at the bottom and never reaches the red cells
preguntas.explicacion: Among the recognized causes of hemolysis is underfilling a tube so that the proportion of anticoagulant to blood rises above one to nine. It is the same arithmetic that lengthens clotting times in a short-drawn citrate tube, where the plasma is outnumbered by the anticoagulant.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Testing Procedures and Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: OGTT preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D II.B pre-collection instructions · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has followed a strict low-carbohydrate diet for a week before an OGTT. Why is that a problem?
opciones: The test requires 3 days of unrestricted diet with at least 150 g of carbohydrate a day
The test requires 3 days of fasting so that glycogen stores are emptied first
The test requires a low-carbohydrate diet only on the day before, not for a week
The test requires the same diet the patient will follow after diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: For at least three days before the OGTT the patient must eat an unrestricted diet containing 150 g or more of carbohydrate per day, keep normal activity and avoid unusual or vigorous exercise; a week of carbohydrate restriction invalidates the conditions of the test. The only fast is the 10- to 16-hour one immediately before the morning of the test. MedlinePlus puts it simply: eat normally for several days beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section What is fasting for a blood test; and MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Cortisol Test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which activity should patients avoid while fasting for a blood test?
opciones: Chewing gum during the fasting hours
Drinking plain water during the fasting hours
Taking a medicine the provider said to continue
Brushing teeth within 30 minutes of the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Besides not eating or drinking anything but plain water, there are three things not to do while fasting: chew gum, smoke, or exercise. Plain water is allowed, and usual medicines are continued unless the provider says to stop. The 30-minute rule about brushing and flossing belongs to the cortisol saliva test, not to a blood draw.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion; PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introductory text
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A blood sample for potassium and glucose was drawn from the arm carrying a dextrose infusion, through the IV catheter as it was placed. Which two problems does the literature attach to this practice?
opciones: Higher hemolysis from flow through the narrow catheter, and contamination by the infusion fluid
Formation of fibrin clots in the serum, and dilution of the anticoagulant in the tube
Falsely low potassium from the catheter material, and bacterial contamination of the tube
Air bubbles that lower the blood gas values, and loss of vacuum in the evacuated tube
preguntas.explicacion: Blood taken from an indwelling catheter, or while an IV is being started, hemolyses more often than a straight venipuncture, which the study puts down to flow through the narrow tubing; samples contaminated by an intravenous infusion made up 2.2 % of that laboratory's rejections. The critical-limits paper adds the classic case: a glucose drawn through a line running glucose gives a falsely critical figure that a properly collected sample clears up.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", Home Care; and MedlinePlus, Convulsions - first aid - series (100212)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room falls to the floor with jerking of all four limbs. What should the assistant do first?
opciones: Clear the area of furniture and sharp objects and cushion the head
Hold the arms and legs still so that the patient does not get hurt
Slide a padded tongue blade between the teeth to protect the tongue
Lift the patient onto the exam table where the jerking can be watched
preguntas.explicacion: The whole goal during a convulsion is to keep the patient from being injured: furniture and sharp objects are moved away, the head is cushioned, and tight clothing is loosened, especially at the neck. The patient is not held down, nothing is put between the teeth, and the patient is not moved unless the spot itself is dangerous.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Quality Assessment (internal and external)
preguntas.subtema: Internal vs external quality assessment · PBT VI.A quality assurance · CCMA 3D k115 · RMA III.C.1.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Which activities count as INTERNAL quality assessment at a waived testing site?
opciones: Reviewing QC records, test results and temperature logs, and documenting problems with a plan to fix them
Subscribing to a PT program and exchanging samples with another site using the same method
Undergoing a voluntary inspection by peers or consultants who evaluate practices and records
Receiving the manufacturer's technical bulletin and posting it in the testing area
preguntas.explicacion: Internal assessment is done by the staff who perform and oversee testing: performing and documenting QC, reviewing QC records and results, checking room and refrigerator temperature logs for completeness, and documenting and reviewing problems and injury or incident reports with an improvement plan. External assessment brings in an outside party: voluntary inspections, PT subscriptions and sample exchanges.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k148 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the room kept at a comfortable temperature for a recording?
opciones: Shivering alters the tracing, so the patient must be warm
Cold skin holds less gel, so the electrodes come loose
Cold raises the heart rate, so the rate reads too high
Cold slows the paper, so the squares stand for less time
preguntas.explicacion: Any movement changes what is recorded, and shivering counts as movement, so being relaxed and warm is part of the preparation. Keeping the room temperature right is listed alongside removing metal objects and identifying the electrode sites before the patient lies down.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.4: Administering Intradermal Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(7) · RMA III.G.2.a(iii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: An intradermal injection is about to be given. How is the needle held and inserted?
opciones: Bevel up, almost flat on the skin, entering at an angle of 5 to 15 degrees
Bevel up, held like a dart, entering at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees
Bevel down, almost flat on the skin, entering at 5 to 15 degrees
Bevel down, held like a dart, entering straight in at 90 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe is held between thumb and forefinger with the bevel up and the needle almost flat against the skin, entering at 5 to 15 degrees, and it advances no more than an eighth of an inch, just far enough to cover the bevel. Bevel up lets the needle pierce smoothly and puts the medication into the dermis. The dart grip and the 45 to 90 degree range belong to subcutaneous and intramuscular injections.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Contact Transmission and Vehicle Transmission; and StatPearls, "Universal Precautions" (NBK470223)
preguntas.subtema: Droplet vs airborne · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What distance separates direct droplet transmission from airborne transmission in the microbiology definition?
opciones: About one meter: droplets travel a meter or less; airborne goes farther
About three meters: droplets travel three meters or less
About six feet: droplets travel six feet or less; airborne travels farther
There is no distance; the difference is whether a mask was worn
preguntas.explicacion: When a person coughs or sneezes, droplets of mucus that may carry pathogens are ejected; direct droplet transmission covers distances of one meter or less and is treated as a form of contact transmission, while transmission over more than one meter is called airborne and is classed as vehicle transmission through the air. Fine droplets can stay suspended, travel far, and dry into droplet nuclei; tuberculosis is the classic airborne example, needing as few as 10 organisms to infect. The 3 to 6 feet figure is the clinical rule of thumb for Droplet Precautions, a different framework.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024)
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen temperature · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a federal drug test reads 27°C three minutes after the void. What does the collector do?
opciones: Collect a second specimen under direct observation and send both for testing
Warm the container in the hand and read the temperature again in four minutes
Discard the specimen and start over with the ordinary collection procedure
Accept it and write the reading on the remarks line of the custody form
preguntas.explicacion: A reading outside 32° to 38°C is marked out of range on the form, and the collector then takes a second specimen under direct observation, sending both of them to a laboratory certified by HHS rather than to an instrumented initial test facility. A comment goes on the remarks line too, but the comment alone does not make the specimen acceptable, and rewarming it is not an option.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(3)(iii)(A) and (B), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Baseline sample and consent · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist stuck by a used needle agrees to have her blood drawn but refuses HIV testing that day. What does the standard require of the sample?
opciones: Keep it at least 90 days so the employee may still choose to have it tested for HIV
Test it for HIV anyway, since consent to the blood draw covers the serologic testing
Discard it, since HIV testing requires a fresh sample drawn after consent is given
Keep it 30 days, the period in which the written opinion has to be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(iii)(B) separates the two consents. If the employee agrees to baseline collection but not, at that moment, to HIV serology, the sample is preserved for at least 90 days; should she decide within those 90 days to have it tested, the test is run as soon as feasible. Testing without her consent is not allowed, and throwing the sample away would defeat the purpose of the rule. The written opinion has its own deadline, 15 days, and is unrelated to the storage period.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Acetaminophen (a681004); and MedlinePlus, Amoxicillin (a685001); FDA, Dosage Forms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k18 · CCMA 3B k86 · RMA III.G.4.e · NCMA 1.6
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient cannot swallow a tablet. Which alternative oral forms of the same drug might be available?
opciones: A suspension or solution, a chewable tablet, or a tablet that dissolves in the mouth
A suppository, a transdermal patch, or an aerosol delivered through a spacer device
An extended-release tablet, a filter needle preparation, or a multi-dose vial product
A sublingual tablet only, since no other form suits a patient who cannot swallow
preguntas.explicacion: One drug often arrives in several forms for the same route: acetaminophen alone is sold as a tablet, a chewable tablet, a capsule, a suspension or solution, an extended-release tablet and an orally disintegrating tablet. For amoxicillin the forms are the capsule, the tablet, the chewable tablet and the suspension. The FDA's list of accepted dosage form terms runs from aerosol and elixir through lotion, ointment, patch and suppository.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Epidemiology: Impact of Safety Devices on Needle Stick Injuries
preguntas.subtema: A device is not a program · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital brings in safety-engineered devices and its injury rate does not fall. Which two problems have been reported in that situation?
opciones: Trouble working the safety mechanism, and needles still discarded improperly
Shortage of sharps containers, and gloves supplied in only one size
Poor lighting at the bedside, and tubes filled in the wrong order
Late reporting of injuries, and no written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices are in wide use, yet the drop in injuries has not always followed. One study saw the rate move from 1.9 to 2.2 injuries for every 100 workers once the devices were in place, and two explanations came up most often: staff had trouble operating the safety mechanism, and needles went on being discarded improperly. Both are matters of training and work practice, which is why buying a device is only one piece of a prevention program.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): can I also perform waived tests / PPM procedures?
preguntas.subtema: Certificate for the highest category · PBT VI.F · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory holds a Certificate of Accreditation. May it also perform waived tests and PPM procedures?
opciones: Yes; a COA or COC covers waived tests and PPM procedures as well
Yes for waived tests, but PPM requires a separate PPM certificate
No; each complexity category needs its own CLIA certificate
Only after notifying the FDA of each waived test added to the menu
preguntas.explicacion: A Certificate of Compliance or of Accreditation is issued for nonwaived testing and also permits waived tests and PPM procedures. A PPM certificate, a Certificate of Registration, a COC or a COA all allow waived tests. The certificate a laboratory holds should match the highest, most complex category it performs, and a site with only a Certificate of Waiver may perform waived tests and nothing else.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Atrioventricular Node
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: The impulse has arrived at the atrioventricular node. What is the delay before it moves on, and what does a longer one do to the tracing?
opciones: About 100 ms, and a longer delay there lengthens the PR interval
About 50 ms, and a longer delay there lengthens the PR interval
About 25 ms, and a longer delay there lengthens the PR interval
About 225 ms, and a longer delay there lengthens the PR interval
preguntas.explicacion: The node holds the impulse about 100 ms. The other figures belong to other legs of the trip: roughly 50 ms from the sinoatrial node to the atrioventricular node, about 25 ms down the bundle branches, and about 225 ms in total from the first impulse to ventricular depolarization. The PR interval covers the nodal delay.

preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, BMI Calculator: Calculate Your BMI
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a) · RMA XI vital signs and measurements
preguntas.pregunta: A muscular 26-year-old athlete has a BMI of 27 and asks whether he is overweight. What is the accurate response?
opciones: BMI ignores muscle mass and body composition, so the provider interprets it
BMI already corrects for muscle mass, so the number stands as measured
BMI is not valid under age 30, so the reading should simply be discarded
BMI is a direct measurement of body fat, so the number settles the question
preguntas.explicacion: Body mass index is built from height and weight alone. It leaves out muscle mass, bone density and body composition, so it is one piece of the picture rather than the whole of it, and the health care provider decides whether a given reading is too high or too low for that person.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: Reasonable Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable safeguards · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is named by OCR as a reasonable safeguard a health care office can adopt?
opciones: Speaking quietly when discussing a condition with relatives in a public area of the office
Guaranteeing that no visitor can ever overhear or glimpse any patient information at all
Requiring every workforce member to obtain the patient's consent before each chart entry
Sending all internal messages about patients through unencrypted e-mail to speed up care
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule expects safeguards of the administrative, technical and physical kinds, and OCR says outright that they are not meant to guarantee privacy against every conceivable risk. What is reasonable varies with the size and the nature of the entity; the examples given are dropping one's voice in public areas, keeping names out of conversations in hallways and elevators, posting reminder signs, and password-protecting the computers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k51 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks how much blood a commercial citrate tube should receive. What is the answer?
opciones: A line printed on the tube marks the volume of blood to be drawn
The vacuum stops the flow well before the tube can be overfilled
The color of the stopper sets the volume for every manufacturer
The laboratory calculates it from the patient's hematocrit result
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for these assays is collected into commercially prepared tubes that already hold their trisodium citrate, and each carries a line showing the volume of blood that should go in. Drawing short of that line leaves too much anticoagulant and lengthens the clotting time measured.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.6: Z-track Method for IM injections
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(1)(a) · RMA III.G.2.a(iv) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: What does the Z-track method for an intramuscular injection involve?
opciones: Pulling the skin about an inch to one side, injecting, and waiting ten seconds
Pulling the skin about an inch to one side, injecting, and withdrawing at once
Pinching the skin into a fold, injecting, and letting go before the needle exits
Holding the skin taut and flat, injecting, and pressing the site for ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The non-dominant hand displaces the skin downward or to one side by about an inch, some two centimeters, and the needle goes in at 90 degrees while that pull is held. Once the medication is in, the needle stays in place ten seconds before coming out in a smooth motion and the skin is released, so the tissue closes over a zigzag path. That keeps the medication in the muscle instead of leaking into subcutaneous tissue.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Chain of Custody in Clinical/Medical Drug Testing
preguntas.subtema: Clinical versus legal testing · CPT D5 5C k91 · PBT III.A.4 · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A urine drug screen is run on a patient in the emergency department for medical management only. Is a chain of custody required?
opciones: No: a purely clinical result is confidential and cannot be used against the patient
Yes: every drug screen carries the same documentation, regardless of purpose
No: chain of custody applies only to blood specimens, never to urine specimens
Yes: emergency department specimens always travel under a custody form
preguntas.explicacion: A medical drug test result is confidential and cannot be turned against the person in a disciplinary or a penal proceeding, which is why no chain of custody is required for it. It becomes essential once an initial positive immunoassay has to be confirmed for use in court, as after an accident or where the case may go to trial. The matrix is not what decides it.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Workstation security · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The check-in monitor faces the waiting room and shows the day's schedule with patient names. Which safeguard is at issue?
opciones: Workstation use and security, a physical safeguard covering how workstations are placed and used
Security awareness and training, the administrative standard for teaching staff the policies
Contingency planning, the administrative standard for keeping care going during a system failure
Evaluation, the administrative standard for periodically testing how well the policies work
preguntas.explicacion: The physical safeguards include workstation use and security, which call for policies setting out the proper use of workstations that can reach ePHI and the physical protections around them. The other three options are administrative safeguards: training the workforce, planning for emergencies that damage the systems, and assessing the policies periodically, on technical and on non-technical grounds.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.1 and 2.1.4
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3B k9 k58 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic short of tubes refills used ones by hand with anticoagulant. Why is that listed as a hazard?
opciones: Refilled tubes carry inappropriate amounts of anticoagulant and haemolyse
Refilled tubes carry too little vacuum and stop drawing after a few drops
Refilled tubes carry the wrong stopper color and confuse the sequence
Refilled tubes carry a broken gel barrier and mix serum back into cells
preguntas.explicacion: Reusing tubes refilled by hand with the wrong amount of anticoagulant appears among the causes of hemolysis. It is the practice that stocking enough tubes is meant to prevent, along with decanting blood from one tube into another to make the supply stretch.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Adult Immunization Schedule by Age: Tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C immunizations · CMA I.A.5 · 2027 I.A.5 · RMA XIII pharmacology immunizations · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A 45-year-old asks how often he needs a tetanus booster after his one Tdap dose. What does the adult schedule call for?
opciones: A Td or Tdap booster every 10 years
A Td or Tdap booster every 5 years
A Td or Tdap booster every 20 years
No further booster once a Tdap dose is on record
preguntas.explicacion: The adult schedule places one dose of Tdap and then a booster of Td or Tdap every ten years thereafter. Separate rules exist for pregnancy, where a Tdap dose is given each time, and for wound management, where a dose of Td or Tdap may be needed regardless of where the ten-year clock stands.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pelvic Inflammatory Disease", Etiology and History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(8) (2027 I.C.6.g(8)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A 22-year-old reports bilateral lower abdominal pain, vaginal discharge and pain with intercourse. Which two pathogens most often cause the suspected condition?
opciones: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae
Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae
Moraxella catarrhalis and Haemophilus influenzae
preguntas.explicacion: Pelvic inflammatory disease is an infection that climbs from the cervix, and about 85 percent of cases trace back to bacteria transmitted sexually or to microbes tied to bacterial vaginosis, with gonorrhea and chlamydia leading. The pain is often bilateral, and some patients have almost no symptoms at all, which does not make the long-term damage any smaller.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Fecal Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT V.B III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A stool specimen arrives for viral studies and the processor is told to prepare it before it goes into storage. Which sequence matches the published procedure?
opciones: About 1 mL of stool into 9 mL of sterile buffered saline, spun 30 minutes, supernatant below −40 °C
About 1 mL of stool into 9 mL of alkaline peptone water, spun 30 minutes, supernatant at 2 to 8 °C
About 1 mL of stool into 10 mL of sterile buffered saline, spun 10 minutes, whole tube at −20 °C
About 5 mL of stool into 9 mL of sterile buffered saline, spun 30 minutes, pellet frozen below −40 °C
preguntas.explicacion: For suspected viral infection the feces go into sterile buffered saline, roughly 1 mL into 9 mL, and the mixture is then spun for half an hour. What is kept is the supernatant, not the pellet, and it is frozen and stored below −40 °C until testing. Alkaline peptone water belongs to a different set-up: it is the enrichment broth used when cholera is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant wraps the cuff over a thin sweater sleeve to save time. What is the consequence?
opciones: Placing the cuff over clothing can shift the reading by as much as 50 mm Hg
Placing the cuff over clothing can shift the reading by as much as 5 mm Hg
Placing the cuff over clothing is acceptable when the fabric is thin and smooth
Placing the cuff over clothing lowers the reading only, so a normal value is safe
preguntas.explicacion: A cuff over clothing can alter the result by up to 50 mm Hg, the largest of the quantified technique errors. The cuff goes on the bare upper arm with nothing underneath it, and the sleeve is not simply rolled up either, because a rolled sleeve constricts the arm above the cuff.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.2 Basic Concepts Related to Wounds
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which findings warn that an abdominal surgical wound may be about to dehisce?
opciones: Redness at the wound margins, increasing drainage, growing pain and a broken suture
Pale flat wound margins, decreasing drainage, easing pain and a suture that has loosened
Blanching margins, clear serous drainage, itching and a suture that has begun to dissolve
Firm raised margins, no drainage, tightness across the line and a suture that has darkened
preguntas.explicacion: In dehiscence the edges of a surgical wound come apart, partly or completely. The warning signs are redness around the margins, drainage that keeps increasing from the incision and pain that keeps growing; a broken suture can mean minor dehiscence or that it is about to happen. It often occurs suddenly in abdominal wounds while the patient is coughing or straining.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Fibrinolysis; and Plasma Anticoagulants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A week after a venipuncture the small clot at the site has disappeared. Which enzyme broke down its fibrin, and from what precursor was it made?
opciones: Plasmin, from plasminogen
Thrombin, from prothrombin
Fibrin, from fibrinogen
Heparin, from basophils
preguntas.explicacion: The gradual removal of a clot is called fibrinolysis: the inactive plasma protein plasminogen is converted into active plasmin, which slowly breaks down the fibrin, while bradykinin dilates the vessel again. Thrombin is the enzyme that builds fibrin, not the one that removes it; fibrin is the clot material itself; and heparin is an anticoagulant from basophils that opposes prothrombin.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles (butterfly)
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw with a butterfly · CPT D3 3J k59 k54 · PBT II.H.1 II.J · CCMA 3E6 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A winged (butterfly) set is connected to evacuated tubes and the first tube to be filled is a light blue citrate tube. What does the WHO device table say must happen first?
opciones: A tube without additive is drawn or discarded, because of the air in the tubing
The tubing is flushed with the light blue tube, which is then sent as the specimen
The tourniquet is tightened until the tubing fills, then the citrate tube goes on
A red clot activator tube is drawn first so that the serum tests are not delayed
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 lists, as a disadvantage of winged steel needles used with vacuum tubes, that the air in the tubing means the first tube has to be either a tube with no additive or a discard tube. Sending the citrate tube that was used to fill the tubing would defeat the point, and the table says nothing about tightening the tourniquet or starting with a red tube.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 6: Accidental Release Measures
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 6 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A bottle of disinfectant concentrate breaks on the processing room floor. Which section of its safety data sheet guides the cleanup?
opciones: Section 6, on containment and cleanup after an accidental release
Section 4, on the first aid to give after contact with the chemical
Section 13, on disposal of the chemical and of its own container
Section 12, on what the chemical does if it reaches the environment
preguntas.explicacion: Section 6 covers the response to spills, leaks and releases: personal precautions such as removing ignition sources or ventilating, the protective equipment that keeps the chemical off skin, eyes and clothing, emergency steps including evacuation and when to call an expert, methods for containment such as covering drains, and the cleanup technique itself. It may distinguish a small spill from a large one. Sections 12 and 13 are among those OSHA does not enforce, and section 4 treats the person, not the floor.

preguntas.subtema: Daily QC for nonwaived quantitative tests · CPT D1 k28 · PBT VI.A quality assurance · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.3.d
preguntas.pregunta: For a nonwaived quantitative test, what control testing does CLIA require at a minimum each day patient specimens are run?
opciones: Two control materials at different concentrations
One negative and one positive control material
A single control material at the medical decision level
Three controls: low, mid-range and high, every 8 hours
preguntas.explicacion: At least once on each day of patient testing, a quantitative procedure needs two controls of different concentrations, while a qualitative procedure needs a negative and a positive control. Graded or titered procedures and tests with an extraction phase have their own variants. The three-level minimum, mid-point and maximum set belongs to calibration verification, not daily quality control.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrioventricular Block", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is seen on the tracing in a third-degree block?
opciones: P waves and QRS complexes at their own separate rates
P waves and QRS complexes at one shared but slow rate
P waves that lengthen the PR until a QRS is dropped
P waves that disappear while the QRS stays regular
preguntas.explicacion: Conduction between the chambers is gone, so the atria and the ventricles beat independently: the P waves march through at their own regular, faster rate while the complexes come at their own regular but slower one, driven by an escape rhythm arising in the junction or in the ventricle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Clinical Significance; and StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor"
preguntas.subtema: Implied consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.b-c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: An unconscious patient needs an urgent procedure and no surrogate is present. Which doctrine lets the team proceed?
opciones: Implied consent, on the assumption a reasonable person would agree
Expressed consent, obtained afterwards and dated to the time of care
Informed permission, given by the admitting service on arrival
Waived consent, recorded once the patient wakes up and agrees
preguntas.explicacion: Consent may be waived in an emergency where the patient cannot communicate and there is no surrogate decision-maker to be found. For an unaccompanied child the same reasoning goes by the emergency exception rule, or the doctrine of implied consent, on the assumption that a reasonable parent would agree. Permission is what a parent gives for a minor, and consent obtained afterwards is not what authorized the care.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Ethics", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Four principles dominate the ethics codes: beneficence, nonmaleficence, distributive justice and autonomy. Which one governs sharing one scarce treatment among several patients?
opciones: Distributive justice, used when more than one patient is involved
Beneficence, the one about advocating for the patient's best interests
Nonmaleficence, the one that draws the boundary against causing harm
Autonomy, the one about the patient deciding free of outside control
preguntas.explicacion: In the four-principle heuristic that most code-writing bodies use, distributive justice is the principle that applies equal or equitable treatment when the matter involves more than one patient. Beneficence is advocating for the patient's best interest, nonmaleficence is not harming the patient, and autonomy is preserving the patient's ability to decide independently of outside control.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5I · PBT VI.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: An emergency laboratory compares specimen rejections by shift over one year. What did the published audit find, and what does it suggest for training?
opciones: Two-thirds of rejections (66 %) came from the night shift, pointing training at the staff who collect at night
Two-thirds of rejections (66 %) came from the day shift, when volume is highest, pointing training at day staff
Rejections were evenly split between shifts, so training was aimed at the units with the most samples instead
Night-shift rejections were higher only for coagulation tubes, so training focused on citrate fill levels
preguntas.explicacion: Over a year of auditing, 66 % of specimen rejections fell in the night shift and 34 % in the day, even though the night runs with fewer laboratory staff. The laboratory answered by documenting rejected samples monthly in more detail and by training the personnel of the departments with the worst rejection rates at regular intervals, aiming to pull the overall rate from 6 % down below 2 %.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Statin Medications", Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on atorvastatin reports diffuse muscle aches with no injury. Which reaction of this class does that fit?
opciones: Myopathy, which is dose dependent and reverses once the statin is discontinued
Rhabdomyolysis, the reaction reported most often in patients taking this class
Necrotizing myopathy, whose weakness clears a day or two after the drug stops
Cognitive dysfunction, the commonest reaction and a reason to change agents
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are generally well tolerated; the reactions seen most are myopathy, hepatotoxicity and new diabetes. Myopathy is dose dependent and shows as diffuse myalgias or otherwise unexplained tenderness or weakness that reverses when the drug is stopped. Rhabdomyolysis is the gravest complication but is rare, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy persists for months, and cognitive change is rare.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A ward asks why the laboratory presses so hard on hemolysis when redrawing a tube takes two minutes. What consequences does the literature attach to it?
opciones: Delayed decisions, a longer stay in the department, and extra needle sticks
Loss of the quality control run and a forced recalibration of the analyser
A mandatory report of the quality failure to the accrediting organization
A penalty against the laboratory's proficiency testing performance that year
preguntas.explicacion: A hemolysed sample usually means drawing and testing a second one. Repeats hold up treatment and the clinical decisions that depend on it, stretch the patient's stay in the emergency department, and leave the patient unhappy at having been stuck more than once. The cost lands on the patient, not on the analyser, which is why the collection step gets the attention.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: The chest electrodes are being placed on a patient. Where does V1 go?
opciones: At the fourth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fourth intercostal space, left of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, in the mid-clavicular line
preguntas.explicacion: V1 sits in the fourth intercostal space just to the right of the sternum, and V2 goes in the same space on the left side. The two spots are found by walking the fingers down from the sternal angle, and they are marked before the skin is cleaned so the location is not lost.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures, a prothrombin time and a complete blood count are ordered on one venipuncture. Which specimen is collected third?
opciones: The purple EDTA tube for the complete blood count
The light blue citrate tube for the prothrombin time
The blood culture bottle for the microbiology order
A non-additive tube drawn ahead of the citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Of the three, the culture bottle sits at position 1, the citrate tube at position 3 and EDTA at position 8, so the EDTA tube is the third one filled. A non-additive tube does hold position 2, but the footnote reserves it for when tissue fluid or thromboplastin contamination is a concern.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Neomycin, Polymyxin, and Hydrocortisone Otic: To use the eardrops
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k70 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has been prescribed eardrops. Which set of instructions is correct?
opciones: Warm the bottle in the hand a minute or two, lie with that ear up, stay five minutes
Warm the bottle under hot tap water, lie with that ear down, stay for two minutes
Use the drops cold from the refrigerator, sit upright, and stay still for ten minutes
Warm the bottle in the hand, lie with that ear up, and get up as soon as it is done
preguntas.explicacion: The bottle is held in the hand for one or two minutes to warm the solution, a suspension is shaken, and the ear canal is cleaned and dried with a sterile applicator first. The patient lies with the affected ear uppermost, the ordered number of drops goes in without the dropper touching anything, and that position is kept for five minutes. A cotton wick may be used and is replaced at least every 24 hours.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which peripheral pulse is described as the hardest to palpate, especially for a less experienced clinician?
opciones: The posterior tibial, found immediately behind the medial malleolus
The popliteal, found a little lateral to the midline in the popliteal fossa
The femoral, found just below the inguinal ligament toward the pubic symphysis
The brachial, found between the medial epicondyle and the tendon of the biceps
preguntas.explicacion: The posterior tibial pulse sits just behind the bony bump on the inner ankle and is considered the most difficult of the peripheral pulses to feel. The popliteal is also sought less often, but the one singled out for difficulty is the posterior tibial, which matters when its absence is being used as a finding.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, Organelles for Energy Production
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A neuron may hold more than a thousand of one organelle, while a bone cell holds only a couple hundred. Which organelle is it, and why the difference?
opciones: The mitochondrion, because a neuron needs far more ATP than a bone cell
The lysosome, because a neuron digests far more debris than a bone cell
The nucleus, because a neuron stores far more genetic material than a bone cell
The Golgi apparatus, because a neuron exports far more protein than a bone cell
preguntas.explicacion: Mitochondria convert the energy held in nutrients such as glucose into ATP, along an inner membrane folded into cristae. Cells that spend a lot of energy carry a lot of them: muscle cells are packed with them for contraction and neurons need them to run their sodium and potassium pumps, while a bone cell is far less active.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a-b · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which feature must appear on a valid HIPAA authorization form?
opciones: An expiration and a statement of the right to revoke it in writing, all in plain language
A witness signature from a workforce member who watched the patient sign the document
A cost estimate of the copies, since the fee has to be agreed before the release is signed
A clause making treatment conditional on the patient granting the authorization requested
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization has to be written in specific terms and in plain language, and it has to state what information is involved, who is disclosing it, who is receiving it, when it runs out, and that it can be revoked in writing. Conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits on the patient signing one is forbidden to a covered entity, save in the limited circumstances the rule spells out.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Overweight & Obesity — Definition & Facts, BMI of adults ages 20 and older
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 weight control · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a) · RMA XI vital signs and measurements · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which body mass index range is classified as overweight in adults aged 20 and older?
opciones: 25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 30
25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 35
24 to 28.9, with obesity beginning at 29
27 to 31.9, with obesity beginning at 32
preguntas.explicacion: The adult table runs 18.5 to 24.9 for healthy weight, 25 to 29.9 for overweight, and 30 or higher for obesity, with 40 and above marked as severe obesity. Body mass index estimates overweight and obesity from weight and height together; it is not a direct measurement of body fat.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, EMR vs EHR - What is the Difference?
preguntas.subtema: EHR versus EMR · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an electronic health record from an electronic medical record?
opciones: The EHR is built to be shared with other organizations involved in the patient's care
The EHR is the version the patient keeps at home, while the EMR belongs to the practice
The EHR holds only billing and demographic data, while the EMR holds the clinical notes
The EHR is a scanned copy of the paper chart, while the EMR is entered directly by staff
preguntas.explicacion: An EMR is the digital version of the paper chart in one clinician's office: it tracks data over time, flags who is due for screening and supports quality work inside that practice, but the information does not travel easily beyond it. An EHR is designed to reach past the organization that collected the data, so the record follows the patient to the specialist, the hospital or the next state.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC4771218 LaRocco et al., Effectiveness of Preanalytic Practices on Urine Cultures (2016), Summary of findings
preguntas.subtema: Urine culture delay · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine for culture cannot reach the microbiology laboratory for about 6 hours. What keeps the culture result valid?
opciones: Refrigerating it or placing it in a boric acid preservative tube, either of which holds it for up to 24 hours
Keeping it at room temperature, which is acceptable for up to 24 hours as long as the cup stays capped
Freezing it, since freezing stops bacterial growth more completely than refrigeration does
Adding a formaldehyde preservative, the additive that best protects bacteria for later culture
preguntas.explicacion: Urine for culture must be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or placed in a preservative; both boric acid and refrigeration hold the specimen adequately for up to 24 hours. Urine left at room temperature for more than 4 hours shows overgrowth of both pathogens and contaminants. Formaldehyde is used to preserve cells and causes false-positive strip reactions, and freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A handwritten order reads QD. Which misreading put that abbreviation on the Do Not Use list?
opciones: It is read as QID, four times daily, instead of every day
It is read as QOD, every other day, instead of every day
It is read as QHS, nightly at bedtime, instead of every day
It is read as PRN, only as needed, instead of every day
preguntas.explicacion: QD means every day, but a handwritten q that trails off, or the period that follows it, gets taken for the letter i, and the order turns into QID, four doses a day. Write daily instead. QOD has its own entry on the list, where the badly written o is the problem.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Network; and Glossary: Out-of-pocket maximum/limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 4 k61 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does a health plan's "network" consist of?
opciones: The providers, facilities and suppliers under contract with the insurer
The list of prescription drugs the plan covers, also called its drug list
The providers the patient may see without a referral from the primary care doctor
The services that count toward the out-of-pocket limit, including out-of-network care
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the network as the set of facilities, providers and suppliers that have a contract with the insurer or plan to deliver health care services. Being in the network is a matter of contract, not of whether a referral is needed: in many HMOs even in-network specialists require one. The glossary's entry on the out-of-pocket limit shows the other side of the coin: care received out of network does not count toward that limit. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, a separate entry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature e · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: A temperature is charted as 38.2 °C with no other detail. What is missing?
opciones: The route used, since each site carries its own average and its own fever cut-off
The thermometer model, since each manufacturer calibrates its device differently
The room temperature, since a warm room lifts every reading by a fixed amount
The patient's baseline, since a value has no meaning until a baseline is on file
preguntas.explicacion: The same patient reads differently at the armpit, the mouth, the ear and the rectum, and the thresholds for calling a value a fever follow the site. A number without its route cannot be graded or compared with the last one, which is why the route is written beside the value and the hour it was taken.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Plasma Anticoagulants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k57 heparin tubes) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which natural anticoagulant is released by basophils, opposes prothrombin, and is also given as a drug to surgical patients at risk of clots?
opciones: Heparin
Protein C
Thrombin
Plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: Several plasma anticoagulants keep clotting confined to the injury: the protein C system, TFPI, antithrombin and heparin. Heparin comes from basophils, is short-acting, opposes prothrombin and also sits on the cells lining the vessels; a pharmaceutical form is given, for example, to surgical patients at risk of clots. Thrombin builds fibrin and plasmin dissolves it; neither is an anticoagulant.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Breathing difficulties - first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.p · 2027 I.B.8.p · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: The wheezing of a patient in respiratory distress fades away. How should that be read?
opciones: Not as improvement: breathing and pulse go on being monitored
As improvement, so the emergency call can now be canceled
As a sign the inhaler worked and that a second dose is not needed
As proof the problem was anxiety rather than a lung problem
preguntas.explicacion: The patient's condition is not assumed to be improving just because abnormal breath sounds such as wheezing can no longer be heard: breathing and pulse are monitored until medical help arrives. Nobody waits to see whether things get better before calling for help, and the patient is not moved after a head, neck, chest or airway injury.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Apgar Score", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.c · RMA III.F.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn scores 6 at five minutes. What does that call for?
opciones: Continued scoring every 5 minutes, since the score is below 7
Continued scoring every minute, since the score is below 7
No further scoring, since only the 1 and 5 minute values are recorded
A single repeat score at 10 minutes, and none after that point
preguntas.explicacion: Every infant is scored at one and five minutes and the values are documented. A five-minute score under 7 means the recording carries on at five-minute intervals, up to 20 minutes, as a way of tracking the response to resuscitation. Seven to ten is reassuring, four to six is moderately abnormal, and zero to three is low.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult and child after onset of puberty, First Aid and When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Lone rescuer sequence · CPT D1 1L k38 · CMA I.B.9.c / 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
