The reading runs about 10 mm Hg low, since the arm below the heart empties faster
The reading is unaffected as long as the cuff itself is at the level of the heart
The reading runs about 6 mm Hg high, the same amount as an unsupported back
preguntas.explicacion: An arm that is not supported adds roughly 10 mm Hg. The arm rests so that the middle of the cuff sits at the level of the right atrium: below that line the reading comes out higher, above it lower. The unsupported back and feet are a separate error worth about 6 mm Hg.

preguntas.subtema: Treatment disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a(5) · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist faxes a patient's lab results to the physician who ordered them. Does HIPAA require the patient's written authorization first?
opciones: No: disclosures for treatment are permitted without authorization
Yes: any disclosure outside the facility requires a signed authorization
Yes, unless the patient signed the notice of privacy practices acknowledgment
No, but only because fax transmissions are outside the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: No authorization is needed for a covered entity to use or disclose PHI in its own treatment, in payment or in health care operations, nor to disclose it so that any other provider can treat the patient; 45 CFR 164.506 sets that out and 164.502(a)(1)(ii) lists it among the permitted uses. Authorization under 164.508 is needed for uses outside those categories, such as marketing or sale of PHI. The acknowledgment of the notice is a separate duty and does not create or remove permissions, and faxes carry PHI like any other medium.

preguntas.subtema: Form of retained records · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: An employer wants to scan its employee medical files and shred the paper. Which item may not be handled that way?
opciones: Chest X-ray films, which the standard has preserved in their original state
Exposure monitoring worksheets, which the standard keeps for thirty years
Any record whose author has left, because nobody can authenticate the entry
Any record older than five years, which has to stay in the form first used
preguntas.explicacion: The standard does not dictate the form or the process by which a record is preserved, so long as the information stays intact and can be retrieved. It makes one exception in that sentence: chest X-ray films are kept in their original state.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which side of the upper limb does each of the two main superficial veins drain?
opciones: The cephalic drains the radial side; the basilic drains the medial side
The cephalic drains the medial side; the basilic drains the radial side
Both drain the radial side, and the median cubital vein drains the medial
The cephalic drains the deep muscles; the basilic drains the skin only
preguntas.explicacion: The cephalic vein takes the radial, or thumb, side of the limb and the basilic takes the medial side; near the elbow the median cubital vein connects the two. Both belong to the superficial system, which drains skin and superficial fascia, while the deep veins drain muscle and bone.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Media Notice
preguntas.subtema: Media notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: At what point does a breach also require notice to prominent media outlets?
opciones: When it affects more than 500 residents of one State or jurisdiction
When it affects more than 500 individuals nationwide, counted across all States
When it affects any number of individuals and involves an electronic device
When it affects fewer than 500 individuals but the entity cannot reach them by mail
preguntas.explicacion: Where a breach touches more than 500 residents of one State or jurisdiction, the entity has to notify prominent media outlets serving that area as well as the individuals, usually by press release. The media notice runs on the individual notice's clock: no unreasonable delay, and 60 days from discovery at the outside. The content is the same.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2; and StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 first drop · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away after a skin puncture?
opciones: It can carry tissue fluid, or debris such as loose flakes of skin
It is arterial in oxygen content, and the test needs a venous value
It holds the alcohol that has not yet dried, which hemolyses it
It is the drop richest in platelets, which would clump in the tube
preguntas.explicacion: The first drop goes onto the gauze because tissue fluid or loose skin may have got into it. On a glucometer the reasoning is the same: that drop can hold interstitial or intracellular fluid, or be hemolysed, so the strip takes the second one. Capillary blood does resemble arterial blood in oxygen, but that is another matter.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: What makes an accidental arterial puncture more painful than a venous one?
opciones: Arteries have thicker walls and more nerves associated with them
Arteries have thinner walls and fewer nerves associated with them
Arteries carry a higher volume of blood at a much lower pressure
Arteries lie deeper and are always covered by the bicipital sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for a draw because they run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and carry more nerves with them, so puncturing one hurts more. The point matters at the elbow, where an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein and make that route the more painful choice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wood's Light", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: How is the Wood's lamp set up and held at the bedside?
opciones: Switched on about 60 seconds first, room dark, held 10 to 30 cm away
Switched on about 10 seconds first, room lit, held 1 to 3 cm away
Switched on about 5 minutes first, room dark, held 50 to 60 cm away
Used the moment it is switched on, room dark, resting on the skin
preguntas.explicacion: The lamp is turned on for roughly a minute before the skin is examined, the room has to be dark, and the instrument is held some 10 to 30 cm from the skin. It gives off no heat and the examination is painless, so the distance is about the light, not about protecting the skin from burning.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "24-Hour Urine Collection", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine 24-hour volume (003425), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: 24-hour start and end · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a 24-hour urine collection at 7 a.m. asks what to do with the urine he passes at 7 a.m. on the first day. What is the correct instruction?
opciones: Void into the toilet and discard it; collect every void after that, including the 7 a.m. void the next morning
Collect it as the first specimen of the period, and stop with the last void before 7 a.m. the next morning
Void into the toilet and discard it, and also discard the 7 a.m. void of the next morning to keep exactly 24 hours
Collect it as a separate first-morning specimen for urinalysis, and start the timed collection with the next void
preguntas.explicacion: The period starts with an empty bladder: the void at the starting time goes into the toilet and is not kept. From then on all urine is saved for 24 hours, and the void at the same clock time the next morning is the last one collected and does go into the container. Keeping the opening void or dropping the closing void both shift the measured period. The container is refrigerated throughout.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Record Keeping (Records); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), documentation and recordkeeping findings
preguntas.subtema: Testing records and logs · CPT D1 1E / k28 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of records should a waived testing site keep so that any result can be traced and problems found?
opciones: Test results, QC results, lot numbers with receipt and expiration dates, temperature and function checks, training and PT
Only the patient results and the QC results, since CLIA requires no other documentation from waived sites
The manufacturer's inserts and the fee receipts for the certificate, which the state agency reviews at renewal
A daily census of patients tested and the names of the operators, retained until the next certificate cycle
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation is not spelled out in most inserts and therefore is not a CLIA requirement for waived sites, but it is a core good practice: test orders and results with any confirmatory results, QC results, lot numbers with dates received, used and expiring, daily temperatures and function checks, failures and corrective actions, recall notices, training and competency, and proficiency testing results. In CMS surveys 45 % of sites did not record name, lot and expiration.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Route of Administration and Types of Orders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · RMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: An order reads "nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN chest pain". What do the two abbreviations mean?
opciones: Sublingual, and as needed
Sublingual, and around the clock
Subcutaneous, and as needed
Slow release, and as needed
preguntas.explicacion: SL is the standard abbreviation for the sublingual route, where the medication is placed under the tongue, and PRN marks an order to be given when the patient requests it or the symptom appears. The other common route abbreviations are PO for oral, PR for a rectal suppository, INH for inhalation, IM for intramuscular and TD for a transdermal patch; subcutaneous is written out, since its abbreviations are error prone.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2; and Annex E
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Recapping a needle cannot be avoided in one particular situation. Which technique is then required?
opciones: The one-hand scoop, never a recap made with both hands
A two-handed recap made slowly with the cap held steady
A recap made by an assistant while the worker holds still
A recap made after the needle has been rinsed and dried
preguntas.explicacion: Where recapping is unavoidable the one-hand scoop is used, and recapping with both hands is expressly forbidden. The scoop is performed near the sharps container, the device is discarded immediately afterwards, and the surface used is then cleaned with disinfectant.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Remote monitoring · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which telehealth arrangement is remote patient monitoring?
opciones: A wearable device sending the patient's readings to the clinician between visits
A live video call in which the clinician watches the patient walk across the room
A specialist reading an image the primary care clinician uploaded the previous day
A brief telephone call in which the clinician asks about new symptoms since Monday
preguntas.explicacion: Remote patient monitoring follows a patient's clinical status between visits, either without interruption or at intervals, using devices or digital platforms; the readings travel in from equipment kept at home or are keyed in by the patient. Continuous glucose monitors are one named example; cardiac rhythm monitors are the other. It stands beside the synchronous and the asynchronous arrangement as the third type of telemedicine service.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In the second step of blood typing, called back typing, what is mixed with red cells known to be type A and type B?
opciones: The patient's serum, to look for anti-A and anti-B antibodies
The patient's red cells, to look for the A antigen or B antigen
The patient's plasma with anti-D reagent, to look for Rh factor
The patient's whole blood, to look for clumping of the donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Blood typing has two steps. In ABO typing the sample's cells are mixed with anti-A and anti-B antibodies and watched for clumping. In back typing the serum, the liquid part without cells, is mixed with cells known to be type A and type B; since type A people have anti-B, type B have anti-A and type O have both, the serum reaction confirms the type. Rh typing is a similar but separate test.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Covered Accounts
preguntas.subtema: Covered accounts · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A practice works out that it holds no covered accounts at all this year. What does the FTC advise it to do about the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Repeat the risk assessment periodically, since a change in the business can create them
Write the program anyway, since every medical office holds covered accounts in practice
Send the Commission a statement recording that the Rule does not reach the practice
Destroy the identification documents on file, which are no longer needed for the Rule
preguntas.explicacion: A financial institution or creditor first has to work out whether it holds covered accounts, looking at the ones it has and the ones it opens, and only then does a written program become compulsory. Holding none means no program is needed, but business models shift and so do services, and accounts can appear through a change of structure, of process or of organization, which is why the assessment is repeated periodically.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Pearls and Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: How is sinus bradycardia defined?
opciones: A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 60 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 40 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm running at fewer than 80 beats per minute
Any irregular rhythm slower than 60 beats per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The depolarization still starts in the sinus node and the tracing still meets the criteria for sinus rhythm; only the rate is below 60. Most of these patients have no symptoms. There is a growing push to move the cut-off down to 50, since many healthy people rest between 50 and 60, but the accepted figure is still 60.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The provider documents a borderline condition at the end of the visit. How is it coded?
opciones: As confirmed, unless the classification has an entry for the borderline form
As uncertain, so only the signs and symptoms are coded for that visit
As confirmed, but only for inpatients and never in an outpatient office
As uncertain, unless the provider repeats it at the following visit
preguntas.explicacion: A borderline diagnosis is treated as confirmed unless the classification carries its own entry for the borderline form of that condition, as it does for borderline diabetes. A borderline condition is not an uncertain diagnosis, so the inpatient and the outpatient setting are treated alike here. Unclear documentation is a reason to query.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Organizational Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Business associate agreements · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a transcription vendor may start receiving electronic protected health information, what must the practice have in place?
opciones: A written business associate agreement obligating the vendor to safeguard the information
A signed authorization from every patient whose dictation the vendor is going to transcribe
A notice of privacy practices addressed to the vendor and acknowledged by its privacy official
An accounting of disclosures listing each record the vendor is expected to receive that year
preguntas.explicacion: The Security Rule lets a covered entity put ePHI in a business associate's hands, to be created, received, kept or transmitted on the entity's behalf, only once satisfactory assurances have been obtained in a contract or another written arrangement. That agreement also obliges the business associate to demand the same of any subcontractor and to report security incidents, breaches included, back to the practice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ambulatory Electrocardiogram Monitoring", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii III.F.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports palpitations about once a month. Which monitoring gives the better chance of catching them?
opciones: A patch or loop recorder worn for about two weeks
A 24-hour Holter, since it records every single beat
A resting 12-lead tracing repeated at each office visit
An exercise stress test run on the treadmill protocol
preguntas.explicacion: The traditional monitor is the right choice when symptoms come every day. For palpitations that appear now and then, loop recorders and patch monitors have a better yield, and a two-week stretch is the balance usually struck between how much it finds and what it costs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Medical and Surgical History
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k44 · CMA I.A.4.e · RMA III.F.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's problem list is blank, but during the medication review he lists several multivitamins and nutritional supplements. Why does that matter?
opciones: Supplement use can uncover a past bariatric surgery the patient did not report as an illness
Supplement use marks an underlying psychiatric condition such as generalized anxiety disorder
Products bought without a prescription are left out of reconciliation because no one ordered them
Nutritional supplements belong under allergies rather than on the list of current medications
preguntas.explicacion: Patients leave out what they do not think of as illness. A stack of vitamins and supplements is a clue to weight-loss surgery and the conditions that came with it, such as hyperlipidemia or sleep apnea. Benzodiazepines are the clue that points elsewhere, to a psychiatric diagnosis. Every product bought over the counter belongs on the medication list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Patient Rights under HIPAA
preguntas.subtema: How results are communicated · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that results never be left as a message on his home phone, only mailed to his address. How is that request treated?
opciones: As a right: patients may say how information reaches them
As a courtesy the clinic may grant if its system allows it
As a restriction that needs the privacy officer's approval
As impossible, since results go out the way the system sends
preguntas.explicacion: The list of patient rights includes stating how one's information is to be handled and communicated to others; the example given is a patient who wants any message from the pharmacy or the hospital mailed to his home rather than left on his telephone. It sits beside the right to ask that disclosures be restricted and the right to receive an accounting of the disclosures that were made.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k143 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen sits at the nursing station for three hours before anyone walks it down. Beyond any effect on culture, what does the delay cost?
opciones: The cells degenerate and the biochemistry shifts, glucose being the value singled out as affected
The cells degenerate and the protein climbs, while the glucose is unchanged by the wait itself
The specimen clots, so no cell count can be reported from any of the three numbered tubes
The organisms lose viability, which is why the specimen is refrigerated as soon as it is drawn
preguntas.explicacion: A lumbar puncture fills three sterile tubes, and the laboratory is meant to work on them straight away: delay lets the cells degenerate and shifts the biochemistry, glucose first of all. Refrigeration is no fix either, since cold costs the survival of Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis, so the specimen waits at room temperature.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Upper Limbs and Table 20.14; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Blood Supply and Lymphatics
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53 site selection) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: You are choosing a vein in the antecubital area. Which vein is the most common venipuncture site, and what does it connect?
opciones: The median cubital vein, linking the cephalic and basilic veins
The basilic vein, linking the median antebrachial and axillary veins
The cephalic vein, running superficially along the biceps brachii
The brachial vein, formed where the radial and ulnar veins join
preguntas.explicacion: More venous blood is drawn from the median cubital than from any other vein: it leaves the basilic in the bend of the elbow and runs diagonally to meet the cephalic, tracing a V, and it lies very shallow in the roof of the cubital fossa, easy to reach. The brachial vein is deep, born where the radial and the ulnar veins meet.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What types of blood tests require fasting?; and MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, What are the different types of blood tests?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: The clerk asks which of the panels she books usually need a fast. Which grouping is named among the common tests that do?
opciones: Blood glucose, a lipid panel and a basic metabolic panel
Blood glucose, a complete blood count and a coagulation panel
A lipid panel, a troponin test and a complete blood count
A basic metabolic panel, a troponin test and a strep screen
preguntas.explicacion: The tests said usually to require fasting are blood glucose tests, cholesterol level tests, that is the lipid panel, and the basic metabolic panel. Liver function tests and a renal function panel may also call for a fast in some cases. A blood count is part of a routine checkup, and troponin is a blood enzyme test used after a suspected heart attack.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Description and Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Technology-based care · CCMA 1A k5 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who spends part of the year in another state asks about her telehealth visits. What does Part B cover through the end of 2027?
opciones: Services the patient can get from anywhere in the country, home included
Services the patient can get only from a clinic in a rural shortage area
Services the patient can get only while admitted to a hospital as inpatient
Services the patient can get only through a Medicare Advantage plan network
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth means medical or health services from a provider located somewhere else in the country, using audio and video technology or, in some cases, audio only. Through December 31, 2027, Part B covers telehealth the patient can get from anywhere in the United States, home included. Advance care planning, depression screening and speech therapy are among the examples.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Accountable care organization; and CMS, Medicare Shared Savings Program - About
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is distinctive about how an accountable care organization is paid?
opciones: Payment is tied to quality goals and outcomes that lead to cost savings
Payment is a fixed sum per patient each month regardless of services used
Payment is made for each separate service the providers happen to furnish
Payment is a single lump sum covering one episode of care from start to end
preguntas.explicacion: The organization's payment is tied to hitting quality goals in health care, and to outcomes that end up saving money. An ACO delivering high-quality care and spending more wisely may share in the savings it earns for Medicare, through what are called performance payments. Capitation, fee for service and bundled episode payment are the other arrangements.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.2 · CCMA 3E k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A methotrexate level is being sent to the laboratory. Under which transport condition will the specimen be accepted?
opciones: Carried on ice and protected from light
Carried at room temperature in a gel tube
Carried frozen at –20 °C in an EDTA tube
Carried at 37 °C in a heated transport block
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples for methotrexate measurement are accepted only if they were carried on ice and in the dark; specimens transported otherwise are rejected. The same passage assigns EDTA whole blood to cyclosporine monitoring and bans gel tubes for drug levels, so the distractors combine real rules from neighbouring drugs with conditions the source never gives for methotrexate.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood
preguntas.subtema: Venipuncture technique · CPT D3 3H k64 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: In addition to anchoring the vein, what does the WHO's Step 6 ask the patient to do so the veins stand out?
opciones: Form a fist
Pump the hand
Lower the arm
Hold a breath
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 lists three actions in sequence: anchor the vein with a thumb below the site, ask the patient to make a fist so the veins are more prominent, and enter the vein swiftly at 30 degrees or less. Pumping the hand, dangling the arm and breath-holding are not part of the WHO procedure; the warm compress and tapping are the only other vein-raising measures in the material.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · CMA I.A.1.g · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What do the two ends of the numeric rating scale for pain stand for?
opciones: Zero is no pain at all and ten is the worst pain the patient can imagine
Zero is mild pain and ten is the point at which analgesia becomes mandatory
Zero is no pain at all and five is the worst pain the patient can imagine
One is the least pain measurable and ten is the average pain of childbirth
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs from 0, no pain, to 10, the worst possible pain. It is quick and widely used but crude, and the number is worth more when the patient is asked to explain it: a 1 usually means a bump or a bruise, while a 10 is compared to childbirth or passing a kidney stone. A high number alone does not decide the treatment.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Disorders of Erythrocytes
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC reports a low mean corpuscular volume (MCV). How are the patient's red cells described?
opciones: Microcytic, smaller than normal
Macrocytic, larger than normal
Normocytic, of normal size
Polycythemic, too numerous
preguntas.explicacion: The MCV is a common test that measures red cell size, used in the morphological approach to anemia: normal-sized cells are normocytic, smaller cells microcytic and larger cells macrocytic. A low MCV therefore means microcytic cells. Polycythemia is not a size term; it is an overproduction of red cells.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: How is lead aVR produced from the limb electrodes?
opciones: The right arm is the positive one and the others a common ground
The left arm is the positive one and the others a common ground
The right leg is the positive one and the others a common ground
The right arm and the left leg are paired against each other
preguntas.explicacion: The augmented leads take one limb as the positive pole and use the remaining limb electrodes together as a common ground: the right arm for aVR, the left arm for aVL and the left leg for aVF. Pairing two electrodes against each other is how leads I to III work.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (venous illumination devices)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k60 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which groups of laboratory parameters can be distorted by venous stasis from a prolonged tourniquet?
opciones: Biochemistry and coagulation factors
Blood cultures and HLA tissue typing
Glucose only, once fluoride is added
Hematology counts only, in the EDTA tube
preguntas.explicacion: In recommending venous illumination devices over prolonged tourniquet use, the chapter says venous stasis from a long application can negatively affect several parameters, naming biochemistry and coagulation factors. The coagulopathies review agrees, asking for minimal tourniquet time to avoid artifacts in clotting tests. Cultures and HLA typing are not among the parameters the chapter lists.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops a rash where the electrode patches were. How is that handled?
opciones: It usually clears when the patches come off and needs no care
It usually clears once an antihistamine cream has been applied
It means the test cannot be repeated on that patient again
It means the gel was left on too long and must be reported
preguntas.explicacion: Skin sensitivity to the adhesive gel is the one complication of a test that is otherwise safe and non-invasive. It settles as soon as the patches are taken off and in most cases needs no treatment at all, although a known allergy to the adhesive is noted as a relative contraindication.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How does the visual analog scale differ from the numeric rating scale?
opciones: The patient marks a line whose ends are labeled, and the distance is the score
The patient chooses among printed words, and each word carries a fixed score
The observer scores facial expression and limb movement instead of asking
The patient scores pain, enjoyment and general activity from zero to ten each
preguntas.explicacion: On the visual analog scale the patient marks a point along a line whose ends read no pain and worst possible pain, and the score is how far the mark lies from the first end. Pictures can be added where patient and clinician have no language in common. Its limitations are the same as those of the numeric scale.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 5.2 Review, Observations, and Replication
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Interference on a tracing has blurred the P waves in every lead. What follows?
opciones: The strip is run again: the P wave has to be plainly visible
The strip is kept: only the QRS complexes have to be visible
The strip is kept and the interference is noted on the log
The strip is run again only if the QRS is blurred as well
preguntas.explicacion: One of the minimum standards is a complex clearly drawn with the P wave in plain view, with no noise obscuring or wiping it out. Because the tracing is reviewed before the patient leaves, a strip below the standard is repeated rather than filed.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.5 and Section 2.2.3, Step 9
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: Before handing a batch of samples to the courier, what final check does the WHO procedure place immediately before dispatch?
opciones: Rechecking the labels on the tubes against the forms
Rechecking that the request form is folded inside the bag
Re-verifying the patient's fasting status by telephone
Recording the tourniquet time for each tube on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Once the draw is done, hands washed and waste discarded, the WHO sequence has the phlebotomist match every tube label against its form before anything is sent, then tell the patient the procedure is over and look at the puncture site again. Patient-to-sample matching, which is the labeling, and the conditions the sample travels under both appear on the list of things that shape a result while it is being collected and moved. The request form does travel with the samples, but in the pocket on the outside of the leak-proof bag, never folded in among the tubes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Invasive Techniques); and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture - catheterized specimen (003752), What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Indwelling catheter: not from the bag · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter needs a urine culture. From where should the specimen be taken?
opciones: Never from the drainage bag, whose contents are considered contaminated
From the drainage bag, after mixing it so the sample is representative
From the drainage bag, provided it was emptied less than 2 hours earlier
From the drainage bag, after adding boric acid to stop any overgrowth
preguntas.explicacion: When a catheter is already in place, urine that has pooled in the collection bag is regarded as contaminated and is never used for culture, no matter how recently the bag was emptied or what preservative is added afterward. Patients with a permanent catheter often carry bacteria in the urine without true infection, which is called colonization, and bag urine would exaggerate that.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory audits a full year of identification errors and finds that most of them share one feature. Which feature is that?
opciones: The sample carried fewer than two patient identifiers
The barcode had been printed for a different test panel
The sample had been labeled after arriving in the laboratory
The requisition and the tube listed different collection times
preguntas.explicacion: In the laboratory that measured its preanalytical quality indicators, identification problems were the second most frequent error, and most of them consisted of a label with fewer than two identifiers; in newborns the rate was ten times higher because the small tubes leave little room to write two. Wrong panels, late labeling and time mismatches are other errors, not the one that dominated.

preguntas.subtema: Hospital retention · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare conditions of participation, how long must a hospital keep its medical records?
opciones: At least five years, either in the original form or a legal reproduction
At least seven years, matching the rule for orders and certifications
At least ten years, matching the rule for Medicare Advantage organizations
For the duration of care plus thirty years, matching the OSHA employee rule
preguntas.explicacion: The medical record service condition wants records written accurately, completed promptly, filed and retained properly, and kept accessible, and it fixes a floor of five years, in original form or a legal reproduction. Seven, ten and thirty years belong elsewhere: documentation of ordered and certified services, Medicare Advantage contracts, and OSHA employee medical records.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, idiopathic and congenital
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes a disease whose cause is unknown, and which describes one that is present at birth?
opciones: Idiopathic for the unknown cause; congenital for present at birth
Congenital for the unknown cause; idiopathic for present at birth
Hereditary for the unknown cause; idiopathic for present at birth
Acute for the unknown cause; hereditary for present at birth
preguntas.explicacion: Idiopathic describes a disease of unknown cause. Congenital means a condition or trait present at birth, which may be genetic or not. Hereditary is narrower: genetic information passed from parent to child through sperm and egg cells. Acute is about the pace, signs that begin and worsen quickly.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How long is the strip captured by a standard resting recording?
opciones: Ten seconds, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Three minutes, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Sixty seconds, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
Ten minutes, taken once the patient is lying down and relaxed
preguntas.explicacion: Everything else in the preparation leads up to a ten-second recording, which is why the patient must be settled before it starts. That same ten seconds is what makes the count-and-multiply method work when the rhythm is too irregular for the square methods.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Burns", First Aid: Minor burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient spills hot coffee on the hand and the skin is unbroken and red. What is the first aid?
opciones: Cool running water or a cool bath for at least 5 to 30 minutes
An ice water bath for at least 5 minutes, then a snug bandage
A layer of butter or ointment at once, then a dry sterile gauze
A cold pack held on the skin for 20 minutes with firm pressure
preguntas.explicacion: Cool water, not ice water, is run over the burn or the part is soaked for 5 to 30 minutes; a clean, cold, wet towel eases the pain. Afterward the area is covered with a dry sterile bandage and protected from pressure and friction. Butter, oil, ice, creams and household remedies do not go on a burn.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method, Action
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: 'Do you understand the fasting instructions?' 'Yes.' Why does this exchange fail as teach-back?
opciones: It is a yes-or-no question; patients tend to say yes whether or not they understood
It tests the patient's memory, which is exactly what teach-back is designed to do anyway
It was asked in the middle of the visit rather than at the very end of it
It was asked of the patient instead of the companion who will supervise the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Neither 'Do you understand?' nor 'Does that make sense?' counts as teach-back, because a patient is likely to answer yes either way. Teach-back asks the patient to put back, in her own words, the thing she needs to know or to do; it is not a test of memory, and it is done in chunks through the visit rather than saved for the end.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access, shape of the day · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under open access, how is a physician's day laid out in the appointment book?
opciones: About half the day is left open, the rest for necessary follow-ups and patients who declined a same-day slot
About a quarter of the day is left open, and the remainder is booked ahead as in the traditional system
The day is booked as usual, but a quarter of the slots are held back for callers with an urgent problem
About half the day is left open, and the remainder is kept for callers the front desk triages as urgent
preguntas.explicacion: Instead of filling a physician's time weeks or months in advance, the model leaves roughly half the day open. Booked ahead are the clinically necessary follow-ups and the visits of those who, having called, preferred not to be seen that same day, a group that usually stays under a quarter. Triaging callers by clinical urgency is exactly what the model does away with.

preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · CMA E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Which right does a hospitalized patient have over the plan of care?
opciones: To be informed of their status, take part in planning, and refuse treatment
To be informed of their status and to demand any treatment they have read about
To take part in planning only when a family representative is at the bedside
To refuse treatment only after a second physician has documented agreement
preguntas.explicacion: The patient, or their representative where state law allows one, has the right to make informed decisions: to be told their health status, to take part in planning the care and the treatment, and to request or refuse treatment. That right explicitly does not become a way to demand services judged medically unnecessary or inappropriate, and no second signature is needed to refuse.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant prepares a controlled substance prescription for the prescriber to sign. Who carries the responsibility if it does not meet the regulation?
opciones: The prescribing practitioner, with a corresponding liability resting on the pharmacist
The medical assistant who prepared it, because the preparation was where it went wrong
The pharmacy technician who entered it, because dispensing is the last step in the chain
Nobody, as long as the practitioner signed it the way a legal document would be signed
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation lets a secretary or an agent prepare a prescription for the practitioner to sign, but if what results fails to meet the law and the regulations in every essential respect, the responsibility rests on the prescribing practitioner, and a corresponding liability falls on the pharmacist who fills a prescription that is not in the form the DEA requires, a central fill pharmacist included.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Children; and StatPearls, "Parental Consent", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old comes for a lipid panel with her mother, who agrees to the draw. Which term describes what the mother gives?
opciones: Informed permission
Informed consent
Pediatric assent
Implied consent
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically under 18, cannot give informed consent; parents or legal guardians permit the intervention instead, and that process is called informed permission. Assent is what the child may add, valuable when reasonable. The exception to the rule is the legally emancipated minor, who consents alone.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Preparing Medications, Vials
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.h(i)
preguntas.pregunta: Why is air pushed into a vial before the medication is drawn out of it?
opciones: A vial is a closed system, and the air maintains the pressure gradient inside
The air pushes the rubber seal outward so that the needle pierces it easily
The air is what dissolves a powdered medication before it can be drawn up
The air replaces what was lost from the vial when its plastic cap came off
preguntas.explicacion: A vial is a closed system, so air matching the amount to be withdrawn is injected first to keep the pressure gradient that lets the solution come out. The vial is then turned upside down above the syringe and the plunger drawn to the mark, with the needle tip kept inside the medication and any large bubbles purged. A multi-dose vial is labeled with the date it was opened; a single-use vial is discarded after one use.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in acute kidney failure has produced no urine at all. Which term names that finding, and how is it built?
opciones: Anuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Dysuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Polyuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Nocturia: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
preguntas.explicacion: The prefix a- or an- means without or lacking, and the ending -uria means in the urine, so anuria is the absence of urine. The distractors reuse the same ending with other prefixes: dys- is difficult or abnormal, and poly- is many or excessive, which is why polyuria is a large output rather than none.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of roots would you expect to see in the terms used by a cardiology practice?
opciones: cardi/o for the heart, angi/o for a vessel, phleb/o for a vein
cardi/o for the heart, aden/o for a vessel, hepat/o for a vein
coron/o for the heart, arthr/o for a vessel, nephr/o for a vein
my/o for the heart, thromb/o for a vessel, splen/o for a vein
preguntas.explicacion: Cardi- and coron- both name the heart, angi- and vasculo- name a blood vessel, and phleb- and ven- name a vein. The roots in the wrong answers belong elsewhere: aden- is a gland, hepat- the liver, arthr- a joint, nephr- the kidney, thromb- a clot and splen- the spleen.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Skeletal System: Classification of Bones
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A report describes the femur as a long bone and a carpal as a short bone. What separates the two classes?
opciones: A long bone is longer than it is wide; a short bone is roughly cube shaped
A long bone is thicker than it is wide; a short bone is thin and curved
A long bone has spongy tissue only; a short bone has compact tissue only
A long bone is found in the limbs only; a short bone is found in the skull
preguntas.explicacion: Bones fall into four shapes. Long bones are longer than they are wide, with a shaft and two bulky ends, and make up the thigh, leg, arm and forearm. Short bones are about as tall as they are wide, like the wrist and ankle bones. Flat bones are thin and curved, as in most of the cranium, and the rest are irregular.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Heart Block
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a Mobitz type II block carry more weight than a Mobitz type I?
opciones: It sits below the node and usually calls for a permanent pacemaker
It sits above the node and usually settles without any treatment
It drops every second beat, which the type I block never does
It stretches the PR interval, which the type I block never does
preguntas.explicacion: Type II usually arises below the atrioventricular node, at the level of the His bundle. It signals heart disease severe enough that it can go on to become a complete block, and it usually calls for a pacemaker, while most patients with type I have no symptoms at all.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2L k15 k40 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient is slow to answer the pre-draw questions. What should you do?
opciones: Slow down, give him time to process, and do not interrupt him
Fill each silence by suggesting the answer you think is likely
Ask the questions in rapid succession so he finishes before tiring
Skip the interview and rely on what the requisition already says
preguntas.explicacion: Avoid hurrying an older patient: some struggle with rapid-fire questioning or with torrents of information, so speak more slowly, allow time to process, and do not interrupt, since a patient who gets interrupted tends to hold back the rest of his concerns. Supplying the answers, or skipping the interview, loses the allergy, fainting and fasting information the WHO interview exists to collect.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, metastasis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Breast cancer has spread to the lung. Which cells does the pathologist find in the lung tumor?
opciones: Breast cancer cells, because a metastasis keeps the type of the primary tumor
Lung cancer cells, because a metastasis takes the type of the organ it reaches
A mix of both, because a metastasis blends the primary and the new tissue
Neither, because a metastasis is made of scar tissue rather than tumor cells
preguntas.explicacion: In a metastasis, cancer cells leave the site where they first grew and settle somewhere else in the body: they break away from the primary tumor, ride the blood or the lymph system, and start a new tumor. That new growth is the same type of cancer as the original, so breast cancer in the lung is still breast cancer.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 6.1 Equipment Precautions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: A lead wire on the machine is found with frayed insulation. What is done?
opciones: The unit is left unused and the problem is reported at once
The unit is used and the wire is taped up for the rest of the day
The back of the unit is opened so the wire can be replaced
The unit is used for the limb leads until a repair is arranged
preguntas.explicacion: The unit is grounded, so a shock is highly unlikely, but the rule is firm: if a short happens or frayed wiring turns up, the equipment is not used. The cover and the back are never removed by the technician, and the damage is reported straight away.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Avoidance of contaminated phlebotomy equipment
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality · CPT D3 3B k54 k58 · D1 1K k32 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why single-use lancing devices and glucose meters are never shared between patients without cleaning.
opciones: Blood-contaminated devices have been implicated in hepatitis B outbreaks
Shared devices lose their calibration and read the glucose far too low
Shared devices carry latex particles from one patient's skin to the next
Shared devices void the manufacturer's warranty on the meter and lancets
preguntas.explicacion: Reusable finger-prick devices and point-of-care instruments such as glucose meters, once contaminated with blood, have been linked to outbreaks of hepatitis B. The rule that follows is plain: common-use items are visibly clean before they touch a patient, and single-use items are not reused.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Airway Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found unresponsive at the bottom of a staircase and a neck injury is suspected. How is the airway opened?
opciones: By pushing the jaw forward without tilting the head or turning the neck
By tilting the head back and lifting the chin with two fingers
By turning the head to one side so that the tongue falls forward
By placing a folded towel under the shoulders to extend the neck
preguntas.explicacion: Where an injury to the cervical spine has not been ruled out, the jaw goes forward and the head is left alone, and the mouth is not allowed to close. The head tilt-chin lift is the standard maneuver only when no spinal injury is suspected. A patient with a possible spinal injury is moved by two people so head and neck do not twist.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether electricity will be passed through the body. What is the answer?
opciones: No: the test is painless and no current is sent through
Yes: a small current goes through and may feel like a tingle
Yes: a current is sent only while the chest leads record
No: but the patches themselves can give a mild shock
preguntas.explicacion: The machine listens rather than stimulates: the test is painless and nothing passes into the patient. The electrodes can feel cold as they go on, and in rare cases a rash or irritation appears where the patches were, which is worth saying in advance.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(i) and (b)(3)(ii), application to laboratories
preguntas.subtema: Labels on incoming containers · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: The label on a drum of laboratory reagent is smeared and hard to read. What does the Hazard Communication standard require of the laboratory?
opciones: Labels on incoming containers must not be removed or defaced
Labels may be replaced with the in-house number of the reagent
Labels may be taken off once the sheet is filed in the binder
Labels must be covered with tape until the drum is emptied out
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are covered by the Hazard Communication standard in a reduced way, and the first of those duties is that nobody removes or defaces the label a container of hazardous chemicals arrives with. The others are keeping the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments and making them readily accessible during each work shift, and giving employees the information and training of paragraph (h). Filing the sheet does not release the container from carrying its own warning.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who needs as much support as possible is being taught to walk on crutches. Which gait pattern gives it?
opciones: The four-point gait: left crutch, right leg, right crutch, then left leg
The two-point gait: left crutch with right leg, then right crutch with left leg
The swing-to gait: both crutches forward, then both legs brought up to them
The three-point gait: both crutches with the injured leg, then the sound leg
preguntas.explicacion: Of the patterns taught, the four-point provides the most support: each crutch and each leg moves on its own, one at a time. The two-point pairs a crutch with the opposite leg, the swing-to sends both crutches out and then both legs, and the three-point — the one used most often — moves both crutches with the injured leg.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Vitamins; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Vitamins (002399)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(e) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How many essential vitamins does the body require, and how are they grouped?
opciones: Thirteen, grouped as fat-soluble and water-soluble
Thirteen, grouped as animal-source and plant-source
Nine, grouped as fat-soluble and water-soluble
Twenty, grouped as essential and conditionally essential
preguntas.explicacion: Thirteen vitamins are essential, meaning the body cannot work properly without them, and they split into two groups by how they dissolve: fat-soluble and water-soluble. Nine is the count of the water-soluble group alone. A few vitamin-like nutrients, choline and carnitine, are also needed but are not counted among the thirteen.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Definition of Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k104 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: What separates sterilization from every other level of processing used on patient-care items?
opciones: It destroys or eliminates every form of microbial life, bacterial spores included
It wipes out many or all pathogens on an object but leaves bacterial spores alive
It takes visible soil off an object with water plus a detergent or enzymatic product
It lowers the count enough that the object is safe to handle, use or throw away
preguntas.explicacion: Sterilization is meant as an absolute: nothing microbial survives it, spores included. Disinfection stops short of that, since it is not sporicidal. Cleaning only lifts the visible soil off, and decontamination is what makes a used item safe for staff to handle. They are consecutive steps, not synonyms, and only one of them is absolute.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (Preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.8.c(3)
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for culture is collected into a container with boric acid preservative, and the ward also wants a dipstick from the same cup. What should be expected?
opciones: The dipstick leukocyte reagent may be less sensitive and the initial pH altered, though the bacteria are preserved
The dipstick glucose and urobilinogen may read falsely positive, though the bacteria are preserved for culture
The dipstick leukocyte esterase may read falsely negative, and the culture will fail to grow at any concentration
The dipstick albumin may read falsely positive, and the bacteria will be killed within the first hour of storage
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the preservative chosen when the bacteria in a urine specimen have to stay alive, but it charges for that: the leukocyte pad on the strip loses sensitivity, the starting pH shifts, and too high a concentration will stop the very growth the culture is after. False-positive glucose and urobilinogen are the formaldehyde pattern, a false-negative leukocyte esterase belongs to mercury salts, and thymol is the one that fakes albumin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Other Routes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(5) · RMA III.G.4.d(vii)
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a drug taken by inhalation act quickly?
opciones: It crosses the wide surface of the respiratory epithelium into pulmonary circulation
It is swallowed with the saliva and taken up by the very vascular gastric mucosa
It diffuses through the single-layered epithelium of the nasal passage into the veins
It is absorbed by the small intestine, whose surface is the largest one in the body
preguntas.explicacion: An inhaled drug spreads over the large surface of the respiratory tract and passes into the pulmonary circulation, entering the systemic circulation through the pulmonary vein and skipping first-pass metabolism. Particles of roughly 1 to 10 micrometers deliver best, and how much arrives also depends on the patient's tidal volume and inspiratory velocity. The nasal epithelium is a separate route with its own path.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient needs HLA tissue typing (ACD tube), a CBC and a plasma glucose. Following the WHO table, which tube is filled second?
opciones: The pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing
The purple EDTA hematology tube for the CBC
The light gray sodium fluoride tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 puts EDTA at position 8, the pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies at position 9, and the gray oxalate/fluoride glucose tube at position 10. The purple tube therefore goes first, the ACD tube second and the gray tube last. No heparin tube is ordered here, and it would sit at position 6 in any case.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Opioid Analgesics", Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has just received an opioid analgesic becomes very drowsy and breathes slowly. Which class effect is this?
opciones: Respiratory depression, one of the effects opioid receptors produce everywhere
Serotonin syndrome, which follows any single opioid dose within a few minutes
Hyperalgesia from opioids, which shows up with the first dose in most patients
Anticholinergic toxicity, seen as dry mouth, retention and slowed breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Opioid receptors sit both inside and outside the nervous system, so the class produces effects across the body: sedation, dysphoria or euphoria, slowed breathing, bradycardia, itching, nausea and vomiting, constipation and pinpoint pupils. Tolerance and hyperalgesia belong to long-term use, not to a first dose, and serotonin syndrome needs a serotonergic opioid together with another serotonergic drug.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3; and Section 3.2.2, Choice of gauge
preguntas.subtema: Site selection and device choice · CPT D2 k53 · D3 k55 · PBT II.E II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Besides confirming that a vein is suitable, what practical decision does the WHO say locating the vein helps the phlebotomist make?
opciones: The correct size of needle to use
Whether a tourniquet is needed
How many tubes one puncture yields
Which antiseptic to apply
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says that the vein should be visible without the tourniquet and that locating it will help in determining the correct needle size; Chapter 3 repeats that the gauge is chosen to fit comfortably into the most prominent vein. The antiseptic is fixed at 70% alcohol for routine draws, and the WHO does not tie the number of tubes to the vein found.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes microaggressions from macroaggressions?
opciones: Micro: brief everyday slights between individuals; macro: overt and rooted in systems
Micro: always intentional insults; macro: unconscious and unintended snubs
Micro: cause no measurable harm; macro: the only form that causes real harm
Micro: only spoken remarks; macro: only physical acts of exclusion
preguntas.explicacion: Macroaggressions are overt, radical discrimination embedded in a society or a system, with internment camps and the Tuskegee study as examples. Microaggressions are the brief everyday insults and snubs, usually unintended and springing from bias the person is unaware of, delivered in words or without them, one to one. Repeated microaggressions do documented harm.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Innate Resistance of Microorganisms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Setting prions aside, which organisms sit at the top of the resistance scale to chemical germicides?
opciones: Bacterial spores, above coccidia, mycobacteria, small nonlipid viruses, fungi and vegetative bacteria
Mycobacteria, above bacterial spores, coccidia, fungi, vegetative bacteria and small nonlipid viruses
Lipid viruses, above vegetative bacteria, fungi, mycobacteria, coccidia and the bacterial spores
Vegetative bacteria, above fungi, small nonlipid viruses, mycobacteria, coccidia and lipid viruses
preguntas.explicacion: Bacterial spores hold the highest innate resistance of all, and the ladder descends from them through coccidia, mycobacteria, small nonlipid viruses, fungi, vegetative bacteria and finally lipid or medium-sized viruses such as herpes and HIV. Each group resists for its own reason: the spore coat and cortex act as a barrier, and mycobacteria have a waxy wall.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A resting strip on a young competitive athlete is regular at 52 per minute with normal P waves. How does the material read that?
opciones: As sinus bradycardia, common in athletes and during sleep
As sinus arrhythmia, common in athletes and during sleep
As a junctional rhythm, common in athletes while resting
As a first-degree block, common in athletes while resting
preguntas.explicacion: A slow sinus rhythm turns up by chance in plenty of healthy adults, and it is described as common in athletes and during sleep, where the vagal tone that slows the sinus node is higher. Every criterion of sinus rhythm still holds except the rate.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities (2008), Factors Affecting Efficacy
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Spaulding showed that killing ten spores took 30 minutes while killing 100,000 took 3 hours. What does that demonstrate?
opciones: The larger the microbial load, the longer a germicide needs, which is why cleaning matters
The larger the microbial load, the more concentrated the germicide has to be to work at all
Spores multiply inside a germicide bath, so the exposure has to outrun their growth rate
Exposure time counts more than the germicide chosen, so any product works if left long enough
preguntas.explicacion: With every other condition held constant, more microbes means more time to destroy them. That is the argument for scrupulous cleaning before disinfection or sterilization: cutting the number of organisms that must be inactivated widens the margin of safety and shortens the exposure needed to kill the whole load. Clumped cells are also harder to inactivate than separated ones.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.4 Postexamination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k150 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old patient with thin, fragile skin has just finished a recording. How are the electrodes taken off?
opciones: The wires come off first, then each electrode by its tab
The electrodes come off first, then the wires from the tabs
The wires and the electrodes come away together in one pull
The wires stay attached until all the copies have printed
preguntas.explicacion: The lead wires are lifted off the electrodes first, and only then is each electrode removed by pulling gently on its tab; they are thrown away after that single use. The step is done carefully because it can hurt and injure the skin, above all in older patients.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR is ordered along with a CBC. Which tube is used for the ESR specimen, and can it be shared with other tests?
opciones: It goes in a black-top ESR tube with 3.2% citrate or a lavender EDTA tube, and is not shared with other tests
It goes in the same lavender EDTA tube as the CBC, and the leftover blood is used for the sedimentation
It goes in a light blue citrate tube filled to 90%, and it can be shared with any PT ordered on the same draw
It goes in a plain red tube, and the serum is transferred to the Westergren tube in the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The blood usually goes into a black-top ESR vacuum tube holding 3.2% sodium citrate; whole blood in a lavender EDTA tube is also acceptable, and the sample must stay in its own ESR-designated tube because of the volume the test needs, so it cannot be shared. The test is run on anticoagulated whole blood, never on serum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ventricular Fibrillation", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which two rhythms are shockable?
opciones: Ventricular tachycardia without a pulse, and ventricular fibrillation
Ventricular fibrillation and asystole after two minutes of CPR
Atrial fibrillation, and ventricular tachycardia without a pulse
Asystole and pulseless electrical activity with a slow rate
preguntas.explicacion: Once either of those two is recognized, the patient is defibrillated at once, with 120 to 200 joules on a biphasic device or 360 joules on a monophasic one. Speed matters: survival was 39.3% with prompt defibrillation against 22.2% when it was delayed by two minutes or more.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which combination of vital signs makes up Cushing's triad?
opciones: Irregular respirations, high blood pressure and a slow pulse
Irregular respirations, low blood pressure and a fast pulse
Rapid shallow respirations, high blood pressure and a fast pulse
Rapid deep respirations, low blood pressure and a slow pulse
preguntas.explicacion: The triad is irregular breathing, hypertension and bradycardia, and it is the body's answer to rising intracranial pressure. It signals that herniation of the brain is near and calls for immediate action, which is why the three values are read together and not one at a time.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Recordkeeping, Updates to OSHA's Recordkeeping Rule
preguntas.subtema: Reporting severe injuries to OSHA · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.11.c / 2027 I.B.10.c · RMA II.B.7.d III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: How quickly must an employer report a work-related fatality, and a work-related inpatient hospitalization, to OSHA?
opciones: A fatality within 8 hours; a hospitalization within 24 hours
A fatality within 24 hours; a hospitalization within 8 hours
Both within 72 hours, by telephone to the area office
Both within 60 days, on the OSHA 300A summary
preguntas.explicacion: Under the recordkeeping rule updated in 2015, as summarized in OSHA's Hospitals eTool, employers report every work-related fatality within 8 hours of learning of it, and every work-related inpatient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours. Reports can be made by phone to the nearest area office, to the 24-hour OSHA hotline at 1-800-321-6742, or through the online serious event form. The 300A summary is an annual posting, not a reporting channel, and 60 days is the HIPAA breach notification limit.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(iii) and (h)(2)(i) to (h)(2)(iii), application to laboratories
preguntas.subtema: The laboratory exception · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which piece of hazard communication information does a laboratory employer NOT have to give its employees?
opciones: Where the written hazard communication program is kept and how to see it
The operations that involve hazardous chemicals in their own work area
The measures they can take to protect themselves from those chemicals
What the Hazard Communication standard itself requires
preguntas.explicacion: Employees have to be told what the standard requires, which operations in the area they work in involve hazardous chemicals, and where the written program with its chemical list and data sheets can be found and consulted. Laboratories receive the information and training of paragraph (h) with one item struck out, namely where to find that written program, because their reduced coverage does not oblige them to have one. Everything else still applies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Foreign Body Airway Obstruction", History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room stands up clutching the throat with both hands and cannot speak. What does this show?
opciones: The universal sign of a blocked airway, which calls for immediate first aid
The first sign of a heart attack, which calls for rest and for chewed aspirin
A panic attack with hyperventilation, which calls for slow, coached breathing
A seizure that begins with a cry, which calls for protecting the head
preguntas.explicacion: Grabbing the neck with both hands is the universal choking sign. Sudden respiratory distress with coughing, gagging or stridor, an inability to speak or cry, and cyanosis point to a foreign body in the airway and call for action, because severe hypoxia leads to loss of consciousness within minutes.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient is admitted to hospital in February and again in September. How often may she owe the 2026 Part A deductible?
opciones: Twice, since $1,736 falls due for each benefit period and there is no yearly cap
Once, since $1,736 is a yearly deductible in the way the Part B deductible is
Twice, but at $283 each time, which is the figure the yearly deductible uses
Not at all, since days one to sixty of an inpatient stay carry no charge
preguntas.explicacion: The 2026 Part A deductible is $1,736 for each inpatient benefit period before Original Medicare begins to pay, and there is no limit on how many benefit periods a person may have in one year, so the deductible can fall due more than once. Days one to sixty cost nothing only after that deductible has been paid.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i) and (c)(2)(ii), Exposure determination; OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: The two exposure lists · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A housekeeper handles regulated waste bags twice a week, while every phlebotomist is exposed daily. How does the exposure determination list them?
opciones: Phlebotomists as a classification where all are exposed; the housekeeper with the task
Both as classifications where all employees are exposed, with no list of tasks needed
Only the phlebotomists, because the housekeeper wears gloves for that one task
Both by name in the medical record, which is where exposed workers are recorded
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(i) asks for three lists: job classifications in which every employee has occupational exposure, job classifications in which only some do, and the tasks or groups of related tasks that expose the people in that second group. Handling regulated waste is exactly such a task. Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) adds that the determination is made without regard to protective equipment, so gloves never take a job off the list. The medical record of (h)(1) is a separate document kept for each exposed employee, not the determination.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A prescription is written for one tablet BID. How often should the patient take it?
opciones: Two doses a day
One dose a day
Three doses a day
Four doses a day
preguntas.explicacion: The frequency abbreviations on a prescription run in a family that is easy to confuse: BID is twice a day, TID three times a day and QID four times a day, while PRN means the patient takes it only as needed. Reading BID as TID or QID hands the patient an extra dose every day.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient had two beers at 11 p.m.; the fasting draw is at 7 a.m. How does that affect the sample?
opciones: Avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw; note it and tell the provider
It is fine, because eight hours have passed and beer counts only as a liquid
It is fine provided he drinks plain water now to dilute the alcohol
It is fine, because alcohol affects only the liver function tests
preguntas.explicacion: No alcohol is to be drunk in the 24 hours before the procedure, next to the 12-hour fast and the ban on coffee and energy drinks that morning. Eight hours is the glucose fasting minimum, not the alcohol window, and the source attaches this rule to blood sampling in general rather than to any one panel.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b · CCMA 3B4 k65
