preguntas.pregunta: Which crutch is the most common one, and what is it best suited to?
opciones: The axilla crutch, best for short-term use, sending the load to arms and torso
The forearm crutch, best for short-term use, sending the load to the forearms
The platform crutch, best for short-term use, sending the load to the upper arms
The axilla crutch, best for long-term use in a patient with weak upper body strength
preguntas.explicacion: Axilla crutches are the commonest type and are meant for the short term; their design moves most of the body weight onto the arms and the torso, and most facilities send patients home with them. They are a poor choice where the wrists are troublesome, the upper body is weak or coordination is impaired.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and IV access · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart notes a central venous line. According to the WHO, who may draw specimens from it, and what caveat applies?
opciones: Nursing staff and physicians under protocol; such specimens risk contamination or wrong results
Any phlebotomist trained in vacuum systems; the results are equivalent to those of a peripheral draw
No one; central lines may never be used for laboratory specimens under any protocol
Only laboratory technicians; they must draw a non-additive discard tube first
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says nursing staff and doctors may take specimens from a central venous line if they follow the protocols, but that a specimen from a central line risks contamination or a wrong laboratory result. It does not describe them as equivalent to a peripheral draw, does not ban them outright, and does not assign the task to laboratory technicians or prescribe a discard tube.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e / 2027 III.G.6.c · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An office visit has an allowed amount of $100 and the plan's coinsurance is 20%. The patient has already met the deductible. What does she owe?
opciones: $20, and the plan pays the rest of the allowed amount for that visit
$80, and the plan pays the rest of the allowed amount for that visit
$100, because coinsurance applies only after the visit has been billed
$120, because the coinsurance is added on top of the allowed amount
preguntas.explicacion: Coinsurance is the patient's percentage of the allowed amount once the deductible is satisfied: 20% of $100 comes to $20, and the plan covers the remainder. The $80 figure inverts the shares. Paying the whole $100 is what happens before the deductible is met, not after. Nothing is added above the allowed amount by a contracted provider, since that ceiling is the negotiated price.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction (Red)
preguntas.subtema: Specimen preparation · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube with no anticoagulant has been filled. How long may the specimen need before it is spun?
opciones: Usually ten to fifteen minutes, and in some specimens up to an hour
Usually two to three minutes, and in some specimens up to ten minutes
Usually thirty seconds, the same contact time asked of an alcohol swab
Usually twenty-four hours, the interval allowed for a coagulation test
preguntas.explicacion: The red top carries no anticoagulant: contact with the tube wall sets off clotting, and the specimen is normally left ten to fifteen minutes before centrifugation, although clotting time varies and can reach a full hour. Thirty seconds is the alcohol contact time, not a clotting interval.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7 · RMA I.B.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which documents must be kept free of abbreviations because the patient and family receive them?
opciones: Consent forms, discharge instructions and patient rights documents
Handwritten drug orders, preprinted forms and progress notes
Laboratory requisitions, referral letters and imaging reports
Staff schedules, inventory records and equipment logs
preguntas.explicacion: Abbreviations are banned from anything the patient or family will read, including documents on patient rights, informed consent forms and discharge instructions. The point is that people should not have to guess: a patient too embarrassed to ask what an entry means may go home and follow it wrong.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Email Communications and Faxes
preguntas.subtema: Email safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance for email communication with patients?
opciones: Encrypt all emails, keep the patient's name out of the subject line, and send the minimum information
Use a personal commercial email account so the message is not stored on the institution's servers
Put the patient's name in the subject line so the message is easy to locate later
Attach the full record whenever a patient asks a question, to avoid follow-up messages
preguntas.explicacion: Institutions should set email rules: the patient's name is left out of the subject line, the address is verified, only the bare minimum of information is transmitted, a standard disclaimer closes every message, all emails are encrypted, and staff never use personal or commercial accounts for patient communication, only the system the institution provides. Similar rules govern faxes, which sit in a secure area with a cover sheet explaining what to do if the fax is misdirected. Sending a whole record in reply to a question violates the minimum necessary principle.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A note printed directly beneath a three-character code title gives examples of what the category holds. What is that note called?
opciones: An Includes note, which further defines the content of that whole category
An inclusion term, a list of the conditions for which that one code is used
An Excludes2 note, saying the condition is not included but may be coded too
A code also note, saying that two codes may be needed with no order given
preguntas.explicacion: An Includes note is printed directly beneath a three-character code title, either to define the category further or to show what it holds. Inclusion terms are a different device: they list the conditions for which a given code is used, they may be synonyms of the title, and the list is not necessarily exhaustive, since the Index can add more.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient turning 65 asks how many ways there are of taking her Medicare coverage.
opciones: Two: Original Medicare, or a Medicare Advantage plan approved by Medicare
Two: Original Medicare, or a Medigap policy bought from a private insurer
Three: Original Medicare, a Medicare Advantage plan, or a Medigap policy
One: Original Medicare, to which every other coverage is only an addition
preguntas.explicacion: There are two main ways of taking the coverage. Original Medicare is Part A and Part B, to which a separate drug plan and supplemental coverage can be added. The other is Medicare Advantage: a bundled private plan approved by Medicare that holds Part A, Part B and usually Part D, often with extra benefits and a limit on out-of-pocket costs, so that supplemental coverage is not needed alongside it.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex F, Blood spillage
preguntas.subtema: Spill disinfectant · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.6.b / 2027 I.B.5.b · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, which disinfectant is applied after the area has been cleaned with water and detergent?
opciones: Sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, a 1:10 bleach dilution prepared daily
Sodium hypochlorite 5.25 percent, used undiluted straight from the bottle
70 percent alcohol, the same solution used to prepare the skin
Sodium hypochlorite 0.05 percent, a 1:100 dilution, kept for a week
preguntas.explicacion: After the glass is removed with tongs, the fluid absorbed with paper towels and the area wiped with water and detergent until visibly clean, the spill area is saturated again with sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, which is 10,000 parts per million of available chlorine, made as a 1:10 dilution of 5.25 percent household bleach and prepared fresh each day. Undiluted bleach is not the instruction, 70 percent alcohol is WHO's skin antiseptic, and a solution kept for a week defeats the daily preparation rule. Gloves come off last, followed by handwashing and an incident record.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation for CBG · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: Before a fingerstick glucose, an assistant swabs the fingertip with alcohol and lances it while the skin is still wet. Why does the guidance advise against this?
opciones: Residual alcohol can dilute the drop or cause hemolysis, so the site must dry completely first
Alcohol left on the skin makes the meter read falsely high, because ethanol is measured as glucose
Alcohol is not recommended at all; the guidance calls for washing with cold water and no antiseptic
Wet alcohol stings on puncture, which is the only concern, so the result itself is not affected
preguntas.explicacion: The site is washed and dried thoroughly, warm water helping the blood come. Routine use of an alcohol swab is not called for, but where one is used the skin has to dry completely before the lancet fires, since alcohol left behind can dilute the sample or hemolyze it and move the reading. Comfort is not the point; the integrity of the sample is. Cold water is not what the procedure describes.

preguntas.subtema: Qualitative QC: positive and negative · CPT D1 k28 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.1.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A rapid antigen test gives only positive or negative results. Under the nonwaived CLIA control rule, which controls are included each day of testing?
opciones: A negative control material and a positive control material
Two control materials at different concentrations
One control material showing graded or titered reactivity
A calibrator from the same lot used to set the cut-off
preguntas.explicacion: Qualitative procedures require a negative and a positive control material each day patient specimens are examined. Two concentrations are the quantitative rule, and a graded or titered control belongs with tests that report graded or titered results. When calibration material doubles as a control it must come from a different lot than the one used to set the cut-off or calibrate the system.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thiazide Diuretics", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.a · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: Hydrochlorothiazide is prescribed for primary hypertension. Which statement matches the approved use of this class?
opciones: It is approved for primary hypertension, alone or added to other antihypertensives
It is approved for hypertension only once a loop diuretic has failed at a full dose
It is approved for edema only, so any use in hypertension is entirely off-label
It is approved for hypertension only in patients who also have chronic kidney disease
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrochlorothiazide and chlorthalidone are approved for primary hypertension and are used either on their own or alongside other antihypertensives to lift the response in severe cases. The same agents are approved as adjuncts for edema in chronic heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis and corticosteroid or estrogen therapy. Loop diuretics are approved for hypertension too, but they are not the first-line choice.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 1: Identification
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 1 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist needs the supplier's emergency telephone number for a cleaning concentrate. Which section of the safety data sheet has it?
opciones: Section 1, which also gives the product identifier and the recommended use
Section 2, which also gives the signal word and the hazard statements
Section 15, which also gives the regulations that apply to the product
Section 16, which also gives the date the sheet was last revised
preguntas.explicacion: Section 1 identifies the product and whoever answers for it: the product identifier as it appears on the label, along with any synonyms; the name, the address and the telephone of whoever is responsible, be that the manufacturer, the importer or another party; a telephone number for emergencies; and the recommended uses of the chemical together with any restriction on them. Section 15 gathers the regulatory information and section 16 the date of preparation or last revision, and neither helps in the middle of an incident.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: U Wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A small extra wave follows the T wave on a strip. What is it, and what is it linked to?
opciones: A U wave, commonly associated with low potassium
A J wave, commonly associated with low body temperature
An epsilon wave, commonly associated with low potassium
A delta wave, commonly associated with a slow AV node
preguntas.explicacion: The U wave is a small deflection that comes after the T wave and is attributed to late repolarization of the papillary muscles or the Purkinje fibers; it is commonly seen with low potassium. The J or Osborn wave sits at the junction of the QRS complex and the ST segment in hypothermia.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Chemical burn or reaction", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.t · 2027 I.B.8.t · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A cleaning solution splashes onto a patient's arm and burns the skin. How is the area flushed?
opciones: With cool running water for 15 minutes or more, after dry powder is brushed off
With cool running water for 30 seconds, and then a neutralizing rinse
With warm soapy water for 5 minutes, scrubbing until the pain settles
With a wet compress held in place, so that the chemical is not spread
preguntas.explicacion: Any dry chemical is brushed off first, and clothing and jewelry come off; then the skin is flushed with cool running water for 15 minutes or longer. Dry lime and elemental metals such as sodium or potassium are the exceptions to flushing with water. The rescuer wears eye and skin protection and avoids becoming contaminated.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(B) and (C), specimen containers
preguntas.subtema: Secondary containers · CPT D1 k31 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Blood has leaked onto the outside of a specimen tube. What does the standard require before it is transported?
opciones: Place it in a second container that prevents leakage and is labeled or color-coded
Wipe the tube with disinfectant and transport it in the usual rack with a new label
Discard the specimen as regulated waste and request a new draw from the patient
Place it in a puncture-resistant container, which is required for every leaking tube
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(B) says that once the outside of the primary container is contaminated it goes inside a second one, chosen so that nothing escapes while the specimen is handled, processed, stored, transported or shipped, and labeled or color-coded as the standard directs. Puncture resistance comes in under (d)(2)(xiii)(C), and only where the specimen could pierce the primary container, not for every leak. Nothing there tells anyone to discard the specimen, or to wipe the tube instead of using the second container.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Personnel and Training; Personnel Considerations
preguntas.subtema: No CLIA personnel requirements for waived sites · PBT VI.F / VI.C · RMA III.C.1.a.vi
preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, what education or training does a testing person at a Certificate of Waiver site need?
opciones: None is required by CLIA, although state or local personnel rules may apply
A high school diploma plus documented training by the manufacturer
The same qualifications as testing personnel for moderate complexity
Completion of a CMS-approved course before the certificate is issued
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA sets no education or training requirement for the director or the testing personnel of a waived site; in CMS surveys most testing personnel were nurses and medical assistants and only 2 % were trained laboratorians. That freedom is federal only: state or local regulations on personnel must still be met, and good practice calls for documented training and competency before anyone reports patient results.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: HIPAA for telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth and HIPAA · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice is choosing a video platform for telehealth visits. What does HIPAA require of the vendor?
opciones: That it comply with the rules and enter a business associate agreement with the practice
That it store every recorded visit for six years so the practice can produce it later
That it be certified by the Office for Civil Rights before any visit may be scheduled
That it encrypt the video only when the patient asks for that protection in advance
preguntas.explicacion: Every telehealth service a covered provider or plan delivers has to comply with the HIPAA Rules. On the technology side the requirement is that the provider work with vendors who comply and who will sign a HIPAA business associate agreement covering whatever video or other remote communication product is used for the visits.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is an electronic health record (EHR)?
preguntas.subtema: EHR components · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which content does an electronic health record contain, according to ONC?
opciones: History, diagnoses, medications, immunization dates, allergies, imaging and test results
Only the notes written by the clinician who owns the practice where the record is kept
Only the data elements a health plan needs to adjudicate a claim for the encounter
Only the documents the patient has personally uploaded through the practice portal
preguntas.explicacion: An EHR is described as the digital counterpart of the paper chart: real time, centred on the patient, available instantly and securely to whoever is authorized. Inside it live the medical history, the diagnoses, the medications, treatment plans, dates of immunizations, allergies, radiology images, and results from the laboratory and from other tests. It also opens access to evidence-based decision tools and takes the friction out of the clinician's workflow.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · CMA I.A.1.g · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which tool assesses pain in an infant by watching face, legs, activity, cry and consolability?
opciones: The revised FLACC observation tool, for infants and young children
The Behavioral Pain Scale, built for adults who are sedated or unconscious
The Nonverbal Pain Scale, built for intubated adults in intensive care units
The visual analog scale, on which a mark is placed along a printed line
preguntas.explicacion: Observational tools take the place of self-report in patients who cannot speak for themselves. The one built on face, legs, activity, cry and consolability serves infants and young children, and it is validated too for children who are nonverbal because of neurologic impairment. The other observational scales listed are for adults.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · RMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: An order uses cc for volume and the microgram symbol for a dose. What is recommended in their place?
opciones: mL instead of cc, and mcg instead of the microgram symbol
mL instead of cc, and mg instead of the microgram symbol
unit instead of cc, and mcg instead of the microgram symbol
cm instead of cc, and nanogram instead of the microgram symbol
preguntas.explicacion: Cubic centimeters written as cc is mistaken for u, meaning units, so mL is used instead. The microgram symbol is mistaken for mg, which is a thousand-fold difference, so mcg is written. Nanogram appears on the same list because it is read as mg and as nasogastric, and the fix there is to spell the word out. Writing unit fixes neither of the two abbreviations in this order.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (tourniquet application)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A muscular patient has very prominent, easily visible veins. What is the guidance on tourniquet use in this case?
opciones: Avoiding the tourniquet is recommended when the veins are prominent
The tourniquet is still mandatory, applied about 3 inches above the site
A tighter tourniquet is used, because large veins collapse under vacuum
The tourniquet is applied only after the first tube has been filled
preguntas.explicacion: Controversy remains about tourniquets in blood sampling, and avoiding them, above all in patients whose veins stand out, is recommended; otherwise a disposable tourniquet goes about 3 inches above the site. It does not describe the tourniquet as mandatory, does not call for extra tightness, and does not delay application until after the first tube.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Risk of Infection After Exposure
preguntas.subtema: HIV transmission risk · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick with blood from an HIV-positive source, what does the CDC give as the average chance of infection?
opciones: About 0.3 percent, roughly 1 in 300
About 1.8 percent, roughly 1 in 55
About 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source
About 0.1 percent, roughly 1 in 1,000
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's brochure gives 0.3 percent, about 1 in 300, as the average risk of HIV infection from a needlestick or cut involving infected blood, which is to say that 99.7 percent of them lead to nothing. A splash into the eye, the nose or the mouth carries roughly 0.1 percent, 1 in 1,000, and non-intact skin less than that. The 1.8 percent figure is the average for hepatitis C after a needlestick, and 6 to 30 percent is the hepatitis B range in someone susceptible.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Routine sputum culture (003723), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Sputum quality · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.3 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · RMA III.C.4.a.v · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands in a sputum cup holding a few milliliters of clear, watery fluid from the mouth. What should the medical assistant do?
opciones: Ask for a new specimen coughed up deeply, because thin, clear material is rejected
Send it as it is, because any material from the mouth still carries airway organisms
Add sterile saline to the cup and send it, because the volume is what was too small
Refrigerate it and send it the next morning, when a fresh specimen can be added to it
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is what a deep cough brings up from the air passages, not spit. The thicker it is, the likelier it truly represents lower respiratory secretions and carries the organism causing the infection, and many laboratories refuse a clear, runny sample for microscopy or culture. Volume and quality are both judged, and the collection can be repeated until there is 10 to 20 mL of it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: How to make a splint — First Aid; and DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.iv · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: An injured finger is being immobilized in the field and no rigid support is at hand. What is the alternative?
opciones: Tape it to the finger beside it, which is called buddy taping
Tape it flat against the palm so the joint cannot bend at all
Pull it straight first and then wrap it against the next finger
Wrap it tightly with cloth strips until the swelling settles down
preguntas.explicacion: An injured part can be taped to an uninjured one to stop it moving, and taping a hurt finger to the finger next to it is the example given for that technique, called buddy taping. Whatever position the injured part was found in is the position it gets splinted in, and ties are never drawn tight enough to cut off the circulation.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.1 Eligibility Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair is sent for a tracing. What decides whether it goes ahead?
opciones: Whether the patient can move onto the table alone or with help
Whether the patient can stand unaided all through the recording
Whether a provider signs off on the extra assistance beforehand
Whether the tracing can be recorded with the patient still seated
preguntas.explicacion: Nobody is automatically excluded from the test. For a patient in a wheelchair the question is only the transfer: it goes ahead if the person can get onto the examination table alone or with help from whoever usually lifts them.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4c: Common Metric Conversions in Health Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(2) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7
preguntas.pregunta: A dose is ordered per kilogram and the patient's weight is recorded in pounds. Which equivalence is used?
opciones: 1 kilogram equals 2.2 pounds
1 kilogram equals 1.2 pounds
1 kilogram equals 16 pounds
1 kilogram equals 10 pounds
preguntas.explicacion: One kilogram is 2.2 pounds, and it is also 1000 grams. Weight-based doses are calculated on the metric weight, in kilograms for children and adults and in grams for newborns, which is why the weight belongs on the order whenever the dose depends on it. The 16 in the household table is the number of ounces in a pound, not a conversion between pounds and kilograms.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Growth chart
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old was at the 75th percentile for weight, moved to the 25th at 9 months and lower at 12 months. Why does that worry the provider?
opciones: The measurements are no longer tracking one curve, which matters more than any single value
The 25th percentile is below the normal range, so a single value there is the concern
Weight percentiles are expected to climb steadily, so any fall at all is abnormal
The child has crossed into the band that defines undernutrition on the charts
preguntas.explicacion: What raises concern on a chart is a measurement that stops following its own line, or one that stays below the 10th or above the 90th percentile for the age. A single value at the 25th percentile is not itself abnormal; a toddler can lose weight after a bout of diarrhea and regain it. Abnormal growth is a sign, not a diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: Layman's terms · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2C k19 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: After explaining a condition in everyday words, what three things should be checked with the patient?
opciones: The health issue, what to do about it, and why acting matters
The diagnosis, the dose of each drug, and the next appointment
The health issue, the cost of the visit, and whom to call later
The diagnosis, the address of the referral, and pharmacy hours
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told not to assume patients know medical terminology, to use simple common language, to ask whether anything needs clarifying, and then to check that three things have landed: what the health issue is, what the patient has to do, and why acting matters. Doses, costs and addresses may all be discussed, but they are not that three-part check.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: Good Samaritan rule
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(4) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A bystander with no duty to act stops to help at a roadside crash. What does the Good Samaritan rule say about that?
opciones: Taking charge assumes a duty to use reasonable care from then on
Taking charge carries no duty at all, since the help was voluntary
Taking charge creates liability only if payment was later accepted
Taking charge is barred unless the helper is licensed in that state
preguntas.explicacion: Under the rule, someone who provides services for another, whether free or for pay, assumes a duty to use reasonable care, and can be held liable if their negligence injures the person helped or a foreseeable third party. At common law a bystander has no moral or legal duty to help if they did not cause the injury, but once they take charge of a helpless person that duty attaches.

preguntas.subtema: History and physical timing · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: When must a history and physical examination be completed for a patient scheduled for surgery under anesthesia?
opciones: Within the 30 days before admission or the 24 hours after it, and before the procedure
Within the 7 days before admission or the 48 hours after it, and before the procedure
No more than 90 days before admission, with no deadline once the patient arrives
At any point during the stay, provided it is filed within 30 days after discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The record has to show a history and physical done and written up within the 30 days that precede admission or registration or the 24 hours that follow it, and in every case before surgery or any procedure needing anesthesia. It goes into the record inside 24 hours of admission and before that procedure. If the examination was done in the preceding 30 days, an update noting any change is required on the same clock.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(d) and (e), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT VI.F (CLIA) · CCMA 3E15 k146 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician's office asks the laboratory for the reference interval it uses for a test and for a list of substances that interfere with the assay. What does CLIA say?
opciones: Reference intervals must be available to the ordering person, and information affecting interpretation, like interferences, is given on request
Reference intervals are proprietary to the performing laboratory; only the manufacturer's package insert may be shared with the laboratory's clients
Reference intervals must be printed on every report, but interference data are released only to CMS or its agent on request
Reference intervals and interference data are provided only when the laboratory holds a certificate of accreditation from CAP
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1291(d) it is the performing laboratory that decides which reference intervals, or normal values, are pertinent, and they must reach both the authorized person who ordered the test and whoever uses the result. Paragraph (e) adds that the laboratory must, on request, make its list of test methods and performance specifications available, and must supply information affecting interpretation, test interferences being the example given, updating it whenever a change affects results.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a flexible spending account is accurate?
opciones: It is an employer arrangement, and the amount put in is not taxed to the employee
It is an employer arrangement, and only the employer may decide the amount put in
It is a bank arrangement open to people enrolled in a high deductible plan
It is a plan arrangement that raises the yearly limit on covered dental services
preguntas.explicacion: A flexible spending account is set up through the employer and lets the worker pay out-of-pocket costs, such as copayments, deductibles and prescription drugs, with money that is not taxed. The employee decides the amount, up to a ceiling the employer sets. Accounts opened at a bank for anyone with a qualifying plan describe the health savings account, and no spending account changes what benefits the health plan covers.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Use only acceptable language access services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which parts of a practice does the toolkit say have to be covered by language access services?
opciones: Scheduling, signage, front desk, the visit, billing and follow-up messages
Only the clinical visit, where medical information is actually exchanged
Only the front desk and the signage, where written English predominates
Only scheduling and billing, where the written records are generated
preguntas.explicacion: Language access services come in where the patient, or a companion taking part, would rather use a language that is not English, and every part of the practice that needs them is to be considered: booking the appointment, the signage, the front desk, the clinical visit, billing, secure messaging, patient portals, follow-up communication and patient feedback.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT) Test, What is a PTT test?; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician orders a prothrombin time and a partial thromboplastin time on the same patient. Why are the two so often ordered together?
opciones: Each measures a different group of the clotting factors
One is run on serum and the other on citrated plasma
One monitors warfarin and the other monitors aspirin
One is drawn first in the order and the other is drawn last
preguntas.explicacion: The PTT checks one group of clotting factors and the PT checks factors that the PTT does not reach, so the two results are read against each other for a full picture of how the blood is clotting. The PTT is also the test used to watch a patient on heparin. Both are collected in the light blue citrate tube and both are run on plasma, not serum.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Blood Glucose Test, section What happens during a blood glucose test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A pregnant patient booked for a glucose challenge test asks whether she must fast. What is the answer?
opciones: No fasting; she drinks the glucose and one sample is drawn an hour later
Fast at least 8 hours; samples are drawn before and 2 hours after the drink
Fast 9 to 12 hours; the test is normally scheduled for the morning
No fasting; a single sample reflects her average glucose over 3 months
preguntas.explicacion: The glucose challenge test used to screen for gestational diabetes needs no fasting: the patient drinks a sugary drink and blood is taken one hour later; a high result leads to an oral glucose tolerance test, which does require fasting and repeated samples. The 9-to-12-hour fast is for cholesterol and the 3-month average is the A1C.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: Patient-initiated e-mail · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes to the office from her own e-mail account asking about her results. What may the office assume?
opciones: That e-mail is acceptable to her, unless she has said otherwise
That she has waived every privacy right she holds over those results
That the message may be forwarded to any provider treating her
That she has consented to receive marketing messages from the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may open the conversation by e-mail themselves, and where they do the provider is entitled to take it that e-mail suits them, unless the patient has said otherwise in so many words. If the provider suspects she may not grasp the risks of unencrypted e-mail, or is worried about liability, the guidance is to alert her to those risks and let her decide whether to go on.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Functional Elements of a Lawsuit; StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Tort Liability Pathway
preguntas.subtema: Elements of malpractice · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: Which four elements must a patient prove to win a medical malpractice suit?
opciones: Duty, breach of duty (negligence), causation and damages
Assault, battery, negligence and abandonment
Intent, foreseeability, restitution and injunction
Duty, consent, documentation and insurance coverage
preguntas.explicacion: A simple mistake is not malpractice by itself. The plaintiff must establish four elements: a duty to the patient, meaning the clinician was responsible for that patient's care; a breach of that duty, the negligence, measured against the standard of care; causation, that the act or omission produced the bad outcome; and damages, the loss for which compensation is sought. The tort pathway states it the same way, duty, breach, proximate cause, damages. Assault, battery and abandonment are separate torts, and restitution and injunctions are remedies.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers; and Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage plan asks whether the plan is allowed to cover less than Original Medicare does.
opciones: No, because the plan has to give at least the coverage Original Medicare gives
Yes, because the plan may drop benefits so long as it lowers her premium too
Yes, because the plan may drop the benefits that fall under Part B rather than A
No, because the plan has to give the same coverage and charge the same amounts
preguntas.explicacion: Rules of its own are allowed to a Medicare Advantage plan, or to any other Medicare plan, but it has to deliver at least the coverage Original Medicare delivers. Cost is where it differs: those plans usually carry different out-of-pocket amounts, a yearly limit among them that Original Medicare has no equivalent for, and most add benefits Original Medicare leaves out, such as vision, hearing and dental care.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Eye Instillations, Eye Ointment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k70 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii)
preguntas.pregunta: How is an eye ointment applied?
opciones: Half an inch into the lower conjunctival sac, running from the inner canthus outward
Half an inch along the upper eyelid margin, running from the outer canthus inward
A thin line over the closed eyelid, which the patient then rubs in with one finger
One drop's worth into the lower sac, with the tube tip resting on the lower eyelid
preguntas.explicacion: Eye ointment follows the same steps as an eye drop, except that half an inch of ointment is laid into the lower conjunctival sac, and the line runs from the inner canthus outward. The patient then closes the lid and moves the eye so the ointment spreads and is absorbed, and should be warned that vision will be blurry for a few minutes. Nothing, dropper or tube, is allowed to touch the eye.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.2
preguntas.subtema: Functional downtime · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Staff complain that the record system takes half a minute to open a chart, though it has never stopped. How does the contingency guidance classify that?
opciones: As a functional downtime, which is to be identified and addressed proactively
As a security incident, which is documented and reported with its outcome
As an EHR limitation, which is recorded on the worksheet and left to the vendor
As a planned downtime, which is announced to users before the work begins
preguntas.explicacion: Unacceptably slow response time counts as a functional system downtime even though the system is running. It matters because delay invites type-ahead errors, where keystrokes the user has already made land in whatever field opens next, so the guidance asks organizations to measure response times and give users an easy way to report them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypertensive Crisis", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which feature separates a hypertensive emergency from a hypertensive urgency?
opciones: Acute organ damage is present in the emergency and absent in the urgency
Acute organ damage is absent in the emergency and present in the urgency
The emergency is defined by a systolic reading above 140 mm Hg
The urgency is defined by a diastolic reading above 120 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: A hypertensive crisis is a severe, sudden rise in blood pressure. It counts as an emergency when acute hypertension-mediated organ damage comes with it, and as an urgency when it does not. Numbers such as 180 over 120 are conventions rather than firm lines, and how fast the pressure rose can matter more than how high it is.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told that two out of ten people gain weight on a new medicine, rather than that few people have side effects. What principle is that?
opciones: Being specific and concrete instead of using vague, subjective terms
Being reassuring, so the patient is not frightened out of the treatment
Being thorough, so every possible side effect is named at least once
Being brief, so the explanation fits inside a fifteen-minute visit
preguntas.explicacion: Vague words get read differently by different people, so clear communication asks for specific, concrete wording: a number instead of "few". The same set of habits covers plain nonmedical language, using the patient's own words, slowing the pace, drawing pictures, demonstrating, and then checking with teach-back.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: How to make a sling — First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.2.d · NCMA 2B.13 · RMA III.H.3.a.iv
preguntas.pregunta: A sling is being applied after a splint. How should the arm sit inside it?
opciones: Elbow at about a right angle, with the hand higher than the elbow
Elbow at about a right angle, with the hand lower than the elbow
Elbow fully extended, with the whole forearm resting along the cloth
Elbow at about a right angle, with the wrist left outside the cloth
preguntas.explicacion: The elbow goes at the point of the triangle and the wrist along the middle of its lower edge, and the sling is adjusted so the hand rides above the elbow, which limits swelling, with the elbow bent to roughly ninety degrees. The knot is tied at the side of the neck and padded. The splint always goes on before the sling.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5
preguntas.pregunta: An Rh negative mother delivered a healthy Rh positive first baby and received no RhoGAM. What is the concern for a second Rh positive pregnancy?
opciones: Her anti-Rh antibodies could cross the placenta and destroy the fetus's red cells
Her anti-A and anti-B antibodies could cross the placenta if the baby is type AB
The first baby's Rh+ cells remain in her blood and agglutinate her own cells
A second Rh+ fetus would sensitize her only if it were also ABO incompatible
preguntas.explicacion: A first pregnancy is usually safe because fetal cells rarely cross the placenta, but at birth the Rh negative parent can be exposed to the baby's Rh positive cells and begin making anti-Rh antibodies. In a later Rh positive pregnancy those antibodies can cross the placenta and hemolyze fetal red cells, causing hemolytic disease of the newborn, which ranges from mild anemia to fetal death.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: HIPAA and Communication With Patients
preguntas.subtema: At the front desk · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's spouse comes to the front desk, with other patients waiting behind him, and asks why the patient is here today.
opciones: Ask the patient whether he objects, and talk away from the desk
Answer at the desk, since a spouse needs no written authorization
Refuse any contact until the spouse produces a signed authorization
Send the spouse to the laboratory, which released the result
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules meet here. Information may be shared with a spouse, parent, guardian or other caregiver involved in the person's care without a formal written agreement, but when other people are present the patient is asked first whether there is any objection. And the conversation itself does not belong at a counter or in a hallway: anything specific waits until the patient is in a private room, with only what is relevant said out loud.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Diagnostic Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: How does the American Diabetes Association define 'fasting' for a fasting plasma glucose?
opciones: No caloric intake at all for at least 8 hours
No food or drink, including water, for 12 hours
No solid food for 8 hours; sweetened drinks allowed
No caloric intake at all for at least 24 hours
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA diagnostic criteria define fasting as no caloric intake for at least 8 hours, with a fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher meeting the threshold for diabetes. Water carries no calories and is allowed; sweetened drinks do carry calories. Twelve hours is the general recommendation for morning sampling, and 24 hours is the alcohol-free window.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Clinical Resource Management Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care: Prospective payment
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What characterizes prospective payment?
opciones: Rates fixed in advance according to average resource consumption
Rates negotiated after the fact from the charges actually billed
Rates set by the share of savings the organization has achieved
Rates paid per member per month, regardless of the care furnished
preguntas.explicacion: Prospective payment methods set fixed rates for health services, worked out from what resources a case consumes on average. The aim is predictability of finances and containment of cost, though the approach can make it hard to foresee what a case will need and to encourage the right amount of care. It sits among the alternative models beside capitation and global payment.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Medical Word Parts (Understanding Medical Words)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's lips and fingertips look blue and the note reads cyanosis. Which color does that word part name?
opciones: Blue, from the color prefix cyano-
Red, from the color prefix erythro-
White, from the color prefix leuko-
Black, from the color prefix melano-
preguntas.explicacion: The color word parts run through much of the vocabulary: cyano- is blue, erythro- red, leuko- white, melano- black, xantho- yellow and chloro- green. That is why red cells are erythrocytes, white cells leukocytes and the skin pigment melanin, and why blue skin is recorded as cyanosis.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Issues of Concern, Impact of Safety Devices on Needle Stick Injuries
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D1 k33 · D3 k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A 2018 Dutch study measured needlestick injuries before and after safety-engineered devices were brought in. What did the rate per 100 healthcare workers do?
opciones: It rose slightly, from 1.9 to 2.2 per 100 workers
It fell by half, from 2.2 to 1.1 per 100 workers
It fell slightly, from 2.2 to 1.9 per 100 workers
It stayed level at 1.9 per 100 workers throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The figures went the wrong way: 1.9 injuries per 100 workers before the devices arrived and 2.2 after them. The devices are not the whole answer on their own, which is why continued training on how to work them, surveillance of injuries and a strong safety culture are described as necessary companions to the technology.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Content of the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Notice content · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which content is the notice of privacy practices required to include?
opciones: The individual's rights, how to exercise them, and whom to contact to make a complaint
The fee schedule for copies of records and the practice's policy on missed appointments
A list of every workforce member authorized to open the electronic health record system
The names of the business associates that handle claims and transcription for the practice
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be in plain language and describe how the entity may use and disclose PHI, the individual's rights and how to exercise them including how to complain, the entity's legal duties including its obligation to protect privacy, and whom to contact for more information. It must carry an effective date, and it must be revised and redistributed promptly when privacy practices change materially.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Employee Exposure Determination (note); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i)
preguntas.subtema: Who the plan covers · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital hires per diem and contract phlebotomists for a busy season. How does the bloodborne pathogens standard treat them?
opciones: They are covered, and the plan must describe how the standard is met for them
They are covered after ninety days, the period allowed for a new hire's training
They are covered by the staffing agency's plan alone, never by the host facility
They fall outside the standard, since the exposure determination lists job titles
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan says plainly that workers who are part-time, temporary, per diem or on contract come under the bloodborne pathogens standard, and that the written plan should describe how the requirements are met for them. Nothing in paragraph (c) allows a waiting period: training comes at the time of initial assignment under (g)(2)(ii)(A), and the hepatitis B vaccine within ten working days of that assignment under (f)(2)(i). The exposure determination is a list of job classifications and tasks, so it excludes nobody by employment status.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Homeostasis", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is a set point in physiology, and what is the normal range around it?
opciones: The value a parameter is held near, and the healthy band it moves within
The healthy band a parameter moves within, and the value it may not exceed
The highest value a parameter may reach, and the band above that value
The value at which an effector switches off, and the band it then avoids
preguntas.explicacion: Each physiological condition has a set point, the value that its normal range fluctuates around, and a normal range, the restricted band of values that is stable and healthy. Body temperature is the usual illustration, with a set point of about 37 degrees Celsius and readings that drift a little above and below it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Respiratory Rate", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What happens to the respiratory rate over the first two years of life?
opciones: It drops from a median near 44 at birth to about 26 during the second year
It drops from a median near 60 at birth to about 40 during the second year
It holds near 30 through the whole period and only falls once the child walks
It climbs from a median near 20 at birth to about 30 during the second year
preguntas.explicacion: Children breathe faster than adults, and the rate falls as they grow: the median goes from around 44 breaths a minute at birth to about 26 in the second year of life. That is why a count that would be alarming in an adult may be ordinary in an infant, and why the value is read against the child's age.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Ischemic Stroke", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(3) (2027 I.C.6.g(3)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms cause an ischemic stroke?
opciones: A thrombus forming in the vessel itself, or an embolus arriving from elsewhere
A thrombus forming in the vessel itself, or a rupture bleeding into the brain
An embolus arriving from elsewhere, or a rupture bleeding into the brain
A rupture bleeding into the brain, or a rise in the pressure inside the skull
preguntas.explicacion: Ischemic stroke comes from either a thrombotic or an embolic event that cuts blood flow to a region of the brain. In the thrombotic kind the clot forms inside the affected vessel, usually on atherosclerotic disease; in the embolic kind debris travels there, most often from the heart. Bleeding into the brain defines the other family, hemorrhagic stroke.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "1) Joint Commission International", IPSG 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse tells the phlebotomist that the patient in bed 12 is the one who needs the draw. Under the Joint Commission International patient identification goal, why is that not enough?
opciones: The room number or location cannot be used as an identifier; at least two identifiers such as name and birth date are needed
Only the bar-coded wristband counts as an identifier, so the nurse's statement must be confirmed by scanning it
The location is acceptable as one identifier, provided a second identifier such as the ordering physician's name is added
Two staff members must independently confirm the bed number before a specimen can be collected
preguntas.explicacion: The first international patient safety goal requires at least two ways of identifying the patient, for example name, identification number, birth date or a bar-coded wristband, and it excludes the room number or location outright. The wristband is one valid option, not the only one; the physician's name identifies the order, not the patient; and a second witness does not turn a location into an identifier.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which range is accepted as the normal body temperature of a resting adult?
opciones: 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F), around an average of 37.0 °C (98.6 °F)
36.0 to 37.0 °C (96.8 to 98.6 °F), around an average of 36.5 °C (97.7 °F)
37.0 to 38.0 °C (98.6 to 100.4 °F), around an average of 37.5 °C (99.5 °F)
35.5 to 36.5 °C (95.9 to 97.7 °F), around an average of 36.0 °C (96.8 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: The figure everyone quotes, 37.0 °C or 98.6 °F, is an average and not a fixed value: the accepted reference band runs from 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F). The hypothalamus holds core temperature inside that narrow band. A single reading at either edge is normal, so it is compared with the patient's own baseline.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", sections Continuing Education Activity and Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k46 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: In which phase of laboratory testing do fasting errors and patient identification errors occur?
opciones: Preanalytical
Analytical
Postanalytical
Interpretive
preguntas.explicacion: Errors can appear in any of the three phases, before the analysis, during it and after it. Preparing the patient badly, and mistakes in collecting the specimen, belong to the preanalytical phase, along with delays in transport. An instrument that malfunctions and a reagent that is unstable are analytical. Transcription errors and critical values communicated poorly are postanalytical.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: Scrub duration · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee scrubs for ten minutes before a sterile procedure, believing longer is safer. What is the effect?
opciones: No added benefit, and more risk of irritating the skin
A longer lasting effect on the resident skin flora
The same effect as a rub, which needs no drying time
A shorter effect, since the antiseptic is rinsed away
preguntas.explicacion: The usual scrub with an antimicrobial agent runs about two to six minutes, following the manufacturer and the institution. Scrub times of ten minutes or more add nothing and raise the risk of skin irritation, and irritated skin is harder to keep clean. Some institutions use shorter staged techniques or an alcohol-based formulation instead, applied as the manufacturer directs and left to dry completely before sterile gloves go on.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What are the four parameters of steam sterilization that an autoclave has to control?
opciones: Steam, pressure, temperature and time
Steam, humidity, temperature and pressure
Steam, pressure, gas concentration and time
Steam, temperature, pH and exposure time
preguntas.explicacion: The principle is that every item meets steam directly, at the temperature and the pressure the cycle calls for, for as long as it calls for, which makes four parameters: steam, pressure, temperature and time. Pressure is only the means of reaching the temperature needed. Relative humidity and gas concentration matter for ethylene oxide, not for steam.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Holter monitor (24h)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii III.F.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being fitted with a Holter monitor. How long is it usually worn?
opciones: 24 to 48 hours, recording continuously during normal activity
2 to 4 hours, recording continuously during normal activity
7 to 10 days, recording continuously during normal activity
24 to 48 hours, recording only when the patient presses it
preguntas.explicacion: The monitor is a small recorder carried in a pouch or pocket, wired to electrodes on the chest, and it writes the rhythm without a break for 24 to 48 hours of ordinary life. The patient goes about the usual routine and returns the device afterwards for the provider to review.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime review · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An unexpected outage has kept the record system down for a day and a half. What does the guidance ask the organization to do afterwards?
opciones: Review it in depth with root-cause or failure modes analysis, as a group
Report it to the certifying body that tested the record system's software
Repeat the yearly downtime drill within the month that follows the outage
Rebuild the disaster recovery plan from scratch before the system restarts
preguntas.explicacion: Unexpected downtimes lasting more than 24 hours are treated as learning material. The organization convenes clinicians and technical staff together to look at the event and how it was handled, identify possible root causes with a structured method, and decide what would prevent or soften the next one.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is diagnosed with polycythemia. What is the main drawback of the condition?
opciones: Higher blood viscosity, so the heart circulates blood with more effort
Too little oxygen delivered directly to the tissues by the red cells
Loss of the plasma buffers that keep the pH between 7.35 and 7.45
A hematocrit that falls below the 36 percent lower limit
preguntas.explicacion: Polycythemia is an overproduction of red cells, and the trouble it causes is not poor oxygen delivery but thicker blood that the heart has to work harder to move. In polycythemia the hematocrit climbs, it does not fall, and the plasma buffers have nothing to do with it. Viscosity is the same property that makes honey pour more slowly than water.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 3: core elements; and MyPlate, USDA: Grains
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement matches what the Dietary Guidelines say about grains in a healthy pattern?
opciones: At least half of the grains eaten should be whole grains
At least a quarter of the grains eaten should be whole grains
Whole grains should replace refined grains completely
Grains are counted in cups, like fruits and vegetables
preguntas.explicacion: Among the core elements of a healthy pattern, grains carry the instruction that at least half of them be whole grain. Refined grains are not forbidden, so a complete swap overstates the rule. Grains are measured in ounce-equivalents; cups are the unit for fruits, vegetables and dairy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Gown barrier levels · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Two isolation gowns carry different fluid barrier levels. What do those levels come from?
opciones: A four-level standard for medical gowns, from the lowest barrier up
The number of layers of fabric the manufacturer sewed together
The quality level that also grades gloves for micro-perforation
The hazardous materials scale that runs from level A down to D
preguntas.explicacion: Medical gowns are graded against a published standard that sets four levels of fluid barrier protection, and a separate guidance document deals with gowns worn to handle hazardous drugs. Choosing well means matching the level to the setting: sterile gowns for surgery, non-sterile ones for contact exposure. The acceptable quality level is a glove measure, and levels A through D belong to the hazardous materials scale, where A is the most protective.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k16 k49 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: About what share of older adults have hearing loss?
opciones: About one-third
About one-half
About one-quarter
About two-thirds
preguntas.explicacion: Age-related hearing loss is common, reaching about one-third of older adults, and the chance of it grows with age. That is why the guidance asks the clinician to be sure the patient can hear before going on: check that a hearing aid is working, look for a build-up of earwax, and keep the background noise in mind.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Verbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Communication cycle · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: What makes verbal communication effective, as the term is defined?
opciones: Words the receiver understands, conveying care and respect
Words the sender prefers, matched to the sender's training
Words taken from the record and repeated as documented
Words in plain language, but delivered only in writing
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal communication is more than talking: it is an exchange of information using words the receiver understands, in a way that carries professional caring and respect. Heavy jargon or slang raises a barrier the sender did not intend, so the receiver's preferred method is assessed and understanding is always verified.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "1) Joint Commission International"
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee argues that a mislabelled tube is just paperwork, since the analyser will still give a correct number. Which published figures answer that?
opciones: Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 18 such errors harms
A tenth of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 100 such errors harms
Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, but no such error has harmed
A quarter of transfusion deaths trace to labeling, and 1 in 3 such errors harms
preguntas.explicacion: Of all the steps before the analysis, collection is arguably the most critical, because an identification error sends the right number to the wrong person. Up to 50 % of transfusion-related deaths follow an identification error, mislabelled blood specimens can end in a hemolytic transfusion reaction, and as many as one in eighteen identification errors leads to patient harm.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies - for Hospital Patients, How to Avoid Exposure; and StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D II.J · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Which materials are acceptable alternatives to natural rubber latex for a patient with latex allergy?
opciones: Vinyl, silicone or neoprene
Powder-free natural rubber latex
Natural rubber without antioxidants
Cornstarch-coated latex gloves
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are advised to ask for equipment made of vinyl or silicone rather than latex, and the alternatives in use include vinyl, silicone, neoprene and polyvinyl chloride; powder-free and latex-free gloves have markedly reduced the prevalence of latex allergy. Powder-free latex is still latex, and it is the natural proteins, not only the added chemicals, that drive the type I reaction.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Do Not Resuscitate", Function
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a-b / 2027 E.7.a · RMA I.C.7 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: A chart holds an advance directive that mentions CPR. Is that the same as a DNR order?
opciones: No: a directive is a legal document, and a DNR is a medical order
No: a directive covers intubation, while a DNR covers only medication
Yes: any written mention of CPR in the chart operates as a DNR order
Yes: once the directive is scanned in, the code status changes to DNR
preguntas.explicacion: Advance directives are legal documents, not medical orders, so a directive that mentions resuscitation is not equivalent to a do-not-resuscitate or do-not-intubate order. The team has to draw the patient's preference out specifically and turn it into an order signed by the provider. On a MOLST or POLST form those same wishes are already written as orders.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Reporting Critical Findings)
preguntas.subtema: Repeat critical values · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.A quality assurance · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's point-of-care potassium is critical again today, as it was at the last two visits and is documented in the chart. What does the reporting policy require?
opciones: Treat it as a reportable event and follow the critical value policy for this instance, even though earlier critical values are known
Skip the call, because a critical value that has already been reported for the same patient does not need to be reported again
Report it only if today's value differs from the previous critical result by more than 10 %, and otherwise just record it
Record it in the log and report all of the day's critical values together to the provider at the end of the clinic session
preguntas.explicacion: A critical value counts as a reportable event even where the patient has had critical values before and they are on record, and the reporting policy is followed the same way each time one appears. Stepping outside the policy is considered only in exceptional cases with evidence behind them, an obvious testing or pre-analytical error for instance. Both the result and whatever was done about it are documented every time.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(14) · RMA III.F.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which imaging method is ruled out for a patient with iron-containing metallic implants?
opciones: Magnetic resonance, whose powerful field can dislodge the metal implants
Computed tomography, whose rotating scanner cannot pass over the metal
Ultrasound, because metal reflects the sound waves back toward the probe
Plain x-ray, because the metal blocks the beam and hides the bone behind
preguntas.explicacion: Patients with iron-containing implants, internal sutures or some prosthetic devices cannot be scanned by magnetic resonance, because the field can move them. The same technique is otherwise attractive since it uses no radiation, but it is costly, noisy and encloses the patient in a tube for as long as half an hour.

preguntas.subtema: Tests waived by regulation · CPT D1 k29 · PBT IV.A.2 / IV.C · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these procedures is named in the CLIA regulation itself as a test a Certificate of Waiver site may perform?
opciones: Spun microhematocrit test
Automated sedimentation rate
Serum hCG color comparison
Benchtop hemoglobin A1c
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation's own list includes non-automated dipstick urinalysis, non-automated fecal occult blood, visual ovulation and urine pregnancy tests, non-automated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, copper sulfate hemoglobin, home-use glucose meters, spun microhematocrit and single-analyte hemoglobin instruments. The sedimentation rate is waived only when non-automated, and pregnancy tests only on urine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Empathy", Definition/Introduction: Neuroanatomical Structures
preguntas.subtema: Empathy and compassion · CCMA 1E k30 · CMAA 2A k22 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A multidimensional approach classifies empathy as which three kinds?
opciones: Cognitive, affective and behavioral
Cognitive, affective and vicarious
Affective, behavioral and moral
Cognitive, behavioral and social
preguntas.explicacion: Empathy is tied to the amygdala, the anterior cingulate cortex and the anterior insular cortex, and a multidimensional approach sorts it into cognitive, affective and behavioral empathy. Cognitive empathy is the kind that motivation can raise with training. The article uses the words vicarious, moral and social in other senses, not as branches of that classification.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles with safety mechanism
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which mechanism is described for winged steel needles that carry a safety feature?
opciones: A needle-locking mechanism that also prevents the set being reused
A blunting mechanism that dulls the tip once the last tube is filled
A color change in the tubing that shows the set has been used once
A hinged shield activated by pressing the wings against each other
preguntas.explicacion: Winged steel needles with a passive or an active safety feature use a needle-locking mechanism that cuts the risk of a stick and stops reuse, and they make the transfer of blood safer when a syringe is used. Joined to vacuum tubes, they still need the first tube to be additive-free or discarded.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with severe neurological impairment of the legs needs the steadiest crutch for the long term. Which one, and at what cost?
opciones: The platform crutch: more stability, but less maneuverability than the others
The forearm crutch: more stability, but it demands good upper body strength
The axilla crutch: more stability, but it cannot be used beyond a few weeks
The platform crutch: more maneuverability, but less stability than the others
preguntas.explicacion: Of the three kinds, the platform crutch is the one seen least often. The weight goes onto the forearms and the platform gives the user more stability than the axilla or forearm types, at the price of maneuvering less easily. They are meant for long-term use, and severe neurological impairment of the legs is the situation named for them.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives
preguntas.subtema: Preservative fill line · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient fills a preservative-containing urine tube only to one-third of the marked line. What is the problem?
opciones: Too little urine leaves the preservative too concentrated, which can inhibit bacterial growth in the culture
Too little urine leaves the preservative too dilute, so it cannot keep the bacteria from multiplying in transit
The tube should be filled to the line with sterile normal saline so the preservative ratio is restored
Too little urine is acceptable for culture, since only 15 to 30 mL is needed for an accurate analysis
preguntas.explicacion: The preservative-to-specimen ratio matters in both directions. Overfilling past the line dilutes the preservative and weakens its action; underfilling leaves an excess of preservative that can suppress the very bacteria the culture is looking for. Topping up with saline dilutes the specimen and the colony count, and the 15 to 30 mL figure applies to urinalysis in a plain cup, not to a preservative tube with a fill line.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Recapping in the numbers · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What share of needlestick injuries did older studies blame on recapping, and what does current hospital surveillance show?
opciones: Between 10% and 25% then; about 5% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 40% and 60% then; about 20% in the surveillance hospitals now
About 5% then; between 10% and 25% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 10% and 25% then; none at all since the standard prohibited it
preguntas.explicacion: Older studies traced ten to twenty-five percent of needlestick injuries to recapping a used needle. Recapping by hand has been discouraged for years and is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard unless no alternative exists, yet it still causes about five percent of the injuries counted in surveillance hospitals. The share fell; it did not disappear, and that is the point of the rule.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k49 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k127 · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: During a child's venipuncture, why does the second adult grasp the child's wrist palm-up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder, and the firm grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the fingers open so the veins of the hand stay visible
It warms the child, and warmth can raise the rate of blood flow sevenfold
It frees the elbow, which the phlebotomist then holds instead
preguntas.explicacion: The immobiliser reaches across the child and grasps the wrist palm-up: reaching across anchors the child's shoulder and stops twisting or rocking, while the firm grasp on the wrist gives the phlebotomist a tourniquet. The immobiliser's other, outstretched hand holds the elbow. Keeping the child warm is a separate measure that may raise the flow.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Preparing Medications, Ampules
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.h(ii)
