opciones: Urine voided 2 to 4 hours after the first morning void, on the same morning
The first void after waking, the most concentrated urine of the night
The second void of the day, regardless of how long after the first
The first morning void of the second day of a timed collection
preguntas.explicacion: Urine that sits in the bladder overnight allows bacterial growth that can change casts and cells, and morphology studies were more reproducible when the bladder incubation time was about 1 to 2 hours. For that reason some laboratories ask for a second morning urine, defined as urine passed 2 to 4 hours after the first morning void. The first void remains the most concentrated specimen, and the day-two first void belongs to a 24-hour collection.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Chambers and Circulation through the Heart; Layers; Left Ventricle
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which chamber pumps blood into the systemic circuit, and why is its wall so much thicker than its counterpart's?
opciones: The left ventricle; it must overcome the high resistance of the long systemic circuit
The right ventricle; it must push blood through the dense capillary beds of both lungs
The left atrium; it receives oxygen-rich blood from all four of the pulmonary veins
The right atrium; it receives blood from both venae cavae and from the coronary sinus
preguntas.explicacion: The ventricles are the primary pumping chambers, and the left ventricle is the major pump for the systemic circuit, ejecting blood into the aorta. Although both ventricles move the same volume per beat, the left wall is much thicker because it must generate far more pressure to overcome the resistance of the long systemic circuit; the pulmonary circuit is shorter and offers less resistance.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A code carries a code also note. What does that instruct the coder to do?
opciones: Report two codes if needed, letting the circumstances of the encounter set the order
Report two codes, with the underlying condition sequenced first in every case
Report a secondary code if it is known, after the code that carries the note
Report only one of the two codes, since they are independent of one another
preguntas.explicacion: A code also note says two codes may be needed to describe a condition fully, but it gives no direction on sequencing, so which comes first turns on the circumstances of the encounter. That is what separates it from a code first note, which puts the underlying condition first, and from a use additional code note, which adds a secondary code where it is known.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a conventional Holter of limited use in small children?
opciones: The wires and the cables get in the way of a child wearing it
The recorder cannot store a rate above 150 beats a minute
The electrodes are manufactured only in adult chest sizes
Three channels are too few to read a child's rhythm from
preguntas.explicacion: Wires and cables are what limit the classic monitor in children. A wireless, water-resistant device cleared in 2011 records a single channel continuously for up to 14 days, and the patient presses a button so the symptoms line up with the rhythm on the recording.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k82 k83 · CMA I.B.8.b · 2027 I.B.7.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: An unresponsive patient is not breathing and an opioid overdose is suspected. How does naloxone fit into the response?
opciones: It is given if available, without letting it interrupt the CPR going on
It is given first, and compressions wait until the patient responds
It is given only after the ambulance crew has taken over the airway
It is given instead of rescue breaths while compressions continue
preguntas.explicacion: When opioid poisoning is suspected in a patient who is not breathing, naloxone is given if it is at hand, and it must not interfere with the CPR already under way. In a patient who still has a pulse but is breathing abnormally, rescue breathing runs at 1 breath every 6 seconds and naloxone follows the protocol in force, with the pulse rechecked.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Patient Labeling Resources: What types of patient labeling are available in the United States?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · RMA III.G.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a form of FDA-approved patient labeling?
opciones: A Medication Guide
A pharmacy receipt
A formulary listing
An insurance benefit
preguntas.explicacion: Patient labeling approved by the FDA takes three forms: the Medication Guide, the Patient Package Insert and the Instructions for Use. Patient labeling is not required for every prescription drug. It is distinct from the prescribing information written for clinicians, which is the label heading by heading, and from anything a pharmacy or an insurer produces for its own purposes.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture - catheterized specimen (003752), How the Test is Performed and Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Catheterized specimen technique · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: How is a catheterized urine specimen for culture obtained?
opciones: The urethral opening is washed with an antiseptic, a thin catheter is passed into the bladder, and urine drains into a sterile container
The urethral opening is washed with an antiseptic, a needle is passed through the lower abdomen, and urine is aspirated
The patient voids the first portion into the toilet and the midstream portion into a sterile container held by the nurse
A thin catheter is passed into the bladder without cleansing, and the first urine to drain is discarded before collecting
preguntas.explicacion: A nurse or trained technician cleans the area around the urethral opening with an antiseptic, passes a thin rubber tube through the urethra into the bladder, lets the urine drain into a sterile container and removes the catheter. It is used when the patient cannot void, when infection is suspected or in urinary retention. A needle through the abdominal wall is suprapubic aspiration, which is rare and mostly done in infants.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A faint during a blood draw is usually vasovagal. Which other forms of reflex syncope are described alongside it?
opciones: Situational syncope, such as cough or micturition, and the carotid sinus form
Cardiac arrhythmia and orthostatic syncope, such as rising from a lying position
Hypoglycaemic syncope and febrile syncope, such as a faint during an infection
Carotid sinus syncope and cardiac syncope, such as a faint from a heart block
preguntas.explicacion: Reflex syncope covers episodes in which the control of blood pressure fails and brain perfusion drops. The vasovagal form is the commonest of them, and the other members of the group are situational syncope and the carotid sinus form, the kind brought on by coughing or passing urine.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.1 Overview of the Digestive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(6) (2027 I.C.6.f(6)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Blood leaving the intestines does not go straight back to the heart. Where does it go first, and why?
opciones: To the liver through the hepatic portal system, so nutrients are processed
To the spleen through the hepatic portal system, so nutrients are stored
To the kidneys through the renal portal system, so nutrients are filtered
To the pancreas through the hepatic portal system, so enzymes are added
preguntas.explicacion: The digestive organs get oxygen and processed nutrients through their arteries, and veins carry blood away from them. Those intestinal veins are unusual: rather than returning blood straight to the heart, they form the hepatic portal system and divert it to the liver, where the processing of those nutrients happens before the blood finishes its circuit.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: For which two situations is a needle and syringe listed as the easier choice?
opciones: Small or difficult veins, and arterial sampling with a heparinized syringe
Small or difficult veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture
Prominent forearm veins, and arterial sampling with a heparinized syringe
Prominent forearm veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture
preguntas.explicacion: For a patient with small or difficult veins, drawing with a syringe can be easier than with an evacuated tube system, and a heparinized syringe can also be used for arterial blood. Collecting large or multiple samples is where the syringe is described as difficult, not where it shines.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: petechiae and purpura · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A non-blanching spot at the puncture site measures about four millimeters. What is it called?
opciones: Purpura, because it is larger than two millimeters
Petechia, because it is smaller than ten millimeters
Erythema, because it sits over an inflamed puncture
Ecchymosis, because it is smaller than ten millimeters
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is two millimeters: a non-blanching spot below that size is a petechia and one above it is purpura. A very large bruised area of bleeding under the skin is called an ecchymosis, and redness that fades under pressure is erythema, not bleeding at all.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(d), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E14 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A reference laboratory accepts specimens from outside clinics. What must it make available to those clients according to CLIA?
opciones: Written instructions on patient preparation, collection, labeling, storage, transport, processing and acceptability
A copy of its CLIA certificate and the qualifications of its laboratory director and testing personnel
A monthly report of the number and condition of specimens rejected from each client's collection site
A price list for each test together with the turnaround time expected from receipt to final report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(d) obliges a laboratory that takes referral work to keep written instructions available to its clients covering, as applicable, the same ground its own policies must cover: how the patient is prepared, how the specimen is collected and labeled, how it is stored, preserved and transported, how it is processed, and when it is accepted or rejected. Certificates, rejection statistics and price lists are not in the standard.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection steps 17, 18 and 20
preguntas.subtema: Split specimen · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 chain-of-custody · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: How is a federal drug test specimen split between the two bottles?
opciones: At least 30 mL into bottle A and at least 15 mL into bottle B
At least 15 mL into bottle A and at least 30 mL into bottle B
At least 22.5 mL into each bottle, so the volumes match
All of it into bottle A, keeping bottle B for a later recollection
preguntas.explicacion: In the donor's presence the collector unwraps the sealed bottles and pours 30 mL or more into bottle A and 15 mL or more into bottle B, then caps both. Whatever urine is left in the collection container is discarded. The two volumes are not interchangeable: bottle A is tested first and bottle B is kept for a retest, which is why it may hold less.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections", Etiology and Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(7) (2027 I.C.6.g(7)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why are uncomplicated urinary tract infections so much more frequent in women than in men?
opciones: Bacteria ascend from the perineum and the urethra is shorter
Bacteria arrive through the bloodstream more often in women
The bladder holds a larger reservoir of urine in women
The kidneys filter a greater volume of plasma in women
preguntas.explicacion: Pathogenic bacteria climb from the perineum and rectum to the area around the urethra, and a shorter urethra shortens their trip, so these infections are common in women and rare in circumcised men. Blood-borne bacteria are an unusual cause. Roughly 40 percent of women in the United States will have one in their lifetime.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Dose Designations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A dose is written as 1.0 mg on a paper order. Which error does that invite, and how should it be written?
opciones: It can be read as 10 mg, so a whole number carries no trailing zero
It can be read as 0.1 mg, so a whole number carries no trailing zero
It can be read as 100 mg, so a whole number carries a leading zero
It can be read as 1 mL, so the unit is changed from mg to mL
preguntas.explicacion: A zero written after the decimal point disappears if the point itself is not seen, and 1.0 mg becomes 10 mg, ten times the dose. Whole-number doses are therefore written without that trailing zero. The mirror-image rule covers doses under one unit: they always get a leading zero, so .5 mg is written 0.5 mg.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(iv), application to laboratories
preguntas.subtema: A laboratory that ships · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory ships a hazardous chemical to another employer. How does the Hazard Communication standard treat it then?
opciones: As a manufacturer or distributor: it must label and send the sheet
As a laboratory still: only the incoming label rules apply to it
As a transporter: only the shipping name and number are needed
As an exempt employer, since the chemical is used in patient care
preguntas.explicacion: The reduced set of duties for laboratories has a limit. Where a laboratory employer ships hazardous chemicals, the rule counts it as a manufacturer of chemicals or as a distributor, so containers leaving the laboratory carry the label paragraph (f) requires of shipped containers, and a safety data sheet goes to distributors and to other employers. Inside the laboratory the short list applies; on the way out, the full labeling rules do.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why a PPD was placed in the skin of the forearm. What is that test looking for?
opciones: Tuberculosis, which that skin test screens for
Prostate disease, which the PSA test screens for
Inflammation, which the CRP test screens for
Thyroid disease, which the TSH test screens for
preguntas.explicacion: PPD stands for purified protein derivative, and it is placed as a skin test for tuberculosis, which the abbreviation TB names. The other three are blood tests on the same list: PSA for prostate disease, CRP for inflammation or heart problems, and TSH for thyroid disease. All three are real abbreviations, but none of them is a test placed in the skin.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3.1 Recording the ECG
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 3F7 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: While the machine is acquiring data, the display shows a bad-lead message. What happens next?
opciones: The faulty lead is corrected and the unit acquires the data again
The recording is allowed to finish and the lead is fixed afterwards
The unit leaves that lead blank and prints the other eleven of them
The unit stops working until the biomedical engineer resets the error
preguntas.explicacion: A bad-lead message in the lower corner of the display is not something to record through: the faulty lead has to be put right, and once it is, the machine goes back and acquires the data by itself. Only a display free of error messages lets the run continue.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Grievance, Appeal and Claim
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E, 5C k76 · CCMA 5M k182 · RMA II.A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to complain about the long waits on her plan's telephone line, not about a benefit that was denied. What is that called?
opciones: A grievance, which is a complaint made to the plan
An appeal, which asks the plan to review a decision
An external review, carried out by a third party
A claim, which asks the plan to pay for a service
preguntas.explicacion: A grievance is a complaint the member communicates to the insurer or plan. An appeal is narrower: it asks the plan to review a decision that denied a benefit or a payment, in whole or in part, and it may end in a review by an independent third party. A claim is a request for a benefit or for the reimbursement of an expense.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles (butterfly)
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k55 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A 3-year-old with small, difficult veins needs one tube of blood. Which device does the WHO device table favor, and what advantage does it list?
opciones: A winged (butterfly) needle, which allows better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle
A vacuum-tube system, which eliminates blood transfer and allows numerous samples from a single puncture
An auto-disable syringe, which prevents reuse and reduces the risk of needle-sticks
A 21 G straight needle with a syringe, which is the most common means of blood sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 describes winged steel needles as good for drawing blood from pediatric patients or from patients with small or difficult veins, allowing better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle, at higher cost and with the air-in-the-tubing caveat. Auto-disable syringes are explicitly not recommended for phlebotomy, and Table 3.1 gives no 21 G option for children.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Stages of POCT · CPT D5 k90 · PBT IV.C · CCMA 3D9 k111 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: In which stage of point-of-care testing do most errors and interfering factors arise?
opciones: The pre-analytical stage, when the sample is collected, handled, prepared and loaded
The analytical stage, while the device is actually measuring the loaded sample
The post-analytical stage, when results are transcribed and communicated to the team
The stages contribute equally, since single-use devices remove most handling steps
preguntas.explicacion: POCT has three stages: pre-analytical, which is collecting the sample, moving it, preparing it and loading it; analytical, which is running the test; and post-analytical, communicating and interpreting results, critical values included. The pre-analytical phase is the controllable variable that matters most, and most interference arises there, through misidentification, hemolysis, clotting, under- or overfilling, a long tourniquet, bubbles and microclots. Such errors fall away with operator experience and training.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug coverage (Part D); and Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether she is obliged to take Medicare drug coverage.
opciones: No, because it is optional and offered by private companies Medicare approves
Yes, because it begins automatically once Part A and Part B have both started
No, because it is optional, but only a Medicare Advantage plan can provide it
Yes, because it is required of everyone who fills a prescription regularly
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare drug coverage is optional, and it comes from private companies that Medicare has approved, insurance companies among them, available to anyone with Medicare. Someone on Original Medicare joins a separate drug plan for it; a Medicare Advantage plan usually has it built in. Even a patient taking no medicines is told to think about it, because of the penalty for joining late.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen that was poorly mixed reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. How does the clot affect the reading?
opciones: It disrupts the stacking of red cells and lowers the value obtained
It disrupts the stacking of red cells and raises the value obtained
It leaves the value unchanged, since only the plasma column is read
It raises the value, in the same way that a tilted tube raises it
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux, the coin-like stacks of red cells whose settling is being measured, so the value comes out lower than the patient's true one. The faults that raise the value are physical ones: a tilted tube, vibration, warmth and an inadequate fill.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Grandfathered health plan
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a grandfathered health plan is correct?
opciones: It is an individual policy bought on or before March 23, 2010, with fewer protections
It is an individual policy bought on or before March 23, 2010, sold by the Marketplace
It is a job-based policy that keeps its status even after benefits are cut sharply
It is a policy that must disclose the ten categories of benefits it leaves uncovered
preguntas.explicacion: A grandfathered plan is an individual policy bought on 23 March 2010 or earlier, sold by an insurer, an agent or a broker rather than through the Marketplace, and it may lack some of the rights the health care law added. The status can be lost when significant changes cut benefits or push costs up. What a plan must disclose is whether it regards itself as grandfathered.

preguntas.subtema: Workstation defined · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.a · CMAA 7A k97 · NCMA 3.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Security Rule's own definitions, what does the word workstation take in?
opciones: A laptop, a desktop or a device doing the same work, plus the media beside it
Only the desktop computers the practice owns and keeps inside its own building
Any device that holds records, the telephone system and the fax machine included
The whole room in which a computer that reaches the records has been installed
preguntas.explicacion: Workstation is defined as an electronic computing device, such as a laptop or a desktop, or any other device performing similar functions, together with the electronic media in its immediate environment. That is why a laptop taken home falls under workstation security and not only under device and media controls.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Frequency
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · RMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A pain medication at the end of life is ordered around the clock rather than as needed. What does that change?
opciones: It is given at regular intervals, so the level in the bloodstream stays consistent
It is given only when the patient asks, at intervals of four to six hours apart
It is given once and without delay, because of how urgent the circumstances are
It is given at a rate that the nurse raises or lowers according to the response
preguntas.explicacion: An around-the-clock frequency means fixed intervals, for example every six hours, so the concentration of the drug in the patient's bloodstream is kept consistent; that is why pain medication at the end of life is often ordered this way instead of as needed. A PRN order waits for a request or a symptom, a STAT order is one urgent dose, and a titration order is the one that is raised or lowered by the nurse.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K 3L k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Bright red blood pulses back into the hub during an attempted venous access. What is done?
opciones: The device is removed at once and direct pressure applied
The device is advanced further until the flow settles down
The device is left in place and the tourniquet reapplied
The device is withdrawn slightly and the tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: An artery entered by accident calls for prompt removal of the line and direct pressure over the site to control the bleeding. Arterial injury sits among the local complications of this kind of procedure, alongside nerve injury, hematoma, bleeding and simple failure of the attempt.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient insists there is a fever because the forehead feels warm to the hand. How reliable is that judgment?
opciones: Unreliable: judging fever by touch is wrong in up to 40% of people, so a reading is taken
Reliable in adults but not in children, whose skin loses heat faster to the room air
Reliable when the hand is placed on the neck instead, where the skin is better perfused
Unreliable only when the room is cold, which chills the skin and hides a real fever
preguntas.explicacion: Deciding whether someone is febrile by feeling the skin is inaccurate in as many as 40% of people, in either direction. When fever is suspected, an instrument reading is obtained and documented with the route used. The patient's own baseline matters too: some people habitually run warmer or cooler than the average.

preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, Heart Tests: Cardiac MRI
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · RMA III.F.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a cardiac MRI has an implanted device. What is the concern?
opciones: The machine can damage the device or shift a metal implant
The machine can erase the record stored inside the device
The dye that is used can react with the metal in the device
The device can distort the rhythm shown on the monitor
preguntas.explicacion: A pacemaker or other implanted device is a reason to speak up before the scan, because the machine can damage it or make metal move. Metal from earlier surgery, piercings, jewelry and some skin patches raise the same question, so the imaging team screens for all of it in advance.

preguntas.subtema: Reports to authorities · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: Which disclosure may be made to a public authority without the patient's authorization?
opciones: A report of a communicable disease or of suspected child abuse, as authorized by law
A report of the patient's employer and insurance details for a workplace injury claim
A report of the patient's diagnosis to a school for enrollment, beyond proof of immunization
A report of psychotherapy notes to a family member concerned about the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Public health disclosures in 164.512(b) include reporting disease and injury to a public health authority and reporting child abuse or neglect to an authority authorized to receive it; disclosures to a school are limited to proof of immunization required by law, with the parent's or adult's documented agreement. Disclosures to an employer are confined to workplace medical surveillance and work-related illness findings with written notice to the worker. Psychotherapy notes need an authorization in almost every case, and a concerned relative is not a public authority.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where does muscle tremor on a tracing come from, and when does it appear?
opciones: From the arm and leg muscles, when the patient is tense or cold
From the chest muscles, when the patient breathes too deeply
From the arm and leg muscles, when the electrodes have dried
From the heart muscle itself, when the rate climbs above 100
preguntas.explicacion: Tremor is a signal thrown off by the patient's own arm and leg muscles. It shows up when the person is tense, cold, or affected by a muscle or nerve disorder, which is why calming and warming the patient is the first thing tried when the baseline is fuzzy rather than wandering.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.10
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for the contracture left by a burn she suffered twelve years ago. What do the guidelines say about coding it?
opciones: There is no time limit, and the acute burn code is not used now
There is a limit of seven years on coding a residual effect
The acute burn is coded first and the residual one after it
Only the acute burn is coded, since it caused the problem
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is what an illness or an injury leaves behind once its acute phase is over, and no time limit governs the use of a sequela code: the residual may show up early or years later. Two codes are normally needed, the residual condition first and the sequela code second, and the code for the acute phase is never used with them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Power of Attorney", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Durable power of attorney · CCMA k218 · CMA E.8.c / 2027 E.7.b · RMA I.C.1.f · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: What does the word "durable" add to a power of attorney for health care?
opciones: It keeps the agent's authority alive after the person loses capacity
It keeps the agent's authority alive after the person has died
It lets the agent decide about the finances as well as the medical care
It lets the agent be replaced by a backup without a new document
preguntas.explicacion: The durable proviso is what protects the appointment if the person loses the functional capacity to decide for themselves, which is exactly the moment the document is needed, so the form is usually headed as a durable power of attorney covering health care. A synonym is health care proxy. Naming a backup agent is a separate choice made when the document is written.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Blood Plasma; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Fibrinolysis; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003423 Venipuncture, Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A red-top tube is left to clot and then centrifuged. What is the fluid above the clot called, and how does it differ from plasma?
opciones: Serum; it is plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed
Plasma; it still contains fibrinogen and the other clotting factors
Buffy coat; the pale layer of leukocytes and platelets above the cells
Whole blood; the formed elements are suspended in the fluid again
preguntas.explicacion: Serum is plasma after the clotting factors have been removed: in a clotted tube it is the fluid squeezed out of the clot as it retracts. Plasma is the fluid part of circulating blood, still carrying fibrinogen and the other factors; serum is what remains liquid after the blood clots in a tube. The buffy coat is the layer of white cells and platelets in a spun, unclotted sample, and whole blood has all the formed elements suspended.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Termination letter · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which element belongs in the letter that ends a clinician-patient relationship?
opciones: The date care ends, and an offer to send the records on once the patient authorizes it
The reason for the dismissal, set out plainly so that the patient is able to dispute it
The names of three colleagues who have already agreed to take the patient on
A statement of the balance owed, since unpaid accounts are a lawful ground to dismiss
preguntas.explicacion: The letter states the date the relationship ends, confirms that care and medication refills run until that date, steers the patient toward emergency help such as a local crisis center, and offers to forward the record to the next clinician the moment a signed release comes back, with the release form in the envelope. Giving a reason is usually not obligatory, and authors are split on whether to name particular colleagues.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Topical, Local, and Regional Anesthesia and Anesthetics", Toxicity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.D.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Systemic toxicity from a local anesthetic is suspected. What is the immediate treatment?
opciones: A 20% intravenous lipid emulsion, 1.5 mL/kg over one minute, then a continuous infusion
A 20% intravenous lipid emulsion, 0.25 mL/kg over one minute, then a continuous infusion
A 20% intravenous dextrose solution, 1.5 mL/kg over one minute, then a continuous infusion
A 20% intravenous lipid emulsion, 1.5 mL/kg over one hour, with no further infusion after
preguntas.explicacion: Toxicity happens when a large amount of anesthetic reaches the circulation. Treatment starts at once with a 20 percent intravenous lipid emulsion, 1.5 mL/kg of lean body mass given over one minute, followed by a continuous infusion at 0.25 mL/kg per minute. The bolus may be repeated up to twice if cardiovascular compromise persists.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Procedures for Evaluating the Circumstances Surrounding an Exposure Incident; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Reviewing an exposure incident · CPT D1 1H 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic reviews a needlestick that happened while a phlebotomist recapped a butterfly needle. Which findings does that review put on record?
opciones: The engineering controls in use, the device brand, the PPE worn and the employee's training
The anti-HBs level of the employee and the hepatitis B status of the source patient
The dates of the last two annual sessions and the names of everyone who attended
The disinfectant used on the surface and the schedule for cleaning that work area
preguntas.explicacion: The written plan has to contain a procedure for looking into the circumstances of every exposure incident, and the model plan spells out what that review determines: which engineering controls were in use, which work practices were followed, the type and brand of the device, the protective clothing worn, where it happened, what procedure was under way, and what training the employee had. Serology results belong to the confidential medical evaluation, not to this review, and training dates and attendance are the separate training record.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Reducing visit demand · CMAA 4A k52 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Part of making open access work is cutting the demand for one-to-one visits. Which measures does the improvement guide name for that?
opciones: Dropping visits kept alive by outdated protocols, running group visits, and using phone and e-mail
Dropping visits kept alive by outdated protocols, running group visits, and charging for same-day slots
Shortening every appointment, opening an evening clinic, and using phone and e-mail for some concerns
Dropping visits kept alive by outdated protocols, hiring locum cover, and stretching follow-up intervals
preguntas.explicacion: Three tactics are named. Some visits survive only because an old clinical protocol demands them, such as routine follow-up for a urinary tract infection or an annual Pap smear, and those sources are identified and addressed. Group visits handle patients who share a chronic condition. And the telephone and e-mail settle concerns that do not need a visit at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Postoperative Wound Infections", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k79 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: Within what window must an infection appear to be classified as a surgical site infection, and which category is the most common?
opciones: Within 30 days of surgery, and superficial incisional infections are over half of them
Within 30 days of surgery, and organ or space infections are over half of them
Within 7 days of surgery, and superficial incisional infections are over half of them
Within 90 days of surgery, and deep incisional infections are over half of them
preguntas.explicacion: Surgical site infections are counted when they occur within 30 days of the operation, or within a year where an implant was placed. The superficial incisional group, limited to skin and subcutaneous tissue, makes up more than half of them, and it is diagnosed by purulent discharge, an organism isolated, the surgeon's clinical diagnosis, or deliberate opening with a sign such as swelling or warmth.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k55 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A supply list gives the size of some catheters in gauge and of others in French. What does the French figure describe?
opciones: Three times the outer diameter in millimeters
One third of the outer diameter in millimeters
Three times the inner diameter in millimeters
One third of the usable length in millimeters
preguntas.explicacion: French sizing takes the outer diameter of the catheter in millimeters and multiplies it by three, so a device measuring six millimeters across is an 18F. It is kept for larger devices and specialized catheters: peripheral lines are not sized that way but by gauge, where the lower number is the wider device and the range stocked runs from fourteen to twenty-six.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with obesity has a pulse that cannot be found with light fingertip pressure. What is the next step at the bedside?
opciones: Palpate more deeply or reposition the limb, since a light touch can miss a pulse
Press as hard as possible, because heavy pressure brings a deep pulse to the surface
Record the pulse as absent, because a pulse that light pressure misses is not present
Move to the opposite limb, because a pulse missed on one side is always felt on the other
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure has to be judged: too much flattens a weak pulse and too little misses a subtle one. Where there is obesity or edema, deeper palpation or moving the limb may be what finds it. When no pulse can be felt at all, Doppler ultrasound is the noninvasive tool used next rather than a chart entry of absent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cortisol", sections Introduction and Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Cortisol follows a diurnal rhythm. When is secretion at its peak?
opciones: Near the time of awakening, after rising in the last hours of sleep
Around 4 p.m., after rising steadily through the afternoon
At night, when ACTH release from the pituitary is highest
About two hours after the first meal of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Cortisol secretion follows a diurnal rhythm: levels begin to rise in the final hours of sleep, peak near the time of awakening, decline gradually through the day and reach their lowest concentration at night; healthy adults produce 8 to 30 mg per day. Around 4 p.m. levels are much lower than in the morning, which is why the second sample is drawn then.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Patient Abandonment, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Abandonment and scheduling · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 4F k60 · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A scheduling error leaves a patient without the coverage her clinician had arranged. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, for which the provider may be liable in damages
As a breach of unsecured PHI that triggers individual notice to the patient
As an information blocking practice, since care was interfered with electronically
As a minimum necessary failure, since the schedule reached the wrong people
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment means ending the relationship one-sidedly, without notice enough for the patient to line up substitute care, and it counts as a breach of duty. It comes in two forms: intentional, such as refusing to see someone who has not paid, and inadvertent, for which the examples given are a misunderstanding about call coverage and negligence arising from errors in the scheduling system. When that happens, damages may fall on the provider who was covering as well as on the primary one.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Vendors & Clearinghouses
preguntas.subtema: Who enrols for eligibility checks · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to complete the practice's HETS enrollment on its behalf so that nobody at the office has to deal with it. What does CMS say?
opciones: The provider itself must acknowledge the rules of behavior and name its relationship with the vendor
The vendor may enroll the provider once it holds a signed trading partner agreement on file
The provider must enroll separately with each contractor whose jurisdiction it bills into
The vendor may enroll the provider, but only for the jurisdiction where the practice sits
preguntas.explicacion: Vendors and clearinghouses are asked to support enrollment, encouraging providers to enroll and sharing their unique identifier, but they are told not to enroll providers themselves. It is the provider who has to read the HETS Rules of Behavior, acknowledge them, and state what its relationship with the vendor is. Enrolling once with a single contractor is enough; there is no need to repeat it with each one.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 4: Limits
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What daily saturated fat limit do the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines set for people age 2 and older?
opciones: Under 10 percent of the day's calories
Under 10 grams for the whole day
Under 20 percent of the day's calories
Under 30 percent of the day's calories
preguntas.explicacion: Saturated fat gets the same ceiling as added sugars: below a tenth of the calories eaten that day, starting at age 2. The limit is written as a share of calories, not as a fixed weight, so it moves with the person's calorie needs. The label's own Daily Value for saturated fat is 20 grams on a 2,000-calorie diet.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), At a glance
preguntas.subtema: Two tiers of precautions · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How do Transmission-Based Precautions relate to Standard Precautions, according to the CDC?
opciones: A second tier added to Standard Precautions for patients with certain known or suspected infections
A replacement for Standard Precautions once a pathogen has been confirmed by the laboratory
The first tier, applied to every patient until an infection has been ruled out
A set that covers bloodborne pathogens only, while Standard Precautions cover respiratory ones
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission-Based Precautions form the second tier of basic infection control: they are layered on top of Standard Precautions whenever a patient may carry, or be colonized by, an agent that calls for extra measures. They never take the first tier's place, and what triggers them is a known or suspected infection rather than a blanket rule for everyone. Contact, Droplet and Airborne are the three categories, chosen by the route of transmission; bloodborne exposure is handled by Standard Precautions and by the OSHA standard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrosurgery", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.2.j
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an implanted defibrillator needs electrosurgery on a small lesion. Which precautions apply?
opciones: Bursts under five seconds, lower power, no cutting current, and stay away from the device
Bursts under thirty seconds, higher power, cutting current only, and stay away from the device
Bursts under five seconds, higher power, no coagulation current, and work over the device
Continuous current at low power, no bursts at all, and work as close to the device as possible
preguntas.explicacion: Current can interfere with pacemakers and implantable defibrillators, causing skipped beats, a discharge, bradycardia, asystole or reprogramming. The recommendations are short bursts of under five seconds, lower power settings, avoiding cutting current, and avoiding the area around the device; confining current to a small area with bipolar forceps also lowers the risk.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Introduction and section Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Where does latex rank among the causes of anaphylaxis in the operating room?
opciones: Second, after muscle relaxants
First, ahead of muscle relaxants
Third, after antibiotics and dyes
Second, after the antiseptic used on skin
preguntas.explicacion: Latex allergy ranks among the frequent triggers of anaphylaxis during surgery, and its prevalence rose as latex gloves came into wide use from the 1980s onward. In occupational health it is named the commonest cause of contact urticaria, and among cases of intraoperative anaphylaxis it comes second, behind the muscle relaxants.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: CLIA certificate (1)-(5); 42 CFR 493.15(c)
preguntas.subtema: CLIA certificates · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic performs only fingerstick glucose and other tests on the CLIA waived list. Which CLIA certificate does it need?
opciones: A certificate of waiver from CMS
A certificate of compliance
A certificate of accreditation
A certificate for PPM procedures
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate of waiver is issued to a laboratory that restricts itself to the waived tests listed in 42 CFR 493.15(c) and no others. A certificate of compliance follows an inspection finding compliance with all condition-level requirements; a certificate of accreditation rests on accreditation by an organization approved by CMS; and a certificate for PPM procedures covers a physician, a dentist or a midlevel practitioner doing only provider-performed microscopy plus, if desired, waived tests. A registration certificate lets an entity do moderate or high complexity testing until surveyed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Notice to the Secretary
preguntas.subtema: Notice to the Secretary · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A breach affects 40 patients. When must the Secretary be notified?
opciones: Annually, within 60 days of the close of the calendar year in which it was discovered
Straight away, and in any event within 60 days of discovering the breach
Annually, within 90 days of the close of the calendar year in which it was discovered
Only if the affected patients ask the practice in writing to make the report
preguntas.explicacion: Notice to the Secretary travels through a breach report form filed electronically on the HHS site. When 500 or more individuals are affected the report goes in straight away and in any event within 60 days of the breach. Where fewer than 500 are affected the practice may report annually, and those reports fall due within 60 days of the close of the calendar year in which the breaches were discovered.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A dark green sodium heparin tube and a light green PST are both ordered. Which comes first in the WHO sequence?
opciones: The dark green sodium heparin tube, then the light green PST
The light green PST, then the dark green sodium heparin tube
Either one, because both contain heparin and share position 6
The light green PST, because gel tubes precede plain heparin tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists the dark green sodium heparin tube at position 6 and the light green plasma separator tube, with lithium heparin and a gel separator, at position 7. They are two separate rows, not a shared position, and the gel tube comes after the plain heparin tube. Footnote d confirms that the PST, if used, is drawn in the position shown.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: E-mail with patients · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: May a practice discuss treatment with a patient by ordinary e-mail?
opciones: Yes, provided the practice applies reasonable safeguards when it does so
No, unencrypted e-mail is forbidden for messages that touch on treatment
Yes, but only after the patient signs an authorization for each message
No, unless the practice first files a security incident report with the Secretary
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets covered providers communicate electronically with patients so long as reasonable safeguards go with it. The precautions given as examples are verifying that the address is right before anything is sent, and sending an alert first to confirm it. Unencrypted e-mail is not forbidden for treatment-related messages, though other safeguards should be used, such as limiting how much the message carries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Blood pressure measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the lower edge of the cuff sit on the arm?
opciones: About 1 inch (2.5 cm) above the crease at the bend of the elbow
About 3 inches (7.6 cm) above the crease at the bend of the elbow
Directly on the crease at the elbow, so the bladder covers the artery
About 1 inch (2.5 cm) below the shoulder, over the thickest part of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff is wrapped snugly around the upper arm with its lower edge about an inch (2.5 cm) above the crease of the elbow, leaving room for the stethoscope. The arm is bare and supported so the upper arm is at heart level, and a bunched sleeve is removed rather than pushed up.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Security safeguards · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Into which three categories does the Security Rule sort the safeguards a practice must put in place?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Preventive, detective and corrective controls
Required, addressable and optional measures
Confidentiality, integrity and availability
preguntas.explicacion: Regulated entities have to put in place safeguards that are reasonable and appropriate, and the rule sorts them into three families: administrative, physical and technical, which is the skeleton of the rule itself. Confidentiality, integrity and availability are the goals those safeguards serve, not the families; required and addressable describe how each implementation specification inside a standard is designated.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 heel anatomy · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague suggests puncturing the back (posterior curve) of a newborn's heel. Why is that spot avoided?
opciones: In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is only 2.33 mm, so the lancet may hit bone
In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is 3.32 mm, too deep for a lancet to reach blood
The posterior heel is where the tibial artery runs closest to the skin surface
The posterior heel is the site the WHO reserves for premature neonates with a 0.85 mm lancet
preguntas.explicacion: In a 7 pound (3 kg) baby, skin sits 3.32 mm above bone at the medial and lateral heel, 2.33 mm at the posterior heel and 2.19 mm at the toe. The posterior heel is left alone precisely because bone is that close. The tibial artery is the hazard of the medial aspect, and the 0.85 mm lancet is simply the size stocked for premature neonates.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Identify and write for your audience
preguntas.subtema: Writing for the audience · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Before drafting a letter that will go to patients, what does the federal plain language guidance say to do first?
opciones: Identify the audience the letter is going to be written for
Choose the template and the letterhead the practice prefers
Decide which class of mail will carry the finished letter
Check the reading level of the last letter the practice sent
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance is built on a set of principles: plain language itself, writing so as to be understood, designing so as to be understood, and testing whether the content really is understandable. Identifying the audience and writing for it is the first of them, because the statutory requirement is that content aimed at the public be written for the specific audience that will read it.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Inhaled Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(5) · RMA III.G.4.d(vii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to use a metered-dose inhaler. Why is a spacer considered best practice?
opciones: It stops particles from settling on the tongue or drifting away into the room air
It warms the medication so that the airway does not spasm as the mist arrives
It lets the patient inhale strongly and quickly, which is what activates a powder
It counts the doses left in the canister so that a refill is ordered on time
preguntas.explicacion: As the patient breathes in from a metered-dose inhaler, part of the small particles land on the tongue or turn to aerosol in the room and never reach the lungs, so a spacer is fitted to get the whole dose in and waste less. The inhaler is shaken, the spacer attached, the patient exhales and then breathes in normally through it. A strong, quick breath is what a dry powder inhaler needs, not this one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: V1 is already marked on a patient's chest. Where does V2 go?
opciones: At the same space, on the other side of the sternum
One space lower, on the other side of the sternum
One space higher, on the other side of the sternum
At the same space, out in the mid-clavicular line
preguntas.explicacion: V1 and V2 are a matched pair in the fourth intercostal space, one on each side of the sternum. The technique is to keep one finger on the space located on the right border and find the same space on the left border with another finger, then mark both spots and check the level again.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wood's Light", Equipment; and Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k63
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is booked for a Wood's lamp examination of the face. What is the instruction before the visit?
opciones: Come without washing, and without makeup, deodorant or any cream
Wash the area well with soap and water and leave it free of cream
Come without washing, but apply a light moisturizer beforehand
Wash the skin well and keep the eyes covered for the whole visit
preguntas.explicacion: The skin to be examined should not have been washed recently and must carry no makeup, deodorant, moisturizer or other topical product, because those liquids can produce a false positive. Covering the eyes is a separate precaution taken during the examination itself, not a reason to wash the face first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Biopsy", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What information should go to the pathologist along with a skin specimen?
opciones: The history, the exact biopsy location, the lesion's duration and the differential diagnosis
The history, the instrument used, the suture material chosen and the dressing applied after
The exact biopsy location, the anesthetic used, the volume injected and the time of injection
The lesion's duration, the antiseptic used, the number of specimens and the container's lot number
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen is only half of what the pathologist needs. Relevant clinical information, the patient's history, how long the lesion has been present, its distribution and symptoms, the exact site sampled and the differential diagnosis, is what lets the slide be read in context, and it markedly improves the chance of a useful histopathologic interpretation.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B14 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks about cooling a feverish child with an ice bath or an alcohol rub. What is the instruction?
opciones: Neither is used: both cool the skin and set off shivering, which drives core temperature up
Both are used, but only after an antipyretic, so that the value does not rebound
The ice bath is acceptable; the alcohol rub is avoided because the skin absorbs it
Neither is used, because cooling the skin has no measurable effect on temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Cold baths, ice and alcohol rubs are ruled out: they chill the skin and provoke shivering, and shivering raises the core temperature, so the child ends up worse. A lukewarm bath or sponge bath may help, and it works better after medicine has been given, otherwise the temperature climbs straight back up.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k59 · D1 1G · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is transferring blood from a syringe into three tubes. How is the rack handled?
opciones: Keep the tubes in the rack, draw the rack closer, and inject downwards
Lift each tube out of the rack and hold it steady in the free hand
Keep the tubes in the rack and tilt them so the blood runs down the wall
Lift the rack up to eye level so the colored stoppers stay in view
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be done, the tubes stay in their rack and the rack is moved towards the worker, with the blood injected downwards into the appropriately colored stopper. Holding a tube in the free hand is what the needle-stick precaution for this step is meant to avoid.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Use of Improved Engineering Controls in a Prevention Strategy
preguntas.subtema: Limits of safety devices · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Why do devices with safety features reduce needlestick injuries without eliminating them?
opciones: Some cannot be activated until the needle is out, and some users bypass them
Their shields are made of plastic, which a needle can pierce from inside
They are sold only for hypodermic needles, not for blood collection sets
They must be removed before the tube is filled, leaving the tip exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Several things keep the risk above zero. With some designs the safety feature cannot be engaged until the needle has already left the patient; a needle can be dislodged during the procedure and leave the sharp exposed; some workers do not activate the feature at all; the feature itself can fail; and with some systems users can work around it, as when a needle is used to connect parts of a needleless intravenous system. Training and monitoring after implementation are what close that gap.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications; CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, duration
preguntas.subtema: Using the hand rub · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How much alcohol-based hand rub goes on the hands, and how is it worked in?
opciones: About 3 to 5 mL, rubbed over every surface until the hands are dry
A single small drop, rubbed into the palms and wiped with a towel
About 15 to 20 mL, poured over the hands and rinsed off with water
Enough to fill a cupped hand, left to evaporate without any rubbing
preguntas.explicacion: When hands are not visibly soiled the alcohol rub is the preferred method, and it is used as the manufacturer directs: roughly three to five milliliters in the palm, rubbed vigorously over all hand surfaces until dry, which takes about twenty seconds. Rubbing until dry is what does the work, so wiping the product off with a towel or letting it sit unrubbed cuts the contact short, and the rub is never rinsed away with water.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Reproductive System: Female Reproductive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(8) (2027 I.C.6.f(8)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Which organs make up the female reproductive system?
opciones: Vagina, uterus, Fallopian tubes, ovaries, accessory glands and external genitals
Vagina, uterus, ureters, ovaries, accessory glands and external genitals
Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, bladder, urethra, accessory glands and mammary glands
Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, uterus, rectum, seminal vesicles and external genitals
preguntas.explicacion: The female reproductive organs produce and sustain the egg cells, carry them to where fertilization can happen, house a developing fetus, deliver it, and make the female sex hormones. The list is the ovaries, the Fallopian tubes, the uterus, the vagina, the accessory glands and the external genital organs.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(A) and (g)(1)(i)(A), specimen containers and labels
preguntas.subtema: Specimen labeling exemption · CPT D1 k31 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Tubes of blood go from the draw room to the in-house laboratory in a closed rack, and the facility applies Universal Precautions to all specimens. Is a biohazard label required?
opciones: Not while they stay in the facility and are recognizable as specimens; it is required once they leave
Yes, always: every container of blood must carry the fluorescent orange-red biohazard label
No, never: labeling applies to regulated waste containers, not to specimens of blood
Only if the primary container becomes contaminated on the outside and needs a second container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(A) wants the containers that carry specimens for storage, for transport or for shipping labeled or color-coded and closed, but it exempts a facility handling every specimen under Universal Precautions, provided those containers are recognizable as specimens; the exemption holds only inside that facility, and the label returns the moment the specimens leave it. Labeling is not limited to waste: (g)(1)(i)(A) reaches any container in which blood is stored, transported or shipped. Contamination on the outside triggers a second container under (d)(2)(xiii)(B), which is a different rule.

preguntas.subtema: Rights stated in the notice · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The notice tells patients they may ask the practice to restrict certain uses of their information. What must the notice say alongside that right?
opciones: That the practice is not obliged to agree to a restriction a patient requests
That the practice will answer any request for a restriction within thirty days
That a restriction once agreed binds every provider the patient later attends
That a request for a restriction has to be renewed at each new plan year
preguntas.explicacion: The statement of individual rights in the notice covers the right to ask for restrictions on uses and disclosures, and it has to say alongside that the entity need not agree, apart from one restriction the rule does make binding. The same statement covers confidential communications, access, amendment and an accounting of disclosures.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Angle of insertion · CPT D3 3I k65 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The bevel is inside the vein and blood has appeared. How is the needle advanced from there?
opciones: Along the vein, at whichever angle of entry proves easiest
Straight down at ninety degrees until the hub meets the skin
Back out a few millimeters and then in again at a steeper angle
Sideways across the vein so the bevel opens against the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The vein is entered swiftly at thirty degrees or less, and the needle then travels along the vein at whatever angle of entry is easiest, rather than being pushed deeper. Driving it beyond the lumen of the vein is what produces a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", What are physical safeguards and How do you protect electronic information; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Storage of PHI Data and Computers
preguntas.subtema: Physical safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Verification
preguntas.subtema: Access barriers · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that her records be mailed to her home. The office tells her to come in person with photo identification. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Requiring a personal visit is an unreasonable barrier when the patient asked for mail delivery
Requiring photo identification is forbidden, since the rule bars verifying who is asking
Requiring mail delivery is forbidden, since mail is not a readily producible means of transfer
Requiring a visit is allowed only if the office also offers the same records through its portal
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of the requester's identity is required, and the rule leaves its manner to the entity's judgment, but it may not become a barrier or an unreasonable delay. OCR gives this exact example: a doctor may not make someone who wants her record mailed home come to the office to request access and prove identity in person. Mail and e-mail are treated as readily producible by all covered entities.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Throat swab culture (003746), How to Prepare for the Test and How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Mouthwash before throat culture · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a sore throat says she gargled with antiseptic mouthwash on the way to the office. Why does that matter for a throat culture?
opciones: Antiseptic mouthwash is specifically to be avoided before the test, which is otherwise unprepared for
Antiseptic mouthwash is required before the test, so the swab picks up only pharyngeal organisms
Antiseptic mouthwash makes the patient gag more, which prevents the swab from reaching the tonsils
Antiseptic mouthwash stains the pharynx, so the provider cannot see where to place the swab
preguntas.explicacion: The one preparation instruction for a throat swab culture is to skip antiseptic mouthwash beforehand, and the sheet lists nothing else to do. The swab is rubbed at the back of the throat near the tonsils, and the provider may scrape several times to improve the chance of catching the organism. Rinsing with plain water belongs to sputum collection, to clear oral contaminants.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, and Will I need to do anything to prepare
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a drug level ordered as a trough but says he took this morning's dose an hour ago. What matters?
opciones: Timing relative to the dose changes the result; report it before drawing
The level is stable through the day, so proceed and label the tube as ordered
Draw it now and relabel the sample as a peak level instead of a trough
Wait 30 minutes, which is the standard window for any trough sample
preguntas.explicacion: For TDM the test may need to be scheduled before or after the regular dose depending on the medicine, and the level in the blood varies over time as the body processes the drug. The trough is the point just before the next dose; a sample an hour after dosing is not that. Relabelling it as a peak invents a measurement that was not ordered.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Objective
preguntas.subtema: SOAP structure · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her stomach hurts, and the clinician finds tenderness on palpation. Where does each item belong in a SOAP note?
opciones: The reported pain is subjective and the tenderness found on examination is objective
Both belong under objective, since the clinician wrote them down during the same visit
Both belong under subjective, since abdominal complaints cannot be measured directly
The reported pain is objective and the tenderness found on examination is subjective
preguntas.explicacion: A common documentation mistake is blurring symptoms and signs. Symptoms are what the patient describes and go under subjective; signs are the objective findings related to the reported symptom and go under objective. The article uses this very pair as its illustration: a report of stomach pain against tenderness found on palpation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Glove quality levels · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.c · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Two boxes of gloves list different acceptable quality levels. What does a lower number mean?
opciones: A better glove, with fewer pinholes and micro-perforations
A thicker glove, made to be worn as the outer of two pairs
A cheaper glove, meant for handling clean supplies only
A sterile glove, treated so that microbes are eliminated
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptable quality level counts how many defective units a batch may contain, so the lower the figure the better the glove: fewer pinholes and less potential for micro-perforation. The recommended minimum sits at 1.5 for surgical gloves; for medical examination gloves it is 2.5. Sterility is a separate property; surgery calls for gloves processed so that no microbes remain, and the evidence supports wearing two layers during an operation.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors (Feb. 13, 2025), Treatment and Reporting; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Reporting an exposure · CPT D1 1H k33 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Immediately after washing a needlestick with soap and water, what does NIOSH tell the worker to do?
opciones: Report the incident to the supervisor and seek medical care right away
Wait 72 hours to see whether symptoms appear before reporting
Test the discarded needle for virus before deciding whether to report
Start the hepatitis B vaccine series on their own before reporting
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH's steps run in order: wash a puncture or a cut with soap and water, flush a splash, irrigate the eyes, tell the supervisor what happened, and get medical care immediately so the risk can be judged; where applicable an incident report is filled in. The 72-hour figure is the outer limit for starting HIV PEP, not a waiting period. The WHO annex says specifically that a discarded needle or syringe is not tested for virus, and any prophylaxis or vaccination is decided during the medical evaluation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Allergies and Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k44 · CMA I.A.4.e · RMA III.F.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports an allergy to penicillin. What does the record need besides the drug name?
opciones: The reaction it caused, because many patients carry the label without a true allergy
The brand name of the product, because generics do not provoke the same reaction
The date another practice first entered the allergy into the chart being reviewed
Whether an antihistamine was taken, because that clears the entry from the list
preguntas.explicacion: An allergy entry is only useful when the nature of the earlier reaction is recorded with it. That matters most with the beta-lactams, where a great many patients are classified as allergic without being so, and validated tools exist to judge how likely a true drug allergy is. Every allergen asked about, medication or food or latex, gets the same treatment.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · CCMA 3B4 k63
preguntas.pregunta: What makes an instrument a speculum?
opciones: It goes into a body cavity to help see inside, lit or unlit
It holds the edges of an opening apart to keep tissue exposed
It grips a structure with a hooked point so it can be pulled
It scrapes loose cells off a surface so they can be studied
preguntas.explicacion: A speculum is defined by its purpose: it is inserted into a cavity of the body to aid observation, and it may or may not be illuminated. Holding the edges apart is the retractor's job, gripping and pulling is what the tenaculum does, and scraping cells off the cervix belongs to the cytological spatula.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: The prevacuum sterilizer is run each morning with a folded towel pack and a test sheet before the first load. What is being checked?
opciones: Whether air is leaking in or is not being removed, since trapped air blocks steam contact
Whether the resistant spores in the pack survive, which is the direct measure of lethality
Whether the chamber holds pressure long enough for a wrapped load to reach its temperature
Whether the wrap material still lets steam through after repeated laundering and folding
preguntas.explicacion: That is the Bowie-Dick test, and it detects air leaks and incomplete air removal. The sheet goes in the middle of the pack, the pack sits horizontally at the front bottom of an otherwise empty chamber over the drain, and a uniform color change means the vacuum is acceptable; a spot means air kept the steam off the indicator. Spores measure lethality, and that is a different test.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee is taught the boundaries of the fossa before palpating it. Which muscles form its lateral and medial borders?
opciones: Brachioradialis on the lateral side and pronator teres on the medial side
Pronator teres on the lateral side and brachioradialis on the medial side
