Biceps brachii on the lateral side and brachialis on the medial side
Brachialis on the lateral side and supinator on the medial side of the fossa
preguntas.explicacion: The triangle is bounded laterally by the medial edge of brachioradialis and medially by the lateral edge of pronator teres, with a line drawn between the epicondyles of the humerus closing the triangle above. Brachialis and supinator lie deeper: they form the floor rather than the sides.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: Within what time after a thrombotic stroke does a thrombolytic agent significantly improve the patient's prognosis?
opciones: Within 3 hours
Within 30 minutes
Within 24 hours
Within 72 hours
preguntas.explicacion: A thrombolytic agent given within 3 hours of a thrombotic stroke improves the prognosis significantly, but some strokes are hemorrhagic, so the cause must be established first. Tissue plasminogen activator is the enzyme used. The 30-minute figure is the usual length of vascular spasm and 72 hours is the RhoGAM window after birth; neither applies here.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A mother phones about her 2-month-old, whose rectal temperature is 38.1 °C (100.6 °F). What does this call for?
opciones: The provider is contacted right away: 38 °C rectally at 3 months or under is reportable
Fluids and a repeat reading in 24 hours, since the value sits only slightly above the normal band
A repeat reading by the axillary route, because a rectal value is read one degree high
A lukewarm sponge bath first, and a call only if the reading has not come down by then
preguntas.explicacion: Infants of 3 months or younger are the one group where the threshold triggers a call on its own: a rectal reading of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher is reported to the provider immediately, whatever the baby looks like. Waiting a day applies to older children, and no route correction is applied to a rectal value.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures form the central nervous system, and which form the peripheral nervous system?
opciones: Brain and spinal cord centrally; the nerves branching from them peripherally
Brain and cranial nerves centrally; the spinal cord and its nerves peripherally
Spinal cord and ganglia centrally; the brain and its coverings peripherally
Brain and meninges centrally; the spinal cord and the ganglia peripherally
preguntas.explicacion: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord, both inside the dorsal body cavity and both wrapped in bone, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid. The peripheral system is everything that branches out from them, and it forms the communication network between the center and the rest of the body.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · CCMA 3E1 k127 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives with her adult son, who answers every question for her. How should you handle the visit?
opciones: Ask the patient how she sees her son's role, and keep addressing her directly
Speak mainly to the son, since he manages her medications at home
Ask the son to leave the room before any question is put to her
Record the son as her legal decision-maker for the rest of the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Check with the patient about how they see the companion's role, to protect privacy, and keep the patient involved, sitting so both can be addressed face to face and not directing remarks only to the companion. Asking the companion to step out is an option for sensitive topics, and legal authority to decide exists only for a named health care agent or proxy.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 5. Cleaning and Disinfecting Environmental Surfaces in Healthcare Facilities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.i · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A culture is knocked over and spills a large volume in the laboratory. How is the hypochlorite used?
opciones: A 1:10 dilution for the first application before cleaning, then a 1:100 terminal disinfection
A 1:100 dilution for the first application before cleaning, then a 1:10 terminal disinfection
A 1:10 dilution applied once after the visible matter has been cleaned up and discarded
A 1:100 dilution applied twice, with the second application left in place for thirty minutes
preguntas.explicacion: With a large spill, over about 10 mL, or with a laboratory culture spill, the stronger 1:10 dilution goes on first, before cleaning, so that the risk from a sharps injury during the cleanup is already reduced. A terminal disinfection with the 1:100 dilution follows. Visible matter is lifted with absorbent material that is then thrown away in labeled containment.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): if you perform only waived tests and wish to add PPM or other nonwaived testing
preguntas.subtema: Adding nonwaived tests · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A Certificate of Waiver site wants to add a moderate complexity analyzer. What must it do before running the first patient sample on it?
opciones: Reapply on Form CMS-116, pay the fee, and receive the appropriate certificate
Notify the state agency within 30 days after the analyzer goes into use
Run two levels of control and document the results for 20 consecutive days
Enroll the new analyte in proficiency testing and pass the first event
preguntas.explicacion: Adding PPM, or any nonwaived test, to a waived-only menu means a fresh application on the very same Form CMS-116 used the first time, this time for whichever certificate fits. Nonwaived testing cannot start until the fee is paid and the new certificate is in hand. The 30-day notice covers ownership, name, location and director; quality control and proficiency testing become requirements once nonwaived testing is running.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section Can I continue taking medicine during a fast
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether to skip his blood-pressure pill before a fasting draw. What is the correct guidance?
opciones: Do not stop a medicine unless the provider said to; ask the provider
Skip every medicine on the morning of the draw, because all pills break a fast
Take it only with a little juice so that the stomach is protected
Take it after the draw with water, never before a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should ask the provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines are fine; for some tests the provider may ask them to stop, but a medicine is never stopped unless the provider says so. Vitamins and supplements should also be reported. Juice is on the list of drinks that break a fast.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Sputum Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT V.C V.D · CCMA 3D1 k113 · RMA III.C.4.a.v · CMA I.C.7.a(4)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being evaluated for pulmonary tuberculosis. Which sputum collection and storage instruction is correct?
opciones: Three early-morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each, kept in a refrigerator
One early-morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL, kept at room temperature
Three specimens collected at any time of day, each frozen at −20 °C
Three early-morning specimens of 2 to 3 mL each, kept in a CO2 incubator
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early-morning sputum specimens, 8 to 10 mL each, is collected and stored refrigerated; in patients who cannot cooperate the organism may be recovered from gastric contents obtained by stomach aspiration. Freezing is not part of the instruction, a single specimen is not a series, and the carbon dioxide incubator belongs to cerebrospinal fluid awaiting culture.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Sharps containers; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Where the container goes · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Where should the sharps container sit while a phlebotomist is drawing blood at the bedside?
opciones: Visible and within arm's reach, and sealed once it is used up
On the cart outside the room, so the patient does not see it
In the utility room, where the used needles are carried after
On the floor by the bed, where it cannot be knocked over easily
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table asks for containers that resist puncture and do not leak, sealed once they are finished with, and kept in sight within arm's reach; the reason given is that this prevents needlestick injuries to patients, to health workers and to the community around them. The bloodborne pathogens standard puts the same idea in regulatory language: while in use the container stays easily accessible, as close as feasible to where the sharps are used, upright, and it is replaced before it overfills.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Introduction and Negligence or breach of duty
preguntas.subtema: Standard of care · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.b · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a similarly trained peer in the same community would reasonably give
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is measured against the standard of care, which the law describes as what a reasonable physician in that community, holding comparable training and experience, would have done for this patient. Perfection is not the yardstick, and some states use the term gross negligence instead. Malpractice is care that falls short of what a colleague in the same post, with the same credentials, would have given, with injury resulting. Written policies and a patient's expectations may serve as evidence, but the legal measure is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: In therapy after shoulder surgery a patient raises the arm while the assistant supplies about half the effort. What is that called?
opciones: Active assist range of motion, with partial help from an outside force
Active range of motion, since the patient starts the movement alone
Passive range of motion, since another person is moving the shoulder
Resisted range of motion, since the arm is working against a force
preguntas.explicacion: In active assist range of motion the patient moves the joint but an outside force supplies part of the effort, and the fifty percent of help given by a physical therapy assistant during shoulder recovery is the example given. Movement by the patient alone is active, and movement supplied entirely from outside is passive.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Parenteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(2) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is absorption from a subcutaneous injection slow and sustained?
opciones: The layer beneath the dermis holds few blood vessels, so the drug leaves it gradually
The layer beneath the dermis is richly vascular, so the drug pools there before moving
The drug has to cross the epidermis first, and that barrier slows every molecule down
The drug travels through the portal vein, so the liver removes part of every dose
preguntas.explicacion: A subcutaneous injection is deposited in the skin layer lying just beneath the dermis and epidermis. Few blood vessels run through that tissue, so uptake is slow and sustained. The sites used are the outer upper arm, the upper back, the thigh in front, the upper buttock behind the hip bone, and the abdomen, staying two inches clear of the navel.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Atrioventricular Node
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the impulse pause at the atrioventricular node before it reaches the ventricles?
opciones: So the atria can finish pumping blood into the ventricles first
So the ventricles can finish filling from the great veins first
So the sinoatrial node can recover before it fires the next time
So the Purkinje fibers can repolarize after the previous beat
preguntas.explicacion: The nodal cells are small and conduct less efficiently than the rest of the system, so the impulse is held up for roughly a tenth of a second. That pause is what lets the atrial muscle complete its contraction and load the ventricles before the ventricular walls are told to squeeze.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Personnel Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Color-blindness screen · PBT VI.C · RMA III.C.1.a.vi
preguntas.pregunta: When staffing a waived testing service, which personnel screen does the good-practice guidance specifically recommend?
opciones: Evaluate staff for color-blindness, since many results depend on color endpoints
Verify that every operator holds a state phlebotomy or laboratory license
Require a medical laboratory technician degree for staff who read PT/INR results
Screen applicants for hepatitis B immunity before allowing fingerstick collection
preguntas.explicacion: Because many waived tests are read against a color chart or a colored line, the guidance advises evaluating staff for color-blindness, which can limit their ability to interpret results. It also warns that temporary or part-time staff may be less proficient, that turnover is high, and that competency must be maintained when volume is low. CLIA itself sets no license or degree requirement for waived testing personnel.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Virtual check-ins · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a brief real-time exchange with her doctor that lasted under ten minutes. What is that called?
opciones: A virtual check-in
An online e-visit
A monitoring session
A telephone triage call
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare describes several ways of using telehealth. E-visits are exchanges that are not face to face and that usually run through an online patient portal. Virtual check-ins are short live exchanges, generally ten minutes or less. Both sit alongside the fuller telehealth visits that stand in for services normally given in person, such as office visits and psychotherapy.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Definition of Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about high-level, intermediate-level and low-level disinfectants is accurate?
opciones: A high-level agent kills everything except small numbers of spores; a low-level one spares spores entirely
A high-level agent is sporicidal at any contact time; an intermediate one is sporicidal only if left overnight
An intermediate-level agent reliably kills spores; a high-level one is defined by killing mycobacteria alone
A low-level agent kills mycobacteria and most fungi; a high-level one is limited to vegetative bacteria
preguntas.explicacion: The ladder is built on what survives. High-level agents are the same chemicals used as sterilants but for shorter exposure, so they leave only small numbers of spores. Intermediate-level agents may kill mycobacteria, vegetative bacteria and most viruses and fungi but not spores, and low-level ones handle most vegetative bacteria and some fungi and viruses within about ten minutes.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Stepping Up or Down a Step or Curb; and Walking and Turning with a Cane
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient using a cane reaches a step going up. Which leg leads, and how is a turn made?
opciones: The stronger leg steps up first, and turns are made on the strong leg
The weaker leg steps up first, and turns are made on the weaker leg
The stronger leg steps up first, and turns are made on the weaker leg
The weaker leg steps up first, and turns are made on the strong leg
preguntas.explicacion: Going up a step or a curb, the stronger leg goes first. Turning is done by pivoting on the strong leg, not the weak one. While walking on the level, the cane swings forward the same distance as the weaker leg and lands even with that foot, and the strong leg then steps past both.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Coding
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.b · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which code set is used to report the patient's diagnosis on a claim?
opciones: ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification used for diagnostic information
ICD-10-PCS, the procedure system used for inpatient facility claims
HCPCS Level II, the system used for supplies, equipment and ambulance
The national drug codes, used for the drugs and biologics dispensed
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic information is coded with ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification maintained on the CDC side. The procedure coding system, ICD-10-PCS, is used for procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A. HCPCS Level II names products, supplies, ambulance services and equipment, and national drug codes identify drugs and biologics, so none of the three carries the diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: What target serum trough range is given for vancomycin, varying with the indication?
opciones: 10 to 20 micrograms per milliliter
1 to 2 micrograms per milliliter
30 to 40 micrograms per milliliter
100 to 200 micrograms per milliliter
preguntas.explicacion: Trough concentrations let the team judge whether the dosing regimen is working and how the drug is being cleared. The target serum trough depends on the indication and typically runs from 10 to 20 micrograms per milliliter. It is obtained ideally within the 30 minutes before a dose, once steady-state conditions have been reached.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, Is there anything else I need to know about fasting before a blood test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasted twelve hours before a blood count on his own initiative, though nobody asked him to. What is the concern?
opciones: Fasting when it was not ordered can itself skew some test results
Fasting beyond eight hours voids any test drawn that same morning
Fasting without an order has to be logged as a protocol deviation
Fasting is harmless here, and the sample is unaffected either way
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told plainly not to fast unless the provider asks them to, because fasting for some blood tests may itself affect the results and hand the provider an inaccurate picture of the patient's health. The instruction is to follow the preparation instructions given; no rule voids a sample because the fast ran long.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), Normal Results and Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Timed drug levels · CPT D2 k45 time of day · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A transplant patient is scheduled for a tacrolimus level. What timing does the reported reference range assume?
opciones: The sample is taken 12 hours after the dose
The sample is taken 2 hours after the dose
The sample is taken immediately before the dose
The sample is taken at any hour of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Tacrolimus is reported as 5 to 25 ng/mL with the sample drawn 12 hours after the dose, and the two other drugs used to suppress the immune response against transplanted organs carry the same note: cyclosporine 25 to 525 ng/mL and sirolimus 4 to 14 ng/mL, both at 12 hours. A level drawn off that schedule cannot be read against the published range.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.3 A-C Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.1 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether a wristwatch and rings are what is spoiling the tracing. What is the case?
opciones: Watches, glasses, rings and bracelets do not cause it
Watches and rings cause it, although glasses do not
Metal objects cause it whenever they touch a lead wire
They cause it only in a room holding several machines
preguntas.explicacion: Jewelry is not the source of electrical interference: watches, glasses, rings and bracelets are named as things that do not cause it, so the hunt goes to the electrode contact and to nearby equipment. Preparation guidance still has metallic objects removed before the recording begins.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Snellen Chart", Issues of Concern: Snellen Chart Procedure
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(10)(b)(ii) · RMA III.F.5.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wearing her best correction cannot read the single large letter at the top of the chart. How is that classified in the United States?
opciones: Less than 20/200, which meets the definition of legal blindness there
Less than 20/100, which meets the definition of legal blindness there
Less than 20/40, which is the threshold used for a driving license
Unrecordable, so the result is entered as no light perception instead
preguntas.explicacion: Failing to read the top letter with the best corrective lens puts the acuity below 20/200, which is the legal definition of blindness in the United States. From there the examiner steps down: counting fingers, then hand movements, then perception of light, and only if light is not perceived is it written as no light perception.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Medicare Advantage Plan (Part C) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient weighing a Medicare Advantage Plan against Original Medicare asks which one caps what she can spend in a year.
opciones: The plan does, through a yearly limit after which it pays all covered services
The plan does not, and neither does Original Medicare without extra coverage
Original Medicare does, through the deductible she pays once each calendar year
Neither does, since a yearly limit belongs to Medigap policies alone
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare sets no yearly limit on what a person pays out of pocket unless she adds supplemental coverage such as a Medigap policy or joins a Medicare Advantage Plan. Advantage plans carry an out-of-pocket limit that varies by plan; once it is reached the plan pays the whole cost of covered services for the rest of the calendar year.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart, Blood Supply to the Myocardium; and Circulatory Pathways; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Right Atrium
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where do the coronary arteries arise, and where does most of the blood from the coronary veins drain?
opciones: From the ascending aorta; into the coronary sinus and then the right atrium
From the aortic arch; into the coronary sinus and then the left atrium
From the pulmonary trunk; directly into the superior vena cava
From the ascending aorta; into the four pulmonary veins and left atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The right and left coronary arteries come off the ascending aorta and are its only branches. Once blood has crossed the capillaries of the myocardium, most cardiac veins empty into the coronary sinus, and that sinus opens on the back wall of the right atrium, just above and toward the midline from where the inferior vena cava enters.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which finding on an arm rules that arm out for a blood pressure cuff altogether, rather than merely calling for caution?
opciones: A dialysis arteriovenous fistula or shunt built into that arm
Swelling from lymphedema that followed surgery on that side
An indwelling venous catheter running in that arm at present
Weakness of that arm left behind by an old cerebrovascular event
preguntas.explicacion: Cuff limitations come in two tiers. A dialysis fistula or shunt, a recent surgical wound and a mastectomy on that side put the limb out of use entirely. Lymphedema, paresis or paralysis, and arterial or venous lines call for caution instead. In either tier the answer is the same: choose the other limb or another site before inflating.

preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(1) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: An insurer asks a substance use disorder treatment program to confirm that a named person is a patient there. What may the program say?
opciones: Nothing that would reveal the person has been diagnosed or treated there
Only the dates of admission and of discharge, with no clinical detail at all
That the regulations bar it from confirming this particular patient
The detail the insurer needs, since payment is a permitted purpose
preguntas.explicacion: An answer that is not permitted has to be framed so that it does not reveal that an identified person has a substance use disorder under diagnosis or treatment. The program may hand the inquirer a copy of the rules and explain that they restrict disclosure in general, but it may not say that they restrict the records of that named patient, which is a confirmation in disguise.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Recommendations and Treatment options; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Antiretroviral drugs for PEP; CDC, HIV at Work
preguntas.subtema: HIV PEP window and duration · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: When must HIV post-exposure prophylaxis begin, and how long does the course last, according to the CDC?
opciones: As soon as possible and within 72 hours; a 28-day course
As soon as possible and within 7 days; a 14-day course
As soon as possible and within 24 hours; a 7-day course
Within 72 hours; a 6-month course, the length of follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who seek care within 72 hours are evaluated rapidly; PEP is not recommended more than 72 hours after exposure because it is unlikely to work, and the regimen is 28 days of a three-drug antiretroviral combination. WHO's annex gives the same limits: start within 72 hours and take the drugs continuously for 28 days. Six months is the length of antibody follow-up after an exposure, not the length of treatment, and the CDC's occupational page adds that PEP must start within 72 hours.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · CCMA 3B4 k63
preguntas.pregunta: A tenaculum is handed to the provider during a gynecological procedure. What does it do?
opciones: It seizes and holds the cervix or the fundus with a hooked point
It reads how deep the uterine cavity runs from the os inward
It exposes the inside of the vagina so the cervix comes into view
It is put into the uterus to lift the organ and move it about
preguntas.explicacion: The tenaculum is hook-shaped and takes hold of the cervix or the fundus so it stays put. Reading the depth of the cavity is the sound's job, exposing the vagina is what the speculum is for, and lifting the uterus from within belongs to the uterine elevator.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, Rationale and EP 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist arrives at room 412 to collect a CBC. Which pair of identifiers satisfies The Joint Commission's NPSG.01.01.01 for laboratory services?
opciones: The patient's stated full name plus the assigned identification number
The room number 412 plus the assigned identification number on the band
The patient's stated full name plus the physical location of the bed
The assigned identification number read from the chart, used on its own
preguntas.explicacion: NPSG.01.01.01 asks for at least two identifiers whenever blood or another specimen is collected. The goal's rationale accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another identifier specific to the person, and EP 1 says outright that where the patient physically is, the room included, does not serve as one. A single identifier off the chart does not reach two.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Laboratory: OSHA Laboratory Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1450
preguntas.subtema: Chemical Hygiene Plan · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory works with hazardous chemicals. Which written program does 29 CFR 1910.1450 require it to develop and implement?
opciones: A Chemical Hygiene Plan
An Exposure Control Plan
A Fire Prevention Plan
A Hazard Communication Program
preguntas.explicacion: The Laboratory Standard reaches workplaces where hazardous chemicals are handled in fairly small amounts, outside any production line, across several different procedures, and it obliges the employer to write and implement a Chemical Hygiene Plan, a document setting out the work practices, the equipment, the protective gear and the procedures able to shield employees from the health hazards of the chemicals in that workplace. The Exposure Control Plan is the bloodborne pathogens document, the Fire Prevention Plan comes from 29 CFR 1910.39, and the written hazard communication program belongs to 1910.1200.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Noncritical Items
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which group do a blood pressure cuff, a bedpan and a pair of crutches belong to, and why?
opciones: Noncritical, because they meet intact skin, which blocks most microbes on its own
Semicritical, because they can reach mucous membranes if a patient is moved carelessly
Critical, because a cuff is inflated over a limb where the vascular system runs beneath
Noncritical, because they are cleaned in a central area away from where they get used
preguntas.explicacion: Noncritical items touch intact skin and not mucous membranes, and intact skin is itself an effective barrier, so their sterility is not critical. That is why cuffs, bedpans, crutches and computers can be decontaminated right where they are used instead of traveling to central processing, unlike critical and many semicritical items.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Avoidance of contaminated phlebotomy equipment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet and infection control · CPT D3 k60 · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Tourniquets have been found carrying methicillin-resistant staphylococci. By which two routes does that happen?
opciones: Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and reuse of a contaminated band
Poor hand hygiene by the patient and storage of the band in a closed tray
Reuse of a contaminated band and application over a sleeve rather than skin
Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and washing the band between patients
preguntas.explicacion: Up to a quarter of tourniquets have been found carrying this organism, and the two causes named are the phlebotomist's lack of hand hygiene and the reuse of bands that are already contaminated. That is why a disposable band is preferred and why gloves go on before the band.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k62 · D2 2O · PBT II.E II.G · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: For which purpose is an arterial sample, rather than a venous one, the indicated specimen?
opciones: Gathering data on arterial blood gases
Gathering data on a complete blood count
Gathering data on coagulation factor levels
Gathering data on a fasting plasma glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Routine draws use veins because they are superficial and the puncture is more comfortable, and arterial sampling is reserved for the case where arterial blood is what the test needs, namely blood gases. The counts, clotting studies and chemistries of everyday work are all run on venous blood.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An intake form is marked NKDA. What has the patient reported?
opciones: The patient has no known drug allergies
The patient has no known dietary allergy
The patient has no known kidney disease
The patient has no known cardiac history
preguntas.explicacion: NKDA means no known drug allergies, and it belongs on the intake form before any medication is given. It records the absence of a known allergy, not the absence of any reaction ever, so a new reaction is still possible and the entry has to be checked at every visit.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.19(b)(1)-(3); CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Provider-performed microscopy (PPM) procedures
preguntas.subtema: Who performs PPM · PBT VI.F · CMA I.C.8.e microscope / I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.vi
preguntas.pregunta: Under a PPM certificate, which practitioners may personally carry out procedures of provider-performed microscopy?
opciones: A physician, a midlevel practitioner, or a dentist, during the patient's visit
Any testing personnel trained by the physician, during the patient's visit
A medical laboratory technician working under the laboratory director
A medical assistant, once competency for the microscope has been documented
preguntas.explicacion: PPM procedures are moderately complex microscopy tests, limited to bright-field or phase-contrast, done on labile specimens from the practitioner's own patients. Only three kinds of practitioners qualify: physicians, midlevel practitioners under physician supervision or in state-authorized independent practice, and dentists. Medical assistants and laboratory technicians are not on that list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · RMA III.E.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What makes the Korotkoff sounds audible in the first place?
opciones: The cuff compresses the artery, turning smooth flow into turbulent flow
The cuff stops the flow completely, and the silence is broken by the valve
The cuff stretches the vessel wall, and the elastic recoil produces the tapping
The cuff presses the vein against the artery, and the two vessels knock together
preguntas.explicacion: At rest the blood moves through the brachial artery in smooth laminar flow, which makes no sound a stethoscope can pick up. Squeezing the artery with the cuff turns that flow turbulent, and the turbulence is what is heard. When the flow smooths out again below the diastolic pressure the sound disappears.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ankle Brachial Index", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62
preguntas.pregunta: An ankle-brachial index is being taken by the manual method. How wide must the cuff be, and what picks up the pulse?
opciones: At least 40 % of the way around the limb, with a doppler or a stethoscope
At least 20 % of the way around the limb, with a doppler or a stethoscope
At least 40 % of the length of the limb, with a doppler as the detector
At least 80 % of the way around the limb, read off an oscillometer alone
preguntas.explicacion: The manual technique asks for a cuff whose width is at least two fifths of the circumference of the limb, and for a doppler or a stethoscope to detect the pulse. The oscillometer belongs to the automated technique, which takes a regular cuff for a calf under 35 cm and a large one above that.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Variability of Vital Signs in Older Adults; and StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound" (NBK539778)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why does systolic pressure tend to rise and diastolic pressure to fall as a patient ages?
opciones: The arteries stiffen progressively, which widens the gap between the two values
The heart contracts more forcefully with age, lifting only the upper of the two
The blood becomes more viscous with age, which raises the peak and lowers the trough
The veins lose their valves with age, so less blood returns between contractions
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries grow stiffer over the years, and the consequence is a higher systolic value, a lower diastolic value and a widened pulse pressure between them. The same stiffness makes auscultatory readings less reliable in older patients, where errors of 30 to 50 mm Hg have been reported.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ACE Inhibitors", Adverse Effects: Hyperkalemia
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on an ACE inhibitor has a potassium of 5.6 mEq/L. Which mechanism accounts for the rise?
opciones: Less angiotensin II means less aldosterone, and potassium stops being secreted
More aldosterone is made, sodium and water return, and potassium leaves in urine
The Na-K-2Cl cotransporter is blocked, so potassium cannot return to the lumen
Bradykinin builds up in the lung, which is also what produces the class's cough
preguntas.explicacion: Hyperkalemia here is the mechanism of the drug showing itself. Blocking angiotensin II cuts the aldosterone that follows it; without aldosterone the tubule stops trading sodium reabsorption for the secretion of protons and potassium, so potassium climbs. Kidney disease or potassium-sparing drugs raise the risk further. Bradykinin accumulation explains the cough of this class, not the potassium.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Body Planes; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Planes of the Body
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A scan is cut horizontally, dividing the body into an upper and a lower portion. Which plane was used?
opciones: The transverse plane, also called the axial plane
The frontal plane, also called the coronal plane
The sagittal plane, also called the lateral plane
The oblique plane, which meets the body at an angle
preguntas.explicacion: The transverse or axial plane is the horizontal one, and it separates upper from lower; the images it produces are called cross sections. The frontal or coronal plane runs from side to side and separates front from back, the sagittal runs from front to back and separates right from left, and an oblique plane cuts at an angle to all three.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.3 Wound Assessment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: A dressing change reveals thick, opaque, yellow-green drainage in the wound bed. How is that classified and handled?
opciones: Purulent drainage, which is never normal and is reported to the provider each time it appears
Serous drainage, which is normal during the inflammatory stage and is simply documented
Serosanguineous drainage, which is expected while the capillaries are still fragile and new
Sanguineous drainage, which means fresh bleeding and calls for pressure over the wound bed
preguntas.explicacion: Purulent exudate is thick and opaque, and its color may be brown, green, yellow or tan. It never counts as a normal finding in a wound bed, so any new purulent drainage goes to the provider. Serous drainage is plasma, thin and watery and clear, and normal in small amounts during the inflammatory stage; serosanguineous adds a little blood, and sanguineous is fresh bleeding.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Infection risk · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1K k31 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which pathogens beyond HIV and the hepatitis viruses are named as transmissible through this procedure?
opciones: Viral haemorrhagic fevers and dengue, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Influenza and tuberculosis, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Viral haemorrhagic fevers and measles, with tetanus through the puncture wound
Dengue and influenza, with tetanus and rabies through the puncture wound itself
preguntas.explicacion: Drawing blood can expose workers and patients to bloodborne pathogens, and the list runs beyond HIV and hepatitis B and C to the viruses of Ebola, Lassa, Marburg and Crimean Congo haemorrhagic fever, and to dengue. Malaria and syphilis may also travel in contaminated blood.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Poisoning first aid", Poison Control
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.h · 2027 I.B.8.h · RMA III.I.1.b · CMAA 3 k45
preguntas.pregunta: Which number reaches poison control from anywhere in the United States?
opciones: The national toll-free Poison Help line, 1-800-222-1222
The state health department line printed on the label
The manufacturer's hotline printed on the product container
The nearest hospital switchboard, which routes the call on
preguntas.explicacion: One national toll-free line, 1-800-222-1222, reaches the local poison control center from anywhere in the country, free and confidential, 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, and it takes questions that are not emergencies as well. If the patient is taken to the hospital, the container of the substance goes along.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology: Peripheral Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many pairs of cranial nerves and how many pairs of spinal nerves does the body have?
opciones: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves and thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves
Thirty-one pairs of cranial nerves and twelve pairs of spinal nerves
Twelve pairs of cranial nerves and twenty-four pairs of spinal nerves
Ten pairs of cranial nerves and thirty-three pairs of spinal nerves
preguntas.explicacion: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves leave the underside of the brain and are named both with words and with Roman numerals. Thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves leave the cord, one pair per segment: eight cervical, twelve thoracic, five lumbar, five sacral and one coccygeal. All of the spinal nerves are mixed, carrying sensory and motor fibers alike.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: TRICARE; and VA, .gov: CHAMPVA benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.d / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Who is covered by TRICARE?
opciones: Uniformed services members, serving or retired, together with their families
Veterans with a service-connected disability rated permanent and total
Civilian employees of the Department of Defense and their dependents
Members of the National Guard only while they are not on active orders
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE covers uniformed services members, serving or retired, and their families, as their health care program. Cover tied to a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled by a service-connected condition, or to that veteran's survivors, belongs instead to the Department of Veterans Affairs program, and being eligible for TRICARE actually rules that program out. Civilian federal employees have a health benefits program of their own.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Parenteral, Exposure Incident
preguntas.subtema: Parenteral exposure · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient bites a phlebotomist's forearm and breaks the skin. Under the standard, this contact is best described as which of these?
opciones: A parenteral exposure, since piercing the skin barrier by a human bite is listed as parenteral
Not an exposure incident, because saliva is not OPIM outside dental procedures
An occupational exposure but not an exposure incident, because no needle was involved
A contact exposure that requires Contact Precautions rather than post-exposure follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines parenteral as piercing through the mucous membranes, or through the skin barrier, in an event such as a needlestick, a human bite, a cut or an abrasion, and an exposure incident as parenteral, mucous-membrane or non-intact-skin contact with blood or OPIM arising from the employee's duties. A bite that breaks the skin is therefore a parenteral route, and if blood is involved the post-exposure evaluation of (f)(3) applies. Saliva is OPIM only in dental procedures, but the bite itself is the parenteral event; needles are one example of the route, not the only one.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: damages; and Wex: tort (Remedies)
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between compensatory and punitive damages?
opciones: Compensatory damages cover the actual loss; punitive ones deter misconduct
Compensatory damages cover the legal fees; punitive ones cover the injury
Compensatory damages are set by statute; punitive ones are set by contract
Compensatory damages are paid by the insurer; punitive ones by the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Damages are what the court awards to make the injured party whole, and in most cases they are compensatory: calculated on the party's real losses, which in a tort case run from medical care, property damage and lost wages to pain and suffering. Where the court wants to deter future misconduct, it can add punitive damages on top.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sweat Testing", Potential Diagnosis and Normal and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: Sweat chloride bands · PBT V.C.4 / V.A · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.4.b
preguntas.pregunta: A sweat chloride result comes back at 45 mmol/L. How is that read?
opciones: Intermediate: cystic fibrosis is possible and repeat or further testing is needed
Normal: cystic fibrosis is unlikely and no further testing is needed at all
Diagnostic: the value confirms cystic fibrosis without any further testing
Invalid: a value in that range means the sample evaporated during collection
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs in three bands: under 30 mmol/L makes cystic fibrosis unlikely, 30 to 59 mmol/L is intermediate and calls for a repeat test or another approach such as genotyping, and 60 mmol/L or above is diagnostic. An intermediate value may simply mean the patient carries one copy of the gene, and a normal result does not by itself rule the disease out.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: FAQs
preguntas.subtema: Identity theft program · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A small practice decides its risk of identity theft is low but agrees that it does hold covered accounts. What does the Rule still require of it?
opciones: A written program, approved by its board or by an appropriate senior employee
A written program, filed with the Commission before the practice may rely on it
A written program, reviewed each year by the insurer that carries its liability cover
No written program, since the Rule reaches only businesses that face a high risk
preguntas.explicacion: The Rule is deliberately flexible: a business facing a high risk of identity theft may need a comprehensive program while one facing a low risk may need only a streamlined one, and where the risk is low the program might focus on how to respond when someone reports that an identity was misused. Even a low-risk business needs a written program approved at that level.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fusiform Incision", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: Sutures were placed on a patient's cheek and on the same patient's forearm. Which removal times apply?
opciones: About 5 to 7 days on the face, and 10 to 14 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 10 to 14 days on the face, and 5 to 7 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 2 to 3 days on the face, and 5 to 7 days on the trunk or an extremity
About 5 to 7 days on the face, and 21 to 28 days on the trunk or an extremity
preguntas.explicacion: Timing follows the site and the tension on the wound. Facial sutures usually come out at five to seven days, while the trunk and extremities are safer at ten to fourteen, depending on how active the patient is and on the quality of the tissue. Nonabsorbable sutures generally sit somewhere in the seven to fourteen day window.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k59 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood was drawn with a syringe and must be transferred into evacuated tubes. How does the WHO say the tube should be held and filled to prevent a needle-stick?
opciones: Place the tube in a rack and fill it with one hand, or use a needle shield between needle and hand
Hold the tube firmly in the free hand and pierce the stopper at an angle toward the fingers
Remove the stopper, rest the tube in the palm and inject slowly against the inner wall of the tube
Hold the tube against the patient's arm so the syringe can be steadied on the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says best practice with a syringe or winged set is to put the tube in a rack before filling, and to use one hand to fill it, or a shield placed between the needle and the hand that holds the tube. The stopper is pierced from directly above with slow, steady pressure and is never removed, because that releases the vacuum. Holding the tube in the hand is exactly the exposure the step is designed to avoid.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Universal Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Standard and universal precautions · CPT D1 1J k31 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C k99 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens standard, what does the term "Universal Precautions" mean?
opciones: Treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if they carried a bloodborne pathogen
Treating as infectious only the blood of patients whose chart shows HIV or hepatitis B
Reasonably anticipated contact of skin, eyes or mucous membranes with blood in the course of one's duties
Controls that isolate or remove the hazard from the workplace, such as sharps containers and safer needles
preguntas.explicacion: In the standard's definitions, Universal Precautions is one approach to controlling infection: every specimen of human blood, and certain other body fluids, is handled as though it were known to carry HIV, HBV or another bloodborne pathogen. Nothing depends on a chart, a test result or a diagnosis, so the same barriers apply to every patient. The other two definitions sit next to it in paragraph (b): reasonably anticipated contact in the course of one's duties is Occupational Exposure, and devices that isolate or remove the hazard are Engineering Controls.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(c), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT VI.F (CLIA) · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A printed report shows the patient's name and ID, the test, the result with units, and the report date, but not where the test was done. Which CLIA report element is missing?
opciones: The performing laboratory's name and the address of its location
The name and address of the authorized person who ordered the test
The date and time the specimen was received in the laboratory
The identity of the testing personnel who performed the test
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(c) lists what a test report must show: positive patient identification, the name and address of the location where the testing was done, the report date, the test performed, the specimen source when appropriate, the result with its units or interpretation, and any information on the condition and disposition of unacceptable specimens. Receipt time and the identity of testing personnel belong to the test record system under 493.1283, not to the report itself.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A new technician shakes each tube vigorously right after collection to make sure the additive mixes. What does the evidence quoted in the rejection study say about this?
opciones: Tubes should be inverted gently several times; instant vigorous mixing may itself produce hemolysis
Vigorous shaking is required for citrate tubes and optional for EDTA tubes, per manufacturers' data sheets
Shaking is harmless for whole blood but must be avoided once the tube has been centrifuged
Tubes must be shaken for one full minute, since gentle inversion leaves fibrin filaments in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers' data sheets and CLSI documents recommend gentle inversion of vacuum tubes several times to bring blood and additive together; a study cited found that mixing immediately after collection for a minute with 15 inversions may not even be mandatory and that instant mixing can cause hemolysis, and a later trial saw no fibrin or microclots with five gentle inversions, or even with none. Shaking is never the instruction.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Removing eye protection · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How are goggles or a face shield handled when the equipment is being taken off?
opciones: By the strap or the earpieces, never by the front surface
By the lower rim, which stays clean during a procedure
By the front, folded inward so the outside faces itself
By the strap, and then wiped dry with the gown's sleeve
preguntas.explicacion: Eye protection comes off second, after the gloves. The front of it is the contaminated side, the part that met whatever was sprayed or splashed, so it is handled by the strap or the earpieces and dropped into the right container for reprocessing or disposal. The same idea governs the mask, taken off by the ties or straps behind the head without touching the front or the mouth area.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.17(c)(1)(i); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), CLIA Requirements for Waived Testing
preguntas.subtema: FDA categorizes, CMS certifies · PBT VI.F CLIA/CMS · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which federal agency assigns the complexity category to a new commercial test system, and which one administers the CLIA certificate program?
opciones: The FDA categorizes the test; CMS administers the certificates
CMS categorizes the test; the FDA administers the certificates
The CDC categorizes the test; the FDA administers the certificates
The state agency categorizes the test; the CDC administers the certificates
preguntas.explicacion: Three agencies implement CLIA. The manufacturer submits categorization data with its marketing application and the FDA decides the category, notifying CMS and CDC. CMS runs the certificate program and the inspections, through the state agencies. CDC consults on new technology and category disputes and provides the scientific and educational side, including guidance for waived sites.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · D1 1J k36 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3C4 k100 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Gloves worn for one draw are still clean to look at. What does the infection control table say?
opciones: One pair per procedure or patient, and gloves are never washed for reuse
One pair per session, and gloves may be washed if they stay unsoiled
One pair per patient, and gloves may be reused after an alcohol rub
One pair per procedure, and gloves are changed only when visibly soiled
preguntas.explicacion: The rule is one pair of non-sterile gloves for each procedure or patient, with two prohibitions beside it: the same pair is not used on more than one patient, and gloves are not washed so that they can be used again. The device itself is single use for the same reason.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Clean catch urine sample (007487), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Clean-catch cleansing, female · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A woman asks how to clean herself before giving a clean-catch urine sample. What should the medical assistant tell her?
opciones: Spread the labia and use two wipes, front to back: one for the inner folds, a second over the urethral opening
Spread the labia and use two wipes, back to front: one for the inner folds, a second over the urethral opening
Clean the urethral opening with one wipe after retracting the surrounding skin, as done for the head of the penis
Rinse the area with warm water and soap, then dry, exactly as done before placing an infant collection bag
preguntas.explicacion: For a clean-catch, a woman sits with her legs apart, separates the labia with two fingers and uses the first sterile wipe on the inner folds and the second on the urethral opening, always wiping from the front toward the back. Retracting the foreskin is the instruction for uncircumcised men, and washing with soap and water is the routine before an infant bag. The labia stay separated while she voids.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which steps belong to preparing a patient for a 12-lead recording?
opciones: Remove metal objects, shave chest hair, and apply the gel
Remove metal objects, shave the arms, and warm the electrodes
Leave metal objects on, shave chest hair, and apply the gel
Remove metal objects, shave chest hair, and chill the room
preguntas.explicacion: Jewelry and watches come off, the chest hair is shaved so contact is good, and the adhesive gel goes on the electrodes. The room temperature is kept comfortable rather than cold, since shivering puts tremor on the tracing, and the sites are identified before the patient lies down.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient applying for Medicaid worries that the savings in her bank account will disqualify her. What do the MAGI rules do?
opciones: They weigh taxable income and tax relationships, and allow no asset or resource test
They weigh income and assets, with each state setting its own limit on resources
They weigh assets alone, because income is verified through the Marketplace instead
They weigh income after disregards that vary by state and by eligibility group
preguntas.explicacion: The MAGI-based method looks at taxable income and at tax filing relationships in order to settle financial eligibility. It replaced the older calculation inherited from the AFDC program, and it deliberately allows neither income disregards varying by state or by eligibility group nor any test of assets or resources.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Cells, Cell Structure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which three parts make up the generalized human cell?
opciones: Cell membrane, nucleus and the cytoplasm between them
Cell wall, nucleus and the cytoplasm between them
Cell membrane, nucleolus and the matrix between them
Cell membrane, mitochondrion and the plasma between them
preguntas.explicacion: Cells differ in size and shape, but the description everyone starts from has three parts: the cell or plasma membrane on the outside, the nucleus as the control center, and the cytoplasm in between, holding the organelles. Human cells have no cell wall, and the nucleolus is a region inside the nucleus rather than a part of its own.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k79 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which organisms are named as the most common cause of surgical site infections of the skin?
opciones: Staphylococcus aureus, then the other gram-positive organisms such as Enterococcus
Escherichia coli, followed by other gram-negative rods such as Pseudomonas species
Candida species, followed by other fungi that colonize the stratum corneum of the skin
Clostridium species, followed by other spore-forming organisms carried on the instruments
preguntas.explicacion: The pathogen most often behind a skin surgical site infection is Staphylococcus aureus, with other gram-positive organisms next: coagulase-negative staphylococci, enterococci and group A streptococci. Gram-negative rods such as Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas are also implicated, but they are not the leading group, and a surgical site infection is one occurring within 30 days of the procedure.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K 2L k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: After identity is verified, which patient factors should be asked about and recorded before the draw?
opciones: Any special diet, medications, supplements and herbal preparations
Insurance plan, the copayment collected and the status of the referral
Blood type, previous transfusions and history of blood donation
Height, weight and the vital signs recorded at the previous visit
preguntas.explicacion: Once identification is confirmed, fasting status and preparation are double-checked, and the patient is asked about the factors documented to affect results, with the answers recorded: herbal preparations, nutritional supplements, the medications taken and any diet out of the ordinary. Patients are likewise told to report vitamins and supplements before a test.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k9 k51 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is filled below its mark. Which way do the clotting times move, and why?
opciones: They lengthen, because the anticoagulant is in excess for the plasma present
They shorten, because the anticoagulant is in excess for the plasma present
They lengthen, because the tube loses part of its vacuum during the short draw
They shorten, because the citrate binds less calcium when the tube is not full
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate tubes come pre-loaded with a fixed amount of anticoagulant and marked with the volume of blood wanted. Draw less than that and the anticoagulant is in excess for the plasma collected, which prolongs the clotting time reported. Full filling is what keeps the nine-to-one proportion intact.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3E k60 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist spends three minutes searching for a vein with the tourniquet in place before drawing a chemistry panel. What effect does this have on the specimen?
opciones: Hemoconcentration, which falsely elevates laboratory results
Hemolysis, because the prolonged pressure ruptures red cells in the vein
Dilution of the sample with tissue fluid, as happens when a finger is squeezed
Platelet clumping in the tube, producing a falsely low platelet count
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet should come off within 1 minute, because prolonged constriction produces hemoconcentration and falsely elevated results; the WHO gives two minutes as the outer limit, and three minutes exceeds both. Tissue fluid dilution is the WHO's warning about squeezing a finger-prick, and platelet clumping is the EDTA artifact, not a tourniquet effect.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Stepping Up or Down a Step or Curb
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a cane reaches a curb going down. Which foot leads?
opciones: The weaker leg goes down first, after the cane is set on the lower level
The stronger leg goes down first, after the cane is set on the lower level
Both legs go down together, with the cane kept on the upper level for balance
The stronger leg goes down first, with the cane left on the upper level
preguntas.explicacion: Going down, the cane is placed below the step, the weak leg follows, and the strong leg comes down beside it. Going up reverses the order: the strong leg first, then the cane and the weak leg together. The saying that carries it is up with the good and down with the bad, and it holds even when both legs were operated on.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Clinical Significance and section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist doubts whether a confused patient can agree to the draw. Who may determine capacity?
opciones: A physician, a nurse practitioner or a physician assistant
A registered nurse, or the technician standing at the bedside
A judge, because capacity is settled by the judiciary system
Any adult relative present, once the doubt has been recorded
preguntas.explicacion: Because of licensure, assessing capacity is not work for a nurse, a nursing assistant, a technician or other support staff; any licensed physician can do it, and so can a nurse practitioner or a physician assistant. What a judge settles is competence, the legal question, and medical providers never determine that.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which additive does the WHO table describe as acting by complement inactivation?
opciones: Acid-citrate-dextrose in the pale yellow tube
Sodium citrate in the light blue coagulation tube
Sodium fluoride in the light gray tube
Lithium heparin in the light green PST
preguntas.explicacion: The mode of action column of Table 2.3 pairs acid-citrate-dextrose with complement inactivation, and the tube is used for HLA typing, paternity and DNA work. Sodium citrate removes calcium by forming calcium salts, sodium fluoride is the antiglycolytic agent that preserves glucose, and lithium heparin in the PST anticoagulates while its gel separates the plasma.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): Will I receive an identifying CLIA number?; CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Proficiency Testing
preguntas.subtema: CLIA identification number · PBT VI.F / VI.C · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What is the ten-character alphanumeric code printed on a CLIA certificate used for?
opciones: To identify and track that laboratory location throughout its history
To code the complexity categories the laboratory is allowed to perform
To identify the laboratory director on every test report issued
To link the certificate to the accreditation organization's file
preguntas.explicacion: Every certificate carries a ten-character alphanumeric CLIA number assigned to that laboratory location; the site uses it in all inquiries to the state agency and CMS. The number matters for proficiency testing too: samples must be tested only at the location holding that number, and testing another site's samples can bring sanctions against every certificate involved, waived sites included.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k87 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A serum specimen is centrifuged at the wrong speed and for too short a time. In Plebani's classification of errors, to which phase does this belong?
opciones: Pre-analytical, the phase of sorting, aliquoting, labeling and centrifugation inside the laboratory
Pre-pre-analytical, the phase of test request, identification, collection, handling and transport outside the lab
Analytical, the phase of interference, sample mix-ups, undetected QC failure and equipment malfunction
Post-analytical, the phase of validation, reporting, turnaround time and manual transcription
preguntas.explicacion: Plebani splits the front end in two: the pre-pre-analytical phase covers test requesting, patient and specimen identification, collection, container choice, handling, storage and transport, mostly done by staff outside the laboratory, while the pre-analytical phase proper starts once the laboratory accepts the specimen and includes sorting, pour-off, aliquoting, pipetting, labeling and centrifugation time and speed. Analytical and post-analytical errors come later.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Issues of Concern: Referrals
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(3) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A physician assistant working under a physician's license is sued over care given in the office. Which doctrine pulls the physician into the case?
opciones: Respondeat superior
Res ipsa loquitur
Proximate causation
Standard of care
preguntas.explicacion: Midlevel providers are an integral part of medicine but practice under a physician's license, and the physician answers for the care they deliver. When a suit comes, the plaintiff aims at the supervising physician under respondeat superior. Causation and the standard of care are elements the plaintiff must prove, not the doctrine that reaches the supervisor.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Identify Relevant Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Registration red flags · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient registering by telephone gives an address that does not match the one on the report the office pulled. Under the Red Flags Rule, what is that?
opciones: A red flag among personal identifying information, which the program must answer
A covered account, because the practice will bill him after the service is given
A creditor test, since the office is deciding whether to let him pay in instalments
A reportable breach, since his information may already have been misused by someone
preguntas.explicacion: Red flags are the patterns, practices or activities that point to possible identity theft, and the categories to consider include alerts from a credit reporting company, suspicious documents such as identification that looks altered, and personal identifying information that does not hold together, with an address that fails to match the credit report given as the first example.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part B (Medical Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does a patient with Original Medicare pay each month, and what does she pay before Part B starts to pay, in 2026?
opciones: A premium of $202.90 a month, and a deductible of $283 once each year
A premium of $202.90 a month, and a deductible of $1,736 for each benefit period
A premium of $311 a month, and a deductible of $283 once during each year
No premium for most people, and a deductible of $434 once during each year
preguntas.explicacion: The Part B premium in 2026 is $202.90 a month, higher for some incomes, and it is owed every month whether or not any covered service is used. The Part B deductible is $283 and is paid once a year. The $1,736 figure is the Part A deductible, which is owed for each hospital benefit period rather than once a year.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: standard of care
preguntas.subtema: Standard of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.b · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: Is the same standard of care applied to everyone whose conduct is judged?
opciones: No: professionals are held higher and children lower than the average adult
No: professionals are held higher and children to the very same adult level
Yes: the reasonable person standard applies to every defendant identically
Yes: unless the defendant carries professional liability insurance coverage
preguntas.explicacion: The usual measure is the reasonable person standard — what the average person would have done in those circumstances. Children are judged against a reasonable child of the same age, and higher or broader standards apply to professionals and people in authority, so a physician's work is measured against a reasonable physician. Without that split, professionals would get away with a great deal.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, biopsy
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A whole suspicious lump is taken out and sent to the laboratory. Which kind of biopsy is that?
opciones: An excisional biopsy, since the entire area was removed
An incisional biopsy, since the entire area was removed
A fine-needle aspiration, since the entire area was removed
A core biopsy, since a wide needle removed the entire area
preguntas.explicacion: A biopsy is the removal of cells or tissue for a pathologist to examine. The common types differ in how much comes out: an incisional biopsy takes only a sample, an excisional biopsy takes the whole lump or suspicious area, and a needle biopsy draws tissue or fluid with a needle, called a core biopsy when the needle is wide and a fine-needle aspiration when it is thin.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(i), (g)(2)(vi) and (g)(2)(viii), Information and Training
preguntas.subtema: Training conditions · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Under the standard, bloodborne pathogens training must be provided in which way?
opciones: Free to the employee, and inside working hours
At the employee's expense, but on paid time
During unpaid time, by an OSHA-certified trainer
Free, but only for full-time employees
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(i) requires the employer to train each exposed employee, to do it free of charge and during working hours, and to institute a program and ensure participation. Paragraph (g)(2)(viii) asks only that the person conducting the training be knowledgeable in the subject as it relates to that workplace; no OSHA certification of trainers is mentioned. The material must also suit the educational level, literacy and language of the employees, per (g)(2)(vi).

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Intrinsic Pathway; and Table 18.1 Clotting Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k57) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Blood placed in a plain glass tube clots on its own. Which factor starts that in-vitro clotting, and through which pathway?
opciones: Factor XII (Hageman factor), through the intrinsic pathway
Factor III (tissue factor), through the extrinsic pathway
Factor IV (calcium ions), through the common pathway
Factor I (fibrinogen), through the fibrinolytic pathway
preguntas.explicacion: The intrinsic, or contact activation, pathway is most often started when factor XII, the Hageman factor, touches foreign material, and a blood sample put into a glass test tube is the classic example. Factor XII then activates XI and IX, and VIII with IX activates factor X. Tissue factor belongs to the extrinsic route, calcium acts throughout the cascade, and fibrinogen is the precursor of fibrin.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.4 Diseases, Disorders and Injuries of the Integumentary System, Burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(1) (2027 I.C.6.g(1)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a sunburn that is red, painful and swollen but has no blisters. How is that burn classified?
opciones: First degree, since it reaches only the epidermis
Second degree, since it reaches only the epidermis
Third degree, since it reaches only the epidermis
Fourth degree, since it reaches only the epidermis
preguntas.explicacion: Burn depth sets the class. A first-degree burn is superficial and affects only the epidermis; it hurts and swells but heals on its own in a few days, and mild sunburn is the everyday example. Blisters mean a second-degree burn, which has reached part of the dermis.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Poisoning first aid", Poison Control
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.h · 2027 I.B.8.h · RMA III.I.1.b
