preguntas.pregunta: What should be taken to the hospital with a patient who has swallowed a poison?
opciones: The container the substance came in, if it can be picked up safely
A written list of every medicine the patient has ever been given
A sample of the vomit collected in a specimen cup for the laboratory
The neutralizing agent the label recommends for that substance
preguntas.explicacion: The container of the poison goes to the hospital with the patient whenever it can be taken. Poison control gives the further instructions, and if convulsions start, seizure first aid is given. Nothing is used to neutralize the poison unless poison control or a provider says so, and no flame or lighter is used where gases may be present.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E13 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A platelet count comes back under the 20,000 mark of the notification list on a patient with no bleeding at all. Which possibility does the notification list tell the laboratory to rule out first?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia caused by the EDTA in the tube itself
Dilution of the specimen by an intravenous infusion nearby
A clot in the tube that has trapped part of the platelets
Interference from lipemia on the optical platelet channel
preguntas.explicacion: A platelet count below 20,000 is listed as needing urgent notification because of the bleeding risk, and the note attached to it is a caution rather than a diagnosis: exclude EDTA-induced thrombocytopenia before the call is made. The upper limit on the same line, above one million, is flagged for the opposite reason, the risk of thrombosis.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Which fittings does the WHO ask for in a dedicated outpatient phlebotomy cubicle?
opciones: A clean surface with two chairs, a hand wash basin and alcohol hand rub
A clean surface with one chair, a sharps bin and a lockable drug cabinet
A clean surface with two chairs, a fridge for the tubes and a light box
A clean surface with one chair, a curtain rail and a wall-mounted screen
preguntas.explicacion: In an outpatient department or clinic the cubicle should hold two chairs at a clean surface, one for the patient and one for the phlebotomist; a basin for washing hands, supplied with soap, running water and paper towels; and alcohol hand rub. The blood-sampling room should also have a comfortable reclining couch fitted with an arm rest.

preguntas.subtema: Culpability terms · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.3 · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does the enforcement regulation define willful neglect?
opciones: Reckless indifference toward the duty to comply, or a conscious and intentional failure
An act or omission the entity would have caught by exercising reasonable diligence
The business care and prudence expected of someone trying to satisfy a legal requirement
Any violation that the entity failed to correct inside the thirty day period allowed
preguntas.explicacion: The enforcement subpart lines up three defined terms. Willful neglect is reckless indifference toward the duty to comply, or a failure to comply that is conscious and intentional. Reasonable cause is an act or omission the entity knew of, or would have known of with reasonable diligence, that nonetheless falls short of willful neglect. Reasonable diligence itself is the business care and prudence expected in similar circumstances.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Understanding "Off-Label Use" of Waived Tests and its example
preguntas.subtema: Off-label use = high complexity · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F CLIA · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic modifies a waived glucose meter's procedure so it can test patients whose hematocrit is outside the range in the insert. Under CLIA, what happens to that testing?
opciones: It becomes high complexity and needs a Certificate of Compliance or Accreditation
It stays waived as long as the modification is written into the site procedure manual
It becomes moderate complexity and can continue under the same Certificate of Waiver
It becomes a PPM procedure that only the physician or midlevel practitioner may run
preguntas.explicacion: Using a cleared test outside its intended use is off-label use. Any off-label use of a waived test is treated as high-complexity testing, which brings in proficiency testing, verified performance specifications, quality control, quality assessment and personnel qualifications. A site with only a Certificate of Waiver would have to upgrade to a Certificate of Compliance or of Accreditation first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Blood Cells, Glucose)
preguntas.subtema: Ascorbic acid interference · CPT D4 4G · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking large doses of vitamin C has a urine reagent strip run. Which pair of pads can read falsely negative?
opciones: The blood and glucose pads
The protein and bilirubin pads
The bilirubin and ketone pads
The ketone and urobilinogen pads
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is listed among the causes of a false-negative blood reaction, alongside captopril, a high specific gravity, acid urine and proteinuria, and among the causes of a false-negative glucose, with high specific gravity and uric acid. It also appears on the nitrite and leukocyte lists, though neither of those pads is paired here. Bilirubin and ketones read falsely low in stale specimens, and urobilinogen after daylight exposure or with formaldehyde.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, OTC Drug Facts Label: What's On The Label
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · RMA III.G.3.d
preguntas.pregunta: On an over-the-counter Drug Facts label, which heading tells the patient how much to take and how often?
opciones: The Directions section
The Warnings section
The Purpose section
The Uses section
preguntas.explicacion: The Drug Facts panel is fixed: active ingredients with their amount per dosage unit, purpose as the product's action or pharmacologic category, uses as the symptoms or diseases it treats or prevents, warnings covering when not to use it and when to call a doctor, directions with how much, how, how often and how long, inactive ingredients, and other information such as storage. Dietary supplements carry a different panel.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging, Computed Tomography
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which imaging technique combines many cross-sectional X-rays into slices, and what is its main drawback?
opciones: Computed tomography, which delivers a much higher radiation dose
Magnetic resonance imaging, which delivers a much higher radiation dose
Ultrasonography, which delivers a much higher radiation dose than X-ray
Positron emission tomography, which cannot show soft tissue detail
preguntas.explicacion: Tomography means imaging by sections. In a CT study the scanner turns all the way around the patient taking X-ray images, and a computer builds them into slices detailed enough to measure a mass in millimeters. The price is radiation: the dose is many times that of a plain X-ray, which matters most in children and in repeated scans.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: Surgical scrub position · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: During a surgical hand scrub, how are the hands and forearms held while rinsing, and why?
opciones: Hands above the elbows, so water runs off the least clean part
Hands below the elbows, as in the routine wash at the sink
Hands flat against the sink, so the water reaches the cuticles
Hands at the same height, so the soap is rinsed off evenly
preguntas.explicacion: In a routine handwash the hands stay below the elbows, so the water travels from the less contaminated area toward the more contaminated one. The surgical scrub turns that around: once scrubbed, the hands are the cleanest part and the forearms and the elbows are the dirtier end, so the hands are held up and away from the body and the water runs from the fingertips down toward the elbows. Reverse the position and the forearm gets washed over the hand.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which peripheral pulse is used for the routine adult vital signs, and why?
opciones: The radial, because it is easy to reach and barely disturbs the seated patient
The brachial, because it lies over the artery the cuff will occlude in a moment
The carotid, because its wide vessel gives the clearest beat to count against a watch
The femoral, because a central vessel resists the changes that cool hands produce
preguntas.explicacion: The radial artery is the site used in routine adult examinations: it is accessible at the wrist and asking for a wrist costs the patient almost nothing. Like other distal pulses it also reflects circulatory trouble early. The carotid is the resuscitation site in adults and the femoral is the sensitive one in septic shock.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Surgical Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k80 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.j
preguntas.pregunta: An alcohol-based skin prep has just been applied and the surgeon reaches for the cautery. What must happen first?
opciones: Let the prep dry for the time the manufacturer specifies, and be sure none has pooled
Wipe the prep off with a dry sterile sponge, since the antisepsis is complete on contact
Cover the prepped area with a moist drape, which keeps the vapor away from the cautery
Raise the oxygen flow, which dilutes the vapor faster than room air can carry it away
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based preps are fuel. Prevention rests on following the manufacturer's dry time and stopping the fluid from pooling under drapes, along with re-holstering the cautery and keeping currents low. Raising the oxygen does the opposite of helping: a higher oxidizer level lowers the temperature at which a fuel ignites, so the lowest oxygen that maintains saturation is used.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Clinical Drug Testing", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Detection windows · CPT D4 4J k86 drug screening · PBT V.C.5 · RMA III.C.4.a.i urine drug screen
preguntas.pregunta: How soon after intake do drugs generally appear in urine, and how long are they detectable after a small dose?
opciones: They appear in 1 to 2 hours and are detectable for 1 to 3 days
They appear in 1 to 2 hours and are detectable for 1 to 3 weeks
They appear in 6 to 8 hours and are detectable for 1 to 3 days
They appear within minutes and are detectable for about 48 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Drugs generally first show up in urine one to two hours after intake, and after a small dose they can be found for one to three days. In plasma the times are shorter, often one to two days. Because metabolism differs from drug to drug, the first and last detection times differ too, and for most substances the metabolite outlasts the parent drug.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Function
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement, incident investigation · RMA III.C.1.a quality assurance
preguntas.pregunta: An accredited hospital runs a root cause analysis after a sentinel event. What is that analysis meant to find?
opciones: The system and process failures behind the event, reached by asking why until deeper causes appear
The individual whose mistake led to the event, so that retraining can be assigned to that person
Whether the occurrence fits the definition of a sentinel event or only of a preventable adverse one
Whether the risk manager received the report inside three business days of the event happening
preguntas.explicacion: A root cause analysis has to look past the individual mistake to the system around it: human and workflow factors, staffing, communication, technology and environment, with why asked again of every answer. A strong analysis brings leadership and frontline staff in, explains anything marked not applicable, and ends in a corrective action plan. The three-business-day clock belongs to a state risk-manager reporting statute.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Advantage Plans (Part C); and Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Besides a Medicare Advantage plan, which of these delivers Part A and Part B benefits through a private plan?
opciones: PACE, the Program of All-inclusive Care for elderly people
A Medigap policy sold by a private insurance company
A stand-alone Medicare drug plan approved by Medicare
A state Medicaid program covering dual eligible people
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare health plans deliver Part A and Part B benefits and generally come from private companies under contract with Medicare. Besides Medicare Advantage they take in Medicare Cost Plans, demonstrations and pilots, and PACE, the Program of All-inclusive Care for elderly people. Medigap helps pay the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than delivering the benefits, a drug plan covers Part D, and Medicaid is a joint federal-state program.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Carbohydrates — Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(a) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reading a label asks which parts of her food count as carbohydrate. Which three forms does food carbohydrate take?
opciones: Sugars, starches, and fiber
Sugars, starches, and glycogen
Sugars, starches, and sugar alcohols
Sugars, fiber, and amino acids
preguntas.explicacion: Carbohydrate reaches the body in three forms, and all three are needed: sugars, starches and fiber. Sugars and most starches are broken down into glucose that circulates in the blood as energy. Fiber is the part that is not broken down at all. Amino acids belong to protein, not to carbohydrate.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 2.3 Instruments of Microscopy, Light Microscopes
preguntas.subtema: Total magnification · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.e · RMA III.B.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A slide is examined with a 10x ocular lens and the 40x objective in place. What is the total magnification?
preguntas.explicacion: Total magnification on a compound microscope is the ocular magnification multiplied by the objective magnification, so a 10x eyepiece with a 40x objective gives 400x. Oculars are typically 10x and objectives run from 4x to 100x, with the value stamped on the metal casing. The coarse knob is for the 4x and 10x objectives; from 40x upward only the fine knob is used.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 3, 8 and 10
preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k51 k57 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A purple EDTA tube for a complete blood count stops filling at roughly half its volume. What does the order-of-draw table require for this tube?
opciones: A full draw, the same requirement it places on citrate and fluoride tubes
A half draw is acceptable, because EDTA is used in a fixed concentration
A full draw only when a cross-match rather than a blood count is ordered
A full draw only when the tube will be held longer than five days before use
preguntas.explicacion: Three rows of the table carry the note that a full draw is required: the citrate tube, the EDTA tube and the fluoride/oxalate tube. It applies to the EDTA tube whichever of its listed uses is ordered, hematology or cross-match, so a half-filled tube is redrawn.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cholesterol Screening", section Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k46 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: The requisition reads 'lipid panel: family history of premature ASCVD'. The patient ate 3 hours ago. What should happen?
opciones: Fasting is mandatory in this case; the draw should be rescheduled
Non-fasting sampling is acceptable for any lipid panel nowadays
Proceed, since fasting matters only when the triglycerides are of interest
Proceed; fasting is required only to diagnose metabolic syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting is no longer routine for every lipid profile, but there are settings where it is preferred, and one where it is required: screening and follow-up in a patient whose family history holds genetic hyperlipidemia or premature ASCVD. The others in that group are diagnosing hypertriglyceridemia, judging residual risk in a treated patient, and assessing the risk of pancreatitis. Metabolic syndrome sits on the non-fasting side.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements, Hemopoietic Growth Factors
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which hormone drives megakaryocytes to produce platelets, and where is it made?
opciones: Thrombopoietin, from the liver and kidneys
Erythropoietin, from the kidneys
Colony-stimulating factor, from the marrow
Interleukins, from leukocytes and marrow
preguntas.explicacion: Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone made by the liver and the kidneys, and it is what pushes megakaryocytes on to produce platelets. Erythropoietin, from the kidney, raises red cell output instead. Colony-stimulating factors steer myeloblasts toward granular white cells or monocytes, and interleukins are cytokine signals released by many kinds of cell.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: One well-known account splits a message into 55, 38 and 7 percent. What does the 38 percent stand for?
opciones: The tone of voice the sender uses
The actual words the sender speaks
The body language the sender shows
The pace at which the two people talk
preguntas.explicacion: In that account body language carries 55 percent, tone of voice 38 percent, and the spoken words only 7 percent. A separate figure often taught is that 80 percent of communication is nonverbal. Pace of the conversation belongs to nonverbal signals but has no percentage attached.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation; and "Peripheral Line Placement", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: After the tourniquet is tightened, the phlebotomist can no longer feel the patient's radial pulse. What does this indicate?
opciones: It is too tight; it should stop venous flow but leave arterial flow intact
It is correct; the pulse disappears once the veins are fully engorged
It is too loose; a properly placed tourniquet always abolishes the radial pulse
It is correct, provided it is released within two minutes of placement
preguntas.explicacion: The tightness is managed to halt venous flow while maintaining arterial blood flow, and the peripheral line chapter repeats it: tight enough to swell the veins without shutting off arterial flow. A lost radial pulse means the artery is occluded, so the band is too tight regardless of how quickly it will be released.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3: Syringes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.c · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why must insulin be drawn with an insulin syringe and never with one marked in milliliters?
opciones: Insulin is prescribed in units, and only an insulin syringe is marked in units
Insulin is prescribed in milliliters, and only an insulin syringe converts them
Insulin syringes carry a filter that keeps particles out of the dose drawn up
Insulin syringes carry a longer needle that reaches the muscle under the fat
preguntas.explicacion: Providers prescribe insulin in units rather than milliliters, and an insulin syringe is calibrated in units, so a syringe marked in milliliters must never be used for it. An orange cap makes these syringes quick to recognize, but the markings are still verified before use. A filter belongs to the blunt fill needle used with an ampule, and insulin goes into subcutaneous tissue, not into muscle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and palpation · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The vein a patient offers lies under a firm pale mark left by repeated punctures. Why is that site avoided?
opciones: Residual scar tissue at a previously attempted site is a contraindication
Scarred skin cannot be disinfected with alcohol and needs povidone iodine
Scarred skin is where the tourniquet must sit, so the vein cannot be seen
Scarred skin bleeds longer, so a pressure dressing would have to be used
preguntas.explicacion: A site attempted before and left with residual scar tissue is listed as a contraindication in its own right. On palpation these veins can also feel fibrosed, which is another entry on the same list, so the arm is examined and a different vein chosen rather than the old track reused.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation and Challenges
preguntas.subtema: Measuring access · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Same-day slots are now available and the manager wants to know whether the change is holding. Which measure does the guide name?
opciones: Appointment availability checked daily, such as the third next available appointment
The number of visits each clinician completed daily, compared with the year before
The count of appointments booked in past months, which shows how demand has moved
The share of calls the front desk answers before the telephone rings a third time
preguntas.explicacion: Once same-day appointments are possible, the practice is told to gauge whether the change works by tracking, day by day, how available appointments are; the example given is the third next available appointment. Counting appointments already held will not serve: the guide warns that the number of visits completed reflects the supply of clinical time more than the demand for it.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Needles on tubing · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Why are winged-steel needles and other needles attached to tubing singled out as a disposal hazard?
opciones: The tubing makes them hard to place in a sharps container
The tubing holds enough blood to soak through the container
The tubing keeps the shield from sliding over the used needle
The tubing has to be cut with scissors before it is discarded
preguntas.explicacion: A needle on a length of flexible tubing is awkward to get into a sharps container, and that awkwardness is itself an injury hazard. The related habit of parking the needle somewhere convenient, in a drip chamber, an intravenous port or bag, or even the bedding, leaves an exposed sharp behind. Cutting a contaminated needle is not an option either: shearing or breaking one is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (Preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.8.c(3)
preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine was preserved with formaldehyde, and the laboratory is asked to run a dipstick on an aliquot. Which pattern of false results does formaldehyde produce on reagent strips?
opciones: False positives for urobilinogen, glucose, the peroxidase reaction and leukocyte esterase
False negatives for the leukocyte esterase reaction, with the other strip reactions unaltered
False positives for albumin only, with the pH of the specimen shifted toward acidity
False negatives for glucose and ketones, with the specific gravity reading raised
preguntas.explicacion: Preservatives are reached for only now and then, precisely because they distort the reading: with formaldehyde in the pot, strip reactions for urobilinogen, glucose, the peroxidase reaction and leukocyte esterase can all come up falsely positive. Mercury salts push leukocyte esterase the other way, to a false negative; thymol fakes albumin; and hydrochloric acid, used to hold cell structures and for steroid assays, moves the pH.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT) Test, What is it used for?; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalized patient is receiving heparin. Which coagulation test is used to monitor that drug, and in which tube is it collected?
opciones: The partial thromboplastin time, in a light blue sodium citrate tube
The prothrombin time with INR, in a light blue sodium citrate tube
The partial thromboplastin time, drawn in a dark green sodium heparin tube
The erythrocyte sedimentation rate, in a black-top citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Monitoring people taking heparin is a use of the PTT (also called aPTT), which measures the seconds the sample takes to clot; the PT/INR is the test tied to warfarin. Like all coagulation studies, the PTT goes in the light blue citrate tube of the WHO table, never in a heparin tube. The ESR measures how fast red cells settle and is a marker of inflammation, not of heparin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Informed Consent Prior to Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Elements of informed consent · CPT D1 1D k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k211 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.2 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which elements do most state statutes set as the minimum for an informed consent discussion?
opciones: Nature, benefits, risks and alternatives, plus the patient's capacity
Cost, insurance coverage, the referral needed and the appointment date
Diagnosis, prognosis, the physician's credentials and the facility's rating
Names of the staff involved, the equipment used and the disposal method
preguntas.explicacion: In most American jurisdictions the statutory floor covers five things: the nature of the therapy, what it stands to achieve, what it risks, which reasonable alternatives exist, and whether the patient has the capacity to decide. The reasoning behind the list is that patients own their bodies and choose which risks to run, yet cannot weigh a risk or an alternative that nobody has described to them. Consent gathered without those pieces is what tort claims are later built on.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine 24-hour volume (003425), How to Prepare for the Test; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Specific Gravity)
preguntas.subtema: 24-hour interfering factors · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(c) · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a 24-hour urine protein test had a CT scan with contrast dye two days ago. Why does this matter?
opciones: Contrast dye given within 3 days before the collection can affect the results, so the provider should be told
Contrast dye given within 3 hours before the collection can affect the results, so a short delay is enough
Contrast dye can affect the results only if it was given during the 24-hour collection period itself
Contrast dye lowers the specific gravity reading, so the collection should be extended to 48 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Among the factors that can distort a 24-hour urine result is radiographic contrast given within the 3 days before the test, along with dehydration, emotional stress, strenuous exercise, vaginal fluid in the urine and urinary tract infection. Three hours would be far too short a window. Contrast media falsely raise, not lower, specific gravity, and the fix is to inform the provider, not to lengthen the collection.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Personal Space
preguntas.subtema: Personal space · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2I k24 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant leans in about two feet from a seated patient to check a dressing. Which space zone has been entered?
opciones: The personal zone, the space usually kept for friends and family
The social zone, the one used in social and business exchanges
The public zone, which generally keeps any physical contact out
The zone under eighteen inches, kept for close relationships
preguntas.explicacion: Proxemics puts the personal zone at eighteen inches to four feet, the social zone at four to ten feet, and the public zone beyond ten feet. Staff normally talk with patients in the social zone to hold professional boundaries, but assessing and doing procedures moves them into the personal zone, where the patient may feel psychological discomfort.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An electronic device reports a very low value in a patient who looks well. How is that handled?
opciones: The value is confirmed manually, since these devices can misread outside the normal band
The value is accepted, since an electronic device removes the human error of listening
The value is repeated on the same device, which is enough to settle the question
The value is charted with a note, and no further reading is taken during that visit
preguntas.explicacion: Automated devices are reliable in the normal range but tend to read hypotensive values too high and hypertensive values too low, and it is exactly the abnormal readings that matter clinically. When a machine gives a suspicious value it is checked by hand. Unexpected findings are repeated with correct technique before decisions are made.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: Site by age · CPT D3 k55 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: For a finger-prick in an adult, which fingers does WHO Table 7.1 recommend, and which does it say to avoid?
opciones: The middle and ring fingers; avoid the thumb and index finger, and the little finger
The thumb and index finger; avoid the middle and ring fingers, and also the little finger
The index and middle fingers; avoid the thumb, the ring finger and the little finger
Any finger except the thumb, provided the lancet is placed on the fingerprint lines
preguntas.explicacion: Table 7.1 recommends the second and third fingers, that is the middle and ring finger. The lancet goes on the side of the pad, set to cut across the fingerprint ridges rather than to follow them. It says to keep off the thumb and the index finger, which callus, and off the little finger, whose tissue is thin. The lancet is not laid ALONG the fingerprint lines: it crosses them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Abandonment, Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Inadvertent abandonment · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A physician leaves on a three-month sabbatical without telling patients or arranging emergency coverage. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, since care stopped with no notice and no substitute clinician
As intentional abandonment, since an absence of that length is planned months beforehand
As no abandonment, because nobody was ever told the relationship had come to an end
As an ending chosen by the patients, who were free to find another clinician meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: Liability for abandonment does not depend on intending to end the relationship. The example given is precisely this one: a healthcare professional who neither notifies patients nor sets up emergency coverage before a long vacation or sabbatical has abandoned them inadvertently. Leaving a patient's calls or e-mails unanswered, and failing to follow up after surgery or after a new medication is started, are treated the same way.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Packaging
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.D.2.n
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between sequential and nonsequential double wrapping?
opciones: Sequential wraps one sheet after the other; nonsequential wraps both sheets at the same time
Sequential wraps two sheets at once; nonsequential adds the second sheet after the cycle ends
Sequential uses woven wrap outside and nonwoven inside; nonsequential reverses those layers
Sequential is used for rigid containers; nonsequential is used only for peel-open pouches
preguntas.explicacion: Both make a double barrier. The sequential wrap uses two sheets applied one after the other, so a package ends up inside a package. The nonsequential, or simultaneous, method uses two sheets wrapped together in one pass, which saves time. Either way the wrapping is done so that the package does not tent or gap.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Tripod Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · RMA III.F.2 · NCMA 2B.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient short of breath sits leaning forward with the elbows resting on the knees. What is this called?
opciones: The tripod position, assumed to enhance lung expansion and air exchange
The lawnchair position, with hips and knees flexed above the level of the heart
The frog-leg position, with hips and knees flexed and rotated outward
The high Fowler position, sitting fully upright at a 90-degree angle
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who cannot get enough air often adopt this posture without being told, leaning forward on their elbows or on a table. It opens the chest and improves air exchange, and it is a visible sign of pulmonary distress during the inspection stage of a chest examination. Lawnchair and frog-leg are variations of supine, used for comfort and for perineal access.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.l · 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches syncope?
opciones: A brief loss of consciousness and postural tone with spontaneous recovery
A loss of consciousness with jerking of the limbs and a slow recovery
A period of confusion and slurred speech with the eyes open throughout
A drop in blood pressure on standing that leaves the patient dizzy only
preguntas.explicacion: Syncope is a transient loss of consciousness and of postural tone from a fall in blood flow to the brain, followed by recovery on its own. It may come without warning or after dizziness, lightheadedness, sweating, nausea and visual disturbance. It accounts for 1 % to 3.5 % of emergency department visits.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, When to Use a Tourniquet; and eCFR, 49 CFR 173.199, Category B infectious substances (UN3373 Biological substance, Category B; eCFR vigente 2026-09-04)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet for hemorrhage · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a / 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: If a tourniquet becomes necessary for life-threatening limb bleeding, where is it placed?
opciones: 2 to 3 inches above the wound, avoiding the joint, noting the time
Directly over the wound, tightened until the bleeding stops
4 to 5 finger widths above the wound, released every 2 minutes
Just below the joint nearest the wound, loosened every 10 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: A tourniquet is used only when continuous pressure has not stopped extremely severe bleeding, and it is applied to the limb 2 to 3 inches, 5 to 7.7 centimeters, above the wound, avoiding the joint and moving above it toward the torso if necessary, preferably over clothing or padding rather than bare skin. The time of application is written down or memorized and told to responders, because a tourniquet left on too long injures nerves and tissue. Four to five finger widths and two minutes are venipuncture tourniquet figures, not first-aid ones.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1283(b), Standard: Test records
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory clearing out its storeroom asks whether the analyser printouts filed with old patient results can be thrown away. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Records of patient testing, printouts included, have to be kept
Printouts may go once the result is reported and verified
Printouts are kept only for tests sent to an outside laboratory
Printouts are kept only when the specimen failed acceptability
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond the four items the record system must contain, the same standard adds a plain sentence: records of patient testing, including instrument printouts where they exist, must be retained. There is no carve-out for tests that were already reported, for referred work, or for problem specimens; the retention rule covers the patient testing record as a whole.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(j)(1) and (j)(2), Documentation and retention period
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA documentation retention · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How long must a covered entity retain its HIPAA policies, procedures and other required documentation?
opciones: Six years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later
Three years from creation, matching OSHA training records
Thirty years, matching OSHA employee medical records
Ten years from creation, matching the period for Medicare claims documentation
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(j) requires policies and procedures to be kept in written or electronic form, together with every communication the rule requires in writing and every action, activity or designation it requires to be documented, for six years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later. The same section requires a privacy official, a complaints contact, workforce training, safeguards, a complaint process, sanctions, mitigation and no retaliation. Three and thirty years are OSHA periods, not HIPAA ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ECG T Wave" (NBK538264)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A strip comes out with tall, narrow, symmetrical T waves through most of the leads. Which disturbance is that linked with?
opciones: Hyperkalemia, though the height does not track the potassium level
Hypokalemia, though the height does not track the potassium level
Hypothermia, though the height does not track the temperature
Hypercalcemia, though the height does not track the calcium level
preguntas.explicacion: Peaked T waves go with a high potassium, and they run narrower than the broad hyperacute waves of early infarction. How high they stand does not necessarily match how high the potassium is; as it climbs, the P wave flattens, the QRS widens and the PR lengthens.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", History and Physical; Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Tetanus after a puncture · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k95 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Besides the bloodborne pathogens, which vaccination history is reviewed after a puncture wound from a needle?
opciones: Tetanus, since the date of the last dose guides what is given
Influenza, since the season decides whether a dose is due
Measles, since a worker without immunity may be excluded
Hepatitis A, since the wound was contaminated with blood
preguntas.explicacion: A needlestick is a puncture wound, so tetanus is assessed alongside the bloodborne pathogens. Three things decide what is given: the kind of wound, how long ago the last tetanus-containing dose was received, and whether the primary series was ever completed. Hepatitis B status is reviewed at the same visit, because it decides whether immune globulin is needed. Hepatitis C has no vaccine, and measles immunity is a work-restriction question rather than a wound question.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Skeletal System: Appendicular Skeleton; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology: Appendicular Skeleton
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of bones belongs to the appendicular skeleton?
opciones: Clavicle, scapula, humerus, radius and ulna
Sternum, ribs, vertebrae and the hyoid bone
Parietal, temporal, frontal and occipital bones
Malleus, incus, stapes and the nasal conchae
preguntas.explicacion: The appendicular skeleton is the limbs and the girdles that hang them on the trunk: clavicle and scapula above, the coxal bones below, and the arm, forearm, thigh, leg, hand and foot bones. The thoracic cage, the vertebral column, the skull and the auditory ossicles all belong to the axial skeleton.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", sections History (1973, 1986) and Treatment Refusal
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA E.1.d (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which 1986 measure made the right to refuse treatment enforceable for patients in facilities using federal insurance programs?
opciones: 42 CFR § 482.13, issued by the executive branch
The AHA's 1973 patient bill of rights
Cruzan v. Director, decided by the Supreme Court
The Norwood-Dingell Bill passed by Congress
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR § 482.13 dates from 1986 and is the founding catalog of patient rights that can actually be enforced in the United States, though its reach extends only to places where federal health insurance programs are used, and it confirmed that a patient with capacity may refuse any treatment. The AHA bill of 1973 had little enforceability, Cruzan came in 1990, and Congress rejected Norwood-Dingell.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Dietary Supplements — Federal Regulation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k27 vitamins and supplements · CMA I.A.6.g(2) · 2027 I.A.6.g(2) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the FDA checks a dietary supplement before it reaches the shelf. What is the correct answer?
opciones: No; unlike medicines, supplements need no FDA approval before being sold
Yes; supplements clear the same FDA approval process that medicines clear
No; but each batch must be tested by the FDA before it may be shipped
Yes; but only for supplements that carry a claim about a body function
preguntas.explicacion: Medicines have to be approved by the FDA before they can be sold; supplements do not. The company itself is responsible for holding evidence that the product is safe and that the label is truthful, and unless a new dietary ingredient is involved that evidence never goes to the agency beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), Reflecting
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k40 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.g / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: The patient says, 'Last time they stuck me four times and I nearly passed out.' The phlebotomist replies, 'Four sticks, and you nearly passed out.' Which technique is this?
opciones: Reflecting
Summarizing
Clarifying
Silence
preguntas.explicacion: Reflecting means saying the patient's own words back, at times exactly as they were spoken, to show that the listening is real. Summarizing restates the account in the provider's words to build a shared understanding; clarifying uses guiding statements to draw out more detail; and silence shows attention by not interrupting, which is a different way of listening, not a way of answering.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: Method actually used · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which urine collection method is used most often for culture, even though it is not the one least likely to be contaminated?
opciones: Clean-catch midstream, because it is neither invasive nor uncomfortable for the patient
Straight catheterization, because it is quick and needs no cooperation at all from the patient
Suprapubic aspiration, because it is quick and needs no cooperation from the patient
Sterile bag collection, because it is simple and needs no cooperation from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Suprapubic puncture gives the cleanest specimen and single catheterization is the next best, but both are invasive, uncomfortable and labor-intensive, so they are kept for patients who cannot collect their own. The clean-catch midstream is therefore the routine method, and its colony counts agree reasonably well with those two. Bag collection is a pediatric option for children who are not toilet trained.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Priority Mail Express
preguntas.subtema: Express delivery days · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A transplant center needs a package on a Sunday. Which feature of Priority Mail Express answers that need?
opciones: It delivers seven days a week, all year, with limited exceptions to that rule
It delivers on weekdays and adds a Saturday run when the label is bought online
It delivers seven days a week only to post office box addresses in large markets
It delivers on any day agreed with the receiving office when the package is sent
preguntas.explicacion: Express is the fastest domestic service, and it runs on every day of the week and every day of the year, limited exceptions aside. Most addresses see it in one to three days, and that delivery time carries a money-back guarantee, which the two-to-three-day estimate for Priority Mail does not.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Minimum essential coverage; and Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act protections · CMAA 5 k73, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which coverage counts as minimum essential coverage?
opciones: A job-based plan, a Marketplace plan, Medicare, Medicaid or CHIP coverage
A job-based plan or a Marketplace plan, but not a public program coverage
A grandfathered policy bought before March 23, 2010, and no other coverage
Any policy that pays cash benefits toward hospital stays and lost earnings
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is any plan meeting the health care law's coverage requirement; the examples given are job-based plans, Marketplace plans, Medicaid with CHIP, and Medicare, and TRICARE and certain other coverage qualify too. Public programs are therefore included. Grandfathered policies are individual plans bought on or before March 23, 2010, a category of their own, and a cash indemnity policy is not health coverage in this sense.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Administrative Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Contingency plan · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What must a practice's contingency plan under the Security Rule provide for?
opciones: Backing up ePHI, restoring lost data and running critical processes in emergency mode
Buying a second electronic health record from a different vendor as a permanent standby
Printing the whole record of every active patient at the close of each business day
Notifying the Secretary of any system failure that lasts longer than a single work shift
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan is the administrative safeguard for responding to emergencies or other events that damage the systems holding ePHI. It has to include plans for backing the information up, restoring whatever is lost, and continuing the critical business processes that protect the security of ePHI while the entity operates in emergency mode.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2D 2M · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: The WHO Annex C script for explaining the procedure opens with which three points?
opciones: The worker's name, the facility, and that they are trained to take blood
The worker's name, the tests ordered, and the colors of the tubes needed
The worker's name, the ordering doctor, and when the results are expected
The worker's name, the patient's diagnosis, and the reason for the tests
preguntas.explicacion: Annex C begins with the worker giving their name and saying they work at the facility, then asks the patient's name to check it against the order and any name band, and then states that the worker is trained and experienced in taking blood. The tests and the clinician who will receive the results come later in the script; the diagnosis is never part of it.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3, Table 18.2, and ch. 18.5
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(2) · RMA III.G.2.b · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which needle and which volume are used for a subcutaneous injection in an adult?
opciones: 25 to 31 gauge, half to five eighths of an inch, and no more than 1 mL
25 to 27 gauge, three eighths to five eighths of an inch, and 0.1 mL
18 to 25 gauge, half to an inch and a half, and 2 to 5 mL for an adult
22 to 25 gauge, one inch, and up to 3 mL given at the vastus lateralis
preguntas.explicacion: Subcutaneous needles run from 25 to 31 gauge and from half an inch to five eighths of an inch, and the volume is no more than 1 mL in an adult, or 0.5 mL in infants and small children, because larger amounts may not be absorbed properly and add discomfort. The first alternative describes an intradermal injection, and the other two describe intramuscular ones.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B 5E · PBT III.A.2 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Blood gas samples from a distant ICU keep arriving clotted, and the wards still draw with syringe, needle and container rather than an evacuated tube system. Which two responses did the emergency laboratory adopt?
opciones: Placing point-of-care blood gas analyzers in the ICUs under laboratory control, and teaching use of the evacuated tube system
Adding heparin to every syringe on arrival in the laboratory, and asking the ICUs to send samples only during the day shift
Accepting clotted gas samples with a cautionary comment, and moving all blood gas testing to the core laboratory
Requiring each ICU to centrifuge gas samples before sending them, and doubling the frequency of the courier rounds
preguntas.explicacion: To cut down the blood gas samples that clotted on long transport routes, the laboratory placed several point-of-care blood gas analyzers in the ICUs and emergency departments, kept under laboratory specialists' control; and since collection with the conventional syringe, needle and container system was still going on in the wards and was thought to add to the fibrin-clotted samples, the education seminars covered venipuncture technique, the right additive tubes, the order of tubes, gentle mixing and transport. Rapid serum tubes were the answer for early-spun serum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Involve appropriate third parties
preguntas.subtema: Third parties in termination · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: The patient about to be dismissed belongs to a managed care plan the practice contracts with. What step comes before the letter goes out?
opciones: Asking the insurer whether its contract restricts how and when the practice may end care
Asking the insurer to move her to another clinician in the network before she is told
Asking the insurer to extend her benefits thirty days so that care is not interrupted
No step at all, since a contract with a plan has no bearing on ending a clinical relationship
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient belongs to a managed care organization the clinician participates in, the insurer should be contacted first to find out what restrictions it places on termination. Contracts with third-party payers often limit referrals to clinicians outside that network, and some insurers require thirty days' notice to the insurer as well as to the patient. Government payers are stricter.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient slid off the drawing chair during a faint and struck the arm of it. What must not be overlooked?
opciones: Injuries from the fall, which need attention straight away
The tube already drawn, which has to be discarded and repeated
The tourniquet, which must be reapplied before the patient moves
The label, which is rewritten because the draw was interrupted
preguntas.explicacion: Any injury sustained in a fall from a faint requires immediate attention, and patients who collapse frequently need a trauma assessment for what they hit on the way down. A fall from a height, or obvious injury and bleeding, is one of the situations in which emergency help is called.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A category offers no unspecified code at all. What may stand in for one?
opciones: The other specified code, which then covers both uses
The code for the symptom that brought her to the office
The three-character category, used as though it were a code
The default code printed beside the main term in the index
preguntas.explicacion: Codes titled unspecified are for a record too thin to support a more specific code, while an other or an other specified title takes the detail the classification has no code of its own for. Where a category carries no unspecified code, the other specified code may stand for both. A three-character category is only a code where nothing is subdivided under it.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(b), Standard: Training; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", To Whom Does HIPAA Apply and Training Employees
preguntas.subtema: Workforce training · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Whom must a covered entity train on its privacy policies and procedures?
opciones: All workforce members, as suited to their functions, including new hires
Only clinical staff who document care in the medical record
Only the privacy official and the contact person for complaints
Only paid employees; volunteers and students fall outside the training rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(b) has every member of the workforce trained on the policies and procedures for privacy, to the degree their own functions make necessary and appropriate: everyone by the compliance date, each new member within a reasonable time of joining, and anyone whose work is touched by a material change in the policies, with the training documented. Clinical guidance applies the rule to interns, volunteers and administrative, food service, clerical and janitorial staff alike, and recommends refreshing it every year.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gynecologic Pelvic Examination", Preparation: Patient Positioning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.d · RMA III.F.2.a.ii · NCMA 2B.10
preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient draped for a pelvic examination?
opciones: Undressed from the waist down and kept under a sheet until she is properly positioned
Positioned first and then draped, so that the foot supports can be adjusted without a sheet
Draped from the shoulders down, with the absorbent pad laid over the abdominal wall instead
Left uncovered from the start, because the external inspection comes before the speculum
preguntas.explicacion: She undresses from the waist down and stays covered by a drape, uncovered only while the examination is actually running and for as short a time as possible. An absorbent pad goes under the buttocks, not over the abdomen. A chaperone, usually the assistant, stays in the room, and consent is obtained before anything begins.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Color Perception", Related Testing
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(10)(a) · RMA III.F.5.b · NCMA 2B.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which cards are used to screen color vision?
opciones: Pseudoisochromatic plates, the Ishihara set being the familiar one
Landolt C cards, on which a broken ring faces in several directions
Tumbling E cards, designed for children and non-readers of the alphabet
LEA symbol cards, designed to remove the language barrier in children
preguntas.explicacion: Color vision is screened with plates carrying numbers formed from dots of particular colors; the Ishihara set is the familiar one, and Hardy-Rand-Rittler plates work the same way. They do not separate the different types of color deficiency well. The Landolt C, tumbling E and LEA symbol charts are acuity charts, not color tests.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a molecular assay will sit for several hours before extraction. Why is it either processed at once or refrigerated?
opciones: Its low pH and urea denature the nucleic acid at ambient temperature
Its bacteria multiply at ambient temperature and consume the target
Its bilirubin breaks down in the light and quenches the fluorescent dye
Its specific gravity climbs as it evaporates, concentrating inhibitors
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is worked on at once or held at 2 to 8 °C, for two reasons. Urine tends to a low pH and carries urea, and the pair denature DNA at 25 °C and above. Long storage in the cold, on the other hand, encourages uric acid, calcium oxalate and phosphorus to precipitate, and those precipitates can inhibit the amplification themselves, so neither extreme is harmless.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Informed Consent Prior to Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Disclosing a small risk · CPT D1 1D k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k211 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.2 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: How small a risk must still be disclosed to a patient, according to the federal decision that shaped informed consent?
opciones: A risk of one percent, if it means death or a lasting harm
A risk of ten percent, no matter what harm it would cause
A risk of one percent, but only for elective procedures
A risk of five percent, unless the patient asks for more
preguntas.explicacion: A federal court held that a risk as small as one percent still has to be disclosed when what it threatens is death, or a complication that changes the patient's life for good, paralysis being the example given. What decides is the severity of the outcome, not the probability on its own. Because the three branches of government have left the minimum standard vague, these rights tend to be enforced afterwards, through tort claims brought by patients.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Recommended Practices Before Testing: Waived test specimens; CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Set?: Collecting the Sample
preguntas.subtema: Unprocessed specimens only · CPT D1 k29 · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A group A strep antigen kit's insert describes testing both a throat swab and a colony from a culture plate. Under a Certificate of Waiver, which specimen may the site test?
opciones: Only the throat swab; testing the culture is not a waived use
Either one, because the kit itself is categorized as waived
Only the culture, because the swab requires an extraction step
Neither, because any test with two specimen types is nonwaived
preguntas.explicacion: Waived tests are approved only for direct, unprocessed specimens that need no operator manipulation: whole blood, urine, a throat or nasal swab, stool, saliva. When one insert covers both a processed and an unprocessed specimen, the waiver applies only to the unprocessed one. Group A strep antigen testing is waived on a throat swab and not on a microbiology culture; urine hCG is waived, serum hCG is not.

preguntas.subtema: Transmission security · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Records are about to be sent to a specialist across an open network. Which technical standard governs that leg of the journey?
opciones: Transmission security, with integrity controls and encryption as its specifications
Integrity, with a mechanism that shows stored information has not been altered
Access control, with unique identifiers and an automatic close of idle sessions
Audit controls, the mechanisms that capture and review activity in the system
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission security is the standard for information traveling over an electronic communications network. Its two addressable specifications are integrity controls, so that what was sent cannot be modified undetected, and encryption where the practice judges it appropriate. The integrity standard next to it looks at information at rest.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Vitamins
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(e) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: Which vitamins are the fat-soluble ones, and where does the body keep them?
opciones: A, D, E and K, stored in the liver, fatty tissue and muscle
A, C, D and K, stored in the liver, fatty tissue and muscle
A, D, E and K, stored in the kidneys and cleared daily in urine
B12, D, E and K, stored in the liver, fatty tissue and muscle
preguntas.explicacion: Four vitamins dissolve in fat: A, D, E and K. They are held in the liver, in fatty tissue and in muscle, and the body takes them up more easily when dietary fat is present at the same time. Vitamin C is water-soluble, and B12, although water-soluble, is the one that can sit in the liver for years.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Permitted uses · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.2.a(5) · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A primary care office faxes a chart to the specialist it is sending the patient to. What permits that disclosure?
opciones: It is a treatment disclosure, and treatment activities need no authorization from the patient
It is a health care operations disclosure, allowed once both offices sign a shared privacy notice
It is a public interest disclosure, allowed because referrals serve the coordination of care
It is an incidental disclosure, allowed because the fax is a by-product of scheduling the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Treatment is defined as providing, coordinating or managing health care, as consultation between providers, and as the referral of a patient from one provider to another. A covered entity may disclose PHI for the treatment activities of any provider, and the example given is a primary care provider sending a record to the specialist who needs it. No authorization is required.

preguntas.subtema: Discharge summary contents · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5H · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient checking out after an inpatient stay asks what her discharge summary has to cover. Which three things does the medical record condition name?
opciones: The outcome of the stay, the disposition of the case, and the arrangements for follow-up
The outcome of the stay, the final diagnosis, and the itemised charges for the admission
The admitting diagnosis, the disposition of the case, and the medicines given on the ward
The outcome of the stay, the consultants seen, and the deadline for completing the record
preguntas.explicacion: Among the items every record must document is a discharge summary carrying the outcome of the hospitalization, the disposition of the case and the provisions for follow-up care. The admitting diagnosis, the results of consultative evaluations and the final diagnosis completed within thirty days of discharge are separate items on the same list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis is breathing deeply, rapidly and with visible effort. Which pattern is this?
opciones: Kussmaul respiration, the compensation the body mounts for metabolic acidosis
Cheyne-Stokes respiration, the cycling pattern seen in advanced heart failure
Biot respiration, the clusters of deep breaths broken by periods of apnea
Apneustic breathing, the long gasping inspirations of upper pontine injury
preguntas.explicacion: Deep, rapid, labored breathing in an acidotic patient is Kussmaul respiration: blowing off carbon dioxide is how the body pushes the pH back up. Ketoacidosis, uremia and the ingestion of toxic alcohols or salicylates are the usual causes, and recognizing the pattern early matters for survival.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Effective Team Event Tools
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through the morning the team stops to re-establish awareness and check the plan still fits. Which team event is that?
opciones: A huddle, an ad hoc meeting to keep care on track
A brief, held before the start to share the plan
A debrief, held afterward to review performance
A call-out, used to broadcast critical information
preguntas.explicacion: A huddle is the ad hoc meeting held to keep care moving toward the goal, to affirm or re-establish awareness of the situation, to reinforce the plan or to judge whether it needs adjusting. A brief comes before the start, to share the plan and assign roles; a debrief comes after, to trade lessons learned.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, BMI Frequently Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A weightlifter is told the body mass index falls in the overweight band. What limitation does this show?
opciones: The index cannot separate fat from muscle and bone, all of which add weight
The index is calculated only for people who do not train, so it will not apply
The index needs a waist measurement added before any category can be assigned
The index reads low in muscular people, so the true category is higher still
preguntas.explicacion: The index compares weight with height and cannot tell what the weight is made of, so someone carrying a lot of muscle can land in the overweight or obesity band. It also says nothing about where fat sits on the body. It is read together with the history, the physical findings and the laboratory results.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Taking gloves off · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How is the second glove removed once the first one is already off?
opciones: Fingers of the bare hand slide under it at the wrist
The bare hand pinches its outer surface at the fingertips
The bare hand pulls it off by the cuff and turns it over
Both gloves are peeled together before the first is dropped
preguntas.explicacion: The first glove is taken off by grasping the palm surface with the other gloved hand and dropping it into the right container. For the second, the fingers of the now bare hand go underneath it at the wrist, so that bare skin never touches the contaminated outside, and it is peeled off over the first. Gloves come off before everything else, and hand hygiene follows immediately, since a glove is not a substitute for washing.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Benefits of This Model
preguntas.subtema: No-shows and access · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: What does the improvement guide say happens to missed appointments once a practice can see patients on the day they call?
opciones: They are likely to fall, so clinical time is used better and less staff time goes on them
They are likely to rise, since a patient who called that morning has less time to plan
They stay where they are, since missed visits follow the reminder system, not the wait
They fall for urgent visits only, since routine ones are still booked several weeks ahead
preguntas.explicacion: Among the benefits listed are savings in cost and in efficiency: with long waits gone, no-shows are expected to fall, clinical time gets used better, and less staff time disappears into managing missed appointments and the backlog. The model also handles routine and urgent requests the same way, so nothing sits waiting for weeks.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k52 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A father says his teething 9-month-old has a temperature of 39 °C (102.2 °F). Why does the provider look for another cause?
opciones: Teething does not push the temperature above 37.8 °C (100 °F), so something else is at work
Teething never changes body temperature at all, so any reading above the normal band is an error
Teething raises the value only in the evening, and the reading was taken at midday
Teething raises the value only after the first tooth erupts through the gum surface
preguntas.explicacion: Teething can nudge a baby's temperature up, but not past 37.8 °C (100 °F). A reading of 39 °C is far above that ceiling, so it is treated as fever from another cause and reported: a child aged 3 to 12 months with 39 °C (102.2 °F) or more is one of the situations where the provider is contacted right away.

preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k55 k56 · PBT II.J II.I · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports repeated hemolysis from one phlebotomist. Which needle choices raise that risk?
opciones: A gauge of twenty-three or finer, or one too wide for the vessel
A gauge of twenty-one or finer, or one too short for the forearm
A gauge of sixteen or wider, or one too long for the antecubital
A gauge of twenty-three or finer, or one too short for the vessel
preguntas.explicacion: Both extremes of gauge appear on the list of factors that raise hemolysis: a needle of twenty-three gauge or under, and a needle too large for the vessel it is being put into. The wider figures, sixteen to eighteen, belong to blood donation rather than to routine sampling.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 2: Hazard(s) Identification
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 2 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section repeats the signal word, the hazard statements and the pictograms that appear on the label?
opciones: Section 2, Hazard Identification, with the hazard classification as well
Section 3, Composition, with the ingredients and their concentrations
Section 8, Exposure Controls, with the limits and the protective gear
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with the routes and the symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Section 2 carries the hazard classification of the chemical, the signal word, the hazard statements, the pictograms, which may be drawn or simply named, the precautionary statements, a note on any hazard that falls outside the classifications, and, for a mixture holding ingredients of unknown toxicity, what percentage of it they make up. It is the section that matches what the reader has already seen on the container label.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): more than one laboratory location; CDC, To Test or Not to Test? (2024), CLIA Certificate of Waiver
preguntas.subtema: One certificate per location · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A practice with three separate office locations runs waived tests at all of them. How many CLIA certificates does it need?
opciones: One for each location, since none of the exceptions applies
One, filed from the main office, covering all fixed sites of the practice
One, provided the total menu stays under 15 waived tests
None, because waived testing at fixed sites is covered by the physician's license
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate is required for each location where testing is performed. The exceptions are narrow: mobile units, health fairs and other temporary sites covered under a designated home base; not-for-profit or government laboratories doing limited public health testing of no more than 15 waived or moderate tests; and hospital laboratories in contiguous buildings on one campus under common direction.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heat emergencies", DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which action is wrong while cooling a patient with heat illness?
opciones: Giving acetaminophen or aspirin to bring the temperature down
Putting cold compresses on the neck, the groin and the armpits
Applying cool wet cloths to the skin and using a fan on the patient
Giving half a cup of a sports drink every 15 minutes while alert
preguntas.explicacion: Fever medicines do not help here and may be harmful. The patient lies down in a cool place with the feet raised about 12 inches (30 cm), cool wet cloths and a fan lower the temperature, and cold compresses go on neck, groin and armpits. Salt tablets, alcohol rubs and drinks with alcohol or caffeine are also out, and nothing by mouth if vomiting.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Diversion Control Division, Definition of Controlled Substance Schedules
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k15 · CMA 2027 I.D.1 · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: On what basis is a substance placed in one of the five schedules of the Controlled Substances Act?
opciones: Accepted medical use, relative abuse potential, and the likelihood of dependence
Accepted medical use, the price of the product, and the route it is given by
The class it belongs to, the strength dispensed, and whether a generic exists
The refills allowed, the storage it needs, and the order form the DEA requires
preguntas.explicacion: The Act sorts controlled substances into five schedules, and three things decide where each one lands: whether the country currently accepts a medical use for it in treatment, how its abuse potential compares with the rest, and how likely dependence is when it is abused. The full list is published each year in 21 CFR 1308.11 through 1308.15. Refill limits and storage follow from the schedule; they do not set it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which electrodes produce lead I?
opciones: Lead I comes from the left and right arm electrodes
Lead I comes from the right arm and left leg electrodes
Lead I comes from the left arm and left leg electrodes
Lead I comes from the right and left leg electrodes
preguntas.explicacion: The three standard bipolar leads each pair two limb electrodes: lead I joins the two arms, lead II the right arm and the left leg, and lead III the left arm and the left leg. Knowing which pair feeds which lead is what lets a technician spot a reversal from the shape of the tracing.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 2.3.2 Calibration Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k157 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How is the machine calibrated in daily use?
opciones: It runs a short self test each time the power is switched on
It is calibrated by the technician before every patient
It runs a self test only when an error code has appeared
It is calibrated once a week against a known signal
preguntas.explicacion: The unit checks itself briefly whenever it is powered up, so no extra calibration step falls to the technician. Deeper checks are periodic and belong to the biomedical engineer, who uses a calibrator that feeds the machine a simulated heartbeat.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Complications: haematoma · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: In a study of blood donors, how often did bruising and hematoma appear at the puncture site?
opciones: In about twelve percent of the donors studied
In about fifty percent of the donors studied
In under one percent of the donors studied
In about thirty percent of the donors studied
preguntas.explicacion: One study of donors found bruising and hematoma where the needle went in for 12.3 percent of them, which makes it the best documented adverse event of the procedure. In the same study syncope happened in under one percent, and nerve injury occurred infrequently.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Grey
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A lactic acid level is ordered. Which tube is used for this test?
opciones: The gray tube with potassium oxalate and sodium fluoride
The lavender tube with EDTA, which is used for hematologic assays
The green tube with heparin, used for stat chemistry
The light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
