preguntas.pregunta: In a rare emergency a phlebotomist judges that stopping to put on a gown would delay care, and draws without it. What does the standard require afterwards?
opciones: The circumstances are investigated and documented, to see whether a change can prevent it
No record is needed, since the judgment of the exposed employee settles the matter
The employee signs the hepatitis B declination form that is kept with the plan
The incident goes in the sharps injury log with the type and brand of the device
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ii) makes the employer ensure the protective equipment is used, and allows one narrow exception: the employee declined it, briefly and for that moment only, in rare and extraordinary circumstances, on the professional judgment that using it would have kept care from being delivered or would have raised the danger to someone. Even then the standard does not stop there: the circumstances are investigated and documented so the employer can see whether something can be changed. The declination form belongs to the hepatitis B vaccine under (f)(2)(iv), and the sharps log records percutaneous injuries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1M k37 k38 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has fainted vomits while still on the floor. What should be done?
opciones: Turn the person onto their side, so choking is prevented
Sit the person upright at once and offer sips of cold water
Raise both legs higher and keep the person face upwards
Place a rolled towel behind the neck and keep the head back
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps for a person who has fainted are to check the airway and breathing, loosen tight clothing at the neck and raise the feet above heart level. If the person has vomited, they are turned onto the side to stop them choking, and kept lying down for ten to fifteen minutes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Types of PPE and Infection Prevention; CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions, Airborne Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Respirators and fit testing · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about N95 respirators for healthcare workers is correct?
opciones: Workers required to use them must be fit tested; a PAPR is an option if fit testing fails
Any worker may use them without fit testing, as with a surgical mask
They protect against droplets only and are replaced by a surgical mask for airborne pathogens
They require fit testing only when used against chemical vapors under Level C
preguntas.explicacion: Protection runs on a scale, with loosely woven cloth masks at the bottom and NIOSH-approved respirators at the top, and fit is a large part of what makes a respirator work. Every worker who is required to wear one, N95 included, has to be fit tested; when the fit test cannot be completed, a powered air-purifying respirator carrying NIOSH approval may be considered instead. Airborne Precautions call for a fit-tested N95 or better, so a surgical mask is no substitute. Level C is a HAZMAT category built around air-purifying respirators.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, BMI Frequently Asked Questions; and NIST, Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which formula gives body mass index from measurements in metric units?
opciones: Weight in kilograms over the height in meters squared
Weight in kilograms over the height in meters, not squared
Weight in kilograms over the height in centimeters squared
Weight in pounds over the height in inches squared, times 703
preguntas.explicacion: In metric units the index is kilograms over meters squared. An alternative metric form divides by the height in centimeters twice and multiplies by 10,000, which comes to the same thing. Pounds over inches squared, times 703, is the customary formula used when height is in inches and weight in pounds.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application and Removal of PPE; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Where to don and doff · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Where should personal protective equipment be put on, and where should it be taken off?
opciones: Both outside the patient room, with the respirator removed after exiting
Both inside the patient room, so the corridor stays free of contamination
Put on inside the room and taken off outside, next to the waste container
Put on outside the room and taken off inside, before the door is opened
preguntas.explicacion: Donning takes place outside the patient room, and so does doffing, with one exception spelled out in the sequence: a respirator is not removed until after leaving the room, because the air inside is the hazard it was worn against. The rest of the equipment comes off in order, gloves first, then eye protection, then gown, then mask or respirator, each dropped into the right container. The bloodborne pathogens standard says the same thing in its own words: all protective equipment is removed before leaving the work area.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5G · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A point-of-care coordinator lists the preanalytical errors her operators are most likely to make. Which pair belongs on that list?
opciones: Containers not properly secured before transport, and concentration shifts while aliquoting
Reagent lots recorded in the wrong column, and controls run at the wrong time of day
Results transcribed into the chart late, and duplicate orders entered by two clinicians
Analyser maintenance skipped for a week, and a calibration accepted outside its limits
preguntas.explicacion: Preanalytical error at the bedside belongs to the same family as in the main laboratory: the patient or the specimen misidentified, and whatever goes wrong while the sample is taken, handled, processed, moved or stored. The examples named run to clotting and hemolysis, a container under-filled or over-filled, containers not secured before transport, a tourniquet left on too long, and shifts introduced while aliquoting.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw with cultures · CPT D4 k78 · PBT II.H.1 venous order of draw · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A set of blood cultures is added to an order that already includes a light blue, a lavender and a gray tube. Where do the culture bottles go in the draw?
opciones: First, before every one of the tubes
After the light blue tube, before the lavender
Last, after the gray tube
Right after a non-additive discard tube
preguntas.explicacion: In the order of draw the WHO reproduces, the blood culture bottle is number 1; the non-additive tube comes second, the citrate tube third, EDTA eighth and the fluoride/oxalate tube tenth. The CDC's procedure likewise has the culture set collected as the first draw of the venipuncture. Filling the bottles after additive tubes risks carrying additive into them, and a discard tube ahead of the bottles is not part of either sequence.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw and discard tubes · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: For which coagulation assay is an initial discard tube specifically required?
opciones: The thrombin generation assay
The prothrombin time on warfarin
The partial thromboplastin time (PTT)
Platelet function testing
preguntas.explicacion: An initial discard tube is not required for coagulation tests, with one exception: the thrombin generation assay. The PT, the aPTT and platelet function tests are named elsewhere in the same section, for the 19 to 22 G needle range and the 9:1 citrate ratio, but none of them is given as a reason for a discard tube.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: You need to describe the position of the little toe relative to the middle toe. Which term fits?
opciones: Lateral, because it lies farther from the midline of the body
Medial, because it lies nearer to the midline of the body
Superior, because it lies above the level of the other toes
Proximal, because it lies nearer to the point of attachment
preguntas.explicacion: Medial points toward the midline of the body and lateral away from it. On the foot the big toe is the medial one and the little toe the lateral one, exactly as the thumb is lateral to the other digits of the hand. Superior and proximal answer different questions: height and distance from the trunk.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Inadvertent Disclosure
preguntas.subtema: The chart that travels · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is wheeled to radiology with the chart on the trolley. What must the transporter be told?
opciones: Not to leave the chart where others could read it
To hand the chart to the first available radiology clerk
To keep the chart closed unless the patient asks to see it
To leave the chart at the desk until the images are done
preguntas.explicacion: Accidental disclosure counts as disclosure. A chart left unattended in a lobby or a procedure suite is the classic example, and when the chart travels with the patient the person pushing the trolley has to know not to leave it anywhere it can be read, on purpose or by accident, by people not involved in that patient's care. Deliberate and accidental disclosure of health information are treated the same way.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Infection Control in Healthcare Personnel (2019), section 7, Background: Exposure management; StatPearls, "OSHA Bloodborne Pathogen Standards", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Underreporting of exposures · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which factors does the CDC list as reasons healthcare personnel fail to report bloodborne pathogen exposures?
opciones: Time pressure, fear of reprimand, not knowing how to report, and cost coverage worries
Low risk from intact skin exposure and the availability of PEP within 72 hours
Immunity from the hepatitis B vaccine and the low 0.3 percent risk for HIV
The 15-day deadline for the written opinion and the 90-day sample storage
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's 2019 guidance blames underreporting among nurses, surgeons, technicians, medical staff and trainees on four things: not enough time, fear of being reprimanded, no idea how the report is made, and worry over who covers the cost of exposure management. It adds that volunteers and trainees may have no workers' compensation, and that off-site services placed inconveniently are one more barrier. StatPearls says much the same, that workers skip reporting where protocols are unclear or the risk looks small. The other options mix true figures with reasons the CDC never gives.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: First-Class Mail
preguntas.subtema: First-Class limits · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A large envelope of forms weighing 11 ounces is going out. May it travel as First-Class Mail?
opciones: Yes, large envelopes go up to 13 ounces under that class of mail
No, First-Class stops at 3.5 ounces for envelopes of every shape
No, a piece above 8 ounces moves to a parcel service priced by weight
Yes, but only once a delivery confirmation service has been added
preguntas.explicacion: First-Class Mail is written for flat, bendable pieces, and the ceiling depends on the shape: 3.5 ounces for a letter-sized envelope and 13 ounces for a large one. The 11-ounce envelope sits inside the large-envelope limit, so nothing needs to change.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Types of Orders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · RMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: An order reads "500 mg acetaminophen by mouth every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain". What type of order is that?
opciones: A PRN order, given when the patient asks for it or when the symptom appears
A routine order, which is followed until some later order cancels it out
A STAT order, given without any delay because the circumstances are urgent
A standing order, applied to any patient who meets clearly defined criteria
preguntas.explicacion: PRN means as needed: the dose is administered when the patient requests it or when the symptom it treats appears, typically pain, nausea or itching, and this order is written in exactly that form. A routine order such as lisinopril 10 mg PO daily runs until it is canceled, a STAT order is a single dose given without delay, and a standing order is a protocol applied to any patient in defined circumstances.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: Sterile saline is being poured into a basin on the field, and the pour is interrupted halfway. What now?
opciones: Do not restart from that bottle, because its lip is now counted as contaminated
Restart at once from the same bottle, as long as it has not touched the basin rim
Restart from the same bottle after wiping its lip with an alcohol swab and letting it dry
Restart from the same bottle, but pour directly over the field so no splashing occurs
preguntas.explicacion: Once pouring stops it is not resumed, because the edge of the container is then treated as contaminated. Solutions are poured from the side of the field rather than across it, held about six inches above, and only from sealed, sterile, unexpired containers. Splashing is avoided as well, since a wet drape wicks microbes up into the field.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Days after a draw, the puncture site shows streaks of redness with drainage and the patient has a fever. What is advised?
opciones: Contact the provider, since these are signs of infection
Apply ice for fifteen minutes each hour until it settles
Raise the arm above the heart and rest it for a further day
Reassure the patient, since bruises last from days to months
preguntas.explicacion: Streaks of redness, pus or other drainage, or a fever around a bruised area are listed as reasons to contact a clinician, because they suggest infection rather than ordinary healing. Ice and elevation are the first-aid measures for an uncomplicated bruise, not for these findings.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which are the relative contraindications to recording a tracing?
opciones: Patient refusal and allergy to the adhesive used on the leads
Patient refusal and a pacemaker that was fitted recently
An implanted defibrillator and a very hairy chest wall
Recent chest surgery and a known allergy to latex gloves
preguntas.explicacion: There are no absolute contraindications to an electrocardiogram; the two relative ones are the patient declining and an allergy to the adhesive that holds the leads. An implanted pacemaker or defibrillator is in fact an indication, since the tracing is one of the ways their function is checked.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Avoidance of contaminated phlebotomy equipment; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet and infection control · CPT D3 k60 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic reuses the same cloth tourniquet on every patient. What risk does the WHO associate with this practice?
opciones: Passing methicillin-resistant staphylococci from one patient to the next
Hemoconcentration of the specimen from an unevenly worn band
Transmission of hepatitis B, as happens with reusable finger-prick devices
Loss of elasticity that prevents the veins from engorging
preguntas.explicacion: Up to 25% of tourniquets may be contaminated with MRSA through poor hand hygiene or reuse of contaminated tourniquets, so a preferably disposable tourniquet is recommended to avoid MRSA for patients and providers alike. Hepatitis B outbreaks are the WHO's example for reusable finger-prick devices and glucometers, a different item.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Stool guaiac test (003393), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: gFOBT sampling · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient receiving a guaiac fecal occult blood kit asks how many samples to collect. What is the standard instruction?
opciones: Two samples from each of 3 different bowel movements, smeared on the card's two windows
Three samples from a single bowel movement, each smeared on a separate card window
One sample from each of 3 bowel movements on 3 different days, sent in a preservative vial
Two samples from one bowel movement, from the first and the last part of the stool
preguntas.explicacion: The home kit asks for 3 different bowel movements; from each one the patient samples two areas of the stool and smears each on one of the two places on that card, then mails the cards to the laboratory. The stool must be kept away from urine, which can spoil the sample. Three specimens from separate days in a vial is the ova-and-parasite routine, and the card is never completed from a single movement.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Screening and Diagnostic Test
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no symptoms has a test to pick up a disease early. Which term describes it?
opciones: A screening, a preventive service done without symptoms
A diagnostic test, run to find what the problem is
A habilitation service, to keep her daily functioning
An emergency service, to check a serious condition
preguntas.explicacion: A screening is preventive care: a test or exam that looks for something in a patient who has no symptoms, no signs and no history of the condition. A diagnostic test is the opposite errand, carried out to work out what an existing health problem is, as an X-ray does when a bone may be broken.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.5 Homeostasis, Negative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Blood glucose rises after a meal, insulin is released, and glucose falls back into range. Which kind of feedback is that?
opciones: Negative feedback, because it reverses the deviation from the set point
Positive feedback, because it reverses the deviation from the set point
Negative feedback, because it drives the value further from the set point
Positive feedback, because it drives the value further from the set point
preguntas.explicacion: Negative feedback reverses a deviation and returns the value to its normal range, and glucose control is the standard example: beta cells in the pancreas detect the excess sugar and release insulin, muscle, fat and liver cells take the glucose up, and as the level drops the release of insulin stops.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Referral
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and referrals · CCMA 5P k183 · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · RMA II.A.4 · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: In many HMO plans, what must a patient obtain before seeing a specialist if they want the plan to pay?
opciones: A referral, which is a written order from their primary care doctor
A preauthorization, the plan's finding that the visit is necessary
A written order from the specialist, sent back to the primary care doctor
A claim, filed by the primary care doctor before the specialist visit
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a referral as an order, in writing, from the primary care doctor so that the patient can see a specialist or receive certain services. In many HMOs that order is required before getting care from anyone other than the primary care doctor, and without it the plan may refuse to pay. The order runs from the primary care doctor to the specialist, not the other way. A preauthorization is the plan's own decision that a service is medically necessary, a different entry, and a claim is the request for payment that comes after the care, not before it.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(B) and (g)(1)(i)(E), Other Regulated Waste Containment; and OSHA, Brief: Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms (OSHA 3636, PDF, GHS)
preguntas.subtema: Regulated waste containers · CPT D1 1G k30 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Into which container does blood-soaked gauze go under the standard?
opciones: A closable container that prevents leakage, labeled with the biohazard legend or red
A puncture-resistant sharps container, since all regulated waste is handled as sharps
Any lined trash can, provided the bag is closed before it leaves the room
A container marked with the GHS pictogram frame, red square set on a point
preguntas.explicacion: Gauze that would release blood when compressed is regulated waste under paragraph (b), and (d)(4)(iii)(B) requires such waste to go in containers that are closable, built to contain contents and prevent leakage, labeled or color-coded per (g)(1)(i), and closed before removal; (g)(1)(i)(E) lets red bags or red containers stand in for the label. Puncture resistance is demanded for sharps containers in (d)(4)(iii)(A), not for soft waste. The red diamond frame is the HazCom pictogram for chemicals, a different standard.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A medication list marks one drug BID and another QID. Which pair of schedules is that?
opciones: Twice a day and four times a day
Twice a day and three times a day
Three times a day and four times a day
Twice a day and once a day at night
preguntas.explicacion: The dosing abbreviations differ by one letter and mean quite different schedules: BID is twice a day, TID is three times a day and QID is four times a day. PRN is the odd one out, because it is not a schedule at all: it means the dose is given as needed. Reading that first letter carefully is the whole trick.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(l), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient telephones the laboratory and asks for a copy of her own completed test report, without going through her physician. What does CLIA allow?
opciones: The laboratory may release it once it authenticates her as that patient
The laboratory may release it only with the ordering physician's consent
The laboratory may release it only to her designated personal representative
The laboratory may not release it, since results go to authorized persons
preguntas.explicacion: Results normally go only to authorized persons, but the report standard carries an explicit exception: on request the laboratory may give the patient, a personal representative, or the persons named in the privacy rule access to completed reports that its own authentication process can identify as belonging to that patient. No countersignature from the ordering provider is required.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: implied contract; and Wex: contract
preguntas.subtema: Contracts in practice · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(1) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient accepts a service at the office without signing any financial agreement. What kind of contract is that?
opciones: An implied-in-fact contract, inferred from what both parties did
An express contract, since the service was requested out loud
An implied-in-law contract, since no benefit was actually given
No contract at all, since payment terms were never agreed in advance
preguntas.explicacion: An express contract is communicated in speech or writing. An implied-in-fact one is formed when the promises are inferred from the parties' intentional conduct and one side knows, or has reason to know, the other will read that conduct as agreement: accepting a merchant's services means paying their reasonable value. An implied-in-law contract is a remedy against unjust enrichment, not a real agreement.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), What is a comprehensive metabolic panel?; MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Urobilinogen in Urine; MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Creatinine Test
preguntas.subtema: Bilirubin on the CMP · CMA I.C.10.c.(3) · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which substance on a comprehensive metabolic panel is a waste product formed when old red blood cells are broken down and is cleared mainly by the liver?
opciones: Total bilirubin
Serum creatinine
Urea nitrogen (BUN)
Urine urobilinogen
preguntas.explicacion: Bilirubin is the waste left when the body breaks old red cells down, and the liver clears most of it, which is why it sits with albumin, total protein and the liver enzymes among the CMP additions. Creatinine comes from muscle breaking down and urea nitrogen from protein breaking down, and the kidneys clear both. Urobilinogen is what intestinal bacteria make out of bilirubin; a little normally shows in urine, and it is read on the urine strip, not in the CMP.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Formative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: Coaching and feedback · CCMA 6L k203 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches formative feedback given to a team member?
opciones: Timely and specific, aimed at behaviors and improvement
General and delayed, aimed at the person's own attributes
Private and formal, aimed at the annual evaluation cycle
Immediate and public, aimed at the team's overall workload
preguntas.explicacion: The point of formative feedback is a team that performs better. It should be appreciative, timely after the behavior, respectful by focusing on behaviors rather than personal attributes, specific to a task, directed toward improvement, considerate of the person's feelings, and tied to the effect on the patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth modalities · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A dermatologist reviews a photograph of a rash uploaded overnight and answers the next morning. Which kind of telehealth is that?
opciones: Asynchronous telemedicine, the store and forward method of sharing information
Synchronous, because a clinician and a patient are both involved in the exchange
Remote patient monitoring, because a device captured the image that was reviewed
A facilitated virtual visit, because staff at a clinic gathered the data beforehand
preguntas.explicacion: Store and forward, the asynchronous route, packages history, images and diagnostic data and ships them off for a specialist to read and advise on afterwards. Teledermatology fits exactly: a photograph of a skin lesion goes up and is read the next day. The same bucket holds e-consultations, secure messaging through the portal and off-site reading of radiology studies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "P wave", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: A strip shows a constant PR interval of 240 ms with every P wave conducted, in a patient with no symptoms. How is that regarded?
opciones: As common and largely benign, often needing no further workup
As an emergency, with a permanent pacemaker fitted without delay
As an artifact, since a PR that long comes from a lead reversal
As a second-degree block, since a beat is about to be dropped
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing is truly blocked in a first-degree block: the impulse is delayed, each P wave still reaches the ventricles one to one, and the finding is relatively common and has largely been treated as benign. Prompt pacing belongs to the Mobitz type II block.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3, footnote b
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw and tube colours · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.J · CCMA 3E6 k129 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: The culture bottles a hospital stocks are yellow, pink and blue rather than the yellow and black striped bottle shown on the chart. What follows?
opciones: Bottle color varies with the maker, so the local laboratory settles which is which
The chart is wrong, and the bottles should be reordered in the striped presentation
Colored bottles hold no broth, so they are drawn after the coagulation tube instead
The bottles must be drawn in the order yellow, pink and blue before any other tube
preguntas.explicacion: Culture bottle color depends on the manufacturer, and the note under the order-of-draw table asks the user to verify color codes with the local laboratory because they differ from place to place. What does not change is the position: the culture container is filled before any other.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Respirator removal · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: When doffing PPE after caring for a patient on Airborne Precautions, where should the respirator be removed?
opciones: After exiting the patient room, unlike the other PPE items
Inside the room, immediately after the gloves
Inside the room, before the gown so the ties are reachable
At the nurses' station, once hands have been washed
preguntas.explicacion: Doffing takes place outside patient rooms, and when a respirator is in use it is not removed until after exiting the patient room. In the sequence the respirator comes off last, after gloves, eye protection and gown, by releasing the ties or straps behind the head without touching the front or mouth area. Removing it inside the room would expose the wearer to the air the respirator was protecting against, and hand hygiene is performed after the removal, not before.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Tachycardia", Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: How is sinus tachycardia defined?
opciones: A sinus rhythm faster than 100 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm faster than 120 beats per minute
A sinus rhythm faster than 150 beats per minute
Any narrow rhythm faster than 100 beats per minute
preguntas.explicacion: Sinus tachycardia carries the same electrical signature as normal sinus rhythm, with P waves upright in I, II and aVL and negative in aVR, each followed by a QRS complex; the only difference is a rate over 100. Finding and treating the underlying cause is what management rests on.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(iii), (f)(2)(ii) and (f)(1)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccination, later acceptance · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declined the hepatitis B vaccine when hired. Six months later, still in the same job, she asks for it. What does OSHA require?
opciones: The employer must make the vaccine available at that time, at no cost, while she remains covered
She must pay for the series herself, since the employer's offer ended with the signed declination
The employer may require a prescreening antibody test before agreeing to provide the series
She must wait for the next annual training session, when the vaccine is offered again to staff
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(iii) covers exactly this case: an employee who first declines and later, while still covered by the standard, decides to accept gets the vaccination made available at that point. Nothing in the standard makes the earlier declination final. Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) keeps every medical procedure under (f), the vaccine included, free of charge and at a reasonable time and place, and (f)(2)(ii) bars the employer from requiring prescreening first. The annual training is a separate duty and is not the trigger for the offer.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Notice in emergencies · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives unconscious and is treated as an emergency. What happens with the notice of privacy practices?
opciones: It is furnished as soon as reasonably practicable afterwards, and no acknowledgment is needed
It is skipped altogether, because emergency treatment is outside the reach of the Privacy Rule
It is mailed within sixty days, the period a health plan has after a material revision
It is read aloud to the accompanying relative, who signs the acknowledgment on the patient's behalf
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency treatment situation the notice comes as soon after the emergency ends as is reasonably practicable. The rule also lifts the duty to make a good faith effort at a written acknowledgment in that situation. Sixty days is the deadline for a health plan to send a revised notice after a material change.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pregnancy Dating", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.d · CCMA 3B3 k64 · RMA III.F.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being prepared for a transvaginal ultrasound. What is the instruction about the bladder?
opciones: Empty it, because a full bladder pushes the uterus out of the field
Fill it, because a full bladder pushes the uterus into better view
Fill it, because the probe uses the bladder as an acoustic window
Empty it, because a full bladder raises the risk of a urinary infection
preguntas.explicacion: The rule reverses between the two approaches. Transabdominal scanning may see better with a full bladder, while a full bladder displaces the uterus backward and out of reach of the vaginal probe, so that study is done with the bladder empty. The patient lies in lithotomy with the buttocks near the table edge so the probe can move through its full range.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC4771218 LaRocco et al., Effectiveness of Preanalytic Practices on Urine Cultures (2016), Summary of findings
preguntas.subtema: Pediatric collection and contamination · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(e) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: For infants and children who need a urine culture, which noninvasive collection showed the lowest contamination rates?
opciones: Cleansing plus a midstream catch, set against bag or diaper collection
Sterile bag collection, compared with midstream or diaper collection
Diaper collection, compared with midstream or sterile bag collection
Midstream collection without cleansing, which equaled cleansing in women
preguntas.explicacion: In children, the evidence pointed to much lower odds of contamination with midstream collection after cleansing than with a sterile bag, a diaper or midstream without cleansing, and that body of evidence was rated high. The picture differs in adults: in women, cleansing made no difference to contamination, and in men a midstream clean-catch beat a first-void collection. Catheterization and suprapubic aspiration remain the invasive references.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Complications
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: A crutch user develops weakness of the hand after leaning on the shoulder rests. What is this?
opciones: Crutch palsy, from pressure on the brachial plexus at the shoulder rest
Crutch palsy, from pressure on the median nerve inside the hand grip
Compartment syndrome, from the arms carrying the whole of the body weight
Peroneal palsy, from the tips of the crutches being set too far from the feet
preguntas.explicacion: Resting body weight on the axillary pad squeezes the brachial plexus and can leave the radial and ulnar nerves palsied. It is repairable with treatment, and it is prevented by teaching that the hands, not the armpits, carry the load. Extra padding helps, though too much of it narrows the gap under the axilla and brings back the problem it was meant to fix.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring; and section Mechanism of Action, Pharmacokinetics
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is on oral vancomycin for colitis and the ward asks for a trough. What does the guidance say?
opciones: Oral vancomycin usually needs no serum concentration monitoring
Oral vancomycin needs a trough within 30 minutes before the dose
Oral vancomycin needs a peak drawn as the capsule is swallowed
Oral vancomycin needs a trough only once steady state is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Taken by mouth, vancomycin usually calls for no serum concentration monitoring, unlike the intravenous route, because barely any of it reaches the circulation: oral bioavailability sits under 10%. The pre-dose trough at steady state and the peak taken at the end of the infusion both belong to the intravenous drug.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Discarding the first drop · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away before applying blood to a glucose test strip?
opciones: It may be hemolyzed, or carry interstitial and intracellular fluid, either of which skews the reading
It contains alcohol from the skin preparation, which the guidance says lowers the glucose reading by about 10 %
It is arterial rather than capillary blood and therefore reads higher than the venous reference method does
It clots too quickly on the strip, so most meters will display an insufficient-sample error message
preguntas.explicacion: Once the lancet has fired, clean gauze wipes the first drop away: it may be hemolyzed, or carry fluid from between and inside the cells, and either distorts the result. Gentle pressure near the site brings a second drop up, and that one touches the tip of the strip with volume enough; some meters flag an insufficient sample and let more blood go onto the same strip.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Into which vessels does the brachial artery divide, and at what point?
opciones: Into the ulnar and radial arteries, at the apex of the cubital fossa
Into the radial and ulnar arteries, at the superior border of the fossa
Into the cephalic and basilic branches, at the apex of the cubital fossa
Into the radial and median branches, at the medial epicondyle of the humerus
preguntas.explicacion: The brachial artery supplies the forearm and splits into the ulnar and the radial artery at the apex of the fossa, the corner that points downwards. Cephalic and basilic are veins, not branches of an artery, and they join one another through the median cubital vein higher in the triangle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which problems are grouped together as the local complications of a venous puncture?
opciones: Failure of the attempt, arterial or nerve injury, hematoma or bleeding
Failure of the attempt, low blood sugar, dehydration or a raised pulse
Arterial injury, latex allergy, a broken tube or a mislabelled specimen
Nerve injury, hemoconcentration, a clotted tube or an expired needle
preguntas.explicacion: Grouped as local complications are failure of the procedure itself, injury to an artery or a nerve, and bleeding or a hematoma where the catheter went in. Faults such as a clotted tube or a wrong label are specimen problems rather than injuries to the patient, though they cost a second draw.

preguntas.subtema: Employee record retention · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer preserve the medical record of an employee covered by the OSHA access standard?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus thirty years
For thirty years counted from the date of hire
For the duration of employment plus five years
For six years after the employee leaves the job
preguntas.explicacion: Unless a specific standard says otherwise, an employee's medical record is preserved for the whole time she is employed and for thirty years after that. Exposure records get thirty years of their own. The standard also carves out exceptions: health insurance claims kept apart from the medical program, minor first aid records, and the records of anyone employed less than a year where they are handed over on termination.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Removing PPE
preguntas.subtema: Doffing sequence · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which item comes off first when removing PPE, in the CDC-recommended sequence?
opciones: Gloves, peeled so the contaminated outside stays inside
The mask or respirator, released from behind the head
The gown, pulled from the shoulders and turned inside out
Eye protection, lifted by the earpieces or the strap
preguntas.explicacion: The doffing sequence starts with the gloves: grasp the palm of one glove with the other gloved hand and peel it off, then slide the bare fingers under the remaining glove at the wrist and peel it over the first. Eye protection follows, handled by strap or earpieces without touching the front; then the gown, untied and pulled away from neck and shoulders, turned inside out; and the mask or respirator last, by the ties behind the head. Hand hygiene follows removal and any time contamination is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "SOAP Notes", Function: Assessment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.1.c · CMA I.A.4.i · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: Where in a SOAP note do the possible diagnoses go, ranked from the likeliest downward?
opciones: Under Assessment, where the subjective and objective findings are pulled together
Under Plan, beside the tests that are ordered to settle the remaining diagnostic doubt
Under Objective, with the examination findings that first suggested them
Under Subjective, right after the present illness and the review of systems
preguntas.explicacion: Assessment is where the two halves of the note meet: problems listed in order of importance, and for each one a differential ordered from most to least likely, including the unlikely conditions that would do harm if missed. The Plan then says which test answers which question, what therapy is needed, who is consulted and what the patient is taught.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Durable Medical Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5 k68, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders oxygen equipment for a patient to use at home every day. Which benefit category does that fall into?
opciones: Durable medical equipment, ordered for extended use
Orthotics and prosthetics, ordered after an injury
Home health care, given at home under doctor's orders
Habilitation services, to keep skills for daily living
preguntas.explicacion: Durable medical equipment is equipment and supplies a provider orders for everyday or extended use, and oxygen equipment, wheelchairs and crutches are the examples given. Braces and artificial limbs fall under orthotics and prosthetics. Home health care is the services and supplies delivered in the home, not the equipment itself.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrioventricular Block", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does Mobitz type I differ from Mobitz type II?
opciones: In type I the PR lengthens beat by beat until one is dropped
In type I the PR stays constant until one beat is dropped
In type I the PR shortens beat by beat until one is dropped
In type I every other P wave is dropped without any warning
preguntas.explicacion: Both are second-degree blocks, and the PR interval is what tells them apart. In type I it stretches with each beat until a P wave finally goes unconducted; in type II it stays the same and a beat drops out without warning. When every other P wave is blocked the two cannot be told apart, and it is called a 2:1 block.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(e)(1)(i) and (e)(1)(ii), Written hazard communication program
preguntas.subtema: The written program · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Besides describing labels, data sheets and training, what must a written hazard communication program contain?
opciones: A list of the hazardous chemicals present, and how non-routine tasks are handled
A copy of every safety data sheet, arranged by section and by supplier
The exposure limits of each chemical and the results of air monitoring
The signed acknowledgment of each employee who attended the training
preguntas.explicacion: The written program describes how the employer will meet what is required on labels and other warnings, on safety data sheets, and on informing and training employees. Beyond that it carries two more pieces: a list naming the hazardous chemicals known to be there, identified as the corresponding data sheet identifies them, and the methods by which employees will be told about the hazards of non-routine tasks and of chemicals inside unlabeled pipes in their work areas. The list may cover the whole workplace or be drawn up area by area.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Leopold Maneuvers", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.d · RMA III.F.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: What does the first of the Leopold maneuvers determine?
opciones: Which fetal pole occupies the fundus, and how high the fundus sits
Which side of the uterus holds the fetal back and which the limbs
Whether the presenting part has descended into the maternal pelvis
Whether the fetal head is flexed or extended above the pelvic brim
preguntas.explicacion: The fundal grip is done facing the mother's head, with a palm on each side of the fundus and the fingertips feeling what lies there. A head in the fundus, meaning a breech, feels hard, round and smooth; a vertex presentation leaves a large, nodular mass up there instead. The same maneuver gives the fundal height for an estimate of gestational age.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Nerves
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.b(4) · CCMA 3B4 k61 · RMA III.F.2.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which nerve is most often injured by the leg supports used in the lithotomy position?
opciones: The common peroneal nerve, which wraps around the head of the fibula
The ulnar nerve, which runs along the inner side of the flexed elbow
The brachial plexus, which is stretched when the arm goes past 90 degrees
The sciatic nerve, which is compressed by the pad under the lower back
preguntas.explicacion: The peroneal nerve rounds the fibular head, exactly where the calf rests against the support, so padding between the bony prominence and the support is what protects it. The sciatic nerve is also at risk in this position but by stretch, from hyperflexion at the hip, not by compression. Ulnar and brachial plexus injuries come from arm position instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Deep Tendon Reflexes", Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.1.a(4)
preguntas.pregunta: Which nerve roots are being tested when the ankle jerk is struck?
opciones: S1, through the tibial nerve, at the Achilles tendon behind the joint
L2 to L4, through the femoral nerve, just below the patella of the knee
C5 to C6, through the musculocutaneous nerve, in front of the elbow
C5 to C6, through the radial nerve, on the radial side of the forearm
preguntas.explicacion: Ankle jerk is S1 by way of the tibial nerve. The knee reflex is L2 to L4, mostly L4, through the femoral nerve; biceps is C5 to C6 through the musculocutaneous nerve; and brachioradialis is C5 to C6 through the radial nerve about 10 cm above the wrist. Each reflex is compared straight away with the same one on the other side.

preguntas.subtema: Operative report · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which document does the surgical services condition require the surgeon to sign, written or dictated right after the operation?
opciones: The operative report, with the techniques, the findings and any tissue removed
The discharge summary with the outcome and the provisions for follow-up care
The history and physical examination updated for any change in condition
The consultation report from the anesthesia service covering the procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The surgical services condition calls for an operative report setting out the techniques used, what was found, and any tissue taken out or altered; it is written or dictated straight after the operation and carries the surgeon's signature. The discharge summary, which records the outcome of the stay, the disposition of the case and the plans for follow-up, sits under the medical record condition and runs on the discharge timetable instead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth workflow · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA k2 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which office processes does HHS say a move to telehealth will change?
opciones: Check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and appointment structure
Only the billing process, since everything else in the visit stays exactly as it was
Only the clinical examination, since the administrative side of the visit is unaffected
Only the consent process, since the rest of the workflow is set by the software vendor
preguntas.explicacion: Moving care to telehealth forces changes on the in-person workflow. The processes named as affected are check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and the structure of the appointment. How much has to change turns on the vendor, on the size and setting of the practice, on the patient population and on the services offered, and the electronic health record should merge easily into the new workflow.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Emancipated minor · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these generally makes a minor emancipated?
opciones: Being on active duty in the armed forces
Being enrolled full time at a university
Being treated for a sexually transmitted infection
Being the oldest sibling in a single-parent home
preguntas.explicacion: Emancipation frees a minor from parental control, and it generally follows from marriage, active duty in the military, or living apart from the parents while managing one's own financial affairs; some states require a court declaration, and the rules vary from state to state. Consenting to care for a sexually transmitted infection is a separate public-health exception that leaves the minor's legal status unchanged.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.3 Specimen collection containers
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k129 k136 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A green-top heparin tube arrives for a viral PCR. Why do current guidelines say to reject it, and which tubes are recommended instead?
opciones: Heparin inhibits DNA amplification in a dose-dependent way and is carried through extraction; EDTA or ACD tubes are recommended
Heparin chelates the magnesium the polymerase needs for amplification; citrate or fluoride tubes are recommended instead
Heparin degrades RNA through its own nuclease activity during storage; serum tubes with clot activator are recommended instead
Heparin causes hemolysis during centrifugation and releases heme into the plasma; plain red-top tubes are recommended instead
preguntas.explicacion: Heparin inhibits the amplification of DNA in a way that depends on the dose, and on which polymerase is in use, and it survives both DNA and RNA extraction, so the consensus is that heparinised plasma has no place in molecular infectious disease testing and current guidelines have heparin-containing specimens rejected. The anticoagulants recommended instead are K2/K3-EDTA and acid citrate dextrose, chelators that lock up the calcium the DNA-degrading nucleases need.

preguntas.fuente: MyPlate, USDA: Vegetables — subgroups
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she eats only salad greens and wants credit for the whole vegetable group. Into how many subgroups are vegetables sorted, and on what basis?
opciones: Five subgroups, sorted by the nutrients the vegetables supply
Five subgroups, sorted by whether they are fresh, frozen or canned
Three subgroups, sorted by the nutrients the vegetables supply
Four subgroups, sorted by how the vegetables are usually cooked
preguntas.explicacion: Vegetables fall into five nutrient-based subgroups: red and orange; dark green; starchy; beans, peas and lentils; and the other vegetables. Variety across the five is the point of the split. Fresh, frozen, canned and dried forms all count toward the group, so that is not what the subgroups track.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Amendment
preguntas.subtema: Amendment denial · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: The provider reviews the amendment request and concludes the entry is accurate. What is the patient entitled to?
opciones: A written denial and the chance to submit a statement of disagreement for the record
A second review by a licensed professional who took no part in the original decision
Automatic deletion of the disputed entry, since the record must reflect what she reports
A refund of any copying fee she paid, since the amendment request was not granted
preguntas.explicacion: When a covered entity denies an amendment request it must give the individual a written denial and let her submit a statement of disagreement to be included in the record. The rule sets out the process for requesting and answering these requests. The independent second review by a licensed professional belongs to the access right, not to amendment.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Practitioner's Manual (2023 Edition), Disposal of Controlled Substances
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.D.1.e · RMA III.G.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A practitioner wants to destroy expired controlled substances kept in the office. Which record is used?
opciones: Form 41, listing the controlled substances disposed of, kept at least two years
Form 222, listing the controlled substances disposed of, kept at least two years
Form 106, listing the controlled substances disposed of, kept at least two years
The biennial inventory, on which the substances are simply crossed off the list
preguntas.explicacion: When a registrant disposes of controlled substances by any route other than handing them to a reverse distributor, the substances being disposed of are listed on a DEA Form 41, and that record is kept for at least two years. Where a reverse distributor is used for Schedules III to V, the practitioner records the date, the manner of disposal, the distributor's details and the quantity, and the distributor completes the Form 41.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Individual Notice
preguntas.subtema: Substitute breach notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The practice has out-of-date addresses for 14 of the patients affected by a breach. What substitute notice is required?
opciones: A notice on its home page for at least 90 days, or in major print or broadcast media
A notice on its home page for at least 30 days, with no toll-free number needed
A single telephone call to each of the 14, which is the alternative for small numbers
A notice to prominent media outlets, the step reserved for a breach of any size
preguntas.explicacion: Where contact information is insufficient or out of date for 10 or more individuals, substitute notice means posting on the home page of the web site for at least 90 days or placing the notice in major print or broadcast media where those people probably live, and including a toll-free number that stays active at least 90 days. For fewer than 10, another written form, a telephone call or another means will do.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling policy · CMAA 4B k49 k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice writing its telehealth policy has already settled how it will judge which visits suit video. Which two scheduling questions are still on the guidance's list?
opciones: Which days video appointments are offered, and whether patients book online or by calling in
Which days video appointments are offered, and which clinician covers each of those days
Whether patients book online or by calling in, and what fee applies to a video appointment
Which days video appointments are offered, and how long each video slot should be booked for
preguntas.explicacion: The scheduling questions put to a practice before it starts are these: when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether on set days of the week or daily; whether patients will schedule online or by telephoning the office; how the practice will decide that a telehealth appointment is appropriate; and how and when appointment reminders will go out.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Tachycardia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the line drawn between ventricular tachycardia that is sustained and the kind that is not?
opciones: At thirty seconds, or sooner if the patient becomes unstable
At ten seconds, or sooner if the patient becomes unstable
At three beats in a row, or sooner if the patient is unstable
At two minutes, or sooner if the patient becomes unstable
preguntas.explicacion: A run under 30 seconds is nonsustained; one that lasts longer, or that comes with hemodynamic instability, is sustained. A separate label sorts the same rhythm by shape: monomorphic when the complexes match one another, polymorphic when they vary.

preguntas.subtema: Advance directives and incapacity · CCMA 5D · CMA I.A.5 · RMA I.C.1.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: An adult arrives for admission too unwell to take in the written information about advance directives. What does the regulation allow the facility to do?
opciones: Give the information to her family or surrogate, and follow it up with her later
Give the information to her family or surrogate, and treat the duty as discharged
Record that she was incapacitated, which excuses the facility from the duty
Delay the admission until a surrogate can be reached to receive the information
preguntas.explicacion: Where an adult is incapacitated at admission or at the start of care and cannot receive the information or say whether she has an advance directive, the provider may pass it to her family or surrogate the way it issues other policy material. The obligation to the individual survives: follow-up procedures must deliver it to her directly once she is able.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Hematocrit specimen age · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA tube for a hematocrit sat on the counter for eight hours before it was spun. Why is the result questionable?
opciones: After about 6 hours at room temperature the risk of hemolysis rises and red cell shape changes, so results become inaccurate
Whole blood for a hematocrit is acceptable for 24 hours at room temperature, so only the color of the plasma column is affected
The EDTA will have clotted the specimen after that long, which is why hematocrit tubes should contain heparin instead
The packed cell column will read falsely low because the red cells settle and compact before the tube is centrifuged
preguntas.explicacion: A hematocrit is best run straight after collection. Kept at room temperature the red cells change shape as their metabolism runs on, and past about 6 hours hemolysis becomes likely enough to spoil the figure. The 24-hour allowance belongs to prothrombin time specimens, not to this one, and EDTA is the anticoagulant of choice for the macrohematocrit sample, so clotting is not the issue.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Osteoarthritis", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(2) (2027 I.C.6.g(2)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of factors raises the risk of developing osteoarthritis?
opciones: Age, obesity, muscle weakness and previous joint injury
Age, low body weight, declining estrogen and family history
Youth, high activity, low calcium intake and vitamin D lack
Age, tobacco use, high blood pressure and high cholesterol
preguntas.explicacion: What raises the risk of osteoarthritis is age, being female, obesity, the anatomy of the joint, weak muscles, and injury to the joint at work or in sport. Low body weight, declining estrogen and family history point instead to osteoporosis, a different disease of the same system, whose risks also include aging and too little calcium or vitamin D.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anoscopy", Preparation: Positioning
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.c.ii · CCMA 3B4 k61
preguntas.pregunta: Which position is adopted most often for an anoscopy?
opciones: Lateral decubitus, with the upper leg flexed at the hip and the knee
Lithotomy, with both legs in supports and the buttocks past the edge
Supine with the knees drawn up, which opens the anal canal widest
Standing and leaning forward over the end of the examination table
preguntas.explicacion: Side-lying with the upper leg bent is the commonest choice, though the knee-shoulder and prone positions also work. A digital rectal examination goes first, to be sure nothing in the canal would be injured by the instrument. The anoscope is introduced with its obturator in place, which is then removed so the canal can be seen as the device is withdrawn.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Warfarin", Mechanism of Action and Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.8
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a sudden change in how many leafy greens a patient eats matter on warfarin?
opciones: Warfarin depletes usable vitamin K, so the vitamin K in the diet shifts the response
Warfarin needs vitamin K to be activated, so more of it in the diet strengthens the drug
Warfarin binds vitamin K inside the stomach, so any food taken with it blocks absorption
Warfarin is a racemic mixture, so food decides which enantiomer the liver handles first
preguntas.explicacion: Warfarin competitively inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, the enzyme that puts vitamin K back into its usable form, so the liver makes less of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X and less protein C and S. The response varies widely from patient to patient, and a diet rich in vitamin K is one of the factors weighed when dosing, alongside genetics, other illnesses, interacting drugs and adherence.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which situation would be expected to raise a patient's recorded body temperature?
opciones: Heavy clothing, a hot and humid room, a recent meal or strong physical activity
A cool examination room, light clothing and ten minutes of quiet sitting first
The early morning hours, when the daily temperature curve reaches its low point
The first half of the menstrual cycle, before the corpus luteum has formed
preguntas.explicacion: Temperature is not fixed: strong emotion, physical exertion, a meal just eaten, clothing that is too heavy, some medicines, a hot room and high humidity all push the value up. The second half of the menstrual cycle adds about one degree Fahrenheit or more, and the daily low point falls in the early morning.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Cuts and puncture wounds", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: How is a minor cut on a patient's finger cleaned in the office?
opciones: Washed thoroughly with mild soap and water after the hands are washed
Wiped with alcohol and left open to the air so a scab forms faster
Scrubbed with a brush and antiseptic until all the redness is gone
Soaked in hydrogen peroxide for 5 minutes and covered with a dressing
preguntas.explicacion: The person giving first aid washes their hands first, then washes the cut itself with mild soap and water, uses direct pressure to stop the bleeding, and applies an antibacterial ointment and a clean non-stick bandage. A wound is never assumed to be clean because no dirt can be seen, and nobody breathes on an open wound.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Red Reflex", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.c · CCMA 3B4 k62 · RMA III.F.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's red reflex is white in one eye and red in the other. What does that call for?
opciones: Urgent referral to an ophthalmologist, since the finding can be sight-threatening
A repeat check at the two-month well-child visit, since reflexes mature slowly
Reassurance, since a difference in color between the two eyes is a normal variant
A repeat check after the erythromycin ointment has been applied to both eyes
preguntas.explicacion: A normal reflex is red, orange or yellow and looks the same in both eyes in color, intensity and clarity. An abnormal or absent one can point to a congenital cataract, to disease of the retina, to a retinoblastoma, to strabismus, or to a refractive error, and it goes to an ophthalmologist urgently. Debris on the surface can also blacken it, so the patient is asked to blink first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Seating and Wheelchair Evaluation", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.ii · NCMA 2B.2 · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: How much clearance should a wheelchair seat leave behind the patient's knees?
opciones: About 1.5 to 2 inches from the seat's front edge to the popliteal fossa
About 4 to 5 inches from the seat's front edge to the popliteal fossa
None: the seat should reach the popliteal fossa so the thigh is supported
About 1.5 to 2 inches between the footplates and the floor when at rest
preguntas.explicacion: The seat should stop an inch and a half to two inches short of the crease behind the knee. A cushion that is too deep tips the pelvis backward and exaggerates the curve of the spine, and a seat that is too wide puts the wheels out of reach for self-propulsion. Foot supports sit about two inches off the ground, and the feet stay level or slightly raised.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: The autoclave tape on a load changed color, but the biological indicator from that same load grew. What does the guideline direct?
opciones: Repeat the spore test at once, and recall nothing but implants unless the machine is faulty
Recall and reprocess the entire load at once, since a grown indicator proves a failed cycle
Accept the load, because the chemical indicator is the reading that governs a steam cycle
Quarantine the load until the next weekly spore test comes back negative, then release it
preguntas.explicacion: Single positive spore tests happen sporadically: spore resistance varies slightly, the machine may be misused, the culture may pick up a contaminant. When the mechanical and chemical readings say the cycle ran properly, the test is repeated at once and only implants are recalled. If the repeat stays positive, the machine is pulled until serviced.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Frostbite", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's fingers are frostbitten and medical help is far away. How are they rewarmed?
opciones: Soaked in warm water, never hot, for 15 to 30 minutes, without rubbing
Soaked in hot water for 5 minutes and then rubbed briskly to warm them
Held near a radiator until the color returns and the skin feels soft
Massaged gently with a warm dry cloth until sensation comes back
preguntas.explicacion: The affected part goes into water that is warm and never hot, and stays there 15 to 30 minutes, at 104 °F to 108 °F (40 °C to 42.2 °C), with the water kept moving; the warming stops once the skin has gone soft and the color and the feeling have come back. The area is not rubbed or massaged, direct dry heat is not used, and blisters are left alone. Refreezing does worse damage than waiting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Deep Tendon Reflexes", Technique or Treatment: Grading
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.1.a(4)
preguntas.pregunta: On the NINDS muscle stretch reflex scale, what does a grade of 2 mean?
opciones: A reflex whose amplitude sits in the lower half of normal
A reflex whose amplitude sits in the upper half of normal
A reflex smaller than normal, or brought out only by reinforcement
A reflex greater than normal, which includes clonus when present
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs 0 for absent, 1 for a small or trace response including one needing reinforcement, 2 for the lower half of normal, 3 for the upper half, and 4 for enhanced, with clonus counted there. Symmetrical reflexes between 1 and 3 are generally normal when no other upper or lower motor neuron signs are present.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which serious adverse event is described as rare during phlebotomy?
opciones: Loss of consciousness accompanied by tonic clonic seizures
Loss of consciousness lasting under a couple of minutes only
Pain at the puncture site with anxiety about the procedure
Bruising and hematoma at the site of the venepuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Serious adverse events tied to drawing blood are rare, and the example given is a loss of consciousness with tonic clonic fits. Pain at the site, anxiety and fainting are put in the less severe group, and bruising with hematoma is the best documented event of all.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits, Who's eligible and How often
preguntas.subtema: Scheduling considerations · CMAA 4A k52 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose Part B enrollment started four months ago asks to book her first yearly Wellness visit. What does the office tell her?
opciones: It cannot take place within 12 months of her Part B enrollment
It can be booked now, since the 12 months run from her birthday
She has to have a Welcome to Medicare visit first to qualify for it
It cannot be booked until she has been enrolled for a full 24 months
preguntas.explicacion: The first yearly Wellness visit cannot fall within 12 months of the start of Part B, nor within 12 months of a Welcome to Medicare preventive visit. Having had that welcome visit is not a condition of qualifying, though: a patient who never had one is still entitled to the Wellness visit once the 12 months have run. After that it is covered once every 12 months.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions; 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3
preguntas.pregunta: Which term names the process that stops blood loss after a vessel is damaged?
opciones: Hemostasis
Hemolysis
Hemorrhage
Hemopoiesis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a torn vessel so that blood loss stops; when it fails the result is hemorrhage, bleeding out of control. Hemolysis is the rupture of red cells with hemoglobin spilling out, as after an incompatible transfusion, and hemopoiesis, from the roots for blood and production, is the making of the formed elements in the marrow.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): types of CLIA certificates
preguntas.subtema: Five certificate types · PBT VI.F CLIA/CMS · RMA III.C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which CLIA certificate is issued to a laboratory that will perform nonwaived testing but has not yet been inspected?
opciones: Certificate of Registration
Certificate of Compliance
Certificate of Accreditation
Certificate of Waiver
preguntas.explicacion: The Certificate of Registration lets a laboratory begin moderate or high complexity testing until the survey determines compliance; it goes only to laboratories applying for a COC or a COA. After a state or CMS survey finds compliance the laboratory receives a Certificate of Compliance; if it is accredited by a CMS-approved organization it receives a Certificate of Accreditation. Waived-only sites get a COW.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Interfering Factors; and StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A blood count drawn in EDTA reports a platelet count far below the patient's usual value, and the smear shows clumps. Which repeat specimen is suggested?
opciones: A repeat count on blood collected into a citrate tube
A repeat count on blood collected into a heparin tube
A repeat count on serum from a clot activator tube
A repeat count on the same EDTA tube after warming it
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets can clump in EDTA because of antibodies that act only in the presence of that anticoagulant, and the analyser then reports a falsely low count. The way round it is to repeat the count on blood taken into a citrate tube instead. Serum has no platelets left to count.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), A Rational Approach: Semicritical Items
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A laryngoscope blade is used on a patient. How is it categorized, and what is the least processing it may receive?
opciones: Semicritical, so at a minimum it needs high-level disinfection after it is cleaned
Critical, so it has to be sterilized because not one bacterial spore may survive on it
Noncritical, so intact skin is barrier enough and a hospital disinfectant will do for it
Semicritical, but an intermediate-level agent is accepted because the contact is so brief
preguntas.explicacion: Blades touch mucous membranes, which puts them in the semicritical group along with respiratory therapy tubing, endoscopes and diaphragm fitting rings. Those items should carry no microorganisms, though small numbers of spores are tolerated, so high-level disinfection is the floor. The brief-contact exception belongs to items like bed rails.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Payment activities · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which office task falls within the payment activities a covered entity may carry out without authorization?
opciones: Determining a patient's eligibility for coverage under her plan
Training a new medical assistant on how the practice rooms patients
Evaluating whether a clinician should keep hospital privileges
Preparing a de-identified data set for a population health project
preguntas.explicacion: Payment covers what providers do in order to be paid and what plans do to collect premiums and deliver benefits. The examples offered include working out eligibility or coverage and adjudicating claims, reviewing services for medical necessity and for justification of charges, and a limited set of disclosures made to consumer reporting agencies. Training, credentialing and de-identification are health care operations instead.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k40 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient has just given her history to the rooming assistant. What does the guidance ask of the next person?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating it tires her
Take the whole history again, so two versions can be compared
Take the history only from the relative who came with her today
Skip the history, since a form was filled in the waiting room
