preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is advised in taking an older patient's history: wherever it can be arranged, she tells her story a single time, even where other staff in the office would normally help gather it, because giving the account once and then again is tiring. Preliminary data may instead be pulled from records or from forms filled in at home.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, leukemia and lymphoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how leukemia and lymphoma differ. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: Leukemia starts in blood-forming tissue, lymphoma in immune system cells
Leukemia starts in immune system cells, lymphoma in blood-forming tissue
Leukemia starts in the lymph nodes, lymphoma in the marrow of the bones
Leukemia starts in bone or soft tissue, lymphoma in the lining of organs
preguntas.explicacion: Leukemia begins in the tissue that forms blood, the bone marrow above all, and abnormal blood cells are then produced in large numbers and pour into the bloodstream. Lymphoma begins in cells of the immune system and falls into two families: Hodgkin lymphoma, marked by the Reed-Sternberg cell, and the non-Hodgkin lymphomas, a large and varied group.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: Incorrect urine collection stayed at 9.2 % in the audited hospital even after staff began speaking to patients. What were patients told about?
opciones: The sampling itself, the type of container, and collecting the midstream portion
Fasting for twelve hours, the type of container, and the time of the first void
The volume required, the transport temperature, and the use of a preservative
The sampling itself, the labeling of the cup, and the delivery time to the bench
preguntas.explicacion: Urine testing is unusually exposed to preanalytical trouble because the patient, not a trained collector, takes the sample. In that laboratory the receiving secretary explained the sampling, the container types, sterile and with or without preservative, and how to catch the midstream portion. Even so, incorrect collection remained at 9.2 % of the urine samples received.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hyperlipidemia", Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with high cholesterol is being worked up for a secondary cause. Which of these appears on that differential?
opciones: Metabolic syndrome, along with hypothyroidism and chronic renal insufficiency
Metabolic syndrome, plus acute conjunctivitis and otitis media in children
Osteoarthritis, along with hypothyroidism and chronic renal insufficiency
Pelvic inflammatory disease, along with obesity and biliary obstruction
preguntas.explicacion: Before hyperlipidemia is called primary, the secondary processes have to be ruled through: diabetes, metabolic syndrome, obesity, anorexia, renal insufficiency that has become chronic, nephrotic syndrome, hypothyroidism, and obstruction of the liver or the biliary tree. A full history and physical with comprehensive labs is what narrows that list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 3F k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart records a vascular graft in the arm the phlebotomist was about to use. What does that mean for the draw?
opciones: The graft is a listed contraindication, so another site is chosen
The graft is acceptable if the puncture is made well below it
The graft is acceptable once the tourniquet is placed above it
The graft only rules out the arm when dialysis is being given
preguntas.explicacion: Among the contraindications tied to the site are scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or an abscess, a hematoma, a vascular graft, venous fibrosis felt on palpation, a previous radical mastectomy on that side, and any device placed for venous access.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: Every row of a refrigerator temperature log is dated and initialled by the person who read the thermometer. Who else reviews and signs the log, and when?
opciones: Whoever directs or supervises the testing, once the month is complete
Whoever directs or supervises the testing, each day a reading is entered
Whoever directs or supervises the testing, only when a reading is out of range
Whoever reads the thermometer, again at the end of every working week
preguntas.explicacion: Each reading is dated and initialled or signed by whoever took it; on top of that, whoever directs or supervises testing reviews and signs the log when it is complete for the month. That same person is contacted straight away when a temperature falls outside the recommended range, but the signature is a monthly review, not a daily one and not an out-of-range one.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Drug Name Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order is written as MS 4 mg. What is the danger, and what is the correct practice?
opciones: It can mean morphine or magnesium sulfate, so the drug name is spelled out
It can mean morphine or a multiple sclerosis code, so the dose is spelled out
It can mean milligrams or micrograms, so the unit is spelled out in full
It can mean a syrup or a solution, so the dosage form is spelled out in full
preguntas.explicacion: MS and MSO4 stand for morphine sulfate and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate, and the three are swapped for each other in handwriting. Two very different drugs behind one set of letters is why all of them are banned, and the practice is to write the complete drug name every time.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Assessment
preguntas.subtema: SOAP assessment · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which content belongs in the assessment section of a SOAP note?
opciones: The synthesis of the findings into a diagnosis, with the differential and its reasoning
The chief concern in the patient's own words, followed by the history of present illness
The vital signs and laboratory results gathered during the encounter that day
The tests still needed and the treatment steps planned for each identified problem
preguntas.explicacion: The assessment brings subjective and objective findings together to reach a diagnosis, weighing the problems, their possible interactions and any change in status, and listing problems in order of importance. The differential runs from most to least likely with the reasoning stated, and should include unlikely conditions that could cause harm if missed. Testing and treatment steps belong to the plan.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Clinical Resource Management Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care: Traditional Reimbursement Models
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CCMA 1A k6 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which payment model pays the clinician for each separate service furnished?
opciones: Fee-for-service, which ties payment directly to each service delivered
Capitation, which pays a fixed amount per patient over a period of time
Global payment, which offers a lump sum for one whole episode of care
Prospective payment, which fixes rates by average resource consumption
preguntas.explicacion: Fee-for-service pays the clinician for every service delivered, so payment is tied directly to the delivery of care; third-party payers reimburse from fee schedules or from negotiated rates. The model leaves clinicians and patients room to choose services, but it has been criticized for rewarding quantity over quality and for containing no costs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Concussion", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.s · 2027 I.B.8.s · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What is a concussion?
opciones: A traumatically induced disturbance of brain function that is transient
A bruise of the scalp with bleeding under the skin above the skull
A fracture of the skull that leaves the brain tissue itself untouched
A permanent loss of brain function following a hard blow to the head
preguntas.explicacion: A concussion is a disturbance of brain function caused by trauma, and it passes. It is one of the traumatic brain injuries, which range from mild transient symptoms to long periods of altered consciousness; because the symptoms are usually self-limited, the term mild traumatic brain injury is often used for it. The outlook is generally good.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why is there no single free-hemoglobin concentration above which every test result must be rejected?
opciones: The interference is optical, chemical or immunological, so the acceptable limit depends on the test and the method
The interference affects only enzymes, so a single limit applies to LDH and CK and none to other analytes
The interference disappears once the serum is diluted, so any sample can be reported after dilution
The interference is constant across analyzers, but each laboratory is free to pick its own limit
preguntas.explicacion: Free hemoglobin interferes in different ways, optically, chemically, or by interacting with antigen or antibody in immunoassays, so the upper limit of hemoglobin tolerated in serum or plasma is test- and method-dependent; the reagent's method description should state the serum index limitations, and laboratories are advised to load those cut-offs into their analyzers. Even specific proteins such as CRP and haptoglobin can be affected.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Treadmill Stress Testing", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: During a treadmill test the patient turns dizzy and unsteady on the feet. What does that call for?
opciones: Stopping the test: growing neurologic symptoms are absolute
Slowing the belt by one stage and going on with the test
Going on until the target heart rate has been reached
Stopping the test only if the tracing changes as well
preguntas.explicacion: Increasing neurologic symptoms such as unsteadiness, dizziness or near-fainting sit on the absolute list, so the test ends there and does not wait for the tracing to change. Mild symptoms in a stable patient with a normal tracing are the ones that do not oblige a stop.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Allergic reactions", Symptoms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which finding turns a mild allergic reaction into one treated as severe?
opciones: Wheezing with difficulty swallowing and swelling of the tongue
A few hives over the neck and the face with mild itching of the skin
Watery red eyes with nasal congestion after mowing a lawn
A rash that appears where a new lotion has been applied
preguntas.explicacion: A mild reaction shows a few hives, itching, a rash, a stuffy nose or watery red eyes. The moderate to severe picture adds wheezing, breathing that sounds high-pitched, trouble swallowing, swelling of the face, eyes or tongue, chest tightness, vomiting, dizziness or unconsciousness, and it is handled as anaphylaxis.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Qualifying life event (QLE)
preguntas.subtema: Coverage enrollment · CMAA 5 k73, 5B k66 · CCMA 5E k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a qualifying life event for a Special Enrollment Period?
opciones: Turning 26 and losing the coverage held through a parent's plan
Turning 26 and choosing a plan with a lower monthly premium
Changing doctors within the network the current plan contracts with
Reaching the out-of-pocket limit of the plan before the year ends
preguntas.explicacion: Qualifying life events fall into four groups: losing coverage, changes in the household, changes in residence, and other events such as income changes or leaving incarceration. Turning 26 and dropping off a parent's plan is listed as a loss of coverage. Wanting a cheaper premium, switching doctors inside the network, or hitting the out-of-pocket limit are not events that open enrollment outside the yearly window.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits, Description
preguntas.subtema: Scheduling considerations · CMAA 4A k52 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient calls to book her yearly Wellness visit and also wants her painful knee looked at. What should the office do?
opciones: Book a separate appointment for the knee so the visit stays on prevention
Add the knee to the Wellness visit, which covers a routine physical exam
Send her to a Welcome to Medicare visit, where new problems are handled
Put the knee on the Health Risk Assessment so it is covered that day
preguntas.explicacion: The yearly Wellness visit is a conversation about a personalised prevention plan, and it is expressly not a routine physical examination. A patient with a specific health worry is told to book a separate appointment for it so that the Wellness visit stays on prevention. The Health Risk Assessment is the questionnaire that feeds the prevention plan, not a way of adding complaints.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4a: Common Household Conversions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(2) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7
preguntas.pregunta: A parent is told to give one tablespoon of a liquid antibiotic. How much is that in the metric system?
opciones: 15 mL, which is also 3 teaspoons
10 mL, which is also 2 teaspoons
5 mL, which is also 1 teaspoon
30 mL, which is also 6 teaspoons
preguntas.explicacion: In the household system a teaspoon is 5 mL and a tablespoon is 3 teaspoons, which comes to 15 mL. Thirty milliliters is an ounce, not a tablespoon, so mixing the two doubles the dose. Patients are familiar with household measures, which is why the equivalences have to be at hand, but the metric system is the one used for the calculation and for what is written down.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A bronchoalveolar lavage specimen for molecular detection of Pneumocystis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis is being sent from the bronchoscopy suite. How is it transported and stored?
opciones: Transported on ice; stored at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, or at −20 to −80 °C for the long term
Transported at room temperature; stored at 4 °C for up to 4 hours, then discarded as unsuitable
Transported on wet ice only if RNA is the target; stored at room temperature for up to 7 days
Transported frozen at −70 °C; stored at 4 to 8 °C for up to 7 days with a mucolytic additive
preguntas.explicacion: For bronchoalveolar lavage the general guideline is transport on ice, storage at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, and −20 to −80 °C for long-term keeping; time and temperature are the preanalytical variables listed for it. Wet ice reserved for RNA targets is the CSF entry, 4 to 8 °C for 7 days with N-acetyl-L-cysteine or dithiothreitol is the sputum entry, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement: Reasonable Reliance
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable reliance · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A public official states that what he is requesting is the minimum necessary for a purpose the rule permits. May the practice rely on that?
opciones: Yes, where the reliance is reasonable in the circumstances of the request
Yes, and the practice is then barred from making its own determination
No, the practice must always decide for itself what the minimum necessary is
No, unless the official supplies a court order covering the same records
preguntas.explicacion: In certain circumstances the rule lets a covered entity rely on the judgment of the requester about how much information is needed, provided the reliance is reasonable. That is permitted for a public official or agency stating the request is the minimum necessary for a permitted purpose, for a workforce member or business associate professional saying the same, and for a researcher with board documentation. Reliance is never obligatory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · PBT II.G · RMA III.C.4
preguntas.pregunta: In the Westergren method, how long does the anticoagulated blood stand in the vertical tube before the result is read?
opciones: Sixty minutes
Fifteen minutes
Ten minutes
Thirty minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The Westergren tube, 2.5 mm in internal bore and 190 to 300 mm long, is left upright for an hour while the red cells settle under gravity, and the distance they fall in millimeters is the result. Ten to fifteen minutes is the clotting time for a red tube before centrifugation; no shorter interval is given for reading the sedimentation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which limb wire is the green one, under the usual color code?
opciones: Left leg, while the right leg wire is black
Right leg, while the left leg wire is black
Left arm, while the right arm wire is black
Right arm, while the left arm wire is black
preguntas.explicacion: The four limb wires are colored so they cannot be swapped: red for the right arm, yellow for the left arm, green for the left leg and black for the right leg. Matching the color to the limb before recording is the quickest guard against a reversal that would distort the tracing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Arrhythmia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A healthy young adult's rate rises with inspiration and falls with expiration. What is that?
opciones: Sinus arrhythmia, a normal finding that indicates good health
Sinus tachycardia, a normal finding after any light exercise
Premature atrial beats, a common finding at that age
A second-degree block, which drops the occasional beat
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing changes vagal tone from beat to beat: inspiration lifts the rate and expiration lowers it. This respiratory form is the common one, is seen most in children and young adults, and is taken as a marker of cardiac health; losing it can point to underlying heart disease.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Tourniquet and Gloves; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(iii)
preguntas.subtema: Latex and the tourniquet · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a history of latex allergy and the phlebotomist has no elastic band at hand. What must she not do?
opciones: Use a latex glove as a tourniquet on that patient
Ask a colleague to bring a latex-free band to the room
Draw the sample without applying a tourniquet at all
Use a clean band that has been reprocessed since its last use
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table is explicit that a latex glove must never stand in as a tourniquet where the patient reports a history of latex allergy, since some patients react to latex. Gloves follow the same logic: one clean, well-fitting disposable pair, latex or latex-free, for each patient or each procedure. The employer must also keep hypoallergenic gloves or similar alternatives within reach for workers who react to the ones normally supplied.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.d · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: A povidone-iodine scrub has been painted on the skin. The clinician wants to begin immediately. What is the problem?
opciones: The product only kills bacteria once dry, and two minutes is the preferred minimum
The product has to be wiped off first, since dried iodine blocks the scalpel's entry
The product has to be rinsed with saline first, or it will stain the drapes and the skin
The product has to be covered with alcohol first, which is what activates the iodine
preguntas.explicacion: Povidone-iodine scrubs, at 7.5 to 10 percent, are painted onto clean skin and left to dry: drying is what makes them bactericidal, and the preferred minimum drying time is two minutes, though it varies by product. Staining of skin, hair and clothing is a known nuisance of the agent, and its microbicidal activity is lost on contact with blood or sputum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.D.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the hands held higher than the elbows while rinsing after a surgical scrub?
opciones: So the water runs from the cleanest area toward the least clean and drips off the elbow
So the water carries the antiseptic down the arm and extends its residual activity there
So the water never touches the forearm, which is scrubbed but is not rinsed at that stage
So the water pressure does not force soap under the nails, where debris was just removed
preguntas.explicacion: After scrubbing, the hands are the cleanest part and the forearms and elbows the least clean, so the arm is passed through the running water in one direction and then raised again to let the water drip off the elbow. Ordinary handwashing runs the other way, hands below the elbows, because there the hands are the dirtier end and the water should run off the fingertips.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Patient Identity and Patient Record Matching
preguntas.subtema: Avoiding duplicate records · CMAA 4D k57 · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.4.a · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A scheduler asks how the system works out that two records belong to the same person. Which fields does ONC name as the minimum?
opciones: Several demographic fields at once: name, date of birth, telephone number and address
The medical record number by itself, since it is unique inside the system that issued it
The insurance member number and group number carried on the card the patient presents
Name and date of birth only, the two identifiers used to confirm a patient before care
preguntas.explicacion: Patient matching is what identifies a patient's data and links it together, both inside a health system and between systems, so that a full view of the record comes into being. The minimum way it is done is by tying several demographic fields together: name, birth date, telephone number and address. ONC calls it critical to interoperability and to the national health IT infrastructure.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: A heavy irregular item has to reach the sterile field. How is it transferred?
opciones: It is opened and held while a second person in sterile gloves lifts it onto the field
It is opened and dropped from a greater height so the wrapper stays clear of the field
It is opened and slid across the drape from the near edge toward the middle of the field
It is opened and set on the one-inch border, then nudged inward with a sterile forceps
preguntas.explicacion: Heavy or irregular items are not tossed. They are opened and held by the person with the packaging, and someone wearing sterile gloves takes them onto the field. Sliding an item across the drape or resting it on the one-inch border defeats the purpose, since that border and the outer wrapper are both counted as unsterile.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office for Human Research Protections, The Belmont Report (April 18, 1979), Part B
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Which three principles does the Belmont Report set out?
opciones: Respect for persons, beneficence and justice
Autonomy, confidentiality and truthfulness
Beneficence, nonmaleficence and fidelity
Respect for persons, privacy and fairness
preguntas.explicacion: The Belmont Report, published in 1979 by the national commission the National Research Act created, names three basic principles for research with human subjects: beneficence, justice, and respect for persons. Respect for persons carries two duties, honoring autonomy and protecting those whose autonomy is diminished. Not harming lives inside beneficence there, as the rule to do no harm.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Stock Rotation and Removal
preguntas.subtema: Stock rotation · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7E k99 · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: How should stock be arranged inside a storage unit, and what happens to what has expired?
opciones: The earliest expiration dates go in front, and expired stock is pulled out at once
The newest deliveries go in front, and expired stock is pulled at the next count
The most used items go in front, and expired stock is kept until it is replaced
The earliest expiration dates go behind, and expired stock is marked for return
preguntas.explicacion: Stock is rotated so that whatever expires first is what the hand reaches first, with later dates behind it. Anything already expired is taken out immediately rather than at the next count, because leaving it there is how an invalid dose gets given by mistake.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guidelines for Health Care Personnel Exposed to Hepatitis C Virus, Test the source patient; Test the HCP; Follow-up testing
preguntas.subtema: HCV testing algorithm · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: According to the CDC, when is the source patient tested for hepatitis C after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Right away, within 48 hours if possible, ideally by RNA testing
Within 72 hours, using an antibody test with no reflex to RNA
At 3 to 6 weeks, when HCV RNA becomes detectable in the source
At 4 to 6 months, alongside the exposed worker's final antibody test
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC has the source patient tested right away, within 48 hours where that can be managed, and prefers a nucleic acid test for HCV RNA, or else an antibody test that reflexes to NAT when positive; the exposed worker is tested at the same time with an antibody test that reflexes to RNA. Where follow-up is indicated, the worker gets an RNA test at 3 to 6 weeks and a final antibody test at 4 to 6 months. Those later dates belong to the worker's schedule, not the source's, and 72 hours is the HIV PEP window.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health: Complementary, Alternative, or Integrative Health — What's In a Name?
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on prescribed medication asks whether she may keep her yoga and acupuncture. Which approach is she describing?
opciones: Conventional and complementary approaches brought together in a coordinated way
Complementary approaches used in place of the conventional ones altogether
Conventional care given by one provider who also supplies the medication
Complementary approaches studied in the laboratory before they are offered
preguntas.explicacion: In integrative health the conventional and the complementary are coordinated and brought together, and it leans on multimodal care: two or more interventions, such as medication or physical rehabilitation alongside acupuncture or yoga, aimed at the whole person rather than one organ system, with care coordinated across providers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Drug Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen interpretation · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient known to take clonazepam has a negative benzodiazepine screen. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: The immunoassay targets oxazepam and may miss other benzodiazepines
The specimen was collected outside the 1-to-2-hour appearance window
The patient's urine was too dilute for any immunoassay to read it
Benzodiazepines are only measurable in blood, never in urine at all
preguntas.explicacion: A negative result means the substance the assay looks for was not detected, either because the concentration sat below the threshold or because there was no use in the relevant window. False negatives are common when the analytes an immunoassay targets are not known: benzodiazepine testing often aims at the metabolite oxazepam and may miss clonazepam or alprazolam. A negative does not rule out use.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, scope of practice · CPT D1 1D scope of practice · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.6 scope of practice · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the phlebotomist whether her potassium result means she has kidney disease. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Say that the ordering provider interprets results, and route the question to that provider
Read the reference interval aloud and show her where her own value falls against it
Tell her the value is normal for her age, since age-based intervals are on the report
Refuse to discuss the report at all, because privacy rules bar giving results to patients
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA puts interpretation on the far side of the bench: reference intervals go to whoever was authorized to order the test and to whoever is responsible for using the results, and the results themselves are released only to those people. Refusing outright is wrong for another reason, since a patient may request access to her own completed report.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 k157 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does one small square on the grid stand for on the time axis?
opciones: 0.04 seconds, and five of them make one large square
0.02 seconds, and five of them make one large square
0.20 seconds, and five of them make one large square
0.10 seconds, and five of them make one large square
preguntas.explicacion: Each large square is divided into five small ones, so a small square is worth 0.04 seconds. That is the unit used to measure the waves: a PR interval of three to five small squares is normal, and a Q wave wider than a single small square is one of the signs of an old infarct.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Adapting Your Communication
preguntas.subtema: Pediatric communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(b) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(a) · RMA I.D.1.a · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: A four-year-old is frightened before a procedure. Which approach is recommended?
opciones: Speak calmly and demonstrate the steps on a doll
Explain the anatomy behind each step in order
Promise the child that it will not hurt at all
Offer the choice of skipping the step for today
preguntas.explicacion: With children, speak calmly and gently, and demonstrating what will be done on a doll or stuffed animal helps; play and drawing build trust. Anatomy sits above a preschooler's developmental level, promising no pain is false reassurance, and the choices offered have to stay inside real limits.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly, Actions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which word choice matches plain-language guidance for talking with patients?
opciones: 'Helpful' rather than 'beneficial'
'Exacerbate' rather than 'make worse'
'Abdomen' rather than 'tummy or belly'
'Venipuncture' rather than 'blood draw'
preguntas.explicacion: The examples are direct: say 'helpful' where you would have said 'beneficial', and 'make worse' where you would have said 'exacerbate', and use everyday words such as tummy or belly rather than abdomen, keeping clear of acronyms. If a medical term really matters, ask whether the patient knows it and then define it simply. The three distractors each run the advice backwards.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: When may a patient buy any Medigap policy she likes without being refused because of her health?
opciones: In the six months that begin the first month she has Part B and is sixty-five
In the six months that begin the first month she has Part A and is sixty-five
In the Medicare Open Enrollment Period, which comes round once every year
In the eight months that follow the day she or her spouse stops working
preguntas.explicacion: The Medigap Open Enrollment Period runs for six months from the first month in which the person has Part B and is sixty-five or older. During it she may enroll in any Medigap policy and the company cannot refuse her over pre-existing health problems. It happens once and does not come round every year the way the Medicare Open Enrollment Period does.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is asked of the patient before a recording begins?
opciones: A brief history of medicines and of adhesive gel allergy
A brief history of surgery and of iodine contrast allergy
The time of the last meal and of the last cigarette
The results of the last two tracings held on file
preguntas.explicacion: A short history of drugs and of allergy to the adhesive gel is taken first, because sensitivity to the adhesive is one of the two relative contraindications. Fasting and smoking questions belong to the exercise stress test, not to a resting tracing.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guidance for SARS-CoV-2 Rapid Testing in Point-of-Care Settings: Quality Practices; Specimen Collection; Reporting
preguntas.subtema: COVID antigen batch practices · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA 2027 I.C.10.d.(7) COVID-19 · RMA III.C.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: A pharmacy runs rapid antigen SARS-CoV-2 tests on several people in a batch under its Certificate of Waiver. Which practice does the CDC guidance for point-of-care sites call for?
opciones: Change gloves between specimens and read each result only within the manufacturer's time frame
Keep the same gloves through the batch to save supplies, but disinfect the counter every hour
Read all cassettes together once the last one has run, so that every result is interpreted at once
Report every negative antigen result to the state health department within 24 hours of testing
preguntas.explicacion: For SARS-CoV-2 testing at the point of care, the guidance calls for new gloves for each person tested, a change of gloves between specimens when processing in batches to avoid cross-contamination, instructions followed in their stated order, results read only within the manufacturer's time frame, and instruments decontaminated after each use. Surfaces near the collection area are disinfected hourly and between collections. Since April 4, 2022, reporting negative rapid antigen results is no longer required.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Normal and Abnormal Complete Blood Count With Differential", section Platelet Tests; Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Pseudothrombocytopenia · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(4)(d) (2027: b.(7)) · RMA III.C.4.d
preguntas.pregunta: An automated CBC on an EDTA sample reports a platelet count of 90,000/µL with a platelet-clump flag, in a patient with no bleeding. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: EDTA-induced platelet clumping has produced a spuriously low count (pseudothrombocytopenia)
True thrombocytopenia, which at this level carries a high risk of spontaneous major bleeding
The clumps were counted as red cells, so the RBC count is falsely high and the platelets truly low
The sample was collected in a citrate tube, which dilutes the platelets by about 10 % in every case
preguntas.explicacion: The adult platelet reference interval is 150,000 to 400,000/µL. Platelet counts may appear low because platelets clump in the presence of the EDTA in the collection tube, causing pseudothrombocytopenia, and clumped platelets can be counted as white cells by the analyzer. Major bleeding is unusual unless platelets fall below 50,000/µL, and the risk of spontaneous major bleeding rises sharply below 20,000/µL. Any abnormality is checked against interfering factors, often with a blood smear.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Health Insurance Marketplace
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An uninsured patient asks the front desk what the Health Insurance Marketplace is for. What does it do?
opciones: Helps people compare health insurance and sign up for coverage
Pays the claims that providers submit for the enrolled members
Sets the fee schedule that every insurer in a state has to use
Certifies the providers a health plan may place in its network
preguntas.explicacion: The Marketplace is a service for shopping and enrolling: it helps people compare health insurance and sign up. The federal government runs it for most states, while some states run their own. Applying with income and household information shows whether the person qualifies for premium tax credits and other savings, or for coverage through Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Federal plain language guidelines
preguntas.subtema: Testing for understanding · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: The office has drafted a letter about a change in visiting hours in language it believes is clear. Which step does the federal plain language guidance add?
opciones: Testing the wording with the audience to see that it is really understood
Having a second staff member read it aloud and correct the punctuation
Sending it to the agency that enforces the writing law for its approval
Rewriting it at the reading level printed on the practice's own website
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance runs in stages: understand the principles, write for understanding, design for understanding, and then test for understanding. Clear writing is judged by whether the specific audience actually makes sense of it, which is the requirement the 2010 statute put on content written for the public.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heart attack first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the office has crushing chest pain and is sweating but is awake and talking. What is done?
opciones: Call for help, sit the patient down to rest, and loosen tight clothing
Walk the patient slowly to a couch and give a full glass of cold water
Lay the patient flat with the legs raised and start chest compressions
Wait for the provider to see the patient before any call is made out
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency help is called first. The patient sits down, rests and is kept calm, tight clothing is loosened, and the assistant asks whether they carry chest pain medicine such as nitroglycerin and helps them take it. Nothing else goes into the mouth unless a heart medicine has been prescribed for that patient.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Who is Covered by the Privacy Rule
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA scope · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A solo practitioner bills every claim on paper and never sends a standard electronic transaction. Is that office a HIPAA covered entity?
opciones: No, because a provider is covered only once it sends health information in a standard transaction
Yes, because sending patients e-mail is by itself an electronic transmission of their health data
Yes, because every provider of medical services is a covered entity regardless of how claims go out
No, because only hospitals and health plans are ever treated as covered entities under the rules
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of organization are covered: health plans, clearinghouses, and any provider, of any size, that transmits health information electronically in a transaction for which HHS adopted a standard, such as a claim or an eligibility inquiry. Using electronic technology like e-mail does not by itself make a provider covered; the transmission has to be a standard transaction.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cystoscopy", Indications
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.4.d.ii · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: Which complaint is among the commonest reasons a patient is referred for cystoscopy?
opciones: Hematuria, whether visible to the eye or found only under the microscope
Nocturia alone, which is what the instrument is designed to investigate
Flank pain alone, since the scope reaches the kidney through the ureter
Proteinuria on a dipstick, which the scope confirms by direct inspection
preguntas.explicacion: Blood in the urine, gross or microscopic, is one of the commonest reasons for referral; microscopic means three or more red cells per high-power field. Other indications include surveillance after urothelial cancer, lower urinary tract symptoms, trauma, abnormalities seen on imaging and removal of foreign bodies. The scope shows urethra, bladder and orifices.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Holter monitor (24h)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii III.F.7
preguntas.pregunta: What is the patient asked to keep while wearing the monitor?
opciones: A diary of activities and of how they felt at each time
A diary of meals and of the medicines taken each day
A record of the pulse counted at the wrist twice a day
A record of the times the electrodes were changed over
preguntas.explicacion: The written record of what the patient was doing and feeling is what gives the recording its meaning, because the provider matches those entries against the rhythm at the same hour. Most devices also have a button that marks the moment a symptom appears.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Pathophysiology; and "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: During a difficult draw the patient begins to sweat and turn pale but does not lose consciousness. What is this state called?
opciones: Near syncope or presyncope
Vasovagal or reflex syncope
Situational reflex syncope
Carotid sinus syncope
preguntas.explicacion: Near syncope or presyncope is the feeling that one is going to pass out without actually doing so, and says it shares the mechanism of syncope, cerebral hypoperfusion. Vasovagal, situational and carotid sinus syncope are the three types of reflex syncope in the vasovagal chapter, all of which involve an actual transient loss of consciousness.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which sequence correctly describes the oral glucose tolerance test?
opciones: Fasting sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample at 2 hours
Fasting sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample at 1 hour
Random sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample drawn at 2 hours
Fasting sample, 150 g of carbohydrate, and a sample at 3 hours
preguntas.explicacion: The OGTT runs like this: a fasting sample after at least 8 hours without food, then 75 g of anhydrous glucose taken dissolved in water, then a second sample at 2 hours; a 2-hour value of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or above meets the diabetes criterion. The one-hour sample belongs to the challenge test, and 150 g of carbohydrate refers to the traditional three-day pre-test diet.

preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, High Blood Pressure: Diagnosis, Blood Pressure Levels
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's reading is 134/84 mm Hg on two separate visits. Which category does that fall in?
opciones: Stage 1 high blood pressure: 130 to 139 systolic or 80 to 89 diastolic
Elevated blood pressure: 120 to 129 systolic together with under 80 diastolic
Stage 2 high blood pressure: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
Normal blood pressure, because the diastolic value has stayed under 85 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: The bands are normal under 120 and under 80; elevated at 120 to 129 with a diastolic under 80; stage 1 at 130 to 139 or 80 to 89; stage 2 at 140 or more or 90 or more; and crisis above 180 or above 120. Note the conjunctions: the first two need both numbers to qualify, while the stages need only one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; Interfering Factors; Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: ESR specimen timing · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(3) · RMA III.C.4.b.iii / 4.d
preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA sample for an ESR was collected three hours ago and has just reached the bench. What should the technician expect?
opciones: The ESR may read falsely low, because testing should begin within 2 hours before the red cells lose their biconcave shape
The ESR may read falsely high, because red cells clump into larger rouleaux the longer the sample stands at room temperature
The result is acceptable, because whole blood for an ESR is stable for 24 hours at room temperature or at 4 °C
The result is acceptable only if the sample is transferred to a black-top citrate tube before the test is set up
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for an ESR goes into a black-top citrate tube or an EDTA lavender one, and the test has to start inside 2 hours of the draw. Delay costs the red cells their biconcave shape, which slows the sedimentation, and clotted blood slows it too by breaking up rouleaux. The 24-hour window belongs to prothrombin time samples, not to this. Reference values run 15 mm/hr or lower for men and 20 or lower for women under 50.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A), Contaminated Sharps Discarding and Containment
preguntas.subtema: Sharps containers and regulated waste · CPT D1 k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: OSHA requires that contaminated sharps be discarded into containers with which combination of features?
opciones: Closable, puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom, and labeled or color-coded
Closable, leakproof and labeled or color-coded, with no requirement at all to resist punctures
Fluorescent orange-red with the biohazard symbol, and emptied by hand when it is three-quarters full
Puncture resistant and leakproof on sides and bottom, but left open during use to speed up disposal
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A) lists four features for the container that receives contaminated sharps: it closes, it resists punctures, it does not leak through the sides or the bottom, and it carries the biohazard label or the color code the standard prescribes. While in use it also has to be easy to reach, kept upright, and replaced before it overfills. A container without puncture resistance is the description of a regulated-waste bag in (d)(4)(iii)(B), not a sharps container; reusable sharps containers must never be opened or emptied by hand; and a container left open during use fails the first requirement.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1, Recommended needle gauge, length and device
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge and device by age · CPT D3 k56 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A blood specimen is needed from a neonate. Which needle gauge, device and length does WHO Table 3.1 recommend?
opciones: 23 G winged (butterfly) set, 0.5 inch or 0.75 cm
22 G straight needle, 1 inch or 2.54 cm
21 G straight needle, 1 to 1.5 inch or 2.54 cm long
25 G winged (butterfly) set, 0.5 inch or 0.75 cm
preguntas.explicacion: For the neonatal column, Table 3.1 marks only one option: a 23 G winged butterfly set of 0.5 inch or 0.75 cm, the same device listed for pediatric, elderly and small-vein patients. The 22 G 1 inch needle is for adults and pediatric patients, the 21 G 1 to 1.5 inch needle for adults only, and 25 G does not appear in the table at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a normal oximeter reading treated with caution in a patient with darker skin?
opciones: Devices may overestimate saturation by about 2%, leaving hypoxemia unrecognized
Devices may underestimate saturation by about 2%, prompting oxygen that is not needed
Devices cannot read at all through darker skin, so a blood gas replaces the test
Devices need a longer sampling time, and a short reading is the one that runs high
preguntas.explicacion: Studies show that oximeters can read about 2% high in people with darker skin pigmentation, and the gap widens at lower saturations. The practical consequence is hypoxemia that goes unnoticed, so the value is weighed with the clinical picture instead of being trusted alone. How much a device errs varies by model.

preguntas.subtema: Coding and indexing · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.d · CMAA 7 k91 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A quality study needs every record of a given procedure from last year. Which requirement makes that search possible?
opciones: A coding and indexing system that retrieves records by diagnosis and procedure
A confidentiality procedure that limits who may receive information from a record
An author identification system that shows who wrote each entry in the record
A retention rule that keeps every record available for at least five full years
preguntas.explicacion: Keeping the records is not enough: the hospital also needs a coding and indexing system for them, and that system has to allow timely retrieval by diagnosis and by procedure, precisely so that studies evaluating medical care can be supported. Retention keeps the records; indexing is what finds them.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.2 Structural Organization of the Human Body
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Put the levels of organization in order from the simplest to the most complex.
opciones: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
Tissue, cell, organ system, organ, organism
Cell, organ, tissue, organism, organ system
Organ, cell, tissue, organ system, organism
preguntas.explicacion: The cell is the smallest unit that can function on its own. A group of similar cells working together makes a tissue; two or more tissue types build an organ; organs that share a job make an organ system; and the systems together make the organism. Below the cell sit the chemical levels of atoms and molecules.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Chambers and Circulation through the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which arteries are the exception to the rule, carrying blood that is poor in oxygen after birth?
opciones: The pulmonary trunk and its branches
The four pulmonary veins to the left atrium
The coronary arteries off the ascending aorta
The venae cavae entering the right atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The pulmonary trunk and the two arteries it splits into carry oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle out to the lungs, the one exception among arteries once a person is born; the pulmonary veins are the matching exception among veins, bringing richly oxygenated blood into the left atrium. The coronary arteries leave the ascending aorta carrying oxygenated blood, and the venae cavae are veins.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: In aseptic non-touch technique, what is a key part and what is a key site?
opciones: A key part is a sterile piece of equipment; a key site is broken skin or an insertion point
A key part is broken skin or an insertion point; a key site is a sterile piece of equipment
A key part is the sterile field itself; a key site is the room where the procedure happens
A key part is the practitioner's gloved hand; a key site is the tray holding the supplies
preguntas.explicacion: Key parts are the sterile pieces handled during the procedure: a needle, its hub, the tip of a syringe, a dressing. Key sites are the places on the patient that must not be contaminated: nonintact skin, an insertion point, or the access site of a device already in place, such as an open wound or an intravenous or urinary catheter site.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.512(f)(1) and (f)(2), Disclosures for law enforcement purposes
preguntas.subtema: Law enforcement disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k37
preguntas.pregunta: A police officer asks the laboratory for a patient's blood type and home address to locate a suspect. Which statement reflects HIPAA?
opciones: Name, address and ABO blood type may be given; analyses of body fluids may not
No information may be disclosed without a court order, not even the name
The full record may be disclosed, since law enforcement requests override the Privacy Rule
Only the results of body fluid analyses may be disclosed, not the address
preguntas.explicacion: When the purpose is to identify or locate a fugitive, a suspect, a material witness or someone missing, 164.512(f)(2) lets a covered entity release only a fixed list: name and address, date and place of birth, Social Security number, ABO blood type and Rh factor, type of injury, date and time of treatment or death, and distinguishing physical characteristics. DNA, dental records and the typing, sampling or analysis of body fluid or tissue are expressly left out. Other law-enforcement disclosures need a court order, a warrant, a subpoena or a qualifying administrative request.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Practitioner's Manual (2023 Edition), Ordering Schedules I and II Controlled Substances
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.D.1.e · RMA III.G.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which DEA form does a practitioner use to order Schedule II controlled substances from a supplier?
opciones: Form 222, or its electronic equivalent through the controlled substance ordering system
Form 41, which the registrant uses to list controlled substances being surrendered
Form 106, which is used to report a theft or a significant loss of controlled stock
An invoice, which is what documents the transfer of Schedule III to V substances
preguntas.explicacion: A DEA Form 222, or its electronic equivalent, has to accompany every distribution or transfer of a substance in Schedule I or Schedule II, transfers between practitioners included. A Schedule III to V transfer is documented by an invoice instead. Form 41 records drugs surrendered for destruction and Form 106 reports theft or significant loss, so neither has anything to do with ordering stock.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Feeling behind a patient's medial malleolus you find a firm cord and cannot tell whether it is the artery or a tendon. Which observation separates them?
opciones: A tendon slides under the fingertips, while an artery stays in place
A tendon feels warmer to the finger pad than the artery beside it
A tendon lies deeper, so far heavier pressure is needed to reach it
A tendon crosses the ankle, while the artery runs along its length
preguntas.explicacion: Firm cords sit next to most pulse points, and rolling the structure under the fingertips tells them apart: tendons move, arteries hold still. Two other habits help when a pulse will not come up, warming the limb and letting the patient relax. Too much pressure flattens a weak pulse and too light a touch misses it, so the force is adjusted, not fixed.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Green
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: How does the heparin in a green top tube prevent coagulation?
opciones: It inactivates thrombin, so fibrin is not formed and the sample stays as plasma
It chelates calcium ions, the same mechanism the citrate tube uses
It preserves the viability of microorganisms in a broth mixture
It works as an antiglycolytic agent that keeps glucose stable for days
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 gives the mode of action of sodium or lithium heparin as inactivating thrombin and thromboplastin, and the tube review says heparin inhibits thrombin formation. Calcium chelation is the mechanism the review assigns to EDTA and to citrate; the broth belongs to the blood culture bottle; and the antiglycolytic agent is the sodium fluoride in the gray tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adverse Drug Reactions", Introduction: ADR Definitions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which definition matches an adverse drug reaction?
opciones: A noxious, unintended response at doses normally used for treatment
Any untoward medical occurrence at all during treatment with a product
A predictable effect other than the principal one the drug was used for
A reaction that follows only when more than the prescribed dose is taken
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO and FDA definition is a response to a drug that is both noxious and unintended and that occurs with doses used ordinarily to prevent, to diagnose, to treat, or to modify a physiologic function. An adverse drug event is the wider term: any untoward occurrence during treatment, whether or not the drug caused it. A predictable effect other than the principal one is a side effect, which is one kind of adverse reaction.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A resting pulse of 54 is recorded at intake. Which of the patient's own complaints would make that slow rate worth flagging?
opciones: Fatigue, lightheadedness or dizziness, fainting or near-fainting, and poor tolerance of exertion
Fatigue, a cough that will not clear, swelling of both ankles, and a poor tolerance of cold
Headache on standing, ringing in the ears, blurred vision, and a poor tolerance of bright light
Fatigue and dizziness, but only when the rate has also fallen below 40 beats in a minute
preguntas.explicacion: Most people whose rate sits below 60 feel nothing at all: healthy young adults and athletes hold a slow resting rate through vagal tone, and people past 65 often drop into one while asleep as the sinus node ages. What turns the number into a finding is the story that comes with it. The complaints listed are tiredness, poor tolerance of exercise, lightheadedness, dizziness, fainting or the feeling of almost fainting, angina or heart failure getting worse, and thinking that has slowed. There is no second rate threshold that has to be crossed before symptoms count.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The median cubital vein sends a named connection to each of the two main superficial veins. What are they called?
opciones: The median cephalic vein and the median basilic vein
The median antebrachial vein and the median basilic vein
The dorsal venous arch and the median antebrachial vein
The accessory cephalic vein and the perforating basilic vein
preguntas.explicacion: Where it links the two superficial channels, the median cubital vein is described as having a link to the cephalic, called the median cephalic vein, and a link to the basilic, called the median basilic vein. The median antebrachial vein is a separate forearm vessel dominant in one variant.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Grey
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: The gray top tube holds two substances. Which one is the anticoagulant, and what does the other one do?
opciones: Potassium oxalate binds calcium; sodium fluoride blocks glycolysis
Sodium fluoride binds the calcium; potassium oxalate blocks glycolysis
Sodium citrate binds calcium; sodium fluoride preserves the cells
Potassium oxalate inhibits thrombin; sodium fluoride binds calcium
preguntas.explicacion: The gray tube contains potassium oxalate, which binds calcium and so prevents coagulation, together with sodium fluoride, which acts as an antiglycolytic agent; that combination is why the tube is used for plasma glucose and lactic acid. Swapping the two roles reverses the review, citrate belongs to the light blue tube, and thrombin inhibition is heparin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", sections Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A ward nurse sees a colleague filling the tubes in the wrong sequence. What is asked of staff outside the laboratory in that situation?
opciones: To know the order of draw and call attention to it at once
To leave the sequence entirely to the laboratory personnel
To let the laboratory refuse the tubes and request a repeat
To write it up and raise it at the next meeting of the staff
preguntas.explicacion: Nurses and clinicians are asked to be aware of the order of draw so that, seeing the sequence go wrong at the bedside, they can call attention to it before the patient is affected. Filling the tubes out of sequence pushes results falsely up or falsely down in biochemistry, hematology, serology and microbiology, and an unnoticed result can reach the clinician.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Range of Motion Exercises
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.1.d · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: Range-of-motion exercises come in three kinds. Which are they?
opciones: Passive, active, and active assist
Passive, resisted, and active assist
Active, resisted, and weight bearing
Passive, active, and weight bearing
preguntas.explicacion: The three kinds are passive, active and active assist. Passive means an outside force moves the joint while the patient stays relaxed, active means the patient moves the joint with no outside help, and active assist means the patient moves it with partial help from someone or something else.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 k60 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the WHO say the tourniquet should be applied when selecting a venipuncture site?
opciones: About four to five finger widths above the venipuncture site, then re-examine the vein
About 2 cm above the site, the width of the area the swab must cover
About four to five finger widths below the site, so the vein fills from the hand
Right over the median cubital vein, with the thumb anchoring just below it
preguntas.explicacion: In Step 3 the WHO guideline places the tourniquet roughly four to five finger widths above the point where the needle will go in, and then has the phlebotomist look at the vein again. The same step says the vein should already be visible before the tourniquet goes on, and that finding it helps in choosing the right needle size. The 2 cm figure belongs to Step 5, the area the alcohol swab has to cover; the thumb below the site is the anchoring hand in Step 6, not the tourniquet; and below the site is the wrong side altogether.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Systems-Level and Organizational Factors
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does psychological safety mean in a clinical team?
opciones: The shared belief that speaking up will not bring reprisal
The shared picture of the plan that every member carries
The habit of watching the stress levels of other members
The readiness to take over work when a colleague falls behind
preguntas.explicacion: Psychological safety is the belief, shared across the team, that a member can speak up and face no reprisal for it, and teams that have it report conflict earlier and turn it into learning rather than blame. The other three options describe a shared mental model, cross-monitoring and backup behavior, which are separate teamwork concepts.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, extinguisher types; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(c)(3)
preguntas.subtema: Extinguisher types · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which extinguishers are most common in a laboratory, and which type is not acceptable for laboratory use?
opciones: Dry chemical BC or ABC and carbon dioxide; water-filled units are not acceptable
Water-filled and foam units; carbon dioxide is not acceptable near electronics
Class D dry powder for all fires; dry chemical units are not acceptable
Carbon dioxide only; ABC units are not acceptable because the powder damages equipment
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's laboratory guidance names two types as the most common in a chemistry laboratory, pressurized dry chemical of type BC or ABC and carbon dioxide, with a specialized Class D dry powder unit added where flammable metals are handled, and it says flatly that a water-filled unit has no place in a laboratory. The same guidance asks employers to train workers on the different types under 29 CFR 1910.157, which also bans carbon tetrachloride and chlorobromomethane agents.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Value judgments
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist thinks 'people like him never fast properly' before asking the question. What does therapeutic communication require here?
opciones: Identify the personal bias and avoid placing that value judgment on the patient
Voice the concern openly so the patient has a chance to correct the record
Skip the fasting question, since the answer is already predictable
Document the impression in the chart as a compliance risk factor
preguntas.explicacion: The first pitfall in the table is value judgments: the provider is told to identify their own biases and judgments and to keep from imposing them on the patient. Implicit bias worsens outcomes and that progress is blocked by denying it exists. Voicing or charting the assumption imposes it; skipping the question forfeits the information.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: How soon after the start of the P wave do the atria begin to contract?
opciones: About 25 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one
About 100 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one
About 75 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one
About 225 ms, so the mechanical event lags the electrical one
preguntas.explicacion: The atria begin contracting roughly 25 ms after the P wave starts. Depolarization is the signal at the beginning of the movement, not the movement itself, so every mechanical event on the pressure curve trails its electrical counterpart on the tracing by a short lag.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads high in the office every time but normal on a home monitor. What is this called?
opciones: White-coat hypertension, where the clinical setting itself lifts the reading
Masked hypertension, where the office reading hides pressures that are high elsewhere
An auscultatory gap, where the sounds vanish and reappear during deflation
Pseudohypotension, where a stiff artery makes the cuff read below the true value
preguntas.explicacion: A transient rise brought on by anxiety about the clinical setting is white-coat hypertension, and those patients are normotensive away from the healthcare environment, so hypertension can be overdiagnosed in them. The mirror image, normal in the office and high at other times of the day, is masked hypertension, and there the diagnosis is missed instead. Automated office monitoring, which records several readings while the patient rests alone, reduces the white-coat effect.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for multi-dose vials
preguntas.subtema: Multi-dose vial beyond-use date · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial was first punctured on March 1 and the manufacturer gives no date for opened vials. Under USP 797 as cited by the CDC, by when should it be discarded?
opciones: Within 28 days of opening, and never past the manufacturer's expiration date
Within 7 days of opening, the limit for single-dose vials kept for the same patient
Within 72 hours of opening, unless it is kept in a clean medication area
On the manufacturer's expiration date, regardless of when it was opened
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC cites USP General Chapter 797: from the first puncture, a multi-dose vial is dated and then thrown out 28 days later, unless the manufacturer names a different date for the opened vial, and that beyond-use date can never run past the original expiration date. A vial never opened simply follows the manufacturer's expiration date. Single-dose vials are not saved for later use at all, not even for the same patient, so the 7-day option describes a rule that does not exist.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(C) and (d)(4)(iv)(B), Gloves and Laundry
preguntas.subtema: Utility gloves · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: The heavy utility gloves kept in the draw room for cleaning spills are cracked and peeling. What does the standard say?
opciones: Discard them: utility gloves are reused only while their integrity holds up
Wash and reuse them, since only single-use gloves are barred from reuse
Reuse them for handling contaminated laundry, where no barrier is needed
Keep them until the yearly review of the written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(C) is the only place the standard allows a glove to be decontaminated and used again, and it puts a condition on it: the glove's integrity has to be intact. Cracking, peeling, tears, punctures or any other sign of deterioration send it to the trash, and so does the loss of its barrier. Employees who handle contaminated laundry must wear gloves and other appropriate equipment under (d)(4)(iv)(B), so that is not a place to use a failing glove.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: tort
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: Into which three general categories do torts fall?
opciones: Intentional torts, negligent torts and strict liability torts
Intentional torts, criminal torts and administrative torts
Negligent torts, contractual torts and statutory torts
Negligent torts, punitive torts and constitutional torts
preguntas.explicacion: A tort is an act or omission that injures another and amounts to a civil wrong the courts attach liability to. Intentional torts are wrongs the defendant knew or should have known would follow from what they did; negligent torts happen when the conduct was unreasonably unsafe; strict liability torts do not turn on how careful the defendant was, only on whether the harm occurred.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Restriction Request; 45 CFR 164.522(a)(1)(ii) and (vi)
preguntas.subtema: Restriction requests · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the practice never to discuss her visits with the sister who drives her to them, though the sister waits in the room. What is the practice's position?
opciones: It need not agree to the restriction, but once it agrees it is bound by what it accepted
It must agree to any restriction a patient requests about treatment, payment or operations
It must agree, because a restriction is binding wherever the patient pays the visit in full
It may not agree, because restrictions would conflict with the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals have the right to ask a covered entity to restrict uses and disclosures made for treatment, for payment or for health care operations, and disclosures to people involved in their care or made to notify family, which is what the sister is. As a rule the entity is under no obligation to agree, and once it agrees it must keep to what it accepted, except where it has to treat her in a medical emergency. The regulation writes in a single restriction that cannot be refused, and it does not fit here: a disclosure to a health plan, for payment or for health care operations and not otherwise required by law, about an item or service the patient herself has paid for in full.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Recognition and Initial Management of Cardiac Arrest
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Where are the hands placed to compress the chest of an adult?
opciones: Heel of one hand on the lower half of the sternum, the other hand on top
Heel of one hand high on the sternum, between the two collarbones
Both palms flat on the left side of the chest, over the apex of the heart
Heel of one hand on the xiphoid process, with the fingers on the ribs
preguntas.explicacion: The heel of the dominant hand goes in the middle of the chest, on the lower half of the sternum, with the second hand overlapping on top and the fingers interlaced. The rescuer keeps the elbows locked and the shoulders directly over the hands so the push comes from the body. The patient should be supine on a firm, flat surface.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Recordkeeping: Training Records and Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Getting a copy of the record · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA II.B.5.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist asks her employer for a copy of her bloodborne pathogens training record. Within what period is it provided?
opciones: Fifteen working days from the request
Ten working days from the request
Thirty calendar days from the request
Three years from the training date
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan allows fifteen working days for handing the employee, or a representative the employee has authorized, a copy of the training record, and the same period for the medical record when the employee, or someone holding written consent, asks for it. Ten working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine after initial assignment; three years is how long the training record itself is kept under (h)(2)(ii), which is a different thing from the time allowed to hand over a copy.

preguntas.subtema: Security training · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which measures belong to the security awareness and training standard that a practice must run for its whole workforce?
opciones: Periodic reminders, guarding against malicious software, watching log-ins, passwords
Periodic reminders, a written test each year, a signed policy, a security officer
Guarding against malicious software, encryption of every message, locked cabinets
Watching log-ins, a sanction policy, a risk analysis, and a business associate list
preguntas.explicacion: Training covers the entire workforce, management included, and hangs four addressable specifications off it: security reminders; procedures that guard against malicious software and that detect and report it; monitoring of log-in attempts with any discrepancies reported; and procedures for creating passwords, changing them and keeping them safe.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Background: HBV; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030
preguntas.subtema: Why HBV cases fell · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Occupational hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers fell sharply after the 1980s. What is that credited to?
opciones: Wide vaccination of workers plus universal precautions and the OSHA standard
The arrival of immune globulin as a treatment for chronic hepatitis B
The switch from glass to plastic tubes in blood collection systems
The end of the use of hollow-bore needles for drawing blood samples
preguntas.explicacion: Surveillance figures put roughly 17,000 new hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers in 1983 and an estimated 800 in 1995, a decline of about 95 percent. It is attributed to the widespread immunization of healthcare workers with the hepatitis B vaccine and to universal precautions and the other measures the bloodborne pathogens standard requires.
