Immune globulin is post-exposure prophylaxis, not a treatment for chronic infection, and hollow-bore needles are still in daily use.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Technical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Access control · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Staff at the front desk share one login for the practice management system. Which technical safeguard does that defeat?
opciones: Access control, which is meant to let only authorized persons reach the ePHI
Transmission security, which guards ePHI while it moves across an electronic network
Facility access control, which limits who can physically enter the computer room
Device and media controls, which govern hardware coming into and out of the office
preguntas.explicacion: Access control is the technical standard requiring policies and procedures for the electronic systems holding ePHI so that only authorized persons can reach it. A shared login also undermines audit controls, the mechanisms that capture and review what is done inside those systems, because the record no longer shows who did what. Transmission security and the physical standards address different points entirely.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Topical and Transdermal Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.e(1) · RMA III.G.4.d(iii)
preguntas.pregunta: Where do the initials, date and time go when a new medication patch is applied?
opciones: On a piece of tape placed close to the patch, applied by the person who put it on
Directly on the patch itself, with a fine marker, before it is pressed onto the skin
On the clear plastic backing, which is left attached to one corner of the new patch
On the patient's wristband, beside the two identifiers checked before the dose given
preguntas.explicacion: Writing on a patch can puncture it and make it ineffective, so the initials, date and time go on a strip of tape stuck near it. Gloves are worn throughout, the old patch comes off first, the skin around it is assessed, cleansed and dried, and the new one is pressed firmly for ten seconds. Placement is checked later on, and for some opioid patches its presence is documented every shift.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: One antecubital fossa is inflamed with cellulitis and the other holds a fresh hematoma. Where does the search for a vein continue?
opciones: Along the forearm, which is inspected together with the antecubital fossa
Through the intravenous line running in one of the two arms
In the antecubital fossa with the smaller of the two problems
On the dorsum of the hand, the site the chapter prefers for an IV
preguntas.explicacion: Site selection begins by extending the arm and inspecting the antecubital fossa or the forearm, so the forearm is the next place to look when both elbows are ruled out. Cellulitis, an abscess and a hematoma are each listed as reasons not to puncture, and an existing line is not used either.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture (003751), Considerations; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Antibiotics before culture · CPT D2 k48 medications · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient started an antibiotic yesterday and now gives a urine for culture. What should be documented, and why?
opciones: The antibiotic, because it can cause a false-negative culture
The antibiotic, because it can cause a false-positive culture
The time of the last void, because a culture needs urine held 8 hours
The antibiotic, because it turns the urine alkaline and lyses the cells
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics already on board can suppress growth and give a false-negative urine culture, so the medication is recorded for the laboratory and the provider. The same rule drives other cultures: throat swabs are taken before antimicrobial treatment starts, and antibiotics can alter the growth in a sputum culture. Alkaline urine and cell lysis come from a stale specimen, not from the drug.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Sinoatrial Node
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: How long does the impulse take to reach the atrioventricular node after it leaves the sinoatrial node?
opciones: About 50 ms, traveling along the internodal pathways
About 100 ms, traveling along the internodal pathways
About 25 ms, traveling along the internodal pathways
About 225 ms, traveling along the internodal pathways
preguntas.explicacion: Three bands of specialized tissue lead from one node to the other, and the trip takes roughly 50 ms; a separate bundle carries the impulse straight across to the left atrium. The 100 ms figure belongs to the pause inside the node, not to the journey toward it.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication
preguntas.subtema: Intake accommodations · CCMA 4 k157 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) / 2027 II.F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.c · CMAA 5 k65 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who is blind asks for the intake forms in a format she can use. What does the ADA require?
opciones: Auxiliary aids such as a qualified reader, large print, Braille or an electronic file
That the patient bring a family member who can read the paperwork aloud to her
That staff complete the forms from memory and have a witness sign them instead
That the visit be rescheduled until the office can order printed materials for her
preguntas.explicacion: Where they are needed for effective communication with someone whose disability affects vision, hearing or speech, auxiliary aids and services have to be provided by the covered entity, so that the communication works as well for her as it does for anybody else. For a person who is blind, has low vision or is deaf-blind, the aids named include a qualified reader, large print, Braille, an electronic file for a screen-reading program, and audio recordings.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Ischemic Stroke", Introduction and Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(3) (2027 I.C.6.g(3)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has the sudden onset of weakness on one side and slurred speech. Which condition does that pattern suggest?
opciones: Acute ischemic stroke, a sudden focal neurological deficit
Acute otitis media, a sudden focal neurological deficit
A transient rise in blood pressure with no neurological deficit
A migraine headache, which produces no focal neurological deficit
preguntas.explicacion: An ischemic stroke means focal neurological deficits appearing suddenly in the territory of one vessel, whether in the brain, the retina or the spinal cord. It is the commonest kind by far, about 87 percent of all strokes, and speed matters: the whole system of care exists to recognize it fast enough to restore blood flow.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Prothrombin time (PT) (003652), Normal Results; What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: INR targets on warfarin · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT IV.A.3 · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.10.b.(5) INR (2027: b.(8)) · RMA III.C.4.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who takes warfarin has a point-of-care INR of 1.5. What does this value indicate?
opciones: It is below the usual therapeutic target of 2.0 to 3.0, so the patient may be at risk of forming a clot
It is above the usual therapeutic target of 0.8 to 1.1, so the patient may be at risk of serious bleeding
It is within the usual therapeutic target of 1.0 to 2.0, so no change in the warfarin dose is expected
It is a normal value for someone who is not on anticoagulants, so the warfarin can be discontinued
preguntas.explicacion: For a person not taking anticoagulants the PT is about 11 to 13.5 seconds and the INR 0.8 to 1.1. For most patients on warfarin the provider aims to keep the INR between 2.0 and 3.0: results above 3.0 carry a higher bleeding risk, while results below 2.0 may leave the patient at risk of developing a blood clot. An INR of 1.5 is therefore under target and the dose is reviewed by the provider, not stopped by the tester.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Otoscopy", Technique or Treatment; and "Rinne Test", Indications
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.10.d(11)
preguntas.pregunta: Which tuning fork is preferred for the Weber and Rinne tests, and why?
opciones: 512 Hz, because it balances tone decay against tactile vibration best
128 Hz, because the longer decay time gives the patient time to answer
1000 Hz, because it sits in the middle of the speech frequency range
512 Hz, because it is the only frequency the mastoid bone transmits
preguntas.explicacion: The 512-hertz fork strikes the best compromise between how long the tone lasts and how much of it the patient feels as vibration rather than hears. The two tuning fork tests that remain in routine use are Weber and Rinne, usually done alongside otoscopy, and neither replaces pure-tone audiometry nor is meant for general screening.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Hazardous Chemicals, Requirements under 29 CFR 1910.1200(h)
preguntas.subtema: HazCom training · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.iii III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: When must an employer train workers on hazardous chemicals under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: When first assigned, and again each time a new chemical hazard appears in the work area
At initial assignment and at least annually thereafter, within one year of the last session
Once, at hire, with a written test kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
Every three years, when the written hazard communication program is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200, as the eTool summarizes it, calls for effective training when the worker is first assigned, and again each time a new chemical hazard turns up in the work area; it has to be given in a language the workers understand, leave room for questions, and cover the protective measures the employer has put in place. The annual cycle inside one year of the previous session belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and employment plus 30 years is that standard's retention period for employee medical records.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(ii) and (c)(2)(i), Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: Exposure Control Plan contents · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a written Exposure Control Plan contain?
opciones: The exposure determination listing job classifications and tasks with occupational exposure
The sharps injury log, with the brand of each device and the department where it happened
The medical record of each exposed employee, including hepatitis B vaccination dates
The safety data sheet for every disinfectant used to decontaminate work surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(ii) names three required elements: the exposure determination of (c)(2), the schedule and method for implementing paragraphs (d) through (h), and the procedure for evaluating the circumstances of exposure incidents. The exposure determination lists job classifications where all or some employees are exposed and the tasks involved. The sharps injury log and the employee medical record are kept under paragraph (h) as separate records, and safety data sheets belong to the Hazard Communication standard at 29 CFR 1910.1200.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 2.4.2 Maintenance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which check belongs to the routine maintenance of the electrocardiograph?
opciones: Looking over the cords for damage and the plugs for bent pins
Wiping the keyboard and the writer with the detergent solution
Soaking the plugs in disinfectant and drying them before use
Opening the back of the unit so the inside can be dusted out
preguntas.explicacion: All the cords are inspected for fraying or other damage, and every plug and connector for a prong or pin that has bent, with each connector checked for a firm seat; what needs repair or replacement is reported. Cleaning is done with the unit off and with the cloth kept away from the keyboard and the writer.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion; StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k87 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.d
preguntas.pregunta: After centrifugation, the serum in a red-top tube shows fibrin strands floating above the gel. What is the most probable cause?
opciones: The tube was centrifuged before the blood had finished clotting
The tube was left at room temperature for too long before being spun
The tube was drawn through an intravenous catheter during an IV start
The tube was inverted too many times right after it was collected
preguntas.explicacion: Blood must be allowed to clot before serum is processed; the high rate of fibrin-containing samples in the emergency laboratory was linked to the short interval between collection and centrifugation, on average about 10 minutes. Waiting longer does not produce fibrin, catheter draws are tied to hemolysis rather than fibrin, and inversion helps additives mix instead of causing strands.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Why first morning urine · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: A urinalysis is ordered and the patient is told to bring the first sample of the day. What makes that void the best one to test?
opciones: It sat in the bladder overnight, so it is concentrated enough to show trace substances and how well the kidneys concentrate
It is the cleanest of the day, because the urethral area has not been used since the previous evening's void
It is the least acidic of the day, so cells, casts and crystals hold their shape for longer in the container
It is drawn before any food or drink, so the glucose and the protein are not raised by what the patient ate
preguntas.explicacion: Urine starts changing the moment it leaves the body, so which void is collected matters. The one held in the bladder through the night comes out concentrated, and that is the point: a concentrated sample shows what the kidneys can do with water, and it carries substances in high enough amounts to be picked up that a watery daytime sample would hide. Other timings are ordered when the question calls for them — a random void, one two hours after a meal, a full 24-hour collection. Cleanliness is a matter of the collection technique, not of the hour.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "SOAP Notes", Function: Subjective — History of present illness
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.4.b · CCMA 3A3 k44 · RMA III.F.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A note organizes the present illness with OLDCARTS. Which letter carries the patient's rating of 8 out of 10?
opciones: S, for severity, rated by the patient on a scale of 1 to 10
C, for characterization, which is how the patient describes it
T, for temporal factor, whether it is worse at some hour
A, for alleviating and aggravating factors that change it
preguntas.explicacion: Severity is the numbered rating, from 1 as the least to 10 as the worst. Characterization is the patient's own description of the concern, temporal factor asks whether it is better or worse at a particular time of day, and the alleviating and aggravating pair asks what makes the complaint better or worse. Onset, location, duration and radiation fill out the rest.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 2, 4, 6 and 8; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151(c)
preguntas.subtema: Using the SDS in an emergency · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist splashes a disinfectant concentrate into her eye. Which section of the product's Safety Data Sheet gives the first-aid measures?
opciones: Section 4, First-Aid Measures, by route of exposure
Section 2, Hazard Identification and signal word
Section 8, Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
Section 6, Accidental Release and cleanup measures
preguntas.explicacion: Section 4 sets out the immediate care an untrained bystander can give, sorted by how the chemical got in: breathed in, onto the skin or into the eye, or swallowed, together with the main symptoms and any warning that a doctor is needed at once. Section 2 classifies the hazard and carries the signal word and pictograms; Section 8 lists exposure limits, engineering controls and the equipment to put on before handling; Section 6 covers containing and cleaning up a spill. For the eye itself the practical first step is the eyewash: 29 CFR 1910.151(c) demands equipment able to drench or flush the eyes and the body quickly, inside the work area, wherever workers may meet injurious corrosive materials.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.3.e · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic freezer that stores patient samples has a continuous temperature monitoring system with an alarm. How often must its temperature still be checked and recorded?
opciones: Daily, and before the room is used for testing, regardless of the alarm or data logger
Weekly, since a continuous monitoring system replaces the manual daily check
Only when the alarm sounds, because the logger already records the temperature
Monthly, when the log sheet is reviewed and filed with the quality records
preguntas.explicacion: It makes no difference whether the unit carries a chart recorder, a temperature alarm, a digital data logger or continuous monitoring: a refrigerator or freezer is read and logged daily, and testing rooms are checked before use. Sample freezers often sit between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), but the range that counts is the one the manufacturer's instructions give for what is inside, since waived testing under CLIA means following those instructions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (venous illumination devices)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet and site location · CPT D3 3F k60 k61 · PBT II.E II.F · CCMA 3E4 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has veins that are hard to see and three tubes are needed. What is recommended instead of keeping the tourniquet on while the veins are located?
opciones: Using a venous illumination device to visualize the veins
Applying a second tourniquet below the first to raise the pressure
Drawing with a syringe, which tolerates a longer tourniquet time
Switching to a 16 to 18 gauge needle so the tubes fill faster
preguntas.explicacion: Venous illumination devices are recommended rather than a prolonged tourniquet to find non-prominent veins, especially when two or more tubes are to be collected, because they avoid the venous stasis that alters biochemistry and coagulation results. Sixteen to eighteen gauge is the WHO's blood donation size, and neither a second tourniquet nor a syringe extends the permitted time.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Throat and Nasal Swabs)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT V.E · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A nasal specimen has just been taken, the swab having been inserted and rotated repeatedly within one nostril. What does the written procedure have the collector do next?
opciones: Spread the material evenly over two or three smears and let the slides air-dry before sending them
Spread the material over a single smear and send the slide to the laboratory while it is still wet
Place the swab in 10 % neutral buffered formalin and send the container without making a smear
Spread the material over two or three smears and refrigerate the slides at 2 to 8 °C for transport
preguntas.explicacion: Swabs are taken under direct vision with good lighting, from areas of exudate, inflammatory membranes or the tonsillar crypts, and for a nasal specimen the patient sits with the head tilted slightly back and facing the light. The material is then spread evenly on two or three smears, the slides are air-dried, and they go to the laboratory for examination.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Audits and Risk Assessment; Risk Analysis
preguntas.subtema: Risk analysis is repeated · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic finished its security risk analysis two years ago and has bought new equipment since. What does the guidance say?
opciones: Repeat it regularly, and whenever practice or technology changes
Repeat it only after a breach has actually been discovered
Repeat it every six years, when the documentation is renewed
Treat the first one as final once the flaws found were fixed
preguntas.explicacion: The security requirements put their weight on risk analysis, and it is not a one-off exercise: the system in place is audited for flaws and gaps that threaten the confidentiality, the integrity or the security of health information; whatever turns up goes through the risk management process and gets corrected; and the analysis is run again at intervals, because technology keeps arriving and clinical practice keeps shifting. The six-year figure is how long the required documentation is kept.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(1) and (b), Definitions: Production Facility, Research Laboratory
preguntas.subtema: Scope of paragraph (e) · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C2 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory only analyzes patient specimens. Do the extra rules for HIV and HBV research laboratories apply to it?
opciones: No: those rules cover culture and production work, not diagnostic analysis
Yes: any laboratory that handles blood must meet them along with the rest
Yes, but only in the area where HIV testing is performed on patient samples
No: they apply only to facilities that manufacture the hepatitis B vaccine
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(1) draws the line itself. The extra requirements bind laboratories doing research and facilities producing, where HIV and HBV are cultured, concentrated, experimented with or manipulated, and they do not reach a clinical or diagnostic laboratory that only analyzes blood, tissue or organs. A production facility is defined in (b) as one working at industrial scale, in large volume or at high concentration with the viruses themselves, which is not the same as making a vaccine. The rest of the standard still applies to the hospital laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2F k43 · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a informed consent · RMA I.C.1.a consents · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A thorough consent discussion is expected to cover all the relevant risks. Which set does it take in?
opciones: The general risks, those particular to this procedure, the risks of no treatment, and the alternatives
The general risks, those particular to this procedure, the cost to the patient, and the recovery time
The risks particular to this procedure only, since the general ones are printed on the facility's form
The risks particular to this procedure and those of the alternatives, with no treatment left out of it
preguntas.explicacion: Consent is not informed if the risk talk is narrow. It is expected to run across four fronts: what any intervention of this kind can bring, what this one in particular can bring, what follows if nothing is done at all, and what the reasonable alternatives carry with them. Declining care is itself an option that has to be weighed, so dropping it shortens the list. The forms promise nothing either: many say outright that the method proposed is not guaranteed to settle the problem. Cost and recovery time belong to the conversation about the visit, not to the risks this discussion has to cover.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A serum lithium level is ordered on a patient taking lithium carbonate. Which heparin tube does the WHO table specify?
opciones: Sodium heparin, because a lithium heparin tube would interfere with the result
Lithium heparin, because it is the anticoagulant of the light green PST as well
Either sodium or lithium heparin, as the table allows for an ammonia level
Neither; lithium is measured in the pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 is explicit in the uses column of the dark green tube: for a lithium level use sodium heparin, and for an ammonia level either heparin will do. Lithium heparin is indeed the anticoagulant of the light green PST, which is exactly why it is the wrong choice when lithium itself is being measured. The ACD tube is for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Subjective
preguntas.subtema: History of present illness · CCMA 3 k190 · CMA I.A.4 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: In the OLDCARTS mnemonic for the history of present illness, which element does the patient rate on a scale of one to ten?
opciones: Severity
Onset
Duration
Radiation
preguntas.explicacion: The history of present illness opens with a single line giving how old the patient is, the sex and why they came, and is then laid out with OLDCARTS: onset, location, duration, character, alleviating and aggravating factors, radiation, temporal factors and severity. Severity is the element carrying a scale, one being the least and ten the worst. Radiation asks whether the symptom travels or stays put.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Identify Relevant Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Identifying information red flags · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A registration form arrives with required boxes empty, and the applicant ignores the notices saying it is incomplete. Which category of red flag covers that?
opciones: Personal identifying information
Suspicious documents presented
Account activity out of pattern
Notice from a law enforcement body
preguntas.explicacion: Under personal identifying information the guidance lists a person who leaves required information off an application and does not answer notices that it is incomplete, alongside addresses that conflict with the credit report, a number listed on the death file, and a person who cannot answer a challenge question.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A blood culture bottle, a light blue citrate tube and a gold serum separator tube are ordered, and no plain tube is on the requisition. Which container is filled second?
opciones: The light blue citrate tube, filled before the serum separator tube
The gold serum separator tube, since a plain tube precedes any anticoagulated one
A discard tube, which every citrate specimen requires before it
Either of the two, because the culture bottle has already taken the carry-over
preguntas.explicacion: The sterile container is filled first and the coagulation tube comes next: the numbered table gives citrate position 3 and the serum separator position 5, and the four-group summary places coagulation tubes straight after the sterile containers and ahead of the plain and gel tubes. A discard tube is not a general rule for citrate specimens; it belongs to a winged set, where air in the tubing has to be cleared, and to the thrombin generation assay. Drawing a culture bottle first does nothing to protect the tubes that follow it from each other.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Orthostatic Hypotension", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · RMA III.E.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What happens in the body during the first seconds after a patient stands up?
opciones: Roughly 300 to 800 mL of blood pools in the legs, and sympathetic tone compensates
Roughly 50 to 100 mL of blood pools in the legs, and the heart rate alone compensates
Blood is pushed out of the legs toward the chest, and the vessels there must dilate
Cardiac output rises at once, and the baroreceptors then bring the pressure back down
preguntas.explicacion: Standing lets 300 to 800 mL of blood pool in the lower limbs, so venous return and cardiac output fall. The baroreceptor reflex answers with more sympathetic outflow and less vagal tone, tightening the vessels so pressure holds. Where that answer is absent or slow, the symptoms of orthostatic hypotension appear.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Beta Blockers", Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient started on metoprolol reports that the resting pulse is slower than before. Which action of this drug class explains the change?
opciones: Blockade of beta-1 receptors, which slows the heart and weakens each contraction
Blockade of beta-2 receptors, which relaxes the smooth muscle of the airways
Competitive inhibition of the enzyme that turns angiotensin I into angiotensin II
Blockade of the sodium-chloride channel in the distal convoluted tubule
preguntas.explicacion: Beta-1 receptors sit mainly in the heart, where catecholamines raise automaticity and conduction speed. A beta blocker occupies them, so chronotropic and inotropic drive fall and the pulse drops; pressure falls too, partly through less renin. Relaxing the airways is a beta-2 effect, and the last two options describe ACE inhibitors and thiazide diuretics.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.512(a) and (b)(1)(i)-(ii), Uses and disclosures required by law and for public health activities
preguntas.subtema: Public health disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports a child's positive lead level to the state health department as state law requires. Under HIPAA this disclosure is which of these?
opciones: Permitted without authorization, as required by law and for public health
Permitted only with the parent's signed authorization
A breach that must be reported to the individual within 60 calendar days of discovery
Permitted only if the child is treated as an emancipated minor
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.512 lists uses and disclosures that need neither authorization nor an opportunity to object: those required by law, and those to a public health authority authorized to collect information to prevent or control disease, injury or disability, including disease reporting and surveillance; reports of child abuse or neglect to an authorized authority are in the same paragraph. Such a disclosure is not a breach. The parent's status as personal representative matters for access requests, not for a report the law compels.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A rural clinic uses needles and syringes rather than an evacuated system. Which advantages does that conventional device offer?
opciones: Widely available, least expensive, and needing no special training
Widely available, least expensive, and needing no blood transfer step
Safest of all devices, cheapest of all, and needing no special training
Widely available, safest of all devices, and giving many tubes per stick
preguntas.explicacion: The hypodermic needle and syringe is listed as widely available, the least expensive option, supplied in a wide range of lengths and gauges, and usable without special training. What it does not avoid is the transfer of blood into tubes, which is where its needle-stick risk comes from.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Safe and Effective Administration of Vaccines and Epinephrine Autoinjection", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 k82 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops hives and wheezing minutes after a vaccination and an epinephrine autoinjector is used. How is the device handled?
opciones: Held around the middle, pressed against the outer thigh, kept there 5 seconds
Held by both ends, pressed against the upper arm, kept there for 30 seconds
Held around the middle, pressed against the abdomen, kept there for 1 minute
Held by the orange tip, pressed against the outer thigh, kept there 10 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The device is grasped around its middle, never over the ends, because a hand over the tip can fire the needle into the rescuer. The blue cap comes off, the orange tip is pressed firmly against the mid outer thigh until a click is heard, and it is held there at least 5 seconds; afterward the needle is covered by that tip and the unit is discarded.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Balance Billing
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8 (2027 III.G.6.b) · CMAA 4 k61, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An out-of-network provider charges $200 and the plan's allowed amount is $110. Beyond her cost sharing, what may he bill the patient?
opciones: Ninety dollars, the gap between what he charged and what the plan allows
A hundred and ten dollars, since the plan pays that sum straight to him
Twenty-two dollars, being twenty percent of the amount the plan allowed
Two hundred dollars, the whole charge, since no contract binds him to the plan
preguntas.explicacion: Balance billing is when a provider bills the patient for the balance the plan does not cover, meaning the difference between the amount actually billed and the allowed amount. The uniform glossary uses these figures as its example. It happens most often with out-of-network providers; a network provider may not balance bill for covered services.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5G · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A very icteric sample and a very lipemic one both give unusable point-of-care readings. Which remedies are described for each?
opciones: Dilution for the excess bilirubin, and ultracentrifugation for the excess lipid
Ultracentrifugation for the excess bilirubin, and dilution for the excess lipid
Warming for the excess bilirubin, and a longer spin for the excess lipid
Dilution for both, since neither pigment nor lipid can be spun out of a sample
preguntas.explicacion: What is done about them depends on which analyser is in front of you and on what its maker's instructions say, though two routes are named: diluting the sample settles an error caused by excess bilirubin, and ultracentrifugation clears one caused by excess lipid. At the point of care these three interferences can only be caught by eye, in a spun aliquot, since there is no index measuring them.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 3.1.1 and 3.2.2
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 3A k55 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is choosing a needle for a routine draw. On what basis is the gauge decided?
opciones: The one that fits the most prominent vein and hurts least
The widest one the tray holds, so the tubes fill more quickly
The finest one the tray holds, so the puncture hurts far less
The one that matches the color of the stopper being filled
preguntas.explicacion: The gauge chosen is the one that sits comfortably in the most prominent vein and hurts the patient least. Going too wide tears the vein and bleeds into the tissue; going too fine damages the blood cells, which invalidates tests that need whole cells or free hemoglobin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anemia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count reports a hemoglobin below the reference value for the patient. Which term names that finding?
opciones: Anemia, meaning the circulating red cell mass has dropped
Leukemia, meaning the circulating red cell mass has dropped
Polycythemia, meaning the circulating red cell mass has dropped
Hemophilia, meaning the circulating red cell mass has dropped
preguntas.explicacion: Anemia is a fall in circulating red cell mass, seen as a lower hemoglobin, hematocrit or red cell count. It is a finding, not a diagnosis, and its causes spread wide: blood loss, hemolysis, marrow failure, inflammation, poor nutrition, kidney disease that has become chronic, pregnancy and inherited disorders of hemoglobin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · D2 k53 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient had a radical mastectomy on the left side two years ago. Where should the blood be drawn?
opciones: From the right arm; a radical mastectomy on the left side rules that arm out
From the left arm, provided the tourniquet stays on for less than one minute
From either arm, since the contraindication applies only during the first six months after surgery
From the left hand only, below the level of the surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Among the site-specific contraindications, the phlebotomy chapter lists a history of radical mastectomy on the same side, alongside scar tissue, cellulitis or abscess, a vascular graft, a hematoma, a vein that feels fibrosed, and any venous access device. The chapter sets no time limit after which the arm becomes acceptable and no exception for the hand or for a short tourniquet time.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dextrocardia", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k151 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which picture on the tracing goes with dextrocardia?
opciones: Right axis deviation with all complexes inverted in lead I
Left axis deviation with all complexes inverted in lead I
Right axis deviation with all complexes inverted in lead II
Right axis deviation with the R wave growing from V1 to V6
preguntas.explicacion: A heart sitting on the right side of the chest shows right axis deviation, inversion of every complex in lead I, an upright P wave in the augmented left lead, and an R wave that never builds up across the anterior chest leads.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.8 Checklist for Applying and Removing Sterile Gloves
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: How are contaminated sterile gloves removed at the end of a procedure?
opciones: Grasp the outside of one cuff, peel it off inside out, then use a bare finger inside the other cuff
Grasp the inside of one cuff, peel it off inside out, then use a gloved thumb under the other cuff
Grasp both cuffs at once and pull the gloves off together so no skin contacts either outer surface
Grasp the fingertips of one glove, pull it halfway off, then push the second glove off against it
preguntas.explicacion: The first glove is taken by its outside cuff with the other gloved hand, avoiding skin, and pulled off inside out into the palm of the hand still gloved. The bare index finger then tucks inside the remaining cuff and peels that glove off inside out and over the first. Waste is discarded appropriately and hand hygiene follows.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 10. Disinfection Strategies for Other Semicritical Devices
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: An FDA-cleared label for high-level disinfection with more than 2% glutaraldehyde at 25 °C sets what range of exposure?
opciones: 20 to 90 minutes, depending on the product
5 to 12 minutes, depending on the product
3 to 10 hours, depending on the product
90 to 180 minutes, depending on the product
preguntas.explicacion: Federal rules require the FDA-cleared label claim to be followed, and for glutaraldehyde above 2 percent at 25 °C those claims run from 20 to 90 minutes. Some other products carry shorter claims, such as 12 minutes for a 0.55 percent ortho-phthalaldehyde at 20 °C. The hours-long exposures belong to the chemical sterilants, where spores are the target.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the wide variation in the superficial veins of the elbow a practical concern?
opciones: Mispuncture has caused bruising, hematoma, altered sensation
Mispuncture makes the tourniquet slip below the level of the vein
Variation changes which tubes may be filled from a single puncture
Variation means the median cubital vein is absent in most patients
preguntas.explicacion: Because the pattern differs so much from patient to patient, adverse effects from puncturing the wrong vessel have been reported across health systems: bruising, hematoma and sensory changes. That variation is the argument put forward for using an illuminator to see the vein first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k75 · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What is a taper needle for?
opciones: Soft delicate tissue and tendon repair, where it spreads tissue instead of cutting it
Tough dermal tissue and scalp repair, where a rounded tip resists bending under force
Skin closure in cosmetic areas, where three sharp edges leave the finest entry point
Ligament repair and fascia, where the three cutting edges pierce the densest structures
preguntas.explicacion: Taper needles are rounded rather than edged, and can be sharp or blunt. They pierce tissue by spreading it apart as they pass rather than cutting it, which makes them suitable for soft, delicate tissue and for tendon repair. The needles with three sharp cutting edges are the cutting and reverse cutting types, which are what skin usually gets.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "24-Hour Urine Collection", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: 24-hour volume and aliquot · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: At the end of a 24-hour urine collection, what does the laboratory do before analysis?
opciones: Records the total volume and submits a representative sample of the pooled urine
Discards the first and last voids and analyzes the pooled urine in between
Divides the urine into three numbered tubes for chemistry, culture and cytology
Records the collection time and refrigerates the whole volume for 24 hours before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Once the full period is over, the total volume is measured and written down, and a representative portion of the mixed urine is sent for analysis; the daily excretion is calculated from that volume. The first void of day one is the only one discarded, and the closing void is kept. Three numbered tubes are the cerebrospinal fluid routine. If a full day is not feasible, a shorter timed collection can be used provided the exact time is recorded.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Hematocrit (003646), Normal Results; StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Hematocrit reference ranges · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.i / 4.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which hematocrit value falls within the usual reference range for an adult woman?
preguntas.explicacion: Common adult reference values are about 37 to 48 % for men and 34 to 43 % for women, so 38 % sits inside the female range. A value of 30 % is below it and would fit anemia, 52 % exceeds even the male range, and 45 to 61 % is the range quoted for newborns, whose hematocrit is high and falls during the neonatal period. Ranges vary slightly between laboratories.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2E k41 · PBT II.A II.C · CCMA 3E2 k124 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: The requisition reads 'Maria Lopez, DOB 03/14/1961'; the wristband reads 03/14/1967. The patient confirms her name. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Defer the blood sampling until the discrepancy has been resolved
Proceed, since the name matched and the date of birth is secondary
Draw the sample now and have the wristband corrected afterwards
Ask the patient which date is right and correct the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Before any blood is withdrawn, the identification data and the tube labeling are double-checked, and if any discrepancy appears among those data the sampling is deferred until the issue is resolved. A matching name does not cancel a mismatched date of birth, and the phlebotomist does not settle the conflict by editing the paperwork on the spot.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Prevent And Mitigate Identity Theft
preguntas.subtema: Responding to a red flag · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A red flag turns up on a patient account and the office has to respond. Which response does the Red Flags guidance offer as an example?
opciones: Reopening the account under a new number, or holding off on collection for now
Reopening the account under a new number, or closing the record to the patient
Referring the account to a debt collector so the balance is chased independently
Freezing the patient's chart until a police report about the account is filed
preguntas.explicacion: The examples of an appropriate response run from watching the account for evidence of theft, changing the passwords or codes that reach it and reopening it with a new number, to declining to pursue collection or to sell the account to a collector, and, in some circumstances, deciding that no response is called for. A recent breach argues for a stronger response.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Issues of Concern, Variability in Antiseizure Medication Levels; and section Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: What does a valproate level mainly reflect, given the short half-life of that drug?
opciones: Short-term compliance, which makes the measurement low-yield
Long-term usage across the preceding weeks of treatment
The unbound fraction, untouched by any change in protein binding
The risk of a breakthrough seizure over the coming month
preguntas.explicacion: Valproate has a short half-life, which makes measuring it low-yield and primarily a reflection of short-term compliance. Phenytoin, with its long half-life, gives a level that reflects long-term usage instead. Free levels, not total levels, are what show the unbound and pharmacologically active fraction when protein binding has been altered.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sterile Technique", The Counted Scrub Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.A.3.b(i) y III.D.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: In the counted brush stroke surgical scrub, how many strokes does each finger receive?
opciones: Forty, since each finger is treated as four sides at ten strokes apiece
Thirty, since each finger is treated as three sides at ten strokes apiece
Twenty, since each finger is treated as two sides at ten strokes apiece
Sixty, since each finger is treated as four sides at fifteen strokes apiece
preguntas.explicacion: Each finger is divided into four sides and each side gets ten strokes, which totals forty per finger. The nails and cuticles come first, thirty strokes in a circular motion across the top of the nails; the palm then takes thirty and the back of the hand thirty. Only after both hands and arms are done does the rinsing start.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 1 and section 4.2 Humidity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E14 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Dried blood spot cards and dry buccal swabs are left in an outdoor specimen lock box for pickup, and the courier is delayed on a humid day. What is the concern?
opciones: High humidity compromises dried specimens kept at ambient conditions, degrading nucleic acids and inviting microbial growth
High humidity rehydrates the dried specimens, so the volume recovered falls below the minimum the assay requires
High humidity matters only for the buccal swabs; dried blood spots stay stable under any ambient conditions
High humidity fixes the dried specimens in place, so they must be soaked in transport medium before extraction
preguntas.explicacion: High humidity hits dried blood spots and dry buccal or oral swabs held at ambient conditions: over long storage viral and microbial nucleic acids degrade, water feeds reactive oxygen species that break DNA apart, and damp specimens grow fungi and bacteria. The scenario given for this variable is a delayed pickup from an uninsulated lock box; where storage cannot be controlled, those sample types are avoided or validated first.

preguntas.subtema: Retention exceptions · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which record is exempt from the long retention period of the OSHA access standard?
opciones: A one-time treatment of a minor cut, if it is kept apart from the medical program
A record of exposure monitoring, once the substance is no longer used in the office
A record belonging to an employee who has left, once the final pay has been issued
A safety data sheet, once the product it describes has been taken off the shelves
preguntas.explicacion: The employee medical record is preserved for the length of employment plus thirty years, with narrow exceptions: health insurance claim files kept separately, first aid records of one-time treatment of minor injuries made on site by a non-physician and kept separately, and the records of employees who worked under a year if handed to them on leaving.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A 17-year-old on active military duty arrives alone for a drug level. Who consents to the draw?
opciones: The minor himself, since active-duty status makes him an emancipated minor
A parent reached by telephone, because he is still younger than eighteen years
The ordering clinician, invoking the emergency exception under EMTALA
A parent, because emancipation applies only to minors who are married
preguntas.explicacion: Minors who are married, on active military duty, or living apart from their parents and managing their own finances are generally considered emancipated, and emancipated minors can consent to or refuse care without parental permission or notification. EMTALA's emergency exception is a different route, for emergency conditions, not for a routine level.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which information must appear on every prescription for a controlled substance?
opciones: Full name and address of the patient, drug, strength, form, quantity and directions
Full name and insurance plan of the patient, drug, strength and treating diagnosis
Full name and date of birth of the patient, drug, and the number of refills allowed
Full name and address of the patient, drug, and the pharmacy chosen to dispense it
preguntas.explicacion: A controlled substance prescription is dated and signed on the day it is issued, and it carries the patient's full name and address, the drug name, the strength, the dosage form, the quantity prescribed and the directions for use, together with the practitioner's own name, address and DEA registration number. The regulation says nothing about the payer or a diagnosis, and refills are governed separately by schedule.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Incomplete Disclosure
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Of the three legal standards used to judge whether informed consent was adequate, which one do many states apply?
opciones: The reasonable patient standard, built on what a typical patient needs to know
The reasonable clinician standard, built on what a typical clinician would say
The subjective standard, built on what this one patient needs to understand
The documentation standard, built on what the consent form has room to hold
preguntas.explicacion: The state decides the standard, and three approaches are recognized: subjective, reasonable patient and reasonable clinician. Many states work from the reasonable patient standard because it turns on what the average patient needs in order to take part in the decision. Even so, the clinician determines which approach fits a given situation.

preguntas.subtema: Workstation use · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A policy states which programs may be run at the front desk computer, how they are to be used and how the desk is laid out. Which standard is that?
opciones: Workstation use, which sets the functions, the manner of use and the surroundings
Workstation security, the physical guard that limits a machine to authorized users
Access control, the technical limit on who may open which record in the system
Facility access controls, which limit physical entry to where the systems are kept
preguntas.explicacion: Two standards sit side by side. Workstation use calls for policies covering which functions are proper, the manner of carrying them out, and what the physical surroundings of a workstation, or of a class of workstations, should look like. Workstation security is the narrower one: the physical measures that keep an unauthorized person away from the machine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient had to be moved from lying to sitting just before the draw. What should the phlebotomist do about it?
opciones: Record the change of position so the results can be interpreted
Cancel the draw and reschedule it for the following morning
Wait 2 minutes, then draw; no note is needed for a brief change
Return the patient to the supine position and draw at once
preguntas.explicacion: Position is meant to be maintained for at least 10 to 15 minutes before venipuncture; when a change cannot be avoided, it is documented so the laboratory results can be read in that light. The draw is not canceled for that reason, two minutes is the WHO's tourniquet limit rather than a stabilization period, and drawing immediately after repositioning defeats the purpose.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Nasal Instillation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii)
preguntas.pregunta: How is a nasal spray administered?
opciones: The patient blows the nose, tilts the head back, and one nostril is held closed
The patient blows the nose, leans forward, and both nostrils are sprayed at once
The patient tilts the head back and the tip is pushed in until it meets the septum
The patient lies on one side and the spray goes into the upper nostril only
preguntas.explicacion: Nasal medication is used mostly for allergies, sinus infections and congestion, and clean technique is enough. Tissues are offered and the patient blows the nose, then sits or lies with the head tilted back, looking upward. The tip of the spray bottle or the dropper goes into one nostril while the other is occluded, and the spray is released as the patient breathes in. Gloves and the medication rights apply as always.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Skeletal System: Divisions of the Skeleton; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology: Appendicular Skeleton
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many bones are in the axial skeleton and how many in the appendicular skeleton?
opciones: 80 axial and 126 appendicular
126 axial and 80 appendicular
106 axial and 100 appendicular
60 axial and 146 appendicular
preguntas.explicacion: The skeleton splits in two. The axial part, with 80 bones, is the skull, hyoid, vertebral column and thoracic cage. The appendicular part, with 126, is the limbs plus the pectoral and pelvic girdles that anchor them. The two together give the adult total of 206.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 580: Medical record retention
preguntas.subtema: Safeguards through disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is shredding charts that state law no longer requires it to keep. Does the Privacy Rule have anything to say about that moment?
opciones: Yes, its safeguards run for as long as the information is held, disposal included
No, its safeguards end on the day the state retention period runs out for a chart
Yes, but only if the practice is destroying more than 500 records at one time
No, because destroying a record is a health care operation and needs no safeguard
preguntas.explicacion: HIPAA fixes no retention period for the clinical record itself; State law does. What the Privacy Rule demands is safeguards, administrative and technical and physical, for however long the covered entity holds the information, and it counts disposal as part of that stretch.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Respiratory System: Conducting Passages
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(5) (2027 I.C.6.f(5)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the upper respiratory tract and which the lower?
opciones: Nose, pharynx and larynx above; trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, pharynx and trachea above; larynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose and pharynx above; larynx, trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, larynx and trachea above; pharynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting passages split into an upper tract of nose, pharynx and larynx and a lower tract of trachea, bronchial tree and lungs. All of them communicate with the outside air and carry a mucous membrane lining, with hairs in some regions to filter the air and cilia in others to move mucus along.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An intensive care manager asks why the laboratory's improvement plan targets the medical units and not the surgical ones. What did the rejection audit show?
opciones: Non-surgical intensive care rejected about four times as many specimens as surgical
Surgical intensive care units rejected about four times as many specimens as medical ones
Neurology intensive care showed the lowest rejection ratio of all the intensive care units
Rejection ratios in intensive care matched those of the adult emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: Inside intensive care the split was wide: 40 % of the rejections came from non-surgical units and 10 % from surgical ones. Neurology intensive care was the worst single unit at 14 %, twice the internal medicine unit at 7 % and three times the surgical units at 4.5 %. That is why the training effort was pointed at the medical units rather than spread evenly.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), If an Exposure Occurs; NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors, Treatment; OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), p. 21
preguntas.subtema: Eye splash first aid · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Blood splashes into a phlebotomist's eye while she uncaps a tube. What is the first thing to do?
opciones: Irrigate the eye with clean water, saline or a sterile irrigant, then report the exposure
Apply an antiseptic eye drop, then complete the incident report before seeking care
Squeeze the eyelids shut and wait for the occupational health nurse to examine it
Flush with a dilute bleach solution, which inactivates bloodborne viruses on contact
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC and NIOSH give the same immediate steps, and they differ by site: soap and water for a needlestick or a cut, plain water for a splash that lands on the nose, the mouth or the skin, and clean water, saline or a sterile irrigant for the eye. Then the exposure is reported to whoever manages exposures, and medical care is sought at once. OSHA's laboratory guidance suggests irrigating eyes and mucous membranes for 15 minutes. The CDC adds that nothing shows antiseptics or squeezing the wound reduce transmission, and that caustic agents such as bleach are not recommended.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Patient Rights under HIPAA
preguntas.subtema: Asking for a correction · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads her record and says one entry is wrong. What right does she have?
opciones: To ask for a correction, which the provider may accept or deny
To have the entry deleted within thirty days of the request
To have the entry rewritten by the clinician who made it
To bill the provider for the time spent finding the mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the rights the privacy rule gives are the right to a notice of privacy practices, to ask that disclosures be restricted, to say how information should be handled and communicated, to inspect and review one's own information and request a change to anything that looks wrong, to obtain a copy, to receive an accounting of disclosures, and to complain to the Office for Civil Rights. The request for a change is a request: the provider may accept or deny it, and a documented diagnosis a patient dislikes is not erased for that reason.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory setting its own storage limits asks how long a nasopharyngeal swab sitting in viral transport medium has been shown to hold up at room temperature.
opciones: As long as three weeks for one coronavirus target, without a meaningful change
As long as three days for one coronavirus target, and no longer for any other
As long as three weeks for every respiratory virus target that was studied
As long as twelve hours, which is the limit quoted for a dry swab instead
preguntas.explicacion: Storage evaluations found nasopharyngeal swabs in transport medium still usable after as long as twenty-one days at room temperature for one coronavirus target, and after a week at 22 °C for herpes simplex virus, adenovirus, influenza and enterovirus. Other work reported a 66 to 74 % loss of influenza A material after two weeks whatever the temperature, so the limit is target-specific.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: A newer machine shows muscle tremor that an older one never wrote. How is that read?
opciones: As an advantage: it also writes small P and Q waves
As a fault: the unit needs the biomedical engineer
As a fault: the standardization has drifted upward
As an advantage: it filters the tremor out by itself
preguntas.explicacion: Picking up the tremor is not a defect. A machine able to reproduce those small signals is also able to write the small P and Q waves that less accurate units have missed, so the answer is to settle the patient rather than to blame or replace the equipment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Heart Sounds", Related Testing
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a(1) · RMA III.F.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the mitral valve heard loudest during auscultation of the heart?
opciones: The 5th intercostal space on the left, at the midclavicular line
The 2nd right intercostal space beside the sternal border
The 2nd left intercostal space beside the sternal border
The 4th left intercostal space beside the sternal border
preguntas.explicacion: The four valve areas run in order: aortic in the 2nd right space, pulmonic in the 2nd left, tricuspid in the 4th left, and mitral in the 5th left at the midclavicular line. The first heart sound is the mitral and tricuspid valves closing in systole; the second is the aortic and pulmonic valves closing in diastole.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Burn Classification", Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which burn injuries are on the list of criteria for transfer to a burn center?
opciones: Burns of the face, hands, feet, genitalia or perineum, and any chemical burn
Burns of the trunk only, and any burn with blisters over a joint surface
Burns of the forearm and calf, and any burn that has not healed in 3 weeks
Burns of the scalp only, and any burn a patient cannot dress unaided
preguntas.explicacion: The burn association sets 10 transfer criteria, which take in burns of the face, hands, feet, genitalia and perineum, any full-thickness area, chemical and electrical burns, inhalation injury, and a total body surface area above 10 %. That surface can be figured with the rule of nines, the Lund-Browder chart or the rule of palms.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a)
preguntas.pregunta: A tracheal bistoury is listed among the ear, nose and throat instruments. What is it?
opciones: A long, narrow surgical knife
A hook that lifts the trachea
A dilator that widens the airway
A tube left after a laryngectomy
preguntas.explicacion: The bistoury of that list is a knife: long and narrow. The tracheal hook, the tracheal dilator and the laryngectomy tube are three separate entries in the same group, which also holds the adenoid curette, the metal tongue depressor, the mouth gag, the tonsil snare and the ear curette.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Waived testing; FDA, CLIA Waiver by Application: What is a CLIA Waiver by Application?
preguntas.subtema: Routes to waived status · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: Besides the tests listed in the regulation itself, by which two routes does a test become waived?
opciones: FDA clearance for home use, or a manufacturer's waiver application with supporting data
State agency approval, or two years of acceptable proficiency testing at the site
A CMS inspection of the site, or accreditation by a CMS-approved organization
A Certificate of Registration, or categorization as PPM by the physician
preguntas.explicacion: Three doors lead to waived status: the tests named in 42 CFR 493.15(c), tests cleared or approved by the FDA for home use, and tests a manufacturer submits to the FDA with scientific data showing the waiver criteria are met (a CLIA Waiver by Application, for a test first categorized as moderate). Inspections, accreditation and site-level proficiency testing concern the laboratory, not the test.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene · CPT D3 3A · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist washes her hands between patients. How long should that last, and which parts are easy to miss?
opciones: At least thirty seconds, covering the wrists and between the fingers
At least ten seconds, covering the palms and the backs of the hands
At least two minutes, covering the forearms as far as the elbows
At least thirty seconds, covering the fingertips and the nails only
preguntas.explicacion: The infection control table asks for hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub, washing carefully for at least thirty seconds and including the wrists and the spaces between the fingers. The pairing instruction on the other side of the table is simply not to forget to clean the hands.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: In the one-year audit of an emergency laboratory, what was the single most frequent reason for rejecting biochemistry specimens?
opciones: Fibrin clots, found in 28 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Hemolysis, found in 28 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Insufficient volume, found in 35 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Lipemia, found in 22 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
preguntas.explicacion: For biochemistry the leading cause was fibrin clots at 28 %, followed by inadequate volume at 9 %; for coagulation, blood gases and CBC the leaders were clotted samples at 35 % and inadequate volume at 13 %. Hemolysis accounted for about 2 % of samples in that laboratory and lipemia for 0.1 %, so the percentages in the distractors are borrowed from other rows of the same study.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2, Infection prevention and control practices
preguntas.subtema: Exposure incidents and post-exposure follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist sustains a needlestick from a used needle. According to the WHO's infection prevention table, what is the time limit after which post-exposure prophylaxis is no longer effective?
opciones: 72 hours
24 hours
48 hours
7 days
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.2 of the WHO guideline pairs each practice with its opposite. On the Do side: report any needle or sharps injury at once, seek help, and start post-exposure prophylaxis as soon as possible following the local protocol. On the Do-not side: do not put off PEP after contact with potentially contaminated material, because past 72 hours it no longer works. The lesson for the exam is twofold: report at once, and the window is three days, not one day and not a week.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate"; Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Tube orientation in ESR · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(3) · RMA III.C.4.b.iii
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR rack was bumped and the Westergren tube stood tilted about 3° off vertical during the hour. What effect does this have?
opciones: Tilting raises the ESR; an angle of 3° can increase the value by as much as 30 %
Tilting lowers the ESR, because the red cells slide along the glass and settle more slowly
Tilting has no measurable effect as long as the reading is taken at exactly 60 minutes
Tilting affects only the Wintrobe method, whose shorter tube is more sensitive to inclination
preguntas.explicacion: The Westergren ESR is the distance red cells settle in a vertical tube after one hour, reported in millimeters per hour. Tube tilt and vibration falsely elevate the result, and an inclination of 3° from vertical can raise the ESR by up to 30 %. Elevated room temperature and direct sunlight also increase it, and air bubbles from an underfilled tube add to the error. Delay in setting up the test has the opposite effect and lowers the value.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Significance of test complexity
preguntas.subtema: Moderate vs high: personnel only · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about the CLIA quality standards for moderate and high complexity testing is accurate?
opciones: They differ only in the personnel requirements
They differ only in proficiency testing rules
High complexity sites are inspected; moderate sites are not
Moderate sites follow the insert only, like waived sites
preguntas.explicacion: Both nonwaived categories must hold a certificate, be inspected, and meet the quality system standards for proficiency testing, quality control, quality assessment and personnel. The single point where the two sets of standards diverge is personnel: who may direct, supervise and perform the testing. Following the insert alone satisfies CLIA only for waived tests.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Competency Assessment · RMA III.C.4.c training for moderate complexity
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant begins performing moderate complexity testing in March. How often must her performance be evaluated and documented?
opciones: At least twice during her first year of testing patient specimens, then at least once a year
At least once during her first year of testing patient specimens, and then at least twice a year
At least twice a year for as long as she tests, with no change after that first year ends
At least once every two years, the same interval at which the certificate itself is renewed
preguntas.explicacion: Competency is evaluated and documented semiannually through the first year an individual tests patient specimens, and annually from then on. The extra scrutiny in year one is the point of the rule. Two years is the life of a CLIA certificate, not a competency interval.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antihistamines", Indications and Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.a · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: An older adult asks why the provider chose cetirizine instead of diphenhydramine for allergic rhinitis. What is the reason?
opciones: Second-generation agents barely enter the brain, so they sedate less and go first
First-generation agents barely enter the brain, so they suit a driver on therapy
Second-generation agents block H2 receptors, so they settle the stomach as well
First-generation agents are the guideline choice once drowsiness has worn off
preguntas.explicacion: First-generation H1 antagonists are lipophilic and cross into the brain, so they bring sedation, slowed reaction times and anticholinergic trouble: dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, blurred vision. Second-generation agents stay peripheral, and guidelines put them first for allergic rhinitis and urticaria. In older adults the risk of falls and of cognitive decline has narrowed the use of diphenhydramine.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(8), Workplace labeling
preguntas.subtema: Portable containers · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist pours a bleach solution from a labeled jug into a basin she will use and empty during her own shift. Must she label the basin?
opciones: No: a portable container for her own immediate use is exempt
No: containers under one liter are exempt from workplace labels
Yes: every container in the work area needs the full label
Yes: unless the jug's own label is carried alongside the basin
preguntas.explicacion: No label is required on a portable container filled from a labeled one when whoever did the pouring means to use it right away herself. The exemption is narrow, and it turns on that immediate personal use rather than on the size of the container: a bottle filled for the next shift, or for somebody else, falls straight back under the workplace labeling rule. Drugs a pharmacy dispenses for direct administration are exempt as well.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Lactose intolerance — Causes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 food intolerance · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(e) · RMA I.A.2 disorders
preguntas.pregunta: What causes the symptoms of lactose intolerance?
opciones: Too little of the enzyme lactase to digest the sugar in milk
An immune reaction to the protein in cow's milk and dairy foods
Too little stomach acid to break down the fat in dairy products
Damage to the small intestine caused by the gluten in malted milk
preguntas.explicacion: Lactose is the sugar of milk and dairy foods, and the enzyme lactase is what digests it. Infants make lactase for breast milk; production may fall off later, which is why the problem is common in adults. An illness or surgery involving the small intestine can also lower how much lactase is made.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi), (d)(3)(vii) and (d)(3)(viii), Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Removing PPE before leaving · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and heads to the cafeteria still wearing her gloves and lab coat. What does the standard require?
opciones: All PPE must be removed before leaving the work area and placed in a designated container
Gloves must be removed, but the lab coat may be worn out if it is not visibly soiled
PPE may be worn out if hands are washed first with soap and running water
PPE may be worn out if it is penetrated by blood, so long as it is changed within the shift
